headline: My Son Loved His Pokemon Card... Then He Found Out What It Was Worth
html_content:
My four-year-old twins have discovered Pokémon cards.

If you're unfamiliar with Pokémon, the basic premise is that there are hundreds of little fictional creatures, each with its own name, appearance, and special abilities. The creatures appear on trading cards that kids (and plenty of adults) collect, trade, and sometimes use to play a game.

Most cards are worth pennies. Some sell for hundreds or thousands of dollars.

My boys know approximately none of this.

As far as they're concerned, Pokémon cards are little pieces of cardboard with cool pictures on them, and they would very much like to own every single one.

It's been a surprisingly good introduction to money. We're working through those first financial questions, like why we can't buy 10 packs every time we go to the store, and why sometimes we have to choose between one thing we want and another.

Mostly, though, they're just having a wonderful time.

We've started visiting a local comic book shop, where some incredibly kind collectors have taken the boys under their wing. They let them dig through boxes of inexpensive cards, help them find their favorites and sometimes hand them a few for free. I suspect they remember what it felt like to fall in love with the hobby themselves.

One of my sons now carries a binder of his favorite cards in a backpack so he can show them to anyone willing to look.

And here's what I've loved most about watching them collect: They have absolutely no idea which cards they're supposed to want.

They pick whatever catches their eye. A cool-looking dragon. A funny little creature with a ridiculous face. Something pink and sparkly. Whether it costs 10 cents or $10 doesn't matter.

They just know what they like.

Or at least, they did.

The Little Sheep That Wasn't Worth Much

Recently, we spent an afternoon with friends whose slightly older kids also collect Pokémon cards.

Naturally, the binders came out.

My son was admiring a card in one of the older boys' collections when the boy announced proudly, "Oh yeah, that's the most expensive card in my binder."

There's nothing wrong with that. Understanding rarity and what other collectors will pay is part of the fun once kids get old enough.

But my son had never thought about his cards that way. So he held up one of his own favorites.

"This one is my favorite," he said. "Is it expensive?"

It was Wooloo, a Pokémon that looks like an impossibly fluffy little sheep. In fairness, it's an excellent sheep.

But no, the card wasn't expensive.

And when he learned that, his face fell. No tears, no tantrum. Just the quiet, unmistakable disappointment of a little kid realizing that something he loves isn't as impressive to someone else as he'd hoped.

It was such a small moment. I haven't stopped thinking about it.

Five minutes earlier, that card was one of his favorite possessions. He loved the fluffy sheep. He was proud of the fluffy sheep. He wanted to show everyone the fluffy sheep.

Then he found out other people wouldn't pay much for it. And suddenly, that seemed to matter.

Nothing about the card had changed. Only the way he was looking at it.

When Do We Start Letting Price Tags Decide?

I've spent more than a decade writing about personal finance, and now that my boys are asking questions about money, I think a lot about what I want them to understand.

I want them to learn how to earn, save, invest and spend responsibly. I want them to know that things cost money, that we can't have everything we want (and that's okay), and that sometimes we have to choose between what feels good now and what's better for us later.

But I'm realizing there's another lesson I need to teach them, too:

Money matters because of what it lets us do, have, experience and enjoy. But the price of something doesn't determine how much we're supposed to enjoy it.

That's harder to master than it sounds.

You might love your house. You saved for years to buy it, you've made it your own, and it's where your family gathers at the end of the day. Then you visit a friend's new place, with its enormous kitchen and professionally landscaped backyard, and suddenly yours feels a little small.

Or you're perfectly happy with your car until a coworker pulls in with a fancier badge on the hood.

Or you have a wonderful vacation, then see someone's photos from a luxury resort and wonder whether you should have gone somewhere nicer.

The house hasn't changed. Neither has the car. You didn't enjoy your vacation any less while you were on it.

But now you have something to compare it to.

You don't have to be particularly materialistic for this to happen. It's human. We look around to figure out what's desirable and successful, and because money offers such a convenient yardstick, price starts standing in for qualities that are much harder to measure.

Quality. Happiness. Achievement. Worth.

Price can even change how we experience something in the moment. In a well-known 2008 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, researchers at Caltech and Stanford had volunteers taste wines labeled with different prices. Some of the "different" wines were actually the same wine. Participants reported enjoying the identical wine more when they were told it was more expensive, and brain scans showed more activity in a region associated with pleasure.

Same wine. Different price tag. Different experience.

Sometimes price tells us something useful. Sometimes it tells us very little.

Expensive and Valuable Aren't the Same Thing

To be clear, there's nothing wrong with liking expensive things. Ask anyone who knows me, I like plenty of expensive things.

Sometimes paying more gets you better quality, better performance, more convenience or an experience you genuinely love. If you've worked hard, saved thoughtfully and can comfortably afford something that makes you happy, you don't need to apologize for buying it.

But here's the distinction I keep coming back to:

There's a difference between wanting something that happens to be expensive and wanting something because it's expensive.

One starts with what you value. The other starts with what someone else values.

And the second one gets awfully expensive, awfully fast. There's always a bigger house. A nicer car. A more exclusive vacation. A watch (or Pokémon card) that costs more than the one you already own. If the goal is to have the thing that impresses other people, there's no finish line.

That's why I think knowing what matters to you is one of the most underrated financial skills there is.

What I Hope My Boys Learn

Since the Wooloo incident, we've been talking more about the difference between expensive and valuable.

I'm trying to help the boys understand that a card can be expensive because it's rare or because lots of people want it. That's real, and understanding how prices work matters. But it doesn't automatically make it a better card for them.

A $100 card might be somebody's dream find. A 10-cent card might be the one you want to carry in your backpack and show everyone you meet. Both are perfectly good reasons to love a card.

So now, when one of them asks, "Is that card expensive?" I tell them I don't know how much money it costs — but is there something about it they think is special?

I don't expect my four-year-olds to walk away with a sophisticated understanding of markets, consumer psychology, and personal values. We're still working on why 10 packs of Pokémon cards isn't a reasonable Monday afternoon activity. And there will be plenty of times when they want something mostly because somebody else has it.

I still do that sometimes, and I'm considerably older than four.

But I hope that as they grow up, they learn to recognize the difference. I hope they can appreciate beautiful, expensive things without feeling they need to own them. I hope they can celebrate what someone else has without wondering whether what they have is good enough. And I hope they understand that enjoying something doesn't require anyone else's approval.

I want my boys to grow up knowing exactly how much money matters.

And exactly how much it doesn't.

So if one of them decides his favorite card in the whole world is a 10-cent picture of a fluffy sheep?

I hope he loves that little Wooloo for as long as he wants.

It's an excellent sheep, after all.

excerpt: HOOD posted a strong beat-and-raise Q2 that sent its earnings outlook surging, landing it a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). Robinhood's earnings and revenue growth outlook highlights its expanding portfolio.
headline: Bull of the Day: Robinhood Markets, Inc. (HOOD)
html_content:
Robinhood Markets, Inc. HOOD is steadily building its credentials as a financial services giant and a Wall Street technology innovator.

HOOD posted a strong beat-and-raise Q2 that sent its earnings outlook surging, landing it a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). Robinhood’s earnings and revenue growth outlook highlights its expanding portfolio.

The free trading app has become a legitimate rival to Fidelity and other online brokerages, serving a broader range of everyday retail investors, sophisticated traders, and more.

HOOD, which joined the S&P 500 in September 2025, boasts 13 different business lines that generate ~$100 million or more in annualized revenue, ranging from options and crypto trading to its credit card unit, prediction market, and more.

Robinhood boosted its in-house artificial intelligence offerings, including rolling out cutting-edge agentic trading accounts to fend off broader fears that AI will eat away at its business and the wider online brokerage and financial services industry.

The stock, which has nearly doubled the Zack Tech sector and blown away the S&P 500 since its 2021 IPO, is down ~30% from its October 2025 peaks.

Robinhood's average Zacks price target implies 25% upside from its current levels, and it would need to climb roughly 43% to return to its all-time high. Plus, HOOD is on the verge of a potential technical breakout. 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Now might be time for investors to consider buying the beaten-down financial technology stock for long-term upside and near-term breakout potential, especially if more money rotates out of AI stocks trading at all-time highs to start third-quarter earnings season. 

Best Non-AI Technology Stocks to Buy Now: Robinhood

Robinhood is closer to a legitimate peer of Fidelity, Charles Schwab, and other online brokerage titans than a meme-stock trading app that users treat like a casino. The firm offers retirement accounts, crypto trading, futures, options, a browser-based desktop trading platform built for active traders, wealth management, prediction markets (to take on Polymarket), and beyond.

HOOD currently operates 13 business lines that each generate ~$100 million or more in annualized revenues, double its total from 2023. The company’s two newest big businesses are its credit card unit and its Robinhood Legend—a browser-based desktop trading platform built for active and intermediate-to-advanced traders.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The trading app powerhouse announced a splashy new AI initiative on September 29, aiming to “put the power of hedge funds in every trader’s pocket.”

The company unveiled its new Robinhood Agents, its agentic AI tools, at its 2026 summit. HOOD said that its “fully embedded AI experience can analyze the market, build strategies, and trade on your behalf around the clock.” On top of that, its “Agent Apps will give your Robinhood Agents another layer of intelligence with institutional-grade data and specialized tools from leading third party providers.”

Furthermore, Robinhood announced plans to launch 24/7 weekend trading for equities and beyond for eligible U.S. customers. Its new AI-boosted efforts and weekend expansion plans are part of its mission to become “the #1 place for active traders.”


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The firm more than tripled its revenue between 2022 and 2025, soaring from $1.36 billion to $4.47 billion. HOOD also went from losing -$6.99 a share in 2022 to posting GAAP earnings of +$2.06 per share last year.

Most recently, Robinhood’s total platform assets jumped by 32% YoY to $369 billion in the second quarter, “driven by continued Net Deposits and higher equity valuation.” Its net deposits climbed by an annualized growth rate of 28% in Q2, with its Average Revenue Per User up 24% to $187.

Meanwhile, its total revenue climbed 32% YoY, and Gold Subscribers rose 39% to 4.8 million. Robinhood Gold users pay ($5/mo or $50/yr) for offerings including 3.6% APY on eligible brokerage cash, bigger instant deposits, lower commissions on futures trades, and other perks.

The growing financial services company grew its GAAP earnings by 48% in the second quarter, crushing our Q2 earnings estimates by 41% in the process.

Robinhood’s improving earnings outlook helps it earn a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) right now. Its recent stretch of positive revisions extends a turnaround that started this summer after its EPS outlook slipped, sparking its pullback. And its Most Accurate estimates came in above its already improved Zacks consensus.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Looking ahead, Robinhood is projected to grow its EPS by over 4% in 2026 and 37% in FY27 to reach $2.94 a share. The nearby chart shows that HOOD is projected to grow its earnings to roughly $3.50 a share in 2028.

On the top line, Robinhood is projected to grow its revenue by 19% in 2026 and 29% in 2027 to reach $6.82 billion, up from $4.47 billion in 2025. 

Buy HOOD Stock Now On the Dip and Hold?

Robinhood stock has climbed ~210% since its 2021 IPO, including a massive downturn that was fueled by the 2022 tech-driven bear market. The stock soared ~1,090% over the last three years, blowing away the Magnificent 7, including Nvidia, and many other AI stocks.

The Wall Street tech stock’s run includes its ~30% drop from its early October 2025 records. This means the stock offers ~43% upside if it ever returns to its peaks. Meanwhile, its average Zacks price target implies 25% upside from its current price of roughly $109 a share.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

HOOD stock completed the bullish golden cross at the end of July, with its 50-day moving average crossing above its 200-day. More recently, the stock experienced a long-term bullish signal when its 21-week moving average moved above its 50-week in late September.

Robinhood stock is finding buyers 50-day and its longer-term 21-week moving average. The bulls also held their ground at its previous peaks throughout 2026.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

HOOD’s selloff, mixed with its strong earnings outlook, has it trading at a 90% discount to its highs at 39.5X forward 12-month earnings.

Robinhood trades at a 70% discount to its highs in terms of its price/earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio at 1.6 vs. the Zacks Tech sector’s 1.2.

Since 1988, the full list has beaten the market more than 2X over with an average gain of +23.9% per year. So be sure to give these hand picked 7 your immediate attention.

headline: Grab These 3 Nuveen Mutual Funds for Outstanding Returns
html_content:
Nuveen, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America (TIAA), manages approximately $2.6 trillion in assets, as of Oct. 1, 2026. Founded by John Nuveen in 1898, the company offers a broad range of investment solutions across public and private markets, including equities, fixed income, real estate, infrastructure and private capital.

Nuveen serves individual and institutional investors through a multi-specialist structure, providing access to diverse investment strategies and asset classes. Its investment specialists include Nuveen Asset Management, Winslow Capital Management, Churchill Asset Management and other affiliated investment businesses.

Below, we share with you three top-ranked mid-cap blend mutual funds, namely Nuveen Quant Small Cap Equity TSCWX, Nuveen Large Cap Value Retirement TRLCX and Nuveen Quant Small Cap Equity Retirement TRSEX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and is expected to outperform its peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of funds.

Nuveen Quant Small Cap Equity primarily invests in small-cap equities with strong prospects for significant long-term capital appreciation, aiming to deliver favorable total returns.

Nuveen Quant Small Cap Equity has three-year annualized returns of 21.4%. As of April 2026, TSCWX held 377 issues, with 2.9% of its assets invested in Bloom Energy.

Nuveen Large Cap Value Retirement mainly invests in large-cap value stocks, with a portion of assets allocated to foreign investments under normal market conditions.

Nuveen Large Cap Value Retirement has three-year annualized returns of 19.2%. TRLCX has an expense ratio of 0.65%.

Nuveen Quant Small Cap Equity Retirement invests primarily in small-cap equities with strong long-term capital appreciation potential, aiming to generate favorable total returns.

Nuveen Quant Small Cap Equity Retirement has three-year annualized returns of 20.6%. Nan Zhang has been one of the fund managers of TRSEX since 2025.

To view the Zacks Rank and the past performance of all mid-cap blend mutual funds, investors can click here to see the complete list of Nuveen mutual funds.

excerpt: Style Box ETF report for SPYD
headline: Should State Street SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 High Dividend ETF (SPYD) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
The State Street SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 High Dividend ETF (SPYD) was launched on October 21, 2015, and is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

The fund is sponsored by State Street Investment Management. It has amassed assets over $7.13 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Value

Companies that find themselves in the large cap category typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Overall, they are usually a stable option, with less risk and more sure-fire cash flows than mid and small cap companies.

Carrying lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, value stocks also have lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. Considering long-term performance, value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in almost all markets; however, they are more likely to underperform growth stocks in strong bull markets.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.07%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 4.48%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

ETFs offer a diversified exposure and thus minimize single stock risk but it is still important to delve into a fund's holdings before investing. Most ETFs are very transparent products and many disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Real Estate sector -- about 24.5% of the portfolio. Consumer Staples and Financials round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Accenture Plc Cl A (ACN) accounts for about 1.67% of total assets, followed by Hp Inc (HPQ) and Target Corp (TGT).

The top 10 holdings account for about 14.81% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

SPYD seeks to match the performance of the S&P 500 High Dividend Index before fees and expenses. The S&P 500 High Dividend Index is designed to measure the performance of the top 80 dividend-paying securities listed on the S&P 500 Index, based on dividend yield.

The ETF has added roughly 9.8% so far this year and is up roughly 12.77% in the last one year (as of 10/13/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $41.96 and $50.68.

The ETF has a beta of 0.73 and standard deviation of 13.92% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 82 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

State Street SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 High Dividend ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, SPYD is a great option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Value segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) and the Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) track a similar index. While Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF has $110.85 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF has $188.60 billion. SCHD has an expense ratio of 0.06% and VTV charges 0.03%.

Bottom-Line

While an excellent vehicle for long term investors, passively managed ETFs are a popular choice among institutional and retail investors due to their low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency.

To learn more about this product and other ETFs, screen for products that match your investment objectives and read articles on latest developments in the ETF investing universe, please visit Zacks ETF Center.

headline: Should You Invest in the iShares U.S. Broker-Dealers & Securities Exchanges ETF (IAI)?
html_content:
Looking for broad exposure to the Financials - Brokers/ Capital markets segment of the equity market? You should consider the iShares U.S. Broker-Dealers & Securities Exchanges ETF (IAI), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on May 1, 2006.

Passively managed ETFs are becoming increasingly popular with institutional as well as retail investors due to their low cost, transparency, flexibility and tax efficiency. They are excellent vehicles for long term investors.

Investor-friendly, sector ETFs provide many options to gain low risk and diversified exposure to a broad group of companies in particular sectors. Financials - Brokers/ Capital markets is one of the 16 broad Zacks sectors within the Zacks Industry classification. It is currently ranked 5, placing it in top 31%.

Index Details

The fund is sponsored by Blackrock. It has amassed assets over $1.32 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs attempting to match the performance of the Financials - Brokers/ Capital markets segment of the equity market. IAI seeks to match the performance of the Dow Jones U.S. Select Investment Services Index before fees and expenses.

The Dow Jones U.S. Select Investment Services Index measures the performance of the investment services sector of the U.S. equity market.

Costs

Cost is an important factor in selecting the right ETF, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts if all other fundamentals are the same.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.37%, making it on par with most peer products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.19%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation in the Financials sector -- about 99.8% of the portfolio.

Looking at individual holdings, Goldman Sachs Group (GS) accounts for about 19.16% of total assets, followed by Morgan Stanley (MS) and Charles Schwab (SCHW).

The top 10 holdings account for about 67.79% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

Year-to-date, the iShares U.S. Broker-Dealers & Securities Exchanges ETF has added roughly 0.64% so far, and it's up approximately 5.45% over the last 12 months (as of 10/13/2026). IAI has traded between $158.28 and $198.06 in this past 52-week period.

The ETF has a beta of 1.09 and standard deviation of 20.19% for the trailing three-year period, making it a high risk choice in the space. With about 40 holdings, it has more concentrated exposure than peers.

Alternatives

iShares U.S. Broker-Dealers & Securities Exchanges ETF carries a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Thus, IAI is a sufficient option for those seeking exposure to the Financials ETFs area of the market. Investors might also want to consider some other ETF options in the space.

State Street SPDR S&P Capital Markets ETF (KCE) tracks S&P Capital Markets Select Industry Index. The fund has $508.59 million in assets. KCE has an expense ratio of 0.35%.

headline: Should Invesco S&P MidCap Quality ETF (XMHQ) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
Looking for broad exposure to the Mid Cap Blend segment of the US equity market? You should consider the Invesco S&P MidCap Quality ETF (XMHQ), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on December 1, 2006.

The fund is sponsored by Invesco. It has amassed assets over $5.46 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs attempting to match the Mid Cap Blend segment of the US equity market.

Why Mid Cap Blend

Compared to large and small cap companies, mid cap businesses tend to have higher growth prospects and are less volatile, respectively, with market capitalization between $2 billion and $10 billion. Thus they have a nice balance of growth potential and stability.

Blend ETFs usually hold a mix of growth and value stocks as well as stocks that exhibit both value and growth characteristics.

Costs

When considering an ETF's total return, expense ratios are an important factor, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts in the long term if all other factors remain equal.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.25%, putting it on par with most peer products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.57%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

While ETFs offer diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk, a deep look into a fund's holdings is a valuable exercise. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Industrials sector -- about 29.4% of the portfolio. Information Technology and Healthcare round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Technipfmc Plc (FTI) accounts for about 4.48% of total assets, followed by Illumina Inc (ILMN) and Everpure Inc (P).

The top 10 holdings account for about 32.08% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

XMHQ seeks to match the performance of the S&P MIDCAP 400 QUALITY INDEX before fees and expenses. The S&P MidCap 400 Quality Index is designed to provide equal-weighted exposure to approximately 800 securities of medium-sized companies in the larger US equity market.

The ETF return is roughly 11.95% so far this year and is up roughly 12.26% in the last one year (as of 10/13/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $97.49 and $119.88.

The ETF has a beta of 0.98 and standard deviation of 18.04% for the trailing three-year period. With about 82 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

Invesco S&P MidCap Quality ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, XMHQ is an excellent option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Mid Cap Blend segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The Vanguard Morningstar Mid-Cap ETF (VO) and the iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap ETF (IJH) track a similar index. While Vanguard Morningstar Mid-Cap ETF has $106.58 billion in assets, iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap ETF has $122.76 billion. VO has an expense ratio of 0.03% and IJH charges 0.05%.

Bottom-Line

Retail and institutional investors increasingly turn to passively managed ETFs because they offer low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency; these kind of funds are also excellent vehicles for long term investors.

excerpt: Smart Beta ETF report for SFY
headline: Is SoFi Select 500 ETF (SFY) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
Making its debut on 04/11/2019, smart beta exchange traded fund SoFi Select 500 ETF (SFY) provides investors broad exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Growth category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

For a long time now, the ETF industry has been flooded with products based on market capitalization weighted indexes, which are designed to represent the broader market or a particular market segment.

Market cap weighted indexes offer a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way of replicating market returns, and are a good option for investors who believe in market efficiency.

On the other hand, some investors who believe that it is possible to beat the market by superior stock selection opt to invest in another class of funds that track non-cap weighted strategies--popularly known as smart beta.

This kind of index follows this same mindset, as it attempts to pick stocks that have better chances of risk-return performance; non-cap weighted strategies base selection on certain fundamental characteristics, or a mix of such characteristics.

Methodologies like equal-weighting, one of the simplest options out there, fundamental weighting, and volatility/momentum based weighting are all choices offered to investors in this space, but not all of them can deliver superior returns.

Fund Sponsor & Index

The fund is sponsored by Sofi. It has amassed assets over $715.99 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs in the Style Box - Large Cap Growth. This particular fund seeks to match the performance of the SOLACTIVE SOFI US 500 GROWTH INDEX before fees and expenses.

The Solactive SoFi US 500 Growth Index follows a rules-based methodology that tracks the performance of 500 of the largest U.S.-listed companies weighted based on a proprietary mix of their market capitalization and fundamental factors.

Cost & Other Expenses

Cost is an important factor in selecting the right ETF, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive cousins if all other fundamentals are the same.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.05%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It's 12-month trailing dividend yield comes in at 0.39%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure that minimizes single stock risk, investors should also look at the actual holdings inside the fund. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation in the Information Technology sector - about 50.2% of the portfolio. Healthcare and Financials round out the top three.

Taking into account individual holdings, Nvidia Corp (NVDA) accounts for about 15.74% of the fund's total assets, followed by Microsoft Corp (MSFT) and Apple Inc (AAPL).

The top 10 holdings account for about 43.96% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

The ETF return is roughly 17.77% so far this year and was up about 22.91% in the last one year (as of 10/13/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $120.71 and $157.29

The fund has a beta of 1.10 and standard deviation of 17.68% for the trailing three-year period. With about 504 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

SoFi Select 500 ETF is an excellent option for investors seeking to outperform the Style Box - Large Cap Growth segment of the market. There are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider as well.

Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG) tracks CRSP U.S. Large Cap Growth Index and the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) tracks NASDAQ-100 Index. Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF has $236.94 billion in assets, Invesco QQQ has $498.86 billion. VUG has an expense ratio of 0.03% and QQQ changes 0.18%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Style Box - Large Cap Growth

Bottom Line

To learn more about this product and other ETFs, screen for products that match your investment objectives and read articles on latest developments in the ETF investing universe, please visit Zacks ETF Center.

headline: Invest in 3 Nomura Mutual Funds for Long-Term Growth
html_content:
Nomura Asset Management is the investment management arm of Nomura Group with approximately $860 billion in assets under management. It offers a wide range of mutual funds, including equity, fixed income and multi-asset strategies as well as private credit investments. The firm provides investment management services to wealth management and institutional clients worldwide, employing fundamental research, disciplined risk management and seasoned investment professionals to manage its actively managed investment strategies in pursuit of risk-adjusted returns across various markets.

We have picked three Nomura mutual funds — Nomura Emerging Markets DEMCX, Optimum Large Cap Growth OCLGX and Nomura Floating Rate DDFCX — which investors should buy now for the long term. These funds have a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or Rank 2 (Buy), with positive three-year and five-year annualized returns, minimum initial investments within $5000 and expense ratios considerably lower than the category average. So, these funds have provided comparatively stronger performance and carry a lower fee. 

Nomura Emerging Markets fund seeks long-term capital appreciation. DEMCX invests primarily in equity securities of issuers located or operating in emerging countries. 

Liu-Er Chen has been the lead manager of DEMCX since Sept. 25, 2006. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as SK Square Co., Ltd. (29.5%), SK hynix Inc. (18.6%) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (3.3%) as of May 31, 2026. 

DEMCX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 58.5% and 24.7%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 2.16%. DEMCX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.             

To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 (Strong Buy) and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here. 

Optimum Large Cap Growth fund seeks long-term growth of capital. OCLGX invests its net assets in securities of large market capitalization companies.

Jeffrey R. Bourke has been the lead manager of OCLGX since July 18, 2022. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as NVIDIA Corp (14.5%), Apple Inc. (10.5%) and Microsoft Corp (7.1%) as of March 31, 2026.  

OCLGX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 19.6% and 7.7%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 1.95%. OCLGX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.              

Nomura Floating Rate fund invests most of its assets in floating-rate loans and other floating-rate debt securities, with allocations across fixed-income sectors determined by economic and market conditions and the manager’s assessment of their return potential.

John P. McCarthy has been the lead manager of DDFCX since Jan. 31, 2017. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as Miscellaneous Bonds (52.1%), Cash (5.1%) and Jefferies Financial Group Inc.  (1.8%) as of April 30, 2026. 

DDFCX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 6.6% and 5.1%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 1.67%. DDFCX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

headline: Is DWS Emerging Markets Equity Instl (SEKIX) a Strong Mutual Fund Pick Right Now?
html_content:
If you have been looking for Non US - Equity funds, it would not be wise to start your search with DWS Emerging Markets Equity Instl (SEKIX). SEKIX bears a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank of 4 (Sell), which is based on various forecasting factors like size, cost, and past performance.

Objective

Zacks categorizes SEKIX as Non US - Equity, a segment stacked high with options. Non US - Equity mutual funds like to invest in companies outside of the United States, an important characteristic since global mutual funds are known to keep a good portion of their portfolio stateside. These kinds of funds can often extend across all cap levels, and will typically allocate their investments between emerging and developed markets.

History of Fund/Manager

DWS is responsible for SEKIX, and the company is based out of New York, NY. DWS Emerging Markets Equity Instl made its debut in March of 2008, and since then, SEKIX has accumulated about $23.86 million in assets, per the most up-to-date date available. Performance

headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Alpha Metallurgical Resources Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Alpha Metallurgical Resources, Inc. AMR need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Nov 20, 2026 $100 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Alpha Metallurgical Resources shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Alpha Metallurgical Resources is a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) in the Mining – Miscellaneous industry that ranks in the Bottom 24% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, no analysts have increased their earnings estimates for the current quarter, while one analyst has revised the estimate downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from earnings of 14 cents per share to a loss of $1.29 per share in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Alpha Metallurgical Resources right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

excerpt: Digital wallets now account for 56% of global online shopping spend, while AI and instant payments are opening new doors. Four stocks stand out: MA, SHOP, PYPL and MQ.
headline: Top Mobile Payments Stocks to Buy as Digital Wallet Adoption Soars
html_content:
An updated edition of the August 24, 2026 article.

Mobile payments are changing how people shop, pay bills and move money. A phone can now replace a wallet at the checkout counter, while a quick scan or tap can complete a purchase in seconds. For businesses, the shift goes beyond convenience. Tap-to-phone technology lets merchants accept payments without buying separate terminals, and faster payment networks help move funds with less delay. As digital payments become part of daily life, companies are competing to make each transaction simpler and safer.

Digital Wallets Become the Default

Digital wallets remain central to this change. Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal have made paying online and in stores easier, supported by contactless technology, QR codes and in-app checkout. Worldpay's Global Payments Report 2026 shows that digital wallets accounted for 56% of global e-commerce spending and 33% of in-person spending in 2025. Wider smartphone use and better internet access are bringing more people into the market, while smartwatches and other connected devices offer more ways to pay. Many wallets still run on card networks, so their growth also creates opportunities for established payment providers.

AI Moves Into the Checkout

Artificial intelligence is adding another layer. Payment companies use it to spot unusual transactions, reduce fraud and make authentication smoother. Tokenization and biometric checks also help protect account details. The bigger change could come from agentic commerce, where AI assistants search for products and complete purchases with a user's approval. Visa, Mastercard and Google are building tools for this emerging model. Adoption is still early, but it could change how consumers reach checkout and how payment companies serve them. Meanwhile, apps such as WeChat, Alipay and PhonePe continue to combine shopping, transfers and financial services in one place.

Stablecoins and Instant Payments Gain Ground

Payments are also moving beyond traditional card rails. Stablecoins and blockchain are drawing interest for cross-border transfers and business settlement, where transactions often face delays and extra costs. Visa said in September 2026 that stablecoin settlement volume had topped a $20 billion annualized rate. Real-time bank payments are growing too. India's UPI handled about 24.07 billion transactions in September 2026, while Brazil's Pix and the U.S. FedNow network are widening access to instant transfers. Europe is pressing ahead with instant-payment rules and payment-services reforms. Buy now, pay later (BNPL) options are becoming easier to access directly at checkout. Fraud, regulation and pressure on fees remain challenges as competition grows.

Market Outlook and Key Players

The growth outlook remains strong. Fortune Business Insights estimates the global mobile payments market at $4.97 trillion in 2025 and $6.46 trillion in 2026, with a projected rise to $46.62 trillion by 2034. That implies a 28% annual growth rate from 2026 to 2034. Asia Pacific held 46.1% of the market in 2025, underlining the scale of adoption across the region.

Against this backdrop, competition is intensifying, as Mastercard Incorporated MA, Shopify Inc. SHOP,PayPal Holdings, Inc. PYPL and Marqeta, Inc. MQ expand their capabilities through new products, technology investments and partnerships. Our Mobile Payments Screen highlights stocks with exposure to the broader mobile-payments market.

Ready to uncover more transformative thematic investment ideas? Explore 40 cutting-edge investment themes with Zacks Thematic Investment Screens and discover your next big opportunity.

4 Mobile Payments Stocks to Buy

Marqeta provides the technology behind mobile payments. Its API-based platform lets banks, fintechs and businesses issue virtual and physical cards, add cards to Apple Pay and Google Pay, control spending and approve transactions in real time. Tokenization helps protect card details while enabling contactless payments.

The company's mobile-payment reach expanded in August 2026 through Google's Wallet for kids offering. Marqeta supplies card issuing, tokenization and spending controls, allowing supervised users to tap to pay with Android phones and Wear OS devices while parents set limits and monitor activity. Partnerships announced with zerohash in July and BVNK in September aim to connect stablecoin balances to payment cards, broadening use cases.

Operating momentum supports this strategy. Second-quarter 2026 total processing volume rose 32% year over year to $120 billion, while net revenue increased 17% to $176 million. Gross profit grew 17% to $122 million. Processing volume in lending, including BNPL, climbed more than 40%, and expense-management volume rose over 50%.

Non-U.S. payments represented 20% of total processing volume. However, Block accounted for 41% of revenue, while lower-yield programs weighed on monetization. Continued wallet integration and cross-border expansion could strengthen Marqeta's position. The company currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Mastercard is a major enabler of mobile payments, connecting banks, merchants and digital wallets through its global network. Its technology lets consumers tap their phones, pay within apps and complete online purchases, while tokenization replaces sensitive card details with secure digital credentials. In July 2026, it introduced Mastercard Wallet Services, giving banks and fintechs tools to add contactless payments to their own iOS and Android apps.

In September, Mastercard launched Wallet Pay to help providers such as Alipay+ and GCash connect wallets to merchants worldwide through NFC, QR codes and online checkout. The offering also supports card issuance and cross-border transfers. Mastercard expanded Agent Connect and Agent Pay capabilities that month, preparing merchants for purchases initiated by AI assistants with customer authorization and fraud checks.

Second-quarter 2026 results show the scale behind these efforts. Net revenues increased 14% year over year to $9.3 billion, while gross dollar volume rose 8% to $2.9 trillion. Switched transactions grew 9% to 47.4 billion. Contactless payments represented 80% of in-person switched purchase transactions, and tokenized transactions exceeded 40% of all switched activity. Expanding wallet partnerships and digital security services will support further growth. The company carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present.

Shopify supports mobile payments through Shop Pay, Shopify Payments and its point-of-sale (POS) software. Shop Pay saves shoppers' payment and delivery details for faster checkout on phones and other devices. Shopify Payments handles transactions for merchants, while Tap to Pay lets eligible retailers accept contactless cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay using compatible iPhones or Android phones, without separate card readers.

In June 2026, Shopify extended Tap to Pay to businesses operating multiple legal entities, helping them route and track store payments separately. Its June developer release also opened AI-powered shopping tools to developers, creating another potential channel for checkout. In October, Shop introduced faster sign-in, synchronized carts across devices and prefilled Shop Pay buttons to reduce abandoned purchases.

Second-quarter 2026 results underscored growing payment adoption. Shopify Payments processed $78.1 billion in gross merchandise value (GMV), up 38% year over year, with penetration rising to 68% from 64%. Total GMV climbed 32% to $115.6 billion, while Merchant Solutions revenues advanced 37% to $2.78 billion.

Shop Pay GMV rose 53%, and free cash flow reached $654 million, providing room for further investment. Greater payment usage and easier mobile checkout will continue to support expansion. It currently carries a Zacks Rank #2.

PayPal supports mobile payments through its PayPal and Venmo apps, enabling consumers to shop, transfer funds and pay merchants without handling cash or physical cards. PayPal checkout connects shoppers with online sellers, while Venmo combines peer-to-peer transfers with merchant payments. Braintree processes transactions for businesses, and PayPal Pay Later offers installment options at checkout.

Recent launches have widened PayPal's reach. In August 2026, PayPal World began allowing U.S. customers to pay at Weixin Pay merchants in China by scanning QR codes through the PayPal app, without a local wallet. Venmo also became a payment option on Google Play for apps, games and subscriptions. New integrations with campus payment platforms opened another channel for tuition payments.

Second-quarter 2026 results highlighted continued transaction growth. Total payment volume increased 10% year over year to $486.45 billion, while payment transactions climbed 8% to 6.75 billion. Venmo volume rose 14% to $93.81 billion, and active accounts reached 439 million.

Revenues improved 5% to $8.68 billion, although transaction margin dollars advanced only 1%. Branded checkout volume increased 2% on a currency-neutral basis, reflecting stabilization. Expanding wallet acceptance and Venmo usage support PayPal's mobile-payments prospects. PYPL currently carries a Zacks Rank #2.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

excerpt: Peoples Bancorp (PEBO) possesses the right combination of the two key ingredients for a likely earnings beat in its upcoming report. Get prepared with the key expectations.
headline: Peoples Bancorp (PEBO) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
html_content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when Peoples Bancorp (PEBO) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 20, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This financial services and products company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.92 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +2.2%.

Revenues are expected to be $123.17 million, up 6.9% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 3.54% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Peoples Bancorp?

For Peoples Bancorp, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +1.09%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #1.

So, this combination indicates that Peoples Bancorp will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Peoples Bancorp would post earnings of $0.84 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.96, delivering a surprise of +14.29%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Peoples Bancorp appears a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

excerpt: FRD is benefiting from record sales volumes, stronger pricing and Century Metals gains, but steel price volatility and supplier concentration remain challenges.
headline: Friedman Surges More Than 127% in 6 Months: What's Driving the Stock?
html_content:
Friedman Industries, Incorporated FRD investors have been experiencing some short-term gains from the stock of late. Shares of the Longview, TX-based diversified metals processing and pipe manufacturer have gained 127.4% in the past six months against the industry’s 19.8% decline. The stock also outperformed the sector and the S&P 500’s 1.9% decline and 11.7% gain, respectively, in the same time frame.

Two major developments of FRD in recent months include the rebranding of its Texas Tubular Products division (this month) and the announcement of its promising first-quarter fiscal 2027 results (in June).

In the fiscal first quarter, Friedman reported higher sales, driven by record sales volumes, improved average selling prices and contributions from the Century Metals acquisition. Most of the year-over-year volume growth came from existing facilities. The flat-roll segment benefited from higher sales volumes, stronger pricing and acquisition contributions, while the tubular segment reported improved sales and operating earnings. Favorable hot-rolled coil (HRC) prices also supported margin expansion.

Management highlighted Century Metals’ positive contributions to growth and profitability, alongside improved performance across existing operations. Looking ahead, FRD expects fiscal second-quarter sales volumes to remain comparable with the fiscal first quarter, with higher average selling prices anticipated to support sequential margin improvement.

FRD’s Six-Month Price Comparison


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Over the past three months, the stock’s performance has remained strong, outperforming that of its peers like Ampco-Pittsburgh Corporation AP and Century Aluminum Company CENX. Ampco-Pittsburgh and Century Aluminum’s shares have gained 2.2% and plunged 45.2%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Despite cyclical and volatile steel market conditions, the favorable share price movement suggests FRD is well-positioned to sustain its positive momentum at present.

Friedman’s flat-roll products segment primarily generates revenues from the sale of company-owned inventory, while also generating revenues by processing and storing customer-owned material on a fee basis. The tubular products segment generates revenues from the sale of company-owned inventory.

FRD’s Growth and Expansion

Friedman continues to strengthen its operating platform through improved capacity utilization and strategic investments in processing infrastructure. Existing facilities contributed most of the recent sales volume growth, highlighting the company's ability to expand organically. The addition of processing capacity at Granite City and ongoing building and processing capability expansion at Sinton provide opportunities to increase production efficiency and accommodate future demand. These initiatives could support sustained volume growth without relying solely on acquisitions.

The successful integration of Century Metals & Supplies has expanded Friedman's presence in the Southeastern United States and Latin American markets. The acquisition broadened its portfolio beyond traditional carbon steel products to include stainless steel, aluminum, copper, brass and coated materials. These additional offerings enable FRD to serve a wider range of industrial requirements and strengthen its diversified metals processing platform. Management has also highlighted Century Metals' meaningful contributions to growth and profitability, supporting its acquisition-led expansion strategy.

Friedman benefits from longstanding customer relationships and an established reputation for reliable service. Its vendor-managed inventory systems simplify customers' inventory planning, while electronic data interchange improves communication and reduces processing errors. Additionally, the customer portal provides convenient access to order information and reports. These technology-enabled services strengthen customer engagement, improve operational coordination and support customer retention, reinforcing FRD's competitive position in the metals processing industry.

Friedman’s Margins and Shareholder Value

Strengthening HRC prices have created a favorable pricing environment for Friedman, contributing to improved sales margins and operating profitability. Management expects higher average selling prices to support further sequential margin improvement in the fiscal second quarter, while sales volumes are anticipated to remain comparable with the preceding quarter. This favorable pricing outlook, combined with expectations of stable sales volumes, could support FRD's near-term profitability.

Friedman maintains a disciplined approach to capital allocation, balancing financial flexibility with shareholder distributions. The company has consistently paid quarterly dividends since becoming publicly traded, reflecting its longstanding commitment to returning capital. Its strategy also includes opportunistic share repurchases, providing an additional mechanism for enhancing shareholder value. Management's emphasis on sustainable dividend payments and prudent capital management supports FRD's long-term financial priorities.

Challenges Ahead for FRD

Friedman faces challenges from fluctuations in steel prices and supplier concentration. Volatility in HRC prices can affect inventory valuations, selling prices and profit margins, while hedging activities may lead to additional earnings fluctuations. Additionally, both the flat-roll and tubular segments depend on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials. The loss of a key supplier or disruptions in material availability could affect production continuity, increase procurement challenges and adversely impact operating performance.

Friedman Stock’s Valuation

Friedman’s trailing 12-month EV/Sales of 0.4X is lower than the industry’s average of 1.7X but higher than its five-year median of 0.2X.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Ampco-Pittsburgh and Century Aluminum’s trailing 12-month EV/Sales currently stand at 0.7X and 1.3X, respectively, in the same time frame.

Our Final Take on FRD

Friedman’s impressive share-price rally over the past six months appears to be supported by improving business fundamentals and favorable growth prospects. Strong organic volume growth, improved capacity utilization, expanding processing capabilities and the successful integration of Century Metals have strengthened its operating platform. Favorable steel prices have also supported margin expansion, while the recent rebranding of its tubular division reflects efforts to strengthen its market identity.

However, sustaining this momentum will depend on Friedman’s ability to execute its growth initiatives consistently amid changing steel market conditions. Steel price volatility can affect margins and inventory values, while dependence on a limited number of suppliers could create procurement challenges. Although FRD employs risk management practices to mitigate commodity price exposure, its performance remains sensitive to industry cycles.

From a valuation standpoint, FRD continues to trade at a discount to the broader industry and its peers, suggesting that the stock may still offer potential value despite its substantial appreciation. However, its valuation has become less attractive relative to historical levels, indicating that some optimism surrounding its improving prospects is already reflected in the share price. Consequently, further upside may increasingly depend on sustained business performance rather than valuation expansion alone.

For existing shareholders, Friedman’s growth opportunities, diversified operations and disciplined capital allocation support staying invested. Prospective investors may also find the stock worth considering, although its sharp rally calls for a measured approach. Overall, FRD's improving fundamentals provide a basis for continued positive momentum, but sustaining the gains will require consistent execution and effective management of industry-related challenges.

excerpt: BDCO's upgrade to "Neutral" reflects stronger cash flow, lower debt and improved refinery performance, though defaults and margin risks persist.
headline: Blue Dolphin Upgraded to Neutral on Improving Fundamentals
html_content:
Blue Dolphin Energy Company BDCO has been upgraded to “Neutral”, reflecting its significantly improved financial position, stronger operational execution and potential upside from favorable jet fuel refining spreads.

The company's robust first-half 2026 performance has eased liquidity and operating concerns that previously weighed on our outlook. Substantial operating cash generation, debt repayments and improved refinery availability have strengthened its near-term financial profile.

Favorable middle-distillate market conditions could continue to support refining profitability. Nevertheless, outstanding debt defaults, exposure to volatile refining margins and significant related-party dependence warrant a cautious stance.

Debt Reduction & Improved Liquidity Strengthen Financial Position

Blue Dolphin's substantial improvement in cash generation and balance-sheet liquidity is a key factor supporting our upgrade. In the first six months of 2026, operating activities generated $39 million in cash, reversing the $3.3-million cash outflow recorded in the prior-year period. The stronger cash flow enabled the company to make $9.2 million in debt-principal repayments, including $7.7 million toward related-party obligations.

Consequently, total debt declined to $39.9 million as of June 30, 2026, from $49.1 million at the end of 2025. Cash and cash equivalents increased sharply to $30.7 million from $1 million over the same period.

Importantly, current assets of $81.2 million exceeded current liabilities of $65.3 million at June-end, marking a meaningful improvement from the working-capital deficit at the end of 2025. Stockholders' equity also increased to $59.8 million from $27.4 million. This financial recovery provides Blue Dolphin with greater flexibility to meet near-term obligations and manage working-capital requirements. Although certain loan agreements remain in default and refinancing risks persist, the reduced debt burden and stronger liquidity position have moderated our previous concerns regarding the company's financial stability.

Stronger Operational Execution Supports Earnings Recovery

Blue Dolphin's improved refinery performance and operational discipline provide additional justification for the upgrade. During the second quarter of 2026, sales volumes increased 56.3% year over year to 1.15 million barrels, supported by improved operating availability at its Nixon refinery.

Refinery downtime declined to just one day from 14 days in the year-ago quarter, although the prior-year period included a planned turnaround. Consequently, refining EBITDA was $23.8 million against a loss of $0.9 million a year earlier, while refining EBITDA per barrel improved to $20.79 from negative $1.21.

For the first half of 2026, refining EBITDA surged to $43 million from $4 million in the year-ago period, reflecting both improved throughput and stronger product margins. The company also refurbished or replaced several critical pieces of refinery equipment, including the naphtha stabilizer heater, boiler deaerator, crude oil desalter and crude oil charge pump. These initiatives are intended to improve product yields, lower energy consumption and minimize future downtime.

Blue Dolphin maintained relatively stable general and administrative expenses despite substantial revenue growth, highlighting its operating leverage. Continued operational reliability and disciplined cost management could support earnings generation even if refining margins moderate from recent elevated levels.

Potential Jet Fuel Spread Tailwinds Could Support Refining Margins

Blue Dolphin's significant exposure to jet fuel provides another potential catalyst for profitability, particularly if favorable middle-distillate market conditions persist. Jet fuel generated $44.2 million in refinery revenues in the second quarter of 2026 and $78.8 million in the first half of the year, representing a substantial portion of the company's product sales. Its Nixon refinery processes light-sweet Eagle Ford crude into jet fuel and other petroleum products, positioning it to benefit when jet fuel selling prices strengthen relative to feedstock costs.

The company's first-half earnings recovery was partly driven by a sharply widened differential between crude oil acquisition costs and refined-product selling prices. Looking ahead, resilient aviation fuel demand and potential supply tightness in middle-distillate markets could help sustain favorable jet fuel spreads.

Such conditions would provide incremental margin support, particularly given Blue Dolphin's relatively simple refining configuration and meaningful jet fuel exposure. Its established affiliate sales arrangement, through which jet fuel is marketed to the Defense Logistics Agency, also provides an existing commercial outlet for production. However, the magnitude and durability of these potential tailwinds remain uncertain, as refining spreads are inherently sensitive to crude prices, product demand and broader market conditions.

Conclusion

Our upgrade of Blue Dolphin to “Neutral” from “Underperform” reflects a meaningful improvement in the company's risk-reward profile. Substantial debt reduction, improved liquidity, stronger refinery execution and potential jet fuel spread tailwinds have reduced the downside risks that previously supported our negative recommendation.

Nevertheless, persistent debt covenant defaults, concentrated affiliate exposure and the possibility of refining margin normalization limit our conviction in a sustained earnings recovery. We believe that the improved financial and operating fundamentals justify a more balanced outlook, with the shares expected to perform broadly in line with the market.

excerpt: Paying your credit card bill every month, but debt not going away? Zacks' Personal Finance editor Meredith Margrave breaks down why paying your credit card's minimum can keep you in debt for years and reveals the simple payment change that can save you thousands.
headline: How a $10,000 Credit Card Balance Can Cost You More Than $21,000
html_content:
I have a financial pet peeve I'd like to share with you... It's "minimum payment due."

It sits right there on your credit card statement next to a perfectly reasonable-looking number — maybe $75, maybe $150, maybe $200. And if you're like most people, you assume that number means something. Surely someone at the credit card company did the math and decided this is an appropriate amount to pay toward your debt each month. It is, after all, exactly what they're asking for.

So you pay it, every month, on time, like a responsible adult. Then six months later you check your balance and discover you've barely made a dent.

What the heck?

If that's happened to you, it's not because you did anything wrong. It's because of something every credit card holder should understand:

Your minimum payment is designed to keep your account current. It isn't designed to get you out of debt.

One of those benefits the credit card company, and the other benefits you. And the gap between those two goals can cost you a staggering amount of money.

How a $10,000 Balance Can Cost You More Than $21,000

Let's say you have a $10,000 credit card balance at a 20% annual percentage rate (APR). That's actually a little generous; credit card accounts that were charged interest carried an average APR of about 22% as of August 2026, according to the Federal Reserve.

How you got there doesn't matter much. Maybe you had a few unexpected expenses, put a vacation on the card, or watched the balance creep up over a couple of years. Either way, you owe $10,000, and you're paying $200 a month toward it. That's $2,400 a year, which is real money. Without interest, you'd be debt-free in a little over four years.

Interest changes that picture dramatically. At a 20% APR, your first month's interest on $10,000 comes to about $167, which means only about $33 of your $200 payment goes toward the money you actually borrowed.

Here's roughly how long it would take to pay off that $10,000 at different fixed monthly payments:

$200 --> 9 years, 1 month to pay it off ($11,680 interest paid)
$300 --> 4 years, 2 months ($4,718 interest paid)
$400 --> 2 years, 9 months ($3,044 interest paid)
$500 --> 2 years, 1 month ($2,266 interest paid)

Illustrative estimates based on a 20% APR compounded monthly, fixed monthly payments, and no new purchases. Actual results depend on your card's interest calculation and terms.

At $200 a month, you'd spend more than nine years paying off the card and about $11,680 in interest — more than you originally borrowed. Your $10,000 debt becomes a nearly $22,000 expense.

Raise that payment from $200 to $300, just $100 more a month, and you'd be debt-free almost five years sooner while saving nearly $7,000 in interest.

Same debt, same interest rate, same credit card company. Just a different payment.

Why Minimum Payments Are So Sneaky

I used a fixed $200 payment to keep the math simple, but your card's actual minimum probably doesn't work that way. Most issuers calculate it with a formula — often a small percentage of your balance, or a percentage of your balance plus that month's interest and fees — with a floor of something like $25 or $35.

That formula has a catch: As your balance goes down, your minimum payment usually goes down, too.

A smaller bill sounds like good news, but think about what it means in practice. Your minimum starts at $200, drops to $175 as you pay the balance down, and then to $150. If you pay only what's required, you end up putting less toward your debt the more progress you make. It's like running a marathon and slowing down every time you get closer to the finish line. You're still moving forward, but you're going to be out there for a very long time.

That's why paying only the minimum can be even more expensive than the table above suggests. And all of those numbers assume you've stopped using the card. If you keep charging new purchases while making minimum payments, the finish line moves even further away.

Your Statement Is Trying to Warn You

Here's something many cardholders don't realize: Your credit card company is required to warn you about all of this.

Under the Credit CARD Act of 2009, monthly statements generally must include a Minimum Payment Warning. It shows how long it would take to pay off your balance making only minimum payments and how much you'd pay in total. It also shows the monthly payment needed to clear the balance in three years, and how much that would save you.

If you carry a balance, pull up your latest statement and find that box. Seeing a $175 minimum payment feels manageable. Seeing that paying $175 a month could keep you in debt for the next decade feels like a problem worth solving. That's what makes the disclosure so useful: It turns a vague monthly obligation into a concrete timeline with real dollar amounts attached.

How to Escape the Minimum Payment Trap

Okay, enough doom and gloom. The good news is that you don't need to find thousands of dollars to make real progress. As the table shows, relatively modest changes to your monthly payment can produce dramatic results. Here's where I'd start.

1. Stop treating the minimum like a recommendation.

The minimum is the least you can pay to keep your account in good standing, and nothing more. Look at your budget, figure out what you can realistically afford to put toward the debt each month, and make that your new payment target, whether it's $250, $400, or $750.

2. Keep your payment fixed, even when your minimum drops.

This is one of my favorite strategies because it's so simple. Say your minimum is $250, and that's what you can comfortably afford. Six months later, the minimum drops to $225. Keep paying $250 anyway. As your balance shrinks, less of each payment goes to interest and more goes to principal, so your payoff speeds up without you spending a dollar more than you'd already budgeted.

3. Find an extra $50 or $100 a month.

I know that's easier said than done. But going from $200 to $300 a month in our example saved nearly $7,000 in interest, which is an enormous return on $100.

That might mean cutting back on takeout for a while, canceling a few subscriptions, or pausing a savings goal that can wait. It might also mean putting part of your next bonus, tax refund, or other windfall toward the balance. The point isn't to make yourself miserable. It's to recognize that an extra $100 toward high-interest debt today saves you considerably more down the road.

4. Lower your interest rate.

If you're carrying a substantial balance, a card with an introductory 0% APR on balance transfers can give you a window to pay down debt without new interest piling up. There are catches: Most balance transfers come with a fee, typically 3% to 5% of the amount you move, and whatever's left when the promotion ends is charged the card's regular rate. Paired with a solid repayment plan, though, a balance transfer can be a powerful tool.

You can also call your current issuer and ask for a lower APR. There's no guarantee, but it costs you nothing to ask.

5. Automate your payments.

If you've read my work for a while, you know I'm a big fan of automating your finances, and debt payments are no exception. Set up autopay for at least the minimum so you never miss a due date, then schedule an additional fixed payment each month if your budget allows. You'll protect your credit history while making steady progress. Just make sure your checking account can comfortably cover both.

What If You Can Only Afford the Minimum?

Sometimes the minimum genuinely is the best you can do. Maybe you recently lost your job, you're dealing with medical bills, or your budget is already stretched so thin that there's nothing left to redirect. If that's where you are right now, please don't read this as advice to skip groceries or risk your mortgage payment to send an extra $100 to your credit card company.

Making the minimum payment is still far better than missing a payment. It keeps your account current, helps you avoid late fees, and protects your credit.

If even the minimum is becoming a struggle, call your issuer before you fall behind. Many offer hardship programs that can temporarily lower your interest rate or your payment. A nonprofit credit counseling agency, such as one affiliated with the National Foundation for Credit Counseling, can also help you build a realistic repayment plan.

The goal isn't perfection. It's understanding what the minimum payment does, and what it doesn't, so you can make informed decisions about your money.

Don't Let Your Credit Card Company Set Your Goals

What frustrates me most about minimum payments is that they create the illusion of progress. You get a bill, you pay the amount requested, and you check it off your list. Meanwhile, month after month, a large share of your hard-earned money goes to interest instead of building your emergency fund, growing in your retirement account, paying for a family vacation, or simply giving your budget some breathing room.

So the next time your statement arrives, look past the minimum payment. Check your interest rate, how much interest you were charged last month, and what that Minimum Payment Warning says. Then ask yourself one question: What's the most I can reasonably afford to pay toward this debt?

The sooner you stop letting your credit card company decide how slowly you pay it back, the sooner that money starts working for you instead.

And I can think of about a thousand things I'd rather do with $7,000 than give it to a credit card company.
