headline: Bear of the Day: Krispy Kreme (DNUT)
html_content:
Krispy Kreme Donuts Overview

Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) Krispy Kreme, Inc (DNUT) is adonut and sweet treat brand best-known for its signature Original Glazed doughnut. The company sells its products through brick-and-mortar locations. Additionally, Krispy Kreme sells through distribution outlets like grocery stores, gas stations, and major fast-food partners such as McDonald’s (MCD).

GLP-1 Use Surges

According to a recent Gallup poll, 11% of U.S. adults, or roughly 28 million people, are on GLP-1 weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, and Mounjaro (up from 11% in 2024). Meanwhile, the Gallup poll does not include the many patients who have found alternative, cheaper paths to access unregulated versions of these drugs. GLP-1 drugs delay gastric emptying and signal fullness to the brain. According to Morgan Stanley, consumers remove confectionary, baked goods, and salty snacks from their diets. In fact, multiple studies suggest that sweet bakery purchases plunge nearly 10% once a patient starts these medications. Given that the majority of Krispy Kreme’s business relies on high calorie, sugary items, the rapid rise of GLP-1s is a significant long-term headwind for the company.

Krispy Kreme: Relative Weakness & Low Share Price

Krispy Kreme shares have chronically underperformed in both the short and long term. Over the past 5 years, DNUT shares have lost 78.8% of their value while the S&P 500 Index has gained 85.4%. With no end in sight to the bearish fundamentals, and little in the way of bullish catalysts, the persistent relative weakness should be a red flag for prospective investors.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Additionally, Krispy Kreme’s stock currently trades at ~$3 per share. Stocks that trade for less than $10 per share typically deter institutional investors because they raise liquidity, scalability, and regulatory concerns. Because institutional investors have the deepest pockets and drive long-term moves, share price action is another problem for Krispy Kreme.

Krispy Kreme Doughnuts: A Consistent Underperformer

Wall Street analysts continue to hold a bearish outlook on Krispy Kreme. Zacks Consensus Analyst Estimates suggest that the company will deliver negative revenue growth through 2027.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Meanwhile, the company’s earnings surprise history has been spotty. Krispy Kreme has missed Wall Street expectations in 8 of the past 19 quarters.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

An Ugly Balance Sheet

On top of tepid growth, high CAPEX, thin operating margins, and a heavy debt load plague Krispy Kreme. Its debt-to-equity ratio has nearly tripled since 2022.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Bottom Line

Krispy Kreme faces severe long-term growth challenges as the rapid adoption of GLP-1 weight-loss medications directly impacts demand for sugary baked goods. Combined with chronic relative weakness, negative revenue growth, and soaring debt, DNUT shares remain an avoid.

Radical New Technology Could Hand Investors Huge Gains

Quantum Computing is the next technological revolution, and it could be even more advanced than AI.

While some believed the technology was years away, it is already present and moving fast. Large hyperscalers, such as Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle, and even Meta and Tesla, are scrambling to integrate quantum computing into their infrastructure.

Senior Stock Strategist Kevin Cook reveals 7 carefully selected stocks poised to dominate the quantum computing landscape in his report, Beyond AI: The Quantum Leap in Computing Power.

Kevin was among the early experts who recognized NVIDIA's enormous potential back in 2016. Now, he has keyed in on what could be "the next big thing" in quantum computing supremacy. Today, you have a rare chance to position your portfolio at the forefront of this opportunity.

excerpt: Whether you're a value, growth, or momentum investor, finding strong stocks becomes easier with the Zacks Style Scores, a top feature of the Zacks Premium research service.
headline: Here's Why CACI International (CACI) is a Strong Value Stock
html_content:
Taking full advantage of the stock market and investing with confidence are common goals for new and old investors, and Zacks Premium offers many different ways to do both.

The research service features daily updates of the Zacks Rank and Zacks Industry Rank, full access to the Zacks #1 Rank List, Equity Research reports, and Premium stock screens, all of which will help you become a smarter, more confident investor.

Zacks Premium also includes the Zacks Style Scores.

What are the Zacks Style Scores?

Developed alongside the Zacks Rank, the Zacks Style Scores are a group of complementary indicators that help investors pick stocks with the best chances of beating the market over the next 30 days.

Each stock is given an alphabetic rating of A, B, C, D or F based on their value, growth, and momentum qualities. With this system, an A is better than a B, a B is better than a C, and so on, meaning the better the score, the better chance the stock will outperform.

The Style Scores are broken down into four categories:

Value Score

Value investors love finding good stocks at good prices, especially before the broader market catches on to a stock's true value. Utilizing ratios like P/E, PEG, Price/Sales, Price/Cash Flow, and many other multiples, the Value Style Score identifies the most attractive and most discounted stocks.

Growth Score

While good value is important, growth investors are more focused on a company's financial strength and health, and its future outlook. The Growth Style Score takes projected and historic earnings, sales, and cash flow into account to uncover stocks that will see long-term, sustainable growth.

Momentum Score

Momentum investors, who live by the saying "the trend is your friend," are most interested in taking advantage of upward or downward trends in a stock's price or earnings outlook. Utilizing one-week price change and the monthly percentage change in earnings estimates, among other factors, the Momentum Style Score can help determine favorable times to buy high-momentum stocks.

VGM Score

If you want a combination of all three Style Scores, then the VGM Score will be your friend. It rates each stock on their combined weighted styles, helping you find the companies with the most attractive value, best growth forecast, and most promising momentum. It's also one of the best indicators to use with the Zacks Rank.

How Style Scores Work with the Zacks Rank

The Zacks Rank, which is a proprietary stock-rating model, employs earnings estimate revisions, or changes to a company's earnings expectations, to make building a winning portfolio easier.

#1 (Strong Buy) stocks have produced an unmatched +23.86% average annual return since 1988, which is more than double the S&P 500's performance over the same time frame. However, the Zacks Rank examines a ton of stocks, and there can be more than 200 companies with a Strong Buy rank, and another 600 with a #2 (Buy) rank, on any given day.

With more than 800 top-rated stocks to choose from, it can certainly feel overwhelming to pick the ones that are right for you and your investing journey.

That's where the Style Scores come in.

To maximize your returns, you want to buy stocks with the highest probability of success. This means picking stocks with a Zacks Rank #1 or #2 that also have Style Scores of A or B. If you find yourself looking at stocks with a #3 (Hold) rank, make sure they have Scores of A or B as well to ensure as much upside potential as possible.

The direction of a stock's earnings estimate revisions should always be a key factor when choosing which stocks to buy, since the Scores were created to work together with the Zacks Rank.

Here's an example: a stock with a #4 (Sell) or #5 (Strong Sell) rating, even one with Style Scores of A and B, still has a downward-trending earnings outlook, and a bigger chance its share price will decrease too.

Thus, the more stocks you own with a #1 or #2 Rank and Scores of A or B, the better.

Stock to Watch: CACI International (CACI)

Based in Reston, VA, CACI International delivers IT applications and infrastructure to improve communications and secure the integrity of information systems and networks, enhance data collection and analysis, and increase efficiency and mission effectiveness. The company’s solutions enrich defense and intelligence capabilities, assure homeland security, improve decision-making, and help customers operate smartly and proficiently.

CACI is a #2 (Buy) on the Zacks Rank, with a VGM Score of B.

It also boasts a Value Style Score of B thanks to attractive valuation metrics like a forward P/E ratio of 18.91; value investors should take notice.

For fiscal 2027, two analysts revised their earnings estimate upwards in the last 60 days, and the Zacks Consensus Estimate has increased $0.58 to $32.24 per share. CACI boasts an average earnings surprise of +11.2%.

With a solid Zacks Rank and top-tier Value and VGM Style Scores, CACI should be on investors' short list.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

excerpt: AI adoption, surging infrastructure spending and accelerating cloud revenues are boosting the cloud computing industry. Here are four cloud ETFs to watch.
headline: A Guide to Cloud Computing ETF Investing
html_content:
Cloud computing is a process in which data or software is stored outside a computer and can be accessed anywhere, at any time, via the Internet. This idea is effective as it helps firms lower IT costs by eliminating the need for servers and related maintenance costs.

Also, it provides greater accessibility. Since everything is on the Internet, users can access any data or document at any moment. Needless to say, such advantages make it a thing of tomorrow.

Global investment in cloud services has increased by leaps and bounds in recent years. Cloud stocks, particularly those tied to artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, have risen massively in price in the recent past.

Growth in Cloud Infrastructure

The widespread adoption of remote connectivity continues to fuel the need for scalable and reliable cloud solutions. Moreover, advancements in cloud technologies, including AI, machine learning (ML) and cybersecurity enhancements, have expanded the use cases for cloud services.

In second-quarter 2026, global cloud infrastructure service spending grew to $143.4 billion (an increase of more than $43 billion from second-quarter 2025), marking the highest growth rate in eight years, per Synergy Research.

Despite its massive size, the cloud market continues to grow, with year-over-year growth accelerating for 11 straight quarters. Fueled by AI demand, growth hit its highest level since 2021, per Statista. Going forward, cloud infrastructure service revenues are on track to top $500 billion for the first time in 2026, per data provided by Statista. 

Goldman Sachs expects the trend of accelerating cloud revenue growth to continue this quarter, with year-over-year growth increasing from 48% in the second quarter to 55% in the third quarter, as quoted on Yahoo Finance.          

AI Keeps Cloud Stocks Resilient

Major cloud providers often hold up better during market pullbacks, geopolitical tensions and economic slowdowns. AI is increasingly being seen as essential infrastructure, supporting continued demand for data centers, computing power and cloud services. These are now viewed as fundamental assets required for future economic competitiveness.

Worldwide AI-optimized infrastructure as a service (IaaS) spending is projected to grow 96% in 2026, reaching $42.3 billion, according to Gartner. The spending is expected to grow 56.5% to $66.1 billion in 2027.

According to the International Data Corporation (IDC), cloud infrastructure spending continues to surge, driven heavily by enterprise AI adoption and data center expansion. Global AI infrastructure spending alone is forecast to reach $497 billion, while total public cloud spending is on track to surpass $1 trillion, as quoted on W. Media.

IDC predicts spending on cloud infrastructure to record a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 14.3% over the 2023-2028 forecast period, reaching $213.7 billion in 2028 and accounting for 75% of total compute and storage infrastructure spend.

Inside Market Share

Global enterprise spending on cloud infrastructure services reached $143 billion in second-quarter 2026, up $43 billion year over year, per Synergy, as quoted on CRN. AWS remains the cloud infrastructure leader, with a 28% global market share in the first quarter of 2026, ahead of Microsoft Azure at 20% and Google Cloud at 15%. Together, the “Big Three” control more than 60% of the market.

Neocloud Expands the AI Infrastructure Market

Neocloud refers to a specialized segment of cloud computing that provides high-performance, AI-focused infrastructure, including powerful GPUs, to businesses through the cloud. It offers flexible and scalable computing for AI training, inference and other demanding workloads without requiring companies to build and maintain costly infrastructure.

Neocloud providers normally lock in multi-year compute contracts, generating a steadier, more predictable revenue stream than the on-demand model of traditional cloud. Companies such as CoreWeave and Nebius are expanding capacity and stand to benefit from this model.

Neocloud revenues are growing over 200% year over year. The broader neocloud market is projected to expand at an average annual growth rate of roughly 58% through 2031, rising toward a market size of $400 billion, according to Synergy Research.

ETFs in Focus

Against this backdrop, we have highlighted a few cloud computing ETFs that could stand to gain in the coming days.

First Trust Cloud Computing ETF SKYY

The underlying ISE Cloud Computing Index is a modified market capitalization-weighted index designed to track the performance of companies actively involved in the cloud computing industry. The $3.46-billion-asset fund charges 60 bps in fees.

Everpure (5.51%), DigitalOcean (3.92%) and Nutanix (3.57%) are the three top holdings of the fund. Software (44.78%), IT Services (24.37%) and Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals (11.96%) are the three top industries of the fund.

WisdomTree Cloud Computing ETF WCLD

The underlying BVP Nasdaq Emerging Cloud Index is an equally weighted Index, designed to measure the performance of emerging public companies focused on delivering cloud-based software to customers. The fund has an asset base of $291.3 million and charges 45 bps in fees. No stock makes up more than 1.94% of the fund.

Global X Cloud Computing ETF CLOU

The underlying Indxx Global Cloud Computing Index provides exposure to exchange-listed companies in developed and emerging markets that are positioned to benefit from the increased adoption of cloud computing technology.

The fund has an asset base of $398.5 million and charges 68 bps in fees. Snowflake (7.31%), Paycom Software (5.41%) and Datadog Class-A (4.77%) hold the top three spots in the fund.

Fidelity Cloud Computing ETF FCLD

The underlying Fidelity Cloud Computing Index reflects the performance of a global universe of companies across the market capitalization spectrum that provide products or services enabling the increased adoption of cloud computing, characterized by the delivery of computing services over the internet.

The fund has an asset base of $153.1 million and it charges 39 bps in fees. Microsoft (4.95%), Snowflake (4.54%) and Salesforce (4.40%) are the top three companies in the fund.

Neocloud Expands the AI Infrastructure Market Neocloud refers to a specialized segment of cloud computing that provides high-performance, AI-focused infrastructure, including powerful GPUs, to businesses through the cloud. It offers flexible and scalable computing for AI training, inference and other demanding workloads without requiring companies to build and maintain costly infrastructure. Neocloud providers normally lock in multi-year compute contracts, generating a steadier, more predictable revenue stream than the on-demand model of traditional cloud. Companies such as CoreWeave and Nebius are expanding capacity and stand to benefit from this model. Neocloud revenues are growing over 200% year over year. The broader neocloud market is projected to expand at an average annual growth rate of roughly 58% through 2031, rising toward a market size of $400 billion, according to Synergy Research. ETFs in Focus Against this backdrop, we have highlighted a few cloud computing ETFs that could stand to gain in the coming days. First Trust Cloud Computing ETF SKYY The underlying ISE Cloud Computing Index is a modified market capitalization-weighted index designed to track the performance of companies actively involved in the cloud computing industry. The $3.46-billion-asset fund charges 60 bps in fees. Everpure (5.51%), DigitalOcean (3.92%) and Nutanix (3.57%) are the three top holdings of the fund. Software (44.78%), IT Services (24.37%) and Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals (11.96%) are the three top industries of the fund. WisdomTree Cloud Computing ETF WCLD The underlying BVP Nasdaq Emerging Cloud Index is an equally weighted Index, designed to measure the performance of emerging public companies focused on delivering cloud-based software to customers. The fund has an asset base of $291.3 million and charges 45 bps in fees. No stock makes up more than 1.94% of the fund. Global X Cloud Computing ETF CLOU The underlying Indxx Global Cloud Computing Index provides exposure to exchange-listed companies in developed and emerging markets that are positioned to benefit from the increased adoption of cloud computing technology. The fund has an asset base of $398.5 million and charges 68 bps in fees. Snowflake (7.31%), Paycom Software (5.41%) and Datadog Class-A (4.77%) hold the top three spots in the fund. Fidelity Cloud Computing ETF FCLD The underlying Fidelity Cloud Computing Index reflects the performance of a global universe of companies across the market capitalization spectrum that provide products or services enabling the increased adoption of cloud computing, characterized by the delivery of computing services over the internet. The fund has an asset base of $153.1 million and it charges 39 bps in fees. Microsoft (4.95%), Snowflake (4.54%) and Salesforce (4.40%) are the top three companies in the fund. excerpt: Nextpower raises fiscal 2027 guidance after an earnings beat, backed by a $5.5B-plus backlog, but rising platform investments and operating costs pose challenges.
headline: Can NXT's Raised Guidance Outweigh Rising Platform Investment Costs?
html_content:
Nextpower Inc. NXT raised the lower ends of several fiscal 2027 guidance ranges after a first-quarter earnings beat, reinforcing management’s confidence in backlog conversion and broader product adoption.

The trade-off is higher spending. NXT is investing aggressively in power conversion, energy storage and other non-tracker offerings, so the key question is whether new revenue streams can scale fast enough to absorb the platform build-out.

NXT’s Guidance Raise Signals Backlog Confidence

Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance now stands at $4.10-$4.40 billion, up from $4.00-$4.40 billion previously. Adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to $870-$930 million from $845-$930 million, while adjusted earnings per share guidance rose to $4.42-$4.73 from $4.30-$4.73.

The higher floor follows first-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.20 per share, which beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.04 by 15.4%. Revenues of $935.2 million also topped the consensus mark of $932.3 million. Backlog exceeded $5.5 billion, giving NXT meaningful visibility into planned deliveries.

How NXT’s New Businesses Expand the Revenue Base

Platform expansion is starting to add measurable scale beyond trackers. Prevalon brought energy-storage backlog significantly above $300 million, while the eBOS business is expected to generate well over $100 million in fiscal 2027 revenues. NX PowerMerge bookings surpassed 850 megawatts, foundations revenues increased 50% year over year, and TrueCapture posted record revenues and backlog.

The strategy also puts NXT alongside a broader set of solar-infrastructure participants. First Solar FSLR focuses on utility-scale photovoltaic modules, while Canadian Solar CSIQ combines solar modules with battery energy storage and utility-scale project development. These companies illustrate adjacent layers of the utility-scale solar ecosystem as NXT broadens its own project participation.

Why NXT’s Investment Ramp Raises Execution Risk

The updated fiscal 2027 outlook includes about $50 million of incremental spending, primarily to accelerate the power conversion business. That investment arrives as operating costs are already rising faster than revenues, with first-quarter adjusted operating expenses up 56% year over year versus 8% revenue growth.

NXT also plans to have more than 10 gigawatts of U.S. inverter manufacturing capacity online by summer 2027, with deliveries expected to begin in early 2027. Certification progress is encouraging, but ramping factories, meeting customer schedules and integrating acquired capabilities remain execution tests.

NXT’s Margin Mix Could Make Results Uneven

Adjusted gross margin reached 36.6% in the first quarter, up from 33% a year earlier. Tariff recoveries, a higher U.S. revenue mix and TrueCapture contributions supported the improvement.

Management still targets structural gross margins in the low 30s and expects tariff-related benefits to normalize through the rest of fiscal 2027. That suggests quarterly profitability could vary as product mix, tariff recoveries and the cost of new-business expansion shift.

What NXT’s Missing Signals Mean for Guidance

The guidance raise improves the near-term operating setup, but it does not remove the cost and execution burden tied to NXT’s platform expansion. Backlog conversion and contribution from eBOS, storage and power conversion will need to keep pace with the spending ramp for the higher outlook to translate into durable earnings growth.

NXT’s Price Performance

In the past six months, shares of NXT have lost 19.4% compared with the industry’s 22.9% decline.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

NXT’s Zacks Rank

NXT currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

excerpt: Month-over-month headline CPI was in-line with expectations at +0.6%, but this is up notably for the past three months.
headline: CPI Jumps Back to Spring Levels, Pre-Markets Fall
html_content:
Wednesday, October 14th, 2026

Pre-market futures have sunk into the red this morning, immediately following the September print on the Consumer Price Index (CPI), which is showing a re-acceleration of inflation after a summer of agreeably dormant, flat levels. Bond yields are also notably higher on the news.

Ahead of the CPI report, the Dow was +227 points, the Nasdaq was +12 and the S&P 500 +25 points. Currently, the Dow is -76, the Nasdaq -217 and the S&P 500 -17 points. The 10-year yield moved from +5.187% ahead of the print to +5.304% now, the 2-year went from +4.774% to +4.924% and the 30-year from +5.540% to +5.609%.
 

CPI Inflation at Highest Rates Since Last Spring


Why the hubbub? We’d just seen the consensus estimate on year-over-year CPI headline (aka “the Inflation Rate”) tick down 10 basis points (bps) from the start of the week, but it came in as earlier expected: +3.7%. The month-over-month tally was in-line with expectations at +0.6%, but this is up notably for the past three months and now stands at the highest level since April of this year. The +3.7% Inflation Rate is highest since May.

We had seen a real flattening on the Inflation Rate over the previous three months, but now we’ve back up in the 2022 range, when inflation had spun out of control based on post-Covid supply chain issues and a slow-moving Fed to raise interest rates. 

Stripping out volatile food and energy costs bring us the core CPI numbers, and here we’re a little warmer than expected: +0.3% on core month over month and +2.6% year over year, both 10 bps higher than analysts were looking for. These numbers may look pretty benign as a static image, but they are going higher; back in June, we were at 0.0% core CPI month over month. 

Tomorrow we’ll hear the other shoe drop when the Producer Price Index (PPI) — the wholesale inflation print relative to CPI’s retail inflation — for September hits the tape. Last month, this came in 200 bps hotter on year-over-year headline than CPI did: +5.4% versus +3.4%. This figure is estimated to tick up to +5.5% in tomorrow’s report, which is clearly well above the Fed’s preferred inflation rate of +2.0%.
 

Q3 Earnings at a Glance: MS, BAC, PGR & More


Investment bank giant Morgan Stanley MS outperformed expectations in its Q3 report this morning, with earnings of $3.03 per share surpassing the $2.83 Zacks consensus. Revenues of $20.34 billion beat the $19.74 billion estimate. This continues Morgan Stanley’s strong earnings performance, which has only posted one miss in the past five years. For more on MS’ earnings, click here.

Bank of America BAC, hit by a $1.2 billion regulatory fine in its Q3, came up short of estimates this morning: earnings of $0.91 per share on revenues of $30.0 billion versus projections for $1.11 per share and $30.62 billion, respectively. This is only the second miss in the past five years for the big bank. Shares are down -7% in early trading, deepening from the stock’s -1.9% year to date.

Keeping with the finance companies another moment, BlackRock BLK posted strong numbers in its Q3 report ahead of today’s open. Earnings of $15.93 per share amounted to a +14% positive surprise, while revenues of $7.75 billion was up +3.96% from the Zacks consensus. Shares are up +2% in this tough trading environment. For more on BLK’s earnings, click here.

Auto insurance major The Progressive PGR posted a mixed Q3 this morning: earnings of $4.60 per share beat the $4.46 estimate on adjusted revenues of $23.36 billion, which narrowly missed the Zacks consensus. This does mark Progressive’s fourth-straight earnings beat, but shares are down -6% in pre-market trading.

excerpt: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) has a major catalyst approaching, with its highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) scheduled for release near mid-November.
headline: A Blockbuster Video Game Release Could Reginite This Stock
html_content:
Take-Two Interactive TTWO has a major catalyst approaching, with its highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) scheduled for release on November 19th. The title has generated massive excitement among gamers, and the blockbuster success of its predecessor suggests the release could be a major growth driver.

TTWO shares have struggled in 2026, but the upcoming release could easily reignite momentum.  


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

GTA 5's Massive Success

Grand Theft Auto V, released more than a decade ago in 2013, was a huge success right out of the gate, generating more than $800 million in worldwide retail sales in its first 24 hours. The momentum continued, with sales surpassing the $1 billion mark in just three days.

And the success has extended well beyond the initial release, with Take-Two recently reporting that GTA 5 has now sold nearly 230 million copies worldwide. The continued demand more than a decade after its initial launch helps underpin the franchise's strong staying power.

Importantly, GTA Online has also been a major positive, allowing Take-Two to generate recurring revenue through in-game purchases and additional content long after the initial sale.

GTA 6 Could Fuel Major Growth

The upcoming release offers a massive opportunity for Take-Two, especially given the enormous installed fan base already built through GTA 5. Notably, the game is launching at $79.99, above the typical $59.99 price point seen when GTA 5 was initially released.

And the company's outlook already reflects expectations for a big boost, with management forecasting $8.0-$8.2 billion in net bookings for its current FY27, up considerably from the $6.72 billion reported in FY26. At the midpoint, the outlook suggests roughly 20% growth, with GTA 6 expected to be a primary driver of the acceleration.

Beyond the initial sales boost, the long-term opportunity also remains significant. GTA 5's continued success through GTA Online provides a strong blueprint for how Take-Two could monetize the new release for years, potentially creating a much higher recurring revenue base.

Our current consensus estimates for its FY27 and FY28 are reflective of a big growth acceleration relative to recent years, with earnings forecasted to climb 71% in its current FY27 (ends in March) and an additional 40% in FY28.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The valuation picture also isn’t overstretched given the potential growth catalyst, with shares currently trading at a 24.4X forward 12-month earnings multiple, well beneath the 37.3X five-year median.

Bottom Line

Take-Two Interactive TTWO has a major catalyst approaching with GTA 6, and the success of its predecessor suggests a new period of fresh growth. GTA 5's nearly 230 million lifetime copies sold and its ability to generate revenue more than a decade after release reflect the franchise's massive appeal. The stock deserves a close eye given the upcoming release and weak price action so far in 2026.

headline: 2 Auto Equipment Providers to Buy as Technology Reshapes Industry
html_content:
The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment industry is navigating a challenging landscape. Vehicle demand remains below pre-pandemic levels, with affordability limiting any meaningful volume recovery. At the same time, electrification and software-led vehicles are shifting revenues toward technology-heavy components, while higher spending on R&D and retooling puts pressure on margins. Tariffs add further cost uncertainty and favor suppliers with established regional manufacturing. We therefore see returns concentrating in companies with strong engineering capabilities, disciplined cost control and localized footprints, while those with narrow portfolios or limited flexibility face a more difficult environment.

Despite a weak industry backdrop, select industry players such as Mobileye Global MBLY and Hesai Group HSAI are positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of advanced driver-assistance systems and the shift toward higher-value, technology-led content per vehicle.

About the Industry

The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment Industry comprises companies that design, engineer, and manufacture components and systems for vehicle manufacturers. These products span powertrain, driveline, metal forming, safety, and structural technologies supporting electric, hybrid, and internal combustion vehicles. OEM suppliers focus on improving vehicle safety, performance, efficiency, and cost competitiveness while meeting increasingly stringent regulatory and emissions standards. The industry primarily serves global automotive manufacturers, with demand closely tied to vehicle production volumes and model mix.

Themes Shaping the Industry Dynamics

Weak Buying Power Holding Back Demand: Even with supply chains largely repaired, vehicle sales are yet to return to pre-pandemic levels. Mobility Global, as reported by Tirereview, forecasts U.S. light-vehicle sales of 16.1 million units in 2026, still short of the 17 million SAAR seen before the pandemic. The core issue is cost of ownership. Households are stretched by pricier food, housing, energy, insurance and fuel, while car payments sit well above earlier levels. With budgets squeezed, fewer buyers can commit to a vehicle, which weighs on equipment makers whose revenues track vehicle volumes.

Shift to Electrified, Software-Led Vehicles: As automakers move toward electric, hybrid and software-defined models, the components they buy are changing. Redesigned platforms need lighter structures, EV-specific driveline parts, advanced safety systems and integrated electronics. This is shifting supplier revenue toward newer, technology-heavy products, while parts tied to older vehicle designs lose importance. Full autonomy is still distant, but electrification and driver assistance are already changing the component mix. Suppliers with strong engineering and matching portfolios gain share, while slower adapters risk falling behind.

Rising Costs of Staying Competitive: Keeping pace with new technology is expensive. Suppliers face higher spending on research, skilled labor and factory retooling for new platforms and materials. New features and tougher performance standards typically demand large upfront outlays before any payback. This makes lean operations, disciplined use of capital and optimized supply chains essential. Firms that hold down costs while continuing to invest in innovation can better protect their margins through market ups and downs.

Tariffs Forcing Sourcing and Production Changes: Trade policy is reshaping how and where U.S. auto parts are made. A 25% Section 232 tariff covers certain imported components, including engines, transmissions and electrical parts. This makes costs harder to predict and pushes automakers to have suppliers build nearer to assembly plants. Local production cuts long-term tariff and supply-chain exposure, but requires more capital and adds execution risk. Suppliers already operating regional facilities hold an edge over smaller, more concentrated competitors.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Gloomy Picture

The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment Industry is part of the broader Zacks Autos/ Tires/ Trucks sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #197, which places it in the bottom 20% of roughly 250 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates mixed to dull near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

The industry’s position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are losing confidence about this group’s earnings growth potential. Over the past year, the industry’s earnings estimates for the current year have declined 9.6%.

Before we present a few stocks that you may still want to consider for your portfolio, let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture.

Industry Lags Sector and S&P 500

The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment Industry has underperformed the S&P 500 and its sector over the past year. The industry has lost 11.5% over this period compared with the sector’s 6% decline. In contrast, the S&P 500 has risen 18.6%.

One-Year Price Performance

Industry's Current Valuation

Since automotive companies are debt-laden, it makes sense to value them based on the Enterprise Value/ Earnings before Interest Tax Depreciation and Amortization (EV/EBITDA) ratio.

Based on the trailing 12-month enterprise value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA), the industry is currently trading at 17.68X compared with the S&P 500’s 18.22X and the sector’s 25.51X.

Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 22.86X and as low as 8.45X, with the median being 18.21X, as the chart below shows.

EV/EBITDA Ratio (Past 5 Years)

2 Stocks Worth Buying

Mobileye: The company builds technology for driver assistance and self-driving cars. Its product range includes EyeQ chips, along with Supervision, Chauffeur and Drive, which keeps it well placed as the auto industry moves toward autonomy. The core EyeQ business is gaining from the growing use of camera-based driver-assistance systems, share gains with customers and rising exports from Chinese automakers.

In the first half of 2026, revenues grew 13%, even though production at its main customers fell 3%. This shows the company is growing faster than its end market. Mobileye has raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $1.97-$2.02 billion and expects slightly more than 39 million EyeQ units to ship. Its product mix is also shifting toward higher-value offerings. A new high-volume Cloud-Enhanced ADAS award from Stellantis begins in 2027, and its profit per unit is expected to match Surround ADAS and be more than double that of base ADAS. Surround ADAS should lift average selling prices from 2028.

Mobileye currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MBLY’s 2026 and 2027 EPS implies year-over-year growth of 36% and 7%, respectively.

You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Price & Consensus: MBLY

Hesai: The company designs and sells 3D lidar sensors for passenger cars, commercial vehicles and robots. It is strengthening its position by expanding beyond cars into robotics. More than 50 embodied AI companies worldwide work with its JT128 lidar, and GGII ranks it No. 1 in China’s humanoid and quadruped robot lidar market. In automotive, Hesai held a 44% share of China’s long-range ADAS lidar market in June 2026, and it has led that market for 17 months in a row.

It also won new design deals with Great Wall Motor, Li Auto, GAC Toyota and Volkswagen, which shows growing acceptance from both Chinese and global automakers. Looking ahead, its Picasso 6D SPAD-SoC chip is ready for the start of production. Lidar built on Picasso, called ETX, is being validated by customers and is moving toward information and quotation requests from global automakers and robotaxi operators, which could open new growth avenues.

HSAI currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for HSAI’s 2026 and 2027 EPS implies year-over-year growth of 42% and 74%, respectively.

Price & Consensus: HSAI

Radical New Technology Could Hand Investors Huge Gains

Quantum Computing is the next technological revolution, and it could be even more advanced than AI.

While some believed the technology was years away, it is already present and moving fast. Large hyperscalers, such as Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle, and even Meta and Tesla, are scrambling to integrate quantum computing into their infrastructure.

Senior Stock Strategist Kevin Cook reveals 7 carefully selected stocks poised to dominate the quantum computing landscape in his report, Beyond AI: The Quantum Leap in Computing Power.

Kevin was among the early experts who recognized NVIDIA's enormous potential back in 2016. Now, he has keyed in on what could be "the next big thing" in quantum computing supremacy. Today, you have a rare chance to position your portfolio at the forefront of this opportunity.

excerpt: ACN's AI momentum, discounted valuation & strong cash flow support growth, but acquisition reliance, pricing pressure & financing costs warrant caution.
headline: Is Accenture Worth Buying as AI Growth Meets Rising Execution Risk?
html_content:
Accenture plc ACN offers investors a clear trade-off. Enterprise AI demand, recurring services and cash generation support the growth case, while uneven discretionary spending, pricing pressure and a heavier acquisition program raise execution risk.

The valuation is lower than several key benchmarks, but fiscal 2026 organic growth was about 3%. The question is whether AI-led demand can lift underlying growth enough to justify a more aggressive stance.

Accenture’s Valuation Looks Discounted to Key Benchmarks

ACN trades at 14.4X forward 12-month earnings, below the Zacks sub-industry at 18.6X, the broader Zacks sector at 20.7X and the S&P 500 at 19.8X. The gap gives investors a valuation cushion if operating momentum improves.


                                                                            Image Source: Zacks Investment Research


                                                                                 Image Source: Zacks Investment Research


                                                                                 Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The stock also trades well below its five-year median of 24.3X. That discount is meaningful, but valuation alone does not resolve concerns around organic growth, pricing and the contribution required from acquisitions.

ACN’s AI Growth Supports the Bull Case

More than 400 clients initiated advanced AI work with Accenture in fiscal 2026, including nearly 100 in the fourth quarter. The company ended the year with nearly 110,000 AI and data professionals. Bookings from eight emerging AI and data partners more than tripled from fiscal 2025, while related revenues more than doubled.

International Business Machines Corporation IBM is also pushing enterprise AI deeper into consulting through large-scale deployment and modernization work. Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation CTSH is expanding enterprise AI services around agentic systems and major cloud platforms. Their activity reinforces the competitive race to turn AI spending into consulting and managed-services revenue.

Accenture’s M&A Push Raises Execution Costs

Accenture deployed $4.9 billion across 17 acquisitions in fiscal 2026. For fiscal 2027, it expects about $8 billion of acquisition investment, including roughly $3 billion tied to Cyber OT transactions that shifted into the new fiscal year and approximately $5 billion of additional planned investment.

The financing burden is rising with that strategy. A $5 billion bond offering completed in July 2026 is expected to add roughly $250 million of interest expense in fiscal 2027, while lower average cash balances are expected to reduce interest income by about $100 million. Successful integration and stronger organic growth therefore matter more.

ACN’s Cash Flow Balances Growth and Shareholder Returns

Fiscal 2026 free cash flow reached $11.62 billion, up from $10.87 billion a year earlier. Accenture returned a record $11.5 billion to shareholders, including $7.5 billion in share repurchases and $4.0 billion in dividends.

Management expects fiscal 2027 free cash flow of $11.0-$11.8 billion and plans to return at least $9.5 billion to shareholders. That cash generation provides room to fund acquisitions while continuing dividends and repurchases, although the capital demands are substantial.

Accenture’s Signals Favor Patience Over Aggression

Accenture has attractive AI exposure, a discounted earnings multiple and substantial free cash flow. Still, fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 3%-6% in local currency includes an expected 2%-2.5% contribution from acquisitions, while management continues to plan for intense competition and uneven discretionary spending.

ACN currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), which supports a wait-and-watch approach rather than an aggressive buy case. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

ACN’s VGM Score of A and Momentum Score of A are favorable, while its Value Score of B and Growth Score of B are also constructive. The Style Scores add useful context, but they are designed to complement the Zacks Rank rather than override it.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

excerpt: Dave & Buster's (PLAY) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Dave & Buster's (PLAY) Up 7.7% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
html_content:
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Dave & Buster's (PLAY). Shares have added about 7.7% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Dave & Buster's due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Dave & Buster's Entertainment, Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

Dave & Buster's Q2 Earnings & Revenues Miss Estimates

Dave & Buster's reported second-quarter fiscal 2026 results, with earnings and revenues missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Both metrics deteriorated on a year-over-year basis.

The company continued to face pressure from lower comparable store sales and weaker entertainment revenues. Higher store operating costs also weighed on profitability. However, food and beverage revenues increased, while management highlighted improving same-store sales trends during July and the fiscal third quarter to date.

Dave & Buster's Q2 Earnings & Revenues

For the fiscal second quarter, the company reported an adjusted loss per share of 27 cents, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of earnings of 19 cents. This resulted in a negative surprise of 242.1%. In the year-ago quarter, it posted adjusted earnings of 40 cents per share.

Quarterly revenues totaled $544.1 million, missing the consensus estimate of $561 million by 3.1% and declining 2.4% year over year. 

Food and beverage revenues, accounting for 38.9% of total revenues in the reported quarter, increased 9.6% year over year to $211.5 million from $192.9 million. Management attributed the improvement partly to enhanced menu offerings and eat-and-play combo initiatives, which supported higher food attach rates.

Entertainment revenues, representing 61.1% of quarterly revenues, declined 8.8% year over year to $332.6 million from $364.5 million. Comparable store revenues fell $15.3 million, partially offset by a $14.2 million increase in noncomparable store revenues.

Comparable store sales, including Dave & Buster's and Main Event locations, declined 2.9% year over year. Management noted improving overall same-store sales in July, with continued improvement during the fiscal third quarter to date.

PLAY's Q2 Operating Highlights

During the fiscal second quarter, operating income amounted to $19.4 million compared with $53 million reported in the year-ago quarter. The operating margin contracted to 3.6% from 9.5%.

Total cost of products increased to $83.2 million from $76.4 million. Operating payroll and benefits rose to $140.2 million from $138.7 million, while other store operating expenses jumped to $192.9 million from $186.9 million. Depreciation and amortization expenses climbed to $73.7 million from $65.2 million.

Adjusted EBITDA in the quarter was $98.9 million compared with $129.8 million in the year-earlier period. The adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 18.2% from 23.3%. Store operating income before depreciation and amortization decreased to $127.8 million from $155.4 million, with the margin contracting to 23.5% from 27.9%.

Dave & Buster's Cash Flow & Liquidity

For the first six months of fiscal 2026, net cash provided by operating activities totaled $160.6 million compared with $129.8 million in the prior-year period.

Capital expenditures were $190 million, down from $243.8 million a year ago. Adjusted free cash flow improved to positive $19.5 million compared to negative $36.5 million in the first six months of fiscal 2025. The company ended the quarter with available liquidity of $492.1 million.

Balance Sheet of PLAY

As of Aug. 4, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $16 million compared with $16.6 million as of Feb. 3, 2026. Long-term debt, net, was approximately $1.50 billion compared with $1.52 billion at the end of fiscal 2025.

PLAY's net total leverage ratio was 3.5 times at quarter-end. The company had $476.1 million of unused commitments under its revolving credit facility and stated that it was in compliance with its debt covenants.

Dave & Buster's Store Development Updates

Dave & Buster's continued to advance its store development initiatives during the fiscal second quarter. The company opened six new domestic stores during the period and ended the quarter with 250 company-owned locations.

The company expects to complete two additional Dave & Buster's remodels during the remainder of fiscal 2026, bringing the full-year total to eight. Internationally, PLAY had six franchise stores open and expects to add at least one more international franchise location during the remainder of fiscal 2026.

In the past month, investors have witnessed a downward trend in estimates revision.

The consensus estimate has shifted -6.83% due to these changes.

At this time, Dave & Buster's has a average Growth Score of C, though it is lagging a lot on the Momentum Score front with an F. However, the stock was allocated a score of A on the value side, putting it in the top quintile for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of C. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending downward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions indicates a downward shift. It's no surprise Dave & Buster's has a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell). We expect a below average return from the stock in the next few months.

excerpt: Social Security beneficiaries are getting a 3.6% raise in 2027, the largest in years. Zacks' Personal Finance expert Meredith Margrave explains why a bigger cost-of-living adjustment isn't the same as getting ahead, and what retirees should watch instead.
headline: Social Security Is Giving Retirees Their Biggest Raise in Years. That's Not Necessarily Good News
html_content:
An extra $75 a month? Who wouldn't want that?

That's about $900 more a year for groceries, utilities, and prescriptions, or maybe something a little more enjoyable. For millions of Americans living on fixed incomes, every additional dollar counts.

So when the Social Security Administration announced on Wednesday that beneficiaries will receive a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in 2027, the largest increase since 2023, it sounded like welcome news. The average retirement benefit will rise by about $75 a month, to roughly $2,170, starting in January, and about 72 million Social Security recipients will see the increase.

In many ways, it is welcome news. But there's something a little uncomfortable about celebrating a bigger Social Security raise: The bigger the increase, the more it tells us about how much prices have been rising.

A Bigger Raise Isn't Always a Better Raise

That extra $75 isn't necessarily putting retirees ahead. It's meant to keep them from falling behind. Those are two very different things.

When most of us hear the word "raise," we think of something positive... a promotion, a reward for hard work, or simply more money left at the end of the month. If your employer gives you a 5% raise while your expenses stay about the same, your financial situation genuinely improves. You can save a little more, spend a little more, or just enjoy some extra breathing room.

Social Security raises don't work that way. The annual COLA isn't a reward or a bonus. It's an inflation adjustment, based on how much the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) rose over the past year. In other words, the government measures how much consumer prices have increased and adjusts benefits to match.

That's an enormously important protection. Without it, a monthly benefit that felt sufficient at 67 could become woefully inadequate by 87. But it also means a larger COLA isn't a sign that retirees are doing better. More often, it's a sign that the cost of maintaining the same standard of living has gone up.

Consider the 8.7% COLA beneficiaries received in 2023, the largest in more than 40 years. On paper, it was an impressive raise. In reality, it reflected one of the most painful stretches of inflation in decades. Retirees weren't enjoying an 8.7% improvement in their lives; their benefits were catching up to prices that had already climbed sharply.

The same principle applies to the 3.6% increase coming in 2027.

Would You Rather Have a Bigger Check or Lower Prices?

Imagine two retirees who each receive $2,000 a month from Social Security.

The first gets a 2% COLA, bringing their benefit to $2,040, while the prices of the things they buy also rise about 2%. The second gets a 5% COLA, bringing their benefit to $2,100, but their prices rise 5%.

Which one is better off? Neither. Despite a much bigger dollar increase, the second retiree hasn't gained any purchasing power. Both are simply keeping pace with inflation.

Now change one detail: Suppose the first retiree's prices rose just 1% instead of 2%. Suddenly, that smaller 2% COLA is delivering a real improvement in what their check can buy.

The point isn't that retirees should root for tiny Social Security increases. It's that the size of the raise matters a lot less than what the money can actually buy. That tends to get lost in the excitement around the annual announcement.

Your Inflation Might Be Different

Even when the COLA accurately tracks the index it's based on, that index may not reflect your expenses.

The CPI-W measures price changes for households headed by working wage earners and clerical workers, not retirees. Older Americans tend to spend a larger share of their budgets on housing and health care, which don't always move in lockstep with overall prices. The Bureau of Labor Statistics actually publishes an experimental index designed to track spending by Americans 62 and older, known as the CPI-E, which weights those costs more heavily. But it isn't the one Social Security uses.

Where you live matters, too. Costs in a small Midwestern town don't rise the same way they do in Boston or San Francisco. And even two retirees in the same neighborhood can face very different expenses depending on their health, housing, and lifestyle.

So while benefits will rise 3.6% across the board, not every beneficiary's cost of living rose exactly 3.6%. Some will come out ahead. Others will find their bigger checks still don't stretch far enough.

Medicare matters here as well. Part B premiums are generally deducted directly from Social Security payments, so any increase comes out of the raise before it reaches your bank account. The Medicare trustees have projected that the standard Part B premium will rise about $6.60, to $209.50 a month, in 2027, and the official figure is expected later this fall. For the average retiree, that would still leave most of the $75 increase intact, but it's worth checking your own numbers.

What Retirees Should Pay Attention To

None of this means the 2027 COLA isn't worth celebrating. For someone struggling to pay the bills, an extra $75 a month can make a real difference, and automatic inflation adjustments are one of Social Security's most valuable features.

But rather than focusing on the size of the increase, retirees would be better served by asking a different question: Will my new benefit cover more of my expenses than my old one did?

You can start answering that now. Look at what you're spending on essentials like housing, food, utilities, transportation, and health care, and compare it with what you were paying a year ago. Social Security will send updated benefit notices in December, typically by mail and through your online account. When yours arrives, look at how much your actual payment will rise after Medicare premiums and any other deductions.

If your expenses have climbed faster than your benefit, your retirement budget may need some attention. If your benefit is keeping pace, or even gaining a little ground, that's worth recognizing, too.

And if you're still working and saving for retirement, there's a lesson here as well. Don't assume Social Security's annual adjustments will fully protect your future purchasing power. Inflation deserves a place in your retirement plan, even if part of your income will adjust automatically.

The Best Social Security Raise Might Be a Boring One

Every October, the COLA announcement generates headlines about how much more money retirees will receive, and naturally, a bigger number gets more attention.

But in an ideal world, retirees wouldn't need large annual increases just to stay in place. They'd have relatively stable prices, predictable expenses, and income that comfortably covered their needs. A modest COLA in a low-inflation economy can leave retirees better off than a much larger one in an economy where everyday necessities keep getting more expensive.

So yes, the 3.6% increase coming in 2027 is good news for the millions of Americans who depend on Social Security. It's just worth remembering what that increase represents.

A bigger check is nice. Being able to afford more with that check is what really matters.

excerpt: With AI monetization accelerating, earnings estimates rising, and an attractive valuation, Monday.com offers investors a compelling opportunity amid the recent tech selloff.
headline: Bull of the Day: Monday.com (MNDY)
html_content:
Monday.com MNDY) is emerging as an attractive artificial intelligence (AI) software investment as the work management platform expands its AI-powered capabilities, accelerates enterprise adoption, and delivers impressive earnings growth.

Amid the recent tech selloff and growing concerns that AI could disrupt traditional software providers, Monday.com is beginning to challenge that narrative by demonstrating how AI can create new revenue opportunities rather than simply threaten existing business models.

With encouraging earnings estimate revisions and a reasonable valuation, MNDY currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), making it a compelling technology stock to consider as its Q3 results approach next month. 

 

How Monday.com Is Benefiting From AI

  • Accelerating AI revenue: Most recently, annual recurring revenue (ARR) from AI products doubled sequentially during Q2, accounting for 17% of total net new ARR. This is particularly encouraging because it demonstrates that customers are willing to pay for Monday.com's AI capabilities.

 

  • AI-powered automation: Monday.com launched its AI Work Platform in May, introducing autonomous AI agents that help businesses automate workflows, qualify sales leads, manage customer-service requests, and execute projects. These capabilities extend across its work management, CRM, and service offerings.

 

  • Growing enterprise adoption: Customers generating more than $100,000 in ARR increased 37% year over year to 2,019 in Q2. Meanwhile, customers contributing more than $500,000 in ARR increased 68% to 114, highlighting opportunities to expand AI adoption among larger businesses.

 

  • Improving profitability: Q2 revenue rose 22% year over year to $364.62 million, while non-GAAP operating income increased 35% to $61.1 million. Management also believes AI-assisted productivity can help the company expand margins without proportionately increasing headcount.

 

Monday.com's Core AI Products

Monday Vibe

An AI-powered application builder that lets users create custom business applications without traditional coding. It became Monday.com's fastest product to surpass $1 million in ARR.

Monday AI Agents

Autonomous agents designed to perform business tasks, coordinate workflows, and execute actions using organizational data, rather than simply providing AI-generated suggestions.

 

Attractive Growth Outlook & Rising EPS Revisions

Based on Zacks estimates, Monday.com's annual revenue is projected to grow 19% to $1.47 billion in FY26, then another 15% in FY27 to $1.69 billion.

More impressively, annual earnings are expected to climb 27% to $5.58 per share this year, with EPS projected to spike another 19% to $6.63 in FY27.

Supporting this outlook, the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate for FY26 has increased from $5.50 to $5.58 over the last 30 days, while FY27 estimates have edged higher from $6.59 to $6.63.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Monday.com's Stellar Execution

Further supporting Monday.com's attractive growth outlook is that the company has exceeded top-and bottom-line expectations in every quarter since it went public in 2021.

Over the last four quarters, MNDY has posted a very impressive average EPS surprise of 23.56% with an average sales surprise of 2.35%.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

MNDY’s Reasonable Valuation

Despite its attractive growth outlook, at around $86 a share MNDY trades at 15X forward earnings, offering a noticeable discount to the Zacks Internet-Software industry's average of roughly 21X and the benchmark S&P 500's 22X.

MNDY also trades at a very reasonable price-to-forward-sales ratio of less than 3X, compared to the elevated P/S multiples many high-growth AI stocks command.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Bottom Line

Monday.com is emerging as a legitimate AI software beneficiary rather than simply a company incorporating AI into its existing products.

With AI monetization gaining momentum, double-digit revenue and earnings growth projected through FY27, and positive EPS revisions, MNDY is starting to offer investors an appealing combination of growth and value.

headline: Bear of the Day: Evercore (EVR)
html_content:
Shares of investment banking and advisory firm Evercore (EVR) could face further downside as financial stocks come under pressure amid rising Treasury yields and renewed concerns about higher interest rates.

With earnings estimates trending sharply lower as uncertainty rises surrounding the investment banking environment, EVR currently lands a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), suggesting investors may want to remain cautious as the stock is now down 25% year to date.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Evercore's Declining Earnings Estimates

The most concerning development for Evercore is the magnitude of downward earnings estimate revisions, signaling deteriorating analyst sentiment despite expectations for continued profitability.

Over the last week, the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate for FY26 has fallen nearly 7% from $19.80 to $18.42 per share. More troubling, FY27 EPS estimates have declined 6% from $23.74 to $22.27 per share.

Near-term revisions have seen an even steeper decline, with the current quarter's EPS estimate plunging 23% in the last seven days from $3.70 to $2.84 per share.

This negative trend raises concerns about Evercore's ability to meet Wall Street expectations as financial-market conditions become increasingly uncertain.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Evercore Faces Risk of Another Earnings Miss

According to the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction), Evercore could fall short of Q3 earnings expectations when it reports in early November.

The "Most Accurate" and recent estimate among Wall Street analysts currently stands at $2.66 per share, and more than 6% below the underlying Zacks Consensus of $2.84, suggesting an increased likelihood of a negative earnings surprise.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Notably, Evercore missed Q2 earnings expectations by more than 3%, with EPS of $2.91 falling short of estimates of $3.02, despite revenue growth supported by stronger dealmaking activity.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Rising Interest Rates Add Pressure

Evercore's investment banking business is particularly sensitive to capital-market activity, mergers and acquisitions, and corporate financing demand.

With the 10-year Treasury yield climbing above 5.3% following hotter-than-expected inflation data, renewed interest rate fears have weighed on financial stocks and broader market sentiment.

Higher borrowing costs could discourage dealmaking and capital raising, potentially pressuring Evercore's advisory and underwriting revenue. Meanwhile, elevated compensation and operating expenses remain additional profitability concerns.

 

Bottom Line

Although Evercore remains a prominent independent investment bank with long-term growth opportunities, rapidly declining earnings estimates suggest that near-term challenges may be intensifying.

With financial stocks facing heightened volatility and interest rate uncertainty threatening investment banking activity, EVR stock could face additional downside until earnings revisions stabilize and the broader market environment improves.

excerpt: Smart Beta ETF report for FTXH
headline: Is First Trust NASDAQ Pharmaceuticals ETF (FTXH) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
The First Trust NASDAQ Pharmaceuticals ETF (FTXH) was launched on 09/20/2016, and is a smart beta exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Health Care ETFs category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

For a long time now, the ETF industry has been flooded with products based on market capitalization weighted indexes, which are designed to represent the broader market or a particular market segment.

Market cap weighted indexes work great for investors who believe in market efficiency. They provide a low-cost, convenient and transparent way of replicating market returns.

However, some investors believe in the possibility of beating the market through exceptional stock selection, and choose a different type of fund that tracks non-cap weighted strategies: smart beta.

Non-cap weighted indexes try to choose stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance, which is based on specific fundamental characteristics, or a mix of other such characteristics.

This area offers many different investment choices, such as simplest equal-weighting, fundamental weighting and volatility/momentum based weighting methodologies; however, not all of these strategies can deliver superior results.

Fund Sponsor & Index

Because the fund has amassed over $1.07 billion, this makes it one of the larger ETFs in the Health Care ETFs. FTXH is managed by First Trust Advisors. Before fees and expenses, FTXH seeks to match the performance of the Nasdaq US Smart Pharmaceuticals Index.

The Nasdaq US Smart Pharmaceuticals Index is a modified factor weighted index, designed to provide exposure to US companies within the pharmaceuticals industry.

Cost & Other Expenses

When considering an ETF's total return, expense ratios are an important factor. And, cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive cousins in the long term if all other factors remain equal.

With on par with most peer products in the space, this ETF has annual operating expenses of 0.60%.

The fund has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.70%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation in the Healthcare sector - about 100% of the portfolio.

When you look at individual holdings, Abbvie Inc. (ABBV) accounts for about 7.46% of the fund's total assets, followed by Eli Lilly And Company (LLY) and Merck & Co., Inc. (MRK).

Its top 10 holdings account for approximately 53.89% of FTXH's total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

The ETF has added about 25.84% and it's up approximately 43.75% so far this year and in the past one year (as of 10/15/2026), respectively. FTXH has traded between $28.93 and $42.76 during this last 52-week period.

The ETF has a beta of 0.45 and standard deviation of 16.99% for the trailing three-year period. With about 51 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

First Trust NASDAQ Pharmaceuticals ETF is a reasonable option for investors seeking to outperform the Health Care ETFs segment of the market. However, there are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider.

VanEck Pharmaceutical ETF (PPH) tracks MVIS US Listed Pharmaceutical 25 Index and the iShares U.S. Pharmaceuticals ETF (IHE) tracks Dow Jones U.S. Select Pharmaceuticals Index. VanEck Pharmaceutical ETF has $1.06 billion in assets, iShares U.S. Pharmaceuticals ETF has $1.54 billion. PPH has an expense ratio of 0.36% and IHE changes 0.37%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Health Care ETFs

Bottom Line

To learn more about this product and other ETFs, screen for products that match your investment objectives and read articles on latest developments in the ETF investing universe, please visit Zacks ETF Center.

headline: Is Fidelity Diversified International Fund (FDIVX) a Strong Mutual Fund Pick Right Now?
html_content:
If you've been stuck searching for Non US - Equity funds, consider Fidelity Diversified International Fund (FDIVX) as a possibility. FDIVX possesses a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank of 1 (Strong Buy), which is based on various forecasting factors like size, cost, and past performance.

Objective

We classify FDIVX in the Non US - Equity category, which is an area rife with potential choices. Investing in companies outside the United States is how Non US - Equity funds set themselves apart, since global funds tend to keep a good portion of their portfolio stateside. Many of these funds like to allocate across emerging and developed markets, and will often focus on all cap levels.

History of Fund/Manager

excerpt: Gold ETFs GLD, IAU, GLDM and IAUM offer long-term exposure as central bank buying and record ETF inflows support demand despite near-term price headwinds.
headline: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights GLD, IAU, GLDM, IAUM, GDX, SGDM and SGDJ
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 15, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. ETFs recently featured in the blog include: SPDR Gold Shares GLD, iShares Gold Trust IAU, SPDR Gold MiniShares Trust GLDM, iShares Gold Trust Micro IAUM, VanEck Gold Miners ETF GDX, Sprott Gold Miners ETF SGDM and Sprott Junior Gold Miners ETF SGDJ

Here are highlights from Wednesday’s Analyst Blog:

Here's Why Gold ETFs Still Make Sense for Long-Term Investors

Gold's performance in 2026 has been less impressive than its strong showing in 2025, with prices down about 4.24% year to date. Near-term headwinds could continue to weigh on the precious metal through the remainder of the year, but the outlook for 2027 appears more encouraging.

A stronger U.S. dollar and the Fed's hawkish stance to curb inflation have weighed on gold prices, constraining the metal's near-term performance. Higher interest rates remain a key headwind for non-yielding assets such as gold, while a stronger dollar makes the precious metal more expensive for buyers using other currencies,

However, strong inflows into gold ETFs and continued central bank purchases provide structural support for the precious metal, helping sustain long-term demand and potentially bolster price resilience amid market volatility. Despite the recent pullback, gold remains up about 2% over the past three months and approximately 0.7% over the past year.

UBS also sees potential for gold to regain momentum over the longer term. According to Yahoo Finance, the bank expects near-term headwinds from higher U.S. real yields and a stronger greenback to potentially pull gold prices toward $4,000. However, UBS anticipates that sustained longer-term demand may help cushion the decline, providing a potential foundation for a recovery.

UBS Sees a Brighter Long-Term Outlook for Gold

As quoted on the abovementioned Yahoo Finance article, UBS anticipates further gains through 2027 despite the potential for near-term price weakness. The bank estimates gold prices to climb to $4,600 per ounce by December of this year, before advancing in 2027 to $5,000 in March and $5,200 in June. The bank expects the rally to continue, with prices potentially reaching $5,400 per ounce by September 2027.

UBS' projections reflect growing optimism about gold's long-term prospects. The bank expects a gradual weakening of the greenback and continued gold accumulation by central banks, particularly China's, to serve as key drivers of the metal's price appreciation over the coming years.

Strong Demand: A Long-Term Tailwind for Gold

Continued central bank buying is expected to remain a key structural support for gold, reinforcing the precious metal's long-term investment appeal. UBS continues to project annual central bank gold purchases in the range of 750 to 1,000 metric tons.

According to the World Gold Council, as quoted on OilPrice.com, central bank gold purchases reached approximately 289 tons in the second quarter this year, up 62% year over year. This sustained buying trend highlights the growing emphasis among monetary authorities on reserve diversification, including reducing their dependence on conventional reserve currencies.

Investor appetite for physically backed gold ETFs remained strong in September, with global funds attracting $10 billion in fresh inflows, bringing third-quarter inflows to a record $31 billion, as per the World Gold Council. The sustained buying pushed global gold ETF holdings up by 67 metric tons to a record 4,256 metric tons.

China Emerges as a Key Driver of Gold Demand

China's appetite for gold remains strong, with both its central bank and households contributing to demand. Per China's State Administration of Foreign Exchange data, as quoted on a CNBC article, the People's Bank of China purchased about 23 metric tons in September, its largest monthly addition in nearly three years, extending its buying streak to 23 consecutive months.

While Beijing continues to diversify its reserves away from the U.S. dollar, Chinese households are also increasing their gold purchases as a safe-haven investment amid economic uncertainty. Customs data show that China imported more than 1,000 metric tons of gold worth $158.8 billion in the first eight months this year, exceeding the full-year 2025 figures of 886 metric tons and $96.5 billion, respectively.

The Portfolio Diversifier Investors Shouldn't Overlook

The precious metal continues to serve as an important portfolio diversifier and hedge for investors across different investment themes, especially during periods of elevated market volatility and economic uncertainty.

According to the World Gold Council, ongoing inflationary pressures, high energy costs, growing concerns about equity valuations, especially across AI-related stocks and increased volatility in bond markets may have encouraged investors to turn to gold for diversification and portfolio resilience.

Given the prevailing market uncertainty, a defensive and conservative investment approach may help investors navigate short-term volatility. Gold stands out as a compelling portfolio allocation, offering diversification benefits and the potential to help mitigate downside risk.

Building Portfolio Exposure to Gold With ETFs

The prospect of a hawkish Fed and interest rates remaining higher for longer, potentially through the end of 2026 and into early 2027, remains a key headwind for non-yielding assets such as gold. While the Fed's policy stance could weigh on the metal's near-term performance, its long-term investment case remains intact.

While gold prices are likely to remain sensitive to rate hike expectations and incoming economic data in the near term, underlying structural tailwinds continue to reinforce the precious metal's long-term bullish outlook.

Against this backdrop, adopting a long-term, passive investment approach may be a prudent way to build portfolio exposure to gold. Rather than reacting to short-term price fluctuations, investors can consider a disciplined buy-and-hold strategy through gold ETFs, aligning their investments with a longer time horizon.

Recent price weakness could also offer an opportunity for investors seeking to gradually build exposure through gold ETFs using a disciplined buy-the-dip approach. The metal has declined about 4.27% over the past month and 0.2% in the latest trading session. Such pullbacks could present an attractive entry point for investors seeking strategic exposure.

By gradually building positions through gold ETFs during market dips, investors can spread their entry points over time and potentially benefit from periods of price weakness while maintaining a long-term investment perspective.

Gold ETFs to Watch for Long-Term Exposure

Below, we have highlighted a few funds in which investors can increase their allocation to gain greater exposure to gold.

Investors can consider SPDR Gold Shares, iShares Gold Trust, SPDR Gold MiniShares Trust and iShares Gold Trust Micro to increase their exposure to the yellow metal.

With a one-month average trading volume of 8.05 million shares, GLD is the most liquid option. It has gathered an asset base of $141.99 billion, also making it the largest fund among the other options. Regarding annual fees, GLDM and IAUM are the cheapest options, charging 0.10% and 0.09%, respectively, which makes them more suitable for long-term investing.

Gold Miner ETFs Worth a Closer Look

These ETFs focus on gold miners, usually magnifying gold's gains and losses. They provide access to the gold mining industry, not the commodity's price.

Investors can consider VanEck Gold Miners ETF, Sprott Gold Miners ETF and Sprott Junior Gold Miners ETF.

With a one-month average trading volume of 19.45 million shares, GDX is the most liquid option. GDX has also gathered an asset base of $26.81 billion, the largest among the other options. Regarding annual fees, SGDM is the cheapest option, charging 0.46%.
