headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Carter Bankshares Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Carter Bankshares, Inc. CARE need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec 18, 2026 $25 Put had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Carter Bankshares shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? excerpt: Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ) is at a 52-week high, but can investors hope for more gains in the future? We take a look at the company's fundamentals for clues.
headline: Canadian Natural Resources Limited (CNQ) Hit a 52 Week High, Can the Run Continue?
html_content:
A strong stock as of late has been Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ). Shares have been marching higher, with the stock up 3.5% over the past month. The stock hit a new 52-week high of $52.57 in the previous session. Canadian Natural Resources has gained 53.1% since the start of the year compared to the 40.4% move for the Zacks Oils-Energy sector and the 59% return for the Zacks Oil and Gas - Exploration and Production - Canadian industry.

What's Driving the Outperformance?

The stock has a great record of positive earnings surprises, having beaten the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the last four quarters. In its last earnings report on August 6, 2026, Canadian Natural Resources reported EPS of $1.58 versus consensus estimate of $1.43 while it beat the consensus revenue estimate by 15.11%.

For the current fiscal year, Canadian Natural Resources is expected to post earnings of $4.05 per share on $34.26 in revenues. This represents a 59.45% change in EPS on a 23.64% change in revenues. For the next fiscal year, the company is expected to earn $3.61 per share on $30.06 in revenues. This represents a year-over-year change of -10.8% and -12.27%, respectively.

Valuation Metrics

Though Canadian Natural Resources has recently hit a 52-week high, what is next for Canadian Natural Resources? A key aspect of this question is taking a look at valuation metrics in order to determine if the company is due for a pullback from this level.

On this front, we can look at the Zacks Style Scores, as they provide investors with an additional way to sort through stocks (beyond looking at the Zacks Rank of a security). The individual style scores for Value, Growth, Momentum and the combined VGM Score run from A through F. The idea behind the style scores is to help investors pick the most appropriate Zacks Rank stocks based on their individual investment style.

Canadian Natural Resources has a Value Score of B. The stock's Growth and Momentum Scores are A and F, respectively, giving the company a VGM Score of B.

In terms of its value breakdown, the stock currently trades at 12.8X current fiscal year EPS estimates, which is not in-line with the peer industry average of 13.1X. On a trailing cash flow basis, the stock currently trades at 9X versus its peer group's average of 4.9X. This isn't enough to put the company in the top echelon of all stocks we cover from a value perspective.

Zacks Rank

We also need to consider the stock's Zacks Rank, as this supersedes any trend on the style score front. Fortunately, Canadian Natural Resources currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) thanks to a solid earnings estimate revision trend.

Since we recommend that investors select stocks carrying Zacks Rank of 1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) and Style Scores of A or B, it looks as if Canadian Natural Resources fits the bill. Thus, it seems as though Canadian Natural Resources shares could still be poised for more gains ahead.

excerpt: Mobileye Global and Hesai Group stand out as auto suppliers embrace advanced driver assistance and lidar, with rising technology demand creating growth opportunities despite industry headwinds
headline: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Mobileye Global and Hesai Group
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 15, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Mobileye Global MBLY and Hesai Group HSAI.

Industry: Auto Equipment

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3006720/2-auto-equipment-providers-to-buy-as-technology-reshapes-industry

The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment industry is navigating a challenging landscape. Vehicle demand remains below pre-pandemic levels, with affordability limiting any meaningful volume recovery. At the same time, electrification and software-led vehicles are shifting revenues toward technology-heavy components, while higher spending on R&D and retooling puts pressure on margins. Tariffs add further cost uncertainty and favor suppliers with established regional manufacturing. We therefore see returns concentrating in companies with strong engineering capabilities, disciplined cost control and localized footprints, while those with narrow portfolios or limited flexibility face a more difficult environment.

Despite a weak industry backdrop, select industry players such as Mobileye Global and Hesai Group are positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of advanced driver-assistance systems and the shift toward higher-value, technology-led content per vehicle.

About the Industry

The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment Industry comprises companies that design, engineer, and manufacture components and systems for vehicle manufacturers. These products span powertrain, driveline, metal forming, safety, and structural technologies supporting electric, hybrid, and internal combustion vehicles. OEM suppliers focus on improving vehicle safety, performance, efficiency, and cost competitiveness while meeting increasingly stringent regulatory and emissions standards. The industry primarily serves global automotive manufacturers, with demand closely tied to vehicle production volumes and model mix.

Themes Shaping the Industry Dynamics

Weak Buying Power Holding Back Demand: Even with supply chains largely repaired, vehicle sales are yet to return to pre-pandemic levels. Mobility Global, as reported by Tirereview, forecasts U.S. light-vehicle sales of 16.1 million units in 2026, still short of the 17 million SAAR seen before the pandemic. The core issue is cost of ownership. Households are stretched by pricier food, housing, energy, insurance and fuel, while car payments sit well above earlier levels. With budgets squeezed, fewer buyers can commit to a vehicle, which weighs on equipment makers whose revenues track vehicle volumes.

Shift to Electrified, Software-Led Vehicles: As automakers move toward electric, hybrid and software-defined models, the components they buy are changing. Redesigned platforms need lighter structures, EV-specific driveline parts, advanced safety systems and integrated electronics. This is shifting supplier revenue toward newer, technology-heavy products, while parts tied to older vehicle designs lose importance. Full autonomy is still distant, but electrification and driver assistance are already changing the component mix. Suppliers with strong engineering and matching portfolios gain share, while slower adapters risk falling behind.

Rising Costs of Staying Competitive: Keeping pace with new technology is expensive. Suppliers face higher spending on research, skilled labor and factory retooling for new platforms and materials. New features and tougher performance standards typically demand large upfront outlays before any payback. This makes lean operations, disciplined use of capital and optimized supply chains essential. Firms that hold down costs while continuing to invest in innovation can better protect their margins through market ups and downs.

Tariffs Forcing Sourcing and Production Changes: Trade policy is reshaping how and where U.S. auto parts are made. A 25% Section 232 tariff covers certain imported components, including engines, transmissions and electrical parts. This makes costs harder to predict and pushes automakers to have suppliers build nearer to assembly plants. Local production cuts long-term tariff and supply-chain exposure, but requires more capital and adds execution risk. Suppliers already operating regional facilities hold an edge over smaller, more concentrated competitors.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Gloomy Picture

The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment Industry is part of the broader Zacks Autos/ Tires/ Trucks sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #197, which places it in the bottom 20% of roughly 250 Zacks industries.

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates mixed to dull near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

The industry's position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are losing confidence about this group's earnings growth potential. Over the past year, the industry's earnings estimates for the current year have declined 9.6%.

Before we present a few stocks that you may still want to consider for your portfolio, let's take a look at the industry's recent stock market performance and valuation picture.

Industry Lags Sector and S&P 500

The Zacks Automotive - Original Equipment Industry has underperformed the S&P 500 and its sector over the past year. The industry has lost 11.5% over this period compared with the sector's 6% decline. In contrast, the S&P 500 has risen 18.6%.

Industry's Current Valuation

Since automotive companies are debt-laden, it makes sense to value them based on the Enterprise Value/ Earnings before Interest Tax Depreciation and Amortization (EV/EBITDA) ratio.

Based on the trailing 12-month enterprise value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA), the industry is currently trading at 17.68X compared with the S&P 500's 18.22X and the sector's 25.51X.

Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 22.86X and as low as 8.45X, with the median being 18.21X.

2 Stocks Worth Buying

Mobileye: The company builds technology for driver assistance and self-driving cars. Its product range includes EyeQ chips, along with Supervision, Chauffeur and Drive, which keeps it well placed as the auto industry moves toward autonomy. The core EyeQ business is gaining from the growing use of camera-based driver-assistance systems, share gains with customers and rising exports from Chinese automakers.

In the first half of 2026, revenues grew 13%, even though production at its main customers fell 3%. This shows the company is growing faster than its end market. Mobileye has raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $1.97-$2.02 billion and expects slightly more than 39 million EyeQ units to ship. Its product mix is also shifting toward higher-value offerings. A new high-volume Cloud-Enhanced ADAS award from Stellantis begins in 2027, and its profit per unit is expected to match Surround ADAS and be more than double that of base ADAS. Surround ADAS should lift average selling prices from 2028.

Mobileye currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MBLY's 2026 and 2027 EPS implies year-over-year growth of 36% and 7%, respectively.

You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Hesai: The company designs and sells 3D lidar sensors for passenger cars, commercial vehicles and robots. It is strengthening its position by expanding beyond cars into robotics. More than 50 embodied AI companies worldwide work with its JT128 lidar, and GGII ranks it No. 1 in China's humanoid and quadruped robot lidar market. In automotive, Hesai held a 44% share of China's long-range ADAS lidar market in June 2026, and it has led that market for 17 months in a row.

It also won new design deals with Great Wall Motor, Li Auto, GAC Toyota and Volkswagen, which shows growing acceptance from both Chinese and global automakers. Looking ahead, its Picasso 6D SPAD-SoC chip is ready for the start of production. Lidar built on Picasso, called ETX, is being validated by customers and is moving toward information and quotation requests from global automakers and robotaxi operators, which could open new growth avenues.

HSAI currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for HSAI's 2026 and 2027 EPS implies year-over-year growth of 42% and 74%, respectively.

excerpt: Five mining and precious-metals royalty companies, FCX, FNV, LUNMF, OR and WPM are poised to beat third-quarter 2026 earnings estimates as elevated metal prices support growth.
headline: 5 Copper and Precious Metals Stocks Likely to Beat Q3 Estimates
html_content:
The mining industry is heading into the third-quarter 2026 earnings season, supported by elevated year-over-year prices for gold, silver and copper. While gold and silver retreated from the record highs reached earlier this year, they still remained well above year-ago levels throughout the quarter. Industrial metals, including copper and zinc, strengthened during the period. 

The mining stocks fall within the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector, which seems positioned for a solid performance this earnings season. Per the latest Earnings Trends report, the sector is among 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors expected to deliver double-digit year-over-year earnings growth. Sector earnings are projected to increase 29.1% on 6.2% revenue growth, supported by higher realized commodity prices. 

Against this favorable backdrop, we have identified five mining and precious-metals royalty companies, FreeportMcMoRan FCX, Franco-Nevada Corporation FNV, Lundin Mining LUNMF, OR Royalties Inc. OR and Wheaton Precious Metals WPM that appear poised to beat earnings estimates this season and are also likely to deliver improved year-over-year results. 

How Have Things Shaped Up for These Companies?

Price movements across key non-ferrous metals during the July–September 2026 period remained favorable, providing meaningful support to miners’ top lines. 

Gold ranged from a low of $3,963 per ounce to a high of $4,755 per ounce in the third quarter. Gold averaged roughly $4,305 per ounce during the quarter, up 23% year over year. In the third quarter of 2026, silver ranged from a low of $55 an ounce to a high of $72.05 an ounce, averaging $63.22 an ounce. Average prices were 59% higher than last year.

Copper prices had touched an all-time high of $6.93 per pound in September, driven by intense front-loading ahead of anticipated U.S. tariffs and supply disruptions. Copper averaged around $6.53 per pound in the third quarter, supported by demand expectations and supply concerns.  

Zinc prices in the third quarter remained elevated and hovered near multi-year highs, supported by persistent global supply tightness, shrinking Western smelter capacity and declining exchange inventories.

Overall, these favorable commodity price trends are expected to have supported revenues for companies such FreeportMcMoRan, Franco-Nevada Corporation, Lundin Mining, OR Royalties and Wheaton Precious. However, operating conditions remained challenging. Higher input costs, particularly fuel and energy expenses, are likely to have partially offset the benefit of stronger commodity prices during the quarter. Miners continued focusing on improving throughput, optimizing portfolios and mining higher-grade ore to help mitigate cost pressures.

How to Pick Earnings Estimates Beating Stocks?

Identifying stocks that are poised to beat on earnings in their upcoming releases might seem a daunting task. However, our proprietary Zacks methodology makes it fairly simple. 

One can pick stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Our research shows that stocks with this combination have up to a 70% chance of an earnings surprise.

Earnings ESP is our proprietary methodology for determining stocks that have the best chances to surprise with their next earnings announcement. It is the percentage difference between the Most Accurate Estimate and the Zacks Consensus Estimate. You can uncover the best stocks before they are reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

5 Potential Outperformers This Season

FreeportMcMoRan has an Earnings ESP of +2.60% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. It is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 27. 

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FCX’s third-quarter earnings has moved up 4% over the past 30 days and is pegged at 75 cents per share. It indicates a 50% increase from the year-ago quarter. The company has an average earnings surprise of 32.6% in the trailing four quarters.

Freeport-McMoRan Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Freeport-McMoRan Inc. price-eps-surprise | Freeport-McMoRan Inc. Quote

The company’s recent operational update for the third quarter of 2026 states copper production of approximately 830 million pounds and gold production of 230,000 ounces. Copper output was below the year-ago level of 912 million pounds and gold production also declined from 287,000 ounces. Consolidated copper sales for third-quarter 2026 are expected to have been around 750 million pounds, 23% lower than the year-ago quarter’s 977 million pounds.

The company states consolidated gold sales for third-quarter 2026 are 100 thousand ounces, which came below expectations, reflecting the impact of deferred gold sales. FCX had sold 336 thousand ounces of gold in the third quarter of 2025.

FCX estimates its third-quarter 2026 consolidated average realized price to exceed $6.50 per pound of copper compared with $4.68 in the year-ago quarter. Consolidated unit net cash costs are expected to have been around $2.10 per pound of copper. 
Higher prices of copper and gold are expected to have negated the impact of lower sales volumes on its results.

Franco-Nevada has an Earnings ESP of +4.44% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 11.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FNV’s third-quarter earnings is pegged at $1.95 per share, implying 36.4% growth from the year-ago quarter’s actual. The estimate has moved up 3% over the past 30 days. FNV has an average earnings surprise of 5.3% in the trailing four quarters.

Franco-Nevada Corporation Price and EPS Surprise

Franco-Nevada Corporation price-eps-surprise | Franco-Nevada Corporation Quote

FNV expects total gold equivalent ounces (GEO) sales of 510,000-570,000 for 2026 and is tracking toward the upper half of this range. The company sold 519,106 GEOs in 2025 (including 11,208 GEOs from Cobre Panamá). Production is expected to be weighted toward the second half, reflecting anticipated production profiles at Candelaria, Tocantinzinho, Côté Gold, Greenstone and Valentine. The outlook also includes anticipated deliveries from processing stockpiled ore at Cobre Panamá. Franco-Nevada expects stream deliveries from Cobre Panamá to total 23,100 gold ounces and 265,000 silver ounces in 2026, with deliveries expected to begin in the third quarter. 

We expect GEOs sold in the third quarter of 2026 to have been higher than the year-ago 125,115 GEOs sold. Higher GEOs and prices are expected to contribute to FNV’s third-quarter results. 

Lundin Mining has an Earnings ESP of +3.25% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. It is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 4.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lundin Mining’s third-quarter earnings is pegged at 29 cents per share, indicating a 61% increase from the year-ago quarter. The estimate has remained unchanged over the past 30 days. LUNMF has an average earnings surprise of 13.8% in the trailing four quarters.

Lundin Mining Corp. Price and EPS Surprise

Lundin Mining Corp. price-eps-surprise | Lundin Mining Corp. Quote

Lundin Mining produced 76,877 tons of copper in the second quarter of 2026, which was down 1% year over year. The company also produced 33,427 ounces of gold in the second quarter of 2026, a 12% decline. Strong contributions from Caserones and improved recoveries at Chapada were offset by lower output at Candelaria due to planned mine sequencing adjustments.

During the quarter, mining activities were primarily focused on Phase 6, with some contribution from Phase 7. Copper concentrate production continued to benefit from high grades in Phase 6 and strong throughput from Full Potential program initiatives, which focus on sustainable operational efficiencies and financial savings. Additional irrigated area in the dump leach continues to benefit copper cathode production. This is expected to have led to higher production figures for the third quarter of 2026. However, lower output at Candelaria due to weather disruptions is expected to have negated some of the impact.

OR Royalties has an Earnings ESP of +9.43% and a Zacks Rank of 2 at present. It is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 11.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for OR Royalties’ third-quarter 2026 earnings is 27 cents per share, indicating a 22.7% year-over-year increase. The estimate has moved up 4% over the past 30 days. OR has an average earnings surprise of 9.98% in the trailing four quarters.

OR Royalties Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

OR Royalties Inc. price-eps-surprise | OR Royalties Inc. Quote

The company reported preliminary third-quarter GEO Deliveries. OR Royalties earned 20,237 attributable GEOs in the third quarter of 2026 compared with 20,326 in the third quarter of 2025. OR Royalties reported preliminary revenues from royalties and streams of $90.2 million during the third quarter, higher than $71.6 million in the year-ago quarter, mainly driven by higher prices. 

Preliminary cost of sales (excluding depletion) was $2.9 million, resulting in a quarterly cash margin of approximately $87.3 million or 96.8%. In the year-ago quarter, cost of sales excluding depletion was $2.37 million and cash margin was $69.3 million or 96.7%.

Wheaton Precious Metals has an Earnings ESP of +1.66% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. It is expected to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 5.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for WPM’s third-quarter 2026 earnings is $1.13 per share, indicating an 82.3% year-over-year increase. The estimate has moved up 1% over the past 30 days. WPM has an average earnings surprise of 12.8% in the trailing four quarters.

Wheaton Precious Metals Corp. Price and EPS Surprise

Wheaton Precious Metals Corp. price-eps-surprise | Wheaton Precious Metals Corp. Quote

Wheaton Precious Metals is likely to have delivered a strong performance in the third quarter of 2026, building on the robust momentum seen in the second quarter of the year.  The company projects an attributable production of 860,000-940,000 GEOs for 2026. The midpoint of the range indicates a 30% year-over-year increase. The company expects production to be weighted to the second half, helped by mine sequencing at Salobo and Peñasquito, the full Antamina contribution and continued ramp-up of newer assets.

Our model projects WPM’s total attributable production of 226,771 GEOs for the third quarter of 2026, indicating an 11.5% year-over-year increase. The total figure includes attributable gold production of 98,177 ounces, which projects a 1.8% year-over-year decline. Our model projects gold sales for the third quarter at 78,423 ounces, indicating a 0.7% dip. Our model projects 7.4 million ounces of total attributable silver production (up 24.1% year over year). Silver sales volume is expected to be 6.27 million ounces, suggesting a 31.6% year-over-year increase. 

Gold sales for the quarter are expected at $333 million, 21.3% higher year over year, as higher prices are expected to have offset the modest decline in volumes. Silver sales are projected to surge 141% year over year to $454 million, on higher volumes and prices. 

Zacks' Research Chief Names "Stock Most Likely to Double"

Our team of experts has just released the 5 stocks with the greatest probability of gaining +100% or more in the coming months. Of those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian highlights the one stock set to climb highest.

This innovative software-as-a-service firm upped its user base +22% year over year. That rate is increasing and margins are expanding as AI efficiencies take effect. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners, but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like D-Wave Quantum, which shot up +680.1%.

excerpt: MS' Q3 earnings beat estimates as record Wealth Management revenues, AI financing opportunities and disciplined capital allocation shape its growth strategy.
headline: Morgan Stanley Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Wealth and AI Strategy
html_content:
Morgan Stanley MS emphasized Wealth Management expansion, artificial intelligence-related financing opportunities and disciplined capital allocation during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management highlighted the firm's integrated business model while acknowledging risks from elevated interest rates and geopolitical uncertainty.

Chairman and CEO Ted Pick stressed that sustained client asset growth and broader institutional capabilities remain central to the firm's long-term strategy, even as market activity becomes less predictable.

MS Beat Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Morgan Stanley reported third-quarter earnings of $3.03 per share, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.83. Earnings increased from $2.80 per share in the year-ago quarter. Revenues reached $20.34 billion, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $19.74 billion. Revenues increased approximately 12% year over year.

Morgan Stanley Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Morgan Stanley price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Morgan Stanley Quote

The firm delivered a 22.6% return on tangible common equity, marking its fifth consecutive quarter above 20%. Pick attributed the performance to the strength of its integrated franchise.

Morgan Stanley Sees Durable Wealth Growth

Chief financial officer Sharon Yeshaya highlighted record Wealth Management revenues of $9.1 billion and net new assets of $232 billion.

IPO-related inflows contributed just over half of net new assets, while fee-based flows reached $80 billion. Yeshaya explained that IPO-related relationships can generate additional advisory opportunities beyond the initial transaction.

During questioning from BMO Capital Markets, Yeshaya emphasized that employee stock plans, retirement mandates and asset consolidation support the firm's client acquisition strategy. She also noted that asset retention remained steady.

MS Expands Focus on AI Financing Opportunities

Pick described artificial intelligence infrastructure investment as a major opportunity across advisory, financing and capital markets businesses.

Responding to Wells Fargo Securities, Pick indicated that annual hyperscaler capital expenditures were running around $1 trillion. He acknowledged uncertainty surrounding future spending levels but emphasized Morgan Stanley's expanding involvement across the AI ecosystem.

Management is increasing its strategic commitment to AI-related opportunities, including public and private financing solutions. Pick also stressed the importance of underwriting discipline as higher borrowing costs influence transaction structures.

Morgan Stanley Targets Further Margin Expansion

Yeshaya indicated that Wealth Management margins should expand over time as the business gains scale and converts additional clients into advisory relationships.

Responding to Bank of America, she emphasized that management would prioritize multiyear investment rather than manage margins toward quarterly targets.

The business generated a 30.4% pretax margin during the quarter. Continued spending on technology, marketing and banking capabilities supports management's strategy of expanding client relationships and improving operating leverage.

MS Expects Net Interest Income Growth

Yeshaya expects Wealth Management net interest income to increase modestly in the fourth quarter, depending on interest rates and client behavior.

During questioning from Jefferies, she also indicated that net interest income should expand in 2027, primarily supported by loan growth.

The firm is strategically expanding its deposit base to strengthen funding capabilities. Yeshaya explained that benefits from transferring eligible assets into the bank should become more visible during 2027 rather than immediately.

Morgan Stanley Balances Trading Strength With Risks

Institutional Securities generated $10 billion in revenues, supported by strong equities performance and increased advisory activity.

Pick explained that investments in derivatives, prime brokerage and global execution capabilities have strengthened the equities franchise. However, he acknowledged that trading volumes remain sensitive to market sentiment.

During questions from UBS, Pick cautioned that higher interest rates could constrain capital raising when financing economics become unfavorable. Management emphasized selective risk allocation rather than pursuing transaction volume indiscriminately.

MS Maintains a Disciplined Strategic Outlook

excerpt: Rising inflation, Fed uncertainty and AI-related risks are rattling markets. Explore these defensive ETFs to help navigate volatility while staying invested for the long term.
headline: Here's Why Investors Should Consider These Defensive ETFs Now
html_content:
Markets have had relatively few reasons for optimism in 2026, as rising economic and geopolitical uncertainties continue to test investor confidence. With volatility persisting, it looks like investors won’t get relief in the near term. The year has proved challenging for investors, and the road ahead may remain bumpy, with markets likely to face further turbulence in the months to come.

The CBOE Volatility Index, which reflects market expectations of near-term volatility, rose about 4.2% over the past trading session, taking the index up around 14.6% over the past five trading sessions and around 18.4% year to date.

The S&P 500 fell 1.11% on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected inflation heightened concerns about further Fed rate hikes, while growing apprehension over debt financing for AI investments added to the pressure on equities.

Driven by surging fuel prices, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose a seasonally adjusted 0.6% in September, bringing annual inflation to 3.7%. This heightened expectations of further interest rate hikes by the U.S. Federal Reserve, while concerns that higher borrowing costs could weigh on AI-related funding added to market jitters, sending the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite down about 1.88% on Wednesday.

This uncertain economic landscape may prompt investors to adopt a more cautious and bearish outlook on U.S. equities, particularly in the near term. This view is reinforced by BlackRock's recent shift in its stance on U.S. equities. Signaling a more bearish stance, the world's largest asset manager downgraded its view on U.S. equities to neutral, pointing to uncertainty and volatility risks tied to AI, as quoted on Reuters. The BlackRock Investment Institute ended its long-standing overweight position in U.S. equities, moving to a neutral stance "to manage potential volatility around the AI buildout."

Thus, in the current economic environment, investors should prioritize long-term wealth creation while positioning their portfolios to better withstand market volatility.

How to Navigate Volatility and Focus on Long-Term Growth

Amid broader economic headwinds and heightened market uncertainty, investors may benefit from reassessing their portfolio allocations and adopting a more cautious, risk-aware approach. Prioritizing stability while maintaining a long-term investment horizon can help investors navigate near-term market turbulence without losing sight of sustainable wealth creation.

Tilting toward defensive funds, combined with passive and long-term investing strategies, such as buy-and-hold investing and dollar-cost averaging, can help investors gradually build disciplined exposure to defensive funds while adding stability to their portfolios.

Increasing exposure to defensive funds can help diversify portfolio risks and potentially improve resilience during market downturns, while a long-term investment approach can keep investors focused on wealth creation over time. Investors should avoid reacting to short-term price movements and making tactical bets.

For investors with substantial allocations to higher-risk assets, gradually shifting toward a more balanced portfolio may also be worth considering.

When Market Risks Rise, Diversification Comes First

Increasing exposure to defensive funds and adopting a more conservative investment approach does not mean abandoning growth-oriented investments or sectors with strong long-term potential. Rather, it underscores the importance of diversification in balancing growth opportunities with portfolio resilience.

Diversification has long been a cornerstone of sound portfolio management, but its importance becomes even more pronounced amid the narrow breadth of the current rally. The AI-driven surge has contributed to an increasingly top-heavy market, making portfolio diversification all the more important.

The S&P 500, for instance, is heavily tilted toward the information technology sector, with tech accounting for roughly 40% of the index, making concentration risks increasingly difficult to ignore. Investors may be taking on greater concentration and systemic risks than they initially realize. When investor expectations shift, crowded trades can unwind rapidly, amplifying market losses.

In the long run, a more diversified approach can help create a healthier balance between risks and rewards, especially in markets where diversification is increasingly less optional and more a form of self-preservation.

These Defensive ETFs Could Help Cushion Market Uncertainties

Defensive funds can offer a dual advantage, helping cushion portfolios during periods of market stress while maintaining exposure to potential. Below we mention a few funds which investors can consider.

Quality ETFs

With market uncertainty persisting, investors may want to prioritize quality investing as part of a defensive portfolio strategy. Companies with robust fundamentals, consistent earnings and durable competitive advantages may offer greater resilience during periods of volatility, making quality ETFs a potential option for investors seeking to manage risk.

Investors can look at funds like iShares MSCI USA Quality Factor ETF QUAL, Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF SPHQ and JPMorgan U.S. Quality Factor ETF JQUA.

Utility ETFs

Utilities are traditionally considered a defensive sector, as relatively stable demand for these companies' services can help shield these companies from economic downturns. Their comparatively low-beta profile makes utility stocks an attractive option for investors seeking to navigate market volatility and economic uncertainty.

Investors should gain from funds like Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund XLU, Vanguard Utilities ETF VPU and iShares U.S. Utilities ETF IDU.

Consumer Staple ETFs

Increasing exposure to consumer staple funds can bring balance and stability to investors’ portfolios. Consumer staples include everyday necessities that typically see steady demand across economic cycles, making the sector less sensitive to economic fluctuations.

Consumer staples stocks are often favored for their defensive characteristics, steady growth potential and relatively low volatility, particularly during economic downturns. At the same time, the sector can participate in broader market recoveries, offering a combination of stability and growth that makes it a valuable component of a diversified portfolio.

Investors can consider State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF XLP, Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF VDC and Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Staples ETF RSPS.

excerpt: Verisk's recurring subscription revenues, AI-driven innovations and insurance analytics growth support its prospects despite rising costs and market headwinds.
headline: Here's Why You Should Hold VRSK Stock in Your Portfolio Now
html_content:
Verisk VRSK stock has declined 20.3% over the past year compared with the industry's 7% dip. The Zacks S&P 500 Composite has rallied 20.2% over the same period.

1-Year Share Price Performance

                                                                  Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for VRSK’s 2026 revenues is $3.2 billion, suggesting 5% year-over-year growth. For 2027, the metric is expected to gain 6.5% to $3.4 billion.

The consensus mark for 2026 earnings per share is pinned at $7.71, suggesting a 7.7% year-over-year jump. The bottom line is expected to increase 13.1% to $8.72 in 2027.

Factors That Augur Well for VRSK’s Success

Recurring Subscription Aids Growth Stability: VRSK’s subscription-backed business model improves revenue visibility and supports persistent growth. The company ended the second quarter of 2026 with subscription revenues rising 8% year over year on an organic constant currency (OCC) basis, subsequent to 9.3% growth in the year-ago quarter.

Verisk’s subscription revenues constituted 83% of the top line, lowering exposure to transactional volatility. The company’s growth across underwriting, catastrophe risk solutions and antifraud analytics is fueled by strong renewals, strong price realization and customer relationship enhancement. Recurring revenue growth trajectory should be sustained on the back of persistent product enhancement and client wins.

AI-Driven Growth Opportunities: Verisk’s AI investments strengthen its competitive position, creating monetization opportunities. XactAI, VRSK’s AI-driven claims automation solution, registered approximately 10X user growth, reaching nearly 7,000 licensees. Premium Audit AI gained momentum, supporting stronger subscription renewals through improved functionality.

VRSK’s Anthropic collaboration introduced AI-fuelled connectors for underwriting and claims, with a top-10 insurer adopting the technology. Customer engagement should improve as AI integration expands across insurance workflows, strengthening pricing power and creating opportunities for more subscriptions and licensing revenues.

Insurance Analytics’ Contribution to Organic Growth: Verisk ended the second quarter of 2026 with underwriting and claims revenues rising 5.6% and 6.1% year over year, respectively, on an OCC basis. The company onboarded eight Core Lines contributors and 10 excess and surplus data contributors during the first half of 2026. An expanding proprietary dataset and improved analytical skill set improve product differentiation, supporting customer wins and creating opportunities from cross-selling and top-line growth in the long run.

Risks Faced by Verisk

Sluggish Insurance Market: In the second quarter of 2026, Verisk’s transactional revenues declined 4.2% on an OCC basis, indicating lower property-related activity, fewer weather events and international travel disruptions. Transactional revenues contributed 17% of the top line during the aforementioned quarter. Management anticipates a soft commercial property market and weather-related transactional weakness to persist through the second half of 2026, disrupting revenue growth.

Rising Operating Costs & Interest Expenses: The company’s selling, general and administrative expenses gained 20.8% year over year during the second quarter of 2026, driven by acquisition, disposition and AccuLynx-related costs, alongside higher consulting and employee-related expenses. Net interest expenses climbed to $53 million from the year-ago quarter’s $36 million, while the effective tax rate increased to 24.6% from 22.7%. It subsequently hurt net income, which declined 10% year over year.

Uncertain AI Monetization: Verisk shoulders execution and monetization risks as insurers rapidly adopt AI and develop proprietary analytical capabilities. Despite rising demand for AI-driven solutions, management identifies incremental AI revenue contribution as tough to quantify. Customer adoption cycles drag out and changing monetization models could curb revenue visibility.

VRSK’s Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

The company currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Business Services sector include Figure Technology Solutions FIGR and Ralliant Corporation RAL. These two companies presently flaunt a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Figure Technology Solutions has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 56.6%. FIGR delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 28.2%, on average.

Ralliant has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 9.4%. RAL delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 7.1%, on average.

Zacks' Research Chief Names "Stock Most Likely to Double"

Our team of experts has just released the 5 stocks with the greatest probability of gaining +100% or more in the coming months. Of those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian highlights the one stock set to climb highest.

This innovative software-as-a-service firm upped its user base +22% year over year. That rate is increasing and margins are expanding as AI efficiencies take effect. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners, but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like D-Wave Quantum, which shot up +680.1%.

headline: Best 3 Non-AI Stocks to Buy Now on the Dip Amid the AI Stock Selloff
html_content:
AI stocks sold off Wednesday and in early morning trading Thursday as investors raced to protect profits.

That said, there are a ton of long-term deals out there on Wall Street right now on stocks that are posting impressive earnings and revenue growth outside of the artificial intelligence spending boom.

First up is Cummins, which manufactures engines and powertrains for trucks, buses, off-highway construction equipment, and more.

Next, we dive into Argenx and its impressive upside as it attempts to expand its flagship autoimmune disease drug Vyvgart.

The final non-AI stock we explore is PACCAR. The major U.S. automotive manufacturer builds commercial trucks across multiple brands and will thrive as trucking remains a backbone of the economy.

Best Stocks to Buy Now and Hold for Long-Term Upside: CMI

Cummins CMI is a historic engine and powertrain manufacturer that operates across trucking, busing, off-highway construction equipment, generators and beyond. CMI’s lineup of engine technologies includes diesel, natural gas, and alternative fuel engines.

It’s worth highlighting that the diesel engine-making powerhouse is benefiting from the AI data center boom via its growing standby power segment and its battery energy storage systems (BESS). But it remains, at its core, an engine maker. 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Cummins posted roughly flat revenue growth over the past two years after averaging 20% revenue growth between 2021 and 2023—it posted a similarly impressive stretch of earnings expansion.

Now it is back in growth mode, with it projected to grow its revenue by 12% in 2026 and another 9% next year to reach $41.13 billion, up from $33.67 billion last year.

Cummins is expected to expand its adjusted earnings by 25% this year and 18% next year. Its recent upward EPS revisions for FY27 land it a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Plus, the chart above highlights its impressive earnings outlook for 2028.  


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The engine maker tripled the S&P 500 over the past 20 years, soaring ~1,500%—including a ~120% climb in the past five years. Yet CMI is down ~29% from its summer highs, which means Cummins offers investors roughly 40% upside if it ever returns to its peaks.

Its drop, coupled with its strong earnings outlook, has Cummins trading nearly in line with its 15-year median at 15.5X forward 12-month earnings.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Cummins is looking to find technical support near its long-term 21-month moving average and its pre-breakout highs. The dividend-paying company with a strong balance sheet is also trading at some of its lower RSI levels in recent years, after reaching its most overbought level earlier this year.

Buy Biotech Stock ARGX Now on the Dip 

Netherlands-based biopharmaceutical stock Argenx ARGX has soared ~3,800% since its 2017 U.S. IPO. Its earnings and revenue growth outlook is impressive as its flagship autoimmune disease drug Vyvgart shines. Argenx’s autoimmune drug Vyvgart reached blockbuster status—a prescription medication that generates at least $1 billion in annual global sales—in its second full year on the market.

ARGX is critically looking to expand its blockbuster drug across multiple autoimmune diseases. It is actively pursuing new indications for Vyvgart and adding to its pipeline via its $2.2 billion acquisition of Forte Biosciences, which closed in late August.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

All of this is part of the company’s Vision 2030 initiative focused on treating 50,000 patients globally by 2030 and securing “10 labeled indications” for Vyvgart, up from three right now. ARGX also aims to “progress five pipeline candidates into registrational development by 2030.”

Argenx is projected to grow its revenue by 49% in 2026 and another 23% next year, climbing from $4.25 billion in 2025 to $7.75 billion in 2027—following 89% growth in 2025 and 78% revenue expansion in 2024. The biotech firm is expected to grow its adjusted earnings by 47% YoY in 2026 and 31% next year to hit $37.58 a share, up from $19.57 in 2025.

ARGX has beaten our bottom line estimates by an average of 17% in the past four quarters. Wall Street is bullish on ARGX, with 26 of the 31 brokerage recommendations Zacks has at “Strong Buys” alongside zero sells. Argenx also sports a pristine debt-free balance sheet that will help it pursue more strategic acquisitions.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Argenx has dropped ~20% from its late-August peaks, with its average Zacks price target implying 43% upside. It recently found support at a key technical range and is attempting to overtake its 200-day moving average.

Valuation-wise, Argenx is trading at a 45% discount to its industry and 52% below its 12-month highs at 22.9X forward 12-month earnings.

PACCAR: A Great Buy-and-Hold Stock that Doesn’t Need AI Help 

PACCAR PCAR is a major U.S. automotive manufacturer building premium commercial trucks under Kenworth, Peterbilt, DAF, and other brands. The firm also sells parts, engines, and offers financing for its various trucks. PCAR is expanding its core diesel truck segment while boosting its battery electric offerings and alternative fuels.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Trucking remains a backbone of the economy, no matter how AI reshapes it. Trucks help deliver roughly 70% of all domestic freight tonnage, and they will continue to dominate commercial transportation even in a possible driverless vehicle future. This backdrop is why PACCAR has reported 87 straight years of profitability and paid a dividend every year since 1941.

PACCAR experienced a cyclical downturn in 2025 and 2024 after averaging 23% revenue expansion and 57% adjusted earnings growth between 2021 and 2023. It is back in growth mode as its customers benefit from “higher freight rates due to constrained industry freight capacity.”


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

PACCAR also said last quarter that “fleet age has increased… providing an opportunity for customers to refresh their fleets with newer, more fuel-efficient trucks.” It notd that the “U.S. EPA provided helpful clarification of emissions regulations” in July that will be “beneficial to customers as they make truck purchasing decisions for the second half of this year and 2027.”

The truck maker is projected to grow its adjusted earnings by 18% in FY26 and 22% in FY27 on 9% and 12% sales growth, respectively. PACCAR’s earnings estimates have continued to improve for 2027 and 2028, ending its downturn and showing its cyclical industry-wide decline is in the rearview.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

PACCAR shares have soared 285% in the last 15 years vs. its sector’s 178%, including a 95% run in the last five years to outpace the S&P 500 and crush its industry’s -14% downturn. This is part of a ~1,500% climb over the last 25 years vs. the benchmark’s 667%—its total return hit ~3,500% when factoring in dividend reinvestments.

The stock is down ~20% from its July records after finding buyers right at its June lows. On the valuation side, it is trading nearly in line with its 15-year median and 30% below its highs at 15.6X forward earnings.

Zacks' Research Chief Names "Stock Most Likely to Double"

Our team of experts has just released the 5 stocks with the greatest probability of gaining +100% or more in the coming months. Of those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian highlights the one stock set to climb highest.

This innovative software-as-a-service firm upped its user base +22% year over year. That rate is increasing and margins are expanding as AI efficiencies take effect. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners, but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like D-Wave Quantum, which shot up +680.1%.

excerpt: A new poll found that more than a quarter of older adults skipped reviewing their Medicare policy options last year. Meredith Margrave explains why being happy with your plan is exactly why you should review it, and the five things to look at before open enrollment ends on December 7.
headline: The Most Expensive Medicare Mistake Might Be Doing Nothing
html_content:
My parents have been telling me for years that I should start an investing newsletter called Now, Don't Touch It.

That's it. That's the whole investing philosophy. You find something good, you put your money into it, and then (this is the really important part) you leave it alone.

It's a running joke in my family, mostly because I've spent years surrounded by friends and colleagues who love to tinker with their investments. They're constantly buying something, selling something, adjusting something, or chasing the next big opportunity.

When it comes to building wealth, constantly messing with a perfectly good plan can do more harm than good. I'd rather make a good decision once and let it do its thing.

But there's a catch. As much as I believe in the financial wisdom of Now, Don't Touch It, there are a few situations where that philosophy can cost you a whole lot of money. One of them starts today.

October 15 marks the beginning of Medicare's annual open enrollment period. Between now and December 7, Medicare beneficiaries can review their coverage and make changes for 2027.

If your immediate reaction is, Well, I like my plan, so why bother?, I have some news you might not like: Your Medicare plan doesn't have to disappear to become a bad deal.

The Problem With Being Perfectly Happy

A new University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging, released today, caught my attention. Among adults 65 and older enrolled in Medicare, 27% said they didn't take any time at all to review their options during the last open enrollment period. Another 33% spent less than an hour. And 80% simply stuck with the coverage they already had.

When researchers asked why, the most common explanation was simple: They were happy with the coverage they already had.

I understand that completely. Health insurance isn't exactly a hobby. Nobody wakes up on a beautiful Saturday morning thinking, You know what would make today perfect? Comparing prescription drug formularies. If your doctors are covered, your medications are affordable, and you haven't had any major problems, why would you spend your afternoon digging through insurance paperwork?

Because the plan you signed up for last year isn't necessarily the plan you're getting next year. Even if your coverage stays largely the same, your needs might not. Maybe you've started a new medication. Maybe your doctor has left the network. Maybe a procedure you've been putting off is finally on the calendar. Or maybe another plan has quietly become a better deal.

You can be completely satisfied with your current coverage and still be paying more than you need to. Those two things aren't mutually exclusive.

This Year, the Stakes Are Even Higher

Medicare plans change every year, but the landscape for 2027 is shifting in some particularly noticeable ways. Several major insurers are pulling back from parts of the Medicare Advantage market, eliminating plans or shrinking their offerings. According to KFF, the average Medicare beneficiary will be able to choose from 28 Medicare Advantage plans with prescription drug coverage in 2027, down from 32 in 2026. And CNN reports that nearly 3.2 million Medicare Advantage enrollees will need to find new coverage for 2027 because their insurers are no longer offering their plans.

Twenty-eight choices still sounds like a lot, and in many places it is. But the number that matters isn't how many plans exist somewhere in America. It's whether the plan you're counting on will still be available where you live, and whether its benefits and costs will still work for you.

Even a plan that survives another year can change its premiums, deductibles, copays, drug coverage, provider network, or rules for getting certain services approved.

Consider a hypothetical retiree who pays $45 a month for a prescription under her current drug coverage. That's $540 a year: not nothing, but manageable. Now imagine her plan changes how it covers that medication, and she pays $125 a month next year instead. That's $1,500 a year, or an extra $960 for the exact same medication.

She hasn't changed doctors. She hasn't developed a new condition. She hasn't done anything differently. But a plan change has quietly opened a nearly $1,000 hole in her retirement budget.

Actual costs will depend on the plan and the medication. Medicare also caps annual out-of-pocket spending on covered Part D drugs, at $2,400 in 2027, which limits how bad things can get for people with very expensive prescriptions. But as this example shows, you can stay well under that cap and still pay hundreds of dollars more than you need to.

When we talk about protecting retirement savings, we spend a lot of time on investments, inflation, and withdrawal rates. We should probably spend more time on the health insurance decisions that can eat into those savings, too.

The 5 Things I'd Check Before December 7

I'm not suggesting you switch Medicare plans every year. Quite the opposite. Sometimes, after comparing your options, you'll find your existing coverage is still a terrific fit. Wonderful! Don't touch it.

Just make that an informed decision rather than a default. There's a difference between leaving a good thing alone and assuming something is still good because you haven't looked at it lately. Here's where I'd start.

1. Find the letter you probably wanted to throw away.

If you're enrolled in a Medicare Advantage or Part D drug plan, your insurer should have sent you an Annual Notice of Change by the end of September. It explains what's changing for next year, including coverage and costs. This is not the piece of mail to set aside for later. Pay particular attention to premiums, deductibles, copays, covered medications, and changes to benefits.

2. Make sure your doctors are still in the picture.

If you have a Medicare Advantage plan, check whether your preferred doctors, specialists, and hospitals will be in-network in 2027. Don't rely only on the insurer's directory; confirm the relationships that matter most directly with your providers. A plan with a terrific premium isn't much of a bargain if it makes it harder or more expensive to see the doctors you trust.

3. Run your prescriptions through the numbers.

This is one of the easiest places to miss a potentially expensive change. Check that your medications are still covered, what they'll cost, and whether your preferred pharmacy is still a good option. Even if your prescriptions haven't changed, the financial details of your coverage might have.

4. Compare the whole cost, not just the premium.

A $0-premium Medicare Advantage plan sounds wonderful, but that doesn't mean your health care costs will be zero. You generally still pay your Medicare Part B premium, and you may face deductibles, copays, and coinsurance. Look at the total picture: premiums, expected out-of-pocket expenses, the plan's out-of-pocket maximum, prescription costs, and the care you're likely to need. A lower monthly premium doesn't automatically mean a cheaper year.

5. See what else is available before you decide to stay put.

You don't have to call a dozen insurance companies or spend days building spreadsheets. Start with the official Medicare Plan Finder at Medicare.gov, which lets you compare the health and drug plans available where you live. If the process gets overwhelming, you can get free, unbiased help from your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP).

One important caution: Switching from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare isn't always as simple as it looks if you also want a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) policy. Depending on your circumstances and your state, you may not qualify for guaranteed acceptance, and insurers could review your health history before agreeing to cover you, or charge you more. Check those rules before you make a change.

Doing Nothing Is Still a Decision

Here's what I really want you to take away from all of this. You don't have to be unhappy with your Medicare plan to justify reviewing it. You don't need to have had a coverage problem, received a shocking medical bill, or learned that your insurer is pulling out of your area. You just need to recognize that the plan you chose for 2026 is being asked to do a different job in 2027.

Medicare open enrollment runs from October 15 through December 7, and changes generally take effect January 1. That's your window to make sure the coverage you're carrying into the new year still makes sense.

My parents might have been onto something with that Now, Don't Touch It newsletter. I still think it's great advice for most long-term investing decisions: Find a strategy that works, stick with it, and resist the urge to change things just because you can.

But Medicare deserves a slightly different rule: Now, Check It. Then, Maybe Don't Touch It.

Sometimes the smartest financial move you can make is simply confirming that yesterday's smart decision is still a smart decision today.

Even a plan that survives another year can change its premiums, deductibles, copays, drug coverage, provider network, or rules for getting certain services approved. Consider a hypothetical retiree who pays $45 a month for a prescription under her current drug coverage. That's $540 a year: not nothing, but manageable. Now imagine her plan changes how it covers that medication, and she pays $125 a month next year instead. That's $1,500 a year, or an extra $960 for the exact same medication. She hasn't changed doctors. She hasn't developed a new condition. She hasn't done anything differently. But a plan change has quietly opened a nearly $1,000 hole in her retirement budget. Actual costs will depend on the plan and the medication. Medicare also caps annual out-of-pocket spending on covered Part D drugs, at $2,400 in 2027, which limits how bad things can get for people with very expensive prescriptions. But as this example shows, you can stay well under that cap and still pay hundreds of dollars more than you need to. When we talk about protecting retirement savings, we spend a lot of time on investments, inflation, and withdrawal rates. We should probably spend more time on the health insurance decisions that can eat into those savings, too. The 5 Things I'd Check Before December 7 I'm not suggesting you switch Medicare plans every year. Quite the opposite. Sometimes, after comparing your options, you'll find your existing coverage is still a terrific fit. Wonderful! Don't touch it. Just make that an informed decision rather than a default. There's a difference between leaving a good thing alone and assuming something is still good because you haven't looked at it lately. Here's where I'd start. 1. Find the letter you probably wanted to throw away. If you're enrolled in a Medicare Advantage or Part D drug plan, your insurer should have sent you an Annual Notice of Change by the end of September. It explains what's changing for next year, including coverage and costs. This is not the piece of mail to set aside for later. Pay particular attention to premiums, deductibles, copays, covered medications, and changes to benefits. 2. Make sure your doctors are still in the picture. If you have a Medicare Advantage plan, check whether your preferred doctors, specialists, and hospitals will be in-network in 2027. Don't rely only on the insurer's directory; confirm the relationships that matter most directly with your providers. A plan with a terrific premium isn't much of a bargain if it makes it harder or more expensive to see the doctors you trust. 3. Run your prescriptions through the numbers. This is one of the easiest places to miss a potentially expensive change. Check that your medications are still covered, what they'll cost, and whether your preferred pharmacy is still a good option. Even if your prescriptions haven't changed, the financial details of your coverage might have. 4. Compare the whole cost, not just the premium. A $0-premium Medicare Advantage plan sounds wonderful, but that doesn't mean your health care costs will be zero. You generally still pay your Medicare Part B premium, and you may face deductibles, copays, and coinsurance. Look at the total picture: premiums, expected out-of-pocket expenses, the plan's out-of-pocket maximum, prescription costs, and the care you're likely to need. A lower monthly premium doesn't automatically mean a cheaper year. 5. See what else is available before you decide to stay put. You don't have to call a dozen insurance companies or spend days building spreadsheets. Start with the official Medicare Plan Finder at Medicare.gov, which lets you compare the health and drug plans available where you live. If the process gets overwhelming, you can get free, unbiased help from your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP). One important caution: Switching from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare isn't always as simple as it looks if you also want a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) policy. Depending on your circumstances and your state, you may not qualify for guaranteed acceptance, and insurers could review your health history before agreeing to cover you, or charge you more. Check those rules before you make a change. Doing Nothing Is Still a Decision Here's what I really want you to take away from all of this. You don't have to be unhappy with your Medicare plan to justify reviewing it. You don't need to have had a coverage problem, received a shocking medical bill, or learned that your insurer is pulling out of your area. You just need to recognize that the plan you chose for 2026 is being asked to do a different job in 2027. Medicare open enrollment runs from October 15 through December 7, and changes generally take effect January 1. That's your window to make sure the coverage you're carrying into the new year still makes sense. My parents might have been onto something with that Now, Don't Touch It newsletter. I still think it's great advice for most long-term investing decisions: Find a strategy that works, stick with it, and resist the urge to change things just because you can. But Medicare deserves a slightly different rule: Now, Check It. Then, Maybe Don't Touch It. Sometimes the smartest financial move you can make is simply confirming that yesterday's smart decision is still a smart decision today. excerpt: Consider investing in Aspiriant mutual funds, such as RMEAX and RMMBX, for diversified strategies.
headline: 2 Aspiriant Mutual Funds to Consider for Your Portfolio
html_content:
Aspiriant is an independent wealth management firm based in Los Angeles, CA. The firm was formed in 2008 through the merger of two existing companies, Kochis Fitz (founded in San Francisco in 1991) and Quintile Wealth Management (founded in Los Angeles in 2002).

Aspiriant’s mutual funds differ by strategy, including asset allocation, market exposure and investment risk. Each Aspiriant mutual fund has its own investment objectives, portfolio composition and risk characteristics, making it a diversified investment option.

We have picked two Aspiriant mutual funds — Aspiriant Risk-Managed Equity Allc Adv RMEAX and Aspiriant Risk-Managed Municipal Bond RMMBX— which investors should buy now for the long term. These funds have a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or Rank 2 (Buy), with positive three-year and five-year annualized returns, minimum initial investments within $5000 and expense ratios considerably lower than the category average. So, these funds have provided a comparatively stronger performance and carry a lower fee. 

Aspiriant Risk-Managed Equity Allc Adv fund invests its net assets (plus borrowings) in equity securities, including common and preferred stock and depositary receipts, and may use rights, warrants, and investment company shares.

John Allen has been the lead manager of RMEAX since Oct. 31, 2015. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as GMO Quality VI. (34.5%), Schwab Fundamental US Large Company Idx (7.2%) and Baillie Gifford Emerging Markets Eqs (5.7%) as of June 30, 2026. 

RMEAX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 16.2% and 8.9%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.29%. RMEAX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.                

To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 (Strong Buy) and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here. 

Aspiriant Risk-Managed Municipal Bond fund invests its total assets in municipal securities whose income is exempt from regular federal income tax, including obligations issued by U.S. states and their subdivisions, authorities, instrumentalities, and corporations, as well as obligations issued by U.S. territories.

Paul L. Brennan has been the lead manager of RMMBX since July 1, 2015. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as Miscellaneous Bonds (12.9%), Other (7.5%) and Cash (6.8%) as of March 31, 2026.  

RMMBX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 3.1% and 0.2%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.34%. RMMBX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

excerpt: We share with you three Vanguard mutual funds. Each has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy).
headline: 3 Vanguard Mutual Funds for Long-Term Wealth Creation
html_content:
Vanguard, established by John C. Bogle in 1975, has evolved into a global investment powerhouse with $12 trillion in assets under management as of Dec. 31, 2025. Based in Valley Forge, PA, the company employs more than 20,000 people and manages a broad lineup of 465 funds across U.S. and international markets, serving tens of millions of investors worldwide.

Unlike most asset managers, Vanguard operates under a mutual ownership model, with its funds owning the company on behalf of shareholders. This structure supports its emphasis on keeping investing costs low through no-load funds and highly competitive expense ratios. A pioneer in index investing, Vanguard has helped reshape long-term investing by making diversified, low-cost investment products widely available.

Below, we share with you three top-ranked Vanguard mutual funds, namely Vanguard Equity Income Fund VEIPX, Vanguard Global Wellington Investor VGWLX and Vanguard PRIMECAP Investor VPMCX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and is expected to outperform its peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of funds.

Vanguard Equity Income Fund primarily invests in dividend-paying, undervalued mid- and large-cap stocks with a history of consistent dividend payments, while maintaining a substantial allocation to equity securities and employing two investment advisors.

Vanguard Equity Income Fund has three-year annualized returns of 16.5%. As of June 2026, VEIPX held 221 issues, with 5.6% of its assets invested in Broadcom.

Vanguard Global Wellington Investor primarily invests in undervalued large- and mid-cap U.S. and international value stocks with improvement potential, while the remainder is allocated to domestic and foreign fixed-income securities for income generation.

Vanguard Global Wellington Investor has three-year annualized returns of 14.4%. VGWLX has an expense ratio of 0.41%.

Vanguard PRIMECAP Investor primarily invests in large- and mid-cap stocks with strong earnings growth potential that the advisor believes are undervalued relative to their long-term prospects.

Vanguard PRIMECAP Investor has three-year annualized returns of 24.4%. Joel P. Fried has been one of the fund managers of VPMCX since 1988.

To view the Zacks Rank and the past performance of all Vanguard mutual funds, investors can click here to see the complete list of Vanguard mutual funds.

excerpt: Smart Beta ETF report for HDV
headline: Is iShares Core High Dividend ETF (HDV) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
The iShares Core High Dividend ETF (HDV) made its debut on 03/29/2011, and is a smart beta exchange traded fund that provides broad exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Value category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

For a long time now, the ETF industry has been flooded with products based on market capitalization weighted indexes, which are designed to represent the broader market or a particular market segment.

Investors who believe in market efficiency should consider market cap indexes, as they replicate market returns in a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way.

But, there are some investors who would rather invest in smart beta funds; these funds track non-cap weighted strategies, and are a strong option for those who prefer choosing great stocks in order to beat the market.

This kind of index follows this same mindset, as it attempts to pick stocks that have better chances of risk-return performance; non-cap weighted strategies base selection on certain fundamental characteristics, or a mix of such characteristics.

The smart beta space gives investors many different choices, from equal-weighting, one of the simplest strategies, to more complicated ones like fundamental and volatility/momentum based weighting. However, not all of these methodologies have been able to deliver remarkable returns.

Fund Sponsor & Index

The fund is sponsored by Blackrock. It has amassed assets over $15.38 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs in the Style Box - Large Cap Value. Before fees and expenses, this particular fund seeks to match the performance of the Morningstar Dividend Yield Focus Index.

The Morningstar Dividend Yield Focus Index offers exposure to high quality U.S. domiciled companies that have had strong financial health and an ability to sustain above average dividend payouts.

Cost & Other Expenses

Cost is an important factor in selecting the right ETF, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive cousins if all other fundamentals are the same.

Operating expenses on an annual basis are 0.08% for this ETF, which makes it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It's 12-month trailing dividend yield comes in at 2.88%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation in the Healthcare sector - about 25.5% of the portfolio. Consumer Staples and Energy round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Exxonmobil Holdings Corp (XOM) accounts for about 9.28% of total assets, followed by Chevron (CVX) and Abbvie (ABBV).

The top 10 holdings account for about 55.79% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

The ETF has added roughly 24.17% so far this year and is up roughly 25.38% in the last one year (as of 10/16/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $23.64 and $29.93

HDV has a beta of 0.53 and standard deviation of 11.40% for the trailing three-year period, which makes the fund a medium risk choice in the space. With about 81 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

iShares Core High Dividend ETF is a reasonable option for investors seeking to outperform the Style Box - Large Cap Value segment of the market. However, there are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider.

Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) tracks Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index and the Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) tracks CRSP U.S. Large Cap Value Index. Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF has $114.12 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF has $190.12 billion. SCHD has an expense ratio of 0.06% and VTV changes 0.03%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Style Box - Large Cap Value

Bottom Line
