excerpt: Gold, silver and copper price strength could boost Q3 results for five mining and royalty stocks, with rising earnings estimates pointing to potential earnings beats.
headline: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights FreeportMcMoRan, Franco-Nevada, Lundin Mining, OR Royalties and Wheaton Precious Metals
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 15, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: FreeportMcMoRan FCX, Franco-Nevada Corp. FNV, Lundin Mining LUNMF, OR Royalties Inc. OR and Wheaton Precious Metals WPM.

Here are highlights from Thursday’s Analyst Blog:

5 Copper & Precious Metals Stocks Likely to Beat Q3 Estimates

The mining industry is heading into the third-quarter 2026 earnings season, supported by elevated year-over-year prices for gold, silver and copper. While gold and silver retreated from the record highs reached earlier this year, they still remained well above year-ago levels throughout the quarter. Industrial metals, including copper and zinc, strengthened during the period. 

The mining stocks fall within the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector, which seems positioned for a solid performance this earnings season. Per the latest Earnings Trends report, the sector is among 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors expected to deliver double-digit year-over-year earnings growth. Sector earnings are projected to increase 29.1% on 6.2% revenue growth, supported by higher realized commodity prices. 

Against this favorable backdrop, we have identified five mining and precious-metals royalty companies, FreeportMcMoRan, Franco-Nevada Corp., Lundin Mining, OR Royalties Inc. and Wheaton Precious Metals that appear poised to beat earnings estimates this season and are also likely to deliver improved year-over-year results. 

How Have Things Shaped Up for These Companies?

Price movements across key non-ferrous metals during the July–September 2026 period remained favorable, providing meaningful support to miners' top lines. 

Gold ranged from a low of $3,963 per ounce to a high of $4,755 per ounce in the third quarter. Gold averaged roughly $4,305 per ounce during the quarter, up 23% year over year. In the third quarter of 2026, silver ranged from a low of $55 an ounce to a high of $72.05 an ounce, averaging $63.22 an ounce. Average prices were 59% higher than last year.

Copper prices had touched an all-time high of $6.93 per pound in September, driven by intense front-loading ahead of anticipated U.S. tariffs and supply disruptions. Copper averaged around $6.53 per pound in the third quarter, supported by demand expectations and supply concerns.  

Zinc prices in the third quarter remained elevated and hovered near multi-year highs, supported by persistent global supply tightness, shrinking Western smelter capacity and declining exchange inventories.

Overall, these favorable commodity price trends are expected to have supported revenues for companies such FreeportMcMoRan, Franco-Nevada Corporation, Lundin Mining, OR Royalties and Wheaton Precious. However, operating conditions remained challenging. Higher input costs, particularly fuel and energy expenses, are likely to have partially offset the benefit of stronger commodity prices during the quarter. Miners continued focusing on improving throughput, optimizing portfolios and mining higher-grade ore to help mitigate cost pressures.

How to Pick Earnings Estimates Beating Stocks?

Identifying stocks that are poised to beat on earnings in their upcoming releases might seem a daunting task. However, our proprietary Zacks methodology makes it fairly simple. 

One can pick stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Our research shows that stocks with this combination have up to a 70% chance of an earnings surprise.

Earnings ESP is our proprietary methodology for determining stocks that have the best chances to surprise with their next earnings announcement. It is the percentage difference between the Most Accurate Estimate and the Zacks Consensus Estimate. You can uncover the best stocks before they are reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

5 Potential Outperformers This Season

FreeportMcMoRan has an Earnings ESP of +2.60% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. It is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 27. 

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FCX's third-quarter earnings has moved up 4% over the past 30 days and is pegged at 75 cents per share. It indicates a 50% increase from the year-ago quarter. The company has an average earnings surprise of 32.6% in the trailing four quarters.

The company's recent operational update for the third quarter of 2026 states copper production of approximately 830 million pounds and gold production of 230,000 ounces. Copper output was below the year-ago level of 912 million pounds and gold production also declined from 287,000 ounces. Consolidated copper sales for third-quarter 2026 are expected to have been around 750 million pounds, 23% lower than the year-ago quarter's 977 million pounds.

The company states consolidated gold sales for third-quarter 2026 are 100 thousand ounces, which came below expectations, reflecting the impact of deferred gold sales. FCX had sold 336 thousand ounces of gold in the third quarter of 2025.

FCX estimates its third-quarter 2026 consolidated average realized price to exceed $6.50 per pound of copper compared with $4.68 in the year-ago quarter. Consolidated unit net cash costs are expected to have been around $2.10 per pound of copper. 
Higher prices of copper and gold are expected to have negated the impact of lower sales volumes on its results.

Franco-Nevada has an Earnings ESP of +4.44% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 11.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FNV's third-quarter earnings is pegged at $1.95 per share, implying 36.4% growth from the year-ago quarter's actual. The estimate has moved up 3% over the past 30 days. FNV has an average earnings surprise of 5.3% in the trailing four quarters.

FNV expects total gold equivalent ounces (GEO) sales of 510,000-570,000 for 2026 and is tracking toward the upper half of this range. The company sold 519,106 GEOs in 2025 (including 11,208 GEOs from Cobre Panamá). Production is expected to be weighted toward the second half, reflecting anticipated production profiles at Candelaria, Tocantinzinho, Côté Gold, Greenstone and Valentine. 

The outlook also includes anticipated deliveries from processing stockpiled ore at Cobre Panamá. Franco-Nevada expects stream deliveries from Cobre Panamá to total 23,100 gold ounces and 265,000 silver ounces in 2026, with deliveries expected to begin in the third quarter. 

We expect GEOs sold in the third quarter of 2026 to have been higher than the year-ago 125,115 GEOs sold. Higher GEOs and prices are expected to contribute to FNV's third-quarter results. 

Lundin Mining has an Earnings ESP of +3.25% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. It is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 4.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lundin Mining's third-quarter earnings is pegged at 29 cents per share, indicating a 61% increase from the year-ago quarter. The estimate has remained unchanged over the past 30 days. LUNMF has an average earnings surprise of 13.8% in the trailing four quarters.

Lundin Mining produced 76,877 tons of copper in the second quarter of 2026, which was down 1% year over year. The company also produced 33,427 ounces of gold in the second quarter of 2026, a 12% decline. Strong contributions from Caserones and improved recoveries at Chapada were offset by lower output at Candelaria due to planned mine sequencing adjustments.

During the quarter, mining activities were primarily focused on Phase 6, with some contribution from Phase 7. Copper concentrate production continued to benefit from high grades in Phase 6 and strong throughput from Full Potential program initiatives, which focus on sustainable operational efficiencies and financial savings. Additional irrigated area in the dump leach continues to benefit copper cathode production. This is expected to have led to higher production figures for the third quarter of 2026. However, lower output at Candelaria due to weather disruptions is expected to have negated some of the impact.

OR Royalties has an Earnings ESP of +9.43% and a Zacks Rank of 2 at present. It is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 11.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for OR Royalties' third-quarter 2026 earnings is 27 cents per share, indicating a 22.7% year-over-year increase. The estimate has moved up 4% over the past 30 days. OR has an average earnings surprise of 9.98% in the trailing four quarters.

The company reported preliminary third-quarter GEO Deliveries. OR Royalties earned 20,237 attributable GEOs in the third quarter of 2026 compared with 20,326 in the third quarter of 2025. OR Royalties reported preliminary revenues from royalties and streams of $90.2 million during the third quarter, higher than $71.6 million in the year-ago quarter, mainly driven by higher prices. 

Preliminary cost of sales (excluding depletion) was $2.9 million, resulting in a quarterly cash margin of approximately $87.3 million or 96.8%. In the year-ago quarter, cost of sales excluding depletion was $2.37 million and cash margin was $69.3 million or 96.7%.

Wheaton Precious Metals has an Earnings ESP of +1.66% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present. It is expected to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 5.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for WPM's third-quarter 2026 earnings is $1.13 per share, indicating an 82.3% year-over-year increase. The estimate has moved up 1% over the past 30 days. WPM has an average earnings surprise of 12.8% in the trailing four quarters.

Wheaton Precious Metals is likely to have delivered a strong performance in the third quarter of 2026, building on the robust momentum seen in the second quarter of the year.  The company projects an attributable production of 860,000-940,000 GEOs for 2026. The midpoint of the range indicates a 30% year-over-year increase. The company expects production to be weighted to the second half, helped by mine sequencing at Salobo and Peñasquito, the full Antamina contribution and continued ramp-up of newer assets.

Our model projects WPM's total attributable production of 226,771 GEOs for the third quarter of 2026, indicating an 11.5% year-over-year increase. The total figure includes attributable gold production of 98,177 ounces, which projects a 1.8% year-over-year decline. Our model projects gold sales for the third quarter at 78,423 ounces, indicating a 0.7% dip. Our model projects 7.4 million ounces of total attributable silver production (up 24.1% year over year). Silver sales volume is expected to be 6.27 million ounces, suggesting a 31.6% year-over-year increase. 

Gold sales for the quarter are expected at $333 million, 21.3% higher year over year, as higher prices are expected to have offset the modest decline in volumes. Silver sales are projected to surge 141% year over year to $454 million, on higher volumes and prices.

Since 2000, our top stock-picking strategies have blown away the S&P's +7.7% average gain per year. Amazingly, they soared with average gains of +48.4%, +50.2% and +56.7% per year.

headline: Encompass Health Corporation (EHC) Hit a 52 Week High, Can the Run Continue?
html_content:
A strong stock as of late has been Encompass Health (EHC). Shares have been marching higher, with the stock up 3.8% over the past month. The stock hit a new 52-week high of $129.96 in the previous session. Encompass Health has gained 20.4% since the start of the year compared to the 3.9% move for the Zacks Medical sector and the 25.1% return for the Zacks Medical - Outpatient and Home Healthcare industry.

What's Driving the Outperformance?

The stock has a great record of positive earnings surprises, having beaten the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the last four quarters. In its last earnings report on August 5, 2026, Encompass Health reported EPS of $1.55 versus consensus estimate of $1.48.

For the current fiscal year, Encompass Health is expected to post earnings of $6.08 per share on $6.46 in revenues. This represents a 11.56% change in EPS on a 8.85% change in revenues. For the next fiscal year, the company is expected to earn $6.6 per share on $7 in revenues. This represents a year-over-year change of 8.53% and 8.3%, respectively.

Valuation Metrics

Though Encompass Health has recently hit a 52-week high, what is next for Encompass Health? A key aspect of this question is taking a look at valuation metrics in order to determine if the company has run ahead of itself.

On this front, we can look at the Zacks Style Scores, as these give investors a variety of ways to comb through stocks (beyond looking at the Zacks Rank of a security). The individual style scores for Value, Growth, Momentum and the combined VGM Score run from A through F. The idea behind the style scores is to help investors pick the most appropriate Zacks Rank stocks based on their individual investment style.

Encompass Health has a Value Score of B. The stock's Growth and Momentum Scores are B and C, respectively, giving the company a VGM Score of A.

In terms of its value breakdown, the stock currently trades at 21X current fiscal year EPS estimates, which is not in-line with the peer industry average of 21X. On a trailing cash flow basis, the stock currently trades at 14.4X versus its peer group's average of 15.8X. Additionally, the stock has a PEG ratio of 2.59. This isn't enough to put the company in the top echelon of all stocks we cover from a value perspective.

Zacks Rank

We also need to look at the Zacks Rank for the stock, as this supersedes any trend on the style score front. Fortunately, Encompass Health currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) thanks to rising earnings estimates.

Since we recommend that investors select stocks carrying Zacks Rank of 1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) and Style Scores of A or B, it looks as if Encompass Health meets the list of requirements. Thus, it seems as though Encompass Health shares could have potential in the weeks and months to come.

excerpt: Inflation Pressures Rise as Services Activity Weakens.
headline: Inflation Pressures Rise as Services Activity Weakens
html_content:
The first full week of Q3 earnings season is nearly complete, and results are somewhat mixed so far. As Zacks Director of Research Sheraz Mian said earlier this week in his Earnings Trends release, early Q3 reports are “tracking modestly below” recent quarters over the same time period.

Pre-market futures are mixed slightly again this morning, with the Dow — looking to close higher for its second-straight week — up +27 points, the tech-(and AI-)heavy Nasdaq — hoping to avoid its worst trading week since July — is down -42 points. The S&P 500 splitting the difference at +11 points. The small-cap Russell 2000 is presently +4 points.

Imports & Exports Bring Us 3rd Higher Inflation Print of the Week

September Import Prices from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) came in at their highest rate since May: +1.1%, versus expectations of +0.8%, and more than double the previous month’s downwardly revised +0.5%. Subtracting potentially volatile fuel prices, this number adjusts to +0.8% — still higher than expected. Year over year, +8.1% is the most expensive Imports month since July of 2022. Ex-petrol, this only drops to +6.0%.

Exports rose +2.2% last month, up from +1.2% posted for August. Agriculture exports grew by the highest number since November of 2022. Year over year, exports blossomed to +11.6%. While it’s good to see Exports earn more than Imports, we’re still looking at higher global inflation numbers, when it’s all said and done.

New York Fed Sees Sharp Decline in Services

Also out this morning is the October Services report from the Federal Reserve of New York: -20.7 is well below the -4.1 analysts were expecting, and hitting its lowest level since March of this year. This follows -8.7 print from September. This is the most rapid selling price since 2022, on weaker cap ex spending. There is also a pessimistic outlook for the tri-state (NY, NJ, CT) area. Compare this with the robust +25.5 posted in the Empire State manufacturing report earlier this week.

Q3 Earnings at a Glance: TRV, RF & More

Dow component The Travelers TRV stormed the gates in Q3 earnings this morning, posting a +29.84% earnings surprise to $9.18 per share (from an expected $7.07). Revenues of $12.45 billion were modestly higher than the Zacks consensus, and almost flat year over year. Shares are down -3% on the news, giving back some of its +32% gains year to date.

Elsewhere, we saw quarterly reports from regional banks Regions Financial RF, Citizens Financial Group CFG and M&T Bank MTB. All three beat on earnings: +8.96%, +2.17% and +2.01%, respectively, but only Regions is higher in pre-market trading following the releases, with shares up +1.2%.

Next week, earnings season shifts to a higher gear, with Netflix NFLX — which just announced a replacement of its CCO from Bela Bajaria to entertainment exec Peter Rice — joining Tesla TSLA reporting after Tuesday’s close. On Thursday, we’ll see Q3 results from Meta Platforms META, General Motors GM and Intuitive Surgical ISRG.

excerpt: Lennar (LEN) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Why Is Lennar (LEN) Down 2.5% Since Last Earnings Report?
html_content:
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Lennar (LEN). Shares have lost about 2.5% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

But investors have to be wondering, will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Lennar due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Lennar Corporation before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

Lennar Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Housing Weakness, Revenues Lag

Lennar reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter fiscal 2026 (ended Aug. 31) results. The quarter’s adjusted earnings and total revenues missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate and declined year over year.

Ongoing softness in housing demand, driven by elevated mortgage rates, led to lower deliveries and a weaker average sales price (ASP) for homes delivered, which drove the quarterly decline.

LEN’s Quarterly Numbers

Adjusted earnings of $1.23 per share missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.29 by 4.7% and fell 38.5% from $2.00 per share a year ago.

Total revenues of $8.05 billion missed the consensus estimate of $8.33 billion by 3.4% and declined 8.6% year over year. Lower deliveries and home prices weighed on results amid affordability pressure. Inventory turn stood at 2.4 times.

Lennar’s Homebuilding Highlights

Homebuilding revenues decreased 6% year over year to $7.76 billion from $8.25 billion. Home sales revenue fell to $7.73 billion from $8.21 billion, reflecting weaker pricing and fewer closings.

Home deliveries declined 3.4% to 20,840 from 21,584 but remained within management's guidance of 20,500-21,500 homes. The ASP of homes delivered decreased 2.9% to $372,000 from $383,000. Management said pricing reflected about 12% in incentives, along with base-price adjustments aimed at sustaining volume.

New orders fell 9.2% year over year to 20,879 homes. Their dollar value decreased 11.1% to $7.5 billion from $8.44 billion, while the ASP of new orders declined to $359,000 from $367,000. Backlog slipped 0.6% to 16,857 homes from 16,953. The backlog value declined 4.6% to $6.35 billion from $6.65 billion, while the average sales price in backlog fell to $376,000 from $392,000. Active communities increased to 1,713 from 1,664.

Gross margin on home sales contracted to 15.8% from 17.5% a year ago. Lower revenue per square foot and higher land costs contributed to the decline, partly offset by lower construction costs from ongoing cost-saving initiatives. Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses rose to 9.2% of home sales from 8.2%, mainly because of lower revenue leverage and higher marketing and selling costs. Net margin on home sales was 6.6%. Construction cost per square foot improved 6% year over year, while cycle time fell to a record 116 days from 126 days.

Lennar's Financial Services & Other Segments Diverge

Financial Services revenues declined to $226.1 million from $314.2 million a year ago. Operating earnings decreased to $129 million from $177 million. The current quarter included $39 million of net one-time items, primarily tied to a litigation accrual reversal following a court judgment.

Multifamily revenues fell to $38.5 million from $228.5 million, while its operating loss narrowed to $3 million from $16 million.

Lennar Other revenues rose to $22 million from $13.9 million, but the segment posted an $84 million operating loss against $62 million of operating earnings a year ago, largely due to $53 million of mark-to-market losses on technology investments.

LEN's Balance Sheet Shows Higher Leverage

Homebuilding cash and cash equivalents totaled $1.15 billion at quarter-end. Lennar had $650 million of borrowings outstanding under its $3.1 billion revolving credit facility. Homebuilding debt to total capital was 16.6% compared with 13.5% a year earlier.

The company repurchased 3 million shares for $256 million at an average price of $85.49 and redeemed $400 million of 5.25% senior notes due June 2026. Of roughly 488,000 homesites owned and controlled, less than 2.5% were owned on the balance sheet.

Lennar's Q4 Outlook Reflects Continued Market Pressure

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Lennar expects new orders of 19,500-20,500 homes (from 20,018 in the year-ago quarter) and deliveries of 22,000-23,000 homes (from 23,034 in the year-ago quarter). The ASP is projected between $370,000 and $380,000 (from $386,000 in the year-ago quarter).

Gross margin on home sales is expected at 15.5-16% (from 17% in the year-ago quarter), while SG&A is projected at 8.7-9% of home sales (from 7.8% in the year-ago quarter). The EPS is expected to be approximately $1.30-$1.65. Management reduced its full-year fiscal 2026 delivery target to about 80,000-81,000 homes from 82,000-83,000, citing continued interest-rate pressure and weaker market conditions. Financial Services operating earnings are forecast at $90-$95 million.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

It turns out, fresh estimates have trended downward during the past month.

The consensus estimate has shifted -26.5% due to these changes.

VGM Scores

At this time, Lennar has a subpar Growth Score of D, though it is lagging a bit on the Momentum Score front with an F. However, the stock has a score of C on the value side, putting it in the middle 20% for value investors.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of F. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending downward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions indicates a downward shift. It's no surprise Lennar has a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell). We expect a below average return from the stock in the next few months.

excerpt: The ongoing AI boom is just one of the reasons why Kevin Matras believes the market is set for its best quarter of the year. Discover how seasonal patterns, historical trends and several other factors point to a strong stock rally to finish out 2026.
headline: Are You Ready For A Year-End Rally?
html_content:
Just 2½ months left in the year. At present, the S&P is up 13.1% YTD, with the Nasdaq up 14.2%.

But I’m expecting a lot more upside to go.

For one, Q4 has just begun. And historically, the fourth quarter is the best quarter of the year. Since 1950, the S&P has gone up 79% of the time, with an average gain of 4.1%.

This year, however, has the potential to be much larger.

I should also mention that October is typically the best month for stocks in midterm years, which we are in. The gain averages 3.0%. And November is close behind with 2.7%. And both have win ratios of greater than 70%, with October up 73.7% of the time and November up 78.9% of the time.

But there’s a lot more going for the market than just the high-probability seasonal tendencies. That includes the soaring earnings outlook. (More on that in a bit.)

For those who wished they would have taken better advantage of this year’s rally, the good news is that it looks like the next few months could be the best few months of the entire year.

But before I get into the myriad of reasons why I think the market is just too strong to hold back right now, let me address some of the recent headlines. 

The Fed 

After the Fed’s quarter-point rate hike last month (the first one in 3 years), stocks rallied on the news. In fact, both the S&P and Nasdaq made new all-time highs shortly thereafter. (Last week’s pullback notwithstanding.)

While the Fed penciled in one more rate hike by year’s end, it’s not likely to come when the Fed meets again later this month (10/28). Plus, with the midterms just a few weeks away, that decision is expected to be punted to the following meeting on 12/9. 

Inflation 

The most recent CPI and PPI inflation reports showed both headline and core rates ticking back up. A bit of a surprise as that was in contrast with the latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCI) index (the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge), which showed inflation easing. It was also in contrast to previous CPI and PPI reports, which have come in better-than-expected. Nonetheless, that was the latest read.

Much of the increase can be attributed to higher oil prices. But that might be ready to turn the corner. Either way, we’ll get four more inflation reports, and two more employment reports before the December Fed meeting. 

Crude Oil 

Tensions in the Middle East continue.

But Middle East crude exports have risen to 16.3M barrels per day, which is the highest since the war began.

That’s approximately 80% of pre-war levels. To be clear, Hormuz volume is only at 40% of pre-war levels. And that’s with Iran exports effectively at zero. But other Middle East routes used by Saudia Arabia, the UAE and Oman, to name a few, have increased significantly, putting combined shipments at just 20% below the pre-war baseline.

Additionally, the G7 announced they would be releasing as much as 100 million barrels of diesel fuel and crude oil over the course of four months.

All of the above should help cap oil. Ease inflation. And help put a lid on rates. 

Treasury Yields 

There’s been much ado about rising Treasury yields. But there needn’t be.

With the Fed Funds Rate (FFR) at 3.88% midpoint, and the 10-yr yield at 5.09%, the spread is 121 basis points.

Historically, over the past 40 years (1985-2025), the spread between the FFR and the 10-yr, has been 100 to 150 bps, with the median at 120.

So, there’s nothing ominous about the recent rise in yields. It’s right in line with the historical norm, and appears to be a simple reversion to the long-run median spread of 120 bps.

Now, here’s why you should get excited about the rest of the year. 

History Repeats Itself 

Last year saw the S&P 500 gain 16.4%. That was on top of 2024’s 23.3%, and 2023’s 24.2%.

The historic AI tech boom has been leading the way.

And it’s reminiscent of the dot-com tech boom in 1995-1999 when the market surged by double-digits each year for 5 long, glorious years in a row, resulting in a 220% increase for the S&P, while plenty of individual stocks were up several hundred percent to several thousand percent.

I believe we could see the same thing again now.

And so does legendary trader Paul Tudor Jones. In a recent interview, he said the AI-driven bull market still has “another year or two to run,” and compared it to the late 1990’s tech boom.

That has been my sentiment all along, and comports with my expectation that we’ll see 5 years in a row of double-digit market gains, just like we did back then.

This year (2026), would be year 4, while 2027 would be year 5. But nobody says it has to stop there. With AI being touted as the most transformational tech breakthrough ever, it could very well last much longer.

Moreover, I think we can soar beyond ‘just’ a 20% gain.

Since 1988, only five times has the S&P had an annual gain of 30% or more. Just 5 times over the last 38 years.

But did you know that 2 of those 5 times happened in the 1995-1999 dot-com boom?

In 1995, it was up 37.6%. And in 1997 it was up 33.4%.

And the last time we saw a 30% gain was back in 2013.

We’re due for one, in my opinion.

Plus, with the AI boom being even bigger than the dot-com boom, driven by real earnings and real growth, if there ever was a reason to see a 30% gain, now is the time.

And AI will be one of the key drivers for stocks for years to come.

A recent comment underscoring the AI trade came from AMD CEO Lisa Su, who characterized the demand for AI as “insatiable,” and said her company alone could grow by 35% a year for the next 3-5 years because of that. In fact, she said the AI market is "faster than anything we've seen before.” And she predicted the AI data center market could grow to “$1 trillion” by 2030.

A resounding outlook for the scale of AI.

Here’s a few more, by NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang:

“AI is the most powerful technology force of our time.”

“AI will revolutionize every industry, from healthcare to transportation.”

“We are at the beginning of a new computing era.”

And while it transforms the world as we know it, it also has the potential to transform one’s portfolio.

But in addition to the ongoing AI boom, there’s plenty of other reasons to expect another year of big gains.

headline: Buy These 3 Balanced Mutual Funds for Higher Returns
html_content:
Investors interested in maintaining exposure to both equity and fixed-income securities may consider betting on balanced mutual funds. These mutual funds are believed to provide higher returns than pure fixed-income investments while maintaining low volatility. 

The proportion of equity and fixed-income investments in these funds may also vary in response to market conditions. While managers may increase the share of fixed-income securities during a downturn to avoid losses, the share of equity securities may be raised in a bullish market. Hence, these funds are expected to harness the inherent strengths of both classes of investments. 

Below, we share with you three top-ranked balanced mutual funds, namely Allspring Diversified Cap Bldr EKBAX, Thornburg Investment Income Builder TIBAX and Vanguard Wellington Investor VWELX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and is expected to outperform its peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of funds. 

Allspring Diversified Cap Bldr fund invests in equity and fixed-income securities with an emphasis on equities, targeting 70% to 90% in equity securities and 10% to 30% in debt securities.

Allspring Diversified Cap Bldr has three-year annualized returns of 30.3%. As of June 2026, EKBAX had 67 issues with 8.6% of its net assets invested in Micron Technology, Inc. 

Thornburg Investment Income Builder fund invests in net assets (plus borrowings for investment purposes) in income-producing securities and at least 50% in common stocks. 

Thornburg Investment Income Builder has three-year annualized returns of 24.3%. TIBAX has an expense ratio of 1.10%. 

Vanguard Wellington Investor fund primarily invests in dividend-paying stocks of well-established large companies, complemented by holdings in fixed income securities such as investment-grade corporate bonds, U.S. government and agency obligations, and mortgage-backed securities to provide stability and moderate current income. 

Vanguard Wellington Investor has three-year annualized returns of 15.7%. Loren Moran has been one of the fund managers of VWELX since 2017. 

To view the Zacks Rank and the past performance of all balanced mutual funds, investors canclick here to see the complete list of balanced mutual funds.

headline: Is iShares U.S. Infrastructure ETF (IFRA) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
Launched on 04/03/2018, the iShares U.S. Infrastructure ETF (IFRA) is a smart beta exchange traded fund offering broad exposure to the Utilities/Infrastructure ETFs category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

The ETF industry has long been dominated by products based on market cap weighted indexes, a strategy created to reflect the market or a particular market segment.

Investors who believe in market efficiency should consider market cap indexes, as they replicate market returns in a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way.

But, there are some investors who would rather invest in smart beta funds; these funds track non-cap weighted strategies, and are a strong option for those who prefer choosing great stocks in order to beat the market.

Based on specific fundamental characteristics, or a combination of such, these indexes attempt to pick stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance.

While this space offers a number of choices to investors, including simplest equal-weighting, fundamental weighting and volatility/momentum based weighting methodologies, not all these strategies have been able to deliver superior results.

Fund Sponsor & Index

Managed by Blackrock, IFRA has amassed assets over $4 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs in the Utilities/Infrastructure ETFs. Before fees and expenses, this particular fund seeks to match the performance of the NYSE FACTSET U.S. INFRASTRUCTURE INDEX .

The NYSE FactSet U.S. Infrastructure Index comprises of equities of U.S. companies that have infrastructure exposure and that could benefit from a potential increase in domestic infrastructure activities.

Cost & Other Expenses

For ETF investors, expense ratios are an important factor when considering a fund's return; in the long-term, cheaper funds actually have the ability to outperform their more expensive cousins if all other things remain the same.

Annual operating expenses for IFRA are 0.30%, which makes it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It's 12-month trailing dividend yield comes in at 1.79%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure that minimizes single stock risk, investors should also look at the actual holdings inside the fund. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

For IFRA, it has heaviest allocation in the Utilities sector --about 42.2% of the portfolio --while Industrials and Materials round out the top three.

When you look at individual holdings, Caterpillar Inc (CAT) accounts for about 4.36% of the fund's total assets, followed by Quanta Services Inc (PWR) and Union Pacific (UNP).

Its top 10 holdings account for approximately 25.62% of IFRA's total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

So far this year, IFRA has added roughly 9.59%, and was up about 9.35% in the last one year (as of 10/19/2026). During this past 52-week period, the fund has traded between $50.77 and $64.07.

IFRA has a beta of 0.95 and standard deviation of 16.21% for the trailing three-year period. With about 168 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

iShares U.S. Infrastructure ETF is an excellent option for investors seeking to outperform the Utilities/Infrastructure ETFs segment of the market. There are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider as well.

First Trust NASDAQ Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure ETF (GRID) tracks NASDAQ OMX Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure Index and the Global X U.S. Infrastructure Development ETF (PAVE) tracks INDXX U.S. Infrastructure Development Index. First Trust NASDAQ Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure ETF has $11.47 billion in assets, Global X U.S. Infrastructure Development ETF has $13.47 billion. GRID has an expense ratio of 0.56% and PAVE changes 0.47%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Utilities/Infrastructure ETFs

Bottom Line

excerpt: The RV biz exploded during COVID but what's happening now?
headline: Bear of the Day: Camping World (CWH)
html_content:
The stock market can be a cruel place sometimes. Just when you think things can't get any worse, the selling continues. That's especially true for companies that are struggling to find their footing in an economy where consumers are becoming increasingly selective about how they spend their money. Big-ticket discretionary purchases are particularly vulnerable. When financing costs are high and consumers are feeling the pinch, buying a new recreational vehicle isn't exactly at the top of everyone's priority list.

That's creating some serious headaches for today's Bear of the Day, Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) Camping World (CWH). Camping World Holdings is one of the nation's largest retailers of recreational vehicles. The company operates a network of RV dealerships, offering new and used motorhomes, travel trailers, and fifth wheels. It also provides financing, insurance, service, maintenance, and accessories through its Camping World and Good Sam brands.

It's a business that benefited tremendously from the pandemic-era boom in outdoor recreation. Consumers had money to spend, financing was cheap, and RV sales were booming. Unfortunately, that environment has changed considerably. Higher borrowing costs, affordability pressures, and a more cautious consumer have created a much more challenging backdrop for the RV industry.

That weakness is showing up where it matters most to us here at Zacks. I'm talking about earnings estimates. Over the last thirty days, four analysts have lowered their earnings estimates for the current year. Not a single analyst has increased estimates during that period. The bearish sentiment has pushed the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year down from 36 cents to just 20 cents per share. That's a decline of nearly 44% in only two months.

Next year's numbers aren't looking much better. Four analysts have also cut their estimates for the following year, pushing the consensus down from 87 cents to 56 cents per share. That's a reduction of more than 35%. Those downward revisions are the primary reason Camping World currently carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell).

Camping World Price and Consensus

Camping World price-consensus-chart | Camping World Quote

The industry backdrop isn't doing the company any favors either. Camping World is part of the Automotive – Original Equipment industry, which ranks in the Bottom 13% of our Zacks Industry Rank. That's not exactly the sort of neighborhood I want to be shopping in when the broader market is already dealing with uncertainty.

There are a few stocks in this industry that are in the good graces of our Zacks Rank. These include Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stocks Adient (ADNT) and ChargePoint (CHPT)

excerpt: Inflation remains elevated, but easing AI-related price pressures could support growth ETFs. Explore five funds with lower P/E ratios and positive momentum.
headline: Are You Worrying Much About Inflation? Growth ETFs in Focus
html_content:
U.S. consumer prices rose 0.6% in September, lifting annual inflation to 3.7% from 3.4% in August, above economists’ forecast of 3.6%, as quoted on CNBC. Core CPI increased 0.3% monthly and 2.6% year over year, also exceeding forecasts.

Surging energy costs drove inflation higher, with gasoline prices jumping 9.1% and accounting for about half of the monthly CPI increase. Shelter costs rose 0.4%, while used vehicle prices gained 0.7%.

Persistent inflation, fueled by energy costs and potentially AI-related demand, continues to keep price pressures well above the Fed’s 2% target.

Is AI-Led Inflation Peaking?

In a surprising forecast, Goldman Sachs economists Rindels and David Mericle said AI-related inflationary pressures are significant but moderate and may be close to peaking, as reported by Goldman Sachs.

Goldman Sachs estimates that AI-related price pressures are currently adding about 45 basis points to core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation. About half of this impact reflects genuine inflationary pressure, while the remainder stems from measurement issues.

Economists expect the impact to peak at 50 basis points by the end of 2026, before falling to just 10 basis points by the end of 2027. The expected slowdown largely reflects the prospect of more moderate price increases for computer memory and other computing equipment.

Will Inflation Cool Down in 2027?

The outlook comes at a challenging time for the Fed, mainly due to rising energy costs. In September 2026, the Fed raised interest rates for the first time since July 2023, to fight surging inflation.

Another rate hike could still be on the table this year. New York Fed President John Williams reiterated his view that another increase might be appropriate, according to Bloomberg, as mentioned on the same Yahoo Finance source.

However, policymakers are not ready to declare victory over inflation, even if AI-related price pressures begin to moderate. So, further rate hikes in 2027 may be possible, though in a tempered manner, if inflation can be controlled.

What Lies Ahead?

Goldman's forecast offers a potentially encouraging development: AI-related inflationary pressures may not continue rising indefinitely. However, energy prices remain a concern. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump said the United States will not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Iran is reportedly strengthening sensitive sites, including nuclear facilities, as it prepares for possible renewed U.S. attacks, The Wall Street Journal reported, as quoted on CNBC. So, the dark clouds over energy-led inflation are not going away yet.

Growth ETFs to Bet On?

With Goldman Sachs’ forecast offering some hope on the inflation front, we expect growth stocks to stay strong, going into 2027. Growth stocks normally underperform in a higher-rate environment.

However, if AI-led inflation falls, only an energy-driven rise needs to be tackled. And if we get positive news on the Iran war front, soaring AI demand should keep the rally going for growth ETFs.

Core CPI increased 0.3% monthly and 2.6% year over year, also exceeding forecasts. Surging energy costs drove inflation higher, with gasoline prices jumping 9.1% and accounting for about half of the monthly CPI increase. Shelter costs rose 0.4%, while used vehicle prices gained 0.7%. In a surprising forecast, Goldman Sachs economists Rindels and David Mericle said AI-related inflationary pressures are significant but moderate and may be close to peaking, as reported by Goldman Sachs. About half of this impact reflects genuine inflationary pressure, while the remainder stems from measurement issues. Economists expect the impact to peak at 50 basis points by the end of 2026, before falling to just 10 basis points by the end of 2027. Goldman's forecast offers a potentially encouraging development: AI-related inflationary pressures may not continue rising indefinitely. However, energy prices remain a concern. excerpt: AI-led selling, rising oil prices and inflation fears reshaped Wall Street last week. Discover five ETF areas that bucked the market downturn.
headline: 5 Top-Performing ETF Areas of Last Week
html_content:
U.S. stocks just recorded a largely losing week as investors moved away from technology and artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks amid rising oil prices and concerns over inflation.

The S&P 500 dropped about 2% last week, the Nasdaq Composite plunged 4.5%. The Nasdaq logged its worst weekly performance since June, per CNBC. The Russell 2000 slumped 3.1% last week.

However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average inched up about 0.7%. Meanwhile, the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) climbed above 22 for the first time in four months, signaling heightened market anxiety.

Semiconductor Stocks Lead Weekly Declines

Chip stocks suffered massive losses, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF SMH falling about 10% last week. Semiconductor stocks faced pressure throughout the week amid concerns about intensifying competition from China. 

AI Infrastructure Debt Raises Investor Concerns

Investors are increasingly questioning whether technology companies are taking on excessive debt to finance the AI infrastructure boom. Shares of neocloud provider CoreWeave, whose total debt has climbed above $51 billion (per CNBC), plunged nearly 12% on Friday, extending its weekly losses to about 24%.

Rising Oil Prices Support Energy Stocks

Energy stocks gained on Friday as crude prices advanced amid escalating tensions between the United States and Iran, alongside renewed concerns over the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

The surge in energy prices added to concerns about inflationary pressures across the economy. Crude oil is now trading near $100 a barrel, Brent is around $110, and William Blair energy research analyst Neal Dingmann thinks the next move could be a "super spike," as mentioned on Yahoo Finance.

Hotter Inflation Complicates the Market Outlook

Investors also faced fresh inflation concerns following hotter-than-expected wholesale price data. U.S. wholesale inflation recorded its largest increase since 2022 (per CNBC), while consumer inflation remained well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. Consumer prices rose 3.7% annually in September as gas prices surged.

Persistent price pressures could limit the Federal Reserve's flexibility to ease monetary policy, adding another potential headwind for equities, particularly technology stocks whose valuations are sensitive to interest-rate expectations.

Winning ETF Areas of Last Week

Long/Short –AGF U.S. Market Neutral Anti-Beta Fund BTAL – Up 7.0%

Long-short ETFs rise during a market sell-off because they are designed to profit from a combination of long positions in selected securities and short positions in others. Their performance depends on the strategy that offers cushion in the struggling market.

Energy – United States Oil Fund LP USO – Up 6.7%

Energy stocks rose last week, thanks to a sharp increase in crude oil prices amid escalating tensions between the United States and Iran, as well as renewed Russia-Ukraine tensions.

Walmart Single-Stock ETF –REX WMT Growth & Income ETF WMTI – Up 5.2%

Walmart Inc. WMT shares rose 6.5% last week. With consumer prices rising, shoppers may favor Walmart's low prices.  WMTI charges 99 bps in fees and yields 35.23% annually.

Insurance –Invesco KBW Property & Casualty Insurance ETF KBWP – Up 5.1%

Insurers can benefit when investors rotate away from volatile AI and semiconductor stocks, seeking businesses with steadier earnings. Major holdings of the fund like The Travelers Companies Inc. TRV and Chubb Limited CB saw shares rising last week.

TRV shares gained on earnings strength while Chubb is rising mainly on pre-earnings positioning and a positive earnings-surprise setup. Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings for CB rose over the past seven fays as well as past one month.

Consumer Staples – Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Staples ETF RSPS – Up 5.1%

Concerns about AI valuations, rising borrowing costs and semiconductor competition encouraged investors to shift toward relatively defensive consumer stocks. This was basically a risk-off trade.

excerpt: BHP agrees to sell its Kambalda Nickel Concentrator to Gold Fields as it restructures its Western Australia nickel business, with remaining asset decisions due by February 2027.
headline: BHP to Sell Few Nickel Assets: What's Next for Its Nickel Business?
html_content:
BHP Group BHP has agreed to divest its Kambalda Nickel Concentrator (KNC) along with a package of tenements and mineralization rights to Gold Fields Limited GFI. This is part of BHP’s efforts to restructure its Western Australia nickel business. 

The transaction is expected to be completed during calendar 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. Financial details were not disclosed. BHP will continue to manage the asset safely and responsibly until the transaction is completed.

The concentrator has a nominal ore processing capacity of 1.6 million tons per year and can produce concentrate containing approximately 13% nickel. Gold Fields plans to conduct a detailed assessment of the acquired assets and evaluate their potential long-term use for both gold and nickel processing.

Gold Fields is a globally diversified gold producer with eight operating mines in Australia, South Africa, Ghana, Chile and Peru and one project in Canada. 

BHP’s Nickel Operations Remain Under Review

In July 2024, BHP announced the temporary suspension of its Western Australia Nickel business, comprising Nickel West and the West Musgrave project. This was due to a sharp deterioration in market conditions caused by an oversupply of nickel and increased availability of lower-cost supply.

Western Australia Nickel holds the majority of tenements hosting nickel sulfide mineral resources in the Agnew-Wiluna belt, Western Australia. The Nickel West asset consists of open-cut and underground mines, concentrators, and a smelter and refinery for downstream processing. The West Musgrave project is a greenfield nickel and copper project in Western Australia's West Musgrave Ranges. The project construction was temporarily suspended at around 30% completion. 

Western Australia Nickel reported an underlying EBITDA loss of $255 million in fiscal 2026 compared with a loss of $589 million in fiscal 2025 as operations transitioned into temporary suspension in December 2024.

BHP plans to review the future of its remaining Western Australia Nickel assets by February 2027.  Potential options include divestment, continued suspension, restarting operations or closure. 

For BHP, the Kambalda divestment could help streamline its portfolio, although the future of the remaining nickel assets remains unresolved. The company’s broader investment case remains supported by its diversified exposure to commodities such as iron ore and copper, reducing its dependence on nickel.

Sibanye Stillwater Limited SBSW has also placed its fully-owned Sandouville nickel refinery in France on care and maintenance since June 30, 2025, amid low nickel prices and elevated operating costs. The last nickel matte delivery from the operation was received in early January 2025. 

Sibanye Stillwater has begun consultations with employee representatives on the refinery's future under French labor law. The company is also working with the French government to identify the best possible outcome for all stakeholders.

Vale S.A. VALE meanwhile produces one of the world's most diverse portfolios of refined nickel under its Vale Base Metals business, serving critical industries in alloys, coatings, batteries, powder metallurgy and chemical applications. Its operations span Canada, the United Kingdom, Japan and Brazil.

In the second quarter of 2026, Vale reported nickel production at 42 kt, up 4.2% year over year. Higher output from Onça Puma, as well as record production at Long Harbour, helped offset the impact of the biennial planned maintenance at Sudbury downstream facilities.

Our team of experts has just released the 5 stocks with the greatest probability of gaining +100% or more in the coming months. Of those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian highlights the one stock set to climb highest.

This innovative software-as-a-service firm upped its user base +22% year over year. That rate is increasing and margins are expanding as AI efficiencies take effect. headline: Pre-Markets Mixed Ahead of New Q3 Earnings, Housing Data
html_content:
Monday, October 19th, 2026

Pre-market futures are mixed but flattening out from last week’s performance, when the tech-heavy Nasdaq saw a bigger selloff than the blue-chip Dow index. Currently, the Dow is -88 points but the Nasdaq is +376 points — not quite making up for Friday’s losses, but we’re early yet. The S&P 500 splits the difference, +38 points, while the small-cap Russell 2000 is +12 points at this hour. 

Spot oil prices remain elevated but are off their inflamed near-term highs: $101 per barrel (/bbl) on WTI and $108/bbl on Brent crude. Bond yields, similarly, are still lofty but cooling from recent levels: the 10-year, for instance, is currently +5.102% — consider that we were near +5.3% back in late September. The 2-year yield is now +4.749% and the 30-year +5.440%. 
 

Q3 Earnings at a Glance: FITB, CLF


We get some marquee names reporting Q3 earnings later this week — including GE, GM and NFLX Tuesday and META and TSLA Wednesday — but we start this week easing back into earnings season:

Fifth Third Bank FITB shares are up modestly on its mixed Q3 report ahead of today’s open. Earnings of $1.13 per share outperformed the Zacks consensus $1.09 by +3.67%, while revenues of $3.28 billion missed expectations by -1.74%. excerpt: A Consumer Reports investigation found that some shoppers were offered prices up to 23% higher than others for the exact same items. Meredith Margrave explains how personalized pricing works and shares five simple ways to find out whether you're paying more than other shoppers.
headline: Are You Being Charged More Than Other Shoppers? Here's How to Find Out
html_content:
Imagine you and I are doing our grocery shopping. Same store. Same shopping list. Same time of day.

We both add a box of cereal to our carts. Except you're being charged $2.99, and I'm being charged $3.69. That's about 23% more for the exact same thing, and neither of us has any idea.

Sound far-fetched? Something remarkably similar actually happened.

In December 2025, Consumer Reports and the Groundwork Collaborative released an investigation in which more than 400 volunteers compared Instacart prices for identical products at the same stores, at the same time. Some shoppers were offered prices up to 23% higher than others, and entire grocery baskets varied in price by an average of about 7%.

Instacart said the tests were randomized and not based on shoppers' personal data, and the researchers didn't find prices tied to factors like ZIP code or income. The company ended the experiments days later. But the investigation made one thing clear: The technology to show different people different prices already exists, and most shoppers would never know.

So how do you know whether the price you're being offered is the best price available — or just the price a company thinks you'll pay?

The Internet Knows More About You Than You Think

Search for a pair of shoes, and suddenly those shoes are following you around the internet. We've all gotten used to it. But the same information that helps companies decide what to advertise to you can also help them figure out how much you're willing to spend.

It's called personalized pricing, sometimes referred to as surveillance pricing: using information about individual shoppers to determine which prices, discounts, or offers to show them. Economists call charging different customers different prices for the same thing price discrimination, and the concept isn't new. Senior discounts and coupons are both versions of it. What's new is the precision. A company can potentially set prices one shopper at a time.

In a January 2025 report, the Federal Trade Commission described pricing technology that can draw on everything from your location and browsing history to your mouse movements and the items you've abandoned in your online shopping cart. To you, closing the browser on something that's too expensive is just a shopping decision. To a company analyzing your behavior, it may be one more clue about the price that would get you to buy.

Not every price difference is surveillance pricing, though. When airfare and hotel rates move with demand and timing, that's dynamic pricing, and it applies to everyone shopping at that moment. Loyalty discounts and shipping costs also vary for legitimate reasons. So how can you tell if personalized pricing is happening to you?

5 Ways to Find Out Whether You're Paying More

Here's the good news: You don't need to be a tech expert. You just need to do a little comparison shopping — not between two stores, but between two versions of the same shopping experience.

1. Check the Price Before You Sign In

Let's say you find a laptop for $1,499 while signed into a retailer's website. Before you buy, open a private or incognito browser window, stay signed out, and look up the same model. Try a different browser or your phone, too. You're checking whether the price changes when the site knows less about you.

Incognito mode doesn't make you anonymous, and it doesn't erase data a retailer has already collected. But it gives you another point of comparison, and sometimes that's all you need.

2. Ask Someone Else What Price They See

This might be my favorite trick because it's so easy. Text the product link to your spouse, your sister, or a friend, and ask what price they're seeing. If they live somewhere else, even better. Just make sure you're comparing the same product, with the same options, at about the same time.

If you're seeing $279 and your friend is seeing $249, you haven't necessarily proved that a company is using surveillance pricing, since a promotion or geographic difference might explain it. But you have found a potentially better price, and that's what we're after.

3. Compare the App With the Website

Some of the best coupons are buried inside retailers' apps. The trade-off is that a signed-in app makes it easier for a company to connect your shopping activity to your account and, depending on your permissions, to your location. Before you check out, compare the final total on the website, both signed in and signed out.

But don't give up a legitimate discount in the name of privacy. If your grocery app is offering $20 off an order and the website isn't, take the discount! We're trying to spend less, not win an award for being the internet's most mysterious shopper.

4. Experiment With Your Location

Location can be one piece of the data used in personalized pricing. Ask someone in another ZIP code to check the same item, or use a virtual private network (VPN) to see an offer from somewhere else. Just be careful: Taxes, shipping costs, and regional promotions vary legitimately, and a lower price is useless if you aren't eligible to buy at it.

5. Don't Buy Immediately — See If an Offer Comes Back

Remember that abandoned shopping cart? It can work in your favor, too. Retailers sometimes follow up on abandoned carts with a discount or promotional offer ("Still thinking it over?"). There's no guarantee this works, and it isn't proof that the original price was personalized. I wouldn't bother for something I need today. But if I'm thinking about spending $900 on a new piece of furniture? I can probably survive another 48 hours without it.

You Found a Lower Price... Here's What to Do

Let's say a retailer shows you a $1,200 price when you're logged into your account, but $1,075 when you browse as a guest. First, confirm that you're comparing identical offers, including taxes, delivery fees, warranties, and promotional eligibility. If everything really is the same, the simplest move is often to check out as a guest.

If you want to buy through your account for rewards or a warranty, take screenshots of both prices and ask customer service: "I'm seeing this item for $1,075, but my account shows $1,200. Can you honor the lower price?" You don't have to accuse anyone of wrongdoing. Just ask for the deal. If the retailer refuses, check competitors or ask about price matching.

And if you suspect a company is using deceptive or unlawful pricing practices, you can file a report with the Federal Trade Commission or your state attorney general. States are already taking action. Maryland's restrictions on surveillance pricing by food retailers and grocery delivery services took effect on October 1, 2026. New York requires companies to disclose when a price was set by an algorithm using a shopper's personal data. Connecticut's ban on prices set using personal data takes effect July 1, 2027, and New Jersey's ban on surveillance pricing for groceries follows on August 1, 2027. This is no longer a hypothetical concern. It's getting serious attention right now.

There's One More Thing You Can Do: Share Less Data

I know, I know. Telling people to protect their privacy online can feel a little like telling them to eat more vegetables. Start with the easy stuff:

Turn off unnecessary location permissions. Your grocery app doesn't need to know where you are every minute of the day.

Review tracking permissions on your phone. You may be able to limit how apps track you across other apps and websites.

Clear cookies periodically. It can reduce some browser-based tracking.

Use guest checkout when it makes sense. You don't need an account with every retailer.

None of this guarantees a lower price, and I wouldn't spend hours tinkering with privacy settings to save 50 cents on crackers. But if you can limit unnecessary data collection without making your life more difficult, why not?

My New Rule for Big Purchases

If I'm ordering a $25 birthday gift, I'm not going to conduct a six-part investigation into whether the internet thinks I have expensive taste. But if I'm about to book a $5,000 vacation or buy a $2,000 appliance? You'd better believe I'm going to spend a few minutes comparing prices in different browsers, checking whether I'm signed in, and asking my husband what the website shows him. Even a 5% difference on a $2,000 purchase is $100.

And that's real money.

The most frustrating part of personalized pricing isn't that prices change. It's that you may never know a better price was available in the first place. Comparing prices before you buy is still the basic rule of smart shopping. We just might need to expand what comparison shopping means.

Because these days, the person getting the better deal might not be shopping at another store. They might be shopping at the exact same store as you.

And I'd really rather not be the one paying more.

Wealth-Building Tips for a Brighter Future

Want to expand your money skills to help you thrive, both now and in the years to come? Need clarity about ways to navigate the twists and turns of the economy, the stock market and more?

Telling people to protect their privacy online can feel a little like telling them to eat more vegetables. Start with the easy stuff: Turn off unnecessary location permissions. Your grocery app doesn't need to know where you are every minute of the day. Review tracking permissions on your phone. You may be able to limit how apps track you across other apps and websites. Clear cookies periodically. It can reduce some browser-based tracking. Use guest checkout when it makes sense. You don't need an account with every retailer. None of this guarantees a lower price, and I wouldn't spend hours tinkering with privacy settings to save 50 cents on crackers. But if you can limit unnecessary data collection without making your life more difficult, why not? My New Rule for Big Purchases If I'm ordering a $25 birthday gift, I'm not going to conduct a six-part investigation into whether the internet thinks I have expensive taste. But if I'm about to book a $5,000 vacation or buy a $2,000 appliance? You'd better believe I'm going to spend a few minutes comparing prices in different browsers, checking whether I'm signed in, and asking my husband what the website shows him. Even a 5% difference on a $2,000 purchase is $100. And that's real money. The most frustrating part of personalized pricing isn't that prices change. It's that you may never know a better price was available in the first place. Comparing prices before you buy is still the basic rule of smart shopping. We just might need to expand what comparison shopping means. Because these days, the person getting the better deal might not be shopping at another store. They might be shopping at the exact same store as you. And I'd really rather not be the one paying more. headline: Top Research Reports for UnitedHealth, ServiceNow & 3M
html_content:
Monday, October 19, 2026

The Zacks Research Daily presents the best research output of our analyst team. Today's Research Daily features new research reports on 12 major stocks, including UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH), ServiceNow, Inc. (NOW) and 3M Co. (MMM), as well as a micro-cap stock Coffee Holding Co., Inc. (JVA). The Zacks microcap research is unique as our research content on these small and under-the-radar companies is the only research of its type in the country.

These research reports have been hand-picked from the roughly 70 reports published by our analyst team today.

You can see all of today’s research reports here >>>

Ahead of Wall Street

The daily 'Ahead of Wall Street' article is a must-read for all investors who would like to be ready for that day's trading action. The article comes out before the market opens, attempting to make sense of that morning's economic releases and how they will affect that day's market action. You can read this article for free on our home page and can actually sign up there to get an email notification as this article comes out each morning.

You can read today's AWS here >>> Pre-Markets Mixed Ahead of New Q3 Earnings, Housing Data

Today's Featured Research Reports

Shares of UnitedHealth have gained +13.1% over the past year against the Zacks Medical - HMOs industry’s gain of +16%. The company’s third-quarter earnings beat estimates. Its diversified operations and disciplined pricing support its growth prospects. Optum remains a key earnings driver, aided by integrated care, AI-enabled solutions and pharmacy services. 

Commercial fee-based membership gains and a healthy sales pipeline provide further opportunities. Higher Medicare Advantage payment rates and improved medical cost management support the earnings outlook. Cash generation also allows continued investment and shareholder returns. Healthcare demand also supports its core business. 

However, elevated commercial medical costs could constrain margin recovery. Regulatory scrutiny and a premium valuation leave limited room for execution setbacks, while debt obligations could restrict financial flexibility. As such, we have a Neutral recommendation for the stock.

(You can read the full research report on UnitedHealth here >>>)

ServiceNow’s shares have declined -7.3% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Computers - IT Services industry’s decline of -11.5%. The company is facing intense software competition, possible budget reallocation toward stand-alone AI spending, variable deal timing, foreign exchange exposure, acquisition execution risk, higher debt and gross-margin dilution from greater hyperscaler and AI usage over time.

Nevertheless, ServiceNow benefits from enterprise workflow digitization and broader adoption of governed, agentic AI across IT, employee, CRM, security and data use cases. AI-native bundles and rising usage are expanding monetization, while higher adoption and consumption support a broader revenue flywheel. 

AI Control Tower, Armis and Veza deepen governance and security cross-selling, while planned mid-market products widen the addressable base. Subscription growth, rising customer commitments and internal AI efficiencies support the long-term model. 

(You can read the full research report on ServiceNow here >>>)

Shares of 3M have outperformed the Zacks Diversified Operations industry over the past year (+8.4% vs. -10.8%). The company is poised to benefit from solid momentum in the Safety and Industrial unit, driven by strength in the industrial adhesives and tapes, abrasives and electrical markets. Strength in the semiconductor, aerospace and defense markets is aiding the Transportation and Electronics unit. 

Solid operational execution, restructuring savings and spending discipline are supporting the margin performance. Synergies from acquisitions made by the company also bolster its growth. Its measures to reward shareholders through dividends are encouraging. 

However, persistent softness in the retail markets, owing to a decrease in consumer discretionary spending, remains a concern for the Consumer unit. High debt levels, if not controlled, are likely to raise financial obligations and hurt profitability. Foreign currency headwinds are an added concern.

(You can read the full research report on 3M here >>>)

Shares of Coffee have gained +11.1% over the past year against the Zacks Beverages - Soft drinks industry’s gain of +25.6%. This microcap company with a market capitalization of $26.03 million has seen its diversified product portfolio, expanding private-label operations and growing roasted and packed coffee business provide opportunities for long-term growth. 

The Second Empire acquisition strengthens production capacity and customer reach, while strong customer retention and new business support revenue development. Lower coffee costs and improved inventory positioning have enhanced profitability. 

However, exposure to volatile commodity prices, reduced hedging protection and customer concentration remain key risks. The increasing dependence on packed coffee also makes sustained customer demand essential, particularly as green-coffee sales weaken. Moreover, recent margin improvements partly reflect temporary benefits from tariff refunds and trading gains, raising concerns about their sustainability.

(You can read the full research report on Coffee here >>>)

Other noteworthy reports we are featuring today include Otis Worldwide Corp. (OTIS), Brown & Brown, Inc. (BRO) and The Ensign Group, Inc. (ENSG).

Mark Vickery
Senior Editor

UnitedHealth's (UNH) Optum Unit Supports Growth, Debt Burden Weighs

Growing Customer Base & Partnerships Aid ServiceNow (NOW)

Safety and Industrial Segment Aids 3M (MMM) Amid Forex Woes

Featured Reports

Otis (OTIS) Gains From Service Growth, China Weakness Ails
Per the Zacks analyst, strong modernization demand, rising repair activity and a growing Service backlog support Otis' prospects. However, weak equipment demand in China and cost inflation are risks.

Brown & Brown Gains From Acquisition Growth, Organic Weakness Weighs
Per the Zacks analyst, BRO's acquisition-led growth and Retail segment strength support revenue expansion, while softer insurance pricing, weak organic growth and margin pressure weigh on earnings.

Ensign Group (ENSG) Gains on Patient Growth Amid Reimbursement Risks
Per the Zacks analyst, strong patient volumes, high occupancy and acquisitions support Ensign Group's growth. However, reimbursement risks and rising labor costs remain concerns.

iDose Driving Glaukos' (GKOS) Growth Despite Reimbursement Uncertainty
Per the Zacks analyst, rising adoption of iDose TR is driving robust sales growth for Glaukos. Glaucoma sales were up 64% in second quarter. However, potential restrictive final LCD can hurt prospect.

Supply-Chain Gains & Royalties Aid Domino's (DPZ), High Costs Ail
Per the Zacks analyst, Domino's benefits from supply-chain gains, higher franchise royalties and global store expansion. However, weak comparable sales and rising costs remain concerns.

New Upgrades

Expansion Initiatives & Cost-Cutting Efforts to Boost CarMax (KMX)
The Zacks analyst is bullish on CarMax's plans to expand off-site reconditioning and auction capacity, as well as its cost discipline to reduce SG&A expenses.

Par Pacific Banks on Favorable Refining Markets & Financial Strength
The Zacks analyst likes Par Pacific's favorable refining outlook, stronger balance sheet and integrated operations, which support cash flow generation and shareholder value creation.

New Downgrades

High Costs and Execution Risks Weigh on MP Materials (MP)
Per the Zacks analyst, MP Materials faces high processing costs, weak cash conversion, customer concentration, commodity price exposure and execution risks, threatening margins and cash flows.

High Mortgage Rates & Macro Risks Hurt Lennar's (LEN) Growth
Per the Zacks analyst, Lennar is hurting due to housing market softness as elevated mortgage rates and macro uncertainties are causing affordability concerns for homebuyers.

Zacks' Research Chief Names "Stock Most Likely to Double"

Our team of experts has just released the 5 stocks with the greatest probability of gaining +100% or more in the coming months. Of those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian highlights the one stock set to climb highest.

This innovative software-as-a-service firm upped its user base +22% year over year. That rate is increasing and margins are expanding as AI efficiencies take effect. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners, but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like D-Wave Quantum, which shot up +680.1%.

excerpt: Sector ETF report for XLY
headline: Should You Invest in the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY)?
html_content:
Launched on December 16, 1998, the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to provide a broad exposure to the Consumer Discretionary - Broad segment of the equity market.

Passively managed ETFs are becoming increasingly popular with institutional as well as retail investors due to their low cost, transparency, flexibility and tax efficiency. They are excellent vehicles for long term investors.

Investor-friendly, sector ETFs provide many options to gain low risk and diversified exposure to a broad group of companies in particular sectors. Consumer Discretionary - Broad is one of the 16 broad Zacks sectors within the Zacks Industry classification. It is currently ranked 12, placing it in bottom 25%.

Index Details

The fund is sponsored by State Street Investment Management. It has amassed assets over $22.37 billion, making it the largest ETF attempting to match the performance of the Consumer Discretionary - Broad segment of the equity market. XLY seeks to match the performance of the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector Index before fees and expenses.

The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector Index seeks to provide an effective representation of the consumer discretionary sector of the S&P 500 Index.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.08%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.82%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure that minimizes single stock risk, investors should also look at the actual holdings inside the fund. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation in the Consumer Discretionary sector -- about 100% of the portfolio.

Looking at individual holdings, Amazon.com Inc (AMZN) accounts for about 23.86% of total assets, followed by Tesla Inc (TSLA) and Home Depot Inc (HD).

The top 10 holdings account for about 68.4% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

So far this year, XLY has lost about 3.57%, and is down about 1.55% in the last one year (as of 10/20/2026). During this past 52-week period, the fund has traded between $105.66 and $124.52.

The ETF has a beta of 1.24 and standard deviation of 20.41% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 50 holdings, it has more concentrated exposure than peers.

Alternatives

State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF carries a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Thus, XLY is a good option for those seeking exposure to the Consumer Discretionary ETFs area of the market. Investors might also want to consider some other ETF options in the space.

iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB) tracks Dow Jones U.S. Select Home Construction Index and the Vanguard Consumer Discretionary Index Fund ETF Shares (VCR) tracks MSCI US Investable Market Consumer Discretionary 25/50 Index. iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF has $2.50 billion in assets, Vanguard Consumer Discretionary Index Fund ETF Shares has $5.89 billion. ITB has an expense ratio of 0.37%, and VCR charges 0.09%.

Bottom Line

To learn more about this product and other ETFs, screen for products that match your investment objectives and read articles on latest developments in the ETF investing universe, please visit Zacks ETF Center.

The fund is sponsored by Invesco. It has amassed assets over $325.27 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs attempting to match the performance of the Industrials - Broad segment of the equity market. PRN seeks to match the performance of the DWA Industrials Technical Leaders Index before fees and expenses.

Costs
