excerpt: KeyCorp (KEY) delivered earnings and revenue surprises of +10.87% and +1.13%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 2026. Do the numbers hold clues to what lies ahead for the stock?
headline: KeyCorp (KEY) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
html_content:
KeyCorp (KEY) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.51 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.46 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.41 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +10.87%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this company would post earnings of $0.42 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.44, delivering a surprise of +4.76%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

KeyCorp, which belongs to the Zacks Banks - Major Regional industry, posted revenues of $2.05 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.13%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.89 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

KeyCorp shares have lost about 3.5% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.4%.

What's Next for KeyCorp?

While KeyCorp has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for KeyCorp was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.49 on $2.12 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $1.83 on $8.07 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Banks - Major Regional is currently in the bottom 31% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

One other stock from the same industry, BankUnited, Inc. (BKU), is yet to report results for the quarter ended September 2026. The results are expected to be released on October 21.

This company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.05 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +10.5%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.9% lower over the last 30 days to the current level.

BankUnited, Inc.'s revenues are expected to be $292.61 million, up 6.1% from the year-ago quarter.

Should You Invest in KeyCorp (KEY)?

excerpt: UnitedHealth, ServiceNow, 3M and Coffee Holding draw attention as new research reports weigh growth drivers, operational strengths and risks across healthcare, software, industry and coffee.
headline: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights UnitedHealth, ServiceNow, 3M and Coffee
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 20, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: UnitedHealth Group Inc. UNH, ServiceNow, Inc. NOW, 3M Co. MMM and Coffee Holding Co., Inc. JVA.

Here are highlights from Monday’s Analyst Blog:

Top Research Reports for UnitedHealth, ServiceNow and 3M

The Zacks Research Daily presents the best research output of our analyst team. Today's Research Daily features new research reports on 12 major stocks, including UnitedHealth Group Inc., ServiceNow, Inc. and 3M Co., as well as a micro-cap stock Coffee Holding Co., Inc.. The Zacks microcap research is unique as our research content on these small and under-the-radar companies is the only research of its type in the country.

These research reports have been hand-picked from the roughly 70 reports published by our analyst team today.

You can see all of today's research reports here >>>

Today's Featured Research Reports

Shares of UnitedHealth have gained +13.1% over the past year against the Zacks Medical - HMOs industry's gain of +16%. The company's third-quarter earnings beat estimates. Its diversified operations and disciplined pricing support its growth prospects. Optum remains a key earnings driver, aided by integrated care, AI-enabled solutions and pharmacy services. 

Commercial fee-based membership gains and a healthy sales pipeline provide further opportunities. Higher Medicare Advantage payment rates and improved medical cost management support the earnings outlook. Cash generation also allows continued investment and shareholder returns. Healthcare demand also supports its core business. 

However, elevated commercial medical costs could constrain margin recovery. Regulatory scrutiny and a premium valuation leave limited room for execution setbacks, while debt obligations could restrict financial flexibility. As such, we have a Neutral recommendation for the stock.

(You can read the full research report on UnitedHealth here >>>)

ServiceNow's shares have declined -7.3% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Computers - IT Services industry's decline of -11.5%. The company is facing intense software competition, possible budget reallocation toward stand-alone AI spending, variable deal timing, foreign exchange exposure, acquisition execution risk, higher debt and gross-margin dilution from greater hyperscaler and AI usage over time.

Nevertheless, ServiceNow benefits from enterprise workflow digitization and broader adoption of governed, agentic AI across IT, employee, CRM, security and data use cases. AI-native bundles and rising usage are expanding monetization, while higher adoption and consumption support a broader revenue flywheel. 

AI Control Tower, Armis and Veza deepen governance and security cross-selling, while planned mid-market products widen the addressable base. Subscription growth, rising customer commitments and internal AI efficiencies support the long-term model. 

(You can read the full research report on ServiceNow here >>>)

Shares of 3M have outperformed the Zacks Diversified Operations industry over the past year (+8.4% vs. -10.8%). The company is poised to benefit from solid momentum in the Safety and Industrial unit, driven by strength in the industrial adhesives and tapes, abrasives and electrical markets. Strength in the semiconductor, aerospace and defense markets is aiding the Transportation and Electronics unit. 

Solid operational execution, restructuring savings and spending discipline are supporting the margin performance. Synergies from acquisitions made by the company also bolster its growth. Its measures to reward shareholders through dividends are encouraging. 

However, persistent softness in the retail markets, owing to a decrease in consumer discretionary spending, remains a concern for the Consumer unit. High debt levels, if not controlled, are likely to raise financial obligations and hurt profitability. Foreign currency headwinds are an added concern.

(You can read the full research report on 3M here >>>)

Shares of Coffee have gained +11.1% over the past year against the Zacks Beverages - Soft drinks industry's gain of +25.6%. This microcap company with a market capitalization of $26.03 million has seen its diversified product portfolio, expanding private-label operations and growing roasted and packed coffee business provide opportunities for long-term growth. 

The Second Empire acquisition strengthens production capacity and customer reach, while strong customer retention and new business support revenue development. Lower coffee costs and improved inventory positioning have enhanced profitability. 

However, exposure to volatile commodity prices, reduced hedging protection and customer concentration remain key risks. The increasing dependence on packed coffee also makes sustained customer demand essential, particularly as green-coffee sales weaken. Moreover, recent margin improvements partly reflect temporary benefits from tariff refunds and trading gains, raising concerns about their sustainability.

(You can read the full research report on Coffee here >>>)

excerpt: Stock Futures Fall Before the Open
headline: Stock Futures Fall Before the Open
html_content:
Pre-market futures are decidedly down at this hour, sinking into the red ahead of economic and earnings reports out this morning. The Dow is off -91 points currently, the Nasdaq -256 points and the S&P 500 -27. The small-cap Russell 2000 is a less-inflamed -6 points. Oil prices are up on oil tankers continuing to be under fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and WTI is back up to triple digits: $100 per barrel (/bbl). Brent crude, the international spot oil price component, is $110/bbl.

Housing Starts & Building Permits Drop in September

The Housing market continues to wallow in recessionary waters, as September Housing Starts came in lower than expected: +1.22 million seasonally adjusted, annualized units is beneath the +1.3 million estimated, for the third-straight month at -5.2%. Single-family homes fell another -4.6% while Multi-family was worse: -6.7%. Mortgage rates climbed around 70 basis points (bps) during the course of September, from +6.8% at the start of the month to +7.5% by the end.

Building Permits, a proxy for future Starts, dipped another -0.2% month over month, -2.1% year over year, to +1.400 million seasonally adjusted, annualized units. This was slightly above expectations for +1.39 million new starts. Single-family was down again, -4%, while Multi-family was up +5.9% on new permits.

Yesterday, the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB) posted a homebuilder confidence survey that reached its lowest level since June of 2012: 29, below already dismal expectations for 31 (50 is the level where homebuilders begin to express confidence in the market). Mortgage rates were cited as the culprit here, as well. And don’t forget Fannie Mae’s forecast from last week, where it bumped up mortgage rate expectations to +7.5% for the full-year 2027.

After today’s open, Pending Home Sales for September are expected to drop -0.4% from the prior month’s +0.3% gain (which was the first positive month in the past three). This follows last week’s Existing Home Sales numbers, which gained +1.5% on headline.

Q3 Earnings at a Glance: GE & GM

GE Aerospace GE reported a strong Q3 this morning, with earnings of $2.25 per share coming in ahead of the Zacks consensus $2.02 by +11.39%, and nicely higher than the $1.66 per share reported in the year-ago quarter. Revenues of $13.29 billion outpaced expectations by +5%. Pre-market trading is lower on this down-day so far, as investors check GE’s high multiple and slight dent in free cashflow.

General Motors GM also outperformed Q3 estimates ahead of today’s open, with earnings of $3.70 per share surpassing the $3.55 analysts had been expecting for a +4.23% positive surprise. Revenues of $50.02 billion amounted to a +3.75% beat, but forward earnings guidance coming down at the midpoint for its full year are bringing shares down -6.2% at this hour.

What to Expect from Today’s Stock Market

Aside from the Pending Home Sales report due at 10am ET this morning, Netflix NFLX becomes the first marquee name to post earnings today, after the closing bell. The streaming entertainment giant, currently carrying a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), is expecting +39% earnings growth on +11.8% in revenues for its Q3.

Elsewhere, United Airlines UAL and Intuitive Surgical ISRG re also two bigger names putting up Q3 numbers after today’s trading day. United, a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) today, is expected to post negative -6.47% earnings growth, while Intuitive, a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), is anticipated to earn +8.75% more year over year, +15% on revenues.

Radical New Technology Could Hand Investors Huge Gains

Quantum Computing is the next technological revolution, and it could be even more advanced than AI.

While some believed the technology was years away, it is already present and moving fast. Large hyperscalers, such as Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle, and even Meta and Tesla, are scrambling to integrate quantum computing into their infrastructure.

Senior Stock Strategist Kevin Cook reveals 7 carefully selected stocks poised to dominate the quantum computing landscape in his report, Beyond AI: The Quantum Leap in Computing Power.

Kevin was among the early experts who recognized NVIDIA's enormous potential back in 2016. Now, he has keyed in on what could be "the next big thing" in quantum computing supremacy. Today, you have a rare chance to position your portfolio at the forefront of this opportunity.

See Top Quantum Stocks Now >>

headline: The Best "Strong Buy" Stocks to Buy Now During Q3 Earnings Season
html_content:
The bulls started buying again on Monday as third-quarter earnings season starts to ramp up, with reports out from Meta, Tesla, and others in the coming days.

No matter what happens this week, the world’s largest semiconductor maker and one of the most important companies in the world, Taiwan Semiconductor, reported a strong beat-and-raise Q3 on October 15. TSMC physically builds and manufactures almost all the cutting-edge semiconductors for Nvidia and most other AI giants.

Taiwan Semi upped its guidance, citing “continued strong demand for our leading-edge process technologies, including the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology.” This backdrop signals that the AI spending boom remains full steam ahead, at least for the biggest and most important players in the industry.

Looking at the full year, total S&P 500 earnings are expected to grow by +28.8% in 2026 on +9.8% higher sales, with growth projected in 15 out of 16 sectors. Better still, S&P 500 earnings are projected to grow another 19.0% in 2027 and 16.9% in 2028.

This backdrop means that investors who can handle some near-term swings might want to buy best-in-class stocks right now as Q3 earnings season heats up.

Let’s explore how investors can use a Zacks screen to help find a handful of the best Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks out of a group of over 200 highly ranked stocks to buy right now and throughout the rest of 2026 and beyond.

Zacks Rank Basics

Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks outperform the market in good and bad times. However, there are over 200 stocks that earn a Zacks Rank #1 at any given time.

Therefore, it’s helpful to understand how to apply filters to the Zacks Rank in order to narrow the list down to a more manageable and tradable set of stocks.

Best "Strong Buy" Stock Screen Parameters

There are only three items on this screen. But together, these three filters can result in some impressive returns.

• Zacks Rank equal to 1

Starting with a Zacks Rank #1 is often a strong jumping off point because it boasts an average annual return of roughly 24.4% per year since 1988.

• % Change (Q1) Est. over 4 Weeks greater than 0

Positive current quarter estimate revisions over the last four weeks.

• % Broker Rating Change over 4 Week equal to Top # 5

Top 5 stocks with the best average broker rating changes over the last four weeks.

This strategy comes loaded with the Research Wizard and is called bt_sow_filtered zacks rank5. It can be found in the SoW (Screen of the Week) folder.

Here is one of the five stocks that qualified for the Filtered Zacks Rank 5 strategy today…

Best "Strong Buy" Stocks to Buy Now: Under-the-Radar Finance Stock SHG

Shinhan Financial Group Co SHG is one of South Korea’s largest banks and financial institutions. It handles everyday banking (checking accounts, savings, and loans), credit cards, stock trading and investment banking, insurance, and money management for both consumers and businesses.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Shinhan Financial benefits from its dominant position in South Korea’s large and stable banking market. On top of that, its wealth management, insurance, and other segments provide upside. It is also expanding outside of South Korea into countries like Vietnam, Japan, India, and beyond.

SHG is projected to expand its revenue by 12% in 2026 and another 8% next year to reach $13.93 billion. The South Korean financial services giant is also expected to grow its adjusted earnings by 33% in FY26 and 12% next year. Plus, Shinhan Financial’s earnings outlook has jumped since its last report, with its upward EPS revisions earning it a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The stock has climbed 105% in the last five years to blow away the Zacks Finance sector’s 44%. SHG is up 35% in the past 12 months to outpace its highly ranked Banks – Foreign industry, which is in the top 23% of roughly 250% Zacks industries.

Investors can buy Shinhan Financial down 18% from its early September highs, while its average Zacks price target implies 41% upside. 

The dividend-paying stock is attempting to find support right now at its 200-day moving average. Shinhan Financial is also trading at its most oversold RSI levels in the last 12 months.

headline: Top Stock Reports for SAP, Accenture & Moody's
html_content:
Tuesday, October 20, 2026

The Zacks Research Daily presents the best research output of our analyst team. Today's Research Daily features new research reports on 12 major stocks, including SAP SE (SAP), Accenture plc (ACN) and Moody's Corp. (MCO), as well as a micro-cap stock Peoples Bancorp of North Carolina, Inc. (PEBK). The Zacks microcap research is unique as our research content on these small and under-the-radar companies is the only research of its type in the country.

These research reports have been hand-picked from the roughly 70 reports published by our analyst team today.

You can see all of today’s research reports here >>>

Ahead of Wall Street

The daily 'Ahead of Wall Street' article is a must-read for all investors who would like to be ready for that day's trading action. The article comes out before the market opens, attempting to make sense of that morning's economic releases and how they will affect that day's market action. You can read this article for free on our home page and can actually sign up there to get an email notification as this article comes out each morning.

You can read today's AWS here >>> Pre-Markets Down, Housing Remains at Recessionary Levels

Today's Featured Research Reports

Shares of SAP have underperformed the Zacks Computer - Software industry over the past year (-18.4% vs. -9.1%). The company lowered its non-IFRS operating profit outlook to €11.8-€12.2 billion, reflecting a more than €100 million impact from the Dremio and Prior Labs acquisitions. Geopolitical risks in the Middle East remain a potential headwind.

Nevertheless, AI strategy is strengthening SAP's competitive edge, despite broader macro uncertainty. More than 90% of SAP's 50 largest deals include AI and SAP BDC, indicating a strong second-half outlook. Indirect channel is outperforming the direct cloud business, reflecting the success of its go-to-market transformation. 

New RISE with SAP and GROW with SAP offerings gained traction, driven by the adoption of its AI-led ERP migration toolchain. SAP announced a €10 billion share buyback through 2027. Following the Sapphire event, Suite and Joule Work saw oversubscribed beta demand, reinforcing confidence in its third-quarter launch.

(You can read the full research report on SAP here >>>)

Accenture’s shares have declined -2.1% over the past year against the Zacks Computers - IT Services industry’s decline of -15.5%. The company’s discretionary spending remains vulnerable to economic uncertainty and pricing competition. AI-driven efficiencies are reshaping delivery models and workforce needs. 

Elevated acquisition spending and financing costs add execution risk, while federal contracting remains sensitive to policy changes despite a recent recovery. These opportunities and risks support a Neutral recommendation.

Nevertheless, Accenture’s investments in AI, cloud, data and cybersecurity support growing demand for enterprise transformation. Large-deal bookings and recurring Managed Services revenue improve revenue visibility and client reach, while acquisitions expand capabilities. Healthy free cash flow supports investment and shareholder returns. 

(You can read the full research report on Accenture here >>>)

Shares of Moody's have outperformed the Zacks Financial - Miscellaneous Services industry over the past year (+0.2% vs. -27.2%). The company’s earnings have beaten the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters. It benefits from a leading credit-ratings franchise, recurring analytics revenue and broader workflow integration. 

Healthy issuances and growing demand for decision-grade intelligence will likely drive revenues. Portfolio simplification and restructuring will improve efficiency, while cash generation is likely to support continued capital returns. 

Still, the ratings business remains sensitive to capital-market activity and revenue mix, which can make growth uneven. Investment in technology, product development and sales keeps expenses elevated, while the expanded restructuring program adds near-term cash costs. Competition across ratings, data and workflow tools requires sustained execution.

(You can read the full research report on Moody's here >>>)

Peoples Bancorp of North Carolina's shares have outperformed the Zacks Banks - Southeast industry over the past year (+43% vs. +15.6%). This microcap company with a market capitalization of $239.68 million has an investment case supported by margin expansion, loan growth, a stronger deposit mix and ample liquidity. 

Lower funding costs and continued lending activity are supporting net interest income, while a predominantly core-deposit base provides funding stability. Sound capital preserves flexibility for growth and credit needs. However, faster loan expansion has increased provisioning, non-performing assets have edged higher and real estate exposure warrants monitoring. 

Softer appraisal activity continues to pressure fee income, while rising operating costs have constrained profitability gains. Interest-rate shifts and securities valuation losses also remain risks. The valuation presents a balanced picture, suggesting some upside if operating momentum strengthens, though current pricing leaves less margin of safety should earnings or credit trends weaken.

(You can read the full research report on Peoples Bancorp of North Carolina here >>>)

Other noteworthy reports we are featuring today include Nucor Corp. (NUE), Tenet Healthcare Corp. (THC) and Toast, Inc. (TOST).

Mark Vickery
Senior Editor

Note: Sheraz Mian heads the Zacks Equity Research department and is a well-regarded expert of aggregate earnings. He is frequently quoted in the print and electronic media and publishes the weekly Earnings Trends and Earnings Preview reports. If you want an email notification each time Sheraz publishes a new article, please click here>>>

Today's Must Read

SAP Banks on Cloud & AI Strength Amid Global Macro Volatility

AI Demand Aids Accenture (ACN), but M&A Execution Risks Prevail

Bond Issuances, Expansion Efforts Aid Moody's (MCO), Higher Costs Ail

Featured Reports

Tenet (THC) to Gain From USPI Strength & Strategic Acquisitions.
Per the Zacks analyst, rising surgical volumes in Tenet Healthcare's USPI business and acquisitions will support growth. However, rising expenses and unfavorable payer-mix trends remain concerns.

AI Tools and Market Expansion Aid Toast (TOST), but Growth Risks Mount
Per the Zacks analyst, Toast benefits from AI-driven tools, market expansion and improving margins. However, slowing growth, hardware costs and continued AI reinvestment could constrain profitability.

The Trade Desk's CTV and AI Prospects Face Macro Headwinds
Per the Zacks analyst, The Trade Desk's CTV, retail and international expansion support long-term opportunities, but slowing revenue growth, macro pressure, and investments remain concerns.

Strong Loan Growth Aid Upstart (UPST), Macro and Execution Risks Loom
Per the Zacks analyst, Upstart benefits from stronger funding, loan growth and improving margins. However, macro uncertainty, rising fixed costs and capital-market dependence remain key risks.

AMN Healthcare (AMN) Gains on Staffing Growth Despite Pricing Pressure
Per the Zacks analyst, rising staffing volumes and MSP scale support AMN Healthcare's growth. However, pricing pressure, intense competition and weak segment performance may limit growth.

New Upgrades

Robust Demand, Capacity Growth and Higher Pricing Aid Nucor (NUE)

headline: Invest in 2 Madison Mutual Funds for Long-Term Growth
html_content:
Madison Investments is an employee-owned, independent investment management firm. The firm offers a range of actively managed investment strategies across equities, fixed-income and asset allocation. All of the investment portfolios are managed based on a disciplined investment approach which emphasizes fundamental research, quality investments and negative outright returns during periods of market decline.

The company’s “Participate & Protect” investment philosophy aims to increase value during market upswings while minimizing potential losses during market declines. Equity investments are selected with a view to their investment potential, rather than to the replication of an index. Fixed-income investments and credit analysis are examined on a fundamental basis. Asset allocation is flexible and designed to reflect current market conditions. All these factors make it a viable investment option.

We have picked two Madison mutual funds – Madison Small Cap BVAOX and Madison Small Cap MSCIX – which investors should buy now for the long term. These funds have a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or Rank 2 (Buy), with positive three-year and five-year annualized returns, minimum initial investments within $5000 and expense ratios considerably lower than the category average. So, these funds have provided comparatively stronger performance and carry a lower fee. 

Madison Small Cap fund invests in U.S. small-cap companies that the advisors believe are undervalued and have potential for capital appreciation.

Faraz Farzam has been the lead manager of BVAOX since Jan. 29, 2010. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as Encompass Health Corp (4.1%), The Scotts Miracle-Gro Co (3.7%) and Knowles Corp (3.6%) as of April 30, 2026. 

BVAOX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 10.2% and 2%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 1.10%. BVAOX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.                 

To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here. 

Madison Small Cap fund invests, under normal circumstances, not less than 80% of the value of its net assets in a diversified portfolio of equity securities (primarily common stocks) of companies with market capitalizations at the time of purchase under $2 billion.

Aaron Garcia has been the lead manager of MSCIX since Jan. 29, 2010. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as Encompass Health Corp (4.1%), The Scotts Miracle-Gro Co (3.7%) and Knowles Corp (3.6%) as of April 30, 2026.  

MSCIX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 10.3% and 2.1%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.34%. MSCIX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

excerpt: Despite the decline in share price, Vicor stands out as an emerging niche player in the AI buildout.
headline: Bull of the Day: Vicor (VICR)
html_content:
Throughout the AI boom, we have seen a steady stream of niche technology companies emerge as critical players in the infrastructure buildout. What began with GPUs and custom semiconductors has expanded into memory, optical networking, advanced packaging and a growing list of other industries.

While there are certainly still opportunities across those segments, I am particularly interested in identifying the next wave of beneficiaries. One emerging opportunity is in power delivery, as AI data centers are beginning to fundamentally rethink how electricity gets from the grid to increasingly powerful processors.

The problem is straightforward. AI systems are becoming so powerful and energy-intensive that traditional data center electrical infrastructure is struggling to keep up. Some next-generation server racks are expected to require as much as one megawatt of electricity, creating enormous challenges in efficiently delivering that power without wasting energy, generating excess heat or consuming valuable space.

To address these challenges, the industry is moving toward a new 800-volt direct current (DC) power architecture, which allows electricity to travel through data centers more efficiently and with fewer conversion steps.

Vicor (VICR) develops highly efficient power conversion modules that help deliver electricity at the precise voltage required by advanced processors. Its technology becomes increasingly valuable as AI chips demand more power in less space, positioning the company to benefit from the industry's shift toward higher-density computing.

The company also carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), supported by an increasingly bullish earnings outlook.

Adding to the investment case, Vicor reported outstanding quarterly results Tuesday morning, with revenue surging nearly 79% year over year and profitability improving dramatically. Shares rallied following the announcement, reinforcing the company's accelerating fundamental momentum.

Despite a powerful rally earlier this year, VICR has since undergone a sharp correction and remains roughly 46% below its previous highs. With an emerging industry tailwind, exceptional growth forecasts and a top Zacks Rank, Vicor stands out as a compelling opportunity in the next phase of the AI infrastructure buildout.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Vicor Shares Rally Following Strong Earnings Results

Vicor delivered an exceptional third-quarter earnings report Tuesday morning, with accelerating revenue growth, expanding profitability and surging demand for its advanced power technologies.

Revenue climbed 78.5% year over year to $197.1 million, representing a 37.5% sequential increase. Earnings per share more than doubled from $0.63 a year ago to $1.33, while gross margins expanded to 68.3%, compared with 57.5% in the year-ago quarter.

Another particularly encouraging development was the company's rapidly expanding order backlog, which reached $406 million, up 166% from $153 million a year earlier. This provides greater visibility into future revenue and reinforces the strength of underlying demand.

Vicor is also benefiting from a growing licensing business, which allows the company to collect royalties on its patented power delivery technologies. Royalty revenue reached $66.6 million during the quarter, more than tripling from a year earlier. This represents an attractive additional revenue stream, although licensing activity can create considerable variability in quarterly results.

The outlook is equally impressive. Consensus forecasts call for revenue growth of 41% this year and another 61% next year. Earnings per share are projected to climb 56.3% this year, followed by another 64.1% increase next year.

These exceptional growth forecasts, alongside favorable earnings estimate revisions, have earned Vicor a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Valuation is certainly a consideration, with shares trading at 46.8x forward earnings. That is a substantial premium, but given the company's accelerating growth, expanding margins and exposure to a potentially transformative industry trend, the multiple is not necessarily unreasonable.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Should Investors Buy Shares in VICR?

Vicor offers exposure to one of the more interesting emerging opportunities within the AI infrastructure boom. As computing power continues to increase, the ability to deliver electricity efficiently is becoming a critical challenge, and Vicor is well positioned to benefit.

The company's latest earnings results suggest that this opportunity is already translating into meaningful business growth. Surging revenue, expanding margins, a rapidly growing backlog and bullish earnings revisions all support the investment case.

Of course, the stock is not without risk. Its premium valuation leaves little room for disappointment, while competition, customer adoption and the timing of next-generation power architectures could all influence future results. The stock's sharp correction from its highs also illustrates how volatile expectations can become.

Nevertheless, I find the combination of an emerging secular growth catalyst, exceptional earnings momentum and a top Zacks Rank particularly compelling. For investors comfortable with the risks of a high-growth technology stock, VICR looks like an attractive way to participate in the next phase of the AI infrastructure buildout.

headline: Should iShares Russell Top 200 ETF (IWL) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
The iShares Russell Top 200 ETF (IWL) was launched on September 22, 2009, and is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Large Cap Blend segment of the US equity market.

The fund is sponsored by Blackrock. It has amassed assets over $2.25 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Blend segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Blend

Companies that find themselves in the large cap category typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Considered a more stable option, large cap companies boast more predictable cash flows and are less volatile than their mid and small cap counterparts.

Typically holding a combination of both growth and value stocks, blend ETFs also demonstrate qualities seen in value and growth investments.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.15%, making it one of the cheaper products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.84%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

It is important to delve into an ETF's holdings before investing despite the many upsides to these kinds of funds like diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Information Technology sector -- about 41.1% of the portfolio. Financials and Telecom round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Nvidia (NVDA) accounts for about 9.33% of total assets, followed by Apple (AAPL) and Microsoft (MSFT).

The top 10 holdings account for about 44.58% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

IWL seeks to match the performance of the Russell Top 200 Index before fees and expenses. The Russell Top 200 Index is a float-adjusted, capitalization-weighted index that measures the performance of the largest capitalization sector of the U.S. equity market.

The ETF has added about 12.66% so far this year and it's up approximately 14.9% in the last one year (as of 10/21/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $156.00 and $194.43.

The ETF has a beta of 1.01 and standard deviation of 15.08% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 205 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

iShares Russell Top 200 ETF carries a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Thus, IWL is a sufficient option for those seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Blend area of the market. Investors might also want to consider some other ETF options in the space.

The iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV) and the Vanguard 500 Index Fund ETF Shares (VOO) track a similar index. While iShares Core S&P 500 ETF has $885.48 billion in assets, Vanguard 500 Index Fund ETF Shares has $1,040.30 billion. IVV has an expense ratio of 0.03% and VOO charges 0.03%.

Bottom-Line

While an excellent vehicle for long term investors, passively managed ETFs are a popular choice among institutional and retail investors due to their low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency.

To learn more about this product and other ETFs, screen for products that match your investment objectives and read articles on latest developments in the ETF investing universe, please visit Zacks ETF Center.

excerpt: The most favorable nine-month stretch of the four-year presidential cycle opened this month.
headline: Don't Get Spooked: Stocks Could Still Soar in Q4
html_content:
October has been known for its volatility.

We certainly saw that play out in the first half of this month. The VIX index hit a four-month high as inflation measures came in above expectations. Last week delivered two hot inflation prints — CPI on Wednesday and PPI on Thursday, the latter the largest annual wholesale increase since 2022 — and the bond market's response evolved in real time.

Meanwhile, the AI financing debate remained front and center. CoreWeave, carrying roughly $50 billion in debt, fell painfully last week and has become the market's chosen proxy for the question. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — whose company holds about a 10% stake in CoreWeave — found it necessary to state publicly that CoreWeave's financial strength is improving and that Nvidia does not need to backstop it.

Two things happened in the first half of October that look like they contradict each other. The market's most crowded theme shed more than a trillion dollars of value in five sessions. And the most favorable nine-month stretch of the four-year presidential cycle opened on October 1st.

Both are true. Reconciling them is the work.

What Actually Happened Last Week

The headline numbers were ugly enough. The Nasdaq fell roughly 4.5% on the week, its worst showing since late June. Friday alone took the Nasdaq down 2.14% and the S&P 500 down 1.09%, with nearly two-thirds of U.S. issues declining. The semiconductor index extended its losing streak to an eighth consecutive session.

Now look at the Dow DIA, which gained about 0.7% on the week and finished Friday above 52,000. That divergence is the entire story. Energy rose 2.5% on Friday to lead all sectors as crude approached $100, while health care and staples absorbed flows as well.

When investors are genuinely frightened, they go to cash and Treasuries. They didn't. They moved down the risk curve inside equities and stayed there. That is a correction in a theme rather than a correction in the market, and the distinction matters a great deal for how you position into the rest of the year.

The Calendar Turned in October

Into that noise, the seasonal backdrop quietly became as good as it gets.

Jeffrey Hirsch, who carries on his father's work at the Stock Trader’s Almanac, defines the most favorable stretch of the entire cycle as the nine months running from the fourth quarter of a midterm year through the second quarter of the following pre-election year. We entered that window on October 1st.

The contrast with the stretch immediately preceding it is stark. Over the weak span from the second through third quarters of midterm years, the Dow has averaged a 2.0% drop, the S&P 500 a 2.5% pullback, and the Nasdaq a 6.6% decline. Over the sweet spot that follows, those same three indexes have averaged gains of 19.3%, 20.2% and 29.4%:


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research. Data via Stock Trader's Almanac

Simply put: this quarter, and the next two, are the three strongest out of the entire four-year presidential cycle. The fourth quarter on its own has historically been the best quarter of the year, higher more than 80% of the time with an average gain north of 4%.

Four years ago, this same window opened from the wreckage of a bear market, just weeks ahead of the October 2022 bottom. Valuations had reset and sentiment was washed out. This time we enter it near record highs, with the ten-year above 5% and core inflation accelerating after two hot prints last week.

So, while seasonality improves the odds, it does not remove the risk. Stocks can certainly go up from here and there are reasons to be optimistic. But the cycle is being asked to deliver its best stretch from a much different starting point rather than a cheap one.

Hirsch addresses this directly, and his answer is that a strong starting point does not cancel the pattern. He also makes a second argument worth weighing: his father identified a “super boom” dynamic in which markets surge following war, inflation and heavy government spending alongside a transformative technology.

He sees artificial intelligence fitting that description, and notes that the late-1990s technology boom overrode the four-year cycle entirely. A powerful enough secular force can swamp a seasonal one.

Bottom Line

The good news is that we do not have to speculate for long. Nearly 80 S&P 500 members report this week, bringing the season to roughly a quarter of the index. Meta and Tesla report this evening.

The aggregate picture is strong but concentrated. Our Director of Research Sheraz Mian has the S&P 500 tracking 24.6% earnings growth on 11.7% higher revenues — an eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with fourteen of sixteen sectors expanding.

The evidence arrives this week. Let the seasonality set your posture. Let the earnings set your conviction.

excerpt: 3M raises its 2026 earnings outlook as AI infrastructure partnerships, strong industrial orders and productivity gains fuel growth and further margin expansion.
headline: MMM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Deals and Higher Outlook
html_content:
3M Company MMM emphasized stronger industrial demand, expanding data center opportunities and continued productivity improvements during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management also raised its full-year earnings outlook while outlining expectations for further margin expansion.

The discussion centered on the company's Artificial Intelligence infrastructure partnerships, improving order trends and ability to offset inflation through pricing. Executives also addressed weakness in consumer electronics and the execution requirements surrounding new optical technologies.


3M Raises 2026 Earnings Outlook

Chief financial officer Anurag Maheshwari raised full-year adjusted earnings guidance to $9.10-$9.15 per share from $8.95-$9.10 on the updated reporting basis.

 

3M Company Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

3M Company price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | 3M Company Quote

Management maintained expectations for adjusted organic sales growth exceeding 3.5%, supported by fourth-quarter growth above 4%. Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance remained approximately $4.8 billion.

The outlook followed adjusted earnings of $2.50 per share, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.40 by 4.20%. Revenues of $6.58 billion missed the consensus estimate of $6.61 billion by 0.40%.

MMM Expands AI Infrastructure Partnerships

Chief executive officer William Brown highlighted an expanded commercial relationship with Amazon involving optical connectivity and other data center products.

Under the agreement, Amazon received warrants to purchase up to 3.2 million 3M shares, tied to $6 billion in cumulative sales over seven years and other milestones.

During questioning from Wolfe Research, Brown clarified that the arrangement carries no minimum volume commitments. He projected expanded beam optics revenues of approximately $40 million in 2026 and $80-$100 million in 2027.

3M Targets Further Margin Expansion

Maheshwari attributed third-quarter adjusted operating margin expansion of 110 basis points to 26.2% primarily to supply-chain productivity, procurement savings and operating improvements.

He said the company expects its 2027 operating margin to exceed the updated Investor Day target of 25.4%. Volume-related incremental margins are approaching 40%.

Responding to JPMorgan's questions, Maheshwari emphasized that margin improvements reflected structural operating changes rather than one-time benefits. Brown added that manufacturing consolidation should contribute more meaningfully beginning in 2028.

MMM Sees Industrial Orders Supporting Growth

Maheshwari reported high-single-digit order growth and high-teens backlog expansion, reflecting strength across industrial, safety, semiconductor and aerospace markets.

Safety and Industrial delivered 7% organic growth, while Transportation and Electronics advanced 0.5%. Consumer sales remained flat amid retailer inventory adjustments.

During Wells Fargo's questioning, Brown indicated that approximately 25% of fourth-quarter revenues were covered by backlog. He emphasized favorable order trends and easier comparisons supporting the company's year-end growth expectations.

3M Advances Optical Capacity and Innovation

Brown discussed a manufacturing partnership with Genius Electronic Optical, accompanied by a 4.7% equity investment, to expand production capacity for expanded beam optics technology.

The company also continues collaborating with Microsoft on optical connectivity deployment. Brown emphasized that manufacturing scale, industry standards and diversified supply remain essential to broader hyperscaler adoption.

Beyond optical technology, 3M introduced 87 products during the quarter, up 24%. Brown expects launches to exceed 350 during 2026, supported by faster development cycles and Artificial Intelligence tools.

MMM Addresses Consumer Market Weakness

Brown acknowledged continued pressure in consumer electronics, particularly LCD displays and Chinese device manufacturers. The segment's demand environment remains challenging entering the fourth quarter.

Responding to Deutsche Bank, he highlighted opportunities involving premium devices, thermal management and foldable technology. Management expects innovation to support renewed growth in 2027.

In the Consumer business, U.S. point-of-sale growth exceeded 2%, although retailer destocking constrained shipments. Brown expects modest improvement as channel inventories stabilize.

3M Maintains Focus on Execution

Management's overall tone remained confident, emphasizing commercial execution, manufacturing productivity and innovation as the principal drivers of sustainable growth.

Brown and Maheshwari maintained that pricing discipline should offset additional oil-related inflation while operational transformation supports future profitability. Execution on optical technology partnerships and recovery across weaker consumer markets remain important priorities.

What MMM's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

MMM currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), indicating a neutral near-term earnings estimate revision outlook. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Its Value Score of C, Growth Score of B and Momentum Score of F reflect relatively stronger growth characteristics alongside weaker price momentum.

The stock's VGM Score of C represents a middle-range combined assessment of value, growth and momentum. Although its Growth Score is favorable, the weaker Momentum Score limits the overall profile. The Zacks Rank may change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest quarterly results.

During questioning from Wolfe Research, Brown clarified that the arrangement carries no minimum volume commitments. He projected expanded beam optics revenues of approximately $40 million in 2026 and $80-$100 million in 2027. 3M Targets Further Margin Expansion Maheshwari attributed third-quarter adjusted operating margin expansion of 110 basis points to 26.2% primarily to supply-chain productivity, procurement savings and operating improvements. He said the company expects its 2027 operating margin to exceed the updated Investor Day target of 25.4%. Volume-related incremental margins are approaching 40%. Responding to JPMorgan's questions, Maheshwari emphasized that margin improvements reflected structural operating changes rather than one-time benefits. Brown added that manufacturing consolidation should contribute more meaningfully beginning in 2028. MMM Sees Industrial Orders Supporting Growth Maheshwari reported high-single-digit order growth and high-teens backlog expansion, reflecting strength across industrial, safety, semiconductor and aerospace markets. Safety and Industrial delivered 7% organic growth, while Transportation and Electronics advanced 0.5%. Consumer sales remained flat amid retailer inventory adjustments. During Wells Fargo's questioning, Brown indicated that approximately 25% of fourth-quarter revenues were covered by backlog. He emphasized favorable order trends and easier comparisons supporting the company's year-end growth expectations. 3M Advances Optical Capacity and Innovation Brown discussed a manufacturing partnership with Genius Electronic Optical, accompanied by a 4.7% equity investment, to expand production capacity for expanded beam optics technology. The company also continues collaborating with Microsoft on optical connectivity deployment. Brown emphasized that manufacturing scale, industry standards and diversified supply remain essential to broader hyperscaler adoption. Beyond optical technology, 3M introduced 87 products during the quarter, up 24%. Brown expects launches to exceed 350 during 2026, supported by faster development cycles and Artificial Intelligence tools. MMM Addresses Consumer Market Weakness Brown acknowledged continued pressure in consumer electronics, particularly LCD displays and Chinese device manufacturers. The segment's demand environment remains challenging entering the fourth quarter. Responding to Deutsche Bank, he highlighted opportunities involving premium devices, thermal management and foldable technology. Management expects innovation to support renewed growth in 2027. In the Consumer business, U.S. point-of-sale growth exceeded 2%, although retailer destocking constrained shipments. Brown expects modest improvement as channel inventories stabilize. 3M Maintains Focus on Execution Management's overall tone remained confident, emphasizing commercial execution, manufacturing productivity and innovation as the principal drivers of sustainable growth. Brown and Maheshwari maintained that pricing discipline should offset additional oil-related inflation while operational transformation supports future profitability. Execution on optical technology partnerships and recovery across weaker consumer markets remain important priorities. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. Its Value Score of C, Growth Score of B and Momentum Score of F reflect relatively stronger growth characteristics alongside weaker price momentum. The stock's VGM Score of C represents a middle-range combined assessment of value, growth and momentum. Although its Growth Score is favorable, the weaker Momentum Score limits the overall profile. excerpt: Senior-housing occupancy reached 90.4% as limited construction and aging demographics create opportunities for Welltower, CareTrust REIT and LTC Properties.
headline: Aging Population Boosts Healthcare REITs: Stocks to Watch
html_content:
An updated edition of the Aug. 31, 2026 article.

The U.S. senior-housing market is showing signs of a structural recovery as rising occupancy, limited new construction and growing demand for specialized care reshape the healthcare real estate landscape. For investors, this creates an opportunity to look beyond traditional healthcare stocks and consider real estate investment trusts (REITs) that own or operate senior-living communities, assisted-living facilities and skilled-nursing properties.

The latest industry data support this shift. According to the National Investment Center for Seniors Housing & Care (NIC) report, senior-housing occupancy reached 90.4% in the third quarter of 2026, extending its recovery for a 21st consecutive quarter. Meanwhile, constrained construction activity has limited the addition of new inventory, potentially strengthening the pricing power of established properties in markets where demand is rising.

The longer-term opportunity is underpinned by population aging. The U.S. Census Bureau's August 2026 report projects that people aged 65 and older will account for 19.6% of the global population by 2060 compared with 10.5% in 2025. This shift is expected to increase the need for age-appropriate housing and a range of healthcare services.

However, the investment case is not without risks. Financing costs, labor expenses, operator credit quality and property valuations can influence returns even when underlying demand remains strong. Against this backdrop, Welltower WELL, CareTrust REIT CTRE and LTC Properties LTC offer distinct ways to participate in the senior-housing and healthcare real estate opportunity.

Healthcare REITs

Healthcare REITs own or finance senior-housing communities, skilled-nursing facilities, assisted-living centers and other healthcare properties. They generate income through rents, property operations or financing arrangements, with performance driven by occupancy, rental growth, operating costs, tenant quality and borrowing expenses.

According to the NIC, senior-housing occupancy reached 90.4% in the third quarter of 2026, with independent-living occupancy at 91.7% and assisted-living occupancy at 89.1%. Limited construction has further supported existing properties. NIC reported just 0.4% year-over-year inventory growth in the second quarter, with fewer than 16,000 units under construction.

However, higher financing costs, labor inflation, maintenance expenses and tenant credit risks remain important challenges. Investors should focus on REITs capable of converting improving occupancy and rental growth into sustainable funds from operations (FFO) and dividend payments.

Operators and Care-Focused REITs

Senior-care operators and healthcare REITs offer different ways to capitalize on aging demographics. The Ensign Group ENSG operates skilled-nursing, rehabilitation and senior-living facilities, making its results sensitive to patient volumes, reimbursement rates and staffing costs.

In contrast, Omega Healthcare Investors OHI and CareTrust REIT primarily own healthcare properties leased to independent operators. Their performance depends on rent collection, tenant financial health, lease structures and financing costs.

Growing demand for assisted living, memory care, rehabilitation and long-term care supports the sector's long-term outlook. Nevertheless, affordability constraints, staffing shortages and regulatory risks make financial discipline and asset quality essential to investment success.

3 Seniors & Aging Demographics Stocks in the Spotlight

Welltower: Welltower is one of the largest healthcare REITs, with senior housing, post-acute care and outpatient medical properties across the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. Its senior-housing operating portfolio includes independent-living, assisted-living and memory-care communities.

WELL reported strong second-quarter 2026 results, supported by occupancy gains, rental growth and improved operating performance. According to the company's July 27 earnings release, normalized FFO increased 25% year over year to $1.60 per diluted share. Total portfolio same-store net operating income (NOI) grew 15.5%, while same-store NOI in its Seniors Housing Operating portfolio advanced 20.5%. Organic same-store revenue in that portfolio increased 9.2%, supported by 330 basis points of average occupancy growth and 5.2% growth in revenue per occupied room. Welltower also reported that $15.5 billion of pro rata gross investments had been completed or were under contract as of its second-quarter announcement, including transactions completed after quarter-end.

These figures indicate the company’s emphasis on expanding its senior-housing platform. Continued occupancy gains and pricing power could support further operating growth, although investors should assess acquisition pricing, financing requirements and the valuation already reflected in the shares. Welltower carried a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

CareTrust: CareTrust REIT is a self-administered healthcare REIT that owns skilled-nursing facilities, assisted-living communities and other healthcare-related properties. It leases these assets to independent operators under long-term agreements, generating rental income from essential care infrastructure.

CTRE's second-quarter 2026 results highlighted growth in its investment portfolio and funds from operations. In its August 2026 earnings release, the company reported net income of 38 cents per share and normalized FFO of 51 cents per share. Normalized FFO per share increased 19% year over year. CareTrust also reported approximately $899.6 million of investment activity completed during the quarter at a blended stabilized yield of 8.9%.

The company increased its full-year 2026 guidance, reflecting its investment activity and operating outlook. CareTrust carries a Zacks Rank #2 at present.

LTC Properties: LTC Properties invests primarily in seniors housing and healthcare properties in the United States, including assisted-living communities, memory-care facilities, independent-living communities and skilled-nursing centers. The company uses a combination of property investments, leases and financing arrangements to generate income.

LTC's last-reported second-quarter 2026 results reflected its ongoing shift toward a larger seniors-housing operating platform. According to its Aug. 5 earnings release, total revenue rose to $98.9 million from $60.2 million a year earlier, while core FFO was 68 cents per share, unchanged year over year.

The strategy could give LTC greater direct exposure to occupancy improvements and revenue growth across senior-housing communities. The stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

headline: These 3 Stocks Surged Following Strong Quarterly Results
html_content:
The Q3 earnings cycle continues to roll along, with several companies – Accenture ACN, Hasbro HAS, and MSCI MSCI – seeing positive reactions following their releases.

Accenture Reports Solid Growth

Accenture delivered a solid quarterly release, with revenue climbing 6% YoY to $18.7 billion and exceeding the high end of management's prior guidance. Adjusted earnings of $3.29 per share similarly reflected positivity, up 9% from the year-ago period.

New bookings reached $22.2 billion, and the company secured 141 client bookings valued at $100 million or more during the period. The results helped ease concerns surrounding AI-related fears that have weighed on many software-related stocks.

Shares are still lagging relative to the S&P 500 in 2026, though the recent post-earnings climb reflects a stark difference compared to its recent release.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Hasbro's Magic Momentum 

Hasbro similarly posted strong quarterly results, with revenue climbing 15% YoY to roughly $1.6 billion and adjusted earnings totaling $2.90 per share, comfortably exceeding expectations.

The Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment led the strong performance, with revenue jumping 31% YoY. Magic: The Gathering remained the biggest highlight, with quarterly sales surpassing $600 million for the first time and up 34% YoY.

Given the strong results, management raised its FY26 revenue growth outlook and increased its adjusted EBITDA guidance. Shares are now up more than 30% in 2026, with the recent release reflecting the second consecutive post-earnings pop.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

MSCI Reports Record Results

MSCI posted adjusted earnings of $5.11 per share and revenue of $892 million, growing 14% and 12% YoY, respectively. Both items exceeded our consensus estimates, reflecting another double-beat for the company.

The company's Index segment was a major bright spot, with revenue climbing 18% YoY to $532.6 million. Asset-based fees jumped nearly 25%, and the company also reported record recurring net-new sales in its Analytics and Private Capital Solutions businesses, further highlighting strong demand for its offerings.

MSCI shares have largely traded sideways throughout 2026, underperforming relative to the S&P 500 by a wide margin. That said, the favorable release could be what’s needed to keep its near-term momentum intact and finally break it out of its back-and-forth nature.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Bottom Line

The Q3 earnings cycle continues to roll along, with Accenture ACN, Hasbro HAS, and MSCI MSCI all enjoying favorable post-earnings reactions.

Accenture's healthy bookings help support its growth outlook, while Hasbro's continued Magic momentum has led to raised guidance. MSCI's results were similarly constructive, with record asset-based fees and healthy subscription trends reflecting continued demand for its offerings.

excerpt: Zoetis offers diversification and stability, while ImmuCell boasts stronger sales growth and expansion potential.
headline: ZTS vs. ICCC: Which Animal Health Stock Is the Better Investment Bet?
html_content:
Zoetis Inc. ZTS and ImmuCell Corporation ICCC operate in the animal health industry but present distinctly different investment opportunities. While Zoetis benefits from an extensive portfolio of veterinary medicines, vaccines and diagnostics across companion animals and livestock, ImmuCell concentrates on preventive health products for newborn calves.

Let us examine how ZTS and ICCC compare across the factors that could influence their investment prospects.

The Case for ZTS

Diversified Portfolio Offers Resilience: Zoetis benefits from a broad animal health portfolio spanning companion animal therapeutics, livestock products and diagnostics. In the second quarter of 2026, livestock revenues grew 11% year over year on an organic operational basis, supported by strong cattle and poultry demand, while companion animal diagnostics advanced 12%. International revenues increased 6%, partially offsetting a 7% decline in U.S. revenues.

This diversification helps reduce the dependence on individual products and markets. However, consolidated organic operational revenues declined 1%, indicating that strength in livestock and diagnostics has not fully compensated for weaker companion animal demand.

Innovation Supports Long-Term Opportunities: Zoetis continues expanding its product portfolio through new therapies and diagnostic technologies. The launches of Lenivia and Portela in Canada and the European Union during 2026 broadened its osteoarthritis treatment offerings for dogs and cats.

International osteoarthritis pain monoclonal antibody revenues increased 7% in the second quarter, supported by these launches. The company also expects potential U.S. approval of long-acting Cytopoint during 2026 and commercial validation of its Vetscan OmniMax chemistry platform by year-end. These developments could support growth, although successful commercialization and customer adoption remain essential.

Companion Animal Weakness Remains Concerning: Zoetis continues to face fewer veterinary clinic visits, affordability pressures and aggressive promotional competition. Its key dermatology franchise revenues declined 16% organically in the second quarter of 2026, while its U.S. in-clinic dermatology market share fell five percentage points sequentially to approximately 86%.

The company reduced its 2026 revenue outlook to $9.12-$9.32 billion, implying an organic operational decline of 1-3%. Adjusted earnings per share are projected at $6.15-$6.25. With market conditions showing little stabilization through July, continued competitive pressure could delay recovery.

The Case for ICCC

Strong Product Demand Drives Growth: ImmuCell reported first-half 2026 product sales of $17.5 million, increasing 20.9% from $14.5 million a year earlier. Its flagship Tri-Shield product recorded 25.1% growth, while domestic sales increased 32.5%. Distributor-level product volume growth accelerated from 21% in the first quarter to 28% in the second quarter. These trends reflect improved product availability, increased commercial activity and stronger customer demand.

The company's focus on calf scours prevention provides a defined growth opportunity, although its dependence on a relatively narrow product portfolio increases exposure to changes in demand and manufacturing performance.

Market Share Gains Strengthen Competitive Position: ImmuCell's First Defense portfolio continues to gain traction among U.S. dairy and beef producers. Its share of calves receiving biological scours prevention increased from approximately 15% in December 2025 to 19% by June 2026. Its share of producer spending also rose from around 29% to 38% over the same period.

Higher calf values have strengthened the economic incentive for disease prevention, with management indicating that the value of a day-old calf increased from approximately $400 to $1,700 since 2024. These developments support opportunities for additional market penetration, particularly as more than half of calves remain untreated with biological scours preventatives.

Capacity Expansion Creates Growth Potential: ImmuCell is undertaking an approximately $8-million manufacturing expansion to address historical production constraints and support demand for First Defense. The initial $3.5-million freeze-drying investment is expected to be completed in the first half of 2027, followed by a $4.5-million colostrum processing expansion targeted for the second half.

The company expects these investments to more than triple production capacity and reduce processing times from two to three months to less than one month. Successful execution could improve product availability and manufacturing economics, although expansion costs, equipment installation and process optimization introduce operational risks.

Manufacturing Costs Pressure Margins: Despite healthy sales growth, ImmuCell's second-quarter 2026 gross margin declined to 33.9% from 43.7% a year earlier. Lower manufacturing volumes, material-related scrap and the transfer of former Re-Tain development costs into production expenses contributed to the decline.
