excerpt: Homeowners insurance now costs more than property taxes in roughly two-thirds of U.S. counties. Meredith Margrave explains how rising insurance premiums and property taxes can push up a "fixed" mortgage payment, and six ways to get that payment back under control.
headline: Your Fixed-Rate Mortgage Payment Isn't as Fixed as You Think
html_content:
One of the great things about buying a house with a fixed-rate mortgage is knowing exactly what your monthly housing payment will be for the next 15 or 30 years. No surprise rent hikes. No worrying about interest rates. Just the same predictable payment, month after month, while you steadily build equity in your home.

That's the idea, anyway.

Except your monthly mortgage payment isn't necessarily fixed at all. It's entirely possible for that payment to climb by 40% in just a few years, even if you've never refinanced, borrowed another dime, or made any major changes to your house.

How do I know? Because that's exactly what happened to us.

The Unwelcome Surprise at Our Five-Year Homeownership Anniversary

Last year, my husband, Michael, and I marked five years in our house in the most thrilling way imaginable: We pulled up our very first mortgage statement from 2020 and compared it with our latest one. We wanted to see how much of the loan we'd paid off.

That part was satisfying. The rest was not.

Somehow, the monthly payment on our fixed-rate mortgage that we'd never refinanced had gone up by roughly 40%.

Forty. Percent.

It didn't take long to find the culprit. You see, most mortgage payments have two parts. Principal and interest pay for the house itself, and on a fixed-rate loan, that amount stays the same for the life of the loan. Escrow is money your lender collects each month to pay your property taxes and homeowners insurance for you, and that amount can change every year.

The amount we were paying into escrow had nearly doubled in those five years, going from around $1,000 a month to more than $1,900 a month. Some of the increase came from property taxes, but most of it came from something we'd barely thought about since closing: homeowners insurance.

We hadn't renovated. We hadn't filed a claim. It was the same house we'd bought in 2020. It had simply become a much more expensive house to insure, and as we soon learned, we had plenty of company.

The Part of Your Mortgage That Was Never Fixed

Here's what many homeowners don't realize until it happens to them. Under federal rules, your mortgage servicer must review your escrow account once a year, comparing what it collected from you with what it actually paid out for taxes and insurance. Then it resets your monthly payment for the year ahead.

If your bills went up, that annual review can hit you twice. First, your monthly escrow payment rises to cover the new, higher costs going forward. Second, if last year's bills came in higher than the servicer expected, your account may have run short, and the servicer can ask you to make up the difference, often by spreading the shortfall across your next 12 payments. Servicers are also allowed to keep a cushion of up to two months' worth of escrow payments, and that cushion grows right along with your bills.

That's how a "fixed" mortgage payment can jump by hundreds of dollars in a single year.

When people talk about housing affordability, the conversation usually revolves around home prices and mortgage rates. Homeowners who locked in a low rate years ago often assume they've insulated themselves from at least one major household expense. But every extra dollar flowing into escrow is a dollar that can't go toward retirement savings, college funds, or a little breathing room in the family budget. And unlike a pricey streaming subscription, homeowners insurance isn't something you can just cancel. Mortgage lenders typically require it, and going without adequate coverage could expose you to a financially devastating loss.

And this can all happen without you doing anything "wrong." You don't have to refinance, renovate, or file a claim. You just have to own a home while the cost of taxing and insuring it goes up... which is exactly what's happening throughout most of the United States.

Why Insurance Is Doing Most of the Damage

While rising property taxes have historically been the bane of many a homeowner, in much of the country, insurance has suddenly become the bigger bully.

According to a new Bloomberg Intelligence analysis, the average homeowners insurance premium now exceeds the average property tax bill in roughly two-thirds of U.S. counties.

And it isn't just a handful of hurricane-prone coastal communities dealing with the problem. Bloomberg found that average premiums have risen 45% over the past decade after adjusting for inflation, with some of the steepest increases in the Midwest and Mountain West, where hail and severe winter weather have driven up losses. In Nebraska, premiums have climbed an inflation-adjusted 79%.

A Consumer Federation of America report found that the typical homeowner's annual premium rose 24% between December 2021 and August 2024, from $2,655 to $3,303. That's an extra $648 a year, nearly double the rate of inflation over the same period. If you pay through escrow, that works out to about $54 more every month, before any shortfall catch-up. Premiums increased in 95% of U.S. ZIP codes, and in about a third of them, they climbed more than 30%.

No wonder 71% of homeowners told the Pew Research Center this spring that their insurance costs had gone up over the past few years, including 42% who said they'd gone up a lot.

Why is this happening? Your insurer doesn't care what you paid for your house. It cares what it would cost to rebuild it. According to a U.S. Treasury Department report, replacement costs for property and casualty insurance losses rose an average of 45% between 2020 and 2023. Meanwhile, hurricanes, wildfires, hailstorms, and floods are producing bigger and more frequent losses, and those costs don't stay neatly confined to the places where disasters strike. Insurers also buy their own insurance, called reinsurance, to protect against catastrophes, and when that coverage gets more expensive, the cost works its way into everyone's premiums.

So you might have the same roof, the same floor plan, and the same perfectly ordinary house you bought five years ago. The cost of insuring it can still look completely different.

How to Get Your "Fixed" Payment Back Under Control

You can't make escrow go away. But you have more control over what goes into it than you might think.

1. Actually read your escrow analysis

That annual escrow statement is easy to toss, but it tells you exactly why your payment is changing. Look at whether the increase came from taxes, insurance, or a shortage. If there's a shortage, ask your servicer whether you can pay it in a lump sum instead of spreading it across the next year's payments. Federal rules give servicers some flexibility here, and paying it off can keep your monthly bill lower.

And if you switch insurers or win a lower tax bill, make sure your servicer has the new information and recalculates your escrow. Otherwise, you could do all the work of lowering your costs and still be wondering why your mortgage bill hasn't budged.

2. Don't automatically renew your insurance policy

After discovering how much our payment had increased, Michael and I did what any sensible homeowners would do: We complained about it to a friend. Fortunately, this friend happens to be a Realtor, and instead of joining us in our outrage, she offered some useful advice. Shop around.

So we did. And, wouldn't you know it, we found comparable coverage at a substantially lower price. It didn't magically restore our 2020 mortgage payment, but it made a meaningful difference. I just wish we'd done it sooner.

Insurance companies don't all price risk the same way. One might consider your home a relatively expensive risk, while another might offer comparable protection for considerably less. Get quotes from several companies, and consider working with an independent insurance agent who can compare multiple insurers for you. Just make sure you're comparing more than the price. A cheaper policy isn't much of a bargain if it offers substantially less protection.

3. Take a closer look at what your policy actually covers

When was the last time you read your homeowners insurance policy? Not the bill, the actual coverage. Look at your dwelling coverage, how your policy handles replacement costs, and any exclusions or limitations for things like wind, hail, or water damage. Make sure the amount of insurance you carry reflects what it would cost to rebuild your home, not simply its market value. And check whether your policy has a separate wind or hail deductible calculated as a percentage of your home's insured value rather than a flat dollar amount. That can make for a very unpleasant surprise when you file a claim.

4. Ask about discounts

Insurers may offer discounts for bundling your home and auto policies, installing protective devices, or making improvements that reduce the likelihood of damage, such as impact-resistant roofing in hail- or storm-prone areas. Just don't spend thousands of dollars on upgrades without first finding out whether they'll actually save you money.

5. Be careful about raising your deductible

A higher deductible is one common way to lower a premium, and if you have a healthy emergency fund, it might be a reasonable trade-off. But remember what you're doing: You're taking on more financial risk in exchange for a lower annual bill. Saving a few hundred dollars a year may not be worth exposing yourself to thousands of dollars in additional costs after a storm.

6. Challenge your property tax assessment

Insurance isn't the only thing flowing through escrow. If your property tax bill has climbed, check your assessment notice. Local governments generally let homeowners appeal an assessment they believe is too high, though deadlines and procedures vary by location, and the windows can be short. Look for errors in your property record, such as the wrong square footage or number of bathrooms, and compare your assessment with similar homes nearby. Also make sure you're receiving every exemption you qualify for, such as a homestead exemption.

Few people bother. Pete Sepp, president of the National Taxpayers Union, has estimated that only 3% to 5% of homeowners file an appeal, but that 30% to 50% of those who do win some kind of reduction. Keep in mind that an appeal can lower your home's assessed value, not your local tax rate.

What "Fixed" Really Means

I'm still glad Michael and I bought our house when we did. I'm glad we locked in a fixed interest rate. And I'm especially glad we spent that fifth homeownership anniversary marveling at how much progress we'd made on our mortgage, even if our little celebration did come with a rather rude financial awakening.

But the experience changed how I think about our housing costs. A fixed-rate mortgage isn't a promise that your house will cost the same amount every month for the next 30 years. It's a promise that one part of your housing payment will stay the same.

The rest? Well, apparently that's still up for negotiation.

You can't control the weather, the cost of construction materials, or your county's tax rate. But you can compare policies. You can ask questions. You can check your assessment and make sure you're paying for the right coverage at a competitive price.

And if you haven't looked at your escrow statement or your homeowners insurance policy in a few years, take it from someone who learned this lesson the expensive way: It might be worth a few hours of your time.

headline: Forget Lipstick... The Economy's New Warning Sign Might Be a Squishy Dumpling
html_content:
A few weeks ago, I was visiting my husband's office for lunch when I noticed his assistant walking down the hall, casually squeezing... a stick of butter.

At least, what appeared to be a stick of butter.

Naturally, I had questions. She laughed and informed me that it was a squeezable toy that looked (and smelled) just like butter. She called it her "emotional support butter."

Okay, then.

The following week, I noticed that several of the younger associates — mostly in their 20s — had little squishy dumplings sitting on their desks.

Then our nanny stopped by with a bamboo basket's worth of colorful dumplings for the boys. Turns out, they're sold in blind boxes, meaning you don't know which color you're getting until you open the package. She had bought six before finally finding the color she wanted.

Six dumplings. For one color.

Suddenly, I was seeing these things everywhere. When my boys and I stopped into our local comic book store this week, an entire aisle had been overtaken by squishable food — dumplings, butter, pastries, fruits, and all manner of tiny, rubbery things that looked like they belonged in a refrigerator rather than a toy store. Marla, who works behind the counter, told me the hype surrounding new squishy "drops" was unlike anything she'd ever seen.

According to market research firm Circana, Americans spent roughly $297 million on squishy toys in the first half of 2026, about four times what they spent during the same period last year.

Nearly $300 million. On things you squeeze.

The more I thought about this strange little craze, the more I wondered what it was saying about the way people spend their money. Then I saw the University of Michigan's latest consumer sentiment numbers, and it all started to make sense.

Is This the New Lipstick Indicator?

If you follow economic folklore, you've probably heard of the lipstick indicator. The idea is that in times of economic stress, people indulge in small purchases that provide an emotional uplift without breaking the budget.

The idea gained traction when Leonard Lauder, the former chairman of Estée Lauder, observed that his company's lipstick sales rose after the 2001 recession. Over the years, people have nominated other small luxuries as its successor. After the Great Recession, market research firm NPD Group reported that nail polish sales were up 65% since the first half of 2008, and the "nail polish index" was born.

Of course, there's a catch.

The lipstick index isn't an official economic indicator, and it hasn't been particularly reliable. During the 2008 downturn, lipstick sales actually fell 5.8%, according to research firm Kline & Company. And sometimes the next supposedly recession-proof treat turns out to be little more than a passing fad.

Still, I think Lauder was onto something. Maybe not about forecasting the economy, but certainly about understanding people.

Why $300 Million in Squishies Makes Sense Right Now

Consider what's happening with consumer confidence. According to the University of Michigan's preliminary October 2026 survey, its Consumer Sentiment Index fell to 46.3, down from 48.1 in September. The index measuring how Americans feel about current economic conditions dropped to 44.7, a record low.

Americans aren't exactly bubbling over with optimism, and it's not hard to see why. Housing is expensive. Groceries are expensive. Borrowing money is expensive.

That doesn't mean people have stopped spending. It means they're more selective. A $5,000 vacation might get reconsidered. A $50,000 car might get pushed another year.

But a $6 squishy dumpling?

That doesn't require a family budget meeting.

And squishies aren't practical. Their entire purpose is to make you feel good. They're soft, satisfying to squeeze, and, apparently, quite good at offering a tiny bit of stress relief.

I find that particularly interesting. The original lipstick indicator was about feeling better by looking better. A fresh lipstick could make you feel a little more polished, a little more confident, a little more put together.

The squishy craze feels different. It's less about how we present ourselves to the world and more about how we're feeling inside.

In 2026, perhaps we're not looking for a little more glamour.

Perhaps we're looking for something to squeeze while we contemplate the price of eggs.

Add the thrill of the hunt, and these toys become almost irresistible. Thanks to social media, limited releases, and blind boxes, you're not just buying a toy. You're buying the possibility of getting the toy you want.

Maybe you'll get the rare color. Maybe you'll find the one everyone on TikTok is talking about.

Maybe you'll have to buy six.

A Squishy Dumpling Can't Predict a Recession

Before we read too much into all this, let's acknowledge something: Sometimes a popular toy is just a popular toy.

Squishies are cheap, collectible, and practically designed for social media. Five Below, the discount chain whose net sales jumped 32.5% in the first quarter, credited "the overall squishy trend" for part of that strength. But the company had stocked its now-viral dumpling for about five years before it took off online. "We started seeing it pop up in social," CEO Winifred Park told analysts. "What we did was amplify what was becoming hot."

It's also worth looking at who's doing the buying. Circana's data on NeeDoh, the best-known squishy brand, found that 60% of purchasers were parents buying for their children, and kids ages 7 to 12 were the largest group of recipients. A toy mostly bought as a gift for a 9-year-old doesn't fit neatly into a theory about stressed-out adults consoling themselves.

But not everyone is buying for the kids. In the same data, 18.2% of NeeDoh purchasers were buying the toys for themselves. That's nearly one in five, and it's exactly the group I keep noticing. The assistant. The young associates. Our nanny.

So even if this craze tells us nothing about whether a recession is coming, it tells us something about how people respond to financial stress. They don't necessarily stop spending on happiness. They start looking for happiness they can afford. And frankly, that's not a bad instinct. At least, not always.

There's Nothing Wrong With a Little Emotional Support Butter

I'm a personal finance writer. I spend an awful lot of time talking about budgeting, saving, and investing. But I'm also a human being, and sometimes I buy things simply because they make me happy.

Money is a tool. Its purpose isn't exclusively to fund some distant version of your life where you're finally allowed to enjoy yourself. A good financial plan should make room for little pleasures now.

The trouble starts when our little treats become a habit we don't really notice. A $6 dumpling is hardly going to derail your retirement. But six of them? That's $36. Do that every week, and you've spent $1,872 in a year — before counting the coffees, the impulse buys at Target, and everything we added to our Amazon carts because we were bored.

I don't bring this up to make anyone feel guilty. Quite the opposite. Being intentional about these purchases makes them more enjoyable. Here's how I'd approach it.

Give yourself permission to have a little fun money. Whether it's $100 a month or $500, depending on your finances, designate some money that's yours to spend however you please. No guilt. No justification required. It just needs to fit within your larger financial plan.

Pay attention to whether you're buying the thing or chasing the feeling. There's a difference between seeing a squishy dumpling, loving it, and buying it — and buying six blind boxes because you're convinced the next one will finally be the right color. The first is a treat. The second might be an expensive way to chase a little dopamine.

Make sure the things you're buying actually make you happy. How many times have you bought something because it was trendy, only to lose interest almost immediately? The best little luxuries aren't the ones everyone else is buying. They're the ones you genuinely enjoy.

What America's Squishy Obsession Really Tells Us

I have no idea how long the squishy craze will last. Maybe by Christmas, the dumplings will be forgotten at the bottom of our junk drawers. But there's something rather endearing about the people I know who have embraced these ridiculous little toys. We're all trying to navigate a world that feels expensive, unpredictable, and occasionally overwhelming. Sometimes a tiny, squishable piece of pretend food makes the day a little better.

I wouldn't make investment decisions based on the contents of a toy store. But there's a financial lesson hiding beneath all that rubbery nonsense: Being good with money doesn't mean denying yourself every little pleasure. It means knowing which pleasures are worth paying for, giving yourself room to enjoy them, and making sure they aren't getting in the way of the bigger things you want.

And if your financial plan is in good shape and a $6 stick of emotional support butter genuinely brightens your workday?

Well.

I can think of worse ways to spend six bucks.

headline: Is Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RSPD) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
Designed to provide broad exposure to the Consumer Discretionary ETFs category of the market, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RSPD) is a smart beta exchange traded fund launched on 11/01/2006.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

For a long time now, the ETF industry has been flooded with products based on market capitalization weighted indexes, which are designed to represent the broader market or a particular market segment.

Investors who believe in market efficiency should consider market cap indexes, as they replicate market returns in a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way.

However, some investors believe in the possibility of beating the market through exceptional stock selection, and choose a different type of fund that tracks non-cap weighted strategies: smart beta.

By attempting to pick stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance, non-cap weighted indexes are based on certain fundamental characteristics, or a combination of such.

While this space offers a number of choices to investors, including simplest equal-weighting, fundamental weighting and volatility/momentum based weighting methodologies, not all these strategies have been able to deliver superior results.

Fund Sponsor & Index

Because the fund has amassed over $374.2 million, this makes it one of the larger ETFs in the Consumer Discretionary ETFs. RSPD is managed by Invesco. Before fees and expenses, RSPD seeks to match the performance of the S&P 500 EQL WEIGHT CONS DISCRETIONARY ID.

The S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary Index equally weights stocks in the consumer discretionary sector of the S&P 500 Index.

Cost & Other Expenses

For ETF investors, expense ratios are an important factor when considering a fund's return; in the long-term, cheaper funds actually have the ability to outperform their more expensive cousins if all other things remain the same.

With on par with most peer products in the space, this ETF has annual operating expenses of 0.40%.

The fund has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.94%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

It is important to delve into an ETF's holdings before investing despite the many upsides to these kinds of funds like diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

RSPD's heaviest allocation is in the Consumer Discretionary sector, which is about 100% of the portfolio.

Looking at individual holdings, Carnival Corp Ltd (CCL) accounts for about 2.49% of total assets, followed by Ralph Lauren Corp (RL) and Marriott International Inc/md (MAR).

Its top 10 holdings account for approximately 23.27% of RSPD's total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

Year-to-date, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF has lost about -4.03% so far, and is down about -4.86% over the last 12 months (as of 10/22/2026). RSPD has traded between $51.62 $60.02 in this past 52-week period.

The fund has a beta of 1.11 and standard deviation of 19.03% for the trailing three-year period. With about 49 holdings, it has more concentrated exposure than peers .

Alternatives

Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF is not a suitable option for investors seeking to outperform the Consumer Discretionary ETFs segment of the market. Instead, there are other ETFs in the space which investors should consider.

Vanguard Consumer Discretionary Index Fund ETF Shares (VCR) tracks MSCI US Investable Market Consumer Discretionary 25/50 Index and the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) tracks Consumer Discretionary Select Sector Index. Vanguard Consumer Discretionary Index Fund ETF Shares has $5.93 billion in assets, State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF has $22.19 billion. VCR has an expense ratio of 0.09% and XLY changes 0.08%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Consumer Discretionary ETFs

Bottom Line

To learn more about this product and other ETFs, screen for products that match your investment objectives and read articles on latest developments in the ETF investing universe, please visit Zacks ETF Center.

headline: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Salesforce, S&P Global, Intuit, Kewaunee Scientific and Key Tronic
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 22, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Salesforce, Inc. CRM, S&P Global Inc. SPGI, Intuit Inc. INTU, Kewaunee Scientific Corp. KEQU and Key Tronic Corp. KTCC.

Here are highlights from Wednesday’s Analyst Blog:

Top Analyst Reports for Salesforce, S&P and Intuit

The Zacks Research Daily presents the best research output of our analyst team. Today's Research Daily features new research reports on 12 major stocks, including Salesforce, Inc., S&P Global Inc. and Intuit Inc., as well as two micro-cap stocks Kewaunee Scientific Corp. and Key Tronic Corp. The Zacks microcap research is unique as our research content on these small and under-the-radar companies is the only research of its type in the country.

These research reports have been hand-picked from the roughly 70 reports published by our analyst team today.

You can see all of today’s research reports here >>>

Ahead of Wall Street

The daily 'Ahead of Wall Street' article is a must-read for all investors who would like to be ready for that day's trading action. The article comes out before the market opens, attempting to make sense of that morning's economic releases and how they will affect that day's market action. You can read this article for free on our home page and can actually sign up there to get an email notification as this article comes out each morning.

You can read today's AWS here >>> Pre-Markets Up on Cooling Metrics, Decent Q3 Reports

Today's Featured Research Reports

Shares of Salesforce have declined -4.7% over the past year against the Zacks Internet - Software industry’s decline of -5.5%. The company’s sensitivity of enterprise spending to macroeconomic conditions, intense competition across CRM, data and AI workflows, and rising leverage and interest costs tied to debt-funded repurchases. 

Pending acquisitions not only enhance product portfolio but also increase integration demands. With meaningful growth drivers and execution risks, we view the risk-reward profile as balanced. Nevertheless, Salesforce is extending its CRM franchise through Agentforce, Data 360 and an interface strategy that brings its data and workflows into more AI surfaces. 

Recurring revenues and backlog remain healthy, while rising agent usage, premium bundle bookings and Slack activity support management’s expectation for organic revenue reacceleration. The company also continues to generate cash and return capital.

headline: 3 Chemical Specialty Stocks to Escape Industry Challenges
html_content:
The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry is facing headwinds from weak demand amid sluggish conditions in Europe, a slow recovery in China and tariff-related disruptions. Profit margins across the sector also remain strained due to persistently high input, supply chain and logistics costs.

Industry players, such as Element Solutions Inc ESI, Perimeter Solutions, Inc. PRM and Quaker Chemical Corporation KWR, are banking on strategic measures, including operating cost reductions, to tide over a persistently challenging environment.

About the Industry

The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry consists of manufacturers of specialty chemical products for a host of end-use markets such as textile, paper, automotive, electronics, personal care, energy, construction, food & beverages and agriculture. These chemicals (including catalysts, surfactants, specialty polymers, coating additives, pesticides and oilfield chemicals) are used based on their performance and have a specific purpose. Specialty chemicals can be single molecules or a combination of molecules referred to as formulations, and they provide a vast range of effects upon which various industries rely. Their compositions significantly influence the performance of the finished products. Specialty chemicals have applications in the manufacturing process of a vast range of products, including paints and coatings, cosmetics, petroleum products, inks and plastics. 

What's Shaping the Future of the Chemical Specialty Industry?

Demand Softness Poses a Headwind: Companies in the chemical specialty space are facing headwinds from weak demand in building and construction as well as industrial end markets, especially in Europe and China, due to economic slowdown. Elevated borrowing costs and inflation have taken a bite out of the residential construction industry. A slower recovery in economic activities in China is hurting demand in that country. Low consumer confidence and high inflation have also dampened demand in Europe. While customer inventory de-stocking is essentially complete, some lingering impacts of the same in certain markets are expected to continue over the near term. The imposition of hefty tariffs has also introduced significant headwinds for the chemical specialty industry. Soft demand conditions, exacerbated by a weak macroeconomic environment and tariff-induced impacts, are likely to weigh on the volumes of chemical specialty companies. 

Cost Pressure Still a Worry: Specialty chemical makers are facing headwinds from raw-material and energy-cost inflation and supply-chain and freight-transportation disruptions. Some companies are exposed to challenges from elevated logistics and labor costs. Tariffs have led to increased costs for raw materials, resulting in higher production expenses for the industry players. Also, the Middle East conflict and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz have led to significant supply disruptions and feedstock cost pressure. Inflationary pressures are expected to continue in the short term and weigh on the margins of chemical specialty companies.

Strategic Actions to Aid Results: The companies in this space are executing a raft of self-help measures, including cost-cutting and productivity improvement, expansion into high-growth markets, restructuring, operational efficiency improvement and actions to strengthen the balance sheet and boost cash flows. The industry participants are aggressively implementing measures to cut costs. These actions are likely to help companies weather macroeconomic challenges.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Downbeat Prospects

The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry is part of the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #166, which places it in the bottom 33% of more than 250 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates a bleak near term. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture.

Industry Underperforms Sector & S&P 500

The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry has underperformed the Zacks S&P 500 composite and the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector over the past year.

The industry has gained 5.7% over this period compared with the S&P 500’s rise of 15.2% and the broader sector’s increase of 13.1%.

One-Year Price Performance

Industry's Current Valuation

On the basis of the trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-EBITDA (EV/EBITDA), which is a commonly used multiple for valuing chemical stocks, the industry is currently trading at 10.97X, below the S&P 500’s 17.92X and the sector’s 12.59X.

Over the past three years, the industry has traded as high as 13.36X, as low as 9.44X, with a median of 11.77X, as the chart below shows.
 

Enterprise Value/EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) Ratio

Enterprise Value/EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) Ratio 

3 Chemical Specialty Stocks to Keep a Close Eye on

Perimeter Solutions: Missouri-based Perimeter Solutions is a leading provider of solutions for the fire safety and specialty products industries. Perimeter’s contracted Fire Safety business, growing fixed service revenues and geographic diversification support long-term growth and earnings visibility. Favorable industry trends are expected to continue to drive demand for fire-retardant products. The company remains focused on expanding its fire prevention and protection business. Its Specialty Products segment continues to broaden earnings sources outside wildfire demand. Recent acquisitions, particularly MMT, are driving sales in this segment. PRM’s strong balance sheet also offers adequate liquidity for growth investments and M&A opportunities. 

Perimeter Solutions has expected earnings growth of 17.2% for 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for PRM’s 2026 earnings has moved up 1.9% over the past 60 days. PRM currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Price and Consensus: PRM

Quaker Chemical: Based in Pennsylvania, Quaker Chemical (doing business as Quaker Houghton) is a global developer, producer and marketer of industrial process fluids and related specialty chemicals. The company continues to outpace underlying markets through new business wins, with momentum in the Asia-Pacific and improving traction in the Americas as prior disruptions ease. KWR is leaning on self-help actions, including a global transformation program to simplify operations and reduce structural costs, while integration and cross-selling broaden the portfolio. Acquisitions remain a steady contributor to consolidated sales growth, with Dipsol a key driver in the Asia-Pacific.

Quaker Chemical has expected earnings growth of 11.8% for the current year. The consensus estimate for KWR’s current-year earnings has been revised 1.7% higher over the past 60 days. Quaker Chemical, carrying a Zacks Rank #2, has an expected long-term earnings per share growth rate of 18.9%.

Price and Consensus: KWR

Element Solutions: Florida-based Element Solutions is a leading specialty chemicals provider, offering innovative and differentiated solutions to its customers across a vast spectrum of industries. ESI is poised for growth, driven by strong execution and strategic positioning in the electronics sector. The company is benefiting from strength in the electronics market. ESI is seeing strong organic growth in its Electronics segment. The Micromax acquisition has strengthened its position to build an industry-leading Electronics portfolio. High-value end markets are contributing to a favorable product mix, while the ongoing pricing and productivity initiatives are boosting margins. 

Element Solutions has an expected earnings growth rate of 21.5% for 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ESI’s 2026 earnings has been stable the past 60 days. ESI surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters at an average of roughly 6.3%. ESI currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Price and Consensus: ESI

headline: Implied Volatility Surging for BBVA Argentina Bank Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in BBVA Argentina Bank S.A. BBAR need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Jan 15, 2027 $11 Put had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for BBVA Argentina Bank shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, BBVA Argentina Bank is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Banks – Foreign industry that ranks in the Top 26% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 30 days, no analysts have increased their earnings estimates for the current quarter, while one analyst has revised the estimate downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from 47 cents per share to 41 cents in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about BBVA Argentina Bank right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

headline: 3 Top-Ranked Small-Cap Blend Mutual Funds With Growth Potential
html_content:
Those with a high-risk appetite as well as an interest in growth and value investing, may chose small-cap blend mutual funds to boost their portfolio. While blend funds, also known as “hybrid funds,” aim for value appreciation by capital gains, small-cap funds are expected to have higher growth prospects than their large and medium counterparts.  

Blend funds provide significant exposure to both growth and value stocks and owe their origin to a graphical representation of a fund’s equity style box. Meanwhile, funds investing the majority of their assets in securities of companies with market capitalization lower than $2 billion are generally considered small-cap mutual funds. Though funds investing in small-cap stocks are believed to have more exposure to market volatility than large or medium ones, they are expected to provide diversification across sectors and companies. Moreover, small-cap companies are believed to be less affected by a global downturn thanks to less international exposure.    

Below, we share with you three top-ranked, small-cap blend mutual funds, namely Goldman Sachs Small Cap Eq Insghts GCSAX, Vanguard Strategic Small-Cap Equity Inv VSTCX and Keeley Small Cap Fund WESCX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and is expected to outperform its peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of small-cap blend funds. 

Goldman Sachs Small Cap Eq Insghts fund invests its net assets plus any borrowings for investment purposes (measured at time of purchase) in a broadly diversified portfolio of equity investments in small-cap U.S. issuers, including foreign issuers traded in the United States, and may invest outside the then-existing small-cap capitalization range. 

Goldman Sachs Small Cap Eq Insghts has three-year annualized returns of 22.2%. As of the end of April 2026, GCSAX had 545 issues and invested 2% of its net assets in Bloom Energy Corp. 

Vanguard Strategic Small-Cap Equity Inv fund invests in small-capitalization domestic equity securities based on the advisor's assessment of their relative return potential. 

Vanguard Strategic Small-Cap Equity Inv has three-year annualized returns of 21.9%. VSTCX has an expense ratio of 0.21%. 

Keeley Small Cap Fund invests at least 80% of its net assets, including any borrowings for investment purposes, in common stocks of smaller companies.

Keeley Small Cap Fund has three-year annualized returns of 21.8%. Joseph Gabelli has been one of the fund managers of WESCX since May 2025.

excerpt: IBM's Q3 earnings call highlights accelerating software growth, robust Red Hat demand and enterprise AI momentum as management raises its 2026 cash flow outlook.
headline: IBM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Software Growth and Cash Flow Outlook
html_content:
International Business Machines Corporation IBM emphasized accelerating software demand, operational efficiency and enterprise AI adoption during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management raised its free cash flow outlook while maintaining its full-year revenue growth expectations.

The discussion centered on recovering software transactions, Red Hat momentum and infrastructure demand. Executives also addressed questions about the sustainability of software growth and opportunities emerging from enterprise AI modernization.

IBM Raises Cash Flow Outlook, Maintains Revenue Guidance

IBM expects full-year 2026 revenue growth of 4% to 5% at constant currency. Management raised its annual free cash flow growth forecast to more than $1 billion year over year.

Chief financial officer James Kavanaugh attributed the improved cash outlook to adjusted EBITDA growth and productivity initiatives, partially offset by higher capital expenditures, cash taxes and interest expenses.

IBM reported operating earnings of $2.95 per share, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.88. Revenue reached $17.1 billion, surpassing the $16.84 billion consensus estimate. Operating pretax margin expanded 70 basis points (bps).

International Business Machines Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

International Business Machines Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | International Business Machines Corporation Quote

IBM's Software Momentum Strengthens on Transaction Recovery

Software revenue increased 9% at constant currency, accelerating four percentage points sequentially. Kavanaugh highlighted strong recurring revenue and improved transactional execution.

Red Hat grew 11%, supported by bookings growth in the high teens. OpenShift annual recurring revenue reached $2.4 billion, growing more than 30%. Data revenue increased 20%, while Transaction Processing advanced 10%.

During questioning from Evercore ISI, CEO Arvind Krishna emphasized that AI-driven application modernization supports sustained demand for OpenShift and Confluent. Kavanaugh clarified that roughly one-quarter of software acceleration came from previously delayed transactions, while three-quarters reflected new business.

IBM Sees Mainframe Demand Supporting Future Growth

Infrastructure revenue increased 5% at constant currency, driven by 32% growth in Distributed Infrastructure. Storage demand remained strong as enterprises expanded AI-related infrastructure.

Krishna highlighted the z17 platform's performance, noting that it generated more than $1 billion of incremental revenue across six quarters compared with previous programs.

Responding to Bank of America, Krishna cautioned that Transaction Processing's double-digit growth should moderate. However, Kavanaugh pointed to expanding installed mainframe capacity as a future software monetization opportunity, particularly entering 2027.

IBM Expands Enterprise AI and Hybrid Cloud Opportunities

Management positioned enterprise AI adoption around data integration, workflow modernization and secure deployment rather than isolated experimentation.

Krishna highlighted Confluent's real-time data capabilities, HashiCorp's security tools and Red Hat's hybrid infrastructure. IBM also discussed its Lightwell security offering, which has developed a pipeline approaching $700 million.

During questions from Jefferies, Krishna emphasized growing enterprise scrutiny of AI investment returns. He explained that meaningful productivity improvements require workflow redesign and integration with existing systems, creating opportunities for IBM's software and consulting businesses.

IBM Targets Margin Expansion Through Productivity

Kavanaugh reiterated IBM's expectation for 100 bps of full-year operating pretax margin expansion, supported by productivity improvements and expense discipline.

Software segment profit margin increased 210 bps, while Infrastructure expanded 120 bps. Consulting margins declined as IBM reinvested productivity savings into digital assets and AI-enabled service delivery.

Consulting revenue increased 2% at constant currency. AI-related work represented approximately 30% of quarterly consulting revenue and 35% of backlog, reflecting customers' focus on enterprise transformation.

IBM Maintains a Disciplined Growth Strategy

Management's commentary reflected confidence in software-led growth while maintaining cautious assumptions for the remainder of 2026.

Krishna and Kavanaugh emphasized continued investment in hybrid cloud, enterprise AI and quantum computing alongside operational efficiency. Their forward-looking priorities center on recurring revenue, infrastructure modernization and stronger cash generation.

What IBM's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

IBM currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), indicating a neutral near-term outlook under the Zacks ranking system. Its Value Score of D, Growth Score of C and Momentum Score of F indicate relatively weak characteristics across these investment styles. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here.

The company's VGM Score of F also reflects an unfavorable combined assessment of value, growth and momentum. Zacks generally favors stocks carrying a Rank #1 or #2 (Buy) alongside Style Scores of A or B. IBM's current combination warrants a cautious interpretation, while its Zacks Rank could change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the third-quarter results.

 

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

excerpt: ResMed (RMD) doesn't possess the right combination of the two key ingredients for a likely earnings beat in its upcoming report. Get prepared with the key expectations.
headline: ResMed (RMD) Earnings Expected to Grow: What to Know Ahead of Next Week's Release
html_content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when ResMed (RMD) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 29, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This maker of medical products for respiratory disorders is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.67 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +4.7%.

Revenues are expected to be $1.39 billion, up 4% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.83% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for ResMed?

For ResMed, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.60%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #3.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that ResMed will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that ResMed would post earnings of $2.9 per share when it actually produced earnings of $2.95, delivering a surprise of +1.72%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

ResMed doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Stay on top of upcoming earnings announcements with the Zacks Earnings Calendar.

Revenues are expected to be $1.39 billion, up 4% from the year-ago quarter. Estimate Revisions Trend The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.83% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period. Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Earnings Whisper Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction). The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier. Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only. A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP. Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell). How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for ResMed? For ResMed, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.60%. On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #3. Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number. For the last reported quarter, it was expected that ResMed would post earnings of $2.9 per share when it actually produced earnings of $2.95, delivering a surprise of +1.72%. Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times. Bottom Line An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss. That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. excerpt: Clean beauty, innovation and digital shopping are reshaping the industry. Explore how ELF, EL and ULTA are adapting to changing consumer preferences.
headline: 3 Beauty Stocks to Explore as Consumer Preferences Reshape the Market
html_content:
An updated edition of the Aug. 25, 2026 article.

The beauty and cosmetics industry remains an attractive space for investors, supported by changing lifestyles, growing interest in personal grooming and a steady flow of product innovations. Skincare, haircare, makeup and fragrances continue to attract consumer attention as beauty routines become more closely linked to everyday wellness. The availability of products across different price ranges also helps the industry cater to a broad customer base.

Consumer expectations are evolving, prompting beauty companies to rethink their product offerings and marketing strategies. Shoppers are increasingly focused on product performance, ingredient quality and affordability. Demand for solutions addressing specific skincare and haircare needs is creating opportunities for specialized offerings. Meanwhile, the growing popularity of premium beauty products and affordable alternatives reflects the diverse spending preferences across consumer groups.

Innovation is helping companies tap into these changing preferences. Brands are exploring improved formulations, convenient packaging and products designed for multiple uses. Interest in personalized beauty solutions and wellness-focused offerings is also encouraging product development. These initiatives can help companies attract new customers, strengthen brand engagement and encourage repeat purchases in a competitive marketplace.

The expansion of digital shopping channels is adding another dimension to industry growth. Online platforms and social media are influencing product discovery, while physical stores remain important for hands-on experiences and expert guidance. Sally Beauty Holdings, Inc. SBH participates in this market through professional haircare and beauty retail, while Kenvue Inc. KVUE has exposure to skincare and personal care through brands such as Neutrogena and Aveeno.

The beauty industry's long-term prospects remain tied to product innovation, consumer engagement and effective distribution strategies. Although promotional activity, competition and cautious discretionary spending could create challenges, companies that respond quickly to changing demand may find opportunities to expand their market presence. Investors seeking exposure to evolving beauty industry trends may explore e.l.f. Beauty, Inc. ELF, The Estee Lauder Companies Inc. EL and Ulta Beauty, Inc. ULTA featured in our Beauty & Cosmetics Screen as stocks worth keeping on their radar. 

Explore 40 cutting-edge investment themes with Zacks Thematic Investing Screens and discover your next big opportunity.

3 Beauty and Cosmetic Stocks in Focus

As consumer interest in ethical, ingredient-conscious and affordable beauty products evolves, e.l.f. Beauty is strengthening its presence through vegan formulations, cruelty-free practices and continuous innovation. The Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) company follows its e.l.f. clean standards, which exclude more than 2,500 ingredients, while its cruelty-free credentials are backed by PETA and Leaping Bunny certifications. Its emphasis on accessible pricing further supports its appeal among value-conscious beauty shoppers. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Innovation remains central to ELF’s efforts to address changing consumer preferences. The company combines community-driven product development with prestige-inspired offerings at affordable prices. Products such as Main Stain Lip Marker, Power Grip Rose Setting Spray and Sheer For It Blush Tint demonstrate this approach. Beyond cosmetics, e.l.f. SKIN extends its presence in skincare, while e.l.f. Hair marks its expansion into haircare with an affordable, vegan and cruelty-free assortment.

Portfolio diversification supports the company's participation in emerging beauty trends. Naturium addresses interest in science-backed skincare through clinically focused, biocompatible formulations, including the Glow Getter collection. Meanwhile, rhode caters to demand for simplified skincare routines and hybrid makeup essentials. Alongside digital engagement and international retail expansion, these initiatives strengthen e.l.f. Beauty's ability to serve diverse consumer preferences across beauty categories.

The growing demand for high-performance skincare, luxury fragrances and ingredient-conscious beauty products is creating fresh opportunities in the global beauty market. The Estee Lauder Companies is addressing these trends through its diverse brand portfolio, scientific expertise and product innovation. Its Beauty Reimagined strategy emphasizes faster innovation and consumer-focused offerings. The company is also advancing green chemistry, ingredient transparency and sustainable packaging while offering natural and vegan formulations across select products.

Innovation remains a key priority as the Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company responds to changing beauty preferences. Clinique and The Ordinary are tapping into emerging ingredient trends through PDRN-based skincare innovations, while Estee Lauder is exploring longevity-focused solutions. The Ordinary and Aveda also support demand for cruelty-free beauty, while Clinique is expanding its sensitive-skin offerings. Meanwhile, M·A·C is introducing new lip products, and Jo Malone London, TOM FORD and Le Labo strengthen their luxury fragrance portfolios.

Digital transformation supports EL's beauty strategy. The company is expanding into social commerce and specialty beauty channels while using AI-enabled insights to improve personalization and marketing effectiveness. These efforts, alongside responsible formulation practices, faster innovation cycles and targeted retail expansion, could enhance consumer engagement and strengthen EL's competitiveness across global beauty categories.

Beauty shopping is increasingly influenced by product transparency, ethical practices and personalized experiences. Ulta Beauty is addressing these preferences through its Conscious Beauty initiative, which helps shoppers identify brands offering clean ingredients, vegan formulations, cruelty-free products and sustainable packaging. The company's Ulta Beauty Collection also emphasizes clean ingredients and cruelty-free standards, supporting its efforts to make conscious beauty choices more accessible.

Product innovation and assortment expansion remain central to Ulta Beauty's strategy. The company is strengthening its K-Beauty portfolio with brands such as Dr.Melaxin, numbuzin and Centellian24, catering to interest in innovative skincare. Brands such as Rare Beauty, amika and Moroccanoil broaden its makeup and haircare offerings. Meanwhile, fragrance launches from Khloé Kardashian and Megan Thee Stallion enhance product discovery. ULTA is also expanding its wellness assortment through brands such as HigherDOSE and good day by Patchology.

Digital transformation boosts this Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) company's efforts to address changing shopping habits. Ulta Beauty is expanding its TikTok Shop presence, leveraging AI-powered shopping tools and using loyalty insights to deliver personalized experiences. ULTA’s growing online marketplace, omnichannel capabilities and international expansion through Space NK could strengthen customer engagement and broaden its reach across evolving beauty categories.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. excerpt: PL and BKSY are riding growing demand for satellite imagery and AI analytics, but one stands out with stronger financials and growth prospects.
headline: Planet Labs vs. BlackSky: Which Space Stock Is the Better Pick?
html_content:
The increasing demand for satellite imagery, geospatial intelligence and AI-powered analytics is opening significant opportunities for companies operating in this space.

Against this backdrop, Planet Labs PBC PL and BlackSky Technology Inc. BKSY are worth mentioning as both are expanding satellite capabilities amid growing customer demand.

Planet Labs provides satellite imagery, geospatial data and analytics to government and commercial customers through its extensive Earth observation satellite fleet. BlackSky is a provider of real-time geospatial intelligence and global monitoring services of some of the world’s most critical and strategic locations, economic assets and events.

Let us examine their growth prospects and challenges to determine which stock offers a more attractive investment opportunity.

The Case for Planet Labs

Planet Labs has a differentiated position in the Earth-observation industry, combining daily global monitoring with a decade-long imagery archive. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues surged 58% year over year to $116 million. Defense and Intelligence revenues (including satellite services revenues) rose more than 90% year over year, while commercial and civil-government revenues increased over 15% and 5%, respectively. The handover of the Pelican satellite to the Swedish Armed Forces supported top-line growth.

Expanding relationships with governments further strengthen its prospects. In August, the company was awarded a satellite services tender by Germany’s Federal Ministry of the Interior, making the country the first civil government to procure its dedicated Constellation Services. The tender includes options and has a maximum possible value of €25 million over five years. On the last earnings call, Planet Labs also highlighted an $8 million award from the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency for its Global Monitoring Service. It was recently selected by the European Space Agency to develop Slovenia’s Space Resilience Node.

On the last earnings call, management added that it had identified more than $4 billion in satellite-services opportunities, with over 25% qualified as near-term. The company had a backlog of approximately $815 million, up about 11% year over year at the end of the fiscal second quarter. Roughly 50% of the backlog applies to the next 12 months and 70% to the next 24 months. Planet Labs estimates that executing contracts already in backlog could generate more than $400 million in revenues over the next four quarters, excluding new business and renewals. Management added that the company is confident it can sustain “high growth rates in future years,” supported by near-term visibility and pipeline strength.

Planet Labs is also expanding capacity and advancing its satellite roadmap to support this opportunity. The company recently opened its Berlin manufacturing facility, which is expected to produce Pelican satellites and eventually scale to as many as 60 satellites per year. It recently launched the Pelican-12 satellite into orbit.

Before that, Planet Labs announced the launch of 20 satellites, which include a Google Project Suncatcher prototype, Tanager-2 and 18 SuperDoves. Suncatcher satellite will test Google’s Tensor Processing Units in space for the first time.

Planet Labs PBC Revenue (Quarterly)

Planet Labs PBC revenue-quarterly | Planet Labs PBC Quote

Planet Labs is accelerating Owl, its upcoming next-generation monitoring satellite. Owl is expected to upgrade Planet Labs' monitoring capabilities from 3-meter to 1-meter-class resolution while providing roughly 10 times more data at about 10 times the speed, added management.  

Financial strength provides another competitive advantage. Planet Labs exited the second quarter of fiscal 2027 with approximately $865 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, up more than 200% year over year. This increase was driven by positive free cash flow and proceeds from capital transactions over the past year.

Planet Labs also has its fair share of challenges. Quarterly performance will remain uneven owing to the timing of satellite deliveries. Sweden’s satellite handover pulled revenues into the fiscal second quarter from the fiscal third quarter. Fiscal third-quarter guidance of $101-$105 million therefore implies a sequential revenue decline, alongside an expected adjusted EBITDA loss of $1-$6 million.

Growth also requires substantial investment. Planet Labs spent about $29 million in capital expenditures in the fiscal second quarter and expects fiscal 2027 capex of $100-$115 million. Management expects capex to increase in future quarters as it plans to channel spending toward manufacturing expansion in San Francisco and Berlin, supply-chain resiliency and next-generation satellite fleets.

Moreover, the increasing competition in the Earth observation space leaves less room for execution missteps. New satellites and AI offerings must deliver commercially, not merely meet development milestones.

The Case for BlackSky

BlackSky is gaining momentum from rising demand for real-time geospatial intelligence and its expanding Gen-3 satellite constellation. Its vertically integrated platform combines high-resolution Gen-3 satellite imagery, low-latency delivery and real-time AI insights through its Spectra platform to address mission-critical national security requirements.

The company's second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 50% year over year to $33.3 million, supported by space-based intelligence and AI services business.

On the August earnings call, BlackSky noted that it has a pipeline of more than 20 Gen-3 satellites underway and is on track to have eight Gen-3 satellites in orbit by the end of the year. The company is on track for an on-time delivery of its first sovereign Gen-3 satellite in 2026. In September, the company announced that it “collected and processed first-light imagery” from the fifth Gen-3 satellite in less than 20 hours after liftoff, underscoring rapid commissioning capabilities.

The company expects rapid growth driven by strong backlog and improving visibility from multi-year subscription contracts for its space-based intelligence and AI services. In the last reported quarter, Space-based intelligence and AI services revenues reached $24.5 million, increasing 50% sequentially.

BlackSky's subscription business is also improving profitability. Second-quarter adjusted EBITDA reached $4.7 million, translating into a 14.2% margin. Its imagery and AI subscription business achieved an approximately $100 million annualized revenue run rate, creating a stronger recurring revenue foundation.

BlackSky Technology Inc. Revenue (Quarterly)

BlackSky Technology Inc. revenue-quarterly | BlackSky Technology Inc. Quote

The company continues to strengthen its international contract portfolio. International subscription revenues surged 150% year over year, highlighting growing demand from overseas government customers.  On the last earnings call, the company noted that it had secured up to $200 million in bookings year to date, while multi-year international contracts for space-based intelligence subscriptions represented more than 80% of total funded backlog.

In October, BlackSky secured a six-figure Gen-3 on-Demand pilot imagery services agreement with a new international intelligence customer. It also expanded its partnership with HEO through a seven-figure annual contract extension for non-Earth imaging services, incorporating Gen-3 capabilities. In September, BlackSky announced that its Gen-3 satellites will be part of a 50-satellite constellation developed under a $1 billion investment involving Marlan Space, Loft Orbital, Mistral AI, along with organizations in the UAE and France.

The company ended second-quarter 2026 with $244.1 million in cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments. BKSY had more than $325 million in total liquidity, following a $150 million ATM raise.

Nevertheless, BlackSky faces challenges. Its smaller revenue base and substantial exposure to defense and intelligence spending increase sensitivity to government procurement cycles. Increasing capex is another concern. Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between $50 million and $60 million.

BlackSky reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $130 million to $150 million and adjusted EBITDA outlook of $12 million to $24 million. However, achieving sustained growth hinges on additional Gen-3 deployment, contract execution and successful commercialization of newer technologies.

Price Performance & Valuations of PL & BKSY

Year to date, PL and BKSY are down 30.4% and 7.4%, respectively.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

PL is trading at a forward price-to-sales multiple of 9.25X, higher than BKSY’s 3.61X.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

How Do the Consensus Estimates Compare for PL & BKSY?

Analysts have upped their earnings estimates for PL by 28.6% for the current fiscal year in the past 60 days.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Estimates have been unchanged for BKSY’s bottom line in the same period.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

PL or BKSY: Which Is a Better Pick

Both PL and BKSY carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) at present.

Planet Labs' financial flexibility, broader customer applications and sizeable backlog give it an edge over BlackSky for investors seeking exposure to the evolving space economy.

Before that, Planet Labs announced the launch of 20 satellites, which include a Google Project Suncatcher prototype, Tanager-2 and 18 SuperDoves. Suncatcher satellite will test Google’s Tensor Processing Units in space for the first time. Planet Labs PBC Revenue (Quarterly) Planet Labs PBC revenue-quarterly | Planet Labs PBC Quote Planet Labs is accelerating Owl, its upcoming next-generation monitoring satellite. Owl is expected to upgrade Planet Labs' monitoring capabilities from 3-meter to 1-meter-class resolution while providing roughly 10 times more data at about 10 times the speed, added management. Financial strength provides another competitive advantage. Planet Labs exited the second quarter of fiscal 2027 with approximately $865 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, up more than 200% year over year. This increase was driven by positive free cash flow and proceeds from capital transactions over the past year. Planet Labs also has its fair share of challenges. Quarterly performance will remain uneven owing to the timing of satellite deliveries. Sweden’s satellite handover pulled revenues into the fiscal second quarter from the fiscal third quarter. Fiscal third-quarter guidance of $101-$105 million therefore implies a sequential revenue decline, alongside an expected adjusted EBITDA loss of $1-$6 million. Growth also requires substantial investment. Planet Labs spent about $29 million in capital expenditures in the fiscal second quarter and expects fiscal 2027 capex of $100-$115 million. Moreover, the increasing competition in the Earth observation space leaves less room for execution missteps. New satellites and AI offerings must deliver commercially, not merely meet development milestones. The Case for BlackSky BlackSky is gaining momentum from rising demand for real-time geospatial intelligence and its expanding Gen-3 satellite constellation. Its vertically integrated platform combines high-resolution Gen-3 satellite imagery, low-latency delivery and real-time AI insights through its Spectra platform to address mission-critical national security requirements. The company's second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 50% year over year to $33.3 million, supported by space-based intelligence and AI services business. On the August earnings call, BlackSky noted that it has a pipeline of more than 20 Gen-3 satellites underway and is on track to have eight Gen-3 satellites in orbit by the end of the year. The company is on track for an on-time delivery of its first sovereign Gen-3 satellite in 2026. In September, the company announced that it “collected and processed first-light imagery” from the fifth Gen-3 satellite in less than 20 hours after liftoff, underscoring rapid commissioning capabilities. The company expects rapid growth driven by strong backlog and improving visibility from multi-year subscription contracts for its space-based intelligence and AI services. In the last reported quarter, Space-based intelligence and AI services revenues reached $24.5 million, increasing 50% sequentially. BlackSky's subscription business is also improving profitability. Second-quarter adjusted EBITDA reached $4.7 million, translating into a 14.2% margin. Its imagery and AI subscription business achieved an approximately $100 million annualized revenue run rate, creating a stronger recurring revenue foundation. BlackSky Technology Inc. Revenue (Quarterly) BlackSky Technology Inc. revenue-quarterly | BlackSky Technology Inc. Quote The company continues to strengthen its international contract portfolio. International subscription revenues surged 150% year over year, highlighting growing demand from overseas government customers. On the last earnings call, the company noted that it had secured up to $200 million in bookings year to date, while multi-year international contracts for space-based intelligence subscriptions represented more than 80% of total funded backlog. In October, BlackSky secured a six-figure Gen-3 on-Demand pilot imagery services agreement with a new international intelligence customer. It also expanded its partnership with HEO through a seven-figure annual contract extension for non-Earth imaging services, incorporating Gen-3 capabilities. In September, BlackSky announced that its Gen-3 satellites will be part of a 50-satellite constellation developed under a $1 billion investment involving Marlan Space, Loft Orbital, Mistral AI, along with organizations in the UAE and France. The company ended second-quarter 2026 with $244.1 million in cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments. BKSY had more than $325 million in total liquidity, following a $150 million ATM raise. Nevertheless, BlackSky faces challenges. Its smaller revenue base and substantial exposure to defense and intelligence spending increase sensitivity to government procurement cycles. Increasing capex is another concern. Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between $50 million and $60 million. BlackSky reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $130 million to $150 million and adjusted EBITDA outlook of $12 million to $24 million.
