excerpt: Thor Industries (THO) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Thor Industries (THO) Down 8.1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
html_content:
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Thor Industries (THO). Shares have lost about 8.1% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Thor Industries due for a breakout? Before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late, let's take a quick look at the most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the important drivers.

THOR Q4 Earnings Miss Expectations

THOR posted adjusted earnings of 78 cents per share for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 93 cents by 16.1%. The bottom line fell 66.9% year over year as North American margins came under pressure from lower volumes, promotions and higher costs.

Quarterly revenues of $2.31 billion topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.15 billion by 7.4% but declined 8.4% year over year. Global independent dealer inventories fell 11.5% from a year earlier, while European growth partly offset weaker North American results.

Margins Contract as Profitability Weakens

Gross profit declined 23% year over year to $285.6 million, while gross margin narrowed 230 basis points to 12.4%. Net income attributable to THOR fell 67.5% to $40.8 million.

Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased to $206.4 million from $237.9 million. Adjusted EBITDA dropped 37.1% to $131.7 million. Management said THOR absorbed a meaningful portion of supplier cost increases to protect retail affordability rather than pass the full burden to dealers and customers.

Towable Sales Slide Amid Dealer Caution

North American Towable net sales fell 22.7% year over year to $687.3 million as unit shipments declined 19.7% to 20,616. Fifth-wheel unit shipments dropped 34.7%.

Gross profit decreased 38.9% to $72.4 million, while gross margin contracted 280 basis points to 10.5% on lower sales, unfavorable mix, promotions and higher material costs. Pretax income fell 77.2% to $17 million. Backlog rose 74.6% to $916.6 million, while dealer inventory fell 16% to 53,330 units and declined 20.6% sequentially.

Motorized Segment Faces Sharper Margin Pressure

North American Motorized net sales declined 10.4% to $499.3 million as unit shipments fell 13.1% to 3,806. A 2.7% increase in overall net price per unit partly offset lower volumes. Class C unit shipments declined 19.1% in the quarter.

Gross margin dropped 600 basis points to 5.3% as material, overhead and warranty cost percentages increased. The segment posted a pretax loss of $5.2 million, while backlog decreased 27.5% to $728.2 million and dealer inventory increased 9.2% to 10,639 units.

THOR Europe Delivers Resilient Top-Line Growth

European RV net sales increased 5% year over year to $969.2 million, supported by a 3.9% rise in unit shipments to 13,370 and a 1.1% increase in overall net price per unit. Favorable currency movements contributed 0.1% to the pricing increase. Sales also benefited from lower promotional activity and a shift toward higher-priced motorized products.

Gross profit rose 3.3% to $148.7 million, while gross margin edged down 30 basis points to 15.3%. Pretax income increased 5.9% to $55 million. European backlog grew 8.4% to $1.65 billion, while dealer inventory declined 7.7% to 20,520 units.

Liquidity Supports Capital Deployment

THOR ended fiscal 2026 with $482 million in cash and cash equivalents and total liquidity of $1.30 billion. Gross debt stood at $875.8 million, while cash from operations for the full fiscal year totaled $321.2 million, down from $577.9 million a year earlier.

During fiscal 2026, THO reduced debt by $59.7 million and repurchased $115.1 million of shares, including $34.3 million in the fourth quarter. Capital expenditures totaled $152.4 million, while the regular quarterly dividend stood at 52 cents per share. The remaining repurchase authorization was $264.2 million as of July 31.

THOR Defers Fiscal 2027 Guidance as Cost Actions Advance

Management expects the fiscal 2027 retail environment to remain relatively flat with fiscal 2026 and held off on issuing annual guidance until it gathers feedback from key September industry events. The company expects current Towable pressures to persist to some degree into the first half of fiscal 2027 and plans to provide full-year guidance later this calendar year.

THOR expects strategic initiatives and restructuring activities to improve its annual earnings profile by more than $100 million once fully implemented. The company has unified its North American RV operations under one group to expand purchasing leverage, standardize operations, align brands and integrate data systems.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

In the past month, investors have witnessed a downward trend in fresh estimates.

The consensus estimate has shifted -62.15% due to these changes.

VGM Scores

Currently, Thor Industries has a average Growth Score of C, though it is lagging a lot on the Momentum Score front with an F. However, the stock was allocated a grade of A on the value side, putting it in the top 20% for value investors.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of B. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending downward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions indicates a downward shift. It's no surprise Thor Industries has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell). We expect a below average return from the stock in the next few months.

excerpt: ESI, PRM and KWR are pursuing growth through cost cuts, operational improvements and strategic expansion as specialty chemicals firms face weak demand and rising costs.
headline: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Element Solutions, Perimeter Solutions and Quaker Chemical
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 23, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Element Solutions Inc ESI, Perimeter Solutions, Inc. PRM and Quaker Chemical Corp. KWR.

Industry: Specialty Chemical

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3012376/3-chemical-specialty-stocks-to-escape-industry-challenges

The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry is facing headwinds from weak demand amid sluggish conditions in Europe, a slow recovery in China and tariff-related disruptions. Profit margins across the sector also remain strained due to persistently high input, supply chain and logistics costs.

Industry players, such as Element Solutions Inc, Perimeter Solutions, Inc. and Quaker Chemical Corp., are banking on strategic measures, including operating cost reductions, to tide over a persistently challenging environment.

About the Industry

The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry consists of manufacturers of specialty chemical products for a host of end-use markets such as textile, paper, automotive, electronics, personal care, energy, construction, food & beverages and agriculture. These chemicals (including catalysts, surfactants, specialty polymers, coating additives, pesticides and oilfield chemicals) are used based on their performance and have a specific purpose. 

Specialty chemicals can be single molecules or a combination of molecules referred to as formulations, and they provide a vast range of effects upon which various industries rely. Their compositions significantly influence the performance of the finished products. Specialty chemicals have applications in the manufacturing process of a vast range of products, including paints and coatings, cosmetics, petroleum products, inks and plastics. 

What's Shaping the Future of the Chemical Specialty Industry?

Demand Softness Poses a Headwind: Companies in the chemical specialty space are facing headwinds from weak demand in building and construction as well as industrial end markets, especially in Europe and China, due to economic slowdown. Elevated borrowing costs and inflation have taken a bite out of the residential construction industry. A slower recovery in economic activities in China is hurting demand in that country. Low consumer confidence and high inflation have also dampened demand in Europe. 

While customer inventory de-stocking is essentially complete, some lingering impacts of the same in certain markets are expected to continue over the near term. The imposition of hefty tariffs has also introduced significant headwinds for the chemical specialty industry. Soft demand conditions, exacerbated by a weak macroeconomic environment and tariff-induced impacts, are likely to weigh on the volumes of chemical specialty companies. 

Cost Pressure Still a Worry: Specialty chemical makers are facing headwinds from raw-material and energy-cost inflation and supply-chain and freight-transportation disruptions. Some companies are exposed to challenges from elevated logistics and labor costs. Tariffs have led to increased costs for raw materials, resulting in higher production expenses for the industry players. Also, the Middle East conflict and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz have led to significant supply disruptions and feedstock cost pressure. Inflationary pressures are expected to continue in the short term and weigh on the margins of chemical specialty companies.

Strategic Actions to Aid Results: The companies in this space are executing a raft of self-help measures, including cost-cutting and productivity improvement, expansion into high-growth markets, restructuring, operational efficiency improvement and actions to strengthen the balance sheet and boost cash flows. The industry participants are aggressively implementing measures to cut costs. These actions are likely to help companies weather macroeconomic challenges.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Downbeat Prospects

The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry is part of the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #166, which places it in the bottom 33% of more than 250 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates a bleak near term. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture.

Industry Underperforms Sector & S&P 500

The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry has underperformed the Zacks S&P 500 composite and the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector over the past year.

The industry has gained 5.7% over this period compared with the S&P 500’s rise of 15.2% and the broader sector’s increase of 13.1%.

Industry's Current Valuation

On the basis of the trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-EBITDA (EV/EBITDA), which is a commonly used multiple for valuing chemical stocks, the industry is currently trading at 10.97X, below the S&P 500’s 17.92X and the sector’s 12.59X.

Over the past three years, the industry has traded as high as 13.36X, as low as 9.44X, with a median of 11.77X.

3 Chemical Specialty Stocks to Keep a Close Eye On

Perimeter Solutions: Missouri-based Perimeter Solutions is a leading provider of solutions for the fire safety and specialty products industries. Perimeter’s contracted Fire Safety business, growing fixed service revenues and geographic diversification support long-term growth and earnings visibility. Favorable industry trends are expected to continue to drive demand for fire-retardant products. 

The company remains focused on expanding its fire prevention and protection business. Its Specialty Products segment continues to broaden earnings sources outside wildfire demand. Recent acquisitions, particularly MMT, are driving sales in this segment. PRM’s strong balance sheet also offers adequate liquidity for growth investments and M&A opportunities. 

Perimeter Solutions has expected earnings growth of 17.2% for 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for PRM’s 2026 earnings has moved up 1.9% over the past 60 days. PRM currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Quaker Chemical: Based in Pennsylvania, Quaker Chemical (doing business as Quaker Houghton) is a global developer, producer and marketer of industrial process fluids and related specialty chemicals. The company continues to outpace underlying markets through new business wins, with momentum in the Asia-Pacific and improving traction in the Americas as prior disruptions ease. KWR is leaning on self-help actions, including a global transformation program to simplify operations and reduce structural costs, while integration and cross-selling broaden the portfolio. Acquisitions remain a steady contributor to consolidated sales growth, with Dipsol a key driver in the Asia-Pacific.

Quaker Chemical has expected earnings growth of 11.8% for the current year. The consensus estimate for KWR’s current-year earnings has been revised 1.7% higher over the past 60 days. Quaker Chemical, carrying a Zacks Rank #2, has an expected long-term earnings per share growth rate of 18.9%.

Element Solutions: Florida-based Element Solutions is a leading specialty chemicals provider, offering innovative and differentiated solutions to its customers across a vast spectrum of industries. ESI is poised for growth, driven by strong execution and strategic positioning in the electronics sector. The company is benefiting from strength in the electronics market. 

ESI is seeing strong organic growth in its Electronics segment. The Micromax acquisition has strengthened its position to build an industry-leading Electronics portfolio. High-value end markets are contributing to a favorable product mix, while the ongoing pricing and productivity initiatives are boosting margins. 

Element Solutions has an expected earnings growth rate of 21.5% for 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ESI’s 2026 earnings has been stable the past 60 days. ESI surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters at an average of roughly 6.3%. ESI currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

These chemicals (including catalysts, surfactants, specialty polymers, coating additives, pesticides and oilfield chemicals) are used based on their performance and have a specific purpose. Specialty chemicals can be single molecules or a combination of molecules referred to as formulations, and they provide a vast range of effects upon which various industries rely. Their compositions significantly influence the performance of the finished products. Specialty chemicals have applications in the manufacturing process of a vast range of products, including paints and coatings, cosmetics, petroleum products, inks and plastics. What's Shaping the Future of the Chemical Specialty Industry? Demand Softness Poses a Headwind: Companies in the chemical specialty space are facing headwinds from weak demand in building and construction as well as industrial end markets, especially in Europe and China, due to economic slowdown. Elevated borrowing costs and inflation have taken a bite out of the residential construction industry. A slower recovery in economic activities in China is hurting demand in that country. Low consumer confidence and high inflation have also dampened demand in Europe. While customer inventory de-stocking is essentially complete, some lingering impacts of the same in certain markets are expected to continue over the near term. The imposition of hefty tariffs has also introduced significant headwinds for the chemical specialty industry. Soft demand conditions, exacerbated by a weak macroeconomic environment and tariff-induced impacts, are likely to weigh on the volumes of chemical specialty companies. Cost Pressure Still a Worry: Specialty chemical makers are facing headwinds from raw-material and energy-cost inflation and supply-chain and freight-transportation disruptions. Some companies are exposed to challenges from elevated logistics and labor costs. Tariffs have led to increased costs for raw materials, resulting in higher production expenses for the industry players. Also, the Middle East conflict and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz have led to significant supply disruptions and feedstock cost pressure. Inflationary pressures are expected to continue in the short term and weigh on the margins of chemical specialty companies. Strategic Actions to Aid Results: The companies in this space are executing a raft of self-help measures, including cost-cutting and productivity improvement, expansion into high-growth markets, restructuring, operational efficiency improvement and actions to strengthen the balance sheet and boost cash flows. The industry participants are aggressively implementing measures to cut costs. These actions are likely to help companies weather macroeconomic challenges. Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Downbeat Prospects The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry is part of the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #166, which places it in the bottom 33% of more than 250 Zacks industries. The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates a bleak near term. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1. Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture. Industry Underperforms Sector & S&P 500 The Zacks Chemicals Specialty industry has underperformed the Zacks S&P 500 composite and the broader Zacks Basic Materials sector over the past year. The industry has gained 5.7% over this period compared with the S&P 500’s rise of 15.2% and the broader sector’s increase of 13.1%. Industry's Current Valuation On the basis of the trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-EBITDA (EV/EBITDA), which is a commonly used multiple for valuing chemical stocks, the industry is currently trading at 10.97X, below the S&P 500’s 17.92X and the sector’s 12.59X. Over the past three years, the industry has traded as high as 13.36X, as low as 9.44X, with a median of 11.77X. 3 Chemical Specialty Stocks to Keep a Close Eye On Perimeter Solutions: Missouri-based Perimeter Solutions is a leading provider of solutions for the fire safety and specialty products industries. Perimeter’s contracted Fire Safety business, growing fixed service revenues and geographic diversification support long-term growth and earnings visibility. Favorable industry trends are expected to continue to drive demand for fire-retardant products. The company remains focused on expanding its fire prevention and protection business. Its Specialty Products segment continues to broaden earnings sources outside wildfire demand. Recent acquisitions, particularly MMT, are driving sales in this segment. PRM’s strong balance sheet also offers adequate liquidity for growth investments and M&A opportunities. Perimeter Solutions has expected earnings growth of 17.2% for 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for PRM’s 2026 earnings has moved up 1.9% over the past 60 days. PRM currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. Quaker Chemical: Based in Pennsylvania, Quaker Chemical (doing business as Quaker Houghton) is a global developer, producer and marketer of industrial process fluids and related specialty chemicals. The company continues to outpace underlying markets through new business wins, with momentum in the Asia-Pacific and improving traction in the Americas as prior disruptions ease. KWR is leaning on self-help actions, including a global transformation program to simplify operations and reduce structural costs, while integration and cross-selling broaden the portfolio. Acquisitions remain a steady contributor to consolidated sales growth, with Dipsol a key driver in the Asia-Pacific. Quaker Chemical has expected earnings growth of 11.8% for the current year. The consensus estimate for KWR’s current-year earnings has been revised 1.7% higher over the past 60 days. Quaker Chemical, carrying a Zacks Rank #2, has an expected long-term earnings per share growth rate of 18.9%. Element Solutions: Florida-based Element Solutions is a leading specialty chemicals provider, offering innovative and differentiated solutions to its customers across a vast spectrum of industries. ESI is poised for growth, driven by strong execution and strategic positioning in the electronics sector. The company is benefiting from strength in the electronics market. ESI is seeing strong organic growth in its Electronics segment. The Micromax acquisition has strengthened its position to build an industry-leading Electronics portfolio. High-value end markets are contributing to a favorable product mix, while the ongoing pricing and productivity initiatives are boosting margins. Element Solutions has an expected earnings growth rate of 21.5% for 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ESI’s 2026 earnings has been stable the past 60 days. ESI surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters at an average of roughly 6.3%. ESI currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). headline: Bear of the Day: Las Vegas Sands (LVS)
html_content:
Las Vegas Sands Corporation develops and operates integrated resorts that combine casinos, hotels, convention space, retail and entertainment.

Its properties are concentrated in two markets: Macao, where it operates The Venetian, The Londoner, The Parisian and Sands Macao, and Singapore, home to Marina Bay Sands. The company sold its Las Vegas assets in 2022 and is now a pure-play Asian gaming operator despite the name.

That concentration was an enormous advantage when both markets were compounding. It is a liability now. Las Vegas Sands has no domestic business to offset weakness abroad, no diversification across regulatory regimes, and a cost structure built for volumes that are no longer showing up at the high end.

The Zacks Rundown

Las Vegas Sands has been badly underperforming the market. A Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), the stock has fallen roughly 43% year to date against a 12% gain for the S&P 500. Shares have been in a well-defined downtrend since the spring and have shown no meaningful ability to hold a rally.

The stock is part of the Zacks Gaming industry group, which currently ranks in the bottom 15% out of more than 250 Zacks Ranked Industries. Because this industry is ranked in the bottom half of all Zacks Ranked Industries, we expect it to underperform the market over the next 3 to 6 months, just as it has over the past year:


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

While individual stocks have the ability to outperform even when included in weak industries, their industry association serves as a headwind for any potential rallies. Stocks in this group are also expected to post below-average earnings growth. With much better alternatives in the current market environment, this stock should be avoided.

Two Straight Misses, Both by the Same Margin

Las Vegas Sands LVS reported third-quarter results earlier this week that missed on both lines and by a wide margin. Adjusted earnings of $0.54 per share came in 23.94% below the $0.71 Zacks Consensus Estimate and fell from $0.78 a year earlier. Revenue of $3.22 billion missed by 3.23% and declined from $3.33 billion.

What makes that print more troubling than a single bad quarter is the one before it. In the prior period, the company earned $0.59 against a $0.77 consensus — a miss of 23.38%. Two consecutive quarters missing by essentially the identical margin is not noise. It suggests the Street's model of this business is structurally wrong, and that analysts have not yet marked down far enough.

The margin story underneath is where the damage lives. Consolidated adjusted property EBITDA fell to $1.119 billion from $1.344 billion, with margin compressing to 34.8% from 40.3% — more than 500 basis points in a single year. Resort operating expenses rose to $2.103 billion from $1.998 billion while revenue declined, which is straightforward operating deleverage.

Singapore is the epicenter. Marina Bay Sands saw revenue fall to $1.294 billion from $1.436 billion. Macao is the subtler problem. Revenue actually rose, to $1.940 billion from $1.906 billion, and management highlighted market share reaching a multi-year high. Yet segment EBITDA fell to $529 million from $601 million and margin compressed to 27.3% from 31.5%. The company is buying share with promotional spending, which is the least durable kind of growth there is.

Deteriorating Forecasts

Analysts have been cutting their numbers, and the estimate trend is firmly negative. The current fiscal year Zacks Consensus Estimate now stands at $3.00 per share on $13.66 billion in revenue. Consistently missing expectations by a wide margin while forward estimates fall is a recipe for stock price underperformance.

Pay particular attention to the bar set for the coming quarter. The consensus calls for $0.80 per share on $3.57 billion — a dramatic sequential recovery from the $0.54 just reported. Given that this company has now missed by roughly 24% twice running, that estimate looks optimistic, and a third disappointment against a visibly high bar would do real damage. These are the types of negative trends that the bears like to see.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Technical Outlook

LVS stock has been in a persistent downtrend for most of 2026. Both the 50-day (blue line) and 200-day (red line) moving averages are sloping downward, and shares have spent the bulk of the year trading beneath them. Every rally attempt has been capped at a progressively lower level, which is the signature of distribution rather than accumulation.


Image Source: StockCharts

Shares would need to reclaim both moving averages and show a genuine inflection in earnings estimate revisions to warrant taking any long positions in the stock.

Final Thoughts

A deteriorating fundamental and technical backdrop shows that this stock doesn't deserve a spot in most portfolios. The fact that LVS is included in one of the worst-performing industry groups adds yet another headwind to a long list of concerns.

Falling future earnings estimates will likely serve as a ceiling to any potential rallies, nurturing the stock's downtrend. Potential investors may want to give this stock the cold shoulder, or perhaps include it as part of a short or hedge strategy.

headline: Bull of the Day: Dollar General (DG)
html_content:
Dollar General Corporation, a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), has spent the past few years quietly rebuilding a business the market had largely written off. The discount retailer stumbled badly through 2023 and 2024 on inventory problems, shrink and a stretched core customer. That turnaround is now showing up in the only place that ultimately matters — the numbers.

Shares have advanced roughly 35% over the past year while the broader retail tape has been anything but hospitable. Relative strength of that kind, paired with four consecutive quarters of meaningful earnings beats, is precisely the combination we look for.

Dollar General is part of the Zacks Retail – Discount Stores industry group, which currently ranks in the top 7% out of more than 250 Zacks Ranked Industries. Because it is ranked in the top half of all Zacks Ranked Industries, we expect this group to outperform over the next 3 to 6 months, just as it has over the past month:


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Stocks in this industry are projected to experience above-average earnings growth while trading at reasonable valuations, a powerful combination that should lead to higher prices over time.

Historical research studies suggest that approximately half of a stock's price appreciation is due to its industry grouping. In fact, the top 50% of Zacks Ranked Industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

It's no secret that investing in stocks that are part of leading industry groups can give us a leg up relative to the market. By focusing on leading stocks within the top 50% of Zacks Ranked Industries, we can dramatically improve our odds of success.

Company Description

Dollar General operates more than 20,000 small-format discount stores across the United States, concentrated in rural and small-town markets that larger competitors have historically underserved. The merchandise mix skews heavily toward consumables — food, cleaning supplies, health and beauty items — with seasonal goods, home products and apparel rounding out the assortment. The company was founded in 1939 and is headquartered in Goodlettsville, Tennessee.

The structural argument here is about location rather than price. Roughly 80% of Dollar General's stores sit in towns of 20,000 people or fewer, where the nearest alternative is often a meaningful drive away. That footprint is extremely difficult to replicate and it makes the chain a convenience business as much as a value business — a distinction that matters when fuel prices climb and household budgets tighten.

It is also worth naming what went wrong, because the recovery only makes sense against it. Dollar General overextended on new store openings, let inventory and shrink get away from it, and watched its core low-income customer absorb two years of cumulative price inflation. Management then slowed unit growth, invested in store labor, and leaned on markdowns and private label. The result has been a steady rebuild, and the fundamentals support that view.

Earnings Momentum and Rising Estimates

Dollar General DG reported fiscal second-quarter results in late August that beat on every line. Adjusted earnings of $2.23 per share rose 19.9% from the year-ago $1.86, and net sales grew 5.2% to $11.29 billion. The company has now delivered a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 19.1%.

The composition of the comp is what I find most encouraging. Same-store sales grew 3.5% on a 2.0% increase in customer traffic and a 1.5% increase in average ticket. Traffic has been the scarce commodity across retail this year — a number of large chains have posted positive comps built entirely on price. Dollar General is bringing more people through the door, and it is doing so while gross margin expands, which argues the gains are not being bought with promotions.

Management responded by raising full-year fiscal 2026 guidance across the board: net sales growth to approximately 4.0–4.3% from 3.7–4.2%, same-store sales to 2.5–2.9% from 2.2–2.7%, and earnings per share to $7.80–$8.00 from $7.20–$7.45.

Analysts have followed. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current fiscal year implies sales growth of 4.3% and earnings growth of 15.9% to $7.94 per share. Rising estimates of this kind are the engine behind the Zacks Rank #1.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Let's Get Technical

DG shares remain above an upward-sloping 50-day (blue line) moving average, and the stock has built a series of higher highs and higher lows over the past 6 months. Volume has expanded on the advances and contracted on the pullbacks, which is the accumulation signature we want to see.


Image Source: StockCharts

This is the kind of stock we want to include in the portfolio — one that is trending well and receiving positive earnings estimate revisions at the same time. Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. As long as that trend remains intact and Dollar General continues to deliver earnings beats, the stock should extend its advance.

Bottom Line

There is a macro argument layered on top of the company-specific one. With core inflation reaccelerating and the consumer increasingly selective, trade-down behavior works in Dollar General's favor. The chain gains share precisely when households tighten up, and we are in one of those stretches.

Backed by a leading industry group, four consecutive earnings beats averaging better than 19%, and a guidance raise that extends well beyond a one-time tariff benefit, it isn't difficult to see why this company is a compelling investment. Dollar General carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) driven by favorable estimate momentum.

Robust fundamentals combined with a strong technical trend certainly justify adding shares to the mix. If you haven't already done so, be sure to put DG on your watchlist.

headline: Should State Street SPDR S&P Dividend ETF (SDY) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
Launched on November 8, 2005, the State Street SPDR S&P Dividend ETF (SDY) is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to provide a broad exposure to the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

The fund is sponsored by State Street Investment Management. It has amassed assets over $22.15 billion, making it one of the largest ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Value

Companies that find themselves in the large cap category typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Considered a more stable option, large cap companies boast more predictable cash flows and are less volatile than their mid and small cap counterparts.

Value stocks have lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios. They also have lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. While value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in nearly all markets when you consider long-term performance, growth stocks are more likely to outpace value stocks in strong bull markets.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.35%, putting it on par with most peer products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 2.36%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

It is important to delve into an ETF's holdings before investing despite the many upsides to these kinds of funds like diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Industrials sector -- about 18.5% of the portfolio. Consumer Staples and Utilities round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Accenture Plc Cl A (ACN) accounts for about 3.35% of total assets, followed by Verizon Communications Inc (VZ) and Chevron Corp (CVX).

The top 10 holdings account for about 20.31% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

SDY seeks to match the performance of the S&P High Yield Dividend Aristocrats Index before fees and expenses. The S&P High Yield Dividend Aristocrats Index measures the performance of the highest dividend yielding S&P Composite 1500 Index constituents that have followed a managed-dividends policy of consistently increasing dividends every year for at least 20 consecutive years.

The ETF has added about 16.92% so far this year and is up about 17.1% in the last one year (as of 10/23/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $135.96 and $159.94.

The ETF has a beta of 0.69 and standard deviation of 11.99% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 158 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

State Street SPDR S&P Dividend ETF carries a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Thus, SDY is a good option for those seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Value area of the market. Investors might also want to consider some other ETF options in the space.

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) and the Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) track a similar index. While Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF has $118.68 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF has $192.91 billion. SCHD has an expense ratio of 0.06% and VTV charges 0.03%.

Bottom-Line

While an excellent vehicle for long term investors, passively managed ETFs are a popular choice among institutional and retail investors due to their low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency.

excerpt: Mutual Fund Report for VWNDX
headline: Is Vanguard Windsor Fund (VWNDX) a Strong Mutual Fund Pick Right Now?
html_content:
Looking for a Large Cap Value fund? You may want to consider Vanguard Windsor Fund (VWNDX) as a possible option. VWNDX bears a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on various forecasting factors like size, cost, and past performance.

Objective

VWNDX is classified in the Large Cap Value segment by Zacks, which is an area full of possibilities. Investors interested in a stable income stream find these mutual funds very appealing because they have a unique investing strategy. Large Cap Value funds invest in stocks with a market capitalization of $10 billion or more, but whose share prices do not reflect their intrinsic value. This tactic often leads to low P/E ratios and high dividend yields; however, these funds' high growth opportunities are often slowed, as large-cap securities are generally in stable industries with low to moderate growth prospects.

History of Fund/Manager

Vanguard Group is based in Malvern, PA, and is the manager of VWNDX. Vanguard Windsor Fund debuted in October of 1958. Since then, VWNDX has accumulated assets of about $4.62 billion, according to the most recently available information. A team of investment professionals is the fund's current manager.

Performance

Of course, investors look for strong performance in funds. This fund carries a 5-year annualized total return of 10.56%, and it sits in the middle third among its category peers. If you're interested in shorter time frames, do not dismiss looking at the fund's 3-year annualized total return of 15.05%, which places it in the bottom third during this time-frame.

It is important to note that the product's returns may not reflect all its expenses. Any fees not reflected would lower the returns. Total returns do not reflect the fund's [%] sale charge. If sales charges were included, total returns would have been lower.

When looking at a fund's performance, it is also important to note the standard deviation of the returns. The lower the standard deviation, the less volatility the fund experiences. Compared to the category average of 11.43%, the standard deviation of VWNDX over the past three years is 11.97%. The standard deviation of the fund over the past 5 years is 15.13% compared to the category average of 13.66%. This makes the fund more volatile than its peers over the past half-decade.

Risk Factors

Investors should note that the fund has a 5-year beta of 0.83, which means it is hypothetically less volatile than the market at large. Another factor to consider is alpha, as it reflects a portfolio's performance on a risk-adjusted basis relative to a benchmark-in this case, the S&P 500. Over the past 5 years, the fund has a negative alpha of -1.27. This means that managers in this portfolio find it difficult to pick securities that generate better-than-benchmark returns.

Holdings

Investigating the equity holdings of a mutual fund is also a valuable exercise. This can show us how the manager is applying their stated methodology, as well as if there are any inherent biases in their approach. For this particular fund, the focus is primarily on equities that are traded in the United States.

Currently, this mutual fund is holding 75.96% in stocks, with an average market capitalization of $265.95 billion. The fund has the heaviest exposure to the following market sectors:

  • Finance
  • Technology
  • Retail Trade
  • Industrial Cyclical

Turnover is about 54%, so those in charge of the fund make fewer trades than its comparable peers.

Expenses

As competition heats up in the mutual fund market, costs become increasingly important. Compared to its otherwise identical counterpart, a low-cost product will be an outperformer, all other things being equal. Thus, taking a closer look at cost-related metrics is vital for investors. In terms of fees, VWNDX is a no load fund. It has an expense ratio of 0.29% compared to the category average of 0.90%. From a cost perspective, VWNDX is actually cheaper than its peers.

Investors should also note that the minimum initial investment for the product is $3,000 and that each subsequent investment needs to be at $1.

Fees charged by investment advisors have not been taken into consideration. Returns would be less if those were included.

Bottom Line

Overall, Vanguard Windsor Fund ( VWNDX ) has a neutral Zacks Mutual Fund rank, and in conjunction with its comparatively similar performance, average downside risk, and lower fees, Vanguard Windsor Fund ( VWNDX ) looks like a somewhat average choice for investors right now.

Over the past 5 years, the fund has a negative alpha of -6.27. This means that managers in this portfolio find it difficult to pick securities that generate better-than-benchmark returns.

Expenses

As competition heats up in the mutual fund market, costs become increasingly important. Compared to its otherwise identical counterpart, a low-cost product will be an outperformer, all other things being equal. Thus, taking a closer look at cost-related metrics is vital for investors. excerpt: Aristotle Funds' PLUDX, POEAX and PLADX combine positive long-term returns, low fees and diversified investment strategies as Fed rate expectations shift.
headline: 3 Aristotle Funds to Buy Amid Shifting Fed Rate Expectations
html_content:
Aristotle Funds has developed into a diversified mutual fund family offering investment options across U.S. and international equities, fixed income and multi-asset strategies. Founded in 2001 as Pacific Funds, the investment company adopted the Aristotle Funds name as it expanded its platform and investment capabilities. The firm follows a multi-manager structure, bringing together specialized investment teams with distinct approaches while benefiting from the resources of a broader organization. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Aristotle Funds managed $14.5 billion in assets.

The broader Aristotle investment organization has expanded significantly through the establishment and acquisition of specialized affiliates. Aristotle Capital Management was formed in 2010, followed by Aristotle Capital Boston in 2014 and Aristotle Atlantic Partners in 2016. Aristotle Pacific Capital was established in 2023, strengthening the organization's fixed-income capabilities. These teams apply different investment disciplines, ranging from fundamental, bottom-up equity research and valuation-focused investing to credit analysis and diversified asset allocation.

Aristotle Funds has continued to broaden its offerings and refine its investment lineup. On July 29, 2026, its Portfolio Optimization Funds were renamed Aristotle Multi-Asset Funds, accompanied by changes to their principal investment strategies. The fixed-income platform also provides investors with exposure to different credit segments and interest-rate sensitivities. As of Sept. 30, 2026, published yield data showed varying income opportunities across its bond strategies, reflecting differences in duration, credit quality and investment mandate.

Aristotle Funds merit consideration in the current environment of elevated interest-rate uncertainty, shifting bond yields and uneven equity-market performance. Its diversified range of equity, fixed-income and multi-asset strategies offers investors different ways to manage risk and pursue returns. However, performance varies across investment teams and market segments.

Astute investors might choose to consider these funds at present. Mutual funds, in general, reduce transaction costs and diversify portfolios without an array of commission charges that are mostly associated with stock purchases (read more: Mutual Funds: Advantages, Disadvantages, and How They Make Investors Money).

We have thus selected three mutual funds that boast a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), have positive three-year and five-year annualized returns and minimum initial investments within $5000, as well as carry a low expense ratio.

Aristotle Ultra Short Income PLUDX invests mainly in short-term, investment-grade, U.S. dollar-denominated fixed and floating-rate debt, including corporate, mortgage-backed, asset-backed, government, agency and money market securities, with duration generally limited to one year.

Ying Qiu has been the lead manager of PLUDX since 2019. The three top holdings for PLUDX are Total Misc. Bonds (39.3%), Palmer Square Loan (2.8%) and Total Cash (2.7%).

PLUDX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 5.4% and 4.1%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.32%. PLUDX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1. To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here.

Aristotle Multi-Asset Capital Opportunities Fund POEAX pursues its objective by investing in a combination of underlying funds, generally remaining fully invested while retaining liquidity reserves for redemptions. It may allocate substantial assets to a single underlying fund.

Carleton J. Muench has been the lead manager of POEAX since 2006. The three top holdings for POEAX are Aristotle Core Equity (32.2%), Aristotle Growth Equity (13.1%) and iShares S&P 500 Value (12%).

POEAX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 18.8% and 8.2%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.70%. POEAX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

Aristotle Short Duration Income PLADX invests in income-generating debt securities, mainly investment-grade corporate, asset-backed, mortgage-related, government and agency debt, while also permitting exposure to high-yield bonds and floating-rate senior loans.

Michael Marzouk has been the lead manager of PLADX since 2011. The three top holdings for PLADX are Total Misc. Bonds (59%), U.S. Treasury Note Bond (3%) and Total Cash (3%).

PLADX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 4.6% and 2.6%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.75%. PLADX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

excerpt: MNTK, CEG and GEV stand out as alternative energy leaders, with rising power demand and renewable energy investments shaping growth prospects.
headline: 3 Alternative Energy Stocks to Watch Amid Rising Power Demand
html_content:
The global wind power market is expected to grow steadily, driven by supportive government policies, decarbonization efforts, energy security concerns and advancements in turbine technology. Meanwhile, rising electric vehicle adoption, declining battery costs and government incentives are boosting demand for clean energy and charging infrastructure. However, higher interest rates pose challenges for capital-intensive renewable energy projects by increasing borrowing costs, pressuring margins and potentially delaying investments. The forerunners in the U.S. alternative energy industry are GE Vernova Inc. GEV, Constellation Energy Corporation CEG and Montauk Renewables MNTK. 

About the Industry

The Zacks Alternative Energy - Other  industry can be fundamentally segregated into two sets of companies. While one group is involved in the generation and distribution of alternative energy and electricity from sources like wind, natural gas, biofuel, hydro and geothermal, the other is engaged in the development, design and installation of renewable projects involving these alternative energy sources. The industry comprises a handful of companies offering fuel cell energy solutions, which have recently gained traction as affordable and cleaner energy alternatives. According to the International Energy Agency, global energy investments are likely to reach $3.4 trillion in 2026. Such investments provide strong growth opportunities for industry participants.

3 Trends Shaping the Future of the Alternative Energy Industry

Wind Power Market Poised for Sustained Growth: The global wind power market continues to expand, driven by supportive government policies for renewable energy, rising focus on decarbonization and energy security, and improving cost competitiveness. Technological advancements, particularly the development of larger and more efficient turbines, are helping wind farms generate more electricity from existing sites while reducing production costs and enhancing project profitability. These factors are expected to drive sustained growth in the industry over the long term. According to a Mordor Intelligence report, the United States Wind Energy Market size was valued at 161.20 GW in 2025 and is estimated to grow from 167.92 GW in 2026 to 205.93 GW by 2031, at a CAGR of 4.17% during the period.

EV Market Surge to Accelerate Clean Energy Adoption: Electric vehicle (EV) companies and charging networks are increasingly using renewable energy sources like solar and wind to power vehicles, reducing fossil fuel usage and emissions. EV adoption is being supported by governments, especially the U.S. government, via subsidies, tax credits, grants and non-cash incentives. Another key driver is the steady decline in battery costs, which lowers the overall price of EVs and makes them more competitive with gasoline-powered cars. These factors have contributed to strong global sales growth. According to a Benchmark Mineral Intelligence report, nearly 2.15 million EVs were sold globally in September 2026, bringing year-to-date 2026 EV sales to 15.5 million. Per a report by Grand View Research, the global EV market size is projected to grow from $2.4 trillion in 2026 to $12.6 trillion by 2033, at a CAGR of 26.7% during the period. This strong growth outlook benefits clean energy companies, particularly those that operate large EV charging networks in the United States, as rising EV adoption directly increases demand for charging infrastructure and its related services.

Higher Interest Rates Pose Challenges for Alternative Energy Growth: The Federal Reserve’s September 2026 interest rate hike, which raised the federal fund target range to 3.75-4.00%, has increased financing concerns for the alternative energy sector. Since renewable energy projects require substantial upfront capital and often depend on debt financing, higher borrowing costs can weaken project economics, pressure profit margins and delay new investments. Capital-intensive technologies such as offshore wind, carbon capture and low-carbon hydrogen may face greater challenges due to their financial and execution risks. Even established renewable energy operators with long-term power purchase agreements may struggle to offset rising financing expenses when electricity prices are contractually fixed, potentially limiting cash flows, distributions and future growth.

Zacks Industry Rank Reflects Gloomy Outlook

The Zacks Alternative Energy industry is housed within the broader Zacks Oils-Energy sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #152, which places it in the bottom 38% of more than 247 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Ranks of all the member stocks, indicates bright near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

The industry’s position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is due to a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts have lost confidence in this group’s earnings growth potential over the past few months. The industry’s bottom-line estimate for the current fiscal year has moved down 8.9% to $2.44 since July 31.

Before we present a few alternative energy stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock-market performance and valuation.

Industry Lags S&P 500 & Sector

The Zacks Alternative Energy- Other Industry has underperformed the Zacks S&P 500 and its sector over the past year. The stocks in this industry have collectively declined 8.3% in the past year against the Zacks Oil-Energy sector’s 41.4% growth. The Zacks S&P 500 composite has gained 15.8% in the same time frame.

One-Year Price Performance

Industry's Current Valuation

On the basis of the trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA ratio, which is commonly used for valuing alternative energy stocks, the industry is currently trading at 19.22X compared with the S&P 500’s 18.00X and the sector’s 6.38X.

Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 26.77X, as low as 9.93X and at the median of 15.38X. 

EV-EBITDA Ratio (TTM)

3 Alternative Energy Stocks to Watch

Montauk Renewables: Based in Pittsburgh, PA, the company is a fully integrated renewable energy company. MNTK specializes in the management, recovery and conversion of biogas into renewable energy. Its second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA increased 144.5% to $12.3 million, while renewable natural gas (RNG) production grew 3% to 1.5 million MMBtu and renewable identification numbers (RINs) sold rose 29.1% to 14.3 million. The company also began generating electricity at its Turkey, NC, facility in July and continued expanding feedstock collection agreements with farms, supporting potential future growth. 

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Montauk Renewables’ 2026 sales implies an improvement of 20.8% year over year. The consensus estimate for 2026 earnings suggests an increase of 1,100% year over year. The company currently carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here. 

Price & Consensus: MNTK



 

Constellation Energy: Based in Baltimore, MD, the company produces and sells electric power, natural gas and energy management services. It serves customers nationwide through its competitive retail platform. Constellation Energy is among the lowest carbon emitters of U.S. investor-owned generators. Its strategy is built around the nation’s largest carbon-free nuclear fleet, complemented by natural gas, oil, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar resources. On Oct. 6, 2026, CEG announced a long-term agreement with Google to add 890 MW of new nuclear capacity to the PJM grid through upgrades at 11 existing nuclear units across Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey. The companies also signed a separate 15-year agreement covering an additional 2,700 MW of power supply within PJM and expanded their technology partnership to deploy Google Cloud and Gemini Enterprise for AI-driven energy operations. 

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Constellation Energy’s 2026 sales implies an improvement of 39.5% year over year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings suggests an improvement of 29.6% year over year. The company currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). 

Price & Consensus: CEG



 

GE Vernova: Based Cambridge, MA, the company is a global electric power company. It designs, manufactures, delivers, and services technologies that generate, transfer, orchestrate, convert and store electricity. On Oct. 20, 2026, GE Vernova announced that it has secured an order from Songon Energies S.A. to supply a 9E gas turbine and generator for the 372-MW Songon combined-cycle power plant near Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, with the facility expected to begin operations in 2029. The project will also provide opportunities for GE Vernova to supply high-voltage substation equipment, digital software and long-term services. The contract could benefit GE Vernova by strengthening its Gas Power business, expanding its presence in West Africa and generating additional revenue opportunities from equipment, digital solutions and recurring service agreements over the project's lifecycle.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company’s 2026 sales implies an improvement of 21.7% year over year. The consensus estimate for 2026 earnings suggests 72.4% growth year over year. The company currently has a Zacks Rank #3.

Price & Consensus: GEV

headline: GE Vernova vs. Public Service Enterprise: Which Is the Better Buy Stock Now?
html_content:
GE Vernova GEV and Public Service Enterprise Group PEG are well positioned to capitalize on the growing need for electricity and investments in power infrastructure. The increasing adoption of electric vehicles, electrification of industrial operations, expansion of data centers, and rising reliance on digital technologies are driving electricity consumption, creating opportunities for power-equipment manufacturers and utility providers.

Both companies are benefiting from structural changes in the energy sector. The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and data centers is boosting demand for reliable power, while the transition toward cleaner energy sources and the need to modernize aging transmission and distribution networks are accelerating investments across the industry. 

GE Vernova stands to benefit from growing demand for power-generation equipment, grid technologies and related services, while Public Service Enterprise is poised to gain from investments in its regulated utility infrastructure, supporting sustained earnings growth under an established regulatory framework.

Against this backdrop, comparing the two companies' financial performance, growth prospects, valuation metrics and earnings outlook can help determine which stock offers the more attractive investment opportunity at present.

Factors Acting in Favor of GEV Stock

GE Vernova has a balanced investment profile. Demand is supported by a broad electricity cycle tied to grid upgrades, electrification, data centers, reliability and energy security, giving the company better revenue visibility than a typical equipment supplier. Power remains the clearest strength, aided by gas turbine demand, pricing, capacity expansion and future service opportunities.

On Oct. 20, 2026, GE Vernova announced that it had secured an order from Songon Energies S.A. to supply a 9E gas turbine and generator for the 372-MW Songon combined-cycle power plant near Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, with the facility expected to begin operations in 2029. The project will also provide opportunities for GE Vernova to supply high-voltage substation equipment, digital software and long-term services. The contract could benefit GE Vernova by strengthening its Gas Power business, expanding its presence in West Africa and generating additional revenue opportunities from equipment, digital solutions and recurring service agreements over the project's lifecycle.

Factors Acting in Favor of PEG Stock

Public Service Enterprise is a regulated utility that owns and operates electric transmission and distribution networks, primarily in New Jersey. Rather than selling equipment, the company invests directly in utility infrastructure, including transmission lines, substations, grid reliability projects and clean-energy initiatives. Because many of these investments are made within a regulated framework, PSEG typically earns a predictable return approved by regulators, providing relatively stable cash flows and earnings growth.

The company’s investment plan remains centered on regulated infrastructure, which provides a clear path for rate-base expansion. For 2026-2030, PSEG continues to target $24-$28 billion of total capital spending, with more than 90% directed to regulated investments. The $22.5-$25.5 billion regulated program is expected to support 6-7.5% compound annual growth in rate base through 2030. PSEG expects to fund the five-year capital plan without issuing new equity or selling assets, limiting dilution while preserving capacity for continued dividend growth.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for GEV & PEG?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for GE Vernova’s 2026 earnings per share (EPS) indicates growth of 72.41% year over year. GEV’s long-term (three to five years) earnings growth rate is 19.21%.
 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Public Service Enterprise’s 2026 EPS implies growth of 8.15%. PEG’s long-term earnings growth rate is 6.09%.

 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Valuation for GEV & PEG

GEV shares trade at a forward 12-month price/sales (P/S F12M) of 4.26X compared with PEG’s 2.79X.

 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

GEV & PEG’s Return on Equity (ROE)

ROE measures how efficiently a company is utilizing its shareholders’ funds to generate profits. GE Vernova’s current ROE is 42.42% compared with Public Service Enterprise’s 12.42%.

GEV & PEG’s Price Performance

In the past year, shares of GE Vernova have risen 39% while those of Public Service Enterprise have declined 12.1%.

 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

GEV or PEG: Which Is a Better Choice Now?

GE Vernova benefits from rising electricity demand, grid modernization and strong gas turbine demand, with new international orders creating opportunities in equipment, digital solutions and long-term services. PSEG offers stable earnings growth through regulated utility investments, expanding grid infrastructure and a long-term capital plan focused on predictable returns and sustained dividend growth.

Our choice at the moment is GE Vernova, given its stronger ROE, and better earnings growth and price performance than Public Service Enterprise. Both GEV and PEG carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) at present. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Heartland Express Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Heartland Express, Inc. HTLD need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec. 18, 2026 $5.00 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Heartland Express shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Heartland Express is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Transportation - Truck industry that ranks in the Bottom 36% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, no analysts have increased their earnings estimates for the current quarter, while two analysts have revised their estimates downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from 5 cents per share to 2 cents in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Heartland Express right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

excerpt: Wondering how to pick strong, market-beating stocks for your investment portfolio? Look no further than the Zacks Rank.
headline: The Zacks Rank Explained: How to Find Strong Buy Computer and Technology Stocks
html_content:
Building a successful investment portfolio takes skill and hard work, no matter if you're a growth, value, income, or momentum-focused investor.

How do you find the right combination of stocks that will generate returns that could fund your retirement, or your kids' college tuition, or your short- and long-term savings goals?

Enter the Zacks Rank.

What is the Zacks Rank?

A unique, proprietary stock-rating model, the Zacks Rank uses earnings estimate revisions, or changes to a company's earnings expectations, to help investors create a winning portfolio.

There are four main factors behind the Zacks Rank: Agreement, Magnitude, Upside, and Surprise.

Agreement is the extent to which all brokerage analysts are revising their earnings estimates in the same direction. The greater the percentage of analysts revising their estimates higher, the better chance the stock will outperform.

Magnitude is the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate for the current and next fiscal years.

Upside is the difference between the most accurate estimate, which is calculated by Zacks, and the consensus estimate.

Surprise is made up of a company's last few quarters' earnings per share surprises; companies with a positive earnings surprise are more likely to beat expectations in the future.

Each one of these factors is given a raw score that's recalculated every night, and then compiled into the Zacks Rank. Using this data, stocks are classified into five groups, ranging from "Strong Buy" to "Strong Sell."

The Power of Institutional Investors

The Zacks Rank also allows individual investors, or retail investors, to benefit from the power of institutional investors.

Institutional investors are the professionals who manage the trillions of dollars invested in mutual funds, investment banks, and hedge funds. Studies have shown that these investors can and do move the market due to the large amounts of money they invest with. Because of this, the market tends to move in the same direction as institutional investors.

These investors are known for designing valuation models that focus on earnings and earnings expectations in order to figure out the fair value of a company and its shares. If earnings estimates are raised, it puts a higher value on a company.

With these changes, institutional investors will act, usually buying stocks with rising estimates and selling those with falling estimates. An increase in earnings expectations can potentially lead to higher stock prices and bigger gains for the investor.

Retail investors who get in at the first sign of upward revisions have a distinct advantage over larger investors since it can often take weeks, if not months, for an institutional investor to build a position. They'll also benefit from the expected institutional buying that could follow.

Not only can the Zacks Rank help you take advantage of trends in earnings estimate revisions, but it can also provide a way to get into stocks that are highly sought after by professionals.

How to Invest with the Zacks Rank

The Zacks Rank is known for transforming investment portfolios. In fact, a portfolio of Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks has beaten the market in 26 of the last 32 years, with an average annual return of +23.82%.

Moreover, stocks with a new #1 (Strong Buy) ranking have some of the biggest profit potential, while those that fell to a #4 (Sell) or #5 (Strong Sell) have some of the worst.

Let's take a look at HP (HPQ), which was added to the Zacks Rank #1 list on September 25, 2026. Headquartered in Palo Alto, CA, HP Inc. is the surviving entity following the November 2015 split of Hewlett-Packard Company into publicly traded entities, Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company and HP Inc. The undivided entity was founded in 1939.

For fiscal 2026, six analysts revised their earnings estimate upwards in the last 60 days, and the Zacks Consensus Estimate has increased $0.25 to $3.23 per share. HPQ boasts an average earnings surprise of 9.4%.

Analysts are expecting earnings to grow 3.5% for the current fiscal year, with revenue forecasted to rise 8.5%.

HPQ has been moving higher over the past four weeks as well, up 8.4% compared to the S&P 500's loss of 1.2%.

Bottom Line

With a #1 (Strong Buy) ranking, positive trend in earnings estimate revisions, and strong market momentum, HP should be on investors' shortlist.

excerpt: NVEC's Q2 revenues fall 8% y/y as medical and defense sales weaken, while robotics demand and distributor growth support its outlook.
headline: NVE Corp Stock Falls 33% After Y/Y Earnings Decline in Q2
html_content:
Shares of NVE Corporation NVEC have fallen 33% since reporting second-quarter fiscal 2027 results. This compares with the S&P 500’s 0.5% return over the same period. Over the past month, the stock has lost 35.9%, while the S&P 500 inched up 0.4%.

Earnings & Revenue Performance

NVEC reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $5.83 million, down 8% from $6.35 million in the year-ago quarter. The decline reflected weaker product sales, partially offset by higher contract research and development revenues. Net income decreased 4% year over year to $3.17 million from $3.31 million in the prior-year quarter. Earnings per share declined to 65 cents from 68 cents in the prior-year period.

NVE Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NVE Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NVE Corporation Quote

NVEC's Product Sales Decline Amid Customer Order Adjustments

Product sales decreased 9% to $5.58 million from $6.14 million in the prior-year quarter. Management attributed the decline primarily to a temporary inventory adjustment at a major medical device customer and a 95% reduction in defense product sales.

Principal financial officer Daniel Nelson explained that medical device customers' inventory adjustments can create short-term ordering fluctuations, while defense revenues remain sensitive to government procurement cycles.

However, distributor sales surged 67% year over year, supported by improving industry conditions, and demand for new and existing commercial products. Management indicated that distributor sales growth accelerated during the quarter.

Contract research and development revenues increased 25% to approximately $259,000 from $208,000 in the prior-year quarter, reflecting progress on existing contracts.

NVEC's Operating Margins Reflect Higher Administrative Costs

Gross profit decreased to $4.56 million from $4.97 million in the year-ago quarter. Nevertheless, the gross margin remained strong at approximately 78%.

Operating expenses increased 4% year over year to $1.36 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses rose 44% to approximately $630,000 due to higher director option grant-date stock prices.

Research and development expenses declined 17% to approximately $727,000, reflecting staffing redeployment.

Operating income decreased to $3.21 million from $3.66 million in the prior-year quarter, resulting in an operating margin of approximately 55%.

The effective income tax rate declined to 14% from 20%, primarily benefiting from favorable tax law changes. This reduction helped cushion the impacts of lower operating earnings, supporting a net profit margin of approximately 54%.

NVEC Reports Strong H1 Growth & Cash Generation

Despite second-quarter weakness, NVEC's first-half fiscal 2027 revenues increased 36% year over year to $16.9 million from $12.5 million.

Product sales increased 35%, while contract research and development revenues advanced 38%. Net income climbed 39% to $9.57 million, with earnings increasing to $1.97 per share from $1.42.

The operating cash flow reached $11.1 million during the first six months compared with $8 million a year earlier.

Cash and marketable securities totaled $44.4 million at September-end, up from $43.5 million at March-end. Management noted that operating cash generation exceeded dividend payments and capital expenditure.

Management Highlights Robotics Opportunities & Revenue Recovery

President and CEO Peter Eames emphasized opportunities in robotics, industrial automation and power conversion.

During the quarter, NVEC introduced miniature wafer-level chip-scale sensors measuring 0.55 millimeters square and a family of seven gear sensor variants designed for precision motion applications.

Eames highlighted early design wins and growing customer interest, although initial orders remain relatively small.

Management expects medical device and defense sales to recover in the third quarter, with revenues returning to growth. Second-half fiscal 2027 revenues are expected to remain broadly consistent with the first-half levels.

Nelson also projected an effective tax rate of 14-16% for at least the remainder of fiscal 2027.

Other Developments

NVEC completed a leadership transition in August, appointing Peter Eames president and CEO. Former CEO Dan Baker became chairman, replacing Terry Glarner.

The company also appointed Carolyn Valentine to its board, expanding membership from five to seven directors.

Separately, NVEC declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1 per share, payable Nov. 30, 2026, to shareholders of record as of Nov. 2, 2026.

headline: Concentra Group Holdings Parent, Inc. (CON) Hits Fresh High: Is There Still Room to Run?
html_content:
Shares of Concentra Group (CON) have been strong performers lately, with the stock up 15.5% over the past month. The stock hit a new 52-week high of $40 in the previous session. Concentra has gained 103.1% since the start of the year compared to the 6.3% gain for the Zacks Medical sector and the 9.7% return for the Zacks Medical Services industry.

What's Driving the Outperformance?

The stock has a great record of positive earnings surprises, as it hasn't missed our earnings consensus estimate in any of the last four quarters. In its last earnings report on August 6, 2026, Concentra reported EPS of $0.52 versus consensus estimate of $0.42 while it beat the consensus revenue estimate by 2.28%.

For the current fiscal year, Concentra is expected to post earnings of $1.65 per share on $2.35 in revenues. This represents a 20.44% change in EPS on a 8.66% change in revenues. For the next fiscal year, the company is expected to earn $1.84 per share on $2.49 in revenues. This represents a year-over-year change of 11.5% and 5.98%, respectively.

Valuation Metrics

Though Concentra has recently hit a 52-week high, what is next for Concentra? A key aspect of this question is taking a look at valuation metrics in order to determine if the company is due for a pullback from this level.

On this front, we can look at the Zacks Style Scores, as these give investors a variety of ways to comb through stocks (beyond looking at the Zacks Rank of a security). These styles are represented by grades running from A to F in the categories of Value, Growth, and Momentum, while there is a combined VGM Score as well. Investors should consider the style scores a valuable tool that can help you to pick the most appropriate Zacks Rank stocks based on their individual investment style.

Concentra has a Value Score of B. The stock's Growth and Momentum Scores are A and D, respectively, giving the company a VGM Score of A.

In terms of its value breakdown, the stock currently trades at 24.2X current fiscal year EPS estimates, which is a premium to the peer industry average of 18X. On a trailing cash flow basis, the stock currently trades at 20X versus its peer group's average of 11.6X. Additionally, the stock has a PEG ratio of 1.45. This isn't enough to put the company in the top echelon of all stocks we cover from a value perspective.

Zacks Rank

We also need to look at the Zacks Rank for the stock, as this is even more important than the company's VGM Score. Fortunately, Concentra currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) thanks to a solid earnings estimate revision trend.

Since we recommend that investors select stocks carrying Zacks Rank of 1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) and Style Scores of A or B, it looks as if Concentra meets the list of requirements. Thus, it seems as though Concentra shares could still be poised for more gains ahead.

How Does CON Stack Up to the Competition?

Shares of CON have been soaring, and the company still appears to be a decent choice, but what about the rest of the industry? One industry peer that looks good is Elevance Health, Inc. (ELV). ELV has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) and a Value Score of A, a Growth Score of B, and a Momentum Score of F.

Earnings were strong last quarter. Elevance Health, Inc. beat our consensus estimate by 50.00%, and for the current fiscal year, ELV is expected to post earnings of $29.45 per share on revenue of $195.52 billion.

Shares of Elevance Health, Inc. have gained 11.8% over the past month, and currently trade at a forward P/E of 16.37X and a P/CF of 11.85X.

The Medical Services industry may rank in the bottom 62% of all the industries we have in our universe, but there still looks like there are some nice tailwinds for CON and ELV, even beyond their own solid fundamental situation.
