headline: Analysts Estimate California Resources Corporation (CRC) to Report a Decline in Earnings: What to Look Out for
html_content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year decline in earnings on higher revenues when California Resources Corporation (CRC) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 2, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.94 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -35.6%.

Revenues are expected to be $947.97 million, up 10.9% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 38.55% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for California Resources?

For California Resources, the Most Accurate Estimate is the same as the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that there are no recent analyst views which differ from what have been considered to derive the consensus estimate. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of 0%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #3.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that California Resources will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that California Resources would post earnings of $1.31 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.99, delivering a surprise of -24.43%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates two times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

California Resources doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

An Industry Player's Expected Results

Among the stocks in the Zacks Oil and Gas - Exploration and Production - United States industry, Cheniere Energy (LNG), is soon expected to post earnings of $4.06 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of -14.5%. This quarter's revenue is expected to be $5.38 billion, up 21% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for Cheniere Energy has been revised 3.8% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. However, a higher Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +12.15%.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), this Earnings ESP indicates that Cheniere Energy will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

Stay on top of upcoming earnings announcements with the Zacks Earnings Calendar.

Should You Invest in California Resources Corporation (CRC)?

Before you invest in California Resources Corporation (CRC), want to know the best stocks to buy for the next 30 days? Check out Zacks Investment Research for our free report on the 7 best stocks to buy.

Zacks Investment Research has been committed to providing investors with tools and independent research since 1978. For more than a quarter century, the Zacks Rank stock-rating system has more than doubled the S&P 500 with an average gain of +24.08% per year. (These returns cover a period from January 1, 1988 through May 6, 2024.)

excerpt: ASRV's Q3 earnings per share rise year over year, supported by improved net interest margins, stronger wealth management fees and better asset quality, despite declining loan balances and rising expenses.
headline: AmeriServ Stock Rises 9% as Q3 Earnings Improve Year Over Year
html_content:
Shares of AmeriServ Financial, Inc. ASRV have gained 8.9% since the company reported its earnings for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026. This compares with the S&P 500 index’s 1.2% decline over the same period. Over the past month, ASRV shares have advanced 3.7%, outperforming the S&P 500’s 1.1% decrease.

AmeriServ reported third-quarter 2026 earnings per share of 18 cents, which increased 20% from 15 cents recorded in the prior-year quarter. 

Net interest income rose $0.4 million, or 4%, while non-interest income increased $0.1 million, or 2.7%. 

Net income of $3.1 million indicated a 21.9% rise from $2.5 million in the year-ago quarter.

AmeriServ Financial, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

AmeriServ Financial, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | AmeriServ Financial, Inc. Quote

AmeriServ's Net Interest Margin and Balance Sheet Trends

Net interest margin expanded 14 basis points year over year to 3.41% in the third quarter, benefiting from effective asset and deposit pricing strategies and a steeper U.S. Treasury yield curve.

Average investment securities increased 21.8% to $311.5 million, reflecting higher loan prepayments, deposit growth and attractive securities yields. Consequently, investment interest income increased 25.7% during the quarter.

Conversely, average loans declined 5.9%, or $62.5 million, as commercial real estate loan repayments exceeded originations. This contributed to a 5.9% decline in loan interest income.

Average deposits totaled $1.2 billion, while the average loan-to-deposit ratio stood at 81%. Total interest expense declined 8.7%, reflecting lower funding costs.

Asset Quality Improves, While Expenses Increase

AmeriServ recorded a $0.003 million recovery of provision for credit losses, compared with a $0.4 million provision in the prior-year quarter. This improvement reflected favorable historical loan loss trends and reduced reserve requirements following portfolio contraction.

Non-performing assets declined 3.8% from year-end 2025 to $8.2 million. Non-performing loans represented 0.77% of total loans at Sept. 30, 2026, while the allowance for credit losses covered 169% of non-performing loans.

However, non-interest expenses increased 1.5% during the quarter, primarily reflecting higher professional fees and technology-related spending.

Professional fees rose $0.7 million due to expanded consulting services, partially offset by lower other expenses and a favorable pension settlement credit.

Wealth Management Supports Fee Income

Wealth management fees increased $0.6 million during the quarter, including a $0.4 million transition payment associated with moving the company's broker-dealer relationship to Ameriprise Financial Services.

Wealth management assets reached $2.8 billion at September 30, reflecting 4.5% growth since year-end 2025. Market appreciation contributed to higher fee income.

Nevertheless, a $0.4 million loss on trading securities and lower bank-owned life insurance revenues partially offset these gains.

Management Commentary and Outlook

President and CEO Jeffrey A. Stopko attributed record quarterly earnings to revenue growth, improving asset quality and effective balance sheet management. He also highlighted progress in restructuring wealth management operations and improving operating efficiency.

Management expects favorable net interest margin performance to continue into the fourth quarter of 2026. The company also emphasized its capital strength and capacity for future lending. 

Other Developments

AmeriServ continued upgrading its core banking processing system during the quarter, contributing to higher technology expenses. The company also advanced its wealth management restructuring through the broker-dealer transition.

Additionally, the board declared a quarterly cash dividend of 3 cents per common share, payable Nov. 16, 2026, to shareholders of record on Nov. 2. The dividend represents a 2.6% annualized yield based on the Oct. 16 closing share price.

excerpt: D-Wave Quantum plunges 30.5% in a month ahead of Q3 earnings. Can rising bookings and quantum advances offset widening losses and lofty valuation?
headline: QBTS Stock Slides Ahead of Q3 Earnings: Is It Time to Sell or Hold?
html_content:
D-Wave Quantum QBTS faces rising pressure heading into November, raising questions about whether the stock’s persistent weakness reflects deteriorating investor sentiment, valuation concerns or a disconnect between its technological progress and near-term commercial prospects.

As the chart shows below, QBTS fell 30.5% over the 30-day period beginning Sept. 28, 2026, underperforming Rigetti Computing RGTI, down 27.8%, and Quantum Computing QUBT, down 23.5%. The computer and technology market, meanwhile, declined just 5.9%. QBTS has also lost nearly 38% over the past six months.

One-Month Price Performance


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Recent Developments Offer Hope, but Financial Performance Remains Mixed

QBTS’ upcoming third-quarter 2026 results should provide more insight. However, recent announcements show continued progress. D-Wave delivered Italy’s first annealing quantum computer in October.  In the same month, it extended its quantum manufacturing collaboration with SkyWater Technology and launched a gate-model simulator beta program. It also finalized an agreement providing access to up to $100 million in U.S. CHIPS and Science Act funding in September.

The financial picture remains mixed. D-Wave reported second-quarter revenues of $3.1 million, essentially flat year over year, while adjusted EBITDA losses widened 85% to $37.1 million. First-half bookings surged 1,120% to $35.5 million, but investors need evidence of conversion into revenues.

Broader market conditions add another layer of uncertainty. Reuters reported on Oct. 23 that investors were questioning the sustainability of AI-related spending amid technology-stock weakness and an impending Federal Reserve decision.

Against this backdrop, QBTS’ November earnings report could prove pivotal in assessing whether commercial progress can justify investor confidence and reverse its deteriorating share-price trend.

QBTS Trades Below Key Moving Averages as Bearish Momentum Persists

QBTS’ technical indicators reinforce its recent weakness. As of October 23, 2026, the stock traded well below its 50-day and 200-day SMAs. Trading below both averages signals sustained selling pressure, while the 50-day SMA’s position below the 200-day SMA indicates the deteriorating price trend. With previous rebounds failing to sustain momentum, now it's time to watch whether upcoming third-quarter results can restore confidence or whether valuation and profitability concerns will continue to weigh on the stock.

QBTS 50-to-200 Day SMA


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

QBTS Valuation Remains Lofty Despite a Discount to Rigetti

D-Wave Quantum’s valuation remains elevated, with its trailing 12-month price-to-sales (P/S) at 58.68X versus 5.47X for the broader market. While QBTS trades at a discount to Rigetti Computing’s 61.26X, it remains considerably more expensive than Quantum Computing’s 29.58X. This premium suggests investors are pricing in substantial future growth, leaving the stock vulnerable if commercial progress falls short of expectations.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Why Holding QBTS May Still Make Sense Despite Near-Term Headwinds

Despite its steep decline, selling QBTS solely on recent weakness may be premature for investors with a high-risk tolerance and a long-term investment horizon. D-Wave’s growing bookings, progress in gate-model quantum computing and access to potential CHIPS Act funding offer reasons to monitor its longer-term growth prospects. However, its elevated valuation and widening losses warrant caution. This Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) stock supports a neutral stance rather than an aggressive buy or sell call, suggesting investors should weigh the company’s commercial progress against execution and valuation risks. excerpt: Sterling Infrastructure (STRL) stock has plunged more than 60% from its all-time high of over $1,000 a share, potentially creating a buying opportunity ahead of Q3 earnings.
headline: Sterling Infrastructure (STRL): Time to Buy the Dip Before Q3 Earnings?
html_content:
Sterling Infrastructure STRL stock has fallen more than 60% from its 52-week and all-time high of over $1,000 a share, putting the infrastructure construction company on investors' radars ahead of its Q3 results on Wednesday, October 28, after the market closes.

With STRL still up 400% in the last three years and trading near $360 a share, the steep selloff may present a compelling buying opportunity as Sterling continues to benefit from surging demand for AI data centers, advanced manufacturing facilities, and other critical infrastructure projects.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Sterling's Q3 Expectations

Sterling is expected to deliver another quarter of impressive growth, with the Zacks Consensus Estimate calling for Q3 earnings of $6.07 per share, representing a 74% increase from EPS of $3.48 in the prior-year quarter.

Quarterly revenue is projected to climb nearly 70% to $1.17 billion compared to $689.02 million a year ago, largely driven by the company's E-Infrastructure Solutions segment, which supports the construction of data centers, semiconductor facilities, and other large-scale industrial projects.

Notably, Sterling has surpassed earnings expectations for 14 consecutive quarters, posting an impressive average EPS surprise of 27.21% in its last four reports.  

Furthermore, Sterling ended Q2 with a record $4.33 billion backlog, up 116% year over year and providing considerable revenue visibility as demand for mission-critical infrastructure continues to accelerate.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

STRL's Valuation Looks Much More Attractive

Following its dramatic pullback, Sterling stock trades at 18X forward earnings, a much more reasonable valuation considering the company's exceptional growth trajectory.

Encouragingly, STRL now trades at a discount to the benchmark S&P 500 and its Zacks Engineering - R and D Services industry average, while trading well below its decade-long peak of 49X forward earnings and closer to its median of 14X during this period.

Adding to the appeal, Sterling raised its full-year 2026 guidance following Q2, projecting adjusted EPS of $19.70-$20.30 per share, with the $20 midpoint representing an 84% increase from 2025.

Meanwhile, revenue is expected to reach $4-$4.15 billion, reflecting roughly 64% growth at the midpoint.

Although concerns about elevated AI infrastructure spending and the sustainability of hyperscaler capital expenditures remain risks, Sterling's rapidly expanding backlog and earnings outlook suggest the recent selloff may be excessive.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Bottom Line

Sterling Infrastructure stands out as one of the more intriguing buy-the-dip targets ahead of its Q3 earnings, particularly for investors seeking exposure to the ongoing AI infrastructure buildout at a more reasonable valuation.

Supporting this outlook, STRL currently sports a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), with its robust earnings momentum, substantial backlog, and increasingly attractive valuation suggesting meaningful upside potential if Sterling delivers another strong quarterly report.

excerpt: Sonoco's downbeat earnings revisions picture lands it a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) right now.
headline: Bear of the Day: Sonoco (SON)
html_content:
Sonoco SON is a packaging giant serving big clients across food & beverage, household products, automotive, and beyond.  

The global packaging firm's earnings outlook has tanked over the last year and a half as Sonoco struggles against ongoing inflation pressures, weaker volumes, and other headwinds. SON missed our Q3 adjusted earnings estimates by 5% and lowered its outlook once again.

Sonoco’s downbeat earnings revisions picture lands it a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) right now.

Should Investors Avoid SON Stock Right Now?

Sonoco is a packaging manufacturing powerhouse that works closely with globally recognized brands. The South Carolina-based company’s packaging portfolio includes Rigid Paper, Metal, Industrial Paper, and Industrial & Specialty offerings.

SON sells its array of packaging products to firms across the economy, from Food & Beverage, Household Products, and Beauty & Personal Care to Construction, Automotive, and beyond.

Sonoco has grown its revenue rather steadily over the last 25 years, outside of a few cyclical-based declines. The firm expanded its reach via its acquisition of Europe’s leading food cans, ends and closures manufacturer Eviosys in December 2024.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

That said, its Q3 revenue dropped 4% YoY, marking its third-straight quarterly decline against its big Eviosys-boosted 2025. SON posted a GAAP net loss of -$732 million, or -$7.36 per share, “reflecting a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $(829) million attributable to the Consumer EMEA/APAC and Industrial APAC businesses.”

Meanwhile, its adjusted EPS dropped 13% YoY, and it provided downbeat guidance on October 21. “During the third quarter, our businesses faced a combination of external challenges,” CEO Howard Coker said in prepared remarks.

“Drought conditions across parts of Europe and the U.S. impacted crop yields and pressured food can demand, while the impact of inflation on raw materials, freight, energy, and other operating costs exceeded our expectations.”


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Sonoco’s recent downward EPS revisions earn it a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell). On top of that, SON is part of the Containers-Paper and Packaging industry that ranks in the bottom 17% of over 250 Zacks industries.

Quantum Computing is the next technological revolution, and it could be even more advanced than AI.

While some believed the technology was years away, it is already present and moving fast. Large hyperscalers, such as Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle, and even Meta and Tesla, are scrambling to integrate quantum computing into their infrastructure.

excerpt: Style Box ETF report for IWX
headline: Should iShares Russell Top 200 Value ETF (IWX) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
Designed to provide broad exposure to the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market, the iShares Russell Top 200 Value ETF (IWX) is a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on September 22, 2009.

The fund is sponsored by Blackrock. It has amassed assets over $3.88 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Value

Large cap companies usually have a market capitalization above $10 billion. They tend to be stable companies with predictable cash flows and are usually less volatile than mid and small cap companies.

While value stocks have lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, they also have lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. Value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in nearly all markets when you consider long-term performance, growth stocks are more likely to outpace value stocks in strong bull markets.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.2%, making it one of the cheaper products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.35%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

It is important to delve into an ETF's holdings before investing despite the many upsides to these kinds of funds like diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Information Technology sector -- about 23.5% of the portfolio. Financials and Healthcare round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Amazon.com Inc (AMZN) accounts for about 8.36% of total assets, followed by Apple (AAPL) and Microsoft (MSFT).

The top 10 holdings account for about 40.94% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

IWX seeks to match the performance of the Russell Top 200 Value Index before fees and expenses. The Russell Top 200 Value Index is a style factor weighted index that measures the performance of the largest capitalization value sector of the U.S. equity market.

The ETF has added roughly 25.04% so far this year and is up roughly 28.97% in the last one year (as of 10/27/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $87.29 and $114.08.

The ETF has a beta of 0.77 and standard deviation of 11.94% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 156 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

iShares Russell Top 200 Value ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, IWX is an excellent option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Value segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) and the Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) track a similar index. While Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF has $118.32 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF has $192.82 billion. SCHD has an expense ratio of 0.06% and VTV charges 0.03%.

Bottom-Line

While an excellent vehicle for long term investors, passively managed ETFs are a popular choice among institutional and retail investors due to their low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency.

excerpt: PARNX, PRBLX and PARMX offer diversified equity strategies, positive three- and five-year returns and expense ratios below 1% amid performance divergence.
headline: 3 Parnassus Mutual Funds to Buy Amid Performance Divergence
html_content:
Parnassus Investments, a pioneer in sustainable investing, has built its reputation around high-quality companies with durable competitive advantages, attractive valuations and responsible business practices. However, the fund family has faced challenges in recent years, reflecting uneven investment performance and waning investor demand for sustainable investment strategies. Despite these headwinds, its recent performance picture is mixed, with stronger returns among large-cap strategies contrasting with persistent weakness in mid-cap offerings.

Parnassus managed approximately $41 billion in assets as of February 2026. The firm has, in recent years, sharpened its focus on U.S. large-cap equities, expanding its investment team and broadening its offerings to include actively managed exchange-traded funds. The firm's latest returns through Oct. 9, 2026, highlight the divergence across its investment strategies. Its large-cap offerings have generally delivered stronger year-to-date results than its mid-cap strategies. Parnassus' growth and value-oriented approaches have benefited from different market opportunities, while its mid-cap investments have encountered greater difficulties.

Recent quarterly results also underscore the challenges of sustaining performance in a volatile market. Parnassus Core Equity fell 0.51% in third-quarter 2026 versus the S&P 500 Index’s 2.30% gain, while its Mid Cap Fund dropped 9.72%, trailing the Russell Midcap Index’s 3% decline. Weakness in technology and materials weighed on large-cap core investments during the third quarter, while mid-cap strategies experienced more pronounced declines.

Astute investors might choose to consider such funds at present. Mutual funds, in general, reduce transaction costs and diversify portfolios without an array of commission charges that are mostly associated with stock purchases (read more: Mutual Funds: Advantages, Disadvantages, and How They Make Investors Money).

We have thus selected three mutual funds that boast a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), have positive three-year and five-year annualized returns and minimum initial investments within $5000, as well as carry a low expense ratio.

Parnassus Mid Cap Growth Investor PARNX primarily invests in mid-cap growth companies but may retain holdings outside its benchmark’s capitalization range and invest in smaller- and larger-capitalization stocks.

Ian Sexsmith has been the lead manager of PARNX since 2013. The three top holdings for PARNX are Teradyne (4.5%), Datadog (4%) and Rockwell Automation (3.6%).

PARNX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 13.9% and 3.7%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.82%. PARNX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2. To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here.

Parnassus Core Equity Investor PRBLX seeks capital appreciation and current income through a diversified portfolio of common and preferred stocks, primarily investing in equities, with a significant allocation to dividend- or interest-paying securities.

Todd C. Ahlsten has been the lead manager of PRBLX since 2001. The three top holdings for PRBLX are Alphabet (5.9%), Applied Materials (5.9%) and Nvidia (5.8%).

PRBLX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 17.3% and 10.2%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.81%. PRBLX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

Parnassus Mid-Cap PARMX primarily invests in mid-cap companies, defined by the Russell Midcap Index’s market-capitalization range at purchase, while retaining flexibility to invest in small- and large-cap stocks.

Lori Keith has been the lead manager of PARMX since 2008. The three top holdings for PARMX are KLA Corp. (3.8%), Bank of New York Mellon (4.6%) and NXP Semiconductors (3.5%).

PARMX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 12.5% and 3.8%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.95%. PARMX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

Bottom Line

Parnassus faces the challenge of rebuilding investor confidence while maintaining its distinctive sustainable-investing philosophy. Its emphasis on financially strong businesses and long-term value creation could remain attractive to investors seeking a disciplined alternative to momentum-driven strategies. Nevertheless, recent outflows and uneven returns warrant attention. Investors should assess performance against appropriate benchmarks, expenses and individual risk tolerance before making decisions. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

headline: Grab These 3 Top-Ranked PIMCO Mutual Funds for Solid Returns
html_content:
Founded in 1971, Pacific Investment Management Company, LLC or PIMCO is an internationally acclaimed investment management firm. Headquartered in Newport Beach, CA, the company provides a wide range of financial services across the globe, with more than 3,220 employees. PIMCO had around $2.27 trillion in assets under management as of March 31, 2026. It is present in 24 locations across the Americas, Europe and Asia.

PIMCO offers a broad lineup of investment solutions for the entire gamut of equities, bonds, currencies, real estate, alternative investments and risk-management services. Though the firm manages an array of mutual funds, it is best known for those based on fixed income.

Below, we share with you three top-ranked PIMCO mutual funds — Pimco Global Core Asset Allocation Fund PGMAX, Pimco Diversified Income Fund PDVAX and Pimco Municipal Bond PMLAX. Each has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and is expected to outperform its peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of PIMCO mutual funds.

Pimco Global Core Asset Allocation Fund invests most of its net assets in a combination of affiliated and unaffiliated funds. PGMAX advisors invest in fixed-income instruments like bonds, debt securities and other similar instruments issued by various U.S. and non-U.S. public or private sector entities. PGMAX advisors also invest in equity securities, forwards and derivatives.

Pimco Global Core Asset Allocation Fund has three-year annualized returns of 18.3%. By the end of June 2026, PGMAX held 25 issues, with 5.3% of its assets invested in Amazon.com.

Pimco Diversified Income Fund invests most of its net assets in a diversified portfolio of fixed income instruments of varying maturities, which may be represented by forwards or derivatives such as options, futures contracts or swap agreements. PDVAX advisors may also invest in investment-grade securities and junk bonds subject to a maximum of 10% of its total assets in securities rated below B by Moody's Investors Service, Inc., or equivalently rated by S&P or Fitch.

Pimco Diversified Income Fund has three-year annualized returns of 7.3%. PDVAX has an expense ratio of 1.15%.

Pimco Municipal Bond fund invests most of its net assets in debt securities whose interest is, in the opinion of the bond counsel for the issuer, exempt from federal income tax. PMLAX advisors invest in U.S. government securities and money market instruments. PMLAX advisors also invest in private bonds with similar tax preference without limitation.

Pimco Municipal Bond fund has three-year annualized returns of 3.4%. David Hammer has been the fund manager of PMLAX since August 2015.

To view the Zacks Rank and the past performance of all PIMCO mutual funds, investors can click here to see the complete list of PIMCO mutual funds.

headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Amneal Pharmaceuticals Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Amneal Pharmaceuticals, Inc. AMRX need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Mar 19, 2027 $2.5 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Amneal Pharmaceuticals shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Amneal Pharmaceuticals is a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) in the Medical – Drugs industry that ranks in the Top 32% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 30 days, one analyst has increased the earnings estimate for the current quarter, while none have revised their estimates downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from 23 cents per share to 24 cents in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Amneal Pharmaceuticals right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

headline: Keurig Dr Pepper, Inc (KDP) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
html_content:
The market expects Keurig Dr Pepper, Inc (KDP) to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook is important in assessing the company's earnings picture, but a powerful factor that might influence its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 3, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.64 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +18.5%.

Revenues are expected to be $7.36 billion, up 71% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.41% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Keurig Dr Pepper?

For Keurig Dr Pepper, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -2.27%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #4.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Keurig Dr Pepper will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Keurig Dr Pepper would post earnings of $0.55 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.57, delivering a surprise of +3.64%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Keurig Dr Pepper doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

excerpt: Hyatt's Q3 earnings could benefit from high-single-digit gross fee growth and a strong development pipeline, but regional challenges may weigh on revenues.
headline: Hyatt to Report Q3 Earnings: Can Fee Growth Drive Results?
html_content:
Hyatt Hotels Corporation H is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 29, before the opening bell.

H’s earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three of the trailing four quarters, and missed once, the average surprise being 58.1%.

Trend in the Estimate Revision of H

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter earnings per share (EPS) is pegged at 69 cents, indicating growth of 330% year over year.

For revenues, the consensus mark is pinned at $1.77 billion, implying a 1% decrease from the prior-year quarter.

Let's look at how things have shaped up in the quarter.

Factors Likely to Shape Hyatt’s Quarterly Results

Hyatt’s third-quarter 2026 top line is expected to have been impacted by weakness in its all-inclusive resort business and regional operating challenges. During its second-quarter earnings call, management indicated that net package revenue per available room (RevPAR) is expected to decline moderately year over year in the third quarter. Booking trends at Hyatt's all-inclusive resorts in Mexico have been improving sequentially but remained below expectations following a security incident earlier in 2026.

Lower flight capacity has also constrained demand, while the company expects the recovery in travel spending among customers seeking four-star properties to take time. These challenges might have offset strength in other parts of Hyatt's portfolio.

The company's top line is also likely to have encountered headwinds from geopolitical disruptions and a less favorable contribution from certain parts of its portfolio. Hyatt expects hotel revenues in the Middle East to have remained significantly below the prior-year level because of the ongoing regional conflict. Management expects this can reduce full-year fees by approximately $10 million. In addition, temporary hotel closures in Jamaica following Hurricane Melissa and softer demand in Mexico have been weighing on the distribution business.

The company has also experienced some portfolio-related room-count reductions, including adjustments related to Playa Hotels and turnover in its UrCove and Lindner portfolios. Although Hyatt expects third-quarter global RevPAR growth to be toward the lower end of its full-year outlook, continued expansion in the asset-light business might have supported gross fee growth in the high single digits.

Our model predicts net fee revenues to increase 25.6%, whereas Owned and Leased as well as Distribution revenues are expected to decline 34.6% and 38.5%, year over year, respectively.

Hyatt's bottom line is likely to have improved, supported by continued growth in its core fee-based business, a larger hotel portfolio and operating efficiencies. Management highlighted strong demand for its luxury and lifestyle brands, a record development pipeline of approximately 154,000 rooms and growing loyalty-program membership, all of which support fee generation.

The company also expects its asset-light model to translate fee growth into higher earnings and cash flow with relatively modest incremental capital requirements. Furthermore, management indicated that distribution-related pressure was concentrated in the first half of 2026 and expected some improvement in the second half. These factors might have supported adjusted EBITDA growth and stronger profitability, even as regional demand challenges limit the pace of revenue growth.

Stocks Poised to Beat on Earnings

Marriott International, Inc. MAR currently has an Earnings ESP of +1.56% and a Zacks Rank of 2. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

MAR’s earnings for the to-be-reported quarter are expected to increase 15.4%. Marriott reported better-than-expected earnings in the trailing three out of four quarters and missed once, the average surprise being 2.5%.

Choice Hotels International, Inc. CHH has an Earnings ESP of +0.19% and a Zacks Rank of 3 at present.

For the to-be-reported quarter, Choice Hotels is expected to register an 8.1% increase in earnings. Choice Hotels reported better-than-expected earnings in the trailing two out of the four quarters and missed twice, the average surprise being negative 4.8%.

Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd. NCLH currently has an Earnings ESP of +2.26% and a Zacks Rank of 3.

For the to-be-reported quarter, Norwegian Cruise’s earnings are expected to decrease 23.33%. Norwegian Cruise reported better-than-expected earnings in each of the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 20%.

Radical New Technology Could Hand Investors Huge Gains

Quantum Computing is the next technological revolution, and it could be even more advanced than AI.

While some believed the technology was years away, it is already present and moving fast. Large hyperscalers, such as Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle, and even Meta and Tesla, are scrambling to integrate quantum computing into their infrastructure.

excerpt: Data center and power demand, along with mission-critical projects, give these construction stocks, like INOD, AGX, TREX, PWR and STRL, strong growth momentum.
headline: 5 Construction Stocks That May Surprise This Earnings Season
html_content:
The U.S. construction sector is expected to have delivered mixed third-quarter 2026 results, supported by robust investments in artificial intelligence (AI)-driven data centers, power infrastructure and public construction projects. However, persistent housing affordability challenges, elevated construction costs and labor shortages likely weighed on profitability.

Construction activity remained uneven during the quarter. Per Dodge Construction Network, total construction starts increased 14.3% year over year in the first nine months of 2026, driven by a 23.7% increase in nonresidential starts and an 18.4% rise in nonbuilding construction. Conversely, residential starts declined 1.7%, highlighting the divergence between infrastructure-led growth and housing-related weakness.

Against this backdrop, third-quarter earnings across the construction sector are likely to reflect differences in end-market exposure, project execution, backlog conversion, pricing power and cost-management capabilities. With the help of the Zacks Stock Screener, some of the companies under the broader Zacks Construction sector, Innodata Inc. INOD, Argan, Inc. AGX, Trex Company, Inc. TREX, Quanta Services, Inc. PWR, and Sterling Infrastructure, Inc. STRL, are poised to beat on earnings this reporting cycle.

Per the latest Earnings Trends report, about 15.4% of companies on the S&P 500 Index have reported in the third-quarter earnings season so far. Of these, the Construction sector's total earnings declined 43% year over year, while revenues fell 8.7%. None of the companies beat earnings per share (EPS) estimates and revenue expectations.

AI and Infrastructure Investments Likely Drove Growth

Accelerating investments in AI-driven data centers, hyperscale facilities and cloud infrastructure are expected to have supported U.S. construction activity during the third quarter of 2026. Growing demand for electrical installations, HVAC systems, modular construction and specialized engineering services likely strengthened revenues and project backlogs. Rising electricity consumption, grid modernization and power generation investments also likely boosted demand for transmission and distribution infrastructure. 

Meanwhile, federal and state infrastructure funding is expected to have sustained highway, bridge, airport and water infrastructure projects. Investments in advanced manufacturing, semiconductor facilities and institutional construction likely provided additional support. These trends may have boosted demand for building materials, equipment utilization and rental activity, although project delays and permitting challenges remained concerns.

Housing Weakness and Soft Commercial Demand Hurt Growth

The residential construction market likely remained under pressure amid elevated mortgage rates, affordability constraints and cautious homebuyer sentiment. Higher home prices and financing costs likely dampened demand, prompting builders to offer pricing discounts and mortgage-rate incentives, potentially squeezing margins. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, September housing starts declined 7.4% year over year, reflecting continued market weakness. Commercial construction likely experienced mixed conditions, with traditional office and retail developments facing softer demand despite healthy investments in specialized industrial and technology-related projects. Building materials, roofing and remodeling activity likely reflected this divergence, with infrastructure-related demand offsetting some residential weakness. Elevated borrowing costs and discretionary spending constraints may have further limited construction activity across certain markets.

Rising Costs and Labor Shortages Likely Pressured Margins

Persistent skilled labor shortages, rising wages, material inflation and supply-chain disruptions are expected to have pressured construction profitability during the quarter. Higher costs for steel, copper, electrical components, fuel and transportation, alongside tariff-related uncertainties, likely increased project expenses. Competition for specialized workers and extended equipment lead times may have further complicated execution schedules. However, favorable pricing, disciplined procurement, modular construction and operational efficiencies likely helped mitigate these pressures. Strong project backlogs and strategic acquisitions may have supported revenue growth, although integration expenses and working-capital requirements remained challenges.

Overall, earnings likely reflected stronger performance in infrastructure-oriented businesses than in residential construction, with backlog conversion, margin trends and cash generation remaining key indicators of sector health.

Q3 Expectations

Per the latest Earnings Trends report, construction sector earnings are expected to grow 3.4% for the third quarter from a year ago. This indicates a decrease from the second quarter of 2026’s 5.8% growth. Revenues are projected to grow 8.6%, nearly the same as 8.7% growth in the preceding quarter.

The Zacks Methodology

Picking the right stock could be difficult unless one knows the proper method. To make the task simple, we rely on the Zacks methodology, combining a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy), or 3 (Hold) and a positive Earnings ESP.

Our proprietary methodology, Earnings ESP, shows the percentage difference between the Most Accurate Estimate and the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Research shows that for stocks with this combination of the Zacks Rank and ESP, chances of a positive earnings surprise are as high as 70%. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they’re reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

Winning Stocks

For investors willing to adopt this strategy, we have highlighted five construction stocks that may stand out this earnings season.

Innodata— a global data engineering and AI systems services firm — topped earnings estimates in all the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 102.2%.

INOD is likely to beat expectations when it reports third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 5, 2026, after the closing bell. This Zacks Rank #3 company has an Earnings ESP of +22.53%. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for INOD’s third-quarter EPS is pegged at 24 cents, same as the year-ago reported figure.

Strong demand for AI data engineering, reusable datasets and high-value pre-training services is expected to have supported Innodata’s quarterly performance. Expanding opportunities in agentic AI, model evaluation and physical AI are also likely to have contributed to revenue growth.

excerpt: Many people avoid checking their bank balance because seeing the number feels too scary to face. Meredith Margrave explains why avoidance only makes things worse, and shares five small steps to finally turn the lights on.
headline: Terrified to Check Your Bank Balance? Here's How to Survive the Fear
html_content:
It's late. The house is quiet, but your mind won't settle. You're lying in bed, staring at the ceiling, and on the nightstand your phone gives off a faint blue glow. You don't touch it.

Then it buzzes, and you flinch. It's like it knows.

You reach for it. The screen is blinding in the dark. You swipe past the texts and the notifications, because none of them matter. There's only one thing you can't outrun, and it's waiting behind a little icon at the bottom of the screen.

Your finger hovers. Your heart thuds, slow and thick. You tell yourself to stop being ridiculous. It's just a number. Just a reality you've been avoiding for weeks.

You tap. The app loads. You hold your breath.

Because monsters, you can fight. Ghosts, you can banish. But this is something else entirely.

This is your bank account.

Who's Afraid of the Big, Bad Bank Balance?

Forget slasher movies. This Halloween, the thing keeping more and more people up at night is the thought of checking their bank balance. What if I've overdrawn? What if I missed a payment? What if it's worse than I thought? Sometimes just imagining the answer is enough to make you put your phone back down.

If that sounds familiar, you're not alone. Back in the early 2000s, a University of Cambridge study gave the feeling a name, "financial phobia," and found that it can show up as anxiety, guilt, and even physical symptoms when people have to deal with their money.

There's a newer name for the feeling, too: FOFO, or "fear of finding out." The term took hold in health care, where it describes people who skip the doctor because they'd rather not hear bad news. Money works the same way. When you suspect things aren't great, the unknown feels safer than the truth. And the fear usually isn't just about the number. It's about what the number might say about you... the overspending, the debt, the missed opportunities, and the guilt and shame that tag along with all of it.

Behavioral economists have their own term for it: the ostrich effect. In one well-known study, researchers found that investors checked their portfolios less often when the market was falling than when it was rising. In other words, even people who follow money closely tend to look away right when looking matters most. If you've been avoiding your balance, it's not because you're bad with money. It's because you're human.

Don't Go in the Basement... Actually, Do

Every horror fan knows the rule: Don't go in the basement. With money, it's the opposite. Ignoring your account feels like relief in the moment, but the thing in the basement doesn't go away just because you won't open the door. It grows.

Think about an unopened bill. Leaving it sealed means you don't have to face it today, but it's still there tomorrow, and now it might have a late fee attached. Every skipped check-in works the same way. Each one adds another layer of dread, until the idea of logging in feels paralyzing. Avoidance feeds the fear, and the longer your mind is left in the dark, the scarier the monster becomes. In my experience, when people finally do look, the reality is usually more manageable than the version they've been carrying around in their heads.

The bigger cost, though, is financial. When nobody's watching the account, overdraft fees pile up, payments slip through the cracks, and late payments can start dragging down your credit score. Left alone long enough, small, fixable problems have a way of turning into big ones.

So let's turn the lights on.

5 Small Steps to Face Your Finance Fears (No "Final Girl" Required)

The goal here isn't to fix everything or overhaul your spending. It's simply to stop running. Take these at whatever pace feels right, but I'd suggest no more than one step a day so you don't overwhelm yourself.

1. Open the door and look.

Log in to your bank's app or website (or your credit card account, if that's where the dread lives). Look at the balance. Then close it.

That's it. You did it. Whatever the number says, you know it now, and knowing puts you back in control.

2. Set a five-minute timer and look around.

Next time, log in and poke around for five minutes. Scroll through recent transactions, see what's coming in and going out, and close the app when the timer goes off. You don't need to analyze or fix anything. The point is to get comfortable seeing the numbers again, so they lose a little of their power each time.

3. Turn on alerts.

Most banking apps let you set notifications for transactions, deposits, and low balances. Turn them on. Small, regular updates keep you in the loop between check-ins, so there's never a big, terrifying reveal waiting for you. If your bank offers a daily balance text or email, turn that on, too. Think of it as the opposite of a jump scare: no surprises, just a quiet heads-up every morning.

4. Let a budgeting app keep watch.

Apps like Rocket Money, EveryDollar, YNAB, and NerdWallet can link to your accounts and track and categorize your spending automatically. Download one, connect your accounts, answer a few questions, and it handles most of the legwork. Some are free, while others charge a subscription, and prices vary widely, so check before you sign up.

You don't have to build a budget yet. Just letting the app show you where your money goes takes a lot of the mental weight off. Glance at it daily if you can.

5. Make check-ins routine.

Pick a regular time to check your account, whether that's every morning with your coffee or every Sunday night before the week starts. A quick peek counts just as much as a full review. The routine is what turns a scary task into a boring one, and boring is exactly what you want. Eventually, checking your balance will feel like brushing your teeth.

The Sequel: Taking Back Control

Every good horror movie leaves room for a sequel, and this is yours. Once looking at your balance no longer makes your stomach drop, you can start putting what you see to work.

Fear doesn't vanish after one brave login. It may still feel uncomfortable for a while, and that's okay. What matters is that it doesn't stop you.

A simple budget is a natural next step. It doesn't need to be complicated. A handful of categories, like housing, groceries, transportation, and savings, is enough to show you how money moves through your month. There's something about seeing it all laid out that makes it easier to digest.

Automatic payments help, too. Putting recurring bills like rent, utilities, and loan payments on autopay means you won't miss a due date, and it's one less thing rattling around in your head. Just keep enough cushion in checking to cover them, because an autopay that hits an empty account can trigger the very overdraft fees you're trying to avoid. (That low-balance alert from Step 3 will earn its keep here.)

From there, keep breaking things into bite-size pieces. This week, set up autopay. Next week, take a closer look at your spending. After that, maybe start a small emergency fund. And reward yourself along the way, whether that's a small treat after a check-in or a celebration when you hit a milestone. Progress deserves to be noticed.

Here's your challenge: Tonight, before the phone goes back on the nightstand, open the app. Look at the number. Then put the phone down and go to sleep.

The monster was never really in your bank account. It was in the not knowing. Once you turn the lights on, it's just a number. And a number, you can work with.

excerpt: O-I Glass and Apogee Enterprises could benefit from rising demand for sustainable glass packaging, energy-efficient windows and innovative construction products.
headline: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights O-I Glass, Inc. and Apogee Enterprises
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 28, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses O-I Glass, Inc. OI and Apogee Enterprises APOG.

Industry: Glass Products

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3015462/2-glass-products-stocks-to-watch-in-a-promising-industry

The Zacks Glass Products industry is poised to benefit from the rising demand for glass, both as a packaging option and for use in construction. This is backed by its endless recyclability and sustainability benefits. Growing demand for energy-efficient, smart windows or smart glass panels will be another catalyst for the industry going forward.

Companies like O-I Glass, Inc. and Apogee Enterprises are expected to gain from efforts to capitalize on this demand by boosting capacity and introducing innovative products to the market.

About the Industry

The Zacks Glass Products industry comprises companies that manufacture and sell glass products. O produces glass containers for packaging beverages, food and pharmaceuticals. Another player in the industry offers coated and high-performance glass used in customized window and wall systems. It caters to the construction industry, ranging from commercial and multi-family residential to institutional buildings. It also provides coated glass for picture framing, wall décor and display applications. 

Nowadays, companies that make glass for buildings offer smart glass windows using artificial intelligence to adjust and suitably increase access to natural light while minimizing heat and glare. Some have developed electrokinetic technology that can be retrofitted on any glass, enabling buildings to cut energy consumption and save on heating and cooling costs. 

Major Trends Shaping the Future of the Glass Products Industry

 

Glass Packaging Gaining Popularity: Glass is increasingly becoming the packaging choice for customers, given its endless recyclability without a loss in quality. More than 80% of recycled bottles are used in making new bottles. This also helps negate the need for raw materials. Every ton of recycled glass saves 1,400 pounds of sand, 430 pounds of soda ash and 400 pounds of limestone/dolomite. 

As consumers are becoming more aware of their environmental footprint, a sharp spike in demand is noticed for refillable bottles, which offer the most sustainable and economical rigid packaging option. Manufacturers are focusing on improving their products by reducing the weight of the bottles for more convenient handling. Also, premium cosmetic and beverage brands are opting for glass to differentiate their products through packaging and ensure quality maintenance. 

Demand in the Construction Sector Holds Promise: In recent years, the use of glass gained popularity in construction as a sustainable alternative to traditional building materials, including wood and bricks, owing to its cost-effectiveness, lightweight, immense strength and environmentally friendly factor. Glass increases the influx of natural light in the building, reduces energy consumption, minimizes carbon emissions and enhances the aesthetic appeal of structures. 

Rising construction activities across the residential, commercial and industrial sectors are likely to fuel the glass products industry's growth. Increasing investments in the renovation or modernization of the existing infrastructure will also drive the industry's growth. Various governments are introducing favorable policies and granting incentives to promote green construction to minimize greenhouse emissions and energy consumption, which bodes well for the industry.

Technological Innovation is the Key: Some players revolutionized the industry by bringing smart glass panels or smart windows to the market. These innovative products are designed to enable people to lead healthier and more productive lives by increasing access to daylight and views while minimizing glare and heat from the sun and keeping occupants comfortable. These products also help cut down on energy consumption from lighting and HVAC, thus reducing carbon emissions.

3 Stocks with Broker Rating Upgrades to Bet On Right Away

U.S. equities have remained resilient this year despite elevated Treasury yields, oil prices above $100, persistent inflation, tariff uncertainties and narrow market breadth. The Federal Reserve's September rate hike and prospects of further tightening have added pressure. Nevertheless, solid corporate earnings have supported market sentiment amid volatility, AI-valuation concerns and broader economic uncertainties.

Amid this backdrop, choosing the right stock can become difficult. One way to simplify this task is to follow brokers' recommendations. Stocks like Allegion plc, United Rentals, Inc. and Clean Harbors, Inc. are worth betting on.

Broker recommendations are generally backed by comprehensive research, encompassing management interactions, regulatory filings, earnings calls, channel checks and industry assessments. Such analysis enables analysts to evaluate a company's fundamentals while considering broader economic trends, industry dynamics, competitive strength and relative peer performance.

A broker rating upgrade often indicates growing confidence in a company's prospects, potentially reflecting positive developments not yet fully incorporated into consensus forecasts or stock valuations. Such upgrades may point to improving earnings prospects, attractive valuations or strengthening investor confidence.

However, broker rating upgrades should not be considered in isolation. Investors should assess them alongside company fundamentals, earnings momentum and valuation metrics to make well-informed decisions within a comprehensive and disciplined investment strategy.

ALLE sells products through distribution and retail channels like specialty distribution, wholesalers, e-commerce and several retail channels, including online platforms and small specialty showroom outlets.

United Rentals, based in Stamford, CT, is the largest equipment rental company across the globe. URI's principal products and services are equipment rental, sale of rental equipment, new equipment, contractor supplies, services and others.

United Rentals' 2026 earnings are projected to increase 18.1% year over year. URI, which sports a Zacks Rank #1 at present, has seen a 4.8% increase in broker ratings over the past four weeks.

CLH's 2026 earnings are expected to jump 36.5% year over year. Clean Harbors, which currently carries a Zacks Rank #2, has witnessed a 5.9% upward revision in broker ratings over the past four weeks.

headline: Is Schwab Fundamental U.S. Broad Market ETF (FNDB) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
The Schwab Fundamental U.S. Broad Market ETF (FNDB) was launched on 08/13/2013, and is a smart beta exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Style Box - All Cap Value category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

For a long time now, the ETF industry has been flooded with products based on market capitalization weighted indexes, which are designed to represent the broader market or a particular market segment.

A good option for investors who believe in market efficiency, market cap weighted indexes offer a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way of replicating market returns.

However, some investors believe in the possibility of beating the market through exceptional stock selection, and choose a different type of fund that tracks non-cap weighted strategies: smart beta.

By attempting to pick stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance, non-cap weighted indexes are based on certain fundamental characteristics, or a combination of such.

This area offers many different investment choices, such as simplest equal-weighting, fundamental weighting and volatility/momentum based weighting methodologies; however, not all of these strategies can deliver superior results.

Fund Sponsor & Index

Because the fund has amassed over $1.5 billion, this makes it one of the largest ETFs in the Style Box - All Cap Value. FNDB is managed by Charles Schwab. FNDB, before fees and expenses, seeks to match the performance of the Russell RAFI US Index.

The RAFI Fundamental High Liquidity US All Index measures the performance of U.S. based companies based on their fundamental size and weight.

Cost & Other Expenses

html_content:
If you're interested in broad exposure to the Consumer Discretionary - Retail segment of the equity market, look no further than the VanEck Retail ETF (RTH), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on December 20, 2011.

Retail and institutional investors increasingly turn to passively managed ETFs because they offer low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency; these kind of funds are also excellent vehicles for long term investors.

Investor-friendly, sector ETFs provide many options to gain low risk and diversified exposure to a broad group of companies in particular sectors. The fund is sponsored by Van Eck. RTH seeks to match the performance of the MVIS US Listed Retail 25 Index before fees and expenses.

The MVIS US Listed Retail 25 Index tracks the overall performance of companies involved in retail distribution, wholesalers, on-line, direct mail and TV retailers, multi-line retailers, specialty retailers and food and other staples retailers.

Costs

Investors should also pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio. Lower cost products will produce better results than those with a higher cost, assuming all other metrics remain the same.

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

VanEck Retail ETF sports a Zacks ETF Rank of 4 (Sell), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. headline: Is First Trust NASDAQ Bank ETF (FTXO) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
Making its debut on 09/20/2016, smart beta exchange traded fund First Trust NASDAQ Bank ETF (FTXO) provides investors broad exposure to the Financials ETFs category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

Market cap weighted indexes were created to reflect the market, or a specific segment of the market, and the ETF industry has traditionally been dominated by products based on this strategy.

Investors who believe in market efficiency should consider market cap indexes, as they replicate market returns in a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way.

But, there are some investors who would rather invest in smart beta funds; these funds track non-cap weighted strategies, and are a strong option for those who prefer choosing great stocks in order to beat the market.

These indexes attempt to select stocks that have better chances of risk-return performance, based on certain fundamental characteristics or a combination of such characteristics.

The smart beta space gives investors many different choices, from equal-weighting, one of the simplest strategies, to more complicated ones like fundamental and volatility/momentum based weighting. However, not all of these methodologies have been able to deliver remarkable returns.

Fund Sponsor & Index

The fund is managed by First Trust Advisors. FTXO has been able to amass assets over $248.88 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs in the Financials ETFs. Before fees and expenses, FTXO seeks to match the performance of the Nasdaq US Smart Banks Index.

The Nasdaq US Smart Banks Index is a modified factor weighted index, designed to provide exposure to US companies within the banking industry.

Cost & Other Expenses

For ETF investors, expense ratios are an important factor when considering a fund's return; in the long-term, cheaper funds actually have the ability to outperform their more expensive cousins if all other things remain the same.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.60%, making it on par with most peer products in the space.

It's 12-month trailing dividend yield comes in at 1.93%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

While ETFs offer diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk, a deep look into a fund's holdings is a valuable exercise. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation in the Financials sector - about 100% of the portfolio.

Taking into account individual holdings, Citigroup Inc. (C) accounts for about 8.17% of the fund's total assets, followed by Jpmorgan Chase & Co. (JPM) and U.s. Bancorp (USB).

The top 10 holdings account for about 58.34% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

The ETF has added about 6.7% and was up about 16.71% so far this year and in the past one year (as of 10/28/2026), respectively. FTXO has traded between $33.72 and $43.87 during this last 52-week period.

The ETF has a beta of 0.92 and standard deviation of 23.61% for the trailing three-year period. With about 51 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

First Trust NASDAQ Bank ETF is a reasonable option for investors seeking to outperform the Financials ETFs segment of the market. However, there are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider.

State Street SPDR S&P Bank ETF (KBE) tracks S&P Banks Select Industry Index and the Invesco KBW Bank ETF (KBWB) tracks KBW Nasdaq Bank index. State Street SPDR S&P Bank ETF has $1.46 billion in assets, Invesco KBW Bank ETF has $6.59 billion. KBE has an expense ratio of 0.35% and KBWB changes 0.35%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Financials ETFs

The ETF industry has long been dominated by products based on market cap weighted indexes, a strategy created to reflect the market or a particular market segment.

Market cap weighted indexes work great for investors who believe in market efficiency. They provide a low-cost, convenient and transparent way of replicating market returns.

On the other hand, some investors who believe that it is possible to beat the market by superior stock selection opt to invest in another class of funds that track non-cap weighted strategies--popularly known as smart beta.

Cost & Other Expenses

Expense ratios are an important factor in the return of an ETF and in the long-term, cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive cousins, other things remaining the same.

headline: Is Plumb Balanced (PLBBX) a Strong Mutual Fund Pick Right Now?
html_content:
Any investors hoping to find a Allocation Balanced fund could think about starting with Plumb Balanced (PLBBX). PLBBX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on various forecasting factors like size, cost, and past performance.

Objective

PLBBX is classified in the Allocation Balanced segment by Zacks, which is an area full of possibilities. Here, investors are able to get a good head start with diversified mutual funds, and play around with core holding options for a portfolio of funds. Allocation Balanced funds look to invest across a balance of asset types, like stocks, bonds, and cash, though including precious metals or commodities is not unusual; these funds are mostly categorized by their respective asset allocation.

History of Fund/Manager

PLBBX finds itself in the Plumb family, based out of Madison, WI. The Plumb Balanced made its debut in May of 2007 and PLBBX has managed to accumulate roughly $34.51 million in assets, as of the most recently available information. The fund's current manager, Thomas G. Plumb, has been in charge of the fund since May of 2007.

Performance

Of course, investors look for strong performance in funds. PLBBX has a 5-year annualized total return of 7.4%, and is in the middle third among its category peers. But if you are looking for a shorter time frame, it is also worth looking at its 3-year annualized total return of 16.71%, which places it in the top third during this time-frame.

It is important to note that the product's returns may not reflect all its expenses. Any fees not reflected would lower the returns. Total returns do not reflect the fund's [%] sale charge. If sales charges were included, total returns would have been lower.

When looking at a fund's performance, it is also important to note the standard deviation of the returns. The lower the standard deviation, the less volatility the fund experiences. The standard deviation of PLBBX over the past three years is 9.2% compared to the category average of 10%. Over the past 5 years, the standard deviation of the fund is 12.95% compared to the category average of 11.86%. This makes the fund more volatile than its peers over the past half-decade.

Risk Factors

Investors should note that the fund has a 5-year beta of 0.79, which means it is hypothetically less volatile than the market at large. Because alpha represents a portfolio's performance on a risk-adjusted basis relative to a benchmark, which is the S&P 500 in this case, one should pay attention to this metric as well. PLBBX's 5-year performance has produced a negative alpha of -4.02, which means managers in this portfolio find it difficult to pick securities that generate better-than-benchmark returns.

Expenses

Costs are increasingly important for mutual fund investing, and particularly as competition heats up in this market. And all things being equal, a lower cost product will outperform its otherwise identical counterpart, so taking a closer look at these metrics is key for investors. In terms of fees, PLBBX is a no load fund. It has an expense ratio of 1.44% compared to the category average of 0.88%. Looking at the fund from a cost perspective, PLBBX is actually more expensive than its peers.

Investors need to be aware that with this product, the minimum initial investment is $2,500; each subsequent investment needs to be at least $50.

Fees charged by investment advisors have not been taken into consideration. Returns would be less if those were included.

Bottom Line

Overall, even with its comparatively similar performance, average downside risk, and higher fees, Plumb Balanced ( PLBBX ) has a high Zacks Mutual Fund rank, and therefore looks a good potential choice for investors right now.
