excerpt: Range Resources (RRC) is at a 52-week high, but can investors hope for more gains in the future? We take a look at the company's fundamentals for clues.
headline: Range Resources Corporation (RRC) Hit a 52 Week High, Can the Run Continue?
html_content:
Have you been paying attention to shares of Range Resources (RRC)? Shares have been on the move with the stock up 52.9% over the past month. The stock hit a new 52-week high of $56.47 in the previous session. Range Resources has gained 59.9% since the start of the year compared to the 40.3% move for the Zacks Oils-Energy sector and the 39.9% return for the Zacks Oil and Gas - Exploration and Production - United States industry.

What's Driving the Outperformance?

The stock has a great record of positive earnings surprises, having beaten the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the last four quarters. In its last earnings report on October 27, 2026, Range Resources reported EPS of $0.81 versus consensus estimate of $0.7.

For the current fiscal year, Range Resources is expected to post earnings of $3.98 per share on $3.52 in revenues. This represents a 32.67% change in EPS on a 13.08% change in revenues. For the next fiscal year, the company is expected to earn $3.69 per share on $3.66 in revenues. This represents a year-over-year change of -7.2% and 3.74%, respectively.

Valuation Metrics

Range Resources may be at a 52-week high right now, but what might the future hold for the stock? A key aspect of this question is taking a look at valuation metrics in order to determine if the company is due for a pullback from this level.

On this front, we can look at the Zacks Style Scores, as these give investors a variety of ways to comb through stocks (beyond looking at the Zacks Rank of a security). These styles are represented by grades running from A to F in the categories of Value, Growth, and Momentum, while there is a combined VGM Score as well. Investors should consider the style scores a valuable tool that can help you to pick the most appropriate Zacks Rank stocks based on their individual investment style.

Range Resources has a Value Score of C. The stock's Growth and Momentum Scores are C and A, respectively, giving the company a VGM Score of B.

In terms of its value breakdown, the stock currently trades at 14.2X current fiscal year EPS estimates, which is a premium to the peer industry average of 9.6X. On a trailing cash flow basis, the stock currently trades at 12.6X versus its peer group's average of 5.4X. This isn't enough to put the company in the top echelon of all stocks we cover from a value perspective.

Zacks Rank

We also need to consider the stock's Zacks Rank, as this supersedes any trend on the style score front. Fortunately, Range Resources currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) thanks to rising earnings estimates.

Since we recommend that investors select stocks carrying Zacks Rank of 1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) and Style Scores of A or B, it looks as if Range Resources passes the test. Thus, it seems as though Range Resources shares could have a bit more room to run in the near term.

How Does RRC Stack Up to the Competition?

Shares of RRC have been soaring, and the company still appears to be a decent choice, but what about the rest of the industry? One industry peer that looks good is Cheniere Energy, Inc. (LNG). LNG has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) and a Value Score of B, a Growth Score of C, and a Momentum Score of A.

Earnings were strong last quarter. Cheniere Energy, Inc. beat our consensus estimate by 4.50%, and for the current fiscal year, LNG is expected to post earnings of $9.52 per share on revenue of $22.23 billion.

Shares of Cheniere Energy, Inc. have gained 12.1% over the past month, and currently trade at a forward P/E of 31.48X and a P/CF of 16.8X.

The Oil and Gas - Exploration and Production - United States industry is in the top 11% of all the industries we have in our universe, so it looks like there are some nice tailwinds for RRC and LNG, even beyond their own solid fundamental situation.

excerpt: China's industrial robot output surged 29.1% in 2026, with 59% of global installations in 2025. Discover three ETFs targeting its robotics boom.
headline: Is China Winning the Robotics Race? See Through the ETF Lens
html_content:
China's industrial robotics sector has recently achieved two historic milestones simultaneously. At a State Council press conference on Oct. 19, 2026, the National Bureau of Statistics reported that China's industrial robot output climbed 29.1% year over year in the first nine months of 2026, maintaining double-digit monthly growth throughout the period. 

Barely a month earlier, the International Federation of Robotics confirmed that China installed 354,000 industrial robots in 2025 alone, accounting for 59% of every new factory robot deployed anywhere on earth, as per the International Federation of Robotics (“IFR”) report. 

Impressively, China now operates approximately 2 million industrial robots — 4.3 times Japan's fleet — whereas EU installations fell 11% and Japan dropped 19%, as cited in TechTimes. 

This latest development puts the spotlight on exchange-traded funds (ETFs) offering exposure to the Chinese companies that are the core accelerators of this robotics revolution.

Looking ahead, investors seeking to capitalize on this trend should assess the companies benefiting from China's robotics boom and the country's long-term objectives in this space before exploring related ETF investment opportunities.

Companies Powering China's Robotics Boom

China's robotics and AI ecosystem is anchored by distinct groups of companies operating across two layers of the value chain.

At the hardware layer, companies like Leader Harmonious Drive manufacture harmonic reducers (strain wave gears) and precision motion control products that act as the vital "joints" and actuator modules in robotic arms, industrial automation and humanoid robots. Similarly, Yushu Technology (operating internationally as Unitree Robotics) is a leading global developer and manufacturer of high-performance consumer and industrial-grade legged robots, including quadruped robot dogs and general-purpose humanoid robots. Together, these kinds of firms supply the essential parts that make humanoid robots function.

At the intelligence layer, Montage Technology designs memory interface chips for servers and AI data centers, while Cambricon Technologies designs neural processing units and AI chips. Meanwhile, Hygon Information Technology develops CPUs and DCUs for AI computing. These companies power the inference and training workloads that increasingly drive robot autonomy.

To this end, it is imperative to mention that China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) designates robotics as the "main driver of economic growth," targeting 100,000 humanoid robots by 2027. In October 2026, Beijing announced a $10 billion worth investment initiative for AI-driven robotics (as cited in TechTimes). This investment strategy, coupled with the initiatives undertaken by the aforementioned companies, is expected to support China's efforts to achieve its humanoid robotics target within the planned timeline.

Viewing Through ETF Lens

The "See Through ETF Lense" approach is justified by the sheer complexity and volatility of this ecosystem. 

Individual stock picking carries substantial risk: Unitree surged 629% on its debut, but its valuation now hinges on execution against aggressive production targets. 

Against this backdrop, a China-focused Robotics ETF offers the most prudent strategy by diversifying across component suppliers, robot makers, and AI software providers — capturing the ecosystem's upside while mitigating single-company risks.

Three China-Focused Robotics ETFs to Consider

Considering the aforementioned discussion, investors eager to capitalize on the rally of China’s robotics industry may consider adding the following ETFs to their portfolios:

Themes China Generative Artificial Intelligence ETF DRGN

This fund, with net asset value of $29.07, offers exposure to 23 Chinese companies that derive significant revenues from Generative AI-related activities. Montage Technology holds the second spot in this fund, with a 6.90% weight, while Cambricon holds the third spot in this fund, with a 6.70% weight. 

Hygon holds the fourth spot in this fund, with a 6.04% weight. DRGN charges 39 basis points (bps) in fees. 

Defiance China Robotics ETF CROB

This fund, with net assets worth $2.3 million, includes Chinese companies engaged in the development, manufacturing, and supply of technologies essential for humanoid robotics, including AI-driven robotics, motion control systems, precision actuators and automation solutions. Leader Harmonious Drive Systems holds the first spot in this fund, with a 7.7% weight.

CROB charges 89 bps in fees. 

China AI ETF AICH

This fund, with net assets worth $1.6 million, offers exposure to companies developing the critical technologies and infrastructure behind China’s AI ambitions, including domestic GPUs, memory chips, optical networking, semiconductor equipment and AI materials. Yushu Technology holds the second spot in this fund, with a 7.7% weight.

AICH charges 86 bps in fees.

text_content: China's industrial robotics sector has recently achieved two historic milestones simultaneously. At a State Council press conference on Oct. 19, 2026, the National Bureau of Statistics reported that China's industrial robot output climbed 29.1% year over year in the first nine months of 2026, maintaining double-digit monthly growth throughout the period. Barely a month earlier, the International Federation of Robotics confirmed that China installed 354,000 industrial robots in 2025 alone, accounting for 59% of every new factory robot deployed anywhere on earth, as per the International Federation of Robotics (“IFR”) report. Impressively, China now operates approximately 2 million industrial robots — 4.3 times Japan's fleet — whereas EU installations fell 11% and Japan dropped 19%, as cited in TechTimes. This latest development puts the spotlight on exchange-traded funds (ETFs) offering exposure to the Chinese companies that are the core accelerators of this robotics revolution. Looking ahead, investors seeking to capitalize on this trend should assess the companies benefiting from China's robotics boom and the country's long-term objectives in this space before exploring related ETF investment opportunities. Companies Powering China's Robotics Boom China's robotics and AI ecosystem is anchored by distinct groups of companies operating across two layers of the value chain. At the hardware layer, companies like Leader Harmonious Drive manufacture harmonic reducers (strain wave gears) and precision motion control products that act as the vital "joints" and actuator modules in robotic arms, industrial automation and humanoid robots. Similarly, Yushu Technology (operating internationally as Unitree Robotics) is a leading global developer and manufacturer of high-performance consumer and industrial-grade legged robots, including quadruped robot dogs and general-purpose humanoid robots. Together, these kinds of firms supply the essential parts that make humanoid robots function. At the intelligence layer, Montage Technology designs memory interface chips for servers and AI data centers, while Cambricon Technologies designs neural processing units and AI chips. Meanwhile, Hygon Information Technology develops CPUs and DCUs for AI computing. These companies power the inference and training workloads that increasingly drive robot autonomy. To this end, it is imperative to mention that China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) designates robotics as the "main driver of economic growth," targeting 100,000 humanoid robots by 2027. In October 2026, Beijing announced a $10 billion worth investment initiative for AI-driven robotics (as cited in TechTimes). This investment strategy, coupled with the initiatives undertaken by the aforementioned companies, is expected to support China's efforts to achieve its humanoid robotics target within the planned timeline. Viewing Through ETF Lens The "See Through ETF Lense" approach is justified by the sheer complexity and volatility of this ecosystem. Individual stock picking carries substantial risk: Unitree surged 629% on its debut, but its valuation now hinges on execution against aggressive production targets. Against this backdrop, a China-focused Robotics ETF offers the most prudent strategy by diversifying across component suppliers, robot makers, and AI software providers — capturing the ecosystem's upside while mitigating single-company risks. Three China-Focused Robotics ETFs to Consider Considering the aforementioned discussion, investors eager to capitalize on the rally of China’s robotics industry may consider adding the following ETFs to their portfolios: Themes China Generative Artificial Intelligence ETF DRGN This fund, with net asset value of $29.07, offers exposure to 23 Chinese companies that derive significant revenues from Generative AI-related activities. Montage Technology holds the second spot in this fund, with a 6.90% weight, while Cambricon holds the third spot in this fund, with a 6.70% weight. Hygon holds the fourth spot in this fund, with a 6.04% weight. DRGN charges 39 basis points (bps) in fees. Defiance China Robotics ETF CROB This fund, with net assets worth $2.3 million, includes Chinese companies engaged in the development, manufacturing, and supply of technologies essential for humanoid robotics, including AI-driven robotics, motion control systems, precision actuators and automation solutions. Leader Harmonious Drive Systems holds the first spot in this fund, with a 7.7% weight. CROB charges 89 bps in fees. China AI ETF AICH This fund, with net assets worth $1.6 million, offers exposure to companies developing the critical technologies and infrastructure behind China’s AI ambitions, including domestic GPUs, memory chips, optical networking, semiconductor equipment and AI materials. Yushu Technology holds the second spot in this fund, with a 7.7% weight. AICH charges 86 bps in fees. excerpt: All Eyes on Fed's FOMC Meeting Outcome.
headline: All Eyes on Fed's FOMC Meeting Outcome
html_content:
We have a solid slate of reports this morning, both of the earnings variety and regarding economic growth. Pre-market indexes continue marching into the green: the Dow +23 points, the Nasdaq +119 (on the continued AI outlook once again viewed favorably) and the S&P 500 +18 points. The small-cap Russell 2000 is currently up 1 point. 

The AI trade — ahead of key hyperscalers reporting Q3 earnings this afternoon: Alphabet GOOGL and Microsoft MSFT — has usurped high oil price fears for the time being. Spot oil prices are now $102 per barrel (/bbl) on West Texas Intermediate (WTI) and $115/bbl on London-based Brent crude following a refinery attack in Saudi Arabia by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels of Yemen.

September Trade & Inventories Spell Economic Health

Ahead of today’s open, the latest Advanced Trade Balance for September is out, dipping deeper into deficit territory to -$134.9 billion, from a slightly improved revision to -$132.1 billion the prior month. Both Imports and Exports were up roughly 2 1/2%, to $344.1 billion and $209.2 billion, respectively. Imports are coming in far ahead based largely on supplies for the grand AI buildout: computers, chips, etc.

Wholesale Inventories for September gained +0.6% month over month, 10 basis points (bps) higher than expected but -10 bps from the prior month’s +0.7%. Year over year Wholesale Inventories are up +7.4% to $1.01 trillion this morning. Meanwhile, Retail Inventories came in at the prior month’s level: +0.3%. Year over year, Retail Inventories are +4.8% to $885.3 billion.

Q3 Earnings at a Glance: ETSY, BIIB, PSX & More

Etsy ETSY is enjoying its best performance in recent memory of late, with Q3 earnings outperforming estimates by +15.67% to $1.55 per share. Revenues cruised to a beat of their own: $692.47 million, which is +3.5% ahead of the Zacks consensus and the year-ago $678 million reported. Shares had already gained +58% year to date, and are up another +6% in pre-market trading. 

Biotech giant Biogen BIIB posted even more impressive numbers ahead of today’s open, with earnings of $2.62 per share versus expectations of $2.06, for a +27.2% positive surprise. Revenues of $2.88 billion outpaced estimates by +8%. The drugmaker also raised guidance, but shares are flat pre-market. BIIB shares have gained +43% year to date. 

Speaking as we were about oil prices, Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy)-rated oil refiner Phillips 66 PSX reported earnings of $14.08 per share, solidly ahead of the $11.97 per share expected. Revenues absolutely destroyed estimates in Q3: $51.51 billion versus the Zacks consensus forecast of $33.72 billion. Shares are up modestly ahead of the opening bell, but have gained +108% year to date.

Apparel brand company V.F. Corp. VFC also posted strong results in its fiscal Q2 report this morning, with earnings of $0.70 per share storming past expectations by +29.63%. Revenues also beat, but by a much more tame +0.07% to $2.70 billion in the quarter. The company did not raise earnings guidance, however, on weakness in its Vans brand. Shares are down -3% in early trading.

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today

At 2pm ET this afternoon, we’ll hear the latest monetary policy decision from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), which is expected to remain unchanged in the +3.75-4.00% range, after a 25 bps hike during the last meeting. Odds for another 25 bps hike increase for the next and final meeting of the FOMC in 2026 on December 9th. Don’t expect much being telegraphed ahead of time by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh; he doesn’t believe in offering guidance on future rate policy.

After the close, Google and YouTube parent Alphabet is expected to have growth +2.44% on earnings year over year, with revenues up +27.82%. Microsoft’s hyperscaling efforts are expected to be pronounced in fiscal Q1: +14% on earnings growth and +16.6% on revenues. ServiceNow NOW in anticipated to have advanced +6.25% in year-over-year earnings, +19.96% on revenues. Meanwhile, Ford F is seen as generating negative growth on both earnings and sales: -13.33% and -3.21%, respectively, in is Q3 report after today’s close.

Zacks' Research Chief Names "Stock Most Likely to Double"

Our team of experts has just released the 5 stocks with the greatest probability of gaining +100% or more in the coming months. Of those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian highlights the one stock set to climb highest.

This innovative software-as-a-service firm upped its user base +22% year over year. That rate is increasing and margins are expanding as AI efficiencies take effect. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners, but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like D-Wave Quantum, which shot up +680.1%.

excerpt: U.S. wind power capacity is set to reach 179.1 GW by 2027. Clearway Energy, Consolidated Edison, OGE Energy and MGE Energy offer promising growth opportunities.
headline: 4 Top Wind Energy Stocks to Bet on for Solid Long-Term Gains
html_content:
An updated edition of the Sept. 3, 2026 article.

Renewable energy is gaining significant traction in the global power landscape as countries prioritize reducing carbon emissions and strengthening energy security. Growing investments in cleaner technologies by governments, utilities and corporations, coupled with rising electricity demand, are driving the need for reliable, low-emission power sources.

Wind energy remains a key contributor to this transition, supported by its abundant supply, technological advancements, expanding onshore and offshore installations and lower generation costs. The sector is well-positioned to support the growing demand for clean and renewable energy as utilities and businesses are increasingly focused on meeting sustainability targets. Beyond environmental benefits, its growing adoption also supports greater energy efficiency and job creation.

Per the U.S. Energy Information Administration’s (EIA) latest Short-Term Energy Outlook, the U.S. wind power sector continues to expand, with installed generation capacity of 167.6 gigawatts (GW) by the end of third-quarter 2026. The EIA forecasts capacity to climb to 170.3 GW by the end of 2026 before increasing further to 179.1 GW by 2027-end. The outlook also projects wind energy to contribute 11% to total U.S. electricity generation in 2026, with its share increasing to 12% in 2027.

The wind energy market is capitalizing on several favorable trends, including growing electricity demand driven by Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered data centers, widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and rapid industrialization. Per the EIA report, the U.S. grid is projected to add 11.4 GW of wind generation capacity in 2026.

The expansion of U.S. wind power capacity is expected to gain momentum from the development and commissioning of major offshore projects, including Vineyard Wind 1, Revolution Wind, Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind and Empire Wind 1. These projects are likely to boost renewable energy capacity and reinforce the clean energy infrastructure.

If you intend to capitalize on this buzzing trend, our Wind Energy Thematic Screen could make it easy to identify high-potential stocks such as Clearway Energy, Inc. CWEN, Consolidated Edison, Inc. ED, OGE Energy Corp. OGE and MGE Energy, Inc. MGEE. By leveraging advanced tools, our thematic screens identify companies shaping the future, making it easier to benefit from emerging trends.

Ready to uncover more transformative thematic investment ideas? Explore 40 cutting-edge investment themes with Zacks Thematic Investing Screens and discover your next big opportunity.

4 Wind Energy Stocks to Bet on Now

Headquartered in Princeton, NJ, Clearway Energy owns and operates a diversified portfolio of contracted renewable and conventional power generation assets across 27 U.S. states, with approximately 13.9 gigawatts (GW) of gross capacity. Its portfolio includes 11.1 GW of wind, solar and battery energy storage systems, along with 2.8 GW of dispatchable combustion-based assets.

Clearway Energy continues to strengthen its wind and solar portfolio through asset upgrades, repowering initiatives and contract extensions to extend operational life and improve cash flow visibility. Its repowering program is progressing as planned, with more than 600 megawatts (MW) of committed wind projects underway and more than 300 MW in development expected to enter construction in 2027. These efforts are likely to enhance asset longevity and support long-term contracted power generation with higher value.

In June 2026, the Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) company secured separate 15-year power purchase agreements (PPAs) for its Langford and Elbow Creek wind facilities with investment-grade and commercial counterparties, respectively. These contracts replaced earlier commodity-linked arrangements, offering improved pricing terms and greater visibility into long-term revenues.

Based in New York, Consolidated Edison is a diversified utility holding company with subsidiaries engaged in both regulated and unregulated businesses. The company is involved in the regulated electric, gas and steam delivery businesses across the US.

The Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company is developing the Brooklyn Clean Energy Hub, a transmission substation designed to enhance New York’s power grid reliability and facilitate offshore wind integration during construction and operation. Scheduled for completion by 2028, the facility will support up to 1,500 megawatts (MW) of electricity.

Consolidated Edison plans to invest $6.6 billion in 2026 and nearly $38 billion during 2026-2030 to modernize and expand its electric, gas and steam infrastructure, enhancing service reliability and supporting long-term rate base growth.

Headquartered in Oklahoma City, OK, OGE Energy provides electricity in Oklahoma and western Arkansas. The Zacks Rank #2 company continues to benefit from its strategic investments, which are focused on infrastructure upgrades. The company also stands to benefit from its efforts to expand its renewable energy generation portfolio, positioning it for sustained long-term growth.

The company offers the Renewable Energy Credit purchase program, the Green Power Wind Rider and the Utility Solar Program, which are rate options that make renewable energy resources available to all OG&E Oklahoma retail customers on a voluntary basis.

OG&E aims to continue to deploy more renewable energy sources that do not emit greenhouse gases. The company expects to expand its generation capacity by 550 megawatts (MW) in 2026 through the Horseshoe Lake and Tinker projects. Additionally, the 300 MW Frontier Energy Storage project is slated to begin operations in the second half of 2027, further strengthening the company’s power generation portfolio.

Based in Madison, WI, MGE Energy generates electricity from coal, natural gas and renewable resources and offers solar and wind generation along with battery storage services.

Renewable energy projects are central to MGE Energy’s efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions and achieve net-zero carbon electricity by 2050. The company also plans to reduce its reliance on fossil fuels while helping customers improve energy efficiency and expand electrification, including the shift to electric transportation.

MGE continues to work on its strategy of making long-term investments in clean energy assets. Since 2015, the Zacks Rank #2 company has incorporated 93 MW of wind generation, 253 MW of solar and 11 MW of battery storage capacity into its renewable electricity portfolio. It plans to add about 18 MW of wind, 252 MW of solar and 125 MW of battery storage by the end of 2030 through projects that have either received or are awaiting approval from PSCW.

You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

excerpt: AAR (AIR) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: AAR (AIR) Down 6.3% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
html_content:
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for AAR (AIR). Shares have lost about 6.3% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

But investors have to be wondering, will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is AAR due for a breakout? Before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late, let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the important drivers.

AAR Q1 Earnings and Revenues Rise Year Over Year

AAR Corp. reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings of $1.49 per share, which improved 38% from the year-ago quarter’s level of $1.08.

The company reported GAAP earnings of $1.00 per share compared with 95 cents in the prior-year quarter.

The year-over-year improvement in the bottom line can be attributed to strong operating performance.

AIR’s Total Sales

In the quarter under review, AAR generated net sales of $918 million. The reported figure increased 24% from $739.6 million recorded in the year-ago quarter.

The year-over-year improvement can be attributed to growth across all three core segments, including continued above-market commercial distribution sales and acquisition contributions. Commercial customer sales increased 28%, while government customer sales rose 14%.

AAR: Segment Details

Parts Supply sales surged 30.5% to $414.8 million from $317.8 million in the prior-year quarter. Organic growth in new-parts distribution was 23%, with commercial distribution rising 21% organically and government distribution increasing 28%.

Repair, Engineering and Software sales jumped 31.4% to $297.5 million. Growth reflected the HAECO Americas acquisition as well as organic growth across Airframe MRO, Component MRO and Software.

Government Solutions sales increased 3.7% to $138.8 million. Growth in Mobility Systems and newer higher-margin government programs more than offset lower activity under the Worldwide Aviation Support Services program.

Legacy Commercial Programs recorded sales of $66.9 million compared with $61.5 million in the prior-year quarter.

AIR’s Operational Update

AIR’s adjusted operating income increased 35.5% to $97 million, while adjusted operating margin improved 90 basis points to 10.6%.

excerpt: SIF and PKE ride on different aerospace growth drivers, but which stock looks more compelling amid contrasting performance and valuations? Let's dive in.
headline: SIFCO vs. Park Aerospace: Which Aerospace Stock Is a Better Buy?
html_content:
The aerospace and defense industry continues to operate in an environment influenced by recovering commercial aircraft production, sustained defense spending and increasing demand for advanced aerospace materials and components. Against this backdrop, SIFCO Industries, Inc. SIF and Park Aerospace Corp. PKE are two aerospace companies serving commercial and defense markets with distinct manufacturing approaches. SIF specializes in producing forgings and machined components for aerospace, defense, energy and commercial space applications. In contrast, PKE develops and manufactures advanced composite materials and structures for aerospace applications.

While both companies cater to the aerospace and defense markets, their distinct business models and operational strategies shape their investment appeal. This raises an important question: which stock is better positioned for investors today? Let's take a closer look.

Stock Performance & Valuation: SIF vs. PKE

SIF (down 22.7%) has underperformed PKE (down 19.7%) over the past three months. However, in the past year, SIFCO stock has surged 181.5% compared with Park Aerospace’s gain of 39.4%.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Meanwhile, SIF is trading at a trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-sales (EV/S) ratio of 1.3X, above its median of 0.3X over the past five years. PKE’s trailing 12-month EV/S multiple sits at 5.8X, above its last five-year median of 3.6X. While SIF appears cheap when compared with the Zacks Aerospace sector’s average of 2.7X, PKE seems to be expensive.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Factors Driving SIFCO Stock

SIFCO benefits from recovering commercial aircraft production and sustained demand for military aerospace components. The company supports major Boeing and Airbus aircraft programs, as well as military platforms such as the F-35 and H-60 Black Hawk. Continued aircraft fleet utilization, defense modernization and sustainment requirements create opportunities for its specialized forging capabilities. Its established presence across these programs positions SIF to benefit from favorable demand trends.

SIFCO's emphasis on manufacturing efficiency and workforce development supports its profitability prospects. Management has reported improved success in recruiting and retaining skilled personnel, helping address production constraints. Ongoing process improvements aimed at increasing throughput and productivity could enhance manufacturing execution and cost efficiency. The substantial improvement in adjusted EBITDA during the first nine months of fiscal 2026 further supports SIF's operational progress.

SIFCO's substantial order backlog provides visibility into future business activity. The backlog reflects established customer relationships, new program content and orders scheduled for future delivery. SIF's longstanding relationships with major aerospace customers, supported by multi-year agreements, provide a foundation for recurring business opportunities. Effective conversion of outstanding orders into shipments could sustain revenue momentum and strengthen future operating performance.

Factors Aiding Park Aerospace Stock

Park Aerospace benefits from its established presence across major GE Aerospace and CFM jet engine programs. Its sole-source-qualified composite materials support engine nacelle and thrust reverser applications, particularly for the Airbus A320neo aircraft family. Increasing aircraft production and the growing market share of LEAP-1A engines could strengthen demand for PKE's materials. Its long-term supply agreement with Middle River Aerostructure Systems further provides a foundation for sustained commercial aerospace business.

Park Aerospace's specialized ablative materials play an important role in critical defense applications, including the PAC-3 MSE Patriot missile system. Efforts to replenish depleted missile inventories and accelerate interceptor production create favorable demand opportunities. PKE's sole-source qualification for key rocket motor materials strengthens its competitive position in this specialized market. Its established relationship with ArianeGroup also supports access to proprietary materials essential for missile applications.

Park Aerospace continues ramping up production at its expanded Newton, KS, facility to meet growing customer demand. The company also plans an additional integrated manufacturing and development facility to support future aerospace opportunities. These investments could enhance production capabilities, improve operational flexibility and support higher output. Improving gross margins and adjusted EBITDA further demonstrate PKE's ability to translate growing business activity into stronger operating performance.

Choose SIF Over PKE Now

Both SIFCO and Park Aerospace offer exposure to favorable aerospace and defense industry trends, but with different investment propositions. While SIF presents an opportunity to benefit from improving operational performance and a healthy order backlog, PKE offers established profitability and a stronger position in specialized aerospace applications.

From a valuation perspective, SIFCO appears relatively attractive compared with Park Aerospace, offering investors exposure to aerospace and defense opportunities at a considerably lower valuation. Although SIF trades above its historical valuation levels, its discount to the broader sector suggests potential room for appreciation if operational improvements continue. In contrast, PKE's premium valuation reflects its stronger profitability and growth prospects but leaves investors with less room for disappointment if execution falls short of expectations.

Considering these factors, SIF appears to be the better buy right now, particularly for value-oriented investors seeking exposure to improving aerospace and defense fundamentals. Its comparatively attractive valuation and ongoing operational improvements support its investment appeal, although sustaining profitability remains important. While Park Aerospace offers stronger profitability and established competitive advantages, SIFCO presents a more compelling risk-reward proposition for investors willing to accept greater execution uncertainty.

excerpt: Burlington (BURL) stock has fallen nearly 20% year to date, but declining earnings estimates and bearish technicals suggest more downside could be ahead.
headline: Bear of the Day: Burlington Stores (BURL)
html_content:
Off-price retail giant Burlington Stores BURL) has struggled in 2026, with shares plunging almost 40% in the last three months and now down nearly 20% year-to-date as declining earnings expectations raise concerns about the retailer's near-term profitability.

Despite the selloff, BURL shares still trade well above $200, and unfavorable earnings estimate revisions suggest investors may want to remain cautious as the stock could face additional downside.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Burlington’s Declining Earnings Estimates

Burlington's near-term profitability outlook has weakened with management expecting Q3 adjusted earnings of $1.60-$1.70 per share, down from $1.80 a year ago, as operating margins face pressure from merchandise pricing investments and softer consumer spending.

Furthermore, comparable-store sales growth most recently slowed to 2% in Q2 from 5% a year earlier, raising questions about underlying demand as inflation and elevated living costs weigh on budget-conscious shoppers.

Most concerning is the negative trend in Burlington's earnings estimate revisions, with analysts becoming increasingly cautious about the company's outlook.

Over the last 60 days, Burlington's current fiscal-year EPS estimate has fallen 5.5% from $12.61 to $11.92 per share, while next year's projection has declined 4.6% from $13.87 to $13.23 per share.

Near-term expectations have also weakened, with earnings estimates for the next two quarters falling roughly 7.6% and 3.2%, respectively.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Rising Costs & Slowing Sales Threaten Burlington's Margins

Compounding these challenges, higher tariffs, elevated freight costs, and potential customer traffic slowdowns could pressure Burlington's margins.

Meanwhile, Burlington's transition toward smaller 25,000-27,000-square-foot stores is intended to improve sales productivity, but execution risks and rising costs remain potential headwinds, especially after the company has missed revenue expectations in two of its last four quarterly reports.

 

BURL Forms a Death Cross

Adding to its bearish outlook, Burlington's technical chart indicates mounting selling pressure, with BURL trading well below its 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages of approximately $262 and $306 a share, respectively.

More concerning, the 50-day SMA (green line below) has fallen below the 200-day SMA (red line), forming a bearish death cross pattern that suggests weakening momentum and the potential for further downside.

With BURL approaching its recent 52-week lows near $226, the stock could remain under pressure until buying interest returns and its technical trend improves.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Burlington's Mediocre Valuation

Even after falling nearly 20% year-to-date, Burlington shares still command a forward P/E multiple near 20X. This is roughly on par with, but not a discount to its Zacks Retail-Discount Stores industry average, which includes noteworthy peers such as Ross Stores ROST) and The TJX Companies TJX).  

While Burlington has opportunities to expand its store footprint and capture market share in the off-price retail segment, the trend of declining EPS revisions is taking away from its modest valuation and leaves shares vulnerable to further selling pressure if earnings expectations continue to decline.

 

Bottom Line

Burlington Stores stock currently lands a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), reflecting the unfavorable trend in earnings estimate revisions.

With profitability expectations weakening and shares offering little valuation discount to industry peers, BURL may be a stock investors want to avoid for now, particularly until earnings revisions stabilize.

headline: Implied Volatility Surging for ATS Corporation Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in ATS Corporation ATS need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Nov. 20, 2026 $15.00 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for ATS Corporation shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, ATS Corporation is a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) in the Manufacturing - General Industrial industry that ranks in the Bottom 38% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter has moved from 31 cents per share to 28 cents in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about ATS Corporation right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

excerpt: Although the revenue and EPS for Silgan (SLGN) give a sense of how its business performed in the quarter ended September 2026, it might be worth considering how some key metrics compare with Wall Street estimates and the year-ago numbers.
headline: Silgan (SLGN) Q3 Earnings: Taking a Look at Key Metrics Versus Estimates
html_content:
Silgan Holdings (SLGN) reported $2.04 billion in revenue for the quarter ended September 2026, representing a year-over-year increase of 1.6%. EPS of $1.31 for the same period compares to $1.22 a year ago.

The reported revenue represents a surprise of -1.59% over the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.07 billion. With the consensus EPS estimate being $1.26, the EPS surprise was +3.97%.

While investors closely watch year-over-year changes in headline numbers -- revenue and earnings -- and how they compare to Wall Street expectations to determine their next course of action, some key metrics always provide a better insight into a company's underlying performance.

Since these metrics play a crucial role in driving the top- and bottom-line numbers, comparing them with the year-ago numbers and what analysts estimated about them helps investors better project a stock's price performance.

Here is how Silgan performed in the just reported quarter in terms of the metrics most widely monitored and projected by Wall Street analysts:
  • Net Sales- Metal Containers: $1.17 billion compared to the $1.22 billion average estimate based on two analysts. The reported number represents a change of +1.4% year over year.
  • Net Sales- Dispensing and Specialty Closures: $699.2 million compared to the $719.52 million average estimate based on two analysts. The reported number represents a change of +1.3% year over year.
  • Net Sales- Custom Containers: $166.8 million versus the two-analyst average estimate of $169.58 million. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of +4.2%.

excerpt: Boston Scientific faces a challenging 2027 as cybersecurity disruptions, EP and WATCHMAN weakness and China pricing pressures weigh on growth prospects.
headline: BSX Q3 Earnings Call Flags Growth Challenges Through 2027
html_content:
Boston Scientific Corporation BSX outlined a challenging near-term outlook during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, citing mounting competitive pressures, cybersecurity disruptions and unfavorable pricing dynamics in China.

Management expects 2027 to mark the trough of its current business cycle, with revenue and adjusted earnings growth remaining under pressure before a recovery driven by product innovation and restructuring initiatives in 2028.

BSX Faces a Difficult Growth Outlook for 2027

Chairman and CEO Michael Mahoney acknowledged that the company's Electrophysiology (“EP”) and WATCHMAN franchises have transitioned from major growth contributors into significant headwinds.

Management expects fourth-quarter organic revenues to decline 1%-3%, with adjusted earnings of 77-79 cents per share. Full-year organic revenue growth is projected at approximately 3.75%, with adjusted earnings of $3.16-$3.18 per share.

Mahoney expects revenue and adjusted earnings growth to remain challenged in 2027, excluding the pending Penumbra acquisition. The company anticipates improved performance in 2028, followed by further acceleration in 2029.

Boston Scientific Details Cybersecurity Disruption

Chief financial officer Jonathan Monson attributed approximately 300 basis points of third-quarter revenue growth pressure to the cybersecurity incident, equivalent to roughly $150 million in lost sales.

The disruption reduced adjusted earnings by approximately 7 cents per share. Despite restoring operations by Sept. 8, management anticipates another 200-300 basis points of revenue pressure in the fourth quarter as customers normalize inventory levels.

Adjusted earnings totaled 73 cents per share, in line with the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Third-quarter revenues reached $5.14 billion, which beat the consensus mark of $5.10 billion.

Boston Scientific Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Boston Scientific Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Boston Scientific Corporation Quote

BSX Confronts EP and WATCHMAN Competitive Pressures

Mahoney reported that EP revenues declined 5%, including an 8% contraction in the United States. Competitive product introductions continue to erode the company's pulsed-field ablation market share.

The WATCHMAN franchise declined 6%, reflecting weaker standalone procedures and changing physician referral patterns. Management expects continued competitive pressure in 2027 despite investments in physician education and commercial resources.

During the JPMorgan Q&A, Mahoney clarified that the company's 2027 outlook assumes no meaningful WATCHMAN market recovery. EP improvement depends heavily on the planned FARAWAVE Ultra launch in early 2028 and FARAFLEX introduction in 2029.

Boston Scientific Advances Restructuring and Innovation

Monson expects the restructuring program to generate more than $500 million in savings over three years, with more than half achieved by the end of 2027.

The initiative targets organizational simplification, supply-chain optimization, shared services and discretionary spending. Management intends to preserve investments in strategically important product platforms despite near-term margin pressures.

Responding to BTIG's questions, Monson identified product mix as the primary obstacle to 2027 earnings growth. Weakness in EP and WATCHMAN, combined with Chinese pricing pressure, is expected to constrain gross margins.

BSX Targets Portfolio Expansion Despite Delays

Interventional Cardiology delivered 19% growth, supported by imaging technologies and drug-eluting products. Neuromodulation increased 13%, providing another source of underlying strength.

Management expects the Penumbra acquisition to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. During the Jefferies Q&A, Monson cautioned that higher financing costs could increase the transaction's previously anticipated earnings dilution.

The pipeline also faces execution challenges. During Piper Sandler's questioning, Cardiovascular Group president Joseph Fitzgerald attributed FARAWAVE Ultra delays to design verification and validation, while FARAFLEX faces clinical enrollment and operational hurdles.

Boston Scientific Focuses on Rebuilding Execution

Mahoney emphasized organizational accountability, forecasting improvements and disciplined investment as central priorities for restoring performance.

Monson acknowledged previous forecasting shortcomings and outlined enhanced scenario analysis, objective modeling and third-party data integration. Management remains focused on stabilizing operations in 2027 while positioning the business for stronger growth thereafter.

What BSX's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

BSX currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), reflecting an unfavorable near-term earnings estimate revision outlook. Its Value and Growth Scores of B indicate relatively favorable characteristics in those categories, while its Momentum Score of D signals weaker momentum. The stock also carries a VGM Score of B.

Although the favorable Value, Growth and VGM Scores highlight certain underlying attributes, the Zacks Rank #4 warrants caution under the combined ranking framework. The Zacks Rank can change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest quarterly results.

excerpt: Expand Energy is leaning on gas marketing, hedges and flexible drilling to weather weak prices, with a $500 million marketing EBITDA target by 2028.
headline: EXE Q3 Earnings Call Eyes Marketing Growth Amid Gas Price Weakness
html_content:
Expand Energy Corporation EXE is positioning its expanded gas marketing platform to cushion weak near-term prices, while preparing for demand growth later in the decade. Management emphasized commercial integration, flexible production and disciplined capital deployment on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call.

New chief executive officer Daniel Brown highlighted the company's scale, inventory and customer access, emphasizing execution on the platform already assembled.

EXE Targets Higher Marketing Margins

Chief financial officer Marcel Teunissen said that the Sept. 16 acquisition of Twin Eagle has broadened the company's reach to industrial, power and other natural gas customers across North America.

Teunissen projected $80 million in combined marketing and commercial EBITDA for the fourth quarter, equivalent to roughly $0.12 per Mcf, despite low expected price volatility.

In response to Goldman Sachs, he outlined a target of a $500 million marketing and commercial EBITDA run rate by 2028, with a longer-term goal of $750 million as LNG opportunities develop.

Asked by Wolfe Research about breakevens, Teunissen said that commercial gains could lower the company's cash breakeven, including dividends, from about $2.8 per Mcf to $2.6 by 2028.

Expand Stays Flexible as Gas Prices Weaken

Chief operating officer Josh Viets told a JPMorgan analyst that incremental gas supply and subdued winter expectations are weighing on the 2027 forward price curve despite strong underlying demand.

Expand reduced drilling activity from approximately 12 rigs to 10 entering the fourth quarter and deferred nine well turn-in-lines during the third quarter. Viets said the company would adjust production timing to market conditions.

He described 2027 as a transition year ahead of roughly 13 Bcf/d of additional demand expected by year-end 2028. Fourth-quarter production guidance of 7.4-7.6 Bcf/d preserves operating flexibility; the company expects 7.45-7.55 Bcfe/d for full-year 2026.

EXE Extends Downside Protection Through Hedging

Teunissen told a Pickering Energy Partners analyst that management hedged more aggressively after judging earlier forward prices inconsistent with supply-demand fundamentals.

The company has hedged 55% of its 2027 gas production at an average price of $3.65 per Mcf. The strategy combines instruments designed to protect downside exposure while retaining some upside participation.

Hedging improved third-quarter realized prices by $0.46 per Mcfe. Adjusted earnings of $1.46 per share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.28, while natural gas, oil and NGL revenue of $1.88 billion missed the $2.06 billion estimate.

Expand Energy Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Expand Energy Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Expand Energy Corporation Quote

Expand Weighs Inflation Against Efficiency Gains

Viets said that diesel costs drove much of 2026 inflation, while greater use of electric fracturing fleets should cut diesel consumption by about 50% in 2027.

He expects low to mid-single-digit cost inflation next year, particularly from pressure pumping and oil-country tubular goods as drilling activity increases.

To counter that pressure, Viets highlighted a 20% improvement in Southwest Appalachia drilling footage per day and a 10% reduction in drilling cost per foot from 2025 to 2026.

EXE Prioritizes Balance Sheet Discipline

With full-year capital investment guidance updated to approximately $3 billion, Teunissen told UBS that drilling and completion spending, dividends and balance sheet strength come before discretionary growth opportunities, including stock repurchases.

Expand repurchased $305 million in shares during the quarter and reported leverage of 0.8x. After the Twin Eagle acquisition added debt, management intends to reduce leverage while preserving opportunities for additional buybacks.

Brown told a Morgan Stanley analyst that acquisitions must improve the portfolio and deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns. He emphasized confidence in achievable synergies rather than pursuing transactions for scale alone.

Expand Focuses on Execution Into 2027

Brown's early message centered on continuous improvement and careful capital allocation across the integrated platform. His appointment places an experienced upstream executive alongside the recently strengthened commercial organization.

Management maintained a measured posture toward near-term gas pricing while pursuing longer-term customer relationships and operational improvements. Its priorities remain flexibility, integration and financial resilience.

EXE's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Send Mixed Signals

EXE carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), reflecting a neutral near-term rating. Its Value Score of A and Growth Score of B indicate favorable valuation and growth characteristics, while its Momentum Score of F points to a weak momentum profile.

The VGM Score of A reflects a favorable weighted combination of value, growth and momentum measures. However, the strongest historical combinations pair favorable Style Scores with Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) stocks. excerpt: Initial Claims Remain Almost Flat.
headline: Initial Claims Remain Almost Flat
html_content:
Pre-market futures are giving back some of their gains accrued over the early part of this trading week, though the depths have recovered slightly since the latest inflation report hit the tape. The Dow is currently -71 points, the Nasdaq -321 (it had gained the most on renewed interest in the AI trade this week) and the S&P 500 is -18 points. Only the small-cap Russell 2000 is +8 points at this hour. 

Bond yields and spot oil prices are dialed back somewhat from a day ago: +5.024% on the 10-year, +4.704% on the 2-year and +5.350% on the 30-year. These are still keeping elevated — especially on the long end, which affects mortgage rates — but off the multi-year highs we were seeing a month ago. Spot oil prices remain at $10 per barrel (/bbl) on WTI and +115/bbl on global Brent crude — precisely where they were a day ago.

The first look at Q3 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was released with the inflation data listed below, and it came out ahead of expectations: +3.4% — subject to a couple of revisions — up from the +3.1% anticipated and the Q2 third installment GDP of +2.2%. The economy is heating up, in other words, or at least it is in an early snapshot.

PCE Inflation Data Slightly Lower than Expectations

The good news regarding our latest inflation report — Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) for September, which had been cited as the Fed’s preferred gauge of inflation — is that we’re not screaming higher as oil prices remain elevated (the war in Iran is now entering its ninth month). Headline PCE Price Index month over month reached +0.5%, in-line with expectations. Year over year, this came in at +3.6%, 10 basis points (bps) below consensus.

Core PCE (subtracting volatile food and energy expenditures) was in-line with estimates at +0.3% month over month, +3.1% year over year, but both were 10 bps higher than a month ago. Again, this does not depict a dire scenario, but it does reflect inflation levels continually increasing. A year ago, PCE was +2.8% year over year, and a year before that we were at +2.3% — much closer to the Fed’s stated inflation level preference of +2.0%.

Both Personal Income and Consumer Spending were a tick below expectations: +0.2% and +0.5%, respectively. Income rates were steady from the previous month while Spending saw a drop off from +0.9% in August. While this tightening of the belt is likely a healthy response to elevated expenditures for the month, Americans are still spending at a higher rate than they are earning. This pushes credit levels higher, with elevated interest rates to deal with.

Weekly Jobless Claims Remain Spectacular

(Or should I say “spooktacular,” as we are two days from Halloween?) Initial Jobless Claims reached +194K last week, down from the slightly upwardly revised +195K the prior week. We haven’t been above +200K new jobless claims since the week of Labor Day, and only approaching +300K new claims per week would give analysts pause regarding the health of the labor market.

Continuing Claims, reported a week in arrears, dipped again to +1.701 million — below the upwardly revised +1.722 million, and the third week in the last six where we’ve been at these 3+ year lows. As we’ve said in the past, we don’t see Jobless Claims as giving the full picture of domestic unemployment; besides retiring Baby Boomers and prosperous Gen Xers, many are seeing their latest pink slip as motivation to get into the ride-share business.

Q3 Earnings Reports at a Glance: LLY, CAT, MA & More

Pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly LLY outperformed expectations in Q3 this morning, beating earnings estimates by +39% to $7.48 per share. Revenues of $24.4 billion were +10.37% higher than the Zacks consensus, as GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound continue to set the pace in the weight-loss market. Shares are up +4% in early trading, now over +20% year to date. 

Caterpillar CAT, on the other hand, is seeing shares fall nearly -12% in early trading this morning, following its Q3 beats on both top and bottom lines. However, the company did not raise guidance, indicating that the company’s recent boon in AI infrastructure buildout may be slowing in the quarters ahead. 

Zacks Rank #2 (Buy)-rated Mastercard MA shares are up over +2% in today’s pre-market, as the company posted a +3.3% positive earnings in Q3 results to $5.31 per share, on revenues of $9.81 billion which came out ahead of the $9.63 billion projected, and up +14% year over year. Volumes and card activity are strong for Mastercard at present.

Crocs CROX continues its stellar performance in 2026, with Q3 results coming in +11.5% ahead of expectations on earnings to $3.69 per share, and revenues of $1.04 billion surpassing forecasts by +3.74%. Shares are +16% in pre-market trading, adding to the company’s +40% gains year to date.

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today

Market news has been favorable this morning, so we’ll check if we continue to see positive sentiment push back against the early-morning setback. After today’s close, we’ll see more headline earnings reports hit the tape — from Amazon AMZN to Starbucks SBUX to Twilio TWLO.

excerpt: Uranium Energy (UEC) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Why Is Uranium Energy (UEC) Down 11.8% Since Last Earnings Report?
html_content:
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for Uranium Energy (UEC). Shares have lost about 11.8% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Uranium Energy due for a breakout? Before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late, let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the important catalysts.

UEC Q4 Earnings Miss Estimates on Higher Costs, Sales Beat on Higher Prices

Uranium Energy reported a loss of 7 cents per share in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, wider than the Zacks Consensus Estimate of a loss of 4 cents.

Uranium Energy reported a fiscal 2026 loss of 28 cents per share compared with a loss of 20 cents in fiscal 2025. Net loss widened to $137.31 million in fiscal 2026 compared with a net loss of $87.66 million in fiscal 2025. The results reflected continued spending on mine development and expansion initiatives.

Operationally, uranium production surged 157% sequentially to 82,744 pounds in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, supported by higher output at Christensen Ranch and the first full quarter of production at Burke Hollow.

UEC’s revenues totaled $17 million in the fourth quarter, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9 million by 89.4%. Fiscal 2026 revenues were $37.25 million, down 44.3% year over year from $66.84 million in fiscal 2025, primarily due to lower sales volumes. 

Uranium Energy sold 400,000 pounds of purchased uranium at a weighted average realized price of $93.13 per pound in fiscal 2026. The company had sold 810,000 pounds of purchased uranium inventory at a weighted average price of $82.52 per pound in fiscal 2025.

Uranium Energy's Operating Costs Pressure Results

Uranium Energy's operating costs remained elevated as the company expanded uranium extraction activities and advanced its development portfolio. For fiscal 2026, total operating costs increased 53.4% year over year to $150.04 million. Mineral property expenditures rose to $102.37 million from $66.06 million, reflecting increased exploration, development and pre-extraction activities.

General and administrative expenses increased to $34.5 million from $27.3 million. The company also incurred around $6.3 million in uranium refining and conversion project expenditures. Consequently, the full-year operating loss widened to $133.2 million in fiscal 2026 from $73.32 million in fiscal 2025.

Uranium Energy Scales Wyoming Production at Christensen Ranch

Christensen Ranch remained the company's largest producing operation during the fourth quarter. Production doubled sequentially to 65,392 pounds of uranium concentrate. Total cash costs declined to $28.38 per pound from $46.69 in the preceding quarter, while total production costs decreased 35% to $35.63 per pound.

The company continued expanding wellfield infrastructure at Christensen Ranch. Four additional header houses received regulatory approval on Sept. 28, 2026, with production expected to commence in the following weeks.

Three additional header houses were under construction, supported by increased drilling capacity. The company operated 17 drill rigs in Wyoming's Powder River Basin at fiscal year-end, compared with 12 a year earlier.

Uranium Energy Advances Burke Hollow Operations

Burke Hollow in South Texas completed its first full quarter of operation, producing 17,352 pounds of uranium concentrate. Total cash costs were $36.13 per pound, while total production costs were $39.93 per pound. Production was limited to a portion of the initial wellfield as the company established operating parameters before further expansion.

During the quarter, 126 injection and recovery wells were brought online. The Hobson Central Processing Plant also completed commissioning across its uranium processing operations. Drilling capacity expanded considerably, with 21 rigs operating in South Texas at fiscal year-end compared with eight in the preceding year.

Uranium Energy's Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Position

Uranium Energy ended fiscal 2026 with $753 million in liquid assets, including approximately $495 million in cash, and no debt. Cash and cash equivalents increased from $148.93 million at July 31, 2025. Working capital totaled $547.61 million, compared with $207.58 million a year earlier.

Net cash used in operating activities increased to $98.56 million for fiscal 2026 from $64.46 million in the preceding year, reflecting continued development spending. The company also held 1,256,000 pounds of purchased uranium inventory at fiscal year-end, valued at approximately $109 million based on prevailing market prices.

Uranium Energy's Development Pipeline and Outlook

Uranium Energy continued advancing its Ludeman ISR project in Wyoming, where wellfield construction and engineering for the satellite ion-exchange plant progressed. At Sweetwater, federal permitting activities continued, with environmental assessment completion anticipated in March 2027 and approval of the Plan of Operations targeted for May 2027. The company also completed 36,000 meters of drilling at its Roughrider project in Saskatchewan to support resource conversion and a planned pre-feasibility study.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

In the past month, investors have witnessed a downward trend in estimates review.

The consensus estimate has shifted -50% due to these changes.

VGM Scores

Currently, Uranium Energy has a poor Growth Score of F, a score with the same score on the momentum front. Following the exact same course, the stock has a grade of F on the value side, putting it in the lowest quintile for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of F. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending downward for the stock, and the magnitude of this revision indicates a downward shift. It's no surprise Uranium Energy has a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell). We expect a below average return from the stock in the next few months.

excerpt: The Zacks Waste Removal Services industry is anticipated to gain from the rising need for ESG Goals, technological developments and innovation in WTE technology. HTO, CLH and BBCP are well-poised to gain from growing demand.
headline: 3 Stocks to Buy From the Booming Waste Removal Services Market
html_content:
The Waste Management industry is experiencing positive trends in government regulations, adoption of advanced technologies and an increasing awareness of environmental issues. Despite rising operating costs, the industry does not shy away from swift industrialization and urbanization. Per Mordor Intelligence, the global waste management sector is expected to see a 6.2% CAGR through 2032. The potential expansion of the global waste management sector can be attributed to better waste collection methods and rising volumes of waste in emerging markets.

Three promising stocks from the Waste Removal Services market are H2O America HTO, Clean Harbors CLH and Concrete Pumping Holdings BBCP.

About the Industry

Companies in the Zacks Waste Removal Services industry play a vital role in the collection, treatment and responsible management of diverse waste types, aiming to minimize their impacts on the environment and public health. This market is categorized into distinct segments based on the kind of waste, including industrial, commercial, domestic and agricultural waste. The Industrial waste segment has gained significance due to the ongoing industrial expansion, creating a substantial demand for efficient waste management solutions. The market encompasses Collection and Disposal services. The Disposal services segment, primarily fueled by the growing need for waste recycling to mitigate environmental impacts, stands as the primary revenue-generating category.

What's Shaping the Future of the Business Services Industry?

Rising Importance of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Goals: Waste management is a cornerstone of ESG principles, as it helps companies improve their ESG ratings by promoting environmental sustainability, fostering social well-being and upholding good governance. Per Grand View Research, the average ESG disclosure score for the waste management industry lies at 50-60%. Embracing responsible waste management meets legal requirements and aligns with consumer and investor desires for sustainable and ethical business practices. At present, waste management is not only a duty but also a chance for businesses to showcase their dedication to ESG values, which underpin lasting success and resilience.

Technology Drives Waste Management Industry Growth: Technology has become a vital component in waste management, addressing the challenges of waste generation and environmental impacts. This transformative correlation promises a more sustainable future. For instance, AI is emerging as a crucial tool to sort waste and keep recyclable materials from going into landfills. Advancing technology results in more effective, eco-friendly waste management, lowering the ecological footprint and promoting sustainability. Waste challenges can be mitigated using technology that leads us toward responsible waste management and a cleaner planet.

Innovations in Waste-to-Energy (WTE)Technology Aid: WTE comprises thermal (pyrolysis, incineration and gasification) and biological solutions (composting and anaerobic digestion), which play crucial roles in sustainable waste management. This technology transforms waste into energy via methods like incineration or gasification. Per a report by Fortune Business Insights, the Waste-to-Energy Market size is estimated to be $38.9 billion in 2026, expected to see a 3.6% CAGR through 2034. The rise is expected to be fuelled by the surge in the amount of waste generation, growing waste management concerns to meet sustainable living standards and increased focus on non-fossil fuels. The industry holds an important position in the era of clean energy, offering a renewable energy source and addressing the mounting challenges around waste management.

Increasing Operating Costs Are Concerning: Waste management is a time-consuming and complex process. It requires higher capital and operating costs to manage waste collection vehicles, bins and processing equipment, along with a huge number of workers. Such high operational expenses are anticipated to keep the bottom line of the companies in this industrial cohort under pressure.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Near-Term Prospects

The Zacks Waste Removal Services industry, which is housed within the Zacks Business Services sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #75. This rank places it in the top 30% of 247 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates a continued outperformance in the near term. Our research shows that the top 50% of Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let us take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and current valuation.

Industry & S&P 500 Rises While Sector Plunges

The Zacks Waste Removal Services industry has moved up marginally over the past year. It outpaced the broader sector’s 12% dip but lagged the S&P 500’s 14.5% rally.

1-Year Price Performance

Industry's Trades Pricier Than Sector, Cheaper Than S&P 500

Based on EV-to-EBITDA (enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization), which is commonly used for valuing waste removal services stocks because of their high debt levels, the industry is currently trading at 12.52X compared with the S&P 500’s 17.88X and the sector’s 10.31X.
