excerpt: Marriott, Wyndham and Choice Hotels face rising costs and economic uncertainty, but travel demand, loyalty programs and expansion plans offer growth opportunities.
headline: 3 Hotel Stocks to Keep on Your Radar Despite Industry Challenges
html_content:
The Zacks Hotels and Motels industry faces challenges from rising labor, utility and maintenance costs, economic uncertainty and cautious consumer spending, which could weigh on hotel occupancy, room rates and profit margins. Intense competition and substantial capital requirements for property upgrades and renovations are also putting pressure on profitability. However, the industry continues to benefit from steady travel demand, higher guest spending and the gradual recovery of business and group travel. Major events, including the FIFA World Cup held earlier this year and ongoing celebrations marking America's 250th anniversary, have created opportunities to drive hotel demand in key markets. Additionally, investments in loyalty programs, digital platforms and enhanced guest services are helping operators strengthen customer retention and improve the guest experience. Industry players, such as Marriott International, Inc. MAR, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc. WH and Choice Hotels International, Inc. CHH, are positioned to benefit from these favorable industry trends.

Industry Description

The Zacks Hotels and Motels industry comprises companies that own, lease, manage, develop and franchise hotels. Some vacation ownership and exchange firms are also part of the industry. Several participants own, construct and operate resorts. Some companies develop lodges and mobile accommodations, including modular, skid-mounted ones and central amenities that provide long-term and temporary workforce accommodations. Some industry players develop, market, sell and manage vacation ownership and associated products. A few hoteliers also offer studios, one-bedroom suites and accommodations to mid-market business and personal travelers.

 

4 Trends Shaping the Future of the Hotels & Motels Industry

Rising Operating Costs and Margin Pressure: Hotel operators continue to face elevated expenses related to labor, utilities, maintenance, insurance and property upkeep. Wage inflation and the need to retain skilled employees can increase payroll costs, while higher utility and maintenance expenses add to the cost of running properties. These pressures can limit the industry's ability to expand profit margins, particularly when operators cannot fully pass on higher costs to guests through room-rate increases.

Economic Uncertainty and Intense Competition: Persistent inflation, economic uncertainty and pressure on household budgets could make travelers more selective about their accommodation spending. Leisure guests may opt for shorter trips, lower-priced properties or alternative lodging options, while corporate clients may exercise greater discipline over travel budgets. At the same time, competition from hotels across different price categories and alternative accommodation providers can limit pricing flexibility. Operators must balance room rates with occupancy levels to remain competitive, potentially constraining revenue growth and profitability.

Recovery in Business and Group Travel: The continued recovery in corporate travel, meetings, conventions and group bookings is creating opportunities for hotel operators to improve occupancy and room-rate performance. Business and group travelers can generate demand beyond leisure travel periods, helping properties maintain more consistent room utilization. Major events, including the FIFA World Cup held earlier in 2026, have also provided opportunities to attract visitors in host cities and surrounding markets. Meanwhile, celebrations marking America's 250th anniversary have supported event-related tourism, although the impact varies by location. These demand drivers can help hotels strengthen revenues and improve operating leverage.

Loyalty Programs, Technology and Enhanced Guest Services: Hotel companies are increasingly investing in loyalty programs, digital booking platforms, personalized guest experiences and operational technology to strengthen their competitive positions. Loyalty memberships can encourage repeat stays, improve direct bookings and help reduce reliance on third-party booking channels and their associated commissions. Technology investments can also streamline reservations, improve service delivery and support more efficient revenue management. In addition, upgraded amenities and personalized services can help hotels differentiate their offerings, attract new customers and build long-term guest relationships. These initiatives can support customer retention, revenue generation and operating efficiency over time.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Dull Prospects

The Zacks Hotels and Motels industry is grouped within the broader sector.

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. The Zacks Hotels and Motels industry currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #166, which places it in the bottom 33% of the 247 Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

The industry's position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries results from a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, analysts are gradually losing confidence in this group's earnings growth potential. 

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to keep an eye on, let us look at the industry's recent stock-market performance and valuation picture.

Industry Outperforms the S&P 500

In the past year, the Zacks Hotels and Motels industry has outperformed the S&P 500. Moreover, over this period, the industry has gained 33.4% against the sector's decrease of 14.4%. Meanwhile, the Zacks S&P 500 composite has rallied 12.2%.

Hotels & Motels Industry's Valuation

Based on the trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA, which is a commonly used multiple for valuing Hotels and Motels stocks, the industry is currently trading at 16.02X compared with the S&P 500's 17.88X. The sector's trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA ratio stands at 10.55X.

Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 40.11X and as low as 13.38X, the median being 15.88X, as the chart shows.

3 Hotels & Motels Stocks to Watch

Marriott: The company continues to benefit from broad travel demand, pricing power, steady room additions and a strong pipeline led by conversions. Growth in Marriott Bonvoy, new U.S. co-branded card agreements and technology investments are supporting fee growth and customer engagement.
 
MAR currently holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Marriott’s 2026 bottom line indicates a surge of 17.2% from the year-ago period’s actual. MAR’s shares have risen 50.4% in the past year. 

You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Price & Consensus: MAR

Wyndham Hotels & Resorts: The company is benefiting from its asset-light business model, extensive global franchise network and strong presence in the economy and midscale segments. New hotel openings, demand for affordable accommodation, and investments in loyalty programs and digital booking platforms are supporting franchise growth and fee-based revenues.

WH presently carries a Zacks Rank #2. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Wyndham Hotels & Resorts’ 2026 EPS implies growth of 6.6% from the year-ago period’s actual. WH’s shares have gained 1.7% in the past year.

Price & Consensus: WH

Choice Hotels International: The company is benefiting from higher franchise-agreement activity, improving hotel retention, conversion-led development and international expansion. Growth in extended-stay brands and increasing engagement through Choice Privileges and Business Direct bode well.

CHH currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The company’s 2026 bottom line is likely to witness a year-over-year improvement of 0.6%. CHH’s shares have gained 18.8% in the past year.

Price & Consensus: CHH

excerpt: ONDS and DPRO are expanding their defense drone businesses, but differences in order momentum, revenues and profitability risks make one stock stand out.
headline: Ondas vs. Draganfly: Which Drone Stock Is the Better Pick Now?
html_content:
The global drone industry has reached a pivotal growth phase driven by increasing uptake across commercial, government and military sectors.

According to a report from Mordor Intelligence, the global drone tech market is expected to witness a CAGR of 9.1% from 2027 to 2032. The convergence of drones with artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing and edge processing is further driving adoption across verticals.

Ondas Inc. ONDS and Draganfly DPRO both operate in the defense and unmanned systems domain, but from very different positions in terms of scale and maturity.

These companies bring unique strengths to the table, which make this an intriguing comparison for investors.

So, the question arises: which stock makes a better investment pick at present? Let us dive into the fundamentals, valuations, growth outlook and risks for each company.

The Case for ONDS

Ondas’ investment appeal is supported by its rapidly expanding autonomous defense portfolio, substantial order momentum and growing exposure to mission-critical defense programs. On Oct. 7, 2026, ONDS announced that it has secured more than $165 million in aggregate orders from the second half of August through Oct. 1. This, when combined with roughly $105 million of orders disclosed on the last earnings call (Aug. 13, 2026), brings total orders to more than $270 million since June 30, improving revenue visibility into 2027.

Management noted that broad-based strength across product categories and geographies contributed to strong order activity. Importantly, the latest wins include strategically significant orders for ULTRA and IonStrike, with both platforms progressing through key customer-validation milestones. ONDS acquired ULTRA through the DZYNE buyout. ULTRA is a long-endurance autonomous aircraft delivering multi-day ISR, while IonStrike targets the growing counter-UAS market, including defense against Shahed-class drones.

The orders also include the recent $56 million Electronic Safe & Arm Devices award, supporting a European loitering munition program. This represents an important early commercial development following Ondas’ acquisition of GATE Technologies and Bron Technologies last month. In September, Ondas also acquired three defense technology businesses (Insignito, Ottopia Defense and Caribou Labs) for $56 million, payable in cash or its common stock, with potential performance-based earn-outs of up to $32 million based upon achieving key performance milestones through 2028.

ONDS is expanding its counter-drone reach through innovation. In September, Ondas launched Dronebuster REACH, extending its non-kinetic counter-UAS capabilities. The first Dronebuster REACH system is already under contract for delivery to the Office of Naval Research following customer acceptance testing. The system will support C-UAS research, evaluation and testing activities, providing an early validation point for Ondas’ new product.

excerpt: UPS and FedEx stocks have rallied following upbeat Q3 results, but which shipping giant offers investors the better combination of growth, value, and dividend income?
headline: UPS vs. FedEx: Which Stock Is the Better Buy After Strong Q3 Results?
html_content:
Shipping giants United Parcel Service UPS) and FedEx FDX) are drawing investors' attention after both companies delivered better-than-expected quarterly results this week and raised their financial outlooks.

UPS stock has surged 13% this month, with FDX rising more than 7% amid improving earnings prospects and increased optimism surrounding the holiday shipping season.

With both companies benefiting from cost-cutting initiatives and improving operational efficiency, which stock offers the better combination of growth, value, and dividend income?


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

UPS vs FedEx: Q3 Results & Raised Guidance

UPS reported Q3 adjusted earnings of $1.69 per share, beating expectations of $1.63 by nearly 4% but declining from $1.74 in the year-ago quarter, which benefited from a one-time $0.30-per-share gain from a sale-leaseback transaction.

Still, UPS’s Q3 revenue increased roughly 7% year over year to $22.85 billion and exceeded estimates of $22.25 billion.

Encouragingly, UPS raised its full-year revenue outlook to $92.6 billion from $91.2 billion and increased its adjusted EPS guidance to $7.28 per share, up from $7.22 previously. The company also lifted its free cash flow target to $6.1 billion, reflecting improving network efficiency and profitability.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Meanwhile, FedEx posted Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.74, easily surpassing expectations of $3.24 by 15% and increasing 28% from $2.93 a year ago, excluding the impact of its FedEx Freight spin-off.

Revenue from continued operations jumped 12% to $22.85 billion and surpassed estimates of $22.33 billion, supported by higher shipping volumes, improved pricing, and cost reductions.

FedEx also raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $18.00-$18.60, compared with its previous forecast of $16.90-$18.10. Furthermore, management now expects revenue growth of approximately 12%, up from its previous forecast of 11%.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Stock Performance & Valuation Comparison

FedEx has delivered stronger longer-term share-price performance, gaining 24% over the past year compared with UPS's 12% advance.

FDX has gained a respectable 30% over the last three years, trailing the S&P 500 but far outpacing UPS's 23% decline. UPS's underperformance reflects a combination of post-pandemic shipping volume declines, restructuring costs, and greater vulnerability to broader macroeconomic headwinds.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

While FedEx has shown stronger momentum, UPS offers the more attractive valuation, trading near 13X forward earnings compared with 15X for FDX, although both trade at attractive discounts to the benchmark S&P 500.

Trading around $106 a share, UPS's discounted valuation could offer greater upside if its restructuring initiatives generate sustainable earnings growth. However, at over $300 a share, FedEx's accelerating revenue and earnings growth may still justify its modest valuation premium.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

UPS & FDX Dividend Comparison

Despite its underperformance in recent years, UPS has a significant advantage for income-oriented investors, offering an annual dividend of $6.56 per share and a compelling 6.2% yield.

While UPS offers nearly four times the dividend yield of FedEx, its annual payout represents over 90% of management's projected 2026 adjusted EPS, raising questions about future dividend growth and sustainability.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

In comparison, FedEx currently pays $4.88 annually, yielding approximately 1.6%.

That said, FedEx offers a more conservative payout ratio that is under 30%, offering greater flexibility to return capital through share repurchases, including $2 billion in buybacks completed between June and September.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

 

Conclusion & Strategic Thoughts

Both UPS and FedEx appear attractive following their upbeat quarterly results and improved financial guidance.

UPS may be the better choice for value and income investors, given its cheaper forward earnings multiple and substantially higher dividend yield. Conversely, FedEx looks more appealing for growth-oriented investors, supported by faster revenue growth, stronger earnings momentum, and its ongoing transformation initiatives.

For now, both stocks land a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) following their sharp rallies, with further upside potentially hinging on upward revisions to FY27 earnings estimates after their strong Q3 results.

excerpt: Ask AI to "analyze my spending" and you get what your banking app already shows. Meredith Margrave shares the prompt to use if you want to find hidden spending problems, the follow-ups that dig deeper, and how to catch AI's mistakes before acting on them.
headline: Don't Ask AI to "Analyze My Spending," Ask It This Instead
html_content:
Earlier this week, I wrote about an uncomfortable discovery: Michael and I were spending more than we thought. Our budget was mostly intact, and we were still saving, just not as much as we had expected. A few evenings of combing through statements turned up nothing obvious, so we decided to let AI take a look.

Before we did, though, I wanted to figure out how to do it without handing a chatbot standing access to our bank accounts. (The short version: Share a one-time, sanitized snapshot of your transactions instead of connecting your accounts, and use the service's privacy settings rather than trusting a request to "forget" your data.)

But getting your data ready is only half the job. The other half is knowing what to ask. And this is where I think a lot of people miss an opportunity.

Don't Ask AI to "Analyze My Spending." Give It an Assignment.

If you upload a spreadsheet and type "Can you analyze my spending?" you'll probably get a tidy summary of your categories. Groceries: $1,800. Restaurants: $890. Shopping: $1,250. That's accurate, but it's also exactly what your banking app already tells you.

A better approach is to treat AI the way you'd treat a sharp new research assistant. Tell it what you're trying to accomplish, give it specific tasks, and make it show its work. Here's the prompt I plan to use:

I'm reviewing my household spending because our expenses appear to have increased over the past several months, but I haven't been able to identify a clear cause.

Analyze the attached transaction data and:

1. Calculate total spending by month and category.
2. Identify the five largest increases in spending, both in dollars and percentages.
3. Look for recurring charges, subscriptions, and possible duplicate payments.
4. Identify merchants where our spending has increased significantly.
5. Look for patterns involving purchase frequency, transaction size, or timing.
6. Separate unusual one-time expenses from ongoing spending changes.
7. Suggest three to five realistic opportunities to reduce spending without making major lifestyle changes.

Show the calculations supporting your findings. Do not invent missing information or assume that every expense is unnecessary. Flag uncertain categories and ask for clarification when needed.

Finally, summarize your findings in plain English, prioritizing the issues with the greatest potential financial impact.

Feel free to copy it, and adjust the opening line to fit your own situation.

Why This Prompt Works

Every piece of that prompt is there for a reason.

The opening sentence gives AI context. It knows we're not building a budget from scratch or preparing a tax return. We're hunting for a change, so it should focus on what's different, not just what's large.

Asking for increases in both dollars and percentages keeps the analysis honest. A streaming service that jumps from $10 to $18 a month is an 80% increase, but it costs you less than $100 a year. Groceries rising 15% on an $1,800 monthly bill costs you about $3,200 a year. You want to see both numbers, because the most dramatic percentage isn't always the most expensive problem.

Separating one-time expenses from ongoing changes is probably the most important instruction on the list. A $3,000 home repair in August will make that month look terrible, but it isn't a leak. It's a planned expense. A $150 increase in restaurant spending that shows up every month, on the other hand, is precisely what we're looking for.

The final paragraph sets the ground rules. Telling AI not to invent information, not to assume every expense is wasteful, and to flag what it isn't sure about makes it less likely to hand you a confident answer built on guesswork.

And notice what the prompt doesn't include: my name, our address, account numbers, or our household income. The analysis doesn't need any of it, so I'm not sharing it.

Then Dig Deeper With Follow-Up Questions

The first response is a starting point, not a final report. Once AI flags something, ask it to explain.

Say it reports that grocery spending rose sharply over six months. That alone doesn't tell you what to do about it. So follow up:

Break down the increase in grocery spending by number of trips, average amount per trip, and store. Which of those factors accounts for most of the change?

If the answer is that you're making eight more trips a month, the fix might be a weekly meal plan. If your average receipt went up at the same store, you might be looking at higher prices or a few new habits that crept into the cart. Those are very different problems with very different solutions.

The single most useful follow-up, though, is one of the simplest: "Show me the transactions behind that number." It forces AI to connect its conclusions to your actual data, and it's the fastest way to spot when something has gone wrong.

Prompts for the Most Common Spending Leaks

If you already have a suspicion about where your money is going, you can skip the broad analysis and go straight to a targeted question. A few I'd keep handy:

The subscription audit. "List every recurring charge with the merchant, amount, billing frequency, and the first date it appears. Flag any charge whose price has changed and any services that seem to overlap."

The annual renewals. "Identify charges that appear once a year, such as memberships, software, or warranties, and estimate when each is likely to renew." These are easy to forget because they show up so rarely.

The payday effect. "Compare our spending in the seven days after each paycheck with the rest of the month. Is there a pattern?"

Death by small purchases. "Total all transactions under $25 by month and by merchant. How much do they add up to, and is that number growing?"

Price creep. "For merchants we pay regularly, such as utilities, insurance, and phone service, show how the amount has changed over time."

Check AI's Math Before You Act on It

Here's the part that matters most: AI can make mistakes, and it tends to make them confidently.

It can miscategorize transactions, misread refunds as purchases, or count a pending charge and its posted version as two separate payments. One of the most common errors comes from uploading both your checking account and your credit card. The payment from checking to your card can be counted as spending, on top of the purchases it paid for, which can double a chunk of your expenses overnight.

So before you cancel anything, do a quick reality check. Ask AI to total each month's spending, then compare those totals with your statements. Pick a handful of the transactions it cites and make sure they exist and say what it claims. If the numbers don't match, ask it to explain the difference.

And keep your own judgment in the loop. If AI suggests cutting childcare because it's one of our largest monthly bills, I'm going to politely suggest that it reconsider. Some big expenses are big because they matter.

Let AI Find the Patterns. You Make the Calls.

Michael and I still don't know where our leak is. It could be a stack of forgotten subscriptions, a grocery bill that has quietly crept higher, or a mistake I made when I built the budget in the first place. Whatever it is, I'd rather find it with a clear assignment than by scrolling through hundreds of transactions one more time.

Because the goal isn't to let AI decide what you should and shouldn't spend money on.

text_content: Earlier this week, I wrote about an uncomfortable discovery: Michael and I were spending more than we thought. Our budget was mostly intact, and we were still saving, just not as much as we had expected. A few evenings of combing through statements turned up nothing obvious, so we decided to let AI take a look. Before we did, though, I wanted to figure out how to do it without handing a chatbot standing access to our bank accounts. (The short version: Share a one-time, sanitized snapshot of your transactions instead of connecting your accounts, and use the service's privacy settings rather than trusting a request to "forget" your data.) But getting your data ready is only half the job. The other half is knowing what to ask. And this is where I think a lot of people miss an opportunity. Don't Ask AI to "Analyze My Spending." Give It an Assignment. If you upload a spreadsheet and type "Can you analyze my spending?" you'll probably get a tidy summary of your categories. Groceries: $1,800. Restaurants: $890. Shopping: $1,250. That's accurate, but it's also exactly what your banking app already tells you. A better approach is to treat AI the way you'd treat a sharp new research assistant. Tell it what you're trying to accomplish, give it specific tasks, and make it show its work. Here's the prompt I plan to use: I'm reviewing my household spending because our expenses appear to have increased over the past several months, but I haven't been able to identify a clear cause. Analyze the attached transaction data and: 1. Calculate total spending by month and category. 2. Identify the five largest increases in spending, both in dollars and percentages. 3. Look for recurring charges, subscriptions, and possible duplicate payments. 4. Identify merchants where our spending has increased significantly. 5. Look for patterns involving purchase frequency, transaction size, or timing. 6. Separate unusual one-time expenses from ongoing spending changes. 7. Suggest three to five realistic opportunities to reduce spending without making major lifestyle changes. Show the calculations supporting your findings. Do not invent missing information or assume that every expense is unnecessary. Flag uncertain categories and ask for clarification when needed. Finally, summarize your findings in plain English, prioritizing the issues with the greatest potential financial impact. Feel free to copy it, and adjust the opening line to fit your own situation. Why This Prompt Works Every piece of that prompt is there for a reason. The opening sentence gives AI context. It knows we're not building a budget from scratch or preparing a tax return. We're hunting for a change, so it should focus on what's different, not just what's large. Asking for increases in both dollars and percentages keeps the analysis honest. A streaming service that jumps from $10 to $18 a month is an 80% increase, but it costs you less than $100 a year. Groceries rising 15% on an $1,800 monthly bill costs you about $3,200 a year. You want to see both numbers, because the most dramatic percentage isn't always the most expensive problem. Separating one-time expenses from ongoing changes is probably the most important instruction on the list. A $3,000 home repair in August will make that month look terrible, but it isn't a leak. It's a planned expense. A $150 increase in restaurant spending that shows up every month, on the other hand, is precisely what we're looking for. The final paragraph sets the ground rules. Telling AI not to invent information, not to assume every expense is wasteful, and to flag what it isn't sure about makes it less likely to hand you a confident answer built on guesswork. And notice what the prompt doesn't include: my name, our address, account numbers, or our household income. The analysis doesn't need any of it, so I'm not sharing it. Then Dig Deeper With Follow-Up Questions The first response is a starting point, not a final report. Once AI flags something, ask it to explain. Say it reports that grocery spending rose sharply over six months. That alone doesn't tell you what to do about it. So follow up: Break down the increase in grocery spending by number of trips, average amount per trip, and store. Which of those factors accounts for most of the change? If the answer is that you're making eight more trips a month, the fix might be a weekly meal plan. If your average receipt went up at the same store, you might be looking at higher prices or a few new habits that crept into the cart. Those are very different problems with very different solutions. The single most useful follow-up, though, is one of the simplest: "Show me the transactions behind that number." It forces AI to connect its conclusions to your actual data, and it's the fastest way to spot when something has gone wrong. Prompts for the Most Common Spending Leaks If you already have a suspicion about where your money is going, you can skip the broad analysis and go straight to a targeted question. A few I'd keep handy: The subscription audit. "List every recurring charge with the merchant, amount, billing frequency, and the first date it appears. Flag any charge whose price has changed and any services that seem to overlap." The annual renewals. "Identify charges that appear once a year, such as memberships, software, or warranties, and estimate when each is likely to renew." These are easy to forget because they show up so rarely. The payday effect. "Compare our spending in the seven days after each paycheck with the rest of the month. Is there a pattern?" Death by small purchases. "Total all transactions under $25 by month and by merchant. How much do they add up to, and is that number growing?" Price creep. "For merchants we pay regularly, such as utilities, insurance, and phone service, show how the amount has changed over time." Check AI's Math Before You Act on It Here's the part that matters most: AI can make mistakes, and it tends to make them confidently. It can miscategorize transactions, misread refunds as purchases, or count a pending charge and its posted version as two separate payments. One of the most common errors comes from uploading both your checking account and your credit card. The payment from checking to your card can be counted as spending, on top of the purchases it paid for, which can double a chunk of your expenses overnight. So before you cancel anything, do a quick reality check. Ask AI to total each month's spending, then compare those totals with your statements. Pick a handful of the transactions it cites and make sure they exist and say what it claims. If the numbers don't match, ask it to explain the difference. And keep your own judgment in the loop. If AI suggests cutting childcare because it's one of our largest monthly bills, I'm going to politely suggest that it reconsider. Some big expenses are big because they matter. Let AI Find the Patterns. You Make the Calls. Michael and I still don't know where our leak is. It could be a stack of forgotten subscriptions, a grocery bill that has quietly crept higher, or a mistake I made when I built the budget in the first place. Whatever it is, I'd rather find it with a clear assignment than by scrolling through hundreds of transactions one more time. Because the goal isn't to let AI decide what you should and shouldn't spend money on. It's to let AI find the patterns, so you can make better decisions. headline: Screening for Undervalued Strong Buy Stocks
html_content:
• (0:30) - Where Should You Be Looking For Strong Value Stocks?
  • (3:30) - Tracey’s Top Stock Picks For Your Watchlist Right Now
  • (19:00) - Episode Roundup: JBL, HRI & ZIM
  • Podcast@Zacks.com

 

Welcome to Episode #459 of the Value Investor Podcast.

Every week, Tracey Ryniec, the editor of Zacks Value Investor portfolio, shares some of her top value investing tips and stock picks.

Are there any cheap stocks?

Many technology stocks, especially in the AI Revolution trade, have sold off in the last month. Additionally, energy companies remain cheap as their earnings rise on higher oil and refined product prices.

Screening for Top Ranked Cheap Stocks

This week, Tracey ran a premium Zacks screen called “Undervalued Zacks #1 Rank Stocks” to find top ranked cheap stocks.

It’s a basic screen which looks only for Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks with price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios under 20 and price-to-sales (P/S) ratios under 1.0.

A P/S ratio under 1.0 means you are getting the sales on sale. A P/S of 0.6 means an investor is paying $0.60 for every $1.00 of sales. That’s a deal.

This screen returned 34 stocks.

3 Undervalued Strong Buy Stocks

1. Jabil Inc. (JBL)

Jabil is a partner with the world’s top brands offering engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions worldwide.

On Sep 30, 2026, Jabil reported fiscal fourth quarter 2026 earnings and saw significant growth in AI infrastructure business. Analysts are bullish. The Zacks Consensus expects earnings to rise 34.5% in fiscal 2027.

Jabil is cheap. It trades with a P/S ratio of just 0.8. It’s a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Should Jabil be on your value investor short list?

2. Herc Holdings Inc. (HRI)

Herc Holdings is a full-service equipment rental firm that operates 615 branches in the United States and Canada. Herc Holdings reported third quarter 2026 results on Oct 27, 2026, and had record equipment rental and revenue. It saw accelerating customer demand.

Shares of Herc Holdings are up 16% year-to-date but it’s still cheap. Herc Holdings traded with a P/S ratio of just 0.9 before it reported earnings and now it’s at 1.1. That’s still cheap.

Herc Holdings is a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Should a rental equipment company like Herc Holdings be on your value short list?

3. ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd. (ZIM)

ZIM Integrated Shipping is a leading global container shipping company. In Feb 2025, it got a $4.2 billion buyout offer at $35 a share. The shares are currently trading around $29 so there is an arbitrage trade.

On Oct 6, 2026, ZIM Integrated Shipping raised full year guidance based on strong market demand and favorable momentum in freight rates. As a result, the 2026 Zacks Consensus Estimate jumped to $8.86 from $3.15 in the last 30 days. That’s earnings growth of 188%.

ZIM Integrated Shipping is dirt cheap. It has a forward P/E of just 3.3. A P/E under 10 usually means a company has deep value.

ZIM Integrated Shipping is a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Other shipping companies also have top Zacks Ranks and are cheap if you don’t want to deal with the ZIM buyout.

Should a shipping company like ZIM Integrated Shipping be on your value short list?

What Else Should You Know About Undervalued Strong Buy Stocks Right Now?

Tune into this week’s podcast to find out.

[In full disclosure, Tracey owns shares of JBL in Zacks Value Investor portfolio.]

Zacks' Research Chief Names "Stock Most Likely to Double"

Our team of experts has just released the 5 stocks with the greatest probability of gaining +100% or more in the coming months. Of those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian highlights the one stock set to climb highest.

Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners, but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like D-Wave Quantum, which shot up +680.1%.

headline: Should State Street SPDR S&P 600 Small Cap Value ETF (SLYV) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
If you're interested in broad exposure to the Small Cap Value segment of the US equity market, look no further than the State Street SPDR S&P 600 Small Cap Value ETF (SLYV), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on September 25, 2000.

The fund is sponsored by State Street Investment Management. It has amassed assets over $4.88 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs attempting to match the Small Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Why Small Cap Value

There's a lot of potential to investing in small cap companies, but with market capitalization below $2 billion, that high potential comes with even higher risk.

Value stocks are known for their lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, but investors should also note their lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. Considering long-term performance, value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in almost all markets; however, they are more likely to underperform growth stocks in strong bull markets.

Costs

When considering an ETF's total return, expense ratios are an important factor, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts in the long term if all other factors remain equal.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.15%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.92%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure that minimizes single stock risk, investors should also look at the actual holdings inside the fund. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Financials sector -- about 20.7% of the portfolio. Consumer Discretionary and Industrials round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Match Group Inc (MTCH) accounts for about 1.04% of total assets, followed by Paycom Software Inc (PAYC) and Sm Energy Co (SM).

The top 10 holdings account for about 8.49% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

SLYV seeks to match the performance of the S&P SmallCap 600 Value Index before fees and expenses. The S&P SmallCap 600 Value Index measures the performance of the small-capitalization value sector in the U.S. equity market. The selection universe for the S&P SmallCap 600 Index includes all U.S. common equities listed on the NYSE, NASDAQ Global Select Market, NASDAQ Select Market and NASDAQ Capital Market with market capitalizations between $250 million and $1.2 billion.

The ETF has gained about 19.02% so far this year and was up about 22.07% in the last one year (as of 10/30/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $83.97 and $112.22.

The ETF has a beta of 1.02 and standard deviation of 20.33% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 466 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

State Street SPDR S&P 600 Small Cap Value ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, SLYV is an outstanding option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Small Cap Value segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The iShares Russell 2000 Value ETF (IWN) and the Vanguard Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF (VBR) track a similar index. While iShares Russell 2000 Value ETF has $14.17 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF has $37.14 billion. IWN has an expense ratio of 0.24% and VBR charges 0.05%.

Bottom-Line

While an excellent vehicle for long term investors, passively managed ETFs are a popular choice among institutional and retail investors due to their low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency.

Why Large Cap Value

Companies that find themselves in the large cap category typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Considered a more stable option, large cap companies boast more predictable cash flows and are less volatile than their mid and small cap counterparts.

While value stocks have lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, they also have lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. Looking at their long-term performance, value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in almost all markets. They are however likely to underperform growth stocks in strong bull markets.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.06%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 2.96%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Consumer Staples sector -- about 19.6% of the portfolio. Healthcare and Energy round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Texas Instrument Inc (TXN) accounts for about 4.67% of total assets, followed by Qualcomm (QCOM) and Procter & Gamble (PG).

Performance and Risk

SCHD seeks to match the performance of the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index before fees and expenses. The Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index is designed to measure the performance of high dividend yielding stocks issued by U.S. companies that have a record of consistently paying dividends, selected for fundamental strength relative to their peers, based on financial ratios.

The ETF has added about 32.65% so far this year and is up about 37.11% in the last one year (as of 10/30/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $26.44 and $35.61.

Objective

HDMBX is one of many different Small Cap Growth funds to choose from. Small Cap Growth mutual funds build portfolios around stocks with market caps under $2 billion and large growth opportunities. History of Fund/Manager

Hartford is responsible for HDMBX, and the company is based out of Woodbury, MN. The fund is currently managed by Ranjit Ramachandran who has been in charge of the fund since February of 2020.

Performance

Investors naturally seek funds with strong performance. This fund has delivered a 5-year annualized total return of 1.81%, and it sits in the middle third among its category peers. But if you are looking for a shorter time frame, it is also worth looking at its 3-year annualized total return of 14.61%, which places it in the middle third during this time-frame.

excerpt: H2O America, Clean Harbors and Concrete Pumping Holdings stand out as waste management stocks benefiting from infrastructure investments, rising demand and industry growth.
headline: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights H2O America, Clean Harbors and Concrete Pumping
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 30, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: H2O America HTO, Clean Harbors CLH and Concrete Pumping Holdings BBCP.

Here are highlights from Thursday’s Analyst Blog:

3 Stocks to Buy from the Booming Waste Removal Services Market

The Waste Management industry is experiencing positive trends in government regulations, adoption of advanced technologies and an increasing awareness of environmental issues. Despite rising operating costs, the industry does not shy away from swift industrialization and urbanization. Per Mordor Intelligence, the global waste management sector is expected to see a 6.2% CAGR through 2032. The potential expansion of the global waste management sector can be attributed to better waste collection methods and rising volumes of waste in emerging markets.

Three promising stocks from the Waste Removal Services market are H2O America, Clean Harbors and Concrete Pumping Holdings.

About the Industry

Companies in the Zacks Waste Removal Services industry play a vital role in the collection, treatment and responsible management of diverse waste types, aiming to minimize their impacts on the environment and public health. This market is categorized into distinct segments based on the kind of waste, including industrial, commercial, domestic and agricultural waste. The Industrial waste segment has gained significance due to the ongoing industrial expansion, creating a substantial demand for efficient waste management solutions. The market encompasses Collection and Disposal services. The Disposal services segment, primarily fueled by the growing need for waste recycling to mitigate environmental impacts, stands as the primary revenue-generating category.

What's Shaping the Future of the Business Services Industry?

Rising Importance of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Goals: Waste management is a cornerstone of ESG principles, as it helps companies improve their ESG ratings by promoting environmental sustainability, fostering social well-being and upholding good governance. Per Grand View Research, the average ESG disclosure score for the waste management industry lies at 50-60%. Embracing responsible waste management meets legal requirements and aligns with consumer and investor desires for sustainable and ethical business practices. At present, waste management is not only a duty but also a chance for businesses to showcase their dedication to ESG values, which underpin lasting success and resilience.

Technology Drives Waste Management Industry Growth: Technology has become a vital component in waste management, addressing the challenges of waste generation and environmental impacts. This transformative correlation promises a more sustainable future. For instance, AI is emerging as a crucial tool to sort waste and keep recyclable materials from going into landfills. Advancing technology results in more effective, eco-friendly waste management, lowering the ecological footprint and promoting sustainability. Waste challenges can be mitigated using technology that leads us toward responsible waste management and a cleaner planet.

Innovations in Waste-to-Energy (WTE)Technology Aid: WTE comprises thermal (pyrolysis, incineration and gasification) and biological solutions (composting and anaerobic digestion), which play crucial roles in sustainable waste management. This technology transforms waste into energy via methods like incineration or gasification. 

Per a report by Fortune Business Insights, the Waste-to-Energy Market size is estimated to be $38.9 billion in 2026, expected to see a 3.6% CAGR through 2034. The rise is expected to be fuelled by the surge in the amount of waste generation, growing waste management concerns to meet sustainable living standards and increased focus on non-fossil fuels. The industry holds an important position in the era of clean energy, offering a renewable energy source and addressing the mounting challenges around waste management.

Increasing Operating Costs Are Concerning: Waste management is a time-consuming and complex process. It requires higher capital and operating costs to manage waste collection vehicles, bins and processing equipment, along with a huge number of workers. Such high operational expenses are anticipated to keep the bottom line of the companies in this industrial cohort under pressure.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Near-Term Prospects

The Zacks Waste Removal Services industry, which is housed within the Zacks Business Services sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #75. This rank places it in the top 30% of 247 Zacks industries.

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates a continued outperformance in the near term. Our research shows that the top 50% of Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let us take a look at the industry's recent stock market performance and current valuation.

Industry & S&P 500 Rises While Sector Plunges

The Zacks Waste Removal Services industry has moved up marginally over the past year. It outpaced the broader sector's 12% dip but lagged the S&P 500's 14.5% rally.

Industry's Trades Pricier Than Sector, Cheaper Than S&P 500

Based on EV-to-EBITDA (enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization), which is commonly used for valuing waste removal services stocks because of their high debt levels, the industry is currently trading at 12.52X compared with the S&P 500's 17.88X and the sector's 10.31X.

Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 15.31X and as low as 11.43X, the median being 13.29X.

3 Waste Removal Services Stocks to Bet On

H2O America: This is a water utility, processing, distribution, wholesale and retail company. HTO's Quadvest buyout solidifies its Texas operations and expands its customer base. During the first nine months of 2026, this acquired company's active connections gained 14% year over year, while its development pipeline supports continued customer growth. Management anticipates this buyout to deliver earnings-accretive beginning in 2028.

HTO's capital investment plan from 2026 through 2030 amounts to $2.7 billion and is anticipated to strengthen water infrastructure and operational prowess. This plan, accompanied by the Quadvest acquisition, is expected to fuel a 13% CAGR in rate base.

The ongoing rate cases in Connecticut and Maine seek recovery of infrastructure investments. Management anticipates nearly 80% of planned CapEx through 2030 to qualify for timely regulatory recovery, further raising top-line visibility. The organic earnings growth target set by management is at 6-8%, supported by customer wins, infrastructure modernization and regulatory rate relief.

HTO sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company's 2026 earnings has been pinned at $2.8 and has been unchanged in the past 60 days. Its shares have risen 37% in a year.

Clean Harbors: This company provides hazardous and non-hazardous waste management services. CLH benefits from rising hazardous waste volumes, prudent pricing and an upsurge in demand for comprehensive waste management solutions. A recently commenced 10-year $600 million contract and manufacturing reshoring are expected to provide a clear view of revenue.

Rising demand for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) remediation, water treatment and disposal services acts as a growth catalyst. Management anticipates PFAS-related revenues to increase 30% in 2026, aided by a solid project pipeline.

CLH is increasing its dedicated data center investment target to $70 million. Additional growth in revenues from an escalation in demand for chemical cleaning, cooling system maintenance and recycling services is expected.

The recent EnviroServe and ES&H buyout expands service capabilities and offers synergies from integration. Meanwhile, higher production of premium Group III base oil, favorable re-refining spreads and operational prowess boost profitability and cash flow generation.

CLH carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for its 2026 bottom line has been kept at $9.94, moving up 2.3% in the past 60 days. Its shares have risen 43.7% in a year.

Concrete Pumping Holdings: This is a concrete pumping and concrete waste management services provider. BBCP benefits from rising demand for large-scale commercial and infrastructure projects, mainly data centers. An upsurge in education activity, accompanied by utilities and energy-related construction, supports fleet utilization and top-line growth.

Robust organic growth from Eco-Pan's concrete waste management business, driven by higher volumes, effective pricing and customer wins. BBCP's profitability is strengthened by its operating model, which diversifies its revenues as well.

The company's U.K. operations are strengthened by Templant temporary power acquisition, further broadening its offerings. Additional support is expected from the Republic of Ireland expansion, supporting long-term growth opportunities.

Improving profitability and prudent capital allocation aid growth investments. A liquidity position of $357 million and a dip in net leverage to 3.6X support the company for organic expansion, fleet investments and strategic buyouts.

BBCP carries a Zacks Rank #2 at present. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for its 2026 bottom line has been pegged at 19 cents, rising 11.8% in the past 60 days. Its shares have rallied 58% in a year.

Why Haven't You Looked at Zacks' Top Stocks?

Since 2000, our top stock-picking strategies have blown away the S&P's +7.7% average gain per year. Amazingly, they soared with average gains of +48.4%, +50.2% and +56.7% per year.

Today you can access their live picks without cost or obligation.

It should not be assumed that any investments in securities, companies, sectors or markets identified and described were or will be profitable. All information is current as of the date of herein and is subject to change without notice. Any views or opinions expressed may not reflect those of the firm as a whole. These returns are from hypothetical portfolios consisting of stocks with Zacks Rank = 1 that were rebalanced monthly with zero transaction costs. These are not the returns of actual portfolios of stocks. The S&P 500 is an unmanaged index. excerpt: JAVTX, JSVDX, JIGFX and JCONX offer exposure to growth, value and international stocks, combining solid returns, low expenses and diverse investment strategies.
headline: 4 Janus Henderson Funds for Navigating Shifting Market Trends
html_content:
Janus Capital was founded in Denver, CO, in 1969 and launched its first mutual fund in 1970. Henderson traces its origins to London in 1934. The two organizations merged in 2017 to form Janus Henderson Group, creating a global asset manager with capabilities across multiple asset classes and investment styles.

Janus Henderson has expanded considerably in recent years. Its assets under management (AUM) reached $493.2 billion as of Dec. 31, 2025, up 30% year over year, supported by favorable market performance, new client assets and currency movements. Net inflows totaled $56.5 billion in 2025 compared with $2.4 billion in 2024. By June 30, 2026, the firm's AUM had reached $500 billion, reflecting its growing global investment platform.

The company also reported stronger financial results in 2025. Full-year revenue increased to $3.10 billion from $2.47 billion in 2024, while net income attributable to Janus Henderson rose to $815.9 million from $408.9 million. Earnings per share (EPS) climbed to $5.23 from $2.56.

The company officially completed its take-private transaction on June 30, 2026, when it was acquired by Trian, General Catalyst and QIA. As a result of this acquisition, Janus Henderson was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and no longer files public quarterly earnings reports as a publicly traded. The day-to-day management, investment objectives, and underlying strategies of Janus Henderson’s mutual funds, however, remain unchanged. The pre-acquisition leadership team, including CEO Ali Dibadj, remains at the helm to maintain operational stability.

In the current market environment, Janus Henderson faces both opportunities and challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI)-related investment demand has supported selected growth-oriented holdings, while elevated valuations, interest-rate uncertainty and geopolitical risks have encouraged greater selectivity. Its diversified investment capabilities and research-driven approach may help capture opportunities across market cycles, although results vary by strategy.

Astute investors might choose to consider such funds at present. Mutual funds, in general, reduce transaction costs and diversify portfolios without an array of commission charges that are mostly associated with stock purchases (read more: Mutual Funds: Advantages, Disadvantages, and How They Make Investors Money).

We have thus selected four mutual funds that boast a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), have positive three-year and five-year annualized returns and minimum initial investments within $5000, as well as carry a low expense ratio.

Janus Henderson Venture JAVTX primarily invests in small-cap growth companies, while also considering larger growth-oriented businesses and foreign securities, including emerging-market investments.

Jonathan D. Coleman has been the lead manager of JAVTX since 2013. The three top holdings for JAVTX are Glaukos (2.6%), Ligand Pharma (2.4%) and Perimeter Solutions (2.2%).

JAVTX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 14% and 3.1%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.90%. JAVTX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1. To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here.

Janus Henderson Small-Mid Cap Value JSVDX primarily invests in small- and mid-cap value stocks, while increasing cash holdings when market conditions or investment opportunities are unfavorable.

Justin Tugman has been the lead manager of JSVDX since 2019. The three top holdings for JSVDX are Littlefuse (3.7%), ICU Medical (3.2%) and Alliant Energy (3.2%).

JSVDX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 13% and 7.3%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.78%. JSVDX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

Janus Henderson Overseas JIGFX primarily invests in a concentrated portfolio of international securities across multiple countries, with limited exposure to U.S. companies.

Julian McManus has been the lead manager of JIGFX since 2018. The three top holdings for JIGFX are Taiwan Semiconductor (7.2%), ASML Holding (5.9%) and SK hynix (5.2%).

JIGFX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 19.4% and 10.3%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.68%. JIGFX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

Janus Henderson Contrarian JCONX primarily invests in undervalued growth stocks across companies of all sizes, seeking long-term capital appreciation. It is classified as non-diversified.

Nick Schommer has been the lead manager of JCONX since 2017. The three top holdings for JCONX are Yandex (5.8%), Marvell Technology (5.5%) and Taiwan Semiconductor (5.4%).

JCONX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 18.4% and 7.8%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.63%. JCONX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

Bottom Line

Janus mutual funds have a long history of active investment management, with strategies spanning growth equities, small-cap stocks, international markets and fixed income. Their performance in the current market environment reflects changing interest-rate expectations, geopolitical uncertainty, AI-driven opportunities and investors' evolving risk appetite.

excerpt: Crocs (CROX) is at a 52-week high, but can investors hope for more gains in the future? We take a look at the company's fundamentals for clues.
headline: Crocs, Inc. (CROX) Hits Fresh High: Is There Still Room to Run?
html_content:
Shares of Crocs (CROX) have been strong performers lately, with the stock up 26% over the past month. The stock hit a new 52-week high of $151.82 in the previous session. Crocs has gained 75.7% since the start of the year compared to the -11.8% gain for the Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector and the 0.3% return for the Zacks Textile - Apparel industry.

What's Driving the Outperformance?

The stock has an impressive record of positive earnings surprises, as it hasn't missed our earnings consensus estimate in any of the last four quarters. In its last earnings report on October 29, 2026, Crocs reported EPS of $3.69 versus consensus estimate of $3.31 while it beat the consensus revenue estimate by 3.74%.

For the current fiscal year, Crocs is expected to post earnings of $14.13 per share on $4.11 in revenues. This represents a 12.95% change in EPS on a 1.68% change in revenues. For the next fiscal year, the company is expected to earn $15.26 per share on $4.22 in revenues. This represents a year-over-year change of 7.97% and 2.82%, respectively.

Valuation Metrics

Though Crocs has recently hit a 52-week high, what is next for Crocs? A key aspect of this question is taking a look at valuation metrics in order to determine if the company has run ahead of itself.

On this front, we can look at the Zacks Style Scores, as they provide investors with an additional way to sort through stocks (beyond looking at the Zacks Rank of a security). These styles are represented by grades running from A to F in the categories of Value, Growth, and Momentum, while there is a combined VGM Score as well. Investors should consider the style scores a valuable tool that can help you to pick the most appropriate Zacks Rank stocks based on their individual investment style.

Crocs has a Value Score of B. The stock's Growth and Momentum Scores are C and A, respectively, giving the company a VGM Score of B.

In terms of its value breakdown, the stock currently trades at 10.6X current fiscal year EPS estimates, which is not in-line with the peer industry average of 16.8X. On a trailing cash flow basis, the stock currently trades at 10.2X versus its peer group's average of 10.9X. Additionally, the stock has a PEG ratio of 1.24. This isn't enough to put the company in the top echelon of all stocks we cover from a value perspective.

Zacks Rank

We also need to consider the stock's Zacks Rank, as this supersedes any trend on the style score front. Fortunately, Crocs currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) thanks to favorable earnings estimate revisions from covering analysts.

Since we recommend that investors select stocks carrying Zacks Rank of 1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) and Style Scores of A or B, it looks as if Crocs meets the list of requirements. Thus, it seems as though Crocs shares could have potential in the weeks and months to come.

How Does CROX Stack Up to the Competition?

Shares of CROX have been soaring, and the company still appears to be a decent choice, but what about the rest of the industry? One industry peer that looks good is G-III Apparel Group, LTD. (GIII). GIII has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) and a Value Score of A, a Growth Score of B, and a Momentum Score of F.

Earnings were strong last quarter. G-III Apparel Group, LTD. beat our consensus estimate by 4.00%, and for the current fiscal year, GIII is expected to post earnings of $2.25 per share on revenue of $2.71 billion.

Shares of G-III Apparel Group, LTD. have gained 10.1% over the past month, and currently trade at a forward P/E of 13.49X and a P/CF of 8.82X.

The Textile - Apparel industry may rank in the bottom 78% of all the industries we have in our universe, but there still looks like there are some nice tailwinds for CROX and GIII, even beyond their own solid fundamental situation.

excerpt: Genomics and synthetic biology are transforming healthcare through precision medicine and gene editing, putting ILMN, QURE and TXG in focus as the markets expand.
headline: 3 Promising Genomics Stocks to Add to Your Portfolio Now
html_content:
An updated edition of the Sept. 8, 2026, article.

Genomics is the study of genomes, which encompass an organism’s entire set of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). Recent scientific advances in this area have heightened interest from pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies seeking insight into disease biology and more effective therapeutic strategies.

Genetics and genomics differ in their scope. Genetics primarily examines individual genes, whereas genomics focuses on analyzing and characterizing an organism’s complete set of genes. Genomics provides insights into how genes function within a biological system, interact with one another and respond to environmental influences.

Insights from genomic research are increasingly being used to evaluate how patients respond to specific drugs. These findings are also driving the development of precise, more targeted treatments, contributing to the advancement of personalized medicine. As demand for innovative therapies continues to grow, genomics is poised to play an increasingly central role in the future of healthcare, despite the complexity inherent in genome-scale research.

The expanding genomics landscape has also supported the growth of synthetic biology, which applies engineering principles to biology. This emerging field involves redesigning organisms for diverse applications, including drug discovery, disease detection, enzyme engineering, gene editing and foundational research.

The rapid progress in the novel space of genomics has been fueled by steep declines in the cost, time, and effort needed to sequence an individual’s genome. Diagnostic companies are using genomic sequencing data to identify genetic variations and connect them to known diseases. In contrast, other companies apply sequencing technologies to develop solutions across healthcare and other industries.

Another major advancement in the field is the emergence of genome-editing technologies, most notably CRISPR/Cas9. Companies specializing in gene editing, such as CRISPR Therapeutics AG (CRSP) and Beam Therapeutics, Inc. BEAM, are exploring these tools to potentially treat or even cure diseases caused by genetic mutations. As the name implies, these technologies enable precise modifications to an organism’s DNA, allowing scientists to correct harmful defects at their source.

According to Fortune Business Insights, the global genomics market was valued at $34.23 billion in 2025 and is expected to expand from $38.24 billion in 2026 to $99.26 billion by 2034, reflecting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.66% over the period.

Per a Grandview Research article, the global synthetic biology market size was valued at $18.9 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $69.2 billion by 2033, at a CAGR of 17.7% from 2026 to 2033.

If you're looking to capitalize on this trend, our Genomics and Synthetic Biology screen makes it easy to identify high-potential stocks at any given time. At present, stocks such as Illumina ILMN, uniQure QURE and 10x Genomics TXG hold potential.

Explore 40 cutting-edge investment themes with Zacks Thematic Investing Screens and uncover your next big opportunity.

3 Genomics Stocks to Consider

Illumina is advancing human health by harnessing the potential of genomics. Illumina benefits from its leading position in the global DNA sequencing and array-based technologies markets. Its broad product portfolio supports applications across disease research, drug development, molecular diagnostics, oncology, reproductive health and agriculture.

The company serves a diverse customer base, including genomic research centers, academic institutions, government laboratories, hospitals, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, diagnostic laboratories and consumer genomics businesses.

On Jan. 30, 2026, Illumina acquired SomaLogic, a proteomics company, to strengthen its presence in the protein analysis market and advance its multiomics strategy. The acquisition expands Illumina's technology portfolio beyond genomics and could create additional growth opportunities through integrated genomics and proteomics solutions.

ILMN currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

uniQure N.V. is a clinical-stage gene therapy company focused on developing one-time AAV-based treatments for rare and severe diseases. The company is advancing a focused pipeline of innovative gene therapies, with lead clinical programs targeting Huntington's disease, refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, and Fabry disease.

uniQure is developing ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130), an investigational gene therapy for Huntington's disease, using its proprietary miQURE gene-silencing platform. Ifezuntirgene inilparvovec is the first investigational therapy for Huntington’s disease to have received Breakthrough Therapy and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations from the FDA. Ifezuntirgene inilparvovec also holds Fast Track designation from the FDA. The company has made important regulatory progress, including submitting a biologics license application to the FDA and a Marketing Authorisation Application in the United Kingdom, creating significant value if approved.

QURE currently carries a Zacks Rank #2. Its shares have gained 8.2% in a month.

10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company developing innovative tools to study complex biological systems. Its commercial portfolio comprises Single Cell and Spatial solutions. The company’s products include instruments such as Chromium, Visium CytAssist and Xenium Analyzer, along with proprietary microfluidic chips, slides, reagents and other consumables. The company also provides software to support workflows ranging from sample preparation to data analysis and visualization. Its revenues are primarily generated from instrument and consumables sales, supplemented by post-warranty service contracts.

TXG currently carries a Zacks Rank #2. Shares of the company have surged 72.6% over the past three months. 

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

Insights from genomic research are increasingly being used to evaluate how patients respond to specific drugs. These findings are also driving the development of precise, more targeted treatments, contributing to the advancement of personalized medicine. As demand for innovative therapies continues to grow, genomics is poised to play an increasingly central role in the future of healthcare, despite the complexity inherent in genome-scale research. The expanding genomics landscape has also supported the growth of synthetic biology, which applies engineering principles to biology. This emerging field involves redesigning organisms for diverse applications, including drug discovery, disease detection, enzyme engineering, gene editing and foundational research. The rapid progress in the novel space of genomics has been fueled by steep declines in the cost, time, and effort needed to sequence an individual’s genome. Diagnostic companies are using genomic sequencing data to identify genetic variations and connect them to known diseases. In contrast, other companies apply sequencing technologies to develop solutions across healthcare and other industries. Another major advancement in the field is the emergence of genome-editing technologies, most notably CRISPR/Cas9. Companies specializing in gene editing, such as CRISPR Therapeutics AG (CRSP) and Beam Therapeutics, Inc. BEAM, are exploring these tools to potentially treat or even cure diseases caused by genetic mutations. As the name implies, these technologies enable precise modifications to an organism’s DNA, allowing scientists to correct harmful defects at their source. According to Fortune Business Insights, the global genomics market was valued at $34.23 billion in 2025 and is expected to expand from $38.24 billion in 2026 to $99.26 billion by 2034, reflecting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.66% over the period. Per a Grandview Research article, the global synthetic biology market size was valued at $18.9 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $69.2 billion by 2033, at a CAGR of 17.7% from 2026 to 2033. At present, stocks such as Illumina ILMN, uniQure QURE and 10x Genomics TXG hold potential. Illumina benefits from its leading position in the global DNA sequencing and array-based technologies markets. Its broad product portfolio supports applications across disease research, drug development, molecular diagnostics, oncology, reproductive health and agriculture. The company serves a diverse customer base, including genomic research centers, academic institutions, government laboratories, hospitals, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, diagnostic laboratories and consumer genomics businesses. On Jan. 30, 2026, Illumina acquired SomaLogic, a proteomics company, to strengthen its presence in the protein analysis market and advance its multiomics strategy. The acquisition expands Illumina's technology portfolio beyond genomics and could create additional growth opportunities through integrated genomics and proteomics solutions. ILMN currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. uniQure N.V. is a clinical-stage gene therapy company focused on developing one-time AAV-based treatments for rare and severe diseases. The company is advancing a focused pipeline of innovative gene therapies, with lead clinical programs targeting Huntington's disease, refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, and Fabry disease. uniQure is developing ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130), an investigational gene therapy for Huntington's disease, using its proprietary miQURE gene-silencing platform. Ifezuntirgene inilparvovec is the first investigational therapy for Huntington’s disease to have received Breakthrough Therapy and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations from the FDA. Ifezuntirgene inilparvovec also holds Fast Track designation from the FDA. The company has made important regulatory progress, including submitting a biologics license application to the FDA and a Marketing Authorisation Application in the United Kingdom, creating significant value if approved. QURE currently carries a Zacks Rank #2. Its shares have gained 8.2% in a month. 10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company developing innovative tools to study complex biological systems. Its commercial portfolio comprises Single Cell and Spatial solutions. The company’s products include instruments such as Chromium, Visium CytAssist and Xenium Analyzer, along with proprietary microfluidic chips, slides, reagents and other consumables. The company also provides software to support workflows ranging from sample preparation to data analysis and visualization. Its revenues are primarily generated from instrument and consumables sales, supplemented by post-warranty service contracts. TXG currently carries a Zacks Rank #2. excerpt: VTRS, RVTY, ELAN and VCYT have earnings beat signals ahead of Q3 results. Can drug launches, lab spending and cancer tests overcome margin pressures?
headline: 4 Medical Stocks With a Healthy Shot at Q3 Earnings Beats
html_content:
The third-quarter 2026 earnings season is revealing a familiar healthcare divide: demand is holding up, but not every business is turning that demand into stronger profits. Laboratories are ordering more equipment, cancer testing continues to expand, and animal health innovation is attracting customers. Meanwhile, pricing pressure, uneven research spending and higher operating costs leave little room for mistakes.

Investors want to know whether this improvement extends to Medical companies awaiting results. Viatris Inc. VTRS, Revvity, Inc. RVTY, Elanco Animal Health Incorporated ELAN and Veracyte, Inc. VCYT offer four different ways to assess the sector's momentum. Each has favorable earnings indicators and business trends that could support results above consensus expectations.

According to the latest Earnings Trends report, the medical sector (one of the 16 broad Zacks sectors within the Zacks Industry) is projected to experience a 0.9% decline in earnings for the third quarter, even as revenues are anticipated to rise by 5%. The disconnect reflects ongoing margin pressure.

Factors at Play for Medical Stocks in Q3

The medical sector encompasses a broad range of businesses, including hospitals, physician groups, nursing care facilities, insurers, pharmaceutical manufacturers, medical device makers, life sciences tools and diagnostics, outpatient and home care providers and animal health medicines.

The clearest positive signal comes from companies supplying laboratories and drug developers. Thermo Fisher’s organic growth and Danaher’s better end-market commentary suggest pharmaceutical and biotechnology customers are becoming more willing to spend. Still, orders for major instruments can be delayed when research funding remains tight. Recurring reagents, screening services and consumables may prove more dependable than equipment purchases. Revvity’s life sciences business faces these conflicting forces, while diagnostic testing offers a more stable source of demand.

Cancer diagnostics is benefiting from a longer shift toward treatment decisions guided by molecular information. Physicians increasingly need tools that distinguish patients who require aggressive intervention from those who may avoid it. Broader clinical evidence and reimbursement coverage could expand adoption, but test volumes alone do not guarantee higher profits. Laboratories must secure payments, maintain pricing and control processing costs. Abbott’s recent cancer diagnostics momentum offers a constructive industry signal, particularly for companies such as Veracyte.

For pharmaceutical manufacturers, demand for affordable medicines remains durable, even as competition squeezes older products. Complex generics, branded treatments and specialty launches can improve the sales mix, but manufacturing reliability remains critical. Disruptions may have delayed some shipments, triggering remediation expenses and weakening operating leverage. Viatris faces precisely that balance between commercial opportunities and supply constraints, with investors also watching whether savings offset pricing erosion.

In animal health, longer parasite seasons and greater emphasis on preventive treatment are helping sustain interest in innovative pet medicines. Digital fulfillment and repeat prescriptions could improve compliance and revenue visibility. However, veterinary visits and discretionary spending remain sensitive to household budgets.

Merck's third-quarter animal health sales rose 4%, with companion animal revenues advancing 6% and livestock revenues increasing 2%. New products supported pet care growth. The results point to an opportunity for Elanco's expanding portfolio, although spending by pet owners, competition and farm economics could create uneven results across categories.

How We Selected Potential Earnings Winners

Backed by in-depth research and market insight, we have leveraged the Zacks Stock Screener to identify top healthcare names that stand out ahead of their earnings releases. These stocks have the ideal combination of two ingredients — a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) — to surpass expectations.

Our research shows that for stocks with this combination, the chances of an earnings beat are as high as 70%. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they are reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.
