headline: 3 Hotel REITs to Watch for Potential Upside This Earnings Season
html_content:
With the third-quarter earnings season underway, the early results are drawing investor interest as companies report strong profits. Instead of buying stocks that have already rallied on solid results, it may make more sense to focus on companies that still have room to surprise positively. Earnings beats often serve as catalysts, boosting sentiment and pushing shares higher.

This is likely to be reflected in the earnings releases of Host Hotels & Resorts HST, Park Hotels & Resorts PK and RLJ Lodging Trust RLJ.

REITs play a vital role in both the physical and digital sides of the economy and often show resilience even in challenging markets. Taking a closer look at the sector’s fundamentals can help investors identify areas of steady performance and long-term growth potential. Here’s a look at where the industry’s strengths lie and how it could still present value amid broader market uncertainty.

The hotel industry, in particular, demonstrated resilient growth in the third quarter of 2026. According to CBRE data, overall hotel occupancy increased 1.8% year over year as demand growth of 3% surpassed the 0.4% rise in supply during the quarter. Revenue per available room (RevPAR) climbed 7% year over year, bolstered by a 4.3% increase in the average daily rate (ADR). Nominal RevPAR rose by 7% year over year, while real (inflation-adjusted) RevPAR growth settled at 3.5%.

The sector faces upward pressure from rising labor costs, as hotel wages grew 4.7% in the third quarter of 2026, outpacing the broader 3.3% national wage growth and inflation of 3.5%.

The Zacks Methodology

Picking the right stock could be difficult unless one knows the proper method. To make the task simple, we rely on the Zacks methodology, combining a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) and a positive Earnings ESP. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they’re reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

Our proprietary methodology, Earnings ESP, shows the percentage difference between the Most Accurate Estimate and the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Research shows that stocks with a favorable Zacks Rank and a positive Earnings ESP have as high as a 70% chance of delivering a positive earnings surprise.

Here are three Hotel REITs that have the right combination of elements to deliver positive surprises this earnings season.

Host Hotels & Resorts currently has an Earnings ESP of +3.24% and carries a Zacks Rank #3. Over the trailing four quarters, the company’s adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) per share outpaced the Zacks Consensus Estimate on all occasions, with the average beat being 5.63%. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

 

Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. Quote

 

Host Hotels is likely to have benefited from its portfolio of luxury and upper-scale hotels across the top U.S. markets and the Sunbelt region. Continued strength in leisure travel demand, healthy group demand and higher room rates, are likely to have supported revenue per available room (RevPAR) growth in the to-be-reported quarter. On its second-quarter earnings call, management indicated that group booking pace for the third quarter had improved from negative low-single digits to positive low-single digits, suggesting a favorable backdrop for group revenues in the third quarter.

The company’s strategic capital allocations are likely to have improved portfolio quality and strengthened its position in key U.S. markets, where it has a greater scale and competitive advantage. This is likely to have given it an edge and driven margin expansion.

Host Hotels is scheduled to release its third-quarter 2026 earnings on Nov. 4, after market close.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for quarterly revenues is pegged at $1.38 billion, which suggests a 3.8% increase from the year-ago quarter’s reported figure. The consensus mark for third-quarter 2026 AFFO per share is pegged at 38 cents, implying an 8.6% increase year over year.

Park Hotels & Resorts has an Earnings ESP of +0.70% and carries a Zacks Rank #2 at present. Over the trailing four quarters, PK’s FFO per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate thrice and missed in the remaining period, with the average beat being 5.35%.

 

Park Hotels & Resorts Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Park Hotels & Resorts Inc. price-eps-surprise | Park Hotels & Resorts Inc. Quote

 

Park Hotels is expected to have benefited from its diverse portfolio of hotels and resorts in the third quarter. The company is likely to report positive RevPAR growth, supported by solid group demand and leisure travel demand. Management’s earlier upward revision of its full-year 2026 RevPAR growth outlook to 3-4.5% from 0.5%-2.5% reinforces expectations of continued operating momentum.

Looking ahead, the company stands to capitalize on premium pricing opportunities, portfolio renovations and operational improvements. The company continues to streamline its portfolio through non-core asset sales, with proceeds expected to support debt reduction and improve financial flexibility.

Park Hotels is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 4, after market close.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter total revenues is pegged at $598 million. The consensus mark for the quarterly FFO per share is pinned at 36 cents, suggesting a 2.9% increase year over year.

RLJ Lodging Trust currently has an Earnings ESP of +6.25% and carries a Zacks Rank of #2. Over the trailing four quarters, the company’s FFO per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three estimates and missed on one occasion, with the average beat being 3.75%.

 

RLJ Lodging Trust Price and EPS Surprise

RLJ Lodging Trust price-eps-surprise | RLJ Lodging Trust Quote

 

RLJ Lodging’s portfolio of premium-branded hotels in major U.S. urban markets is likely to have benefited from continued strength in business travel, leisure and group demand. Management guided to a meaningful improvement in third-quarter group booking pace, with reservations pacing at 110% of the year-ago period, supporting occupancy and room-revenue growth. Management also expects third-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA contribution to be approximately 100 basis points higher than the prior-year quarter.

RLJ’s investment case is further supported by multiple growth drivers, including hotel conversions, high-impact renovations and revenue-enhancement initiatives aimed at increasing food and beverage and other ancillary revenues. The successful ramp-up of previously completed projects and the ongoing repositioning of its portfolio are expected to contribute to operating growth.

RLJ Lodging is slated to report third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 4, after market close.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for quarterly revenues is presently pegged at $341.7 million, which indicates an increase of 3.5% year over year. The consensus mark for the quarterly FFO per share is pinned at 32 cents, suggesting an 18.5% increase year over year.

excerpt: KimberlyClark shares have stagnated for several years as topline growth struggles to advance.
headline: Bear of the Day: KimberlyClark (KMB)
html_content:
KimberlyClark (KMB), the consumer staples giant behind household brands like Huggies, Kleenex and Cottonelle, has faced considerable selling pressure as its underlying growth continues to disappoint, while its massive acquisition of Kenvue introduces a new set of financial challenges.

The company has struggled to generate meaningful organic growth for years, with annual sales largely stagnant over the last decade. That lackluster performance has been reflected in the stock price, with KMB shares declining approximately 19% over the last five years, compared with a 66% gain for the S&P 500.

And while management is pursuing a significant transformation of the business, the near-term outlook remains challenging. Weak sales trends, downward earnings revisions and the additional financial burden of its Kenvue acquisition have created an increasingly uncertain fundamental picture.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

KimberlyClark Shares Fall Alongside Earnings Estimates

Even before accounting for the Kenvue transaction, KimberlyClark's underlying business has been showing signs of weakness.

In the second quarter, revenue from continuing operations increased just 0.6% year over year to $4.2 billion, while organic sales were essentially flat.

The company also faced considerable pressure in China, its core growth segment, where social media allegations surrounding its diaper products disrupted sales and contributed to management lowering its full year outlook.

KimberlyClark now expects 2026 organic sales growth to trail its underlying categories by approximately one percentage point, while adjusted earnings per share attributable to the company are expected to decline slightly on a constant-currency basis.

Its October preliminary update reaffirmed that outlook, offering little indication of an imminent acceleration.

Not surprisingly, analysts have been cutting their earnings forecasts, pushing KimberlyClark to a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell).

Over the last 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for current year earnings has declined 8.1% to $6.83 per share, while next year estimates have fallen 8.2% to $7.03. Earnings estimates have been in steep decline since the start of 2025.

With earnings expectations deteriorating across multiple periods, there is little evidence that the fundamental outlook has reached an inflection point.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Should Investors Avoid KMB Stock?

KimberlyClark has long been regarded as a defensive consumer staples investment, supported by its recognizable brands, recurring demand and consistent dividend payments.

However, defensive businesses are not necessarily defensive investments, particularly when growth stalls and earnings expectations continue to decline.

The Kenvue acquisition certainly introduces opportunities for improving profitability and expanding the company's market presence. But it also raises the stakes considerably, with a larger debt burden and meaningful execution risks.

Until management demonstrates improving organic growth, successful integration and a stabilization in earnings estimates, KMB appears likely to remain under pressure.

For now, investors may be better served looking elsewhere in the consumer staples sector.

headline: 3 Top-Ranked Lord Abbett Mutual Funds With Stellar Track Records
html_content:
Founded in 1929, Lord Abbett is an independent, privately held global investment management firm. As of June  30, 2026, the firm managed approximately $262 billion in assets.

The company offers a comprehensive range of investment strategies, including domestic and international equities, fixed income, multi-asset solutions and alternative investments. Supported by an experienced team of investment professionals, Lord Abbett serves institutional and individual clients in more than 30 countries.

Its products are distributed through mutual funds, separate accounts, sub-advised accounts, and managed account platforms, all driven by an active management approach and a strong long-term focus on client outcomes.

Below, we share with you three top-ranked Lord Abbett mutual funds, namely Lord Abbett Developing Growth LADFX, Lord Abbett Growth Opportunities LGOVX and Lord Abbett International Growth LAVGX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and is expected to outperform its peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of funds.

Lord Abbett Developing Growth targets small-cap companies with above-average long-term growth potential and may invest in foreign and emerging-market equities, including depositary receipts.

Lord Abbett Developing Growth has three-year annualized returns of 21.2%. As of April 2026, LADFX held 91 issues, with 3.6% of its assets invested in Comfort Systems USA.

Lord Abbett Growth Opportunities primarily invests in mid-cap equities with strong revenue and earnings growth prospects, while maintaining limited exposure to foreign and emerging-market securities.

Lord Abbett Growth Opportunities has three-year annualized returns of 21.9%. LGOVX has an expense ratio of 0.60%.

Lord Abbett International Growth invests primarily in large foreign companies with above-average, long-term growth potential and may also invest in emerging markets and U.S. companies.

headline: 3 AllianceBernstein Mutual Funds for Long-Term Returns
html_content:
AllianceBernstein (AB) was founded more than 50 years ago as a global investment management company offering a range of equity, fixed-income, alternative, and multi-asset investment strategies. The company has $839 billion in assets under management across 53 locations in 27 countries and jurisdictions worldwide.  

AllianceBernstein uses research capabilities across multiple asset classes and combines a global perspective on markets with fundamental research to identify opportunities. The range of strategies that the firm offers includes growth and value equities, corporate and tax-exempt fixed income, as well as alternative and multi-asset strategies. 

Responsible investment is an integral part of AB’s business and investment practices. AB conducts business in accordance with responsible business practices, attempts to reduce resources used in investment practices, and supports sustainability initiatives worldwide through its global research network and investment capabilities.  

We have picked three AllianceBernstein mutual funds — AB High Income AGDAX, AB All Market Real Return AMTAX and Bernstein International Small Cap SCB IRCSX — which investors should buy now for the long term. These funds have a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or Rank 2 (Buy), with positive three-year and five-year annualized returns, minimum initial investments within $5000 and expense ratios considerably lower than the category average. So, these funds have provided comparatively stronger performance and carry a lower fee.

AB High Income fund seeks primarily a high level of current income and, secondarily, capital appreciation. AGDAX invests in sovereign debt obligations of developing countries and in U.S. and non-U.S. corporate fixed-income securities. 

Matthew S. Sheridan has been the lead manager of AGDAX since Oct. 31, 2005. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies such as DaVita Inc. (0.6%), Advance Auto Parts, Inc. (0.5%) and Avis Budget Group, Inc. (0.5%) as of April 30, 2026.

AGDAX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 8.2% and 3.6%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.86%. AGDAX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.                      

To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 (Strong Buy) and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds,please click here.

AB All Market Real Return fund seeks to maximize real return, or return after adjusting for inflation, through an aggressive investment strategy involving a variety of asset classes. AMTAX invests primarily in instruments expected to outperform broad equity indices during rising inflation, including inflation-indexed fixed income (such as TIPS and similar non-U.S. bonds), commodities and commodity-related equities, real estate equities (including REITs), inflation-sensitive equities, securities and derivatives linked to other assets, and currencies.

Daniel J. Loewy has been the lead manager of AMTAX since March 31, 2015. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies like Welltower Inc. (3.1%), Prologis, Inc. (2.8%) and Equinix, Inc. (2.1%) as of April 30, 2026. 

AMTAX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 15.9% and 9%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 1.13%. AMTAX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1. 

Bernstein International Small Cap SCB fund invests in small-cap equities and related instruments, primarily investing in companies located outside the United States. 

Andrew Birse has been the lead manager of IRCSX since Dec. 21, 2015. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies like Balfour Beatty plc (1.8%), Elite Material Co., Ltd. (1.8%) and Nanya Technology Corp (1.3%) as of June 30, 2026. 

IRCSX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 21.3% and 8.2%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 1.18%. IRCSX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

headline: Is iShares Emerging Markets Equity Factor ETF (EMGF) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
Launched on 12/08/2015, the iShares Emerging Markets Equity Factor ETF (EMGF) is a smart beta exchange traded fund offering broad exposure to the Broad Emerging Market ETFs category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

The ETF industry has long been dominated by products based on market cap weighted indexes, a strategy created to reflect the market or a particular market segment.

A good option for investors who believe in market efficiency, market cap weighted indexes offer a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way of replicating market returns.

If you're the kind of investor who would rather try and beat the market through good stock selection, then smart beta funds are your best choice; this fund class is known for tracking non-cap weighted strategies.

This kind of index follows this same mindset, as it attempts to pick stocks that have better chances of risk-return performance; non-cap weighted strategies base selection on certain fundamental characteristics, or a mix of such characteristics.

This area offers many different investment choices, such as simplest equal-weighting, fundamental weighting and volatility/momentum based weighting methodologies; however, not all of these strategies can deliver superior results.

Fund Sponsor & Index

The fund is managed by Blackrock, and has been able to amass over $1.79 billion, which makes it one of the larger ETFs in the Broad Emerging Market ETFs. This particular fund, before fees and expenses, seeks to match the performance of the MSCI Emerging Markets Diversified Multiple-Factor Index.

The STOXX Emerging Markets Equity Factor Index (USD) composes of stocks of large and mid-capitalization companies in emerging markets that have favourable exposure to target style factors subject to constraints.

Cost & Other Expenses

Expense ratios are an important factor in the return of an ETF and in the long-term, cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive cousins, other things remaining the same.

With one of the cheaper products in the space, this ETF has annual operating expenses of 0.26%.

The fund has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 2.20%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Most ETFs are very transparent products, and disclose their holdings on a daily basis. ETFs also offer diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk, though it's still important for investors to research a fund's holdings.

When you look at individual holdings, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturingaccounts for about 10.22% of the fund's total assets, followed by Samsung Electronics Ltd and Sk Hynix.

EMGF's top 10 holdings account for about 31.91% of its total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

So far this year, EMGF has added roughly 14.23%, and it's up approximately 13.3% in the last one year (as of 11/04/2026). During this past 52-week period, the fund has traded between $55.64 and $76.28.

The ETF has a beta of 0.75 and standard deviation of 19.31% for the trailing three-year period. With about 742 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

iShares Emerging Markets Equity Factor ETF is a reasonable option for investors seeking to outperform the Broad Emerging Market ETFs segment of the market. However, there are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider.

Vanguard Emerging Markets Stock Index Fund ETF Shares (VWO) tracks FTSE Emerging Markets All Cap China A Inclusion Index and the iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (IEMG) tracks MSCI Emerging Markets Investable Market Index. Vanguard Emerging Markets Stock Index Fund ETF Shares has $116.99 billion in assets, iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF has $145.97 billion. VWO has an expense ratio of 0.06% and IEMG changes 0.09%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Broad Emerging Market ETFs

Bottom Line

Making its debut on 11/08/2017, smart beta exchange traded fund John Hancock Multifactor Small Cap ETF (JHSC) provides investors broad exposure to the Style Box - Small Cap Blend category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

The ETF industry has long been dominated by products based on market cap weighted indexes, a strategy created to reflect the market or a particular market segment.

Because market cap weighted indexes provide a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way of replicating market returns, they work well for investors who believe in market efficiency.

If you're the kind of investor who would rather try and beat the market through good stock selection, then smart beta funds are your best choice; this fund class is known for tracking non-cap weighted strategies.

By attempting to pick stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance, non-cap weighted indexes are based on certain fundamental characteristics, or a combination of such.

While this space offers a number of choices to investors, including simplest equal-weighting, fundamental weighting and volatility/momentum based weighting methodologies, not all these strategies have been able to deliver superior results.

Fund Sponsor & Index

The fund is managed by John Hancock. JHSC has been able to amass assets over $701.34 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs in the Style Box - Small Cap Blend. Before fees and expenses, this particular fund seeks to match the performance of the JOHN HANCOCK DIMENSIONAL SMALL CAP INDEX.

The John Hancock Dimensional Small Cap Index is designed to comprise a subset of securities in the U.S. Universe issued by companies whose market capitalizations are smaller than the 750th largest U.S. company but excluding the smallest 4% of U.S. companies at the time of reconstitution.

Cost & Other Expenses

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Operating expenses on an annual basis are 0.42% for this ETF, which makes it on par with most peer products in the space.

JHSC's 12-month trailing dividend yield is 1.02%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

ETFs offer diversified exposure and thus minimize single stock risk, but it is still important to delve into a fund's holdings before investing. Most ETFs are very transparent products and many disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

Representing 19.6% of the portfolio, the fund has heaviest allocation to the Industrials sector; Financials and Consumer Discretionary round out the top three.

Alternatives

By attempting to pick stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance, non-cap weighted indexes are based on certain fundamental characteristics, or a combination of such. While this space offers a number of choices to investors, including simplest equal-weighting, fundamental weighting and volatility/momentum based weighting methodologies, not all these strategies have been able to deliver superior results. headline: Should Vanguard Russell 1000 Value Index Fund ETF Shares (VONV) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
Looking for broad exposure to the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market? You should consider the Vanguard Russell 1000 Value Index Fund ETF Shares (VONV), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on September 22, 2010.

The fund is sponsored by Vanguard. It has amassed assets over $22.60 billion, making it one of the largest ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Value

Companies that find themselves in the large cap category typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. They tend to be stable companies with predictable cash flows and are usually less volatile than mid and small cap companies.

Value stocks are known for their lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, but investors should also note their lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. While value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in nearly all markets when you consider long-term performance, growth stocks are more likely to outpace value stocks in strong bull markets.

Costs

Investors should also pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio. Lower cost products will produce better results than those with a higher cost, assuming all other metrics remain the same.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.06%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.53%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

It is important to delve into an ETF's holdings before investing despite the many upsides to these kinds of funds like diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Information Technology sector -- about 18.9% of the portfolio. Financials and Healthcare round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Amazon.com Inc (AMZN) accounts for about 6.08% of total assets, followed by Apple Inc (AAPL) and Microsoft Corp (MSFT).

Performance and Risk

VONV seeks to match the performance of the Russell 1000 Value Index before fees and expenses. The Russell 1000 Value Index measures the performance of large-capitalization value stocks in the United States.

The ETF return is roughly 24.22% so far this year and was up about 28.55% in the last one year (as of 11/04/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $87.76 and $114.39.

The ETF has a beta of 0.83 and standard deviation of 12.56% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 873 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

Vanguard Russell 1000 Value Index Fund ETF Shares holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 1 (Strong Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, VONV is a great option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Value segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) and the Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) track a similar index. While Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF has $120.21 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF has $193.97 billion. SCHD has an expense ratio of 0.06% and VTV charges 0.03%.

Bottom-Line

Passively managed ETFs are becoming increasingly popular with institutional as well as retail investors due to their low cost, transparency, flexibility and tax efficiency. They are excellent vehicles for long term investors.

headline: 4 Utility Stocks Set to Outperform Q3 Earnings Estimates This Season
html_content:
The companies operating in the Zacks Utilities sector’s third-quarter 2026 earnings are likely to have benefited from surging electricity demand driven by AI-powered data centers, hyperscale facilities and manufacturing reshoring. Favorable regulatory rate approvals, increased capital investments in grid modernization and transmission infrastructure are expected to have supported earnings growth. Additionally, warmer-than-normal late-summer temperatures likely boosted cooling demand and electricity sales, while expanding power agreements with technology companies created additional revenue opportunities. According to the latest Earnings Preview, the utility sector’s earnings are projected to increase 8.3% on revenue growth of 5.5%.

With the assistance of the Zacks Stock Screener, we have identified four utilities, namely PPL Corporation PPL, Evergy, Inc. EVRG, The Southern Company SO and Duke Energy DUK, which are poised to beat on earnings this reporting cycle.
 
These stocks have the ideal combination of two ingredients — a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy), or 3 (Hold) — to surpass expectations. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they are reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

Key Catalysts Influencing Utility Stocks' Q3 Performance

Utilities are expected to have benefited from the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence applications and hyperscale data centers, which is driving substantial growth in electricity demand, creating significant opportunities for utilities. Increasing power requirements are expected to boost electricity sales, accelerate infrastructure investments and support long-term earnings growth, strengthening the investment appeal of utility stocks.

Utility companies are expected to have benefited from favorable electricity rates, strategic acquisitions, effective cost-control measures and expanding energy-efficiency initiatives. Continued investments in grid modernization and resilience to mitigate the impact of extreme weather events, along with the growing integration of cost-efficient renewable energy sources, are also likely to have strengthened operational efficiency and supported overall financial performance.

U.S. utilities are gaining from growing electricity demand across commercial and industrial sectors, supported by expanding economic activities and rising power consumption. The resurgence of domestic manufacturing, driven by reshoring initiatives, is further increasing electricity requirements and boosting utility revenues. These developments are expected to stimulate grid infrastructure investments, drive rate-base growth and support sustained long-term earnings expansion.

In addition, warmer-than-normal temperatures across several U.S. regions during late summer led to increased demand for air conditioning and cooling services, driving higher electricity consumption. The resulting rise in power sales volumes is likely to have boosted utility revenues and supported earnings growth during the third quarter of 2026.

Ongoing investment to upgrade the utility infrastructure and favorable rate approvals from the commission have also aided the performance of the utilities in the third quarter.

Utility Stocks Positioned for Upbeat Quarterly Earnings

PPL Corporation is a diversified utility holding company based in Allentown, PA. PPL generates electricity and distributes electricity and natural gas to more than 3.6 million utility customers in the United States. PPL's $23 billion 2026-2029 capital plan provides a strong foundation for rate-base growth, with investments expected to drive approximately 10.3% average annual rate-base growth through 2029.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for its third-quarter earnings is pegged at 53 cents per share, indicating an increase of 10.42% from the year-ago reported figure. PPL currently has an Earnings ESP of +0.38% and a Zacks Rank #2. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Evergy plans to invest $21.6 billion during 2026-2030 in transmission, distribution upgrades and customer-focused platforms to enhance reliability.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for its third-quarter earnings is pegged at $1.71 per share, indicating an increase of 6.88% from the year-ago reported figure. SO currently has an Earnings ESP of +0.84% and a Zacks Rank #3.

Duke Energy benefits from relatively predictable earnings and cash flows, supported by ongoing infrastructure investments and rate-base expansion. DUK has reported nearly 7.6 GW of data center Electric Service Agreements, which could support higher electricity sales and additional capital investments over the long term.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for its third-quarter earnings is pegged at $1.87 per share, indicating an increase of 3.31% from the year-ago reported figure. DUK currently has an Earnings ESP of +1.07% and a Zacks Rank #3.

excerpt: Texas Instruments stock has outperformed AI leader Nvidia amid a recovery in analog semiconductor demand.
headline: Bull of the Day: Texas Instruments (TXN)
html_content:
While the leading-edge, high-performance semiconductors powering the AI boom have garnered most of the attention in recent years, some of the less flashy analog and embedded chips are also playing a critical role in the expansion of advanced technologies and infrastructure.

Texas Instruments TXN, the world's largest analog semiconductor manufacturer, has been enjoying accelerating fundamental growth, significant earnings upgrades and increasingly bullish stock price momentum.

After sitting out much of the AI boom, TXN had been weighed down by cyclical headwinds as its automotive and industrial customers worked through large inventories accumulated following the pandemic. However, the stock emerged from that slump earlier this year, and the bullish catalysts continue to mount.

Furthermore, amid a particularly volatile stretch for large segments of the semiconductor industry, Texas Instruments and several other major analog chipmakers have demonstrated notable relative strength. Although there have certainly been bumps along the way, these stocks have generally held up well during recent bouts of selling in former market leaders.

Below, we'll review the emerging opportunities for Texas Instruments, its improving earnings outlook and the valuation picture.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Emerging Opportunities for Texas Instrument

Texas Instruments is positioned to benefit from several powerful trends, including industrial automation, automotive electrification, expanding data center infrastructure and the broader recovery in semiconductor demand.

Unlike the advanced processors developed by Nvidia and other AI leaders, analog semiconductors perform essential functions such as managing power, converting signals and interfacing with real-world systems.

These chips are required across virtually every modern electronic system, and their importance only increases as devices and infrastructure become more sophisticated.

The automotive industry offers a clear example as the average number of semiconductors per vehicle doubled between 2017 and 2021, reaching roughly 1,700, with demand continuing to rise as electrification, advanced safety systems and autonomous driving features become more widespread

The expansion of AI data centers of course is interesting as well. While GPUs capture the headlines, these facilities also require enormous amounts of power management, monitoring and supporting electronics, creating additional demand for analog components.

Meanwhile, the company's industrial and automotive markets are recovering from a prolonged inventory correction, providing a more cyclical source of growth.

Texas Instruments also enjoys a structural manufacturing advantage through its investments in 300mm wafer fabrication, which can reduce production costs substantially compared with traditional 200mm manufacturing.

The company recently began production at its newest fab in Sherman, Texas, part of a broader $60 billion US manufacturing expansion spanning seven facilities in Texas and Utah. With additional capacity coming online, TXN is positioning itself to capture rising demand while benefiting from greater economies of scale and tighter control over its supply chain.

TXN Stock Jumps on Earnings Beat and Upgrades

Texas Instruments' latest quarterly results offered compelling evidence that the recovery continues to gain momentum.

Third quarter revenue increased 28% year over year to $6.06 billion, while earnings per share surged 77% to $2.62. Operating profit climbed an impressive 73%, highlighting the substantial operating leverage in the business.

Importantly, the strength was broad-based, with management reporting continued growth across industrial, automotive and data center markets. The company's analog segment was particularly strong, generating 32% revenue growth, while embedded processing revenue increased 21%.

Over the last 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for current year earnings has increased 5.6% to $8.89 per share, while next year estimates have jumped 13% to $11.12. These developments have contributed to a powerful trend in analyst earnings upgrades, earning TXN a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Even more encouraging, revisions have been overwhelmingly positive, with no downward adjustments among the revisions recorded across the current and next fiscal years.

That combination of accelerating earnings growth and consistently rising estimates is precisely what we look for when identifying stocks with the potential to outperform.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Shares of TXN Trade Near Historical Average

Despite its impressive rally this year, Texas Instruments' valuation is becoming more reasonable as earnings expectations catch up with the stock price.

TXN currently trades around 34x forward earnings, a premium to the broader market and respective industry, though one that should be considered in the context of its accelerating profit growth, strong market position and cash generating capabilities.

The company generated $7.4 billion in free cash flow over the trailing 12 months.

Although the stock is hardly a bargain on conventional valuation measures, the sharp increase in forward earnings estimates has helped moderate its valuation even as shares have advanced.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Should Investors Buy Shares of TXN?

Texas Instruments offers investors exposure to several important secular growth themes without relying exclusively on the more speculative corners of the AI trade.

The combination of recovering industrial demand, expanding data center opportunities, improving margins and powerful earnings revisions makes for an increasingly compelling fundamental picture.

Of course, the cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry and the stock's premium valuation remain important risks. That said, most evidence points to an early stage of cyclical recovery.

Nevertheless, with earnings momentum accelerating and shares demonstrating impressive relative strength, TXN looks well positioned to continue outperforming in the months ahead.

Although there have certainly been bumps along the way, these stocks have generally held up well during recent bouts of selling in former market leaders. Below, we'll review the emerging opportunities for Texas Instruments, its improving earnings outlook and the valuation picture. Image Source: Zacks Investment Research Emerging Opportunities for Texas Instrument Texas Instruments is positioned to benefit from several powerful trends, including industrial automation, automotive electrification, expanding data center infrastructure and the broader recovery in semiconductor demand. Unlike the advanced processors developed by Nvidia and other AI leaders, analog semiconductors perform essential functions such as managing power, converting signals and interfacing with real-world systems. These chips are required across virtually every modern electronic system, and their importance only increases as devices and infrastructure become more sophisticated. The automotive industry offers a clear example as the average number of semiconductors per vehicle doubled between 2017 and 2021, reaching roughly 1,700, with demand continuing to rise as electrification, advanced safety systems and autonomous driving features become more widespread The expansion of AI data centers of course is interesting as well. While GPUs capture the headlines, these facilities also require enormous amounts of power management, monitoring and supporting electronics, creating additional demand for analog components. Meanwhile, the company's industrial and automotive markets are recovering from a prolonged inventory correction, providing a more cyclical source of growth. Texas Instruments also enjoys a structural manufacturing advantage through its investments in 300mm wafer fabrication, which can reduce production costs substantially compared with traditional 200mm manufacturing. The company recently began production at its newest fab in Sherman, Texas, part of a broader $60 billion US manufacturing expansion spanning seven facilities in Texas and Utah. With additional capacity coming online, TXN is positioning itself to capture rising demand while benefiting from greater economies of scale and tighter control over its supply chain. TXN Stock Jumps on Earnings Beat and Upgrades Texas Instruments' latest quarterly results offered compelling evidence that the recovery continues to gain momentum. Third quarter revenue increased 28% year over year to $6.06 billion, while earnings per share surged 77% to $2.62. Operating profit climbed an impressive 73%, highlighting the substantial operating leverage in the business. Importantly, the strength was broad-based, with management reporting continued growth across industrial, automotive and data center markets. The company's analog segment was particularly strong, generating 32% revenue growth, while embedded processing revenue increased 21%. Over the last 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for current year earnings has increased 5.6% to $8.89 per share, while next year estimates have jumped 13% to $11.12. These developments have contributed to a powerful trend in analyst earnings upgrades, earning TXN a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). Even more encouraging, revisions have been overwhelmingly positive, with no downward adjustments among the revisions recorded across the current and next fiscal years. That combination of accelerating earnings growth and consistently rising estimates is precisely what we look for when identifying stocks with the potential to outperform. Image Source: Zacks Investment Research Shares of TXN Trade Near Historical Average Despite its impressive rally this year, Texas Instruments' valuation is becoming more reasonable as earnings expectations catch up with the stock price. TXN currently trades around 34x forward earnings, a premium to the broader market and respective industry, though one that should be considered in the context of its accelerating profit growth, strong market position and cash generating capabilities. The company generated $7.4 billion in free cash flow over the trailing 12 months. Although the stock is hardly a bargain on conventional valuation measures, the sharp increase in forward earnings estimates has helped moderate its valuation even as shares have advanced. Image Source: Zacks Investment Research Should Investors Buy Shares of TXN? Texas Instruments offers investors exposure to several important secular growth themes without relying exclusively on the more speculative corners of the AI trade. The combination of recovering industrial demand, expanding data center opportunities, improving margins and powerful earnings revisions makes for an increasingly compelling fundamental picture. Of course, the cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry and the stock's premium valuation remain important risks. That said, most evidence points to an early stage of cyclical recovery. Nevertheless, with earnings momentum accelerating and shares demonstrating impressive relative strength, TXN looks well positioned to continue outperforming in the months ahead. excerpt: AC Immune (ACIU) delivered earnings and revenue surprises of +27.27% and +299.42%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 2026. Do the numbers hold clues to what lies ahead for the stock?
headline: AC Immune (ACIU) Reports Q3 Loss, Beats Revenue Estimates
html_content:
AC Immune (ACIU) came out with a quarterly loss of $0.16 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of a loss of $0.22. This compares to a loss of $0.2 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +27.27%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this biopharmaceutical company would post a loss of $0.22 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.03, delivering a surprise of +113.64%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

AC Immune, which belongs to the Zacks Medical - Biomedical and Genetics industry, posted revenues of $3.99 million for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 299.42%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.17 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

AC Immune shares have lost about 33.4% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.6%.

What's Next for AC Immune?

While AC Immune has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for AC Immune was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is -$0.22 on $1 million in revenues for the coming quarter and -$0.60 on $22.52 million in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Medical - Biomedical and Genetics is currently in the top 45% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the same industry, Regenxbio (RGNX), has yet to report results for the quarter ended September 2026. The results are expected to be released on November 5.

This biotechnology company is expected to post quarterly loss of $1.35 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -12.5%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 42.3% lower over the last 30 days to the current level.

Regenxbio's revenues are expected to be $9.6 million, down 67.7% from the year-ago quarter.

excerpt: Wall Street closed mixed on Tuesday, pulled up by tech and industrial stocks.
headline: Stock Market News for Nov 4, 2026
html_content:
Wall Street closed mixed on Tuesday, pulled up by tech and industrial stocks. Investor sentiment remained cautious but selective, as uncertainty surrounding the U.S. midterm elections kept investors on the sidelines, while renewed strength in technology and semiconductor stocks offered some support. Two of the three benchmark indexes ended in the green while one ended in the red.

How Did the Benchmarks Perform?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) fell 197.26 points, or 0.4%, to close at 51,786.72. Twenty-one components of the 30-stock index ended in negative territory, while nine ended in positive.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite added 207.69 points, or 0.8%, to close at 25,372.01.

The S&P 500 gained 27.52 points, or 0.4%, to close at 7,568.92. Four of the benchmark index's 11 broad sectors closed in the green. The Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK), the Industrials Select Sector SPDR (XLI) and the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR (XLC) advanced 1.3%, 1% and 0.9%, respectively, while the Materials Select Sector SPDR (XLB) declined 1.9%.

The fear gauge CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) fell 1.5% to 20.83. A total of 16.6 billion shares were traded on Tuesday, lower than the last 20-session average of 17.4 billion. Decliners outnumbered advancers by a 1.6-to-1 ratio on the S&P 500.

Chipmaker Stocks Rebound as Investors Return to AI Trade

Chipmaker stocks rallied on Wall Street on Tuesday as investors returned to artificial intelligence (AI)-related shares following a recent selloff. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, a key gauge of semiconductor stocks, advanced 3% during the session, supporting the Nasdaq Composite and the broader technology sector. The rebound came as investors sought opportunities in technology shares after concerns over escalating AI infrastructure spending and uncertain returns had weighed on market sentiment.

The rally also reflected bargain hunting following several sessions of losses. The Nasdaq-100 had closed more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record high on Monday, entering correction territory. This decline created opportunities for investors to purchase semiconductor shares at lower valuations.

Consequently, Broadcom Inc. AVGO and NVIDIA Corporation NVDA jumped 3.1% and 2.3%, respectively. While NVDA currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), AVGO has a #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Wall Street Takes Midterm Elections in Stride as Investors Await Results

U.S. midterm elections weighed on Wall Street on Tuesday, as investors largely remained focused on technology stocks and the potential implications of changing congressional control. However, investors largely refrained from making major election-driven bets ahead of the results.

The possibility of Democrats gaining control of the House, while the Senate remained competitive, added uncertainty around future fiscal policy, taxation, government spending and corporate regulation. A potential Democratic victory also raised concerns about greater scrutiny of AI companies and data-center investments. However, investors viewed the elections as an event that could remove a prolonged source of market uncertainty. Attention remained on the eventual congressional balance and its implications for corporate America.

Economic Data

Per the U.S. Census Bureau, Factory Orders for September increased 1.8% against a consensus of 1.1% for the period. The number for August was revised up to 0.3% from the previously reported 0.1%.

excerpt: Diamondback Energy raises its 2026 production outlook as disciplined spending, improving Barnett well economics and recovery technology shape its Permian strategy.
headline: FANG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Capital Discipline and Permian Growth
html_content:
Diamondback Energy, Inc. FANG emphasized capital discipline, improving well economics and long-term Permian Basin opportunities during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management outlined plans to preserve financial flexibility while evaluating future production growth.

The company reported adjusted earnings of $5.86 per share, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.92. Revenues of $5.43 billion surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.29 billion. Beyond these earnings beats, management focused on Barnett development, recovery technology and future capital allocation.

Diamondback Energy, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Diamondback Energy, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Diamondback Energy, Inc. Quote

FANG Maintains Discipline Amid Oil Price Volatility

CEO Kaes Van't Hof emphasized maintaining a low reinvestment rate while directing capital toward the company's highest-return drilling opportunities. He indicated that the full-year reinvestment rate could approach 30% based on prevailing commodity prices.

Diamondback generated approximately $2.15 billion in adjusted free cash flow during the quarter, supporting debt reduction and shareholder distributions. Management views financial flexibility as essential to navigating commodity cycles.

During the UBS analyst discussion, Van't Hof explained that capital allocation responds to market conditions. The company repurchased shares during periods of price weakness while pursuing discounted debt repurchases when bond market opportunities emerged.

Diamondback Raises 2026 Outlook but Defers 2027 Plans

Diamondback increased its 2026 oil production guidance to approximately 524,000 barrels per day from more than 522,000 previously. Total production guidance increased to approximately 1.015 million barrels of oil equivalent per day.

Full-year capital expenditure guidance rose to $3.95-$4.00 billion from approximately $3.9 billion. Fourth-quarter spending is projected at $1.00-$1.05 billion, with oil production expected between 518,000 and 528,000 barrels daily.

Responding to Stifel and RBC Capital Markets analysts, Van't Hof indicated that production growth in 2027 would require additional spending. COO Daniel Wesson highlighted potential service-cost inflation, while management deferred formal 2027 guidance until February.

FANG Sees Barnett Development Economics Improving

The Barnett formation featured prominently in discussions about future inventory productivity. Van't Hof said successful geological delineation is transitioning into full-field development, particularly around the Spanish Trail area.

Chief Engineer Albert Barkmann explained that favorable reservoir characteristics and higher pressures have supported strong initial well results. Longer laterals, shared infrastructure and drilling efficiencies remain important cost-reduction opportunities.

During discussions with Raymond James and Wolfe Research analysts, management highlighted improving development economics. Barkmann identified well costs of $850-$900 per lateral foot as an important range for competitive capital efficiency.

Diamondback Explores Gas and Power Opportunities

Management described rising natural gas demand from LNG exports and power generation as a potential long-term opportunity for Permian producers. Van't Hof emphasized securing access to downstream markets rather than pursuing aggressive gas-directed drilling.

Diamondback acquired a 7.5% equity interest in the Solitude Pipeline System. Management expects pipeline access to support commercial discussions with LNG counterparties seeking dependable natural gas supplies.

CFO Jere Thompson said the Bryant Ranch power project had secured equipment and prepared essential infrastructure, with final agreements remaining under negotiation. Van't Hof emphasized maintaining the company's operational strengths while exploring infrastructure investments.

FANG Targets Recovery Gains Through Technology

Diamondback is evaluating chemical enhanced oil recovery to increase the proportion of oil extracted from existing reservoirs. Management identified approximately 10% recovery as the current baseline.

During discussions with Texas Capital Securities and Barclays analysts, Barkmann explained that a 1-2 percentage-point recovery improvement could add 50,000-100,000 barrels per well. Van't Hof indicated that $50-$100 million could support ongoing testing.

Separately, Operations EVP Chad McAllaster discussed autonomous artificial lift systems and preventive maintenance.

AI-enabled optimization is reducing downtime and compression requirements, while management continues evaluating applications in subsurface analysis and completion design.

Diamondback Keeps Long-Term Flexibility Central

Management's overarching message emphasized maintaining low operating costs, prioritizing productive inventory and preserving flexibility amid changing commodity markets.

Although Diamondback remains positioned for continued operational activity, its 2027 growth ambitions depend on commodity prices, service costs and capital returns. Longer-term investments remain concentrated within the Permian Basin.

What FANG's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

Diamondback currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), reflecting favorable earnings estimate revision trends. Its Value Score of B indicates attractive valuation characteristics, while its Growth Score of A highlights favorable growth attributes.You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

The Momentum Score of C reflects a comparatively moderate momentum profile.
The company's VGM Score of A indicates a favorable combination of Value, Growth and Momentum characteristics.

A Zacks Rank #2 paired with an A-rated VGM Score is considered attractive within the Zacks framework for potential near-term performance. However, the Zacks Rank can change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest quarterly results.

excerpt: Wall Street Rallies as Midterm Election Uncertainty Eases.
headline: Wall Street Rallies as Midterm Election Uncertainty Eases
html_content:
With the long-awaited end of the U.S. midterm elections finally upon us, the uncertainty regarding their outcome is helping pre-market futures rally this morning. The blue-chip Dow is up +1013 points at this hour, the S&P 500 is +80 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq, even with its AI infrastructure now in the crosshairs of the Democratic Party, is +97 points. The small-cap Russell 2000 is also up an impressive +47 points at this hour.

Perhaps as much as the uncertainty being over, Wall Street traditionally tends to favor divided government. With big wins for Democrats in both the House (upwards of 250 members are expected to be seated in January) and Senate (a 54-seat majority, with two states still outstanding) and the Trump White House representing the GOP, the U.S. now has the epitome of divided government. (Had 60 seats somehow gone Democratic, that would have meant potential veto overrides — a much different story.)

Bond yields are mixed this morning: the 10-year and 2-year are down to +4.935% and +4.593%, respectively. The 30-year, on the other hand, has ticked up to +5.326% ahead of today’s open. Spot oil prices have cooled to $93 per barrel (/bbl) on WTI and $102/bbl on Brent crude, partly on the prospect that a Congressional makeover may put pressure on the White House to bring the Iran war to an end in the near term.

Finally, a quick look at a CNBC Voter Poll shows where the pressure points for the midterms were: among those issues voters found “crucial,” Corruption led the way: +54%, followed by Cost of Living +49%, Immigration +36%, the War in Iran +34% and AI Data Centers +23%. Young voters, age 18-29, skewed Democratic by +47 points.

ADP Private-Sector Jobs Steady at +86K

Meanwhile, “Jobs Week” continues this morning with private-sector payroll results for October from Automatic Data Processing ADP, where the headline +86K new jobs was exactly where the downwardly revised tally for September came in. This is roughly the mid-point in private-sector jobs gains since this past spring, between May’s high at +122K and August’s low +36K. Today’s result was also ahead of the consensus expectation of +75K.

Medium-sized businesses (between 50-499 employees) grew the most private-sector jobs last month: +33K. Small firms gained +28K and large companies added +24K to their workforces. By industry, Trade/Transportation/Utilities led with +39K new private-sector positions, with Education/Healthcare at +28K and Leisure/Hospitality +19K. Professional/Business Services lost -27K jobs, Mining was -8K and Information Services -2K.

Earnings Reports at a Glance: MCD, CVS & More

This morning, CVS Health CVS posted a big +29% earnings beat to $2.09 per share, though company plans to separate its healthcare business looks to be pushing shares down -4% in pre-market trading.

McDonald’s MCD outpaced estimates by +6.25% in its Q3 this morning, with shares +2% on the news. The stock is still down year-to-date, and domestic sales remain challenged.

Kraft-Heinz KHC saw a +23% earnings surprise to $0.53 per share, but pre-market trading is flat, just as the stock has been performing through 2026 thus far.

Wayfair W posted a +12% earnings beat in its Q3 results this morning, helping add +4% to its share price ahead of the bell, adding to its +10% gains year to date.

excerpt: The Zacks Foreign Bank stocks like IBN, CM and KB are expected to gain from restructuring efforts despite challenging industry trends.
headline: 3 Foreign Bank Stocks to Invest in Despite Challenging Industry Trends
html_content:
The Zacks Foreign Banks Industry faces a challenging operating environment amid divergent interest-rate trends, uneven economic growth and funding pressures. Rising deposit costs, subdued credit demand and margin compression might weigh on net interest income (NII) and profitability. Geopolitical uncertainties, trade tensions and economic weakness in certain regions could constrain lending activity and increase credit risks.

Nevertheless, ongoing restructuring initiatives, digital transformation and greater focus on fee-generating businesses are expected to support operational efficiency and revenue diversification. Against this backdrop, ICICI Bank IBN, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce CM and KB Financial Group KB remain well-positioned to navigate industry challenges.

About the Industry

The Zacks Foreign Banks Industry consists of overseas banks with operations in the United States. Since a foreign banking organization may have federal and state-chartered offices in the country, the Federal Reserve plays a major role in supervising its U.S. operations. In addition to providing a broad range of products and services to customers in the United States, these banks offer financial services to corporate clients having businesses in the country. Financial firms establish relationships with U.S. corporations operating in their home countries. Some units of foreign banks offer a broad range of wholesale and retail services, and conduct money-market transactions for their parent organizations. Some industry players are involved in developing only specialized services like wealth/asset management and investment banking.

3 Themes Impacting the Foreign Banks Industry

Divergent Interest Rate Trends to Pressure Margins: The uneven global interest-rate environment is likely to challenge foreign banks’ NII growth and margin stability in the near term. While the Federal Reserve and Bank of England have maintained relatively elevated rates, the European Central Bank has paused its tightening cycle, and the Bank of Japan continues monetary policy normalization. Despite higher rates in several economies, rising funding costs, intense deposit competition and subdued credit demand could constrain interest income growth.

Moreover, the net interest margin (NIMs) may remain under pressure amid divergent monetary policies and uneven loan repricing. In markets experiencing lower rates, declining asset yields and slower funding-cost adjustments could squeeze margins. Meanwhile, persistently elevated rates elsewhere may dampen lending activity and heighten credit risks. Although selective rate hikes and improving loan demand could offer some relief, broad-based margin expansion appears unlikely. Overall, funding pressures and uncertain credit growth could weigh on foreign banks’ near-term profitability.

Uneven Global Economic Growth to Weigh on Banks’ Prospects: The uneven pace of global economic growth is likely to remain a headwind for foreign banks’ operating performance and profitability. While the United States and select Asian markets have shown relative resilience, sluggish growth in parts of Europe, structural weaknesses in China and financial vulnerabilities in emerging economies continue to cloud the industry’s outlook. Heightened geopolitical tensions, trade-policy uncertainty, elevated debt levels and subdued business confidence could further dampen borrowing demand, restricting loan growth and revenue expansion.

Prolonged economic weakness could strain borrowers’ repayment capacity, particularly in sectors exposed to trade disruptions, high financing costs and weak consumer demand. This may increase credit costs and provisioning requirements, weighing on banks’ earnings.

Restructuring Efforts to Drive Efficiency: Global lenders continue to streamline operations by exiting non-core markets, reducing low-return businesses and reallocating capital toward higher-growth, fee-generating segments such as wealth management, transaction banking and digital platforms. These efforts are strengthening the revenue mix and improving capital efficiency while deepening client relationships. At the same time, workforce optimization, branch rationalization and technology-driven automation are supporting tighter cost control and lower cost-to-income ratios. Continued restructuring should therefore provide a lift to profitability by aligning capital, costs and resources with higher-return growth opportunities.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Dismal Prospects

The Zacks Foreign Banks Industry is an 83-stock group within the broader Zacks Finance Sector. The industry currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #157, which places it at the bottom 36% of more than 250 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates underperformance in the near term. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

The industry’s positioning in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is because of a relatively weak earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. The aggregate earnings estimate revisions show that analysts are not very optimistic regarding this group’s growth potential. Since the end of August 2026, the industry’s most recent earnings estimates for the year have been unchanged.

Despite the near-term challenges, we present a few stocks from the industry that you may want to consider for long-term gains. But before that, let us check out the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture.

Industry vs. S&P 500 & Sector

The Zacks Foreign Banks Industry has outperformed the S&P 500 and its sector in the past two years. Stocks in the industry have collectively surged 66.2%. The S&P 500 composite has rallied 33.7% and the Zacks Finance Sector has appreciated 24.3%.

2-Year Price Performance

Industry's Valuation

One may get a good sense of the industry’s relative valuation by looking at its price-to-tangible book ratio (P/TBV), which is commonly used for valuing foreign banks because of large variations in their earnings from one quarter to the next.

The industry currently has a trailing 12-month P/TBV of 2.98X. This compares with the highest level of 3.40X, the lowest level of 1.43X and the median of 1.86X over the past five years. The industry is trading at a significant discount compared with the market at large, as the trailing 12-month P/TBV for the S&P 500 composite is 10.59X, as shown in the chart below.

Price-to-Tangible Book Ratio (TTM)

As finance stocks typically have a lower P/TBV ratio, comparing foreign banks with the S&P 500 may not make sense to many investors. However, a comparison of the group’s P/TBV ratio with that of its broader sector ensures that it is trading at a decent discount. The Zacks Finance Sector’s trailing 12-month P/TBV of 6.00X and the median level of 4.93X for the same period are above the Zacks Foreign Banks Industry’s ratios.

Price-to-Tangible Book Ratio (TTM)

3 Foreign Bank Stocks to Invest In

ICICI Bank: Headquartered in Mumbai, this Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) company is one of India’s largest private-sector banks, offering diversified banking and financial services. As of Sept. 30, 2026, the bank had total assets of INR 27.25 trillion, supported by an extensive network of 7,656 branches and 12,143 ATMs/cash recycling machines.

ICICI Bank continues to strengthen its digital banking capabilities through iMobile Pay, its business banking platforms and technology-driven customer solutions. These initiatives are enhancing customer engagement, streamlining loan processing and creating cross-selling opportunities across retail and corporate banking segments.

Technology investments are supporting fee-based revenues. Platforms such as DigiEase and iLens are simplifying customer onboarding and lending processes. Non-interest income increased 14.2% year over year in the first half of fiscal 2027, extending the growth trend witnessed during fiscal 2022-2026. Continued digital adoption and expanding customer relationships are expected to support fee income growth.

ICICI Bank’s strong domestic franchise remains a key advantage, with domestic loans accounting for 92.2% of its total loan book as of September 2026. Following steady retail and rural lending growth in recent fiscal years, these loans increased 14.8% year over year in the first half of fiscal 2027. Its expanding retail deposit base and focus on stable funding should support loan growth and help mitigate funding-cost pressures amid an uncertain interest-rate environment.

Over the past six months, ICICI Bank shares have gained 15.8% on the NYSE. Earnings estimates for the current fiscal year have been revised 6.1% higher in the past 30 days.

Price & Consensus: IBN

Canadian Imperial: Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, CIBC is one of the country’s leading diversified financial institutions. The bank provides personal and business banking, commercial banking, wealth management and capital markets services across Canada, the United States and international markets. As of July 31, 2026, CIBC had total assets of C$1.18 trillion, net loans and acceptances of C$611.4 billion, and deposits of C$852.2 billion.

CIBC’s diversified operations and expanding lending franchise continue to support revenue growth. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026, total revenues increased 14.9% year over year to C$24.77 billion, while NII rose 13.1% to C$13.16 billion. Non-interest income climbed 17.1% to C$11.61 billion, benefiting from stronger trading activities, wealth management fees and capital markets performance.

The positive momentum continued in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, with revenues increasing 15% year over year to C$8.37 billion. Reported net income rose 15% to C$2.41 billion, while adjusted net income jumped 26% to C$2.65 billion. The net interest margin improved to 1.63% from 1.58% a year earlier, reflecting stronger loan and deposit margins. Continued investments in technology and digital banking capabilities should further support operating efficiency and customer engagement.

CIBC’s expanding balance sheet and solid capitalization provide financial flexibility. As of July 2026, deposits increased 5.5% from October 2025, while net loans and acceptances grew 3.7%. The bank maintained a Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 13.4%, reflecting a sound capital position. Although elevated credit costs, economic uncertainty and higher technology-related expenses remain concerning, diversified revenues, steady lending growth and a strong funding base should support its long-term profitability.

CM shares have gained 5.8% on the NYSE in the past six months. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company’s current fiscal-year earnings has been unchanged in the past 30 days. The company carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Price & Consensus: CM

KB Financial: Headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, KB Financial is one of the country’s largest financial holding companies by consolidated assets. Established in 2008, the group operates a diversified financial-services business through KB Kookmin Bank and subsidiaries spanning securities, credit cards, insurance, asset management, consumer finance and other financial services.

KB Financial’s diversified business model continues to support earnings growth beyond traditional lending operations. In 2025, group NII increased 1.9% year over year to 13.07 trillion Korean won, while net fee and commission income rose 6.4% to 4.10 trillion Korean won, reflecting improving contributions from securities and other fee-generating businesses.

The momentum continued in the first nine months of 2026, with net profit attributable to shareholders rising 13.1% year over year to 5.79 trillion Korean won. Group NII increased 2.9% to 9.99 trillion Korean won, while net non-interest income rose 27.3% to 4.76 trillion Korean won. Net fee and commission income jumped 38.5% to 4.09 trillion Korean won, supported by robust securities-related fees and investment product sales.

Non-banking businesses contributed approximately 40% to cumulative net profit, highlighting KB Financial’s diversified earnings base. However, third-quarter net profit declined 4.3% sequentially to 1.91 trillion Korean won amid weaker fee income. Despite near-term margin and market-related pressures, its expanding non-interest income streams, disciplined cost management and balanced business portfolio are expected to support profitability.

Currently, KB Financial sports a Zacks Rank of 1. Its shares have gained 1.8% on the NYSE in the past six months. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company’s 2026 earnings has been revised 8.2% higher in the past 30 days. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Price & Consensus: KB

excerpt: Steel demand hasn't been this strong in three decades, and this mill is cashing in.
headline: Bull of the Day: Nucor (NUE)
html_content:
Nucor (NUE) , is a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and the largest U.S. steel producer, operating scrap-fed electric arc furnace mills nationwide.

The company topped Q3 estimates on record shipments and a sharp pricing rebound, driving shares to all-time highs. With the CEO calling demand the strongest in 31 years, the outlook remains bullish.

About the Company

Based in Charlotte, North Carolina, Nucor operates through three segments. Steel mills are its earnings engine, while steel products include joists, decking, rebar fabrication and building systems. Raw materials cover scrap recycling and direct reduced iron.

The company is valued at $62 billion and has a Forward PE of 12. The stock has Zacks Style Scores of “C” in Value, “B” in Growth, and “B” in Momentum. Nucor has paid 214 consecutive quarterly dividends, with its current $0.56 payout scheduled for November 10.

Earnings Beat

Nucor delivered a strong third quarter, with EPS of $5.80 topping estimates and more than doubling year over year. Revenue reached $11.25 billion, while adjusted EBITDA climbed to $2.28 billion. Mill utilization was 89%, reflecting strong production levels.

The downstream steel products business was the standout, as pricing finally caught up with higher input costs. Segment pricing rose 7% sequentially, expanding EBITDA margins by approximately 200 basis points.

Management expects fourth quarter earnings to be in line with or modestly above Q3, as higher pricing offsets fewer shipping days and planned outages. Full-year steel mill shipment growth is now expected toward the upper end of its 5% to 10% range, with the CEO anticipating a financially stronger 2027.

Demand remains broad-based across heavy equipment, energy, manufacturing, defense and digital infrastructure. Automotive sheet shipments are up 4% despite flat North American vehicle production, while a new GM SUV contract marks a win in a market traditionally dominated by integrated mills.

Nucor Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Nucor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Nucor Corporation Quote

Growth Projects Ramping

Nucor's West Virginia sheet mill remains on time and budget, with first coils expected by December and utilization targeting 50% by year-end 2027. Its new 500,000-ton automotive galvanizing line in Berkeley began production in October, targeting 50% utilization by Q2 2027 and full run rate by year-end.

The company generated $2.7 billion in free cash flow through the first nine months and returned nearly $1.4 billion to shareholders. Capital spending should fall from roughly $2.5 billion in 2026, supporting stronger cash generation in 2027.

Nucor targets returning at least 40% of net earnings to shareholders and will return excess cash when attractive growth opportunities are unavailable.

Estimates Are Rising

Analysts earnings estimates are going higher across the board.

For the current quarter, estimates have been taken from $4.52 to $5.62 over the last 90 days. That’s a jump of 24%.

For the current year, we see a move of 10% higher over that same time frame, with numbers going from $17.86 to $19.61. And the momentum continues for next year, with estimates up 16% over the last 90 days.

Price targets are going higher as well, with Wells Fargo hiking to $305, Barclays to $320 and JP Morgan at $304. Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating, lifting its price target to $335 from $302.

The Technical Take

Since March, the stock has been very strong moving from the $160 area to an all-time high of $287 this week. Investors will now look if there is follow through higher or if a pullback is warranted.

For those looking for entries into the name, let’s look at those moving averages:

21-day: $261

50-day: $256

200-day: $225

In Summary

Nucor has a powerful combination of catalysts: record shipments, expanding downstream margins, major growth projects coming online and strong demand across data centers, infrastructure and manufacturing.

With capital spending set to decline,free cash flow poised to climb and the CEO expecting an even stronger 2027, this Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) steel leader has plenty of room to keep building on its momentum.

AI’s second wave is moving from infrastructure to implementation and these companies are at the forefront of this transition, positioned to become what Amazon and Google were to the internet era.
