excerpt: Aflac, Unum, Globe Life, Trupanion and Employers Holdings face medical cost inflation and pricing pressure, but rising demand for supplemental coverage offers growth opportunities.
headline: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Aflac, Unum, Globe, Trupanion and Employers
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 6, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Aflac Inc. AFL, Unum Group UNM, Globe Life GL, Trupanion TRUP and Employers Holdings, Inc. EIG.

Industry: Accident & Health Insurance

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3024755/5-accident-health-insurers-to-watch-despite-cost-pressure

TheZacks Accident and Health Insurance industry is expected to benefit from an increase in underwriting exposure. Aflac Inc., Unum Group, Globe Life, Trupanion and Employers Holdings, Inc. are likely to gain from increasing demand for group insurance and prudent underwriting standards. However, higher inflation and rising medical costs could offset the positives. The industry has been witnessing soft pricing over the past several quarters, and this is not expected to change anytime soon. The increasing adoption of technology in operations will help the industry function smoothly. The industry is witnessing a rise in demand for embedded insurance and supplemental health products.

Per a CBIZ report, the industry has maintained its profitability streak, reflecting solid reserves, prudent claims management, stable loss trends and fewer claims. 

About the Industry

The Zacks Accident and Health (A&H) insurance industry comprises companies providing workers' compensation insurance, mainly to employers operating in hazardous industries. Insurers provide group, individual and voluntary supplemental products, including employer-funded workers' compensation that protects employees without reducing their pay. Claims are covered by insurers or state funds. Such coverage supports employee morale and productivity while reducing employers' claim costs. Growing awareness of these benefits strengthens the industry's outlook. Per Business Research Insight, the A&H Insurance market, worth about $323.24 billion in 2026, is projected to expand to about $452.53 billion by 2035—reflecting a CAGR of about 3.8%.

5 Trends Shaping the Future of the Accident & Health Insurance Industry

Pricing Pressure to Continue: Pricing pressure continues to weigh on the U.S. Accident & Health insurance industry. Rising medical expenses, elevated claims frequency and increased healthcare utilization are compelling insurers to raise premiums to preserve underwriting margins. However, intense competition, particularly in employer-sponsored and voluntary benefits markets, limits insurers from doing the same. SpendEdge projects workers' compensation pricing to increase at a 3%-5%  CAGR between 2022 and 2026, while CBIZ forecasts a more modest 2% rise.

Persistent Medical Inflation: Medical inflation remains a major challenge for Accident & Health insurers. Aon projects global medical costs to rise by approximately 9.8% in 2026, outpacing general inflation in many markets. Higher hospital wages, diagnostic expenses, provider fees, healthcare utilization, and costly medicines are driving this increase. The resulting pressure extends beyond claims costs, forcing insurers to balance profitability with adequate benefits and affordable premiums—without weakening coverage or limiting customers' access to essential healthcare.

Growing Demand for Supplemental Health Insurance: Demand for supplemental health insurance is gaining traction as consumers seek greater financial protection against rising medical expenses. Per LIMRA, workplace supplemental health insurance new annualized premiums rose 7% year over year to more than $2.1 billion in the first half of 2026. Hospital indemnity premiums increased 14%, followed by critical illness (up 6%) and accident insurance premiums (up 2%), creating growth opportunities for insurers.

Mixed Claims Frequency Trends: The Accident & Health insurance industry is witnessing mixed claims trends. Improved workplace safety and effective risk management have reduced accident-related claims, while rising healthcare utilization and costly medical claims remain concerns. Per the National Council on Compensation Insurance, lost-time workers' compensation claim frequency declined 2% in 2025, compared with a 5% drop in 2024. However, increasing medical claim severity is offsetting the benefits of lower claim frequency, highlighting the need for prudent underwriting and effective claims management to sustain profitability.

Increasing Adoption of Technology:The insurance industry is increasingly adopting AI, data analytics, automation, cloud computing and blockchain to improve operational efficiency and competitiveness. Telemedicine is gaining traction, helping insurers contain costs, while machine learning and predictive analytics enhance risk assessment. Policies are also increasingly incorporating telehealth services. Per CBIZ, AI could reduce workers' compensation claim expenses by approximately 45%. However, higher technology investments may pressure expense ratios.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bleak Prospects

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. The Zacks Accident and Health Insurance industry, housed within the broader Zacks Finance sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #196, which places it in the bottom 21% of the 247 Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

The industry's position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are gradually losing confidence in this group's earnings growth potential.  Current year estimates have declined 3.9% in a year.

Before we present a few stocks one can have in their portfolio, given their business advancement endeavors, it's worth taking a look at the industry's performance and current valuation.

Industry Versus Sector and S&P 500

The Accident and Health Insurance industry has outperformed its sector and the Zacks S&P 500 composite year to date. The stocks in this industry have collectively gained 12.2% year to date compared with the Finance sector's increase of 3.6% and the Zacks S&P 500 composite's rise of 3.6% over the same period.

Current Valuation

On the basis of a trailing 12-month price-to-book (P/B), commonly used for valuing insurance stocks, the industry is currently trading at 1.75X compared with the Zacks S&P 500 composite's 7.09X and the sector's 4.5X.

Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 2.14X, as low as 1X and at the median of 1.76X.

5 Accident & Health Insurance Stocks in Focus

We are presenting five Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) stocks from the Zacks Accident and Health Insurance industry. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. 

Aflac: This Columbus, GA-based company offers voluntary supplemental health and life insurance products and operates through Aflac Japan and Aflac U.S. The top line benefits from strategic growth investments, robust persistency rates and enhanced productivity. Aflac introduces products and upgrades existing ones to address the changing needs of its customers, as well as integrates digital solutions into its offerings to align with the ongoing trend of digitization. This, in turn, should support its profit margins. The Argus buyout will provide it with a platform to build the company's network of dental and vision products and further strengthen its U.S. segment. 

AFL delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 6.56% on average. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 implies a year-over-year decrease of 6%. The consensus estimate for 2027 earnings implies a 9.4% year-over-year increase and has moved north 5 cents in the past 30 days.  The expected long-term earnings growth rate is pegged at 9%.

Unum Group: Chattanooga, TN-based Unum Group provides long-term care insurance, life insurance, employer- and employee-paid group benefits and related services. This insurer is poised to grow on the operational excellence of Unum U.S. and Colonial Life. Encouraging sales trends, strong persistency in group lines and growth of new product lines like dental and vision, coupled with favorable risk results, should benefit Unum U.S. and Colonial Life, the two largest operating segments. The company has an impressive dividend track record, having increased dividends 17 times in the last 16 years and yielding better than the industry average. It estimates a 10-15% increase in dividends going forward.

For 2026, UNM expects adjusted operating income per share to be between $8.30 and $8.50.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 implies a year-over-year increase of 6.3% and 9.1%, respectively. The consensus estimate for 2027 earnings has moved 2 cents north in the past 30 days.  The expected long-term earnings growth rate is pegged at 11.9%.

Globe Life: Based in McKinney, TX, Globe Life is an insurance holding company providing individual life and supplemental health insurance to lower-middle to middle-income households throughout the United States. This insurer has been witnessing a positive trend in revenues, driven by premium growth in its Life Insurance and Health Insurance segments and net investment income.

The strong performance of the American Income and Liberty National divisions should drive the top line in the future. Liberty National is likely to continue to benefit from improved productivity and agent count. GL's expansion initiatives to capture heavily populated and less penetrated areas should drive growth in the future. Net life sales, as well as net health sales, are expected to grow in the mid-teens for Liberty National.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings indicates a 6.6% and 5.8% year-over-year increase, respectively. The consensus estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings has moved down 1.5% and 0.8%, respectively, in the past 30 days.

Trupanion: Headquartered in Seattle, WA, Trupanion is a provider of insurance for cats and dogs in the United States, Canada, Continental Europe and Australia. It operates in a total addressable market worth more than $40 billion, which is a large but underpenetrated market.
 
This pet insurer is well-poised to grow, courtesy of its heightened focus on pets' health and well-being in an underpenetrated pet insurance market, product launches, extended operating boundaries and a solid capital position. This pet insurer continues to invest in areas where it believes it can achieve high internal rates of return. Improving pricing should add to its upside.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 suggests a 40% and a 10.9% increase, respectively, on a year-over-year basis. TRUP delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 53.03%, on average. It has a Growth Score of A.  The consensus estimates for 2026 and 2027 earnings witnessed no movement in the past 30 days.  The expected long-term earnings growth rate is pegged at 26.5%.

Employers Holdings: Based in Henderson, NV, Employers Holdings is the 19th largest provider of workers' compensation insurance to small businesses in the low-to-medium hazard industries. EIG should continue to benefit from a solid presence in attractive markets and prudent underwriting. Its multiple distribution channels provide competitive advantages. 

The consensus estimate for 2026 earnings suggests a 145.2% increase, but that for 2027 suggests a 0.7% decrease on a year-over-year basis. The consensus estimate for 2026 earnings has moved 5 cents north but that for 2027 earnings has moved 6 cents south in the past 30 days. Employers Holdings delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 21.28%, on average.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

Industry: Accident & Health Insurance Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3024755/5-accident-health-insurers-to-watch-despite-cost-pressure TheZacks Accident and Health Insurance industry is expected to benefit from an increase in underwriting exposure. Aflac Inc., Unum Group, Globe Life, Trupanion and Employers Holdings, Inc. are likely to gain from increasing demand for group insurance and prudent underwriting standards. However, higher inflation and rising medical costs could offset the positives. The industry has been witnessing soft pricing over the past several quarters, and this is not expected to change anytime soon. The increasing adoption of technology in operations will help the industry function smoothly. The industry is witnessing a rise in demand for embedded insurance and supplemental health products. Per a CBIZ report, the industry has maintained its profitability streak, reflecting solid reserves, prudent claims management, stable loss trends and fewer claims. About the Industry The Zacks Accident and Health (A&H) insurance industry comprises companies providing workers' compensation insurance, mainly to employers operating in hazardous industries. Insurers provide group, individual and voluntary supplemental products, including employer-funded workers' compensation that protects employees without reducing their pay. Claims are covered by insurers or state funds. Such coverage supports employee morale and productivity while reducing employers' claim costs. Growing awareness of these benefits strengthens the industry's outlook. Per Business Research Insight, the A&H Insurance market, worth about $323.24 billion in 2026, is projected to expand to about $452.53 billion by 2035—reflecting a CAGR of about 3.8%. 5 Trends Shaping the Future of the Accident & Health Insurance Industry Pricing Pressure to Continue: Pricing pressure continues to weigh on the U.S. Accident & Health insurance industry. Rising medical expenses, elevated claims frequency and increased healthcare utilization are compelling insurers to raise premiums to preserve underwriting margins. However, intense competition, particularly in employer-sponsored and voluntary benefits markets, limits insurers from doing the same. SpendEdge projects workers' compensation pricing to increase at a 3%-5% CAGR between 2022 and 2026, while CBIZ forecasts a more modest 2% rise. Persistent Medical Inflation: Medical inflation remains a major challenge for Accident & Health insurers. Aon projects global medical costs to rise by approximately 9.8% in 2026, outpacing general inflation in many markets. Higher hospital wages, diagnostic expenses, provider fees, healthcare utilization, and costly medicines are driving this increase. The resulting pressure extends beyond claims costs, forcing insurers to balance profitability with adequate benefits and affordable premiums—without weakening coverage or limiting customers' access to essential healthcare. Growing Demand for Supplemental Health Insurance: Demand for supplemental health insurance is gaining traction as consumers seek greater financial protection against rising medical expenses. Per LIMRA, workplace supplemental health insurance new annualized premiums rose 7% year over year to more than $2.1 billion in the first half of 2026. Hospital indemnity premiums increased 14%, followed by critical illness (up 6%) and accident insurance premiums (up 2%), creating growth opportunities for insurers. Mixed Claims Frequency Trends: The Accident & Health insurance industry is witnessing mixed claims trends. Improved workplace safety and effective risk management have reduced accident-related claims, while rising healthcare utilization and costly medical claims remain concerns. Per the National Council on Compensation Insurance, lost-time workers' compensation claim frequency declined 2% in 2025, compared with a 5% drop in 2024. However, increasing medical claim severity is offsetting the benefits of lower claim frequency, highlighting the need for prudent underwriting and effective claims management to sustain profitability. Increasing Adoption of Technology:The insurance industry is increasingly adopting AI, data analytics, automation, cloud computing and blockchain to improve operational efficiency and competitiveness. Telemedicine is gaining traction, helping insurers contain costs, while machine learning and predictive analytics enhance risk assessment. Policies are also increasingly incorporating telehealth services. Per CBIZ, AI could reduce workers' compensation claim expenses by approximately 45%. However, higher technology investments may pressure expense ratios. Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bleak Prospects The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. The Zacks Accident and Health Insurance industry, housed within the broader Zacks Finance sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #196, which places it in the bottom 21% of the 247 Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1. The industry's position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are gradually losing confidence in this group's earnings growth potential. Current year estimates have declined 3.9% in a year. Before we present a few stocks one can have in their portfolio, given their business advancement endeavors, it's worth taking a look at the industry's performance and current valuation. Industry Versus Sector and S&P 500 The Accident and Health Insurance industry has outperformed its sector and the Zacks S&P 500 composite year to date. The stocks in this industry have collectively gained 12.2% year to date compared with the Finance sector's increase of 3.6% and the Zacks S&P 500 composite's rise of 3.6% over the same period. Current Valuation On the basis of a trailing 12-month price-to-book (P/B), commonly used for valuing insurance stocks, the industry is currently trading at 1.75X compared with the Zacks S&P 500 composite's 7.09X and the sector's 4.5X. Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 2.14X, as low as 1X and at the median of 1.76X. 5 Accident & Health Insurance Stocks in Focus We are presenting five Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) stocks from the Zacks Accident and Health Insurance industry. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. Aflac: This Columbus, GA-based company offers voluntary supplemental health and life insurance products and operates through Aflac Japan and Aflac U.S. The top line benefits from strategic growth investments, robust persistency rates and enhanced productivity. Aflac introduces products and upgrades existing ones to address the changing needs of its customers, as well as integrates digital solutions into its offerings to align with the ongoing trend of digitization. This, in turn, should support its profit margins. The Argus buyout will provide it with a platform to build the company's network of dental and vision products and further strengthen its U.S. segment. AFL delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 6.56% on average. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 implies a year-over-year decrease of 6%. The consensus estimate for 2027 earnings implies a 9.4% year-over-year increase and has moved north 5 cents in the past 30 days. The expected long-term earnings growth rate is pegged at 9%. Unum Group: Chattanooga, TN-based Unum Group provides long-term care insurance, life insurance, employer- and employee-paid group benefits and related services. This insurer is poised to grow on the operational excellence of Unum U.S. and Colonial Life. Encouraging sales trends, strong persistency in group lines and growth of new product lines like dental and vision, coupled with favorable risk results, should benefit Unum U.S. and Colonial Life, the two largest operating segments. The company has an impressive dividend track record, having increased dividends 17 times in the last 16 years and yielding better than the industry average. It estimates a 10-15% increase in dividends going forward. For 2026, UNM expects adjusted operating income per share to be between $8.30 and $8.50. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 implies a year-over-year increase of 6.3% and 9.1%, respectively. The consensus estimate for 2027 earnings has moved 2 cents north in the past 30 days. The expected long-term earnings growth rate is pegged at 11.9%. Globe Life: Based in McKinney, TX, Globe Life is an insurance holding company providing individual life and supplemental health insurance to lower-middle to middle-income households throughout the United States. This insurer has been witnessing a positive trend in revenues, driven by premium growth in its Life Insurance and Health Insurance segments and net investment income. The strong performance of the American Income and Liberty National divisions should drive the top line in the future. Liberty National is likely to continue to benefit from improved productivity and agent count. GL's expansion initiatives to capture heavily populated and less penetrated areas should drive growth in the future. Net life sales, as well as net health sales, are expected to grow in the mid-teens for Liberty National. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings indicates a 6.6% and 5.8% year-over-year increase, respectively. The consensus estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings has moved down 1.5% and 0.8%, respectively, in the past 30 days. Trupanion: Headquartered in Seattle, WA, Trupanion is a provider of insurance for cats and dogs in the United States, Canada, Continental Europe and Australia. It operates in a total addressable market worth more than $40 billion, which is a large but underpenetrated market. This pet insurer is well-poised to grow, courtesy of its heightened focus on pets' health and well-being in an underpenetrated pet insurance market, product launches, extended operating boundaries and a solid capital position. This pet insurer continues to invest in areas where it believes it can achieve high internal rates of return. Improving pricing should add to its upside. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 suggests a 40% and a 10.9% increase, respectively, on a year-over-year basis. TRUP delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 53.03%, on average. It has a Growth Score of A. The consensus estimates for 2026 and 2027 earnings witnessed no movement in the past 30 days. The expected long-term earnings growth rate is pegged at 26.5%. Employers Holdings: Based in Henderson, NV, Employers Holdings is the 19th largest provider of workers' compensation insurance to small businesses in the low-to-medium hazard industries. EIG should continue to benefit from a solid presence in attractive markets and prudent underwriting. Its multiple distribution channels provide competitive advantages. The consensus estimate for 2026 earnings suggests a 145.2% increase, but that for 2027 suggests a 0.7% decrease on a year-over-year basis. The consensus estimate for 2026 earnings has moved 5 cents north but that for 2027 earnings has moved 6 cents south in the past 30 days. Employers Holdings delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 21.28%, on average. excerpt: Applied Digital Corporation (APLD) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Why Is Applied Digital Corporation (APLD) Down 40.6% Since Last Earnings Report?
html_content:
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Applied Digital Corporation (APLD). Shares have lost about 40.6% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

But investors have to be wondering, will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Applied Digital Corporation due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Applied Digital Corporation before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

Applied Digital Q1 Earnings Miss on Higher Costs, Revenues Beat

Applied Digital Corporation reported a first-quarter fiscal 2027 loss from continuing operations of 76 cents per share, wider than the 7-cent loss a year ago. The figure missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of a 26-cent loss by 192.3%, as higher operating costs, interest expense and fair-value losses pressured results.

Revenues rose 322% year over year to $341.9 million, beating the $134 million consensus by 154.95%. High-performance computing (HPC) tenant fit-out services and new rental revenue led growth. APLD had 1.41 GW of critical IT load under lease across five campuses, representing $36 billion of base-term contracted revenues.

APLD's Q1 HPC Hosting Powers Revenue Growth

The HPC Hosting Business generated $262.6 million in revenues, including $183.5 million from tenant fit-out services, $65.8 million of base rent and $13.3 million from tenant recoveries. Segment operating profit was $33.4 million for the quarter.

Phase 1 of Building 2 at Polaris Forge 1, representing 75 MW, became ready for service on July 1, lifting live capacity at the campus to 175 MW. A second 75 MW phase became ready on Oct. 1, after quarter-end, taking live capacity to 250 MW.

Applied Digital's Q1 Hosting Business Holds Steady

The Data Center Hosting Business generated $37.8 million in revenues compared with $37.9 million a year earlier. The 106 MW Jamestown facility and 180 MW Ellendale facility were operating at full capacity as of Aug. 31.

Segment operating profit rose 121% year over year to $13.3 million, primarily reflecting lower cost of revenues from more advantageous power pricing. Reported assets for the business totaled $111.9 million at quarter-end.

APLD's Q1 Cost Base Weighs on Profitability

Services cost of revenues increased 318% year over year to $245.7 million, mainly due to higher tenant fit-out expenses and ChronoScale GPU hardware costs. Data center rental and other cost of revenues totaled $43.9 million, including $22.4 million of depreciation and amortization and $13.3 million of reimbursable tenant recovery expenses.

Selling, general and administrative expenses climbed 289% to $114.7 million. The increase reflected $51.7 million of higher stock-based compensation, $12.1 million of additional professional service expense and $9.9 million of higher personnel costs.

Interest expense surged 866% to $77.4 million, while interest income rose to $35.8 million. APLD also recorded a $49.5 million loss on the change in fair value of derivatives and an $11.4 million loss on the change in fair value of its Babcock & Wilcox investment.

Applied Digital's Adjusted Results Strengthen

Adjusted revenues, which exclude ChronoScale, rose to $300.4 million from $64.2 million. Adjusted operating income was $37.8 million compared with an adjusted operating loss of $3.6 million a year ago, while adjusted operating margin improved to 13% from negative 6%.

Adjusted net loss from continuing operations narrowed to $4.1 million, or 1 cent per share, from $7.6 million, or 3 cents. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $64.4 million from $0.5 million, while net operating income was $58.8 million with an 89% margin.

APLD's Balance Sheet and Cash Flows

Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $3.7 billion as of Aug. 31, while debt stood at $6.4 billion. 

Operating activities provided $63.9 million of cash compared with $81.5 million used a year ago.

Investing activities used $2.08 billion, largely reflecting $2.07 billion of purchases of property, equipment and other assets. Financing activities provided $1.54 billion, supported by long-term debt borrowings and preferred stock issuance during the quarter.

Applied Digital's Expansion Pipeline Advances

APLD closed $1.59 billion of 7% senior secured notes due 2031 to fund construction of the third 150 MW HPC building at Polaris Forge 1 and repay the $300 million bridge facility. The company also expanded revolving commitments to $430 million during the quarter.

Subsequent to quarter-end, Applied Digital secured up to approximately 1 GW of potential power capacity in Finland and entered a power purchase agreement with Base Electron for capacity and energy from an approximately 1,200 MW natural gas-fired generation facility planned in North Dakota.

Management expects initial Polaris Forge 2 operations to lift the delivered critical IT load across its North Dakota campuses to 300 MW by the end of calendar 2026.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

Since the earnings release, investors have witnessed a downward trend in estimates review.

The consensus estimate has shifted -44.13% due to these changes.

VGM Scores

At this time, Applied Digital Corporation has a nice Growth Score of B, a grade with the same score on the momentum front. However, the stock was allocated a score of F on the value side, putting it in the fifth quintile for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of F. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending downward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions indicates a downward shift. It's no surprise Applied Digital Corporation has a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell). We expect a below average return from the stock in the next few months.

Performance of an Industry Player

Applied Digital Corporation is part of the Zacks Financial - Miscellaneous Services industry. Over the past month, Jefferies (JEF), a stock from the same industry, has gained 9.5%. The company reported its results for the quarter ended August 2026 more than a month ago.

Jefferies reported revenues of $2.22 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +8.5%. EPS of $1.09 for the same period compares with $1.05 a year ago.

For the current quarter, Jefferies is expected to post earnings of $0.95 per share, indicating a change of -1% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

Jefferies has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) based on the overall direction and magnitude of estimate revisions. Additionally, the stock has a VGM Score of A.

excerpt: Does Assurant (AIZ) have what it takes to be a top stock pick for momentum investors? Let's find out.
headline: Are You Looking for a Top Momentum Pick? Why Assurant (AIZ) is a Great Choice
html_content:
Momentum investing revolves around the idea of following a stock's recent trend in either direction. In "long context," investors will be essentially be "buying high, but hoping to sell even higher." With this methodology, taking advantage of trends in a stock's price is key; once a stock establishes a course, it is more than likely to continue moving that way. The goal is that once a stock heads down a fixed path, it will lead to timely and profitable trades.

While many investors like to look for momentum in stocks, this can be very tough to define. There is a lot of debate surrounding which metrics are the best to focus on and which are poor quality indicators of future performance. The Zacks Momentum Style Score, part of the Zacks Style Scores, helps address this issue for us.

Below, we take a look at Assurant (AIZ), which currently has a Momentum Style Score of B. We also discuss some of the main drivers of the Momentum Style Score, like price change and earnings estimate revisions.

It's also important to note that Style Scores work as a complement to the Zacks Rank, our stock rating system that has an impressive track record of outperformance. Assurant currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy). Our research shows that stocks rated Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and #2 (Buy) and Style Scores of "A or B" outperform the market over the following one-month period.

You can see the current list of Zacks #1 Rank Stocks here >>>

Set to Beat the Market?

Let's discuss some of the components of the Momentum Style Score for AIZ that show why this insurer shows promise as a solid momentum pick.

Looking at a stock's short-term price activity is a great way to gauge if it has momentum, since this can reflect both the current interest in a stock and if buyers or sellers have the upper hand at the moment. It is also useful to compare a security to its industry, as this can help investors pinpoint the top companies in a particular area.

For AIZ, shares are up 2.83% over the past week while the Zacks Insurance - Multi line industry is up 0.32% over the same time period. Shares are looking quite well from a longer time frame too, as the monthly price change of 12.46% compares favorably with the industry's 4.99% performance as well.

While any stock can see a spike in price, it takes a real winner to consistently outperform the market. Over the past quarter, shares of Assurant have risen 9.24%, and are up 41.54% in the last year. In comparison, the S&P 500 has only moved -4.52% and 9.35%, respectively.

Investors should also take note of AIZ's average 20-day trading volume. Volume is a useful item in many ways, and the 20-day average establishes a good price-to-volume baseline; a rising stock with above average volume is generally a bullish sign, whereas a declining stock on above average volume is typically bearish. Right now AIZ is averaging 386,538 shares for the last 20 days..

Earnings Outlook

The Zacks Momentum Style Score also takes into account trends in estimate revisions, in addition to price changes. Please note that estimate revision trends remain at the core of Zacks Rank as well. A nice path here can help show promise, and we have recently been seeing that with AIZ.

Over the past two months, 2 earnings estimates moved higher compared to none lower for the full year. These revisions helped boost AIZ's consensus estimate, increasing from $22.05 to $22.40 in the past 60 days. Looking at the next fiscal year, 3 estimates have moved upwards while there have been no downward revisions in the same time period.

Bottom Line

excerpt: Inflation, politics and AI concerns are all posing big challenges to investors right now, but Andrew Rocco believes the market will push past these hurdles in the coming months. Learn why the recent selloffs could be setting up the next leg higher.
headline: Q4 QQQ Roadmap: Navigating AI Turbulence & Market Headwinds
html_content:
Let’s look at what’s actually happening with the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) as we wrap up 2026.

If you step back and look at the big picture, three clear takeaways stand out:

1) The market is still climbing a massive wall of worry. If someone had told you earlier this year where oil prices and interest rates would end up, you probably wouldn’t have believed the market could hold up this well. 

2) AI is carrying the entire narrative. Right now, the economy and the stock market are practically glued to AI. The moment investors worry that data center or infrastructure spending might slow down, tech stocks take an immediate hit.

3) The broad indices don't tell the full story. Serious rotation is happening under the hood. 

From Market Savior to "Tech Destruction" 

Remember last year when everyone complained that big tech was single-handedly dragging the rest of the market up? The script has flipped. QQQ just logged its worst three-day drop since "Liberation Day." In fact, Morgan Stanley noted that U.S. tech momentum recently hit levels worse than during the dot-com bust.

So, what’s holding equities back right now? It boils down to four main worries:

• Inflation and stubborn interest rates

• Political headwinds surrounding AI

• Debt and funding fears in AI infrastructure

• Pure technical gravity and profit-taking

Here is why there's good reason to believe the market will push past these hurdles in the coming months.

Inflation & Interest Rates

Recent energy spikes reignited inflation fears and pushed yields higher, but geopolitical energy shocks are usually short-lived. We’ve already seen oil cool off following reports of potential progress on a U.S.–Iran agreement.

On the rate front, market projections lean toward 3 to 4 quarter-point hikes extending into mid-to-late 2027. But as the team at BlueKurtic Market Insights pointed out, stocks can actually perform quite well during rate-hiking cycles—provided the pace is steady.

This looks more like a limited, non-cyclical adjustment (likely capping out at 2 to 3 hikes) rather than an aggressive tightening regime. The last time we saw a similar non-cyclical adjustment was in 1997, and the S&P 500 went on to gain 40% over the following year.

Politics & the Midterm Effect: Why Gridlock is Good

AI buildouts have run into public pushback—a recent Reuters poll showed only about a third of Americans approve of the current rapid pace of data-center construction. Markets have also been trying to price in the political "Blue Wave," which added fuel to the tech sell-off over fears of tighter regulation.

However, markets are forward-looking mechanisms. This setup is shaping up to be a classic "sell the rumor, buy the news" event.

Historically, a divided government is actually great for stocks—divided setups typically deliver higher average returns than when one party controls both Congress and the White House. On top of that, midterm seasonality is heavily on our side: the S&P 500 has finished higher six months after every single midterm election since 1950. That’s 19 straight elections with an average gain of nearly 15%, regardless of who won.

AI Debt & Funding Fears

Fears spiked in October when CoreWeave (CRWV) saw its bond yields jump to distressed levels, causing its stock to tumble. The market briefly priced CRWV as if bankruptcy were imminent—at one point in September, Polymarket showed a 50% chance of a 2027 bankruptcy.

Today? That probability has plummeted to just 12%. The extreme solvency fears were largely overblown.

Technical Gravity & Necessary Reset 

Earlier this year, several AI stocks simply went too far, too fast.

Take SanDisk (SNDK): it blew way past its Fibonacci extensions, surged 4,000% in a single year, and stretched 264% above its 200-day moving average. Anything more than 200% above that trendline is extreme. Think of the 200-day moving average as a rubber band—stretch it too far, and it inevitably snaps back.

Even the strongest market leaders need to reset. What we’re seeing right now across names like Marvell (MRVL), Arm Holdings (ARM), and Micron (MU) is a standard pullback to test those major moving averages. Historically, that first test of a rising 200-day line offers one of the best risk-reward entry points you can ask for. 

Bottom Line 

While scary headlines around AI leverage, rates, and politics caused a sharp pull-back, the underlying technical frame of this market remains healthy. Extended tech leaders are flushing out excess leverage and returning to key support levels. Combined with favorable post-midterm seasonality and the benefits of political gridlock, this reset looks less like the end of the run and more like a setup for the next leg higher.

Top Market Moves to Watch Right Now

One of the market's strongest trends is the tech sector's resurgence. It's no surprise that the rapid expansion of Artificial Intelligence is driving much of the sector's momentum.

This trend could be highly lucrative for both short-term traders and long-term investors, even as the market reaches record highs.

And we're expecting more outsized gains in the months ahead.

In fact, I'm about to add a stock to the portfolio that has exceptional upside.

But one of our top analysts found one that works behind the scenes, designing key components that help AI systems run at full speed. headline: Should iShares Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF (ISCV) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
Launched on June 28, 2004, the iShares Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF (ISCV) is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to provide a broad exposure to the Small Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

The fund is sponsored by Blackrock. It has amassed assets over $687.37 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs attempting to match the Small Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Why Small Cap Value

Small cap companies have market capitalization below $2 billion. They usually have higher potential than large and mid cap companies with stocks but higher risk.

Value stocks are known for their lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, but investors should also note their lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. While value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in nearly all markets when you consider long-term performance, growth stocks are more likely to outpace value stocks in strong bull markets.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.06%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.92%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure that minimizes single stock risk, investors should also look at the actual holdings inside the fund. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Financials sector -- about 24.3% of the portfolio. Consumer Discretionary and Industrials round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Best Buy (BBY) accounts for about 0.58% of total assets, followed by Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) and Hf Sinclair (DINO).

Performance and Risk

ISCV seeks to match the performance of the MORNINGSTAR US SML CP BRD VLUE EXTD INDX before fees and expenses. The Morningstar US Small Cap Broad Value Extended Index comprises of small-capitalization U.S. equities that exhibit value characteristics.

The ETF has added about 15.19% so far this year and it's up approximately 21.25% in the last one year (as of 11/09/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $63.71 and $81.79.

The ETF has a beta of 1.02 and standard deviation of 18.68% for the trailing three-year period. With about 1048 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

iShares Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, ISCV is a great option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Small Cap Value segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The iShares Russell 2000 Value ETF (IWN) and the Vanguard Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF (VBR) track a similar index. While iShares Russell 2000 Value ETF has $13.86 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF has $36.90 billion. IWN has an expense ratio of 0.24% and VBR charges 0.05%.

Bottom-Line

While an excellent vehicle for long term investors, passively managed ETFs are a popular choice among institutional and retail investors due to their low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency.

Why Large Cap Value

Large cap companies usually have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Overall, they are usually a stable option, with less risk and more sure-fire cash flows than mid and small cap companies.

Carrying lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, value stocks also have lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. When you look at long-term performance, value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in nearly all markets. But in strong bull markets, growth stocks are more likely to be winners.

Costs

When considering an ETF's total return, expense ratios are an important factor, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts in the long term if all other factors remain equal.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.05%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.86%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Financials sector -- about 23.9% of the portfolio. Healthcare and Industrials round out the top three.

Performance and Risk

MGV seeks to match the performance of the CRSP U.S. Mega Cap Value Index before fees and expenses. The Morningstar US Mega Cap Value Index seeks to accurately represent the mega-cap value segment of the U.S. equity market and deliver low turnover.

The ETF has added roughly 18.72% so far this year and it's up approximately 23.07% in the last one year (as of 11/09/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $135.53 and $171.32.

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) and the Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) track a similar index. While Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF has $119.68 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF has $191.98 billion. SCHD has an expense ratio of 0.06% and VTV charges 0.03%.

headline: Should Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth ETF (SCHG) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
The Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth ETF (SCHG) was launched on December 11, 2009, and is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Large Cap Growth segment of the US equity market.

The fund is sponsored by Charles Schwab. It has amassed assets over $59.82 billion, making it one of the largest ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Growth segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Growth

Companies that find themselves in the large cap category typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Considered a more stable option, large cap companies boast more predictable cash flows and are less volatile than their mid and small cap counterparts.

While growth stocks do boast higher than average sales and earnings growth rates, and they are expected to grow faster than the wider market, investors should note these kinds of stocks have higher valuations. Something to keep in mind is the higher level of volatility that is affiliated with growth stocks. When you consider growth versus value, growth stocks are usually the clear winner in strong bull markets but tend to fall flat in nearly all other environments.

Costs

When considering an ETF's total return, expense ratios are an important factor, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts in the long term if all other factors remain equal.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.04%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.42%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

It is important to delve into an ETF's holdings before investing despite the many upsides to these kinds of funds like diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Information Technology sector -- about 51% of the portfolio. Telecom and Consumer Discretionary round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Nvidia (NVDA) accounts for about 12.61% of total assets, followed by Apple (AAPL) and Microsoft (MSFT).

The top 10 holdings account for about 60.55% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

SCHG seeks to match the performance of the Dow Jones U.S. Large-Cap Growth Total Stock Market Index before fees and expenses. The Dow Jones U.S. Large-Cap Growth Total Stock Market Index is float-adjusted market-capitalization weighted and includes the large-cap growth portion of the Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index.

The ETF has added about 1.92% so far this year and is up about 2.62% in the last one year (as of 11/09/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $28.10 and $36.93.

The ETF has a beta of 1.20 and standard deviation of 19.31% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 189 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, SCHG is an outstanding option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Growth segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG) and the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) track a similar index. While Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF has $213.96 billion in assets, Invesco QQQ has $445.82 billion. VUG has an expense ratio of 0.03% and QQQ charges 0.18%.

Bottom-Line

An increasingly popular option among retail and institutional investors, passively managed ETFs offer low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency; they are also excellent vehicles for long term investors.

excerpt: Colder forecasts and steady LNG demand lift natural gas prices, while ample inventories cap gains. WMB, EQT and EE offer exposure as winter approaches.
headline: Natural Gas Prices Gain 3.5% for the Week: What's Next?
html_content:
U.S. natural gas futures ended the week of Nov. 6 higher as cooler weather forecasts raised expectations for heating demand. Prices recovered after three straight weeks of losses, helped by steady liquefied natural gas (LNG) export demand. However, mild weather across much of the country and relatively high inventories continued to limit gains.

With winter approaching, investors interested in natural gas stocks may want to consider The Williams Companies WMB, EQT Corporation EQT and Excelerate Energy EE.

Natural Gas Prices Recover During the Week

Natural gas futures gained ground during the week as weather forecasts turned colder for parts of the Northeast and Midwest. The December contract settled at $2.998 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) on Nov. 6, posting a weekly gain of 3.5%. The advance ended three consecutive weeks of declines. Expectations of increased heating consumption, slightly lower production readings and steady LNG export demand supported prices. However, forecasts continued to show warmer-than-normal temperatures across much of the United States through mid-November. These conditions kept heating demand relatively weak and prevented natural gas futures from moving firmly above the $3 mark.

Gas Inventories Rise Less Than Expected

The Energy Information Administration reported a 77-billion-cubic-foot (Bcf) increase in natural gas inventories for the week ended Oct. 30, compared with analysts' expectations of an 81-Bcf build. The increase was still above the five-year average of 61 Bcf. Total inventories totaled 3,801 Bcf, or 54 Bcf above the five-year average, but 109 Bcf below the year-ago level. The figures suggest that supplies remain comfortable ahead of winter, although the smaller-than-expected build provided some relief.

Colder Weather May Support Natural Gas Prices

Natural gas prices may find further support as winter approaches and households begin using more fuel for heating. Forecasts already indicate colder conditions in parts of the northern and northeastern United States, which may lift consumption in the coming weeks. LNG exports remain another source of demand. However, inventories are still above their five-year average, and additional storage builds remain possible if mild weather continues. A sustained period of colder temperatures would help reduce inventories and improve the outlook for prices.

headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Check Point Software Technologies Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. CHKP need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec 18, 2026 $200 Put had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Check Point Software shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Check Point Software is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Security industry that ranks in the Top 34% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 30 days, one analyst has increased the earnings estimate for the current quarter, while nine analysts have revised their estimates downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from $2.95 per share to $2.80 in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Check Point Software right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

excerpt: The mean of analysts' price targets for Vir Biotechnology (VIR) points to a 75.6% upside in the stock. While this highly sought-after metric has not proven reasonably effective, strong agreement among analysts in raising earnings estimates does indicate an upside in the stock.
headline: Wall Street Analysts Predict a 75.59% Upside in Vir Biotechnology (VIR): Here's What You Should Know
html_content:
Vir Biotechnology, Inc. (VIR) closed the last trading session at $12.21, gaining 4.4% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $21.44 indicates a 75.6% upside potential.

The mean estimate comprises nine short-term price targets with a standard deviation of $4.1. While the lowest estimate of $17.00 indicates a 39.2% increase from the current price level, the most optimistic analyst expects the stock to surge 145.7% to reach $30.00. It's very important to note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.

But, for VIR, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

Why VIR Could Witness a Solid Upside

There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 15.6% over the past month, as one estimate has gone higher compared to no negative revision.

Moreover, VIR currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much VIR could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

excerpt: Nutex Health's Q3 2026 earnings call highlights rising hospital visits, stable arbitration collections and expansion plans despite an 18.7% revenue decline.
headline: NUTX Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Reimbursement and Hospital Growth
html_content:
Nutex Health Inc. NUTX emphasized improving hospital volumes, stable collections and disciplined expansion during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, even as year-over-year revenues declined.

Management highlighted reimbursement developments, arbitration costs and hospital openings as key considerations for future performance. Executives also addressed revenue-per-visit trends, capital allocation and potential regulatory changes during the analyst discussion.

Nutex Addresses Revenue and Reimbursement Trends

Chief financial officer Jon Bates attributed the revenue decline primarily to favorable collection-estimate adjustments that inflated the comparable 2025 period. Third-quarter revenues declined 18.7% to $217.6 million.

Earnings per share of $5.71 exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.53. Revenues also surpassed the $216.9 million consensus estimate.

Nutex Health Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Nutex Health Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Nutex Health Inc. Quote

Bates explained that revenue per visit has stabilized near $4,000 during 2026, compared with approximately $5,600 in third-quarter 2025. Management expects the metric to remain within its recent range if collection assumptions remain stable.

NUTX Maintains Strong Arbitration Collections

Chairman and chief executive officer Thomas Vo emphasized continued collection strength under the No Surprises Act's independent dispute resolution process.

Approximately 50-60% of billable visits enter arbitration, while 40-50% result in award determinations. Nutex prevailed in more than 80% of determinations over the past nine months and collected more than 80% of award amounts on average for the specified historical awards.

During analyst questioning, Bates acknowledged slightly weaker physician-side collections, although hospital reimbursements remained stable. Management continues monitoring this divergence without identifying a material underlying cause.

Nutex Sees Patient Demand Supporting Growth

Chief operating officer Wesley Bamburg highlighted accelerating patient volumes, supported by expanded clinical capabilities and coordinated business development.

Third-quarter hospital visits increased 18.1% to 54,622, while same-hospital visits rose 12.4%. Management attributed the improvement to localized marketing, physician engagement and broader diagnostic and specialty services.

During the Lake Street Capital Markets discussion, Bamburg emphasized systematically sharing successful business development practices across facilities. Investments in imaging, automation and artificial intelligence remain focused on improving clinical efficiency and expanding patient services.

NUTX Monitors Regulatory and Arbitration Changes

Vo highlighted favorable federal court rulings concerning arbitration award enforcement and qualifying payment calculations. Management views these developments as supportive of fairer reimbursement practices.

The company supports the proposed Murphy legislation, which would strengthen arbitration enforcement, while opposing the Pallone proposal that would eliminate the federal IDR process beginning in 2028.

Responding to B. Riley Securities, Vo acknowledged uncertainty surrounding legislative outcomes. Bates also noted that reduced administrative fees and improvements to the federal arbitration portal could streamline disputes, although procedural delays remain challenging.

Nutex Prioritizes Hospital Expansion and Cash Deployment

Management expects two hospitals, located in San Antonio and Jacksonville, to open during fourth-quarter 2026. Four additional facilities under construction are targeted for late 2027 or early 2028.

During the StoneX discussion, Bates identified hospital development as management's preferred use of capital. The company held $249.9 million in cash at September-end, supporting expansion and infrastructure investments.

Vo reiterated an external growth target of three to five hospitals annually. Share repurchases, dividends and alternative investments remain under board consideration, with growth retaining priority.

NUTX Expands Its Physician Network Strategy

President Warren Hosseinion outlined plans to establish one or two independent physician associations annually around existing hospitals.

The population health division manages nearly 40,000 members. Planned patient enrollment in Dallas and San Antonio during 2027 will complement existing physician networks.

During the Lake Street discussion, Hosseinion emphasized that these networks are intended to improve referrals, care coordination and hospital utilization rather than maximize membership.

Nutex Maintains Its Operational Priorities

Management's overall tone remained constructive but measured, emphasizing patient growth, consistent reimbursement and disciplined spending.

Executives remain focused on converting stronger hospital utilization into sustainable financial performance while navigating reimbursement uncertainty and executing planned facility openings.

NUTX Zacks Rank and Style Scores Signal Mixed Prospects

NUTX currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), indicating a neutral near-term outlook. Its Value Score of A, Growth Score of A and VGM Score of A reflect favorable valuation and growth characteristics, while its Momentum Score of D indicates weaker price momentum. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

The combination presents mixed signals because strong fundamental Style Scores coexist with a neutral Zacks Rank and weak momentum. The Zacks Rank may change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest quarterly results.

excerpt: SENEA's second-quarter fiscal 2027 sales growth and debt reductions highlight underlying strength, despite earnings pressure, margin challenges and rising costs.
headline: Seneca Stock Slips Post Q2 Earnings Despite Sales Growth, Debt Cuts
html_content:
Shares of Seneca Foods Corporation SENEA have lost 1.8% since the company reported earnings for the quarter ended Sept. 26, 2026, compared with the S&P 500 Index’s 2.3% decline over the same period. Over the past month, the stock has declined 17.7%, underperforming the S&P 500’s 6.3% decrease.

Seneca’s Earnings Snapshot

Seneca reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 net sales of $492.6 million, up 7.1% from $460 million in the year-ago quarter. Earnings per share declined 0.5% to $4.27 from $4.29, while net earnings decreased 1.7% to $29.2 million from $29.7 million.

Vegetable segment sales increased 8.9% to $459.9 million from $422.2 million, while Fruit and Snack segment sales declined 4.9% to $26.4 million from $27.8 million. Other revenues decreased 36.9% to $6.3 million from $10.1 million.

Vegetable segment pre-tax earnings increased to $44.2 million from $25.5 million, while Fruit and Snack segment pre-tax earnings declined to $1.2 million from $3.7 million.

SENEA’s Sales Drivers

Seneca attributed the quarterly revenue increase of $32.6 million primarily to higher selling prices and favorable product mix, which contributed $27.3 million. Higher sales volumes added another $5.3 million.

Canned vegetable revenues increased 3.7% to $391.2 million from $377.3 million, while frozen vegetable revenues rose 53.1% to $68.7 million from $44.9 million. The improvement reflected a shift from contract-packed frozen vegetables toward branded frozen products.

Fruit product revenues remained relatively stable at $22.8 million, while snack product revenues declined to $3.6 million from $4.9 million, primarily due to lower sales volumes.

Seneca Foods Corp. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Seneca Foods Corp. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Seneca Foods Corp. Quote

Seneca’s Margins and Costs

Gross margin contracted to 12.5% from 13.4% in the prior-year quarter. The decline primarily reflected a $7.2 million LIFO inventory charge, compared with a $7.7 million credit in the year-ago period.

Excluding LIFO effects, gross margin improved year over year.

Operating income declined 9.2% to $37.7 million from $41.5 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 15% to $23.6 million from $20.5 million, partly reflecting additional selling expenses associated with the Green Giant frozen business.

Net interest expense decreased 55.1% to $2.1 million from $4.7 million, benefiting from lower outstanding term-loan borrowings and a lower average interest rate.

Meanwhile, FIFO pre-tax earnings increased 47.4% to $45.7 million, reflecting stronger underlying performance after excluding LIFO adjustments.

SENEA's Financial Position

Seneca reported operating cash flows of $81.1 million for the first six months of fiscal 2027, compared with $83 million in the prior-year period.

Inventories totaled $795.9 million as of Sept. 26, 2026, compared with $613.9 million as of March 31, 2026. Cash and cash equivalents were $10.7 million.

SENEA made voluntary term-loan prepayments totaling $100 million during the six-month period, including $50.0 million during the fiscal second quarter.

Capital expenditures totaled $34.7 million for the six-month period, compared with $18.8 million a year earlier.

Seneca’s Management Commentary

Chief executive officer Paul Palmby highlighted mid-single-digit sales volume growth across most core businesses, despite contract-packing timing differences and challenges associated with Green Giant's supply chain and pricing adjustments.

Palmby indicated that seasonal crop production was progressing close to budget across most crops, positioning Seneca to meet customer requirements.
Management also highlighted encouraging holiday promotional activity among retail partners, reflecting continued consumer demand.

SENEA's Outlook

Seneca did not provide specific earnings or revenue guidance for fiscal 2027.

However, management expressed confidence in crop availability and seasonal production conditions. SENEA expects its existing operations and liquidity sources to support cash requirements for at least the next 12 months.

Seneca’s Other Developments

Seneca finalized the purchase price for its previously acquired Green Giant U.S. frozen business during the first six months of fiscal 2027, without adjustments to the purchase price.

SENEA received $1.7 million in contingent consideration and incurred $0.2 million in acquisition-related transition service fees during the fiscal second quarter. These integration-related activities remain relevant to Seneca's operating expenses and product mix.

excerpt: Pre-Market in Green
headline: Pre-Market in Green
html_content:
Pre-market futures are up to start a new trading week, still filling in the crater left by last week’s big selloff — the worst trading week in around 18 months — and the ebb-and-flow lower from early October highs. The Dow is +620 points, the Nasdaq +229 and the S&P 500 is +62 points at this hour. The small-cap Russell 2000 is +39 points.

Cooling rhetoric on the U.S.’s sabre-rattling versus Iran is helping spot oil prices pull back further: $87 per barrel (/bbl) on WTI and $93/bbl on Brent crude — well off early April highs that saw WTI climb to nearly $113/bbl. Bond yields are also relatively subdued: the 10-year is currently sitting at +4.84%, the 2-year is +4.52% nd the 30-year +5.42%.

News headlines are being dominated this morning by NVIDIA NVDA CEO Jensen Huang reportedly having engaged in a year-long affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Shares of the world’s largest corporation by market cap are down -6% on the news. A public apology from Huang has already been made, and the company has opened an internal investigation. We expect hearings in U.S. Congress on this matter, as well.

Energy Companies Up on Earnings Reports: NRG, CEG

Natural-gas supplier NRG Energy NRG shares are up +7% this morning, following huge Q3 beats on its report out before this morning’s opening bell. Earnings came in at $4.63 per share, a +36% positive surprise, and the company announced it is selling six natural gas plants for $4 billion. Revenues of $9.47 billion in the quarter came in a whopping +40.6% ahead of estimates.

Constellation Energy CEG, the top nuclear power producer in the U.S., posted Q3 earnings of $5.06 per share this morning, ahead of the $3.90 in the Zacks consensus by +29.7%. Revenues of $9.55 billion outpaced estimates by almost a full billion dollars, +45% year over year. This is the fourth-straight quarterly beat for the company, and shares are up +2.8% on the news.

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today & This Week

After today’s open, we’ll hear from Fed Presidents Austan Goolsbee (Chicago) and Tom Barkin (Richmond, VA) on their outlook for future monetary policy. Also, Monthly Wholesale Trade numbers for September are expected. A month ago, this metric gained +0.5% on headline.

After the close today, we’ll see more earnings results — including from two Zacks Rank #2 (Buy)-rated companies: The Trade Desk TTD and Grand Theft Auto maker Take-Two Interactive Software TTWO look to outperform their expected quarterly losses on both top and bottom lines. Groupon GRPN, a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) stock, is expected to post strong earnings growth for its quarter.

Later this week, key Inflation Reads hit the tape, including the October Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Tuesday and Producer Price Index (PPI) on Friday. These will illustrate where the economy stands on both retail inflation and wholesale inflation, respectively. Last month, headline CPI reached +3.7% while PPI was +6.3% — both far ahead of the optimal inflation rate of +2%, according to the Fed.

excerpt: Autoscope shares gain following Q3'26 results as higher y/y royalty revenues and lower operating expenses drive profitability despite weaker product sales.
headline: AATC Stock Gains Marginally as Q3 Earnings Turn Profitable
html_content:
Shares of Autoscope Technologies Corporation AATC have gained 0.9% since reporting third-quarter 2026 results, outperforming the S&P 500 index’s 3.9% fall. Over the past month, the stock has risen 4.9% compared with the S&P 500's 6.3% decline.

Autoscope Technologies reported third-quarter 2026 revenues of $2.1 million, up 10.6% from $1.9 million in the year-ago quarter. The company posted net income of $366,000, or 7 cents per share, against a net loss of $209,000, or 4 cents per share, in the prior-year period. The earnings improvement reflected higher royalty revenues and the absence of a one-time foreign currency adjustment recorded in the third quarter of 2025.

Autoscope Technologies Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Autoscope Technologies Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Autoscope Technologies Corporation Quote

AATC's Royalty Revenues & Product Sales

Royalty revenues increased 11% year over year to $2.1 million, primarily benefiting from higher sales volumes. Royalties accounted for 99.6% of the total quarterly revenues compared with 99.2% in the prior-year quarter.

Product sales declined 40% to $9,000 from $15,000 a year earlier. The decrease primarily reflected lower sales of the company's IntelliSight product, which generated no comparable sales during the quarter.

Autoscope generates royalty revenues through its exclusive distribution arrangement with Econolite, which markets its video detection products across North America and the Caribbean. This arrangement reduces manufacturing and marketing expenses but also limits reported revenues compared with a direct-sales model.

AATC's Margins & Operating Expenses

Gross profit increased to approximately $2 million from $1.8 million in the year-ago quarter. However, the gross margin contracted to 97% from 97.3%, primarily reflecting software development-related amortization costs.

Royalty gross margin declined to 98.7% from 100%, owing to costs associated with capitalized software development for OptiVu.

Product sales recorded a negative gross margin of 288.9% compared with a negative 240% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting limited sales volumes and fixed software amortization expenses.

Operating expenses declined 2.1% to $1.5 million from $1.6 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased 10.4% to $807,000, benefiting from lower consulting fees and reduced costs associated with foreign subsidiary closures.

Conversely, research and development expenses increased 9.3% year over year to $715,000 due to higher consulting fees and employee-related costs.

Operating income increased to $481,000 from $260,000, reflecting improved revenue generation and expense management.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $575,000 from $332,000, excluding depreciation and amortization expenses.

AATC's Liquidity & Cash Flow Position

Autoscope ended Sept. 30, 2026, with cash and cash equivalents of $1.6 million compared with $735,000 as of Dec. 31, 2025.

The operating cash flow for the first nine months of 2026 declined to $3.3 million from $3.9 million in the comparable prior-year period. Management attributed the decrease primarily to lower cash contributions from accounts receivable and inventory.

The company maintained quarterly dividend payments of 15 cents per share, distributing $2.5 million in the first nine months.

Autoscope reported $1.4 million in current maturities of long-term debt at quarter-end, with refinancing planned before the December 2026 maturity.

AATC's Management Commentary

Chief executive officer Andy Markese attributed the quarterly performance to stability in royalty operations and disciplined expense management.

Management emphasized continued collaboration with its strategic distribution partner to accelerate OptiVu adoption while strengthening its existing operations.

The company highlighted its artificial intelligence-driven traffic detection and analytics technologies, which support roadway safety and traffic management applications.

However, management cautioned that seasonal purchasing patterns, government spending constraints and dependence on distribution partners could influence future performance.

Other Developments

On Nov. 5, 2026, Autoscope announced a quarterly cash dividend of 15 cents per share, payable Nov. 30 to shareholders of record as of Nov. 19.
