headline: LifeMD, Inc. (LFMD) Reports Q3 Loss, Misses Revenue Estimates
html_content:
LifeMD, Inc. (LFMD) came out with a quarterly loss of $0.11 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of a loss of $0.14. This compares to a loss of $0.1 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +21.43%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this company would post a loss of $0.2 per share when it actually produced a loss of $0.16, delivering a surprise of +20%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates two times.

LifeMD, which belongs to the Zacks Medical Services industry, posted revenues of $44.63 million for the quarter ended September 2026, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.53%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $60.17 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates two times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

LifeMD shares have lost about 47.8% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 11.3%.

What's Next for LifeMD?

While LifeMD has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for LifeMD was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.03 on $60.81 million in revenues for the coming quarter and -$0.48 on $207.62 million in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Medical Services is currently in the top 31% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

headline: Buy These 3 Vanguard Mutual Funds for Outstanding Returns
html_content:
Vanguard, one of the world’s largest asset management corporations, was founded by John C. Bogle on May 1, 1975. Headquartered in Valley Forge, PN, the company had $13.6 trillion in assets under management globally as of Jun. 30, 2026. Vanguard has more than 20,000 employees worldwide and offers 465 funds globally.

Vanguard is owned entirely by funds, a unique feature among mutual fund firms. According to the company, this structure allows management to focus more on shareholder interests. Among the most significant advantages, Vanguard claims to offer low-cost, no-load funds. This means that the fund doesn’t charge investors when fund shares are being bought or sold.

Below, we share with you three top-ranked Vanguard mutual funds, namely Vanguard Equity Income Investor VEIPX, Vanguard International Core Stock Investor VWICX and Vanguard Growth & Income Investor VQNPX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and is expected to outperform its peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of funds.

Vanguard Equity Income Investor primarily invests in undervalued mid- and large-cap stocks with above-average, consistent dividend payouts. Two independent advisors manage separate equity portfolios, emphasizing income and value.

Vanguard Equity Income Investor has three-year annualized returns of 19.9%. As of June 2026, VEIPX held 221 issues, with 8% of its assets invested in Broadcom.

Vanguard International Core Stock Investor invests in large- and mid-cap foreign companies across developed and emerging markets, emphasizing reasonable valuations, growth prospects, strong management, capital allocation and competitive advantages.

headline: Bear of the Day: Boston Scientific (BSX)
html_content:
I last wrote about Boston Scientific (BSX) as the Bear of the Day in early August after their Q2 report and management's lowered guidance propelled analysts to notch down their EPS estimates for this year and next, causing BSX shares to fall into the cellar of the Zacks Rank.

Here's how I described the situation then...

Boston Scientific manufactures medical devices and products used in various interventional medical specialties worldwide, including cardiovascular and surgical categories.

On July 29, BSX reported revenue of $5.44 billion for their June quarter, up 7.5% over the same period last year. EPS came in at $0.86, compared to $0.75 in the year-ago quarter.

The reported revenue compares to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.38 billion, representing a surprise of +1.07%. The company delivered an EPS surprise of +3.61%, with the consensus EPS estimate being $0.83.

In response to the conference call and management's lowered guidance, analysts notched down their EPS estimates for this year and next, causing BSX shares to fall into the cellar of the Zacks Rank.

Since its 2025 highs near $110, BSX has been in a steady bear market, making new 52-week lows above $42 last month -- despite nearly doubling revenues in the last 5 years to cross $21 billion.

The stock may soon sort out a bottom after this report given other strong metrics under the hood of the business which continues to grow the top and bottom lines at mid-single digits. 

(end of August 3 article excerpt)

That link will take you to a review of their quarterly results delivered on October 28, which put them back in the cellar of the Zacks Rank as analysts once again lowered their growth forecasts.

In the past two months, the Zacks consensus EPS estimate for this year has dropped from $3.29 to $3.17, representing just 3.6% annual growth. And next year has fallen to flatline from $3.39 to $3.09. 

Shares look somewhat reasonable on a P/E basis at 15X. But with growth continuing to flatline, it looks more expensive trading over 3x sales that are also projected to go negative.

excerpt: Smart Beta ETF report for DVY
headline: Is iShares Select Dividend ETF (DVY) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
The iShares Select Dividend ETF (DVY) made its debut on 11/03/2003, and is a smart beta exchange traded fund that provides broad exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Value category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

The ETF industry has long been dominated by products based on market cap weighted indexes, a strategy created to reflect the market or a particular market segment.

Market cap weighted indexes offer a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way of replicating market returns, and are a good option for investors who believe in market efficiency.

If you're the kind of investor who would rather try and beat the market through good stock selection, then smart beta funds are your best choice; this fund class is known for tracking non-cap weighted strategies.

Non-cap weighted indexes try to choose stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance, which is based on specific fundamental characteristics, or a mix of other such characteristics.

Methodologies like equal-weighting, one of the simplest options out there, fundamental weighting, and volatility/momentum based weighting are all choices offered to investors in this space, but not all of them can deliver superior returns.

Fund Sponsor & Index

DVY is managed by Blackrock, and this fund has amassed over $23.71 billion, which makes it one of the largest ETFs in the Style Box - Large Cap Value. DVY seeks to match the performance of the Dow Jones U.S. Select Dividend Index before fees and expenses.

The Dow Jones U.S. Select Dividend Index measures the performance of a selected group of equity securities issued by companies that have provided relatively high dividend yields on a consistent basis over time.

Cost & Other Expenses

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Operating expenses on an annual basis are 0.38% for DVY, making it on par with most peer products in the space.

DVY's 12-month trailing dividend yield is 3.29%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure that minimizes single stock risk, investors should also look at the actual holdings inside the fund. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

Representing 25.4% of the portfolio, the fund has heaviest allocation to the Financials sector; Utilities and Consumer Staples round out the top three.

Taking into account individual holdings, Pfizer (PFE) accounts for about 2.45% of the fund's total assets, followed by Altria Group Inc (MO) and Hp Inc (HPQ).

The top 10 holdings account for about 19.52% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

The ETF has added roughly 17.76% and is up about 18.12% so far this year and in the past one year (as of 11/13/2026), respectively. DVY has traded between $137.33 and $165.50 during this last 52-week period.

The ETF has a beta of 0.66 and standard deviation of 13.41% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 104 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

iShares Select Dividend ETF is a reasonable option for investors seeking to outperform the Style Box - Large Cap Value segment of the market. However, there are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider.

Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) tracks Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index and the Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) tracks CRSP U.S. Large Cap Value Index. Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF has $123.2 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF has $197.15 billion. SCHD has an expense ratio of 0.06% and VTV changes 0.03%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Style Box - Large Cap Value

Bottom Line

html_content:
NVIDIA’s NVDA leadership turmoil is creating an opportunity for rival semiconductor companies to gain ground in the artificial intelligence (AI) chip market. Following Jensen Huang’s resignation, investors are shifting toward competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices AMD, Broadcom AVGO and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM, betting that the disruption could weaken NVIDIA’s dominance. NVDA shares lost 4.3% yesterday, while AMD added 5.9% and AVGO added 5.5%.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years, resigned on Thursday after two separate extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and the other with an employee — were made public. 

Mark Franklin, head of multi-asset solutions for Asia at Manulife Investment Management, said investors are rotating into other advanced chipmakers on expectations that they could narrow the technological gap with NVDA, as quoted on CNBC.

Chipmakers Stand to Benefit

Investors see TSMC, Broadcom and AMD as potential beneficiaries because they face less direct exposure to Nvidia’s management uncertainty. TSMC, in particular, could benefit regardless of which chip designer eventually gains market share, as it manufactures NVIDIA’s advanced processors.

The rotation has also spread to more defensive areas of the semiconductor industry. Analog chipmakers Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and Germany’s Infineon have gained 13%, 12% and 14%, respectively, this week as investors diversify their exposure.

AI Spending Remains Strong

Despite the reshuffling within the semiconductor industry, the broader AI investment cycle remains intact. Franklin pointed to major technology companies' plans for higher AI spending in 2027, with further increases possible in 2028.

However, growing competition and the spread of open-source technologies could eventually make AI capabilities more commoditized, putting pressure on chip prices and investment returns.

What Lies Ahead of NVIDIA Now?

Most analysts flagged uncertainty over NVIDIA’s medium- to long-term product strategy, including how its new leadership would coordinate with partners across the AI ecosystem. According to Dylan Patel, CEO of semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis, Huang personally built relationships with manufacturers and component suppliers, helping NVIDIA secure scarce production capacity ahead of competitors, per the same CNBC article.

The Huang saga comes at a challenging time for NVIDIA, as Google and Amazon expand their proprietary AI chip businesses and compete for limited supply-chain capacity. Meanwhile, AMD and other chipmakers are stepping up efforts to capture a larger share of the growing AI market.

Investors will closely monitor management's strategy for navigating the leadership crisis. However, some may view the recent selloff as a buy-the-dip opportunity. Reflecting this interest, NVDA shares rose about 2% in premarket trading on Nov. 13, 2026, at the time of writing.

Opportunities for ETF Investors

Against this backdrop, investors can play the AMD-heavy or AVGO-heavy ETFs for the near term. Some of these ETFs also host NVDA, which is good for the investors looking to explore buy-the dip opportunity.

Examples of such ETFs are AOT Growth and Innovation ETF AOTG, iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX, Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF IGPT, Amplify Video Game Leaders ETF GAMR, VanEck Fabless Semiconductor ETF SMHX, Strive U.S. Semiconductor ETF SHOC, Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF SOXQ and SP Funds S&P World (ex-US) ETF SPWO.

excerpt: Energy Fuels is ramping up Pinyon Plain production to meet its 2026 uranium targets, but declining shares, high valuation and losses raise concerns.
headline: UUUU Bets on Pinyon Plain to Meet 2026 Output Goals: Will It Pay Off?
html_content:
Energy Fuels Inc. UUUU mined 385,000 pounds of contained uranium in the third quarter of 2026 from its Pinyon Plain, La Sal and Pandora mines, bringing its year-to-date production to 1.125 million pounds. The company maintains its targets of mining 2-2.5 million pounds of contained uranium and processing 1.5-2.5 million pounds of finished uranium in 2026.

The Pinyon Plain mine accounted for the bulk of production so far this year, contributing 945,000 pounds, while La Sal and Pandora together produced the remaining 180,000 pounds. Grades at Pinyon Plain improved in the third quarter compared with the first half of 2026 as mining advanced through the main zone. The company expects grades to improve further in the coming periods as operations move into the Juniper Zone.

To accelerate output from the lower-cost Pinyon Plain mine during the remainder of 2026, Energy Fuels has redeployed miners from the La Sal Project to Pinyon Plain. This is expected to support higher mined ore stockpiles at the White Mesa Mill for processing in the fourth quarter of 2026 and potentially into 2027, depending on market conditions, contractual requirements and the mill's processing schedule.

Meanwhile, peer Cameco Corporation CCJ reported a 20% year-over-year decline in its share of uranium production to 3.5 million pounds in the third quarter of 2026. Its attributable production for the first nine months of the year totaled 13.6 million pounds.

Cameco has lowered its 2026 production outlook, now expecting its share of total uranium production to be 19.5-20.5 million pounds compared with its previous guidance of 19.5-21.5 million pounds. The revised forecast also points to a decline from the 23.4 million pounds produced in 2025.

UUUU Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Energy Fuels shares have declined 57.1% in a year against the industry’s 26.5% growth.  Cameco has fallen 15.3%, whereas Centrus Energy LEU has declined 58.4%.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

UUUU is trading at a forward 12-month price/sales multiple of 11.73X, a significant premium to the industry’s 3.91X.  It also appears to be highly overvalued compared with Cameco and Centrus Energy, which are trading at lower multiples of 11.65X and 4.51X, respectively. 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Energy Fuels’ 2026 earnings is pegged at a loss of 38 cents per share. The bottom-line estimate for 2027 stands at loss of 1 cent per share. 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Here is how the EPS estimates have been revised over the past 60 days.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Energy Fuels currently carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell).

headline: Woodward (WWD) Q4 Earnings Preview: What You Should Know Beyond the Headline Estimates
html_content:
Analysts on Wall Street project that Woodward (WWD) will announce quarterly earnings of $2.50 per share in its forthcoming report, representing an increase of 19.6% year over year. Revenues are projected to reach $1.13 billion, increasing 14% from the same quarter last year.

Over the last 30 days, there has been an upward revision of 0.5% in the consensus EPS estimate for the quarter, leading to its current level. This signifies the covering analysts' collective reconsideration of their initial forecasts over the course of this timeframe.

Before a company reveals its earnings, it is vital to take into account any changes in earnings projections. These revisions play a pivotal role in predicting the possible reactions of investors toward the stock. Multiple empirical studies have consistently shown a strong association between trends in earnings estimates and the short-term price movements of a stock.

While it's common for investors to rely on consensus earnings and revenue estimates for assessing how the business may have performed during the quarter, exploring analysts' forecasts for key metrics can yield valuable insights.

In light of this perspective, let's dive into the average estimates of certain Woodward metrics that are commonly tracked and forecasted by Wall Street analysts.

It is projected by analysts that the 'Net sales- Aerospace' will reach $769.12 million. The estimate points to a change of +16.4% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus estimate for 'Net sales- Industrial' stands at $367.32 million. The estimate suggests a change of +10% year over year.

The average prediction of analysts places 'Segment earnings- Aerospace' at $185.44 million. Compared to the current estimate, the company reported $162.00 million in the same quarter of the previous year.

The consensus among analysts is that 'Segment earnings- Industrial' will reach $67.31 million. Compared to the present estimate, the company reported $49.00 million in the same quarter last year.

excerpt: RDW's NASA contract advances lunar solar power technology to support future Moon missions and sustainable operations.
headline: Can Redwire's $40M NASA Deal Boost Lunar Power Capabilities?
html_content:
Redwire Corporation RDW is expanding its space infrastructure capabilities through a new NASA contract to demonstrate power generation technology for future lunar operations. On Tuesday, the company announced that it had been selected for an approximately $40 million award to provide an integrated power generation system for NASA's Moon Base program. The project will use Redwire's flight-proven Roll-Out Solar Array (ROSA) technology to support future lunar rovers, habitats and resource utilization activities.

Under the contract, Redwire will support NASA's Moon Base Infrastructure Office in conducting an autonomous power generation demonstration near the lunar South Pole. The integrated system will incorporate solar arrays, batteries and wireless power-transfer hardware for NASA's Mini-Communications and Solar Tower initiative.

The demonstration will validate vertically deployed solar power generation, mast-mounted payload operations and the system's ability to survive the lunar night. These capabilities are important for establishing dependable power infrastructure to support future activities on the Moon. Redwire will build on its development work under NASA's Vertical Solar Array Technology program, which advanced ROSA for vertical deployment and retraction in lunar gravity conditions.

The contract follows the successful installation and deployment of Redwire's eighth and final ROSA wing on the International Space Station, completing a major power modernization effort. The company is developing more than 65 solar array wings for various space missions. The new award provides an opportunity to extend its established solar array technology from Earth orbit to lunar surface infrastructure and support NASA's efforts toward a sustained presence on the Moon.

Companies Advancing Lunar Power Generation Technologies

The growing focus on establishing a sustainable presence on the Moon is encouraging aerospace companies to develop reliable power generation and infrastructure technologies. Lockheed Martin Corporation LMT and Northrop Grumman Corporation NOC are also advancing capabilities for future lunar operations.

Lockheed Martin is developing Vertical Solar Array Technology to provide continuous power for lunar habitats, mobility vehicles and resource utilization systems.

Northrop Grumman is developing Lunar Infrastructure Demo missions to mature power and data systems, including technologies designed to survive the lunar night and support a sustained presence at the Moon's South Pole.

Earnings Estimates for RDW Stock

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings per share suggests year-over-year growth of 54.88% and 51.89%, respectively.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

RDW Stock Is Trading at a Premium

Redwire is trading at a premium relative to the industry, with a forward 12-month price-to-sales of 3.66X compared with the industry average of 2.2X.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

RDW Stock Price Performance

Over the past year, RDW’s shares have risen 48.5% against the industry’s 12.8% decline.

excerpt: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) has a major catalyst approaching, with its highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) scheduled for release on November 19th.
headline: This Video Game Publisher Has a Huge Catalyst Looming
html_content:
Take-Two Interactive TTWO has a major catalyst approaching, with its highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) scheduled for release on November 19th. The title has generated massive excitement among gamers, and the blockbuster success of its predecessor suggests the release could be a major growth driver.

TTWO shares have displayed relative strength over the past month leading up to the release, with a positive outlook provided in its latest quarterly release.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

GTA 5's Massive Success

Before getting into the new installment, it’s useful to look at its highly successful predecessor. Grand Theft Auto V, released in 2013, was a huge success right out of the gate, generating more than $800 million in worldwide retail sales in its first 24 hours. The momentum continued, with sales surpassing the $1 billion mark in just three days.

To this day, it ranks as the 3rd highest-selling video game ever, with Take-Two recently reporting that GTA 5 has sold nearly 230 million copies worldwide. Continued demand more than a decade after its initial launch helps underpin the franchise's staying power.

Importantly, GTA Online has also been a major positive, allowing Take-Two to generate recurring revenue through in-game purchases and additional content long after the initial sale.

The chart below helps highlight the massive revenue spike that the release of GTA V brought for the company.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Latest Results Set Stage for GTA 6

Take-Two's latest quarterly results revealed some weakness ahead of the major release, with net bookings of $1.6 billion declining 18% YoY. Revenue also fell 16% YoY to $1.5 billion, though its GAAP net loss narrowed considerably to $54 million from $134 million in the year-ago period.

Still, the outlook remains highly positive, with management reiterating its FY27 net bookings guidance of $8.0-$8.2 billion, up considerably from the $6.7 billion reported in FY26. At the midpoint, the outlook suggests roughly 20% growth, with GTA 6 expected to be the primary driver.

Importantly, management also highlighted unprecedented preorder activity for the upcoming release, providing a positive indication of the massive demand surrounding the title.

The company's guidance for its upcoming fiscal Q3 particularly reflects the expected growth acceleration, with net bookings forecasted between $3.35-$3.5 billion, more than double the $1.6 billion delivered in its latest quarter.

Beyond the initial sales boost, the long-term opportunity remains significant. GTA 5's continued success through GTA Online provides a strong blueprint for how Take-Two could monetize the new release for years, potentially creating a much higher recurring revenue base.

Bottom Line

Take-Two Interactive TTWO has a major catalyst approaching with GTA 6, and its latest quarterly results reinforced expectations for a successful release.

While it’s been well known for some time now when the game will be released, it still feels like many are underscoring just how big it will become, with the company set to reap the benefits for years to come.

The stock deserves close attention given the upcoming release, with the franchise's staying power and recurring revenue opportunity providing additional upside potential.

headline: Why Is Comtech (CMTL) Down 16.6% Since Last Earnings Report?
html_content:
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Comtech Telecommunications (CMTL). Shares have lost about 16.6% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Comtech due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at the most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for Comtech Telecommunications Corp. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

CMTL Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates Despite Revenue Decline

Comtech reported mixed fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results, with the bottom line surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate while revenues missed expectations. Non-GAAP earnings were breakeven compared with a loss of 25 cents per share in the year-ago quarter. The bottom line topped the consensus estimate of a loss of 27 cents per share.

Revenues declined 12.1% year over year to $66 million, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $112 million by 40.68%. Lower sales of location-based and call handling solutions weighed on performance. However, improved gross margins and positive operating cash flow highlighted operational progress. Funded backlog reached $520.4 million.

CMTL's Net Income Improves Year Over Year

On a GAAP basis, net loss attributable to common shareholders was $14.73 million or a loss of 49 cents per share compared with a net loss of $11.56 million or 39 cents per share in the year-ago quarter. The reported results included losses from discontinued operations related to the planned divestiture of most of the Satellite and Space Communications (S&S) business.

Non-GAAP net loss from continuing operations attributable to common shareholders narrowed to approximately $0.01 million from $7.30 million in the prior-year quarter. Higher gross profit and improved operating performance supported the adjusted bottom line despite lower sales.

Comtech's Revenue Performance Reflects Business Transition

Net sales from continuing operations totaled $66.23 million compared with $75.33 million in the prior-year quarter. The year-earlier period included $8.4 million of revenues from a legacy satellite contract that has since become inactive.

Excluding this contract, lower sales of location-based and call handling solutions affected revenues. This was partly offset by higher sales of Next Generation 9-1-1 (NG9-1-1) solutions and cybersecurity training services. The company is increasingly concentrating on its Allerium public safety operations.

CMTL's Margins Expand Despite Higher Expenses

Gross profit increased to $26.87 million from $26.17 million in the year-ago quarter. Gross margin expanded to 40.6% from 34.7%, benefiting from customer adoption of its solutions and migration to NG9-1-1 core services and call handling platforms.

Operating loss from continuing operations widened to $3.88 million from $0.75 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased to $24.33 million from $19.03 million, while research and development expenses declined to $2.78 million from $3.07 million.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $6.53 million from $5.07 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $9.19 million from $7.51 million, with the corresponding margin improving to 13.9% from 10%.

Comtech's Bookings and Backlog Support Revenue Visibility

Net bookings totaled $32 million compared with $58.5 million in the prior-year quarter. The book-to-bill ratio declined to 0.48x from 0.78x, reflecting the timing of large, multiyear contract awards.

Revenue visibility, comprising funded backlog and the unfunded value of certain multiyear contracts, stood at approximately $862 million. Quarterly contract awards included more than $8 million from a domestic mobile network operator and approximately $6.5 million for cybersecurity training and support of U.S. government customers.

CMTL's Cash Flow and Liquidity Show Improvement

Cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations reached $18.47 million compared with cash utilization of $1.17 million in the year-ago quarter. Improved working capital management, including collections of accounts receivable and contract assets, supported cash generation.

As of July 31, 2026, cash and cash equivalents stood at $34.98 million compared with $35.37 million a year earlier. Consolidated year-end liquidity reached $61.3 million. The company also generated positive consolidated operating cash flow for the sixth consecutive quarter.

Comtech's Strategic Divestiture Shapes Its Outlook

Comtech entered into an agreement to sell most of its S&S business to an affiliate of Gilat Satellite Networks for a base purchase price of $157.5 million. The transaction is expected to close in calendar 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

Following the divestiture and approximately one year of transition implementation, Comtech anticipates annual cost savings of $16 million to $18 million, excluding one-time expenses. Transition-related investments are expected to total approximately $13 million to $15 million, primarily during fiscal 2027 and 2028.

The company estimates that fiscal 2026 pro forma adjusted EBITDA would have ranged from $37 million to $39 million, reflecting the retained businesses and anticipated restructuring benefits. Management intends to use the transaction proceeds to substantially reduce debt and strengthen financial flexibility while focusing on Allerium's public safety and communications technologies.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

In the past month, investors have witnessed a downward trend in fresh estimates.

The consensus estimate has shifted 54.29% due to these changes.

VGM Scores

Currently, Comtech has a strong Growth Score of A, a grade with the same score on the momentum front. Following the exact same course, the stock has a score of A on the value side, putting it in the top 20% for value investors.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of A. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending downward for the stock, and the magnitude of this revision indicates a downward shift. Notably, Comtech has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

excerpt: Fastenal (FAST) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Fastenal (FAST) Up 10.3% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
html_content:
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for Fastenal (FAST). Shares have added about 10.3% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Fastenal due for a pullback? Before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late, let's take a quick look at the most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the important drivers.

Fastenal Q3 Earnings Beat on Expense Leverage, Sales Miss Estimates

Fastenal reported mixed third-quarter 2026 results, with earnings beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate and net sales missing the consensus mark. Year over year, however, both metrics grew. Customer contract wins and pricing actions supported growth, while expense leverage helped offset pressure from sales to larger accounts. Contract customer daily sales rose 18.8%, and operating margin expanded 90 basis points (bps) to 21.5%.

Fastenal’s Q3 Earnings & Sales Highlights

Fastenal’s quarterly earnings of 35 cents per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.9% and increased 19.8% year over year from 29 cents per share.

Net sales rose 15.5% year over year to $2.46 billion but missed the consensus mark of $2.49 billion by 1%.

FAST's Contract Accounts Drive Sales Gains

Sales benefited from customer contracts signed since the first quarter of 2024 and a modest improvement in industrial production. Product pricing added approximately 240 bps to third-quarter sales growth. Currency movements created a roughly 10-bps headwind. Contract customers accounted for 76.5% of revenues, up from 73.8% a year earlier. Non-contract daily sales increased 7.8%. The number of contracts rose 6.4% to 3,744, with signings weighted toward national multi-site accounts. Average customer sites generating at least $50,000 in monthly sales increased to 3,288 from 2,771. Sales from those sites grew 27.6% to $1.46 billion, highlighting the concentration of growth among larger customers.

Fastenal's Manufacturing Markets Lead Demand

Manufacturing contributed 76.6% of quarterly revenues, with daily sales rising 17.2%. Heavy manufacturing increased 20.2% and accounted for 44.6% of revenues, benefiting from key accounts in aerospace, machined products and industrial equipment. Other manufacturing daily sales advanced 13.2%.

Non-residential construction daily sales grew 12%, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of growth. Other end markets advanced 12.4%, helped by transportation and reseller customers. Total non-manufacturing daily sales increased 12.3%. Direct material daily sales rose 18.6%, outpacing the 14.3% growth in indirect materials. Direct cutting tools and abrasives gained 19.5%, while direct non-fasteners and hardware increased 21.2%.

FAST's Digital Footprint Expands

Digital Footprint sales increased 16.1% to $1.54 billion and represented 61.4% of revenues compared with 61.3% a year ago. This measure includes sales through Fastenal Managed Inventory (FMI) technology and eBusiness transactions excluding overlapping orders. FMI sales grew 14.6% to $1.12 billion, while eBusiness sales climbed 14.8% to $721.5 million. FASTBin and FASTVend sales increased 17.6% to $827.2 million, outpacing overall company growth. Fastenal signed 7,484 weighted FASTBin and FASTVend machine-equivalent units (MEUs), up 6.2%. The installed base reached 143,878 MEUs, up 7.4%, reinforcing its emphasis on automated inventory management.

Fastenal's Expense Leverage Lifts Profitability

Gross profit rose 14.4% to $1.1 billion, but gross margin declined approximately 40 bps to 44.8%. A mix shift toward large customers reduced gross margin by about 50 bps, while pricing relative to costs exerted a roughly 30-bps drag. That price-cost headwind narrowed about 10 bps from the preceding quarter. Sourcing savings, supplier rebates and tariff refunds provided relief. SG&A expenses increased 9.4% to $573.9 million, below revenue growth. As a share of sales, SG&A improved 130 bps to 23.3%, supported by labor productivity and fixed-cost leverage. Operating income climbed 20.2% to $530.8 million, while net income increased 19.7% to $401.6 million.

FAST's Cash Generation Supports Shareholder Returns

Operating cash flow increased 9% year over year to $421.6 million, equaling 105% of net income compared with 115.3% a year ago. Higher receivables and inventory requirements absorbed cash as sales expanded. Year over year, accounts receivable increased 19.9%, inventories rose 3.1% and accounts payable advanced 29.3%.

Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, totaled $349.6 million compared with $332.1 million a year earlier. It represented 87.1% of net income, down from 99%. The company returned $328.4 million to shareholders through $298.2 million in dividends and $30.2 million in repurchases. Total debt ended the quarter at $100 million, down from $195 million a year ago.

Fastenal Maintains Capital Plan

Fastenal maintained its fiscal 2026 net capital investment expectation of $310-$330 million compared with $230.6 million in 2025. Spending priorities include replacing the Atlanta hub, improving distribution efficiency, completing delayed IT projects and adding trucking capacity. The company expects an ongoing tax rate of approximately 24.6%, absent discrete tax items or changes to tax law.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

Analysts were quiet during the last two month period as none of them issued any earnings estimate revisions.

VGM Scores

Currently, Fastenal has a nice Growth Score of B, though it is lagging a lot on the Momentum Score front with a D. Charting a somewhat similar path, the stock has a grade of F on the value side, putting it in the fifth quintile for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of D. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Fastenal has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

The Progressive Corporation’s third-quarter 2026 earnings per share of $4.60 beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.1%. The bottom line increased 13.6% year over year.

Behind the Headlines

Net premiums written were $22.3 billion in the quarter, up 4% from $21.4 billion a year ago. 

Net premiums earned grew 5% to $21.9 billion. The reported figure met the Zacks Consensus Estimate.

Net realized loss on securities was $170 million, versus a $295 million gain in the year-ago quarter.

Combined ratio improved 80 basis points (bps) from the prior-year quarter’s level to 88.7. The Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at 89.4.

September Numbers in Details

Operating revenues grew 5.2% year over year to $7.7 billion, driven by 4.9% higher net premiums earned, a 13.2% increase in net investment income, a 5% rise in fees and other revenues and 6.7% higher service revenues. 

Total expenses decreased 5.6% to $6.6 billion, largely attributable to the absence of policyholder credit expense in the current month.

September Policies in Force

Policies in force were strong in the Personal Lines segment, up 6% year over year to 39.2 million. Progressive’s Commercial Lines segment policies rose 5% year over year to 1.3 million.  

In the Personal Lines segment, Agency Auto increased 7% year over year to 11.3 million, while Direct Auto increased 8% to 16.8 million. Special Lines improved 6% to 7.4 million. 

The Property business had 3.6 million policies in force, flat year over year.

Financial Update

Progressive’s book value per share was $59.51 as of Sept. 30, 2026, down 1.6% from $60.45 as of Sept. 30, 2025.

Return on equity in September 2026 was 25.7%, down from 37.1% reported in the year-ago period. The total debt-to-total capital ratio deteriorated 330 bps to 19.6.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

Since the earnings release, investors have witnessed a downward trend in estimates revision.

VGM Scores

At this time, Progressive has a average Growth Score of C, a grade with the same score on the momentum front. Charting a somewhat similar path, the stock has a score of B on the value side, putting it in the top 40% for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of C. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending downward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Notably, Progressive has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

headline: 3 Top-Ranked AI Stocks Holding Up Despite the Selloff
html_content:
The AI trade has experienced some extraordinary volatility in recent weeks, with sharp selling across semiconductors, infrastructure providers and many of the market's former leaders.

The correction has raised questions about the next phase of the AI boom. While investment in artificial intelligence continues to grow, investors appear increasingly concerned about valuations, capital spending and whether the stocks that led the previous rally can continue outperforming.

I think there is a reasonable possibility we are entering a more challenging market environment. However, that doesn't mean investors should abandon AI stocks altogether.

In fact, periods of market weakness can help identify the strongest opportunities. Stocks that hold up relatively well while their peers suffer sharp declines often deserve closer attention, particularly when that price strength is supported by improving fundamentals.

Three stocks worth highlighting are Arista Networks (ANET), Zeta Global (ZETA) and Littelfuse (LFUS). Each offers exposure to a different segment of the AI boom, with strong earnings momentum, favorable analyst revisions and technical setups worth watching.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Arista Networks: AI Networking Demand Remains Strong

Arista Networks is a leading provider of high-performance networking equipment and software used in data centers, cloud infrastructure and increasingly complex AI computing systems.

As AI clusters expand, the networking infrastructure connecting thousands of processors becomes increasingly important. Arista is a major beneficiary of this trend, particularly as Ethernet networking gains adoption across AI data centers.

The company's latest earnings report demonstrated just how strong demand remains.

Third-quarter revenue surged 58.5% year over year to $3.66 billion, exceeding management's guidance of $3.3 billion. Adjusted earnings rose to $1.20 per share from $0.77 a year earlier, while adjusted operating margin reached an impressive 49.1%.

Looking ahead, management expects continued rapid expansion in AI networking, with AI-related revenue projected to double to approximately $7 billion in 2027.

Analysts have responded by unanimously raising their earnings estimates across timeframes, supporting Arista's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

With exceptional revenue growth, strong profitability and rising earnings estimates, Arista remains one of the more compelling businesses within the AI infrastructure industry.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Zeta Global: AI Adoption Drives Accelerating Growth

Zeta Global offers a different way to participate in the AI boom, focusing on the application of artificial intelligence rather than the infrastructure required to build it.

The company operates an AI-powered marketing and customer intelligence platform, helping businesses analyze consumer data, identify customers and automate marketing campaigns.

Its Athena AI platform has become an increasingly important growth driver, as companies look to integrate artificial intelligence into their everyday operations.

The latest earnings report was particularly impressive.

Third-quarter revenue surged 46% year over year to $493 million, while adjusted earnings reached $0.38 per share. Adjusted EBITDA increased 55% to $121 million, and free cash flow jumped 73% to $82 million.

The company also reported positive GAAP net income of $38 million and raised its full-year revenue outlook to approximately $1.86 billion, representing expected growth of 42%.

Importantly, the company has now delivered 21 consecutive quarters of beating expectations and raising guidance.

Analysts have responded enthusiastically, with current year earnings estimates climbing 8.2% over the last week, earning Zeta a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

With accelerating AI adoption, expanding profitability and sharply rising earnings estimates, Zeta offers an interesting opportunity as the AI boom broadens beyond infrastructure spending.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Littelfuse: AI Infrastructure Supports Earnings Growth

Littelfuse is another beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending, although its business differs considerably from the more familiar semiconductor and networking companies.

The company develops circuit protection, power control and sensing technologies used across electronics, industrial equipment, transportation and electrical infrastructure.

These components are essential for managing electricity safely and efficiently, making them increasingly important as data centers become more power-intensive.

Littelfuse also benefits from industrial automation and electrification, providing additional growth opportunities beyond AI.

The company's latest results were exceptionally strong.

Third-quarter revenue reached a record $767 million, up 23% year over year, with organic growth contributing 22%. Adjusted earnings surged 96% to $5.79 per share, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 690 basis points to 28.4%.

Free cash flow also climbed 64% to $216 million, reflecting substantial improvement in operating performance.

Looking ahead, analysts expect earnings to increase approximately 72% this year, alongside projected revenue growth of roughly 25%.

The strong results and favorable estimate revisions have earned Littelfuse a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

With sharply improving earnings and exposure to several long-term industrial growth trends, Littelfuse offers a differentiated way to participate in the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Should Investors Buy ANET, ZETA and LFUS?

The recent correction has made it clear that investors are becoming more selective about AI stocks. However, that same volatility can help distinguish potential leaders from weaker names.

Arista Networks, Zeta Global and Littelfuse have all delivered impressive operating results, with favorable earnings revisions supporting their top Zacks Ranks.

If their relative price strength continues as the broader market stabilizes, these three stocks could be among the more attractive opportunities for investors looking to maintain AI exposure in a changing market environment.

headline: Are You Ready For A Year-End Rally?
html_content:
Just 7 weeks left in the year. At present, the S&P is up 8.5% YTD, with the Nasdaq up 7.5%.

But I’m expecting a lot more upside to go.

For one, even though Q4 has gotten off to a rough start, historically the fourth quarter is the best quarter of the year. Since 1950, the S&P has gone up 79% of the time, with an average gain of 4.1%.

This year, however, still has the potential to be much larger.

Additionally, and regardless of politics, stocks typically rally after midterms. Since 1950, between election day and the end of the year, it’s higher 68% of the time. And looking out over a 12-month period from midterms, the odds improve even more dramatically with the S&P up every time with an average gain of more than 15%.

But there’s a lot more going for the market than just the high-probability seasonal tendencies and cyclical tendencies. That includes the soaring earnings outlook. (More on that in a bit.)

For those who wished they would have taken better advantage of this year’s rally, the good news is that it looks like the next month and a half, could be the best month and a half of the entire year. 

History Repeats Itself

Last year saw the S&P 500 gain 16.4%. That was on top of 2024’s 23.3%, and 2023’s 24.2%.

The historic AI tech boom has been leading the way.

And it’s reminiscent of the dot-com tech boom in 1995-1999 when the market surged by double-digits each year for 5 long, glorious years in a row, resulting in a 220% increase for the S&P, while plenty of individual stocks were up several hundred percent to several thousand percent.

I believe we could see the same thing again now. Five years in a row of double-digit market gains, just like we did back then.

This year (2026), would be year 4, while 2027 would be year 5. But nobody says it has to stop there. With AI being touted as the most transformational tech breakthrough ever, it could very well last much longer.

Moreover, I think we can soar beyond ‘just’ a 20% gain.

Since 1988, only five times has the S&P had an annual gain of 30% or more. Just 5 times over the last 38 years.

But did you know that 2 of those 5 times happened in the 1995-1999 dot-com boom?

In 1995, it was up 37.6%. And in 1997 it was up 33.4%.

And the last time we saw a 30% gain was back in 2013.

Whether it’s this year or next, we’re due for another one, in my opinion.

Plus, with the AI boom being even bigger than the dot-com boom, driven by real earnings and real growth, if there ever was a reason to see a 30% gain, now is the time.

And AI will be one of the key drivers for stocks for years to come.

A recent comment underscoring the AI trade came from AMD CEO Lisa Su, who characterized the demand for AI as “insatiable,” and said her company alone could grow by 35% a year for the next 3-5 years because of that. In fact, she said the AI market is "faster than anything we've seen before.” And she predicted the AI data center market could grow to “$1 trillion” by 2030.

A resounding outlook for the scale of AI.

And while it transforms the world as we know it, it also has the potential to transform one’s portfolio.

But in addition to the ongoing AI boom, there’s plenty of other reasons to expect another year of big gains.

A Productivity Boom Is Underway Too

We are now in the strongest productivity environment since the late-1990’s tech boom.

In fact, full-year productivity growth is trending at 2.0%, making it the strongest period in more than 25 years.

What’s noteworthy is that productivity growth typically slows in the late stages of expansion as capacity tightens and incremental gains are harder to extract.

But it accelerates at the beginning of a new growth phase when new technologies are adopted, and businesses unlock efficiencies that weren’t previously possible.

That’s why people are comparing it to the late 1990’s. Productivity jumped back then due to the technology gains from the internet boom.

And we could be seeing the same thing now, thanks to the technology gains from the AI boom.

The pattern is clear, as productivity jumps, broader economic expansion follows. And the current above-trend productivity gains are another marker for potentially big growth ahead – for the economy and the market.

The Earnings Outlook Is For Growth

Let’s also not forget that earnings are the main driver of stock prices.

And it’s pointing to strong growth.

Q3 earnings season is in full swing. And that’s great news since stocks typically go up during earnings season.

And I’m expecting another stellar performance with the EPS growth rate for the S&P 500 projected at 28.8%.

Q4’26 is forecast at 27.9%.

Wow!

So, the next step is to get that list down to the best 5-10 stocks that you can buy.

Proven Profitable Strategies

Picking the best stocks is a lot easier when there’s a proven, profitable method to do it.

And by concentrating on what has proven to work in the past, you’ll have a better idea as to what your probability of success will be now and in the future.

Of course, this won't preclude you from ever having another losing trade. But if your stock picking strategy picks winners more often than losers, you can feel confident that your next trade will have a high probability of success.

The best part about these strategies (aside from the returns) is that all of the testing and hard work has already been done. There’s no guesswork involved. Just point and click and start getting into better stocks on your very next trade.

headline: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Parker-Hannifin, IDEX, Crane and Applied Industrial
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 16, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Parker-Hannifin Corp. PH, IDEX Corp. IEX, Crane Co. CR and Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc. AIT

Industry: Industrial Manufacturing

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3029325/4-industrial-manufacturing-stocks-to-gain-on-robust-industry-trends

The Zacks Manufacturing – General Industrial industry is gaining from solid momentum in the manufacturing sector, increased investments in product development and technological advancements. The industry participants’ efforts to digitize business operations and expand market presence through strategic acquisitions are also expected to support the industry’s growth.

However, cost inflation and challenges due to a shortage of skilled labor have marred the industry's outlook. Parker-Hannifin Corp., IDEX Corp., Crane Co. and Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc. are a few industry participants that are likely to capitalize on the prevalent opportunities.

About the Industry

The Zacks Manufacturing – General Industrial industry comprises companies that produce a wide range of industrial equipment. Some industry players offer power transmission products, bearings, engineered fluid power components and systems, industrial rubber products, vapor-abrasive blasting equipment, vehicle-powered truck refrigeration systems, adhesive, gel coat equipment, flow-control components and linear motion components. 

Industrial manufacturing companies also reconstruct and assemble pumps, valves, speed reducers and hydraulic motors. The companies provide services to original equipment manufacturing and maintenance, repair and overhaul customers. These end users belong to the mining, oil and gas, forest products, agriculture and food processing, fabricated metals, chemicals and petrochemicals, transportation and utilities industries.

Major Trends Shaping the Future of the Manufacturing General Industrial Industry

Strength in the Manufacturing Sector: The industry has been benefiting from an increase in manufacturing activities. After witnessing a contraction in economic activities for 10 successive months till December 2025, the manufacturing sector expanded for the 10th consecutive month in October. 

Per the Institute for Supply Management’s (ISM) report, the Manufacturing Purchasing Manager’s Index touched 55.5% in October. A figure more than 50% indicates an expansion in manufacturing activity. Also, the New Orders Index expanded, registering 55.5% in the same month.

Investments in Innovation & Technological Advancements: The industry participants’ constant focus on innovation, product upgrades and the development of new products to stay competitive in the market should drive growth. With the gradual development of business models and cutting-edge technologies, several industry players have been banking on digitizing their business operations for a while now. Digitization enables industry participants to boost their competitiveness through enhanced operational productivity, product quality and better cost management.

Acquisition-Based Growth Strategy: The industry players rely on an acquisition-based growth strategy to broaden their customer base and enhance their product portfolio. This helps them foray into new markets and solidify their competitive position. Exposure to various end markets helps industrial manufacturing companies offset risks associated with a single market.

Rising Costs Hurt Margins: Industry participants have been encountering input cost inflation and other expenses, which have been denting profitability. Also, supply-chain issues might increase raw material and other logistics expenses. The latest ISM report’s Supplier Deliveries Index reflects slower deliveries for the 11th straight month in October. 

The rise in expenses, along with a tough labor market, poses a threat to margins. However, companies have been focused on cost management initiatives to mitigate cost-related challenges. These efforts include simplifying operations, improving supply-chain efficiency and applying disciplined pricing strategies.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Prospects

The Zacks Manufacturing – General Industrial industry, housed within the broader Zacks Industrial Products sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #89. This rank places it in the top 36% of 247 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of the member stocks, indicates bright near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

Given the industry’s bright near-term prospects, we will present a few promising stocks for your portfolio. But before that, it is worth taking a look at the industry’s stock market performance and current valuation.

Industry Lags Sector and the S&P 500

The Zacks Manufacturing – General Industrial industry has underperformed the broader sector and the Zacks S&P 500 composite index over the past year. Over this period, the industry has grown 8.6% compared with the sector and the S&P 500 Index’s rise of 10.7% and 13%, respectively.

Industry's Current Valuation

On the basis of forward 12-month Price-to-Earnings (P/E), which is a commonly used multiple for valuing manufacturing stocks, the industry is currently trading at 22.05X compared with the S&P 500’s 18.82X. It is also above the sector’s P/E ratio of 19.61X.

In the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 25.05X and as low as 15.95X, with the median being 21.35X.

4 Manufacturing-General Industrial Stocks Leading the Pack

Parker-Hannifin: This Cleveland, OH-based company supplies precision-engineered solutions to a wide variety of mobile, industrial and aerospace markets. Commercial and defense demand across OEM and aftermarket channels is aiding PH’s performance. Also, growth across all market verticals bodes well for the company.

The consensus estimate for this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company’s 2026 earnings has been revised 6.6% upward over the past 60 days. The company outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average earnings surprise being 7.8%. Shares of PH surged 15.1% in the past year. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

IDEX: Headquartered in Lake Forest, IL, IDEX is an applied solutions company that specializes in a diverse range of applications such as fluid and metering technologies, health and science technologies and fire, safety and other products. The company is benefiting from strength in the Fluid & Metering Technologies segment, driven by an increase in demand for products across the municipal water end market. Higher demand for mining application solutions is also supporting the company’s performance.

This Zacks Rank #2 stock has gained 44.7% in the past year. The company outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average earnings surprise being 7.6%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for its 2026 earnings has been revised 1.9% upward over the past 60 days.

Crane: Based in Stamford, CT, Crane Company manufactures and delivers specialized industrial solutions and components through sales representatives and industrial distributors. CR is well-positioned to gain from its original equipment manufacturer (OEM) business, driven by higher commercial aircraft build rates. Solid momentum in the commercial and military aftermarket businesses, driven by continued high utilization of aircraft, is aiding the company’s performance as well.

Shares of this Zacks Rank #2 company have gained 14.1% in the past year. The company outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average earnings surprise being 10.7%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings has been revised 4.4% upward over the past 60 days.

Applied Industrial: Headquartered in Cleveland, OH, Applied Industrial is a distributor of value-added industrial products including engineered fluid power components, bearings, specialty flow control solutions, power transmission products and miscellaneous industrial supplies. It is well-positioned to gain from robust demand for technical MRO services. Also, volume gains in fluid power and automation operations bode well.

Shares of this Zacks Rank #2 company have gained 20.5% in the past year. AIT outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average earnings surprise being 3.6%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings has been revised 0.5% upward over the past 60 days.

7 Best Stocks for the Next 30 Days

Just released: Experts distill 7 elite stocks from the current list of 220 Zacks Rank #1 Strong Buys. They deem these tickers "Most Likely for Early Price Pops."

Since 1988, the full list has beaten the market more than 2X over with an average gain of +23.9% per year. So be sure to give these hand picked 7 your immediate attention. 

See them now >>

excerpt: GASFX, FSUTX, FKUTX and FIUIX offer growth opportunities amid rising electricity demand and AI-driven power needs
headline: 4 Utilities Mutual Fund Picks to Ride Rising Power Demand
html_content:
The U.S. utilities sector has staged a remarkable comeback since the end of September, with the State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLU) advancing 11.7% as of date. The sudden rally reflects a combination of declining Treasury yields, defensive sector rotation and growing optimism about electricity demand. Utilities emerged as one of the strongest-performing sectors in October, even as technology stocks faced considerable selling pressure.

A major catalyst has been investors' shift toward defensive investments amid heightened volatility in technology and AI-related stocks. Utilities generally offer relatively predictable earnings, stable cash flows and regular dividend payments, making them attractive when investors become cautious about growth-oriented investments. Additionally, a retreat in Treasury yields toward the end of October improved the relative appeal of utility dividends, while easing some concerns about borrowing costs.

Beyond the near-term investment rotation, the sector has substantial long-term growth opportunities. The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence, particularly energy-intensive data centers, is driving electricity consumption higher. Increasing electrification across manufacturing, transportation and residential markets is adding to demand. The Energy Information Administration expects U.S. electricity consumption to reach record levels in both 2026 and 2027, supported partly by data center expansion. Utilities are consequently increasing investments in power generation, transmission networks and grid modernization.

In this environment, utility mutual funds provide stability and growth potential. Hence, astute investors should consider such funds at present. Mutual funds, in general, reduce transaction costs and diversify portfolios without an array of commission charges that are mostly associated with stock purchases (read more: Mutual Funds: Advantages, Disadvantages, and How They Make Investors Money).

We have thus selected four utility mutual funds that boast a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), have positive three-year and five-year annualized returns and minimum initial investments within $5000, and carry a low expense ratio.  

Hennessy Gas Utility Investor GASFX passively tracks an index of U.S. natural gas companies, investing primarily in common stocks of gas distribution, pipeline and diversified utilities businesses to replicate its performance.

Ryan Kelley has been the lead manager of GASFX since 2013. Three top holdings of GASFX are Cheniere Energy (5.5%), Oneok (5.2%) and Berkshire Hathaway (5.1%).

GASFX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 18.8% and 11.9%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.97%. GASFXhas a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1. To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here.

Fidelity Select Utilities FSUTX invests primarily in domestic and foreign utility companies, including electricity, gas, water and renewable energy businesses, selecting securities through fundamental analysis.

Pranay Kirpalani has been the lead manager of FSUTX since December 2024. Three top holdings of FSUTX are NextEra Energy (13.4%), American Electric Power (6.7%) and Constellation Energy (6.4%).

FSUTX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 17.1% and 10.5%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.63%. FSUTX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

Franklin Utilities FKUTX invests primarily in global utility companies, emphasizing U.S. electricity and gas providers, particularly businesses generating substantial earnings from regulated operations.

Blair Schmicker has been the lead manager of FKUTX since 2009. Three top holdings of FKUTX are NextEra Energy (9.1%), Entergy (6.4%) and The Southern Company (5%).

FKUTX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 18.6% and 10.1%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.71%. FKUTX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

Fidelity Telecom and Utilities FIUIX invests primarily in domestic and foreign telecommunications and utility companies, using fundamental analysis to select stocks based on financial strength, industry position and market conditions.

Alex Boyajian has been the lead manager of FIUIX since 2025. Three top holdings of FIUIX are NextEra Energy (10.6%), Verizon (9,1%) and American Electric Power (5.9%).

FIUIX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 15.8% and 9.9%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.71%. FIUIX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

Bottom Line

The sector's outlook remains constructive, supported by rising electricity demand, infrastructure spending and opportunities for earnings growth. However, elevated interest rates, regulatory scrutiny, affordability concerns and delays in data center projects could limit further gains. Higher capital requirements also pose financing challenges. Nevertheless, utilities with strong balance sheets, favorable regulatory environments and access to growing electricity markets appear well-positioned to benefit from the ongoing transformation of America's power infrastructure.

The Energy Information Administration expects U.S. electricity consumption to reach record levels in both 2026 and 2027, supported partly by data center expansion. Blair Schmicker has been the lead manager of FKUTX since 2009. Three top holdings of FKUTX are NextEra Energy (9.1%), Entergy (6.4%) and The Southern Company (5%). FKUTX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 18.6% and 10.1%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.71%. FKUTX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1. headline: Aercap Holdings N.V. (AER) Hit a 52 Week High, Can the Run Continue?
html_content:
A strong stock as of late has been AerCap (AER). Shares have been marching higher, with the stock up 20.6% over the past month. The stock hit a new 52-week high of $183.22 in the previous session. AerCap has gained 22.2% since the start of the year compared to the 15.6% gain for the Zacks Transportation sector and the 15.3% return for the Zacks Transportation - Equipment and Leasing industry.

What's Driving the Outperformance?

The stock has an impressive record of positive earnings surprises, as it hasn't missed our earnings consensus estimate in any of the last four quarters. In its last earnings report on October 28, 2026, AerCap reported EPS of $6.56 versus consensus estimate of $4.57.

For the current fiscal year, AerCap is expected to post earnings of $22.3 per share on $9.1 in revenues. This represents a 45.09% change in EPS on a 6.87% change in revenues. For the next fiscal year, the company is expected to earn $19.72 per share on $8.51 in revenues. This represents a year-over-year change of -11.54% and -6.47%, respectively.

Valuation Metrics

Though AerCap has recently hit a 52-week high, what is next for AerCap? A key aspect of this question is taking a look at valuation metrics in order to determine if the company is due for a pullback from this level.

On this front, we can look at the Zacks Style Scores, as these give investors a variety of ways to comb through stocks (beyond looking at the Zacks Rank of a security). The individual style scores for Value, Growth, Momentum and the combined VGM Score run from A through F. The idea behind the style scores is to help investors pick the most appropriate Zacks Rank stocks based on their individual investment style.

AerCap has a Value Score of B. The stock's Growth and Momentum Scores are D and B, respectively, giving the company a VGM Score of B.

In terms of its value breakdown, the stock currently trades at 7.9X current fiscal year EPS estimates, which is not in-line with the peer industry average of 13.3X. On a trailing cash flow basis, the stock currently trades at 5.3X versus its peer group's average of 4.7X. Additionally, the stock has a PEG ratio of 0.59. This isn't enough to put the company in the top echelon of all stocks we cover from a value perspective.

Zacks Rank

We also need to consider the stock's Zacks Rank, as this is even more important than the company's VGM Score. Fortunately, AerCap currently has a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy) thanks to a solid earnings estimate revision trend.

Since we recommend that investors select stocks carrying Zacks Rank of 1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) and Style Scores of A or B, it looks as if AerCap passes the test. Thus, it seems as though AerCap shares could have potential in the weeks and months to come.

How Does AER Stack Up to the Competition?

Shares of AER have been soaring, and the company still appears to be a decent choice, but what about the rest of the industry? One industry peer that looks good is Herc Holdings Inc. (HRI). HRI has a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy) and a Value Score of B, a Growth Score of C, and a Momentum Score of F.

Earnings were strong last quarter. Herc Holdings Inc. beat our consensus estimate by 26.95%, and for the current fiscal year, HRI is expected to post earnings of $11.38 per share on revenue of $5.04 billion.

Shares of Herc Holdings Inc. have gained 36% over the past month, and currently trade at a forward P/E of 21.01X and a P/CF of 4.15X.

The Transportation - Equipment and Leasing industry may rank in the bottom 71% of all the industries we have in our universe, but there still looks like there are some nice tailwinds for AER and HRI, even beyond their own solid fundamental situation.
