excerpt: Three gaming stocks - TTWO, RSI and ACEL - offer growth potential through strong franchises, digital expansion and rising player engagement despite industry headwinds.
headline: 3 Gaming Stocks Offering Growth Amid Industry Headwinds
html_content:
The Zacks Gaming industry is facing a challenging operating landscape as economic uncertainty, inflationary pressures and evolving consumer spending patterns affect demand. Heightened competition among casino operators, sportsbooks and online gaming platforms is also increasing promotional spending and putting pressure on profitability. Rising labor costs, higher gaming taxes and regulatory complexities continue to weigh on margins. Additionally, weakness in Macau's gross gaming revenues (“GGR”) is creating near-term challenges for casino operators with exposure to the region. Nevertheless, expanding digital gaming platforms, growing interest in interactive entertainment and continued adoption of online wagering offer promising growth avenues. Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. TTWO, Rush Street Interactive, Inc. RSI and Accel Entertainment, Inc. ACEL are among the stocks that could benefit from favorable industry developments.

Industry Description

The Zacks Gaming industry includes companies that own and operate integrated casinos, hotels and entertainment resorts. Some industry players also deliver technology products and services across the lotteries, electronic gaming machines, sports betting and interactive gaming markets. Some firms develop and operate gaming establishments and associated lodging, restaurants, horse racing and entertainment amenities. Many companies are involved in developing and selling gaming applications. E-sports or sporting events or tournament services, content management systems, video software, mobile applications and e-sports data platform solutions are provided as well.

Key Themes Shaping the Gaming Industry

Macroeconomic Pressure on Discretionary Spending: Persistent inflation, elevated living costs and economic uncertainty are prompting consumers to exercise greater caution with discretionary purchases. Casino visits, sports wagering and online gaming are entertainment-related activities that may experience spending pressure as households prioritize essential expenses. Lower-income consumers could be particularly sensitive to these conditions, potentially affecting regional casino operators that rely heavily on local patrons. Furthermore, companies may need to increase promotional incentives to retain customers, limiting their ability to expand margins.

Regulatory Pressure and Taxation Weigh on Industry Margins: Gaming companies are facing a complex regulatory environment as more states legalize sports betting and online casino gaming. Differences in licensing rules, tax rates and compliance requirements across jurisdictions can raise operating costs and make expansion harder. Higher gaming taxes may also reduce earnings potential, particularly for operators competing in heavily taxed markets. In addition, stricter oversight of advertising, player protection and responsible gaming practices could require further compliance investments. The emergence of prediction markets is adding to competitive pressures and raising questions about the regulatory framework governing wagering activities.

Macau's GGR Weakness Creates Challenges for Casino Operators: Macau's casino market is experiencing a slowdown, raising concerns for gaming companies with substantial regional exposure. According to Macau's Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau, GGR dropped 12.1% year over year to MOP18.52 billion ($2.29 billion) in June 2026 before declining 8.4% to MOP20.26 billion ($2.51 billion) in July. GGR subsequently fell 1.2% in both August and September, reaching MOP21.89 billion ($2.72 billion) and MOP18.06 billion ($2.24 billion), respectively. The downward trend extended into October, when revenues decreased 10% year over year to MOP21.68 billion ($2.68 billion), marking the fifth straight monthly decline. Despite the recent weakness, cumulative GGR for the first 10 months of 2026 rose 1.6% year over year to MOP208.8 billion ($25.8 billion). The prolonged softness highlights an uneven recovery and could remain a headwind for Macau-dependent casino operators.

Digital Gaming and Sports Betting Present Growth Opportunities: The increasing adoption of mobile gaming and online wagering continues to create opportunities for gaming operators to broaden their customer base. However, recent U.S. revenue trends indicate divergent performance across gaming segments. According to the American Gaming Association, sports betting revenues declined 15.6% year over year to $1 billion in August 2026, while iGaming revenues increased 12.3% to $1.03 billion. Traditional casino gaming revenues also rose 0.9% to $4.44 billion. These trends highlight the relative resilience of online casino gaming and brick-and-mortar operations amid softness in sports wagering.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Dull Prospects

The Zacks Gaming industry is grouped within the broader Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector. Carrying a Zacks Industry Rank #153 places it in the bottom 38% of more than 247 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

The industry’s position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are gradually losing confidence in this group’s earnings growth potential.

We will present a few gaming stocks that you can add to your investment portfolio, given their strong fundamentals. However, it is worth looking at the industry’s shareholder returns and current valuation first.

Industry Underperforms the S&P 500

The Zacks Gaming industry has underperformed the S&P 500 Index and the broader Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector in the past year.

The industry has declined 29.3% over this period against the S&P 500 Index’s growth of 13%. In the same time frame, the sector has declined 6.2%.

1-Year Price Performance

Gaming Industry's Valuation

Since gaming companies are debt-laden, valuing them based on the EV/EBITDA (Enterprise Value/ Earnings before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortization) ratio makes sense. The industry currently has a trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA ratio of 13.48 compared with the S&P 500’s 16.14.

Over the past three years, the industry has traded as high as 57.44X and as low as 12.49X, with a median of 19.08X, as the chart below shows.

Enterprise Value-to-EBITDA Ratio (Past 3 Years)

3 Gaming Stocks to Watch

Take-Two Interactive Software: The company is poised to benefit from a strong gaming pipeline, continued demand for its popular franchises and expanding digital revenue streams. Take-Two Interactive Software's focus on developing high-quality titles, including upcoming releases, could drive player engagement and boost sales.

This Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) player’s shares have increased 10.9% in the past year. TTWO’s current-year earnings are likely to witness a gain of 68.5% year over year. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Price & Consensus: TTWO

Rush Street Interactive: The company is well-positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of online casino gaming and sports betting across regulated markets. Expansion into new jurisdictions, rising player engagement and improvements in Rush Street Interactive’s digital platforms are likely to support revenue growth.

This Zacks Rank #2 player’s shares have declined 35.9% in the past month. RSI’s current-year earnings are likely to witness growth of 64.9% year over year.

Price & Consensus: RSI

Accel Entertainment: The company is likely to benefit from the expansion of its distributed gaming operations and continued demand for the slot machine offerings at local bars, restaurants and gaming establishments. Accel Entertainment’s focus on adding new locations, upgrading its gaming terminals and enhancing player experiences could support revenue growth.

This Zacks Rank #2 company’s shares have gained 24.5% in the past month. RSI’s current-year earnings are likely to witness growth of 26.7% year over year.

Price & Consensus: ACEL

Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. TTWO, Rush Street Interactive, Inc. RSI and Accel Entertainment, Inc. ACEL are among the stocks that could benefit from favorable industry developments. Industry Description The Zacks Gaming industry includes companies that own and operate integrated casinos, hotels and entertainment resorts. Some industry players also deliver technology products and services across the lotteries, electronic gaming machines, sports betting and interactive gaming markets. Some firms develop and operate gaming establishments and associated lodging, restaurants, horse racing and entertainment amenities. Many companies are involved in developing and selling gaming applications. E-sports or sporting events or tournament services, content management systems, video software, mobile applications and e-sports data platform solutions are provided as well. Key Themes Shaping the Gaming Industry Macroeconomic Pressure on Discretionary Spending: Persistent inflation, elevated living costs and economic uncertainty are prompting consumers to exercise greater caution with discretionary purchases. Casino visits, sports wagering and online gaming are entertainment-related activities that may experience spending pressure as households prioritize essential expenses. Lower-income consumers could be particularly sensitive to these conditions, potentially affecting regional casino operators that rely heavily on local patrons. Furthermore, companies may need to increase promotional incentives to retain customers, limiting their ability to expand margins. Regulatory Pressure and Taxation Weigh on Industry Margins: Gaming companies are facing a complex regulatory environment as more states legalize sports betting and online casino gaming. Differences in licensing rules, tax rates and compliance requirements across jurisdictions can raise operating costs and make expansion harder. Higher gaming taxes may also reduce earnings potential, particularly for operators competing in heavily taxed markets. In addition, stricter oversight of advertising, player protection and responsible gaming practices could require further compliance investments. The emergence of prediction markets is adding to competitive pressures and raising questions about the regulatory framework governing wagering activities. Macau's GGR Weakness Creates Challenges for Casino Operators: Macau's casino market is experiencing a slowdown, raising concerns for gaming companies with substantial regional exposure. According to Macau's Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau, GGR dropped 12.1% year over year to MOP18.52 billion ($2.29 billion) in June 2026 before declining 8.4% to MOP20.26 billion ($2.51 billion) in July. GGR subsequently fell 1.2% in both August and September, reaching MOP21.89 billion ($2.72 billion) and MOP18.06 billion ($2.24 billion), respectively. The downward trend extended into October, when revenues decreased 10% year over year to MOP21.68 billion ($2.68 billion), marking the fifth straight monthly decline. Despite the recent weakness, cumulative GGR for the first 10 months of 2026 rose 1.6% year over year to MOP208.8 billion ($25.8 billion). The prolonged softness highlights an uneven recovery and could remain a headwind for Macau-dependent casino operators. Digital Gaming and Sports Betting Present Growth Opportunities: The increasing adoption of mobile gaming and online wagering continues to create opportunities for gaming operators to broaden their customer base. However, recent U.S. revenue trends indicate divergent performance across gaming segments. According to the American Gaming Association, sports betting revenues declined 15.6% year over year to $1 billion in August 2026, while iGaming revenues increased 12.3% to $1.03 billion. Traditional casino gaming revenues also rose 0.9% to $4.44 billion. These trends highlight the relative resilience of online casino gaming and brick-and-mortar operations amid softness in sports wagering. Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Dull Prospects The Zacks Gaming industry is grouped within the broader Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector. Carrying a Zacks Industry Rank #153 places it in the bottom 38% of more than 247 Zacks industries. The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one. The industry’s position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are gradually losing confidence in this group’s earnings growth potential. We will present a few gaming stocks that you can add to your investment portfolio, given their strong fundamentals. However, it is worth looking at the industry’s shareholder returns and current valuation first. Industry Underperforms the S&P 500 The Zacks Gaming industry has underperformed the S&P 500 Index and the broader Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector in the past year. The industry has declined 29.3% over this period against the S&P 500 Index’s growth of 13%. In the same time frame, the sector has declined 6.2%. 1-Year Price Performance Gaming Industry's Valuation Since gaming companies are debt-laden, valuing them based on the EV/EBITDA (Enterprise Value/ Earnings before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortization) ratio makes sense. The industry currently has a trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA ratio of 13.48 compared with the S&P 500’s 16.14. Over the past three years, the industry has traded as high as 57.44X and as low as 12.49X, with a median of 19.08X, as the chart below shows. Enterprise Value-to-EBITDA Ratio (Past 3 Years) 3 Gaming Stocks to Watch Take-Two Interactive Software: The company is poised to benefit from a strong gaming pipeline, continued demand for its popular franchises and expanding digital revenue streams. Take-Two Interactive Software's focus on developing high-quality titles, including upcoming releases, could drive player engagement and boost sales. This Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) player’s shares have increased 10.9% in the past year. TTWO’s current-year earnings are likely to witness a gain of 68.5% year over year. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. Price & Consensus: TTWO Rush Street Interactive: The company is well-positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of online casino gaming and sports betting across regulated markets. Expansion into new jurisdictions, rising player engagement and improvements in Rush Street Interactive’s digital platforms are likely to support revenue growth. This Zacks Rank #2 player’s shares have declined 35.9% in the past month. RSI’s current-year earnings are likely to witness growth of 64.9% year over year. Price & Consensus: RSI Accel Entertainment: The company is likely to benefit from the expansion of its distributed gaming operations and continued demand for the slot machine offerings at local bars, restaurants and gaming establishments. Accel Entertainment’s focus on adding new locations, upgrading its gaming terminals and enhancing player experiences could support revenue growth. This Zacks Rank #2 company’s shares have gained 24.5% in the past month. RSI’s current-year earnings are likely to witness growth of 26.7% year over year. headline: Should WisdomTree U.S. SmallCap Dividend ETF (DES) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
Looking for broad exposure to the Small Cap Value segment of the US equity market? You should consider the WisdomTree U.S. SmallCap Dividend ETF (DES), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on June 16, 2006.

The fund is sponsored by Wisdomtree. It has amassed assets over $2.11 billion, making it one of the average sized ETFs attempting to match the Small Cap Value segment of the US equity market.

Why Small Cap Value

Small cap companies have market capitalization below $2 billion. They usually have higher potential than large and mid cap companies with stocks but higher risk.

Carrying lower than average price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios, value stocks also have lower than average sales and earnings growth rates. While value stocks have outperformed growth stocks in nearly all markets when you consider long-term performance, growth stocks are more likely to outpace value stocks in strong bull markets.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.38%, putting it on par with most peer products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 2.3%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Financials sector -- about 25.8% of the portfolio. Consumer Discretionary and Industrials round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Tfs Financial Corp (TFSL) accounts for about 1.17% of total assets, followed by Entertainment Properties Trust (EPR) and Northwestern Energy Group Inc (NWE).

The top 10 holdings account for about 9.52% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

DES seeks to match the performance of the WisdomTree U.S. SmallCap Dividend Index before fees and expenses. The WisdomTree U.S. SmallCap Dividend Index is a fundamentally weighted index measuring the performance of the small-capitalization segment of the US dividend-paying market.

The ETF return is roughly 19.49% so far this year and is up roughly 22.78% in the last one year (as of 11/16/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $31.77 and $41.73.

The ETF has a beta of 0.91 and standard deviation of 18.28% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 508 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

WisdomTree U.S. SmallCap Dividend ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, DES is an outstanding option for investors seeking exposure to the Style Box - Small Cap Value segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

The iShares Russell 2000 Value ETF (IWN) and the Vanguard Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF (VBR) track a similar index. While iShares Russell 2000 Value ETF has $13.94 billion in assets, Vanguard Morningstar Small-Cap Value ETF has $37.42 billion. IWN has an expense ratio of 0.24% and VBR charges 0.05%.

Bottom-Line

Retail and institutional investors increasingly turn to passively managed ETFs because they offer low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency; these kind of funds are also excellent vehicles for long term investors.

headline: Should ProShares S&P 500 Ex-Technology ETF (SPXT) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
The ProShares S&P 500 Ex-Technology ETF (SPXT) was launched on September 22, 2015, and is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Large Cap Blend segment of the US equity market.

The fund is sponsored by Proshares. It has amassed assets over $373.99 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Blend segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Blend

Large cap companies typically have a market capitalization above $10 billion. Overall, they are usually a stable option, with less risk and more sure-fire cash flows than mid and small cap companies.

Blend ETFs usually hold a mix of growth and value stocks as well as stocks that exhibit both value and growth characteristics.

Costs

Expense ratios are an important factor in the return of an ETF and in the long term, cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts, other things remaining the same.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.09%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.26%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure which minimizes single stock risk, it is still important to look into a fund's holdings before investing. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Financials sector -- about 19.6% of the portfolio. Healthcare and Consumer Discretionary round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Amazon.com Inc (AMZN) accounts for about 5.83% of total assets, followed by Alphabet Inc-Cl A (GOOGL) and Meta Platforms Inc-Class A (META).

The top 10 holdings account for about 28.49% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

SPXT seeks to match the performance of the S&P 500 Ex-Information Technology & Telecommunication Services Index before fees and expenses. The S&P 500 Ex-Information Technology Index provide exposure to the companies of the S&P 500 with the exception of those companies included in the information technology sector.

The ETF has added about 10.31% so far this year and is up roughly 13.66% in the last one year (as of 11/16/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $99.02 and $113.64.

The ETF has a beta of 0.85 and standard deviation of 12.56% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 429 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

ProShares S&P 500 Ex-Technology ETF carries a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Thus, SPXT is a good option for those seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Blend area of the market. Investors might also want to consider some other ETF options in the space.

The iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV) and the Vanguard 500 Index Fund ETF Shares (VOO) track a similar index. While iShares Core S&P 500 ETF has $874.99 billion in assets, Vanguard 500 Index Fund ETF Shares has $1,042.48 billion. IVV has an expense ratio of 0.03% and VOO charges 0.03%.

Bottom-Line

An increasingly popular option among retail and institutional investors, passively managed ETFs offer low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency; they are also excellent vehicles for long term investors.

If you're interested in broad exposure to the Healthcare - Services segment of the equity market, look no further than the State Street SPDR S&P Health Care Services ETF (XHS), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on September 28, 2011.

While an excellent vehicle for long term investors, passively managed ETFs are a popular choice among institutional and retail investors due to their low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency.

Additionally, sector ETFs offer convenient ways to gain low risk and diversified exposure to a broad group of companies in particular sectors. Healthcare - Services is one of the 16 broad Zacks sectors within the Zacks Industry classification. It is currently ranked 4, placing it in top 25%.

Index Details

The fund is sponsored by State Street Investment Management. It has amassed assets over $240.63 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs attempting to match the performance of the Healthcare - Services segment of the equity market. XHS seeks to match the performance of the S&P Health Care Services Select Industry Index before fees and expenses.

The S&P Health Care Services Select Industry Index represents the health care sub-industry portion of the S&P Total Stock Market Index. The S&P TMI tracks all the U.S. common stocks listed on the NYSE, AMEX, NASDAQ National Market and NASDAQ Global Select Market. The Health Care Index is a modified equal weight index.

Costs

Since cheaper funds tend to produce better results than more expensive funds, assuming all other factors remain equal, it is important for investors to pay attention to an ETF's expense ratio.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.35%, making it one of the least expensive products in the space.

html_content:
A smart beta exchange traded fund, the Northern Trust High Yield Value-Scored Bond ETF (HYGV) debuted on 07/17/2018, and offers broad exposure to the High-Yield/Junk Bond ETFs category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

The ETF industry has traditionally been dominated by products based on market capitalization weighted indexes that are designed to represent the market or a particular segment of the market.

Market cap weighted indexes offer a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way of replicating market returns, and are a good option for investors who believe in market efficiency.

On the other hand, some investors who believe that it is possible to beat the market by superior stock selection opt to invest in another class of funds that track non-cap weighted strategies--popularly known as smart beta.

Based on specific fundamental characteristics, or a combination of such, these indexes attempt to pick stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance.

The smart beta space gives investors many different choices, from equal-weighting, one of the simplest strategies, to more complicated ones like fundamental and volatility/momentum based weighting. However, not all of these methodologies have been able to deliver remarkable returns.

Fund Sponsor & Index

The fund is managed by Northern Trust Etfs. HYGV has been able to amass assets over $1.01 billion, making it one of the larger ETFs in the High-Yield/Junk Bond ETFs. This particular fund, before fees and expenses, seeks to match the performance of the NORTHERN TRUST HY VLU-SCRD US CORP BD ID.

The Northern Trust High Yield Value-Scored US Corporate Bond Index measures the performance of a diversified universe of high yield, US-dollar denominated bonds of companies exhibiting favorable fundamental qualities, market valuations and liquidity.

Cost & Other Expenses

Expense ratios are an important factor in the return of an ETF and in the long-term, cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive cousins, other things remaining the same.

With on par with most peer products in the space, this ETF has annual operating expenses of 0.37%.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 7.78%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Most ETFs are very transparent products, and disclose their holdings on a daily basis. ETFs also offer diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk, though it's still important for investors to research a fund's holdings.

When you look at individual holdings, Cashaccounts for about 2.62% of the fund's total assets, followed by Tenneco Inc Callable Notes Fixed 8% 17/nov/2028 and Moss Creek Resources Holdings Inc Callable Notes-8.25%-9-1-2031.

Its top 10 holdings account for approximately 8.39% of HYGV's total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

So far this year, HYGV has added about 0.21%, and it's up approximately 1.85% in the last one year (as of 11/16/2026). During this past 52-week period, the fund has traded between $38.29 and $41.08.

The ETF has a beta of 0.43 and standard deviation of 4.90% for the trailing three-year period. With about 976 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

excerpt: A stronger dollar, rising Treasury yields and Fed rate hike bets put UUP, USDU, EUM and GLL in focus.
headline: Play U.S. Dollar's Biggest Weekly Gain in Two Months With These ETFs
html_content:
The U.S. dollar logged its strongest weekly gain in two months on Friday, hovering near a 19-month high as stronger-than-expected inflation data and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials boosted expectations of a larger interest rate hike, per Reuters. Rising Treasury yields further supported the greenback.

Strong Inflation Data and Fed Commentary Lift the Dollar

Recent U.S. economic data have strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve could deliver a larger-than-usual rate hike next month. Stronger-than-expected inflation figures, combined with hawkish remarks from Fed officials, have prompted traders to reassess the interest rate outlook.

The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% month over month on a seasonally adjusted basis, as quoted on CNBC. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy prices, increased 0.3%, exceeding economists' expectations of a 0.2% gain. In September, headline CPI rose 0.6%, while core CPI advanced 0.3%.

Meanwhile, the jobs data came in robust. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 on a seasonally adjusted basis, far exceeding the Dow Jones consensus estimate of 59,000 (per CNBC), according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) (read: U.S. Job Growth Beats Expectations in October: Sector ETFs in Focus).

Fed Rate Hike in the Cards?

Robust U.S. employment data and accelerating inflation made the case for a Fed rate hike stronger and contributed to the dollar's strength. According to the CME FedWatch tool, traders were pricing in roughly a 90% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month.

Two-year U.S. Treasury yields climbed about 34 basis points during the week to approximately 4.87%, putting them on track for their biggest weekly increase since April 2025, per the same Reuters article.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of major currencies, remained close to its highest level since April 2025. The index also recorded its third consecutive week of gains.

Dollar ETFs in Focus

Overall, rising U.S. yields, persistent inflation pressures and expectations of further Fed tightening have strengthened the dollar. Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund UUP added 1.7% last week and is up about 9% this year. WisdomTree Bloomberg US Dollar Bullish Fund USDU has added about 6.4% in the year-to-date frame.

Tough Time for Emerging Markets?

The dollar strength can weigh on emerging market investing, as countries that are reliant on the U.S. dollar may see weaker local currencies and financial systems. ProShares Short MSCI Emerging Markets EUM has gained about 5.5% over the past month.

Gold Under Pressure?

The uptick in the U.S. dollar is negative for raw materials and commodities, as these are priced in the U.S. dollar. ProShares UltraShort Gold GLL has surged about 11.3% over the past month.

headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Capital Clean Energy Carriers Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Capital Clean Energy Carriers Corp. CCEC need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the December 18, 2026 $05.00 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Capital Clean Energy Carriers, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently,Capital Clean Energy Carriers is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Transportation - Shipping Industry that ranks in the Top 11% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, no analysts have increased their earnings estimate for the current quarter, while two have dropped their estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate to move from 60 cents per share to 57 cents per share in the same time period.

Given the way analysts feel aboutCapital Clean Energy Carriers right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

excerpt: A Virtual Health Stock with a Strong Run of Positivity and a Data Storage Device Stock with Growing Analyst Earnings Optimism.
headline: Top Stock Picks for Week of November 16, 2026
html_content:
Hinge Health, Inc. HNGE operates a digital musculoskeletal (MSK) care platform designed to transform how arthritis, back pain, joint injuries, and post-surgical rehabilitation are treated. Hinge Health's expanding AI-led care platform supports an Outperform view as rapid growth increasingly translates into higher margins and cash generation. Enrollment gains, member renewals and enterprise distribution reinforce the core MSK business. The growing adoption of Migraine and GI care adds opportunities to deepen client relationships, while HingeSelect extends the platform into hybrid care. Higher guidance reflects better yield and operating discipline, giving the company room to invest while returning capital. HNGE, which went public in May 2025, is projected to double its revenue between 2025 and 2027, and its upward earnings revisions earn Hinge Health a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). The digital health firm is gaining steam as it expands its corporate clients (+28% YoY in Q3), which offer their employees access to Hinge’s growing number of AI- and wearable-boosted virtual health offerings.

It is also expanding its margins and free cash flow and diversifying far beyond Hinge’s original focus of musculoskeletal care—think arthritis, back pain, and more—through organic initiatives and acquisitions. HNGE raised its fiscal 2026 guidance after the strong report on November 2. Its upward EPS revisions earn it a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and extend a strong run of positivity.

Western Digital Corporation (WDC) develops and manufactures data storage devices and solutions. Western Digital reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter sales, margins and free cash flow, led by multi-year customer visibility and a technology-led strategy focused on areal density. Sustained growth in cloud and AI data storage as customers retain more information for longer is a plus. Its high-capacity HDDs offer attractive economics for large-scale storage, while the ePMR ramp and planned HAMR launches expand its ability to meet demand. Longer customer planning horizons improve visibility, and higher prices per terabyte support further margin gains. Strong cash generation, a net cash position and a higher dividend reinforce shareholder returns. Western Digital's fiscal 2026 performance and first-quarter fiscal 2027 results demonstrate how higher-capacity products, favorable pricing and manufacturing discipline are translating demand into greater profitability. Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for Western Digital, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 20.2% over the past month to $24.36. Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

headline: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Kinder Morgan, The Williams and MPLX LP
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 17, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Kinder Morgan, Inc. KMI, The Williams Companies Inc. WMB and MPLX LP MPLX

Industry: Oil & Gas - Pipeline

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3030140/3-oil-gas-pipeline-stocks-offering-resilience-in-uncertain-times

Unlike exploration and production operations, the midstream energy space is generally less vulnerable to fluctuations in oil and natural gas prices. Despite this, the outlook for the Zacks Oil and Gas - Production and Pipelines industry is gloomy, primarily due to the conservative spending of upstream companies, which is likely to continue hurting the demand for transportation and storage assets.

Also, heavy spending on some gas pipelines is yielding low returns. However, players in the industry like Kinder Morgan, Inc., The Williams Companies Inc. and MPLX LP are well-positioned to sail through the prevailing uncertainties.

About the Industry

The Zacks Oil and Gas - Production and Pipelines industry comprises companies that own and operate midstream energy infrastructure assets. The properties consist of extensive pipeline networks that transport crude oil, liquids and natural gas. The midstream energy players are also involved in the processing and storing of natural gas. The companies have interests in natural gas distribution utilities, serving millions of retail customers across North America. 

Some companies are ramping up investments in renewable energy and power transmission businesses. The firms invested in wind farms, solar energy operations, geothermal projects and hydroelectric facilities. Thus, with a diversified portfolio of renewable energy projects, the firms have room to generate extra cash flows in addition to stable fee-based revenues from transportation assets.

What's Shaping the Future of Oil & Gas - Production & Pipelines Industry?

High Debt Load: The industry is inherently capital-intensive, as evident from the debt-to-capitalization ratio of 58.44%, where borrowing is a common practice to finance large infrastructure projects. However, elevated leverage can constrain financial flexibility, hindering midstream energy companies' capacity to invest in new developments, navigate economic downturns, or address unforeseen costs.

Shift to Renewables: Energy majors will increasingly face challenges in providing sustainable energy to the world while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. To address the issues of climate change, there will be a gradual shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy. This will lower the demand for the partnerships’ pipeline and storage networks for oil and natural gas.

Explorers’ Conservative Capital Spending: Oil and gas exploration and production companies are facing heightened pressure from investors to focus on stockholders’ returns rather than production. This is hindering the production growth of commodities, thereby denting the demand for pipeline and storage assets.

Heavy Pipeline Spending Yields Low Returns: Some companies belonging to the industry are investing heavily in gas pipelines that generate relatively low returns, while dependence on better customer contract terms creates uncertainty over future profitability.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Gloomy Prospects

The Zacks Oil and Gas - Production and Pipelines is a 10-stock group within the broader Zacks Oil - Energy sector. The industry currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #153, which places it in the bottom 38% of more than 250 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates bleak near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Although the prospects remain unfavorable, we present a few stocks that investors can retain or keep an eye on, given their solid potential. But before that, let us take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and its current valuation.

Industry Lags S&P 500 & Sector

The Zacks Oil and Gas - Production and Pipelines industry has underperformed the Zacks S&P 500 Composite and the broader Zacks Oil - Energy sector over the past year.

The industry has jumped 11.4% over this period compared with the 13.1% surge of the S&P 500 and the 29.9% rally of the broader sector.

Industry's Current Valuation

Based on the trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-EBITDA (EV/EBITDA), a commonly used multiple for valuing oil and gas production and pipeline stocks, the industry is currently trading at 12.73X, lower than the S&P 500’s 16.14X. It is, however, above the sector’s trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA of 5.64X.

Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 15.61X, as low as 11.21X and at a median of 13.24X.

3 Oil & Gas Pipeline Stocks Well Poised to Gain

Kinder Morgan: The company is a North American midstream energy major, deriving stable fee-based revenues. KMI has strong growth potential from the increasing liquefied natural gas (LNG) demand across the globe. This is because Kinder Morgan, carrying a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), is responsible for transporting almost 40% of the natural gas that is being supplied to the LNG export facilities of the United States.

MPLX: MPLX’s midstream business comprises transporting crude oil and refined products. The partnership, with a Zacks Rank of 3, generates stable cash flows from its long-term contracts with the shippers. Its crude oil and natural gas gathering systems also generate stable fee-based revenues.

The Williams Companies: The company is also a leading midstream player, well-positioned to capitalize on increasing clean energy demand. This is because WMB has a massive network of natural gas transportation pipelines that transport roughly 33% of the total natural gas used in the United States. 

With a Zacks Rank of 3 at present, The Williams Companies also serves the rising power demand from the expanding data centers. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

headline: Bull of the Day: Ingram Micro (INGM)
html_content:
Ingram Micro Holdings Corp. INGM recently reported a record quarter on strong AI infrastructure and cloud demand. This Zacks #1 (Strong Buy) is expected to grow sales by 16.8% in 2026.

Ingram Micro is a technology company for the global information technology ecosystem. It brings products and services from technology manufacturers and cloud providers to a diversified base of business-to-business technology experts.

It offers an AI-powered digital platform, called Ingram Micro Xvantage, which offers a comprehensive business-to-consume-like experience integrating hardware and cloud subscriptions, personalized recommendations, instant pricing, order tracking, and billing automation.

Ingram Micro also offers technical pre- and post-sales professional support.

Ingram Micro Beats Again in the Fiscal Third Quarter of 2026

On Oct 29, 2026, Ingram Micro reported fiscal third quarter 2026 results and beat on the Zacks Consensus Estimate by $0.13. Earnings were $0.91 versus the Zacks Consensus of $0.78.

It was the eighth consecutive earnings beat in a row.

It was a record quarter with net sales jumping 20.8% to $15.2 billion year-over-year. Every geographic segment saw growth.

Advanced Solutions offerings increased by 40%, Client and Endpoint Solutions rose by 10%, Cloud-based Solutions increased by 31%, and Other services grew 35%.

“Our double-digit year-over-year growth is reflective of balanced strength both geographically and by line of business, but remains most robust in Advanced Solutions, including GPU and AI infrastructure as well as Cloud-based Solutions,” said Mike Zilis, CFO.

Ingram Micro Raised Full Year Guidance

With this kind of growth, it’s not surprising that Ingram Micro raised its full year guidance.

For the fourth quarter it gave a range of $1.05 to $1.15. The Zacks Consensus had been at $1.05 but now sits at $1.10 after the earnings.

Estimates are on the rise for 2026 and 2027 as well. One estimate has been revised higher for both 2026 and 2027 in the last week.

The 2026 Zacks Consensus Estimate is up $0.02 in the last week to $3.58. That is earnings growth of 23.5% as the company only made $2.90 a year ago.

The 2027 Zacks Consensus Estimate is also moving higher, with one estimate raised in the last week. The Consensus is now looking for $3.91 which would be earnings growth of another 9.2%.

Here’s what it looks like on the price, consensus, and surprise chart.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Ingram Micro is a Deep Value Stock

While the AI stocks have sold off in the last month, Ingram Micro has escaped the worst of it.

Here’s the one-month chart compared to NVIDIA.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

But the stock is still dirt cheap. Ingram Micro trades with a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 7.9. A P/E ratio under 10 usually indicates deep value.

But it has other deep value fundamentals too. The company has a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of just 0.1. That means an investor is paying just $0.10 for every $1.00 worth of sales. A true bargain.

Ingram Micro is also shareholder friendly. On Oct 29, 2026, the Board of Directors raised the quarterly dividend by 2.3% to $0.088 from $0.086 per share. The dividend is payable on Nov 23, 2026, to shareholders of record as of Nov 9, 2026.

It’s yielding 1.2%.

For investors looking for an AI Revolution stock which is cheap and flying under the radar, Ingram Micro should be on your short list.

excerpt: Housing remains in a deep freeze.
headline: Bear of the Day: Ethan Allen (ETD)
html_content:
Ethan Allen Interiors Inc. ETD continues to wait for a turnaround in the housing market. This Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) is expected to see another year of declining earnings.

Ethan Allen operates 172 retail design centers in North America, including 142 company owned and 30 independently owned centers, which offer complimentary interior design service and sell home furnishings, including custom furniture and accents, for every room in the house.

The company manufactures about 75% of its custom-crafted furniture in its own North American manufacturing facilities.

Ethan Allen Missed on the First Quarter of 2027

On Nov 9, 2026, Ethan Allen reported first quarter 2027 results and missed on the Zacks Consensus by $0.15. Earnings were $0.10 versus the consensus of $0.25.

It was the first miss in the last four quarters.

Net sales were $129.6 million down from $147 million a year ago.

Retail and Wholesale segment written orders were down 1.2% and 1.3% year-over-year, respectively, primarily due to lower design center traffic, a soft housing market, global unrest, and U.S. mid-term election uncertainty.

But the Retail written orders did rise 13.2% sequentially when compared with the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. The first quarter ended Sep 30, 2026, and the momentum continued into the month of October which saw a 0.3% increase.

The company continues to plan for the future turnaround in the business. It expects to open new retail design centers in Burlington (VT), Huntersville (NC), and Naples (FL) in fiscal 2027.

Ethan Allen Cuts the Dividend

Ethan Allen ended the quarter with $92.2 million in cash and cash equivalents. It has no outstanding debt.

The company is shareholder friendly and has paid a generous dividend, and occasional special dividends.

During the fiscal first quarter 2027, it paid $92.2 million cash dividends, including special dividends totaling $3.25 per share and a regular quarterly dividend of $0.39 per share.

However, on Nov 9, 2026, the Board of Directors announced a quarterly dividend of just $0.20 per share, which was $0.19 lower than the prior quarter.

“Years of declining earnings and insufficient investment in the business, coupled with the recent rash distribution of special dividends, have left Ethan Allen in a position where a more disciplined approach to capital allocation is essential,” said Douglas G. Bergeron, Executive Chairman.

“As we have previously emphasized, the Company must balance shareholder distributions with the investments necessary to restore growth and profitability,” he added.

If this dividend holds for the entire fiscal year, it’s $0.80 per share which is yielding 4.8%.

Earnings Are Expected to Fall Again

With the housing market in a recession since 2022, when the Federal Reserve raised interest rates sharply, Ethan Allen’s business has slowed.

Earnings have fallen double digits the last three years and are expected to fall another 44.1% this year. It’s not a surprise that the company is getting more cautious with capital allocation.

Zacks has one analyst estimate on the company and that analyst is bearish.

One estimate has been lowered in the last week for both fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 is now looking for $0.90 which is down from $1.30 just a week ago.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2028 is now looking for $1.05, down from $1.30.

Here’s what it looks like on the price and consensus chart.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Shares of Ethan Allen Plunge to Five-Year Lows

It’s a tough time in the housing industry. Shares of Ethan Allen have sold off and are now at 5-year lows.You can see how much it has lagged the Russell 2000 small cap ETF (IWM). 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

It’s not even that cheap on a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) basis. It’s still got a forward P/E of 19.4.

Investors might want to steer clear of the furniture retailers like Ethan Allen until housing starts to come out of its deep freeze.

headline: Should You Invest in the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM)?
html_content:
Looking for broad exposure to the Technology - Broad segment of the equity market? You should consider the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM), a passively managed exchange traded fund launched on March 13, 2001.

An increasingly popular option among retail and institutional investors, passively managed ETFs offer low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency; they are also excellent vehicles for long term investors.

Additionally, sector ETFs offer convenient ways to gain low risk and diversified exposure to a broad group of companies in particular sectors. Technology - Broad is one of the 16 broad Zacks sectors within the Zacks Industry classification. It is currently ranked 2, placing it in top 13%.

Index Details

The fund is sponsored by Blackrock. It has amassed assets over $9.74 billion, making it one of the largest ETFs attempting to match the performance of the Technology - Broad segment of the equity market. IGM seeks to match the performance of the S&P North American Technology Sector Index before fees and expenses.

The S&P North American Expanded Technology Sector Index comprises of North American equities in the technology sector and select North American equities from communication services to consumer discretionary sectors.

Costs

When considering an ETF's total return, expense ratios are an important factor, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts in the long term if all other factors remain equal.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.37%, making it one of the cheaper products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.16%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

While ETFs offer diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk, a deep look into a fund's holdings is a valuable exercise. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation in the Information Technology sector -- about 83.5% of the portfolio, followed by Telecom.

Looking at individual holdings, Apple (AAPL) accounts for about 9.87% of total assets, followed by Microsoft (MSFT) and Nvidia (NVDA).

The top 10 holdings account for about 57.14% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

Year-to-date, the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF has gained about 11.11% so far, and is up about 12.33% over the last 12 months (as of 11/17/2026). IGM has traded between $113.31 and $174.19 in this past 52-week period.

The ETF has a beta of 1.42 and standard deviation of 24.88% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 298 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 1 (Strong Buy), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Because of this, IGM is a great option for investors seeking exposure to the Technology ETFs segment of the market. There are other additional ETFs in the space that investors could consider as well.

State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) tracks Technology Select Sector Index and the Vanguard Information Technology Index Fund ETF Shares (VGT) tracks MSCI US Investable Market Information Technology 25/50 Index. State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF has $109.89 billion in assets, Vanguard Information Technology Index Fund ETF Shares has $133.64 billion. XLK has an expense ratio of 0.08%, and VGT charges 0.09%.

Bottom Line

headline: Is JPMorgan Diversified Return U.S. Mid Cap Equity ETF (JPME) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
Making its debut on 05/11/2016, smart beta exchange traded fund JPMorgan Diversified Return U.S. Mid Cap Equity ETF (JPME) provides investors broad exposure to the Style Box - Mid Cap Blend category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

Market cap weighted indexes were created to reflect the market, or a specific segment of the market, and the ETF industry has traditionally been dominated by products based on this strategy.

Investors who believe in market efficiency should consider market cap indexes, as they replicate market returns in a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way.

If you're the kind of investor who would rather try and beat the market through good stock selection, then smart beta funds are your best choice; this fund class is known for tracking non-cap weighted strategies.

Non-cap weighted indexes try to choose stocks that have a better chance of risk-return performance, which is based on specific fundamental characteristics, or a mix of other such characteristics.

Even though this space provides many choices to investors--think one of the simplest methodologies like equal-weighting and more complicated ones like fundamental and volatility/momentum based weighting--not all have been able to deliver first-rate results.

Fund Sponsor & Index

Managed by J.P. Morgan, JPME has amassed assets over $495.22 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs in the Style Box - Mid Cap Blend. Before fees and expenses, this particular fund seeks to match the performance of the Russell Midcap Diversified Factor Index.

The JP Morgan Diversified Factor US Mid Cap Equity Index utilizes a rules-based approach that combines risk-based portfolio construction with multi-factor security selection, including value, quality and momentum factors.

Cost & Other Expenses

For ETF investors, expense ratios are an important factor when considering a fund's return; in the long-term, cheaper funds actually have the ability to outperform their more expensive cousins if all other things remain the same.

Operating expenses on an annual basis are 0.24% for this ETF, which makes it on par with most peer products in the space.

The fund has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.78%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

ETFs offer diversified exposure and thus minimize single stock risk, but it is still important to delve into a fund's holdings before investing. Most ETFs are very transparent products and many disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

Representing 12.3% of the portfolio, the fund has heaviest allocation to the Consumer Staples sector; Healthcare and Industrials round out the top three.

Taking into account individual holdings, Skyworks Solutions Inc (SWKS) accounts for about 0.7% of the fund's total assets, followed by Kimberly-clark Corp (KMB) and Exelixis Inc Common Stock (EXEL).

Its top 10 holdings account for approximately 5.11% of JPME's total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

The ETF has added about 16.33% so far this year and is up about 19.04% in the last one year (as of 11/17/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $104.47 and $129.19

The fund has a beta of 0.88 and standard deviation of 13.60% for the trailing three-year period. With about 346 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

JPMorgan Diversified Return U.S. Mid Cap Equity ETF is a reasonable option for investors seeking to outperform the Style Box - Mid Cap Blend segment of the market. However, there are other ETFs in the space which investors could consider.

Vanguard Morningstar Mid-Cap ETF (VO) tracks CRSP US Mid Cap Index and the iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap ETF (IJH) tracks S&P MidCap 400 Index. Vanguard Morningstar Mid-Cap ETF has $106.29 billion in assets, iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap ETF has $121.93 billion. VO has an expense ratio of 0.03% and IJH changes 0.05%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Style Box - Mid Cap Blend

Bottom Line

headline: Should iShares S&P 100 ETF (OEF) Be on Your Investing Radar?
html_content:
The iShares S&P 100 ETF (OEF) was launched on October 23, 2000, and is a passively managed exchange traded fund designed to offer broad exposure to the Large Cap Blend segment of the US equity market.

The fund is sponsored by Blackrock. It has amassed assets over $19.55 billion, making it one of the largest ETFs attempting to match the Large Cap Blend segment of the US equity market.

Why Large Cap Blend

Large cap companies usually have a market capitalization above $10 billion. They tend to be stable companies with predictable cash flows and are usually less volatile than mid and small cap companies.

Blend ETFs are aptly named, since they tend to hold a mix of growth and value stocks, as well as show characteristics of both kinds of equities.

Costs

Cost is an important factor in selecting the right ETF, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive counterparts if all other fundamentals are the same.

Annual operating expenses for this ETF are 0.2%, putting it on par with most peer products in the space.

It has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 0.9%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

Even though ETFs offer diversified exposure that minimizes single stock risk, investors should also look at the actual holdings inside the fund. Luckily, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

This ETF has heaviest allocation to the Information Technology sector -- about 43.6% of the portfolio. Telecom and Healthcare round out the top three.

Looking at individual holdings, Apple (AAPL) accounts for about 10.49% of total assets, followed by Nvidia (NVDA) and Microsoft (MSFT).

The top 10 holdings account for about 50.81% of total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

OEF seeks to match the performance of the S&P 100 Index before fees and expenses. The S&P 100 Index measures the performance of the large-capitalization sector of the U.S. equity market. It is a subset of the S&P 500 and consists of blue chip stocks from diverse industries in the S&P 500 with exchange listed options & the Index represented approximately 45% of the market capitalization of listed U.S. equities.

The ETF has added roughly 6.96% so far this year and it's up approximately 8.55% in the last one year (as of 11/17/2026). In the past 52-week period, it has traded between $308.21 and $389.44.

The ETF has a beta of 1.03 and standard deviation of 15.98% for the trailing three-year period, making it a medium risk choice in the space. With about 105 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk.

Alternatives

iShares S&P 100 ETF carries a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on expected asset class return, expense ratio, and momentum, among other factors. Thus, OEF is a good option for those seeking exposure to the Style Box - Large Cap Blend area of the market. Investors might also want to consider some other ETF options in the space.

The iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV) and the Vanguard 500 Index Fund ETF Shares (VOO) track a similar index. While iShares Core S&P 500 ETF has $857.61 billion in assets, Vanguard 500 Index Fund ETF Shares has $1,022.93 billion. IVV has an expense ratio of 0.03% and VOO charges 0.03%.

Bottom-Line

An increasingly popular option among retail and institutional investors, passively managed ETFs offer low costs, transparency, flexibility, and tax efficiency; they are also excellent vehicles for long term investors.

headline: Buy 2 GMO Mutual Funds for Portfolio Diversification
html_content:
GMO is an investment management firm headquartered in Boston, MA. With nearly 50 years of experience serving a global client base of institutional investors, financial intermediaries and families, GMO offers a range of mutual funds that use a long-term, valuation-oriented approach to investing in stocks, bonds, multi-asset classes and alternatives. 

Fundamental research and quantitative analysis are used by GMO’s investment teams to identify market opportunities. Valuations are continually assessed to ensure that optimal investment decisions are made. Environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations are also incorporated into the investment approach of GMO. 

We have picked two GMO mutual funds — GMO Quality GQLIX and GMO International Equity GMOUX — which investors should buy now for the long term. These funds have a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2 (Buy), with positive three-year and five-year annualized returns, minimum initial investments within $5000 and expense ratios considerably lower than the category average. So, these funds have provided comparatively stronger performance and carry a lower fee.

GMO Quality fund invests in stocks of high-quality companies selected by GMO, with flexibility to invest across sectors, regions and market capitalizations. GQLIX advisors also invest in U.S. Treasury securities and money market instruments. 

Thomas R. Hancock has been the lead manager of GQLIX since March 23, 2009. Most of the fund’s holdings were in companies like Microsoft Corp. (7.6%), Alphabet Inc. (4.7%) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (4.5%) as of Aug. 31, 2026. 

GQLIX’s 3-year and 5-year annualized returns are 21.1% and 12.3%, respectively. Its net expense ratio is 0.62%. GQLIX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #2.

headline: Is Fidelity Equity Dividend Income (FEQTX) a Strong Mutual Fund Pick Right Now?
html_content:
Having trouble finding a Large Cap Value fund? Fidelity Equity Dividend Income (FEQTX) is a potential starting point. FEQTX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank of 2 (Buy), which is based on various forecasting factors like size, cost, and past performance.

Objective

Large Cap Value mutual funds invest in stocks with a market capitalization of $10 billion or more, but whose share prices do not reflect their intrinsic value; this value investing strategy often leads to low P/E ratios and high dividend yields, though growth levels are often curtailed. The high-growth opportunity of these funds is slowed even further, as large-cap securities are generally in stable industries with low to moderate growth prospects. Therefore, Large Cap Value funds are usually more appealing to investors who are interested in a stable income stream.

History of Fund/Manager

FEQTX is a part of the Fidelity family of funds, a company based out of Boston, MA. Fidelity Equity Dividend Income made its debut in August of 1990, and since then, FEQTX has accumulated about $6.17 billion in assets, per the most up-to-date date available. John Sheehy is the fund's current manager and has held that role since April of 2017.

Performance

Obviously, what investors are looking for in these funds is strong performance relative to their peers. This fund has delivered a 5-year annualized total return of 11.25%, and is in the middle third among its category peers. But if you are looking for a shorter time frame, it is also worth looking at its 3-year annualized total return of 18.93%, which places it in the bottom third during this time-frame.

It is important to note that the product's returns may not reflect all its expenses. Any fees not reflected would lower the returns. Total returns do not reflect the fund's [%] sale charge. If sales charges were included, total returns would have been lower.

When looking at a fund's performance, it is also important to note the standard deviation of the returns. The lower the standard deviation, the less volatility the fund experiences. FEQTX's standard deviation over the past three years is 11.4% compared to the category average of 10.97%. Looking at the past 5 years, the fund's standard deviation is 13.84% compared to the category average of 13.14%. This makes the fund more volatile than its peers over the past half-decade.

Risk Factors

Investors should note that the fund has a 5-year beta of 0.67, which means it is hypothetically less volatile than the market at large. Another factor to consider is alpha, as it reflects a portfolio's performance on a risk-adjusted basis relative to a benchmark-in this case, the S&P 500. The fund has produced a positive alpha over the past 5 years of 1.72, which shows that managers in this portfolio are skilled in picking securities that generate better-than-benchmark returns.

Holdings

Examining the equity holdings of a mutual fund is also a valuable exercise. This can show us how the manager is applying their stated methodology, as well as if there are any inherent biases in their approach. For this particular fund, the focus is mostly on equities that are traded in the United States.

Currently, this mutual fund is holding 78.59% in stocks, which have an average market capitalization of $297.74 billion. The fund has the heaviest exposure to the following market sectors:

  • Technology
  • Finance

This fund's turnover is about 53%, so the fund managers are making fewer trades than comparable funds.

Expenses

For investors, taking a closer look at cost-related metrics is key, since costs are increasingly important for mutual fund investing. Competition is heating up in this space, and a lower cost product will likely outperform its otherwise identical counterpart, all things being equal. In terms of fees, FEQTX is a no load fund. It has an expense ratio of 0.52% compared to the category average of 0.93%. FEQTX is actually cheaper than its peers when you consider factors like cost.

Investors need to be aware that with this product, the minimum initial investment is $0; each subsequent investment has no minimum amount.

Fees charged by investment advisors have not been taken into consideration. Returns would be less if those were included.

Bottom Line

Overall, Fidelity Equity Dividend Income ( FEQTX ) has a high Zacks Mutual Fund rank, and in conjunction with its comparatively similar performance, average downside risk, and lower fees, Fidelity Equity Dividend Income ( FEQTX ) looks like a good potential choice for investors right now.

excerpt: Three large-cap blend mutual funds stand out for strong three-year returns, diversified equity exposure and potential for capital appreciation and income.
headline: 3 Top-Ranked Large-Cap Blend Mutual Funds Worth Buying
html_content:
Investors looking for exposure to both value and growth stocks, while seeking returns at a lower level of risk, may consider large-cap blend mutual funds. Large-cap funds offer more stability than mid- or small-cap funds and are thus safer.

Generally, companies with a market capitalization of more than $10 billion are considered large caps. However, due to their significant international exposure, large-cap companies run the risk of being hit by global woes.

Blend funds, also called hybrid funds, owe their origin to the graphical representation of their equity style box. In addition to diversification, blend funds offer a great mix of growth and value investments.

Below, we share with you three large-cap blend mutual funds, viz.Northern Large Cap Core Fund NOLCX, Vanguard Growth and Income Fund VQNPX and Voya Growth and Income Portfolio IAVGX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund #1 Rank (Strong Buy), as we expect these to outperform their peers in the future. Investors can click here to see the complete list of funds.

Northern Large Cap Core Fund invests most of its net assets in a broadly diversified portfolio of equity securities of large-capitalization domestic and foreign companies that are traded in the United States. NOLCX advisors choose to invest in stocks that have market capitalization similar to the companies listed on the Russell 1000 Index.

Northern Large Cap Core Fund has three-year annualized returns of 24.6%. As of the end of June 2026, NOLCX had 153 issues and invested 8.2% of its net assets in NVIDIA.

Vanguard Growth and Income Fund seeks capital appreciation along with dividend income higher than the return of the Standard & Poor's 500 Index by investing most of its net assets in common stocks that are part of the S&P 500 Index. VQNPX advisors use quantitative methods to select a group of stocks that are expected to give a higher total return than that of the index.

Vanguard Growth and Income Fund has three-year annualized returns of 23.2%. VQNPX has an expense ratio of 0.39%.

Voya Growth and Income Portfolio fund invests most of its net assets in common stocks of companies. IAVGX advisors choose to invest in companies that, according to them, have the potential for capital appreciation and income growth, or both.

Voya Growth and Income Portfolio fund has three-year annualized returns of 21.1%. James Dorment has been one of the fund managers of IAVGX since December 2015.

excerpt: Wolverine (WWW) is at a 52-week high, but can investors hope for more gains in the future? We take a look at the company's fundamentals for clues.
headline: Wolverine World Wide, Inc. (WWW) Soars to 52-Week High, Time to Cash Out?
html_content:
Shares of Wolverine World Wide (WWW) have been strong performers lately, with the stock up 30.2% over the past month. The stock hit a new 52-week high of $25.6 in the previous session. Wolverine has gained 39.3% since the start of the year compared to the -7.9% gain for the Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector and the -34.6% return for the Zacks Shoes and Retail Apparel industry.

What's Driving the Outperformance?

The stock has a great record of positive earnings surprises, as it hasn't missed our earnings consensus estimate in any of the last four quarters. In its last earnings report on November 12, 2026, Wolverine reported EPS of $0.79 versus consensus estimate of $0.46.

For the current fiscal year, Wolverine is expected to post earnings of $1.93 per share on $2.01 in revenues. This represents a 44.03% change in EPS on a 7.3% change in revenues. For the next fiscal year, the company is expected to earn $1.93 per share on $2.11 in revenues. This represents a year-over-year change of 0.1% and 4.95%, respectively.

Valuation Metrics

Wolverine may be at a 52-week high right now, but what might the future hold for the stock? A key aspect of this question is taking a look at valuation metrics in order to determine if the company has run ahead of itself.

On this front, we can look at the Zacks Style Scores, as these give investors a variety of ways to comb through stocks (beyond looking at the Zacks Rank of a security). The individual style scores for Value, Growth, Momentum and the combined VGM Score run from A through F. The idea behind the style scores is to help investors pick the most appropriate Zacks Rank stocks based on their individual investment style.

Wolverine has a Value Score of C. The stock's Growth and Momentum Scores are B and A, respectively, giving the company a VGM Score of A.

In terms of its value breakdown, the stock currently trades at 13.1X current fiscal year EPS estimates, which is not in-line with the peer industry average of 13.4X. On a trailing cash flow basis, the stock currently trades at 15X versus its peer group's average of 11.1X. Additionally, the stock has a PEG ratio of 1.46. This isn't enough to put the company in the top echelon of all stocks we cover from a value perspective.

Zacks Rank

We also need to look at the Zacks Rank for the stock, as this supersedes any trend on the style score front. Fortunately, Wolverine currently has a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy) thanks to favorable earnings estimate revisions from covering analysts.

Since we recommend that investors select stocks carrying Zacks Rank of 1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy) and Style Scores of A or B, it looks as if Wolverine meets the list of requirements. Thus, it seems as though Wolverine shares could have a bit more room to run in the near term.

excerpt: The Zacks Style Scores offers investors a way to easily find top-rated stocks based on their investing style. Here's why you should take advantage.
headline: Here's Why ANI Pharmaceuticals (ANIP) is a Strong Value Stock
html_content:
Taking full advantage of the stock market and investing with confidence are common goals for new and old investors, and Zacks Premium offers many different ways to do both.

Featuring daily updates of the Zacks Rank and Zacks Industry Rank, full access to the Zacks #1 Rank List, Equity Research reports, and Premium stock screens, the research service can help you become a smarter, more self-assured investor.

Zacks Premium includes access to the Zacks Style Scores as well.

What are the Zacks Style Scores?

The Zacks Style Scores is a unique set of guidelines that rates stocks based on three popular investing types, and were developed as complementary indicators for the Zacks Rank. This combination helps investors choose securities with the highest chances of beating the market over the next 30 days.

Based on their value, growth, and momentum characteristics, each stock is assigned a rating of A, B, C, D, or F. The better the score, the better chance the stock will outperform; an A is better than a B, a B is better than a C, and so on.

The Style Scores are broken down into four categories:

Value Score

For value investors, it's all about finding good stocks at good prices, and discovering which companies are trading under their true value before the broader market catches on. The Value Style Score utilizes ratios like P/E, PEG, Price/Sales, Price/Cash Flow, and a host of other multiples to help pick out the most attractive and discounted stocks.

Growth Score

Growth investors are more concerned with a stock's future prospects, and the overall financial health and strength of a company. Thus, the Growth Style Score analyzes characteristics like projected and historic earnings, sales, and cash flow to find stocks that will see sustainable growth over time.

Momentum Score

Momentum traders and investors live by the saying "the trend is your friend." This investing style is all about taking advantage of upward or downward trends in a stock's price or earnings outlook. Employing factors like one-week price change and the monthly percentage change in earnings estimates, the Momentum Style Score can indicate favorable times to build a position in high-momentum stocks.

VGM Score

What if you like to use all three types of investing? The VGM Score is a combination of all Style Scores, making it one of the most comprehensive indicators to use with the Zacks Rank. It rates each stock on their combined weighted styles, which helps narrow down the companies with the most attractive value, best growth forecast, and most promising momentum.

How Style Scores Work with the Zacks Rank

A proprietary stock-rating model, the Zacks Rank utilizes the power of earnings estimate revisions, or changes to a company's earnings outlook, to help investors create a successful portfolio.

It's highly successful, with #1 (Strong Buy) stocks producing an unmatched +23.7% average annual return since 1988. That's more than double the S&P 500. But because of the large number of stocks we rate, there are over 200 companies with a Strong Buy rank, plus another 600 with a #2 (Buy) rank, on any given day.

With more than 800 top-rated stocks to choose from, it can certainly feel overwhelming to pick the ones that are right for you and your investing journey.

That's where the Style Scores come in.

You want to make sure you're buying stocks with the highest likelihood of success, and to do that, you'll need to pick stocks with a Zacks Rank #1 or #2 that also have Style Scores of A or B. If you like a stock that only has a #3 (Hold) rank, it should also have Scores of A or B to guarantee as much upside potential as possible.

As mentioned above, the Scores are designed to work with the Zacks Rank, so any change to a company's earnings outlook should be a deciding factor when picking which stocks to buy.

A stock with a #4 (Sell) or #5 (Strong Sell) rating, for instance, even one with Scores of A and B, will still have a declining earnings forecast, and a greater chance its share price will fall too.

Thus, the more stocks you own with a #1 or #2 Rank and Scores of A or B, the better.
