excerpt: SLB secures a long-term offshore drilling services contract with Var Energi in Norway, boosting revenue visibility and growth opportunities through 2034.
headline: SLB Expands Norway Footprint With Var Energi Offshore Drilling Deal
html_content:
Var Energi has selected SLB SLB as its primary integrated drilling services supplier for two offshore rigs on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. The agreement strengthens SLB’s offshore presence and provides opportunities for long-term revenue generation through sustained drilling operations.

Long-Term Contract Enhances SLB’s Revenue Visibility

The agreement covers an initial four-year period, with four additional one-year extension options that could keep operations running through 2034. SLB will support exploration and development drilling aboard the Transocean Barents and Deepsea Bergen rigs.

The long contract duration strengthens SLB’s long-term backlog visibility and supports sustained demand for its drilling technologies and services.

Integrated Services Support SLB’s Operational Efficiency

SLB will integrate technical expertise, digital workflows and operational execution to streamline well delivery.

The approach aims to accelerate decision-making, improve drilling consistency and enhance operational efficiency, strengthening SLB’s competitive positioning in complex offshore environments.

Expanded Partnership Boosts SLB’s Growth Potential

The selection builds on SLB’s existing relationship with Var Energi, encompassing digital well planning and subsea production systems through its OneSubsea joint venture.

The expanded engagement creates opportunities to deploy a broader range of technology and deepen customer relationships.

What Does SLB’s New Contract Signal for Investors?

From an investment perspective, the agreement reinforces SLB’s long-term revenue opportunities, customer relationships and international offshore exposure.

The benefits depend on project execution, utilization levels and the exercise of extension options. SLB’s expanding presence in technologically demanding offshore markets strengthens the business model, improves revenue visibility and enhances its attractiveness to investors.

SLB’s Zacks Rank & Key Picks

SLB currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

SLB’s latest offshore drilling agreement highlights the importance of sustained exploration activity, advanced drilling technologies and efficient project execution. These factors influence investment opportunities across the broader energy sector, particularly as higher oil prices encourage upstream spending and strengthen demand for drilling services.

Some better-ranked energy sector stocks include Patterson-UTI Energy, Inc. PTEN, APA Corporation APA and Woodside Energy Group Ltd WDS. WDS currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), while PTEN and APA carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) each. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Patterson-UTI provides drilling and completion services to oil and gas producers, primarily in the United States. In the third quarter of 2026, PTEN reported a 9% sequential increase in revenues to $1.3 billion, benefiting from stronger drilling and completion demand. Higher service pricing and anticipated rig reactivations position PTEN for improved financial performance and free cash flow generation in 2027.

APA explores and produces oil and natural gas, with operations in the United States, Egypt and the North Sea. APA generated free cash flow of $699 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from $339 million a year ago. Supported by strong operational performance and higher commodity realizations, APA raised its 2026 free cash flow outlook to approximately $2.9 billion and outlined a preliminary $2.5 billion capital budget for 2027, including investment in the GranMorgu offshore development.

Woodside Energy is a global oil and natural gas producer with offshore operations and major development projects in Australia and international markets. WDS advances its offshore growth strategy, with the Trion project targeting first oil in 2028. Progress on this development strengthens WDS’ production outlook and supports earnings growth.

Beyond Nvidia: AI's Second Wave Is Here

The AI revolution has already minted millionaires. But the stocks everyone knows about aren't likely to keep delivering the biggest profits. AI’s second wave is moving from infrastructure to implementation and these companies are at the forefront of this transition, positioned to become what Amazon and Google were to the internet era.

excerpt: Investors need to pay close attention to LUV stock based on the movements in the options market lately.
headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Southwest Airlines Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Southwest Airlines Co. LUV need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the January 15, 2026 $12.50 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Southwest Airlines, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently,Southwest Airlines is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Transportation - Airline Industry that ranks in the Bottom 6% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, no analysts have increased their earnings estimate for the current quarter, while eight have dropped their estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate to move from $1.29 per share to 72 cents per share in the same time period.

Given the way analysts feel aboutSouthwest Airlines right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

Check out the simple yet high-powered approach that Zacks Executive VP Kevin Matras has used to close recent double and triple-digit winners. In addition to impressive profit potential, these trades can actually reduce your risk.

excerpt: While high vehicle prices, rising interest rates and tariffs remain concerns, domestic auto industry players like F, RIVN and HOG are worth watching.
headline: 3 Domestic Auto Stocks to Watch Amid Weak Demand, High Borrowing Costs
html_content:
The Zacks Domestic Auto industry faces a challenging outlook as weakening consumer confidence, record vehicle prices and rising financing costs weigh on affordability and demand. Higher interest rates could make vehicle purchases even more expensive heading into 2027, particularly for lower-credit buyers. While EV sales have shown some signs of recovery, the end of federal tax credits raises questions about the sustainability of demand growth. Meanwhile, trade tensions and tariffs are adding to manufacturing costs, leaving automakers to balance margin protection with competitive pricing.

Despite industry headwinds, Ford F, Rivian Automotive RIVN and Harley-Davidson HOG are leveraging new growth opportunities, operational improvements and disciplined cost management to navigate a challenging market.

Industry Overview

The Zacks Domestic Auto industry includes companies involved in the design, manufacturing and sale of vehicles worldwide. These range from passenger cars and crossover vehicles to sport utility vehicles, trucks, vans, motorcycles and electric vehicles. The industry is highly cyclical and closely tied to consumer spending, while also supporting a large employment base. At the same time, it is undergoing a major transformation as automakers invest heavily in new technologies. The role of software, electrification and digital connectivity is reshaping how vehicles are developed and sold. Many companies also operate engine and transmission plants and invest in research, development and testing of electric and autonomous vehicles.

Factors Shaping the Industry Dynamics

Weak Consumer Demand and Affordability Woes: The U.S. auto market is facing a challenging demand environment. Per Cox Automotive, October's seasonally adjusted annual sales rate (SAAR) slipped to 15.5 million vehicles, its lowest pace since January, compared with 16 million in September and 15.7 million a year earlier. Weak consumer confidence has added to concerns about demand, putting Cox Automotive's 16.1-million-unit full-year forecast at risk. Affordability is a big hurdle, with average new-vehicle transaction prices hitting a record $51,109 in October, per Kelly Blue Book. Inflation, fuel costs and consumer sentiment will influence spending in the final two months of the year.

Rising Interest Rates and Higher Financing Costs: Borrowing costs are set to put further pressure on vehicle demand. The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points in September 2026, its first increase in three years, with another hike expected in December. Stronger employment data and persistent inflation have reinforced expectations of tighter monetary policy. Auto loan rates are already reflecting this trend, with new-vehicle financing averaging around 10.5% in October and used-car loans nearing 15%, per Cox Automotive. Higher EMIs could further strain affordability in 2027, particularly for near-prime and subprime buyers.

Trade Tensions Add to Cost and Pricing Pressures: U.S. automakers face growing uncertainty from strained trade relations with Canada, a key market and manufacturing partner. The share of new vehicles sold in Canada that were built in the United States fell to 28.4% in the first half of 2026, down from 35.4% a year earlier, per JD Power Canada data as cited in Fortune. Tariffs on vehicles, auto parts and metals are raising production costs for manufacturers, including General Motors and Stellantis. Some of these costs are being passed on to buyers through higher prices and fewer incentives. Further tariff increases in 2027 could deepen the pressure on both demand and margins.

EV Growth Faces Challenges:The U.S. EV market is showing some resilience, although the recovery remains uneven. Third-quarter sales reached 262,649 units, up 6.1% sequentially and the highest quarterly volume since the third quarter of 2025. October also marked the first year-over-year increase in new EV sales in 2026, with 83,262 units sold, up 3%. However, sales fell 3.9% from September, while EV penetration slipped to 6.2% from 6.5%, per Cox Automotive. Rising inventory and the expiration of federal tax credits highlight the industry's continued dependence on competitive pricing and incentives to sustain demand.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Glum Prospects

The Zacks Automotive – Domestic industry is part of the broader Zacks Auto-Tires-Trucks sector. The industry currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #219, which places it in the bottom 11% of more than 245 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

The industry’s positioning in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are getting pessimistic about this group’s earnings growth potential. Over the past year, the industry's earnings estimate for 2026 and 2027 has declined 40% and 43%, respectively.

Despite that, we will present a couple of stocks that you might consider adding to your watchlist. But before that, let us discuss the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture.

Industry Tops Sector, Lags S&P 500

The Domestic Auto industry has outperformed the auto sector but underperformed the Zacks S&P 500 composite over the past year. The industry has returned 7.5% compared with the sector and the S&P 500’s growth of 0.9% and 13.8%, respectively.

One-Year Price Performance

Industry's Current Valuation

Since automotive companies are debt-laden, it makes sense to value them based on the EV/EBITDA (Enterprise Value/Earnings before Interest Tax Depreciation and Amortization) ratio. On the basis of the trailing 12-month enterprise value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA), the industry is currently trading at 46.99X compared with the S&P 500’s 16.23X and the sector’s 26.37X. Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 69.8X, as low as 10.28X and at a median of 31.89X, as the chart below shows.

EV/EBITDA Ratio (Past Five Years)

3 Stocks to Keep an Eye On

Ford: The company’s strong position in the high-margin truck and SUV segments remains a key competitive advantage. The F-Series maintained its lead in retail market share among full-size truck brands in the third quarter of 2026. Beyond vehicle sales, the legacy automaker is building higher-margin, recurring revenue streams through its software, services and parts businesses. Ford Energy also offers an opportunity to expand into energy storage by leveraging the company's battery manufacturing capabilities.

Cost discipline and financial flexibility provide further support. Ford ended the third quarter with $25.3 billion in cash and $46.4 billion in liquidity and remains on track to achieve $1 billion in material and warranty cost savings, excluding tariffs and Novelis. Its roughly 5% dividend yield adds to its appeal for income-focused investors.

Ford stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for F’s 2026 EPS moved north by 4 cents in the past 30 days to $1.90, implying year-over-year growth of 74%. The company surpassed earnings estimates in three of the trailing four quarters.

Price & Consensus: F

You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Rivian: This EV maker is gaining traction with its R2 SUV, which emerged as its best-selling model in the third quarter of 2026, surpassing the R1 lineup and electric delivery vans. Total deliveries jumped 46% year over year to a record 19,248 vehicles, prompting the company to raise its 2026 delivery outlook to 67,000-70,000 units. As R2 production ramps up, higher factory utilization should improve cost absorption and support profitability. Management expects the model to reach a positive automotive gross margin exit rate by year-end.

Beyond vehicle sales, Rivian has growth opportunities through its partnerships with Volkswagen, Uber and Amazon, spanning software development, autonomous mobility and commercial delivery vehicles. These relationships could diversify revenue streams and strengthen its long-term growth prospects.

Rivian stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for RIVN’s 2026 and 2027 bottom line implies year-over-year improvement of 15% and 16%, respectively. The company surpassed earnings estimates in each of the trailing four quarters.

Price & Consensus: RIVN

Harley-Davidson: The company’s efforts to bring wholesale shipments in line with retail demand and improve dealer profitability are supporting its recovery. North American retail sales rose 9% in the third quarter of 2026, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of growth, with new models such as Super Glide and Deadwood helping drive demand. The shift toward an asset-light model at Harley-Davidson Financial Services could improve capital efficiency and reduce balance-sheet exposure.

Meanwhile, restructuring and cost-control initiatives remain central to the earnings recovery strategy. The motorcycle giant is on track to achieve $150 million in fixed-cost savings and targets at least $350 million in HDMC-adjusted EBITDA in 2027. Financial flexibility also remains healthy, with consolidated cash and equivalents of $2.1 billion at the end of September 2026, up from $1.8 billion a year earlier.

Harley-Davidson stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for HOG’s 2026 and 2027 revenues implies year-over-year improvement of 5% and 1.3%, respectively. The company’s EPS estimate for the next year implies growth of 150% from 2026 projected levels.

Price & Consensus: HOG

The AI revolution has already minted millionaires. But the stocks everyone knows about aren't likely to keep delivering the biggest profits. AI’s second wave is moving from infrastructure to implementation and these companies are at the forefront of this transition, positioned to become what Amazon and Google were to the internet era.

Tariffs on vehicles, auto parts and metals are raising production costs for manufacturers, including General Motors and Stellantis. Some of these costs are being passed on to buyers through higher prices and fewer incentives. Further tariff increases in 2027 could deepen the pressure on both demand and margins. Third-quarter sales reached 262,649 units, up 6.1% sequentially and the highest quarterly volume since the third quarter of 2025. October also marked the first year-over-year increase in new EV sales in 2026, with 83,262 units sold, up 3%. However, sales fell 3.9% from September, while EV penetration slipped to 6.2% from 6.5%, per Cox Automotive. Rising inventory and the expiration of federal tax credits highlight the industry's continued dependence on competitive pricing and incentives to sustain demand. The industry currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #219, which places it in the bottom 11% of more than 245 Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1. The industry’s positioning in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are getting pessimistic about this group’s earnings growth potential. Over the past year, the industry's earnings estimate for 2026 and 2027 has declined 40% and 43%, respectively. Despite that, we will present a couple of stocks that you might consider adding to your watchlist. But before that, let us discuss the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture. The industry has returned 7.5% compared with the sector and the S&P 500’s growth of 0.9% and 13.8%, respectively. Ford Energy also offers an opportunity to expand into energy storage by leveraging the company's battery manufacturing capabilities. Cost discipline and financial flexibility provide further support. Ford ended the third quarter with $25.3 billion in cash and $46.4 billion in liquidity and remains on track to achieve $1 billion in material and warranty cost savings, excluding tariffs and Novelis. excerpt: Retail Sales Increased in Line with Expectations
headline: Retail Sales Increased in Line with Expectations
html_content:
Pre-market futures are mixed at this hour, following yet another day lower on Monday: yesterday’s close showed a -1.4% slide on the Dow, -2% on the S&P 500 and -2.5% on the Nasdaq. Currently, we’re -309 points on the Dow, -1.75 points on the S&P 500 and +103 on the tech-heavy Nasdaq. The small-cap Russell 2000 is -9 points at this hour.

Spot oil prices and bond yields are staying where they have been, generally, so there’s not much newsworthy going on there. Interest is being drawn, magnet-like, to the NVIDIA (NVDA) earnings release later this afternoon. Plenty of what we’ve got going on in the market this morning is “wait and see.”

Retail Sales, Import & Export Numbers Out for October

We saw a slowdown in October Retail Sales this morning, with headline coming in at +0.2% — as expected, but down from the +0.8% from September and +1.3% from August. Subtracting high-ticket-price autos, this buoys somewhat to +0.6% (from +1.1% the prior month). Gasoline sales rose +1.5% on a -1% dip in prices at the pump last month.

Import Prices were a bit higher than expected at +1.1% for October, in-line with the previous month’s tally. Expectations were for +0.7% import price growth. Non-fuel prices came in at +0.8%, up 30 basis points (bps) month over month. It would appear the longer-term fuel import price hikes have permeated other parts of the import economy. Foreign exporters appear to not be absorbing tariff costs, and are passing them along.

Exports for October also came in at +1.1% — much higher than the +0.3% analysts were expecting, but well below the +2.4% export growth for September. For now, it look like we’re fairly “even Steven” on the import/export market ahead of the all-important holiday shopping season.

Earnings Reports Ahead of the Opening Bell: DIS, HD

The Walt Disney Co. (DIS) reported fiscal Q4 earnings ahead of today’s open, beating expectations on the bottom line by a solid dime to $1.77 per share, while revenues of $25.95 billion outpaced estimates by +2.74%. Strength in streaming, theme parks and sports led to the healthy quarter numbers, but shares are down -1.3% on the news as forecasts on slowing theme park visits are seeing investors look elsewhere.

The Home Depot (HD) also released its earnings report this morning, matching the Zacks consensus $3.86 per share on revenues of $43.4 billion which surpassed forecasts by +1.59%. The company was able to raised prices, and to their sales growth, but Home Depot visits fell in the quarter. The continuing sluggish housing market will likely keep visits lighter going forward. Shares are down -2.28% on the news.

NVIDIA Reports Q3 Earnings After the Close

The biggest news in the world of AI over the past week is the saga of CEO Jensen Huang, which has led to his departure from the company. This is such a fresh development that it’s unlikely today’s conference call after NVIDIA’s earnings numbers are released will be able to point investors in a firm direction.

Thus, we’ll stick with the estimates: the Zacks consensus expects earnings of $2.50 per share — +92.31% above their year-ago tally. Revenues are no slouch, either: $108.19 billion is forecast for the company’s Q3, ended October. NVIDIA has a string of five-straight earnings beats, and it continues to be the prime player in the AI space.

But what portends for the future at the company? That’s what investors will be really wanting to know.

Beyond Nvidia: AI's Second Wave Is Here

The AI revolution has already minted millionaires. But the stocks everyone knows about aren't likely to keep delivering the biggest profits. AI’s second wave is moving from infrastructure to implementation and these companies are at the forefront of this transition, positioned to become what Amazon and Google were to the internet era.

excerpt: BIDU's Q3 earnings call highlights 94% AI Cloud Infra growth, longer GPU Cloud contracts and ad weakness as AI investments weigh on near-term profitability.
headline: Baidu Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Cloud Growth and Ad Pressure
html_content:
Baidu, Inc. BIDU expects AI cloud expansion to increasingly offset advertising weakness, but executives cautioned that the search overhaul and continued AI spending will constrain near-term profitability. The third quarter of 2026 earnings call emphasized longer customer commitments, improving cloud economics and disciplined investment.

Adjusted earnings of $1.01 per ADS exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 85 cents. Revenues of $4.60 billion fell short of the consensus estimate of $4.61 billion.

Baidu, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Baidu, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Baidu, Inc. Quote

BIDU Secures Longer Cloud Commitments

CEO Robin Li expects AI Cloud Infra to sustain rapid growth in coming quarters. Revenues increased 94% year over year to RMB 8.2 billion, led by GPU Cloud's 191% growth.

Responding to Citigroup, AI Cloud group executive vice president Dou Shen said customers increasingly embed AI in core operations, creating recurring training and inference requirements. Relationships are expanding into storage and networking.

Li said that the three largest GPU Cloud customers by contract value renewed for multiyear terms. One renewal term was six times longer, improving demand visibility alongside increased prepayments.

Baidu Faces Continued Advertising Pressure

Answering UBS, chief financial officer (CFO) Haijian warned that macroeconomic conditions, competition and the AI search transformation will keep advertising under considerable pressure.

He also said that stronger engagement will take time to translate into revenues. User experience remains the priority over near-term monetization. Online marketing revenues declined 22% year over year to RMB 11.9 billion.

Haijian also expects near-term profit and margin pressure as investment continues in infrastructure, chips and foundation models. Addressing JPMorgan, Shen identified better revenue mix, utilization and integrated technology optimization as drivers of longer-term cloud margin expansion.

BIDU Links Spending to Demand and Cash Collection

Responding to Jefferies, Haijian said that third-quarter capital expenditures decreased by RMB 4 billion sequentially. Previously built computing reserves and higher utilization supported cloud growth despite lower spending.

For the fourth quarter and 2027, he plans to use existing capacity further and align new investment with customer demand and cash collection cycles.

Capital returns remain part of that balance. Haijian expects the first dividend declaration before year-end, subject to board approval and market conditions. Baidu has repurchased $373 million of shares since the beginning of 2026.

Baidu Prioritizes Applications in Model Development

In response to Goldman Sachs, Li said that ERNIE investment will target capabilities needed by Baidu's applications while improving training efficiency. ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview supports coding and complex tasks across professional software and tools.

Li outlined two routes to returns: better internal applications at lower cost and external model services through Qianfan's model-as-a-service platform.

Asked by Macquarie about Kunlunxin, Li confirmed its listing process was advancing. He expects M100 inference chips to enter volume production soon and plans M300 for ultra-large multimodal models next year.

BIDU Keeps Agent Monetization in Development

Responding to BofA Securities, Li described AI-native application monetization as an early-stage effort, with models varying by users, tasks and value delivered.

Li emphasized reliable task completion and measurable productivity gains. His current priority is building products that attract users and retain them, with willingness to pay tied to useful outcomes.

Li reported that DuMate's September monthly active users increased more than 30-fold quarter over quarter without large-scale marketing campaigns. AI Applications revenues were RMB 2.6 billion, flat year over year.

Baidu Balances AI Expansion With Investment Returns

Haijian framed the company's direction around maintaining necessary AI investment while improving efficiency and returns. Cloud's growing contribution remains central to his medium- to long-term revenue and profit outlook.

Li's application-driven approach places product usefulness and customer adoption at the center of continued model development, with monetization progressing alongside those capabilities.

BIDU's Zacks Rank and Style Scores

Baidu presently carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), an unfavorable near-term signal in the estimate-revision-based framework. Its Momentum Score of B indicates stronger momentum characteristics, but does not override the weak rank.

You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

The Value Score of C reflects a middle-tier value assessment, while the Growth Score of F indicates weak growth characteristics. The VGM Score of D combines value, growth and momentum into a weaker overall style assessment. The Zacks Rank can change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the results.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren’t winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks’ Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

excerpt: LMND's expansion in Europe, backed by AI-driven insurance and strategic partnerships, offers long-term growth potential despite regulatory and competitive hurdles.
headline: Can Europe Expansion Become a Long-Term Growth Driver for Lemonade?
html_content:
Lemonade Inc. LMND has significant growth opportunities in Europe, where its AI-powered, digital-first insurance platform could help it gain traction in traditional insurance markets. With an established presence in Germany, the Netherlands and France, the company can diversify its revenue streams and reduce reliance on the U.S. market. Its expansion of homeowners insurance in France, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom, supported by partnerships with BNP Paribas Cardif and Aviva, strengthens its growth prospects.

Europe's fragmented insurance landscape and growing demand for convenient, personalized solutions offer opportunities for Lemonade to attract customers and expand its product portfolio. Its renters, homeowners, pet and life insurance offerings also provide cross-selling opportunities.

Lemonade's AI-driven underwriting, claims processing and customer service capabilities could facilitate expansion without a proportional increase in operating expenses. This scalability may improve operating leverage, customer acquisition efficiency and long-term profitability.

Moreover, geographic diversification could mitigate exposure to U.S.-specific competitive pressures and catastrophe-related risks while broadening its premium base.

However, intense competition, varying regulatory requirements and limited brand recognition remain challenges. Currency fluctuations, claims volatility and elevated customer acquisition costs could further constrain profitability.

Nevertheless, disciplined underwriting, strong customer retention and successful replication of its U.S. digital distribution model could position Europe as a meaningful contributor to Lemonade's long-term revenue growth and margin expansion.

What About Others?

Trupanion TRUP is expanding its footprint in Europe through acquisitions and strategic partnerships, targeting underpenetrated pet insurance markets such as Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Czechia, and Slovakia. Its veterinarian-direct payment model offers differentiation and opportunities to build customer loyalty. 

Meanwhile, Allianz ALIZY benefits from its established distribution network in Europe, strong brand recognition and broad insurance portfolio, enabling it to leverage existing customer relationships and cross-selling opportunities. 

While Trupanion focuses on scaling its specialized pet insurance business, Allianz can capitalize on its diversified European presence. Both Trupanion and Allianz benefit from rising insurance penetration.

LMND’s Price Performance

Shares of LMND have lost 37.7% year to date, underperforming the industry.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

LMND’s Expensive Valuation

LMND trades at a price-to-book value ratio of 7.29, above the industry average of 2.94.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for LMND’s 2026 EPS witnessed southbound movement in the last 30 days while that for 2027 EPS moved north in the same time.

excerpt: MDU raises its five-year capital investment plan 12% to nearly $3.5 billion, targeting utility and pipeline expansion amid growing energy demand.
headline: MDU Resources Raises Five-Year Capital Investment Plan by 12%
html_content:
MDU Resources Group, Inc. MDU announced a five-year capital investment plan of nearly $3.5 billion for 2027-2031, representing a 12% increase from its previous $3.1 billion plan for 2026-2030. The revised plan also marks a 22% increase over capital investments during 2022-2026.

Capital Investments Boost Utility and Pipeline Growth

The spending will support infrastructure upgrades and capacity expansion across the company's regulated electric utility, natural gas distribution and pipeline businesses. The planned investments include $1.52 billion for the electric utility segment, $1.35 billion for natural gas distribution and $621 million for pipeline operations. 

Electric utility spending will focus on system upgrades, substation improvements, transmission expansion and generation projects, including the Jamestown-to-Ellendale transmission line. Natural gas distribution investments will support system modernization, customer additions and capacity expansions. Pipeline projects include the Line Section 32 Expansion and Minot Industrial Expansion. These investments are expected to support growing customer demand across MDU Resources' eight-state service territory.

However, the plan excludes the separately approved Bakken East Pipeline project, which is expected to require an additional $2.8-$3.1 billion in capital expenditures through 2031. The 350-mile pipeline is designed to transport 1.4 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas, with phased in-service dates in late 2029 and late 2030. MDU Resources is evaluating participation by financial and strategic investors while expecting to retain majority ownership and operational control.

Funding Plans Address Rising Capital Requirements

MDU Resources expects to issue approximately $70 million in equity in 2027 and $100 million in 2028, with the remaining funding expected to come from internal cash flows and debt. These estimates do not include equity needs of the Bakken East Pipeline Project. 

The company reaffirmed its 2026 earnings per share (EPS) guidance of 93 cents to $1.00 and maintains its long-term EPS growth objective of 6-8%. However, funding the additional investment in Bakken East and managing financing requirements remain important considerations for shareholders.

Higher Capital Spending Supports Utility Expansion

Rising capital investments in gas distribution networks and electric infrastructure support system modernization, capacity expansion and reliability improvements. These investments also strengthen service capabilities and address growing energy demand. Apart from MDU, several other utilities have expanded their capital investment

American Electric Power AEP increased its 2027–2031 capital investment plan by approximately 30% to $100 billion from $78 billion. The investments will target generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure to meet rising data-center and industrial demand, supporting expected annual rate base growth of more than 13% through 2031. 

Alliant Energy Corporation LNT boosted its planned capital investments for 2027–2030 by 19% to $15.9 billion. The investment will target generation, energy storage and distribution infrastructure, supporting 13% annual rate-base growth plus construction work in progress.

PPL Corporation PPL raised its 2027–2030 capital investment plan by approximately 8.7% to $25 billion. The investments will target generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure to meet rising data-center demand and electricity needs, supporting an average annual rate-base growth target of nearly 10%.

MDU’s Stock Price Performance

In the past three months, the company’s shares have declined 5.4% against the industry’s 1.9% growth.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

MDU’s Zacks Rank

MDU Resources currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

excerpt: CDE's New Gold acquisition expands its Canadian footprint and copper exposure, but ramp-up setbacks and capital demands put sustained cash growth to the test.
headline: Can Coeur's New Gold Deal Turn Canadian Ramp-Ups Into Cash Growth?
html_content:
Coeur Mining CDE has changed materially since completing its New Gold acquisition in March 2026. The deal added New Afton and Rainy River, introduced copper to the portfolio and expanded Coeur’s Canadian production base.

The question now is whether improving mine rates can turn that added scale into sustained cash growth. Early ramp-up problems reduced 2026 guidance, making operating consistency central to the payoff from the enlarged asset base.

Coeur Gains a Much Larger Canadian Production Base

New Afton and Rainy River contributed a combined $354.7 million of third-quarter revenues. The two mines also broadened Coeur beyond its legacy U.S. and Mexican operations, giving the company another source of production and cash generation.
Canada accounted for about 36% of third-quarter sales, while copper contributed $61.7 million of quarterly revenues. The larger platform gives Coeur more production capacity if underground performance continues to improve.

Agnico Eagle Mines Limited AEM provides a useful industry reference point for Canadian mine execution. The company said its third-quarter operating performance kept it on track to achieve 2026 production and cost guidance, underscoring the value of consistency across a large mining portfolio.

CDE is Seeing Better Mining Rates After Setbacks

New Afton has sustained its targeted mining rate of 16,000 tons per day after conveyor repairs. Rainy River’s underground mining rate improved sequentially from about 2,300 tons per day to 3,400 tons per day.

Those gains matter because earlier setbacks forced Coeur to lower 2026 gold guidance for both assets. New Afton’s nine-month target was reduced to 50,000-60,000 ounces from 60,000-80,000, while Rainy River’s target fell to 190,000-230,000 ounces from 230,000-275,000.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is currently pegged at 74 cents and indicates a year-over-year decline of 7.5%. 
 


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Coeur Still Faces Infrastructure and Grade Challenges

Rainy River still needs additional mining horizons to sustain its targeted underground rate into 2027. Heavy rainfall in the third quarter also increased reliance on lower-grade stockpiles, showing that higher mine rates do not remove near-term production risk.

New Afton’s conveyor failure interrupted ore delivery before repairs were completed in September. The incident shows how infrastructure disruptions can affect output even as underground performance improves.

Pan American Silver Corp. PAAS offers another relevant precious-metals comparison. It generated $377 million of attributable free cash flow in the third quarter, although lower-than-expected production at some operations also showed how mine-level execution can influence cash results.

CDE Needs Canadian Growth to Lift Capital Returns

The New Gold transaction enlarged Coeur’s invested capital before a full year of contribution from New Afton and Rainy River. Trailing 12-month return on invested capital stands at 6.1%, below the 13.5% industry median.

That gap raises the importance of converting higher mining rates into sustained production and cash gains. Coeur also expects 2026 capital expenditures of $520-$605 million, so the enlarged portfolio must generate adequate returns while the company continues funding development.

Coeur’s Ratings Reflect Growth With Execution Risk

The Canadian assets give Coeur more production capacity, but the investment case still depends on sustained operating improvement. Higher mining rates are encouraging, yet guidance reductions, infrastructure needs and capital intensity leave execution as the key variable.

CDE currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), along with a Growth Score of B, Value Score of C, Momentum Score of F and VGM Score of C. The Growth Score points to relatively favorable growth characteristics, but Style Scores complement the Zacks Rank rather than override it. The weak Momentum Score and unfavorable Rank indicate that investors still need evidence that operating progress can translate into durable earnings improvement.

excerpt: Winnebago Industries shares have been in a sustained decline amid shrinking margins and falling sales growth.
headline: Bear of the Day: Winnebago Industries (WGO)
html_content:
Winnebago Industries (WGO) is one of the best-known names in RVs and outdoor recreation, with a long history and several established brands. But a strong brand hasn’t been enough to get it through a tough cycle. High interest rates, years of built-up inflation, fragile consumer confidence and cautious dealers continue to weigh on big discretionary purchases like RVs and boats, where affordability and financing matter most.

The latest quarter confirmed it. Fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS fell 31% from a year ago to $0.49, and revenue fell 17%. Operating margin dropped to 4.2% from 7.0% a year earlier, as discounting increased and buyers shifted toward cheaper models.

WGO currently carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), making it today’s Bear of the Day.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

WGO Earnings Estimates Move Lower

The main problem is still negative earnings momentum. Current year estimates have ben lowered by 18.3% over the last 30 days, while next year EPS forecasts have plummeted 60.58% over the last 60 days.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Furthermore,Winnebago has struggled to grow sales for several years, and the outlook doesn’t change that. Current year revenue is expected to contract 0.5% this year and grow just 3.5% next year, though even that may be optimistic given the recent results.

Management is leaning on cost cuts to grow earnings while the industry’s wholesale outlook keeps getting worse. Cost-cutting can help margins for a while, but it can’t replace demand.

Bottom Line on WGO Stock

There is something to like here. Free cash flow rose to $144.6 million last year, net leverage improved to 2.2x, and the dividend yields about 4.6%. But estimates are falling, sales are flat, margins are shrinking, and the RV cycle has yet to turn.

Shares are down about 23% this year and trade well below their 52-week high of $50. A low price alone isn’t a reason to buy. I’d stay away from WGO until estimates stabilize and demand improves. Next earnings are expected December 18.

text_content: Winnebago Industries (WGO) is one of the best-known names in RVs and outdoor recreation, with a long history and several established brands. But a strong brand hasn’t been enough to get it through a tough cycle. High interest rates, years of built-up inflation, fragile consumer confidence and cautious dealers continue to weigh on big discretionary purchases like RVs and boats, where affordability and financing matter most. The latest quarter confirmed it. Fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS fell 31% from a year ago to $0.49, and revenue fell 17%. Operating margin dropped to 4.2% from 7.0% a year earlier, as discounting increased and buyers shifted toward cheaper models. WGO currently carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), making it today’s Bear of the Day. Current year revenue is expected to contract 0.5% this year and grow just 3.5% next year, though even that may be optimistic given the recent results. Management is leaning on cost cuts to grow earnings while the industry’s wholesale outlook keeps getting worse. Cost-cutting can help margins for a while, but it can’t replace demand. headline: Is Invesco Global Water ETF (PIO) a Strong ETF Right Now?
html_content:
Launched on 06/13/2007, the Invesco Global Water ETF (PIO) is a smart beta exchange traded fund offering broad exposure to the Industrials ETFs category of the market.

What Are Smart Beta ETFs?

Products that are based on market cap weighted indexes, which are strategies designed to reflect a specific market segment or the market as a whole, have traditionally dominated the ETF industry.

Investors who believe in market efficiency should consider market cap indexes, as they replicate market returns in a low-cost, convenient, and transparent way.

If you're the kind of investor who would rather try and beat the market through good stock selection, then smart beta funds are your best choice; this fund class is known for tracking non-cap weighted strategies.

This kind of index follows this same mindset, as it attempts to pick stocks that have better chances of risk-return performance; non-cap weighted strategies base selection on certain fundamental characteristics, or a mix of such characteristics.

The smart beta space gives investors many different choices, from equal-weighting, one of the simplest strategies, to more complicated ones like fundamental and volatility/momentum based weighting. However, not all of these methodologies have been able to deliver remarkable returns.

Fund Sponsor & Index

The fund is managed by Invesco. PIO has been able to amass assets over $269.1 million, making it one of the average sized ETFs in the Industrials ETFs. Before fees and expenses, PIO seeks to match the performance of the NASDAQ OMX Global Water Index.

The NASDAQ OMX Global Water Index is designed to track the performance of companies worldwide that are creating products that conserve and purify water for homes, businesses and industries.

Cost & Other Expenses

Cost is an important factor in selecting the right ETF, and cheaper funds can significantly outperform their more expensive cousins if all other fundamentals are the same.

Annual operating expenses for PIO are 0.75%, which makes it one of the more expensive products in the space.

PIO's 12-month trailing dividend yield is 0.88%.

Sector Exposure and Top Holdings

While ETFs offer diversified exposure, which minimizes single stock risk, a deep look into a fund's holdings is a valuable exercise. And, most ETFs are very transparent products that disclose their holdings on a daily basis.

Looking at individual holdings, Pentair Plc (PNR) accounts for about 9.21% of total assets, followed by Ferguson Enterprises Inc (FERG) and Ecolab Inc (ECL).

PIO's top 10 holdings account for about 59.7% of its total assets under management.

Performance and Risk

Year-to-date, the Invesco Global Water ETF has added about 1.81% so far, and is up roughly 1.72% over the last 12 months (as of 11/18/2026). PIO has traded between $42.19 $48.63 in this past 52-week period.

PIO has a beta of 0.98 and standard deviation of 15.77% for the trailing three-year period, which makes the fund a medium risk choice in the space. With about 52 holdings, it effectively diversifies company-specific risk .

Alternatives

Invesco Global Water ETF is not a suitable option for investors seeking to outperform the Industrials ETFs segment of the market. Instead, there are other ETFs in the space which investors should consider.

First Trust Water ETF (FIW) tracks ISE Clean Edge Water Index and the Invesco Water Resources ETF (PHO) tracks NASDAQ OMX US Water Index. First Trust Water ETF has $1.89 billion in assets, Invesco Water Resources ETF has $2.1 billion. FIW has an expense ratio of 0.50% and PHO changes 0.59%.

Investors looking for cheaper and lower-risk options should consider traditional market cap weighted ETFs that aim to match the returns of the Industrials ETFs

headline: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Sprout and HealthStream
html_content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 18, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Sprout Social, Inc SPT and HealthStream, Inc. HSTM

Industry: Internet Services

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3031412/buy-internet-service-players-sprout-social-and-healthstream

The ongoing digitization of the global economy is expected to support continued growth in the Internet Services industry as more consumers and businesses move online. This creates demand for a diverse range of products, services and infrastructure, including cloud platforms, software, digital commerce, online advertising and cybersecurity.

Our picks are Sprout Social and HealthStream, two high-quality businesses with innovative technology and opportunities to sustain growth despite macroeconomic headwinds. Sprout Social is shifting its focus toward larger customers, which could stabilize revenues, deepen customer relationships and support cross-selling. HealthStream, meanwhile, is leveraging technology and industry expertise to strengthen its competitive moat. Both operate in attractive markets and are incorporating AI into their offerings.
 
AI is becoming an increasingly important growth driver for the industry. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026, up 49.5% year over year, highlighting the scale of investment and adoption underway. Companies are using AI and machine learning to enhance existing products, introduce new features, improve operational efficiency and differentiate their offerings. Growing AI computing demand is also driving investment in cloud infrastructure, data centers and processing capacity, benefiting digital infrastructure and cloud-service providers. However, the extent of these opportunities varies across the industry's diverse business models.
 
A stronger economy generally supports industry demand, while macroeconomic uncertainty, inflation, tariffs, weakening consumer confidence and higher interest rates pose headwinds for the industry, especially considering its capital-intensive nature. Meanwhile, increasingly accessible AI tools are lowering barriers to entry, allowing smaller players to develop competing offerings with fewer resources but intensifying competitive pressures across the industry.
 
Valuations across the industry have declined significantly over the past six months. This, alongside rising earnings estimates, suggests that opportunities may exist among companies with sound business models, attractive growth prospects and the financial flexibility to navigate a challenging operating environment.

About the Industry

Internet - Services companies primarily rely on digital platforms, software and supporting technology infrastructure to deliver products, services and infrastructure to individual or corporate consumers. Given the increased digitalization of the world and the industry's role as a digital enabler, the range of offerings is very broad and may include ecommerce, search, social networking, cloud-based software, collaboration and business productivity solutions.

Companies generally monetize their offerings through advertising, subscriptions, licenses, usage-based charges, commissions and transaction fees. Alphabet, Baidu and Akamai are some of the larger players, while Crexendo, Inuvo, Marchex, Sify and Trivago are some of the smaller or more specialized players. Very large players (mainly Alphabet) tend to skew averages.

Factors Determining Industry Performance

  • AI Adoption Creates New Growth and Monetization Opportunities: Rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is creating significant growth opportunities across the Internet - Services industry while reshaping competition and business models. Companies are integrating generative AI into search engines, digital advertising, ecommerce platforms, cloud-based software and business productivity applications to improve personalization, customer engagement, search relevance and operational efficiency. Alphabet and Baidu are incorporating AI into search and advertising, while companies such as Sprout Social and Shopify are using it to enhance software and ecommerce offerings. AI is also creating new monetization opportunities through premium subscriptions, enterprise AI solutions, usage-based services and enhanced advertising capabilities.

 

  • Digital Consumption, Advertising and Online Transactions Drive Growth: Secular growth in digitization continues to support the Internet - Services industry, as work, entertainment, shopping and other activities increasingly move online. Rising Internet penetration, smartphone usage, social media engagement and online video consumption are expanding digital audiences and creating opportunities for advertising and monetization. Younger generations, particularly Gen Z, are accustomed to conducting more of their daily activities online, reinforcing the shift toward digital platforms. Growing digital advertising expenditure, supported by AI-powered targeting, personalization and campaign optimization, is enhancing the effectiveness of online campaigns and attracting greater marketing budgets to digital channels. Meanwhile, the expansion of ecommerce, social commerce, cross-border trade, digital payments and on-demand services is supporting transaction growth across online marketplaces, mobility and food delivery businesses. Companies such as Alphabet, The Trade Desk, Shopify, DoorDash and Uber are positioned to benefit from these trends through advertising, ecommerce and transaction-based business models. However, growing reliance on digital platforms also raises privacy and cybersecurity concerns.

 

  • Enterprise Digitalization and Cloud Adoption Support Growth: Continued digital transformation across businesses is supporting demand for cloud platforms and collaboration tools, as well as cybersecurity, data management and productivity applications. Companies’ modernization efforts increasingly involve the migration of workloads to cloud environments to improve scalability, flexibility and cost efficiency. Growing AI adoption is further driving demand for cloud computing, data storage and processing capacity, benefiting providers of cloud services and digital infrastructure. The shift toward subscription-based and usage-based pricing models also provides opportunities for recurring revenues, customer expansion and scalable growth.

 

  • Macroeconomic and Competitive Challenges Weigh on Growth: increasing macroeconomic uncertainty is leading to tighter enterprise budgets, longer sales cycles and increased scrutiny of technology spending, which are at times delaying purchasing decisions. Higher interest rates increase borrowing costs and raise the cost of funding investments across the Internet Services industry. However, smaller companies, particularly those focused on AI and infrastructure, are more exposed to these pressures because of their limited financial resources, greater dependence on external capital and lower financial flexibility, potentially widening the resource gap between them and larger players. They also have to compete for consumer attention, advertising budgets and online transactions, with the resultant pricing pressure and increase in customer acquisition costs limiting their ability to monetize their offerings and generate attractive returns. At the same time, increasingly accessible AI tools are lowering barriers to entry, allowing smaller players and new entrants to develop competing products and services with fewer resources. This creates opportunities for a broader range of companies to participate in the industry, while intensifying competitive pressures for established players.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Near-Term Pressure

The Zacks Internet - Services industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #160, which places it among the bottom 35% of more than 245 Zacks-classified industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average rank of all the member stocks, indicates that constituent companies may be undergoing some difficulties.

Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions over the past year, there have been significant improvements in both the 2026 and 2027 estimates. The 2026 estimates were growing gradually until June this year, but shot up after that. Even with the slight moderation from the September peak, they still aggregated a 77.2% increase from November 2025. The 2027 estimate jumped in April, peaked in June but has moderated only slightly since then, netting a 15.7% increase from November 2025 actuals.

Historically, the top 50% of Zacks-ranked industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1. So the industry being in the bottom 50% indicates that investor sentiments remain muted.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock-market performance and valuation picture.

Stock Market Performance Weakened Recently

The industry has returned more than both the broader Technology sector and the S&P 500 through most of the past year, starting a downward trajectory in August. The industry’s net loss of 1.4% over the past year is considerably weaker performance than the broader sector’s 6.1% gain and the S&P 500’s 10.7% gain.

Industry Valuation: Reasonable

On the basis of forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, we see that the industry is currently trading at an 18.27X multiple, which is a discount to its median value of 24X over the past year. This is close to the S&P 500’s 18.29X although a significant premium to the broader technology sector’s 16.61X. Overall, the industry has traded between a low of 17.72X and a high of 29.79X over the past year, both points being a premium to the sector. The S&P 500 has traded within a tighter range over the past year. At these levels the industry appears fairly valued.

2 Solid Bets

Sprout Social, Inc: Sprout Social, Inc. is a cloud-based software company headquartered in Chicago, IL. It provides businesses with tools to manage, analyze and optimize their social-media presence across platforms such as Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Facebook and X. Its subscription-based platform integrates content publishing, message management, customer service, social listening, influencer marketing and performance analytics into a unified dashboard.

Businesses use Sprout to schedule posts, respond to customers through a centralized inbox, monitor brand sentiment and generate data-driven marketing insights. The company is increasingly incorporating AI to automate workflows, analyze social data and help organizations turn online conversations into actionable business intelligence and more effective customer engagement strategies.

As social media evolves from a marketing channel into a broader business platform supporting customer care, brand monitoring, crisis management, sales discovery and reputation analytics, demand for integrated SaaS solutions that can manage these functions is increasing. Sprout Social is increasing its focus on large enterprises, where broader adoption across departments, higher subscription values and opportunities to expand product usage can support revenue growth.

This strategy is gaining traction, with the number of customers contributing at least $30,000 in annual recurring revenue reaching 3,925 at the end of the third quarter of 2026, up 6% year over year, while customers contributing at least $50,000 grew 11% to 2,155. Average contract value increased 12% to $18,009. Larger enterprise relationships also offer opportunities to deepen customer engagement through additional users, social profiles and product modules, supporting cross-selling opportunity, recurring revenues and customer lifetime value. As subscription revenues expand, the scalability of the SaaS model offers scope for operating leverage and margin improvement.

AI presents both competitive challenges and opportunities for Sprout. While generative AI lowers barriers to entry and enables competitors, including social media platforms, to develop their own analytics and engagement tools, Sprout's established platform, accumulated social data, data normalization capabilities and analytical infrastructure provide potential differentiation. Processing and interpreting large volumes of unstructured social data across platforms, while maintaining historical context and delivering actionable insights, requires specialized capabilities and ongoing investment.

Sprout is also embedding AI into sentiment analysis, social listening and customer engagement workflows through its Trellis agentic AI capabilities, which can automate tasks and make its platform more valuable to customers. Its ability to combine extensive social data, analytical tools and integrated workflows could help it maintain a competitive position as AI reshapes the industry. The estimated trailing 12-month subscription revenue contribution from customers with at least $30,000 in ARR grew 18% year over year to $301.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, indicating increasing revenue contribution from larger customers.

Reallocation of resources to larger, more sophisticated customers could weaken revenue and retention of smaller customers. Although the number of customers contributing at least $30,000 in ARR increased in the last quarter, it declined slightly sequentially, indicating some moderation in new customer additions within this segment.

The transition is occurring against a backdrop of macroeconomic uncertainty, tighter customer budgets, greater scrutiny of spending and more demanding purchasing approvals, which are lengthening sales cycles and weighing on both new business and customer expansion. If larger-account acquisition and expansion do not accelerate sufficiently to compensate for the slower growth in smaller customer segments, revenue growth could be muted for a prolonged period of time as the company reshapes its customer base.

Sprout topped estimates in the last quarter, with EPS beating by 50%. The 2026 estimate has increased 22 cents (20.2%) in the last 30 days while the 2027 estimate increased 28 cents (18.4%). Revenue and EPS increased 7.8% and 59.8% in 2026 and 3.9% and 38% in 2027.

The shares of this Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stock have gained 8.2% over the past year.

HealthStream, Inc. : The Nashville, TN-headquartered healthcare technology company primarily provides cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) applications to US-based healthcare providers including hospitals and other care institutions, both government and private, as well as pharmaceutical and medical device companies, nursing schools and nursing students. 

Its technology facilitates workforce development, training and learning, clinical education, competency assessment, nurse and staff scheduling, credentialing, privileging and provider enrollment. Its product portfolio also includes performance assessment and simulation-based education solutions, supported by its proprietary hStream technology platform, which facilitates interoperability across applications.

HealthStream is positioned to benefit from secular demand for trained healthcare professionals and the need for hospitals and healthcare systems to effectively deploy and manage their workforces. Its addressable market expanded 9% in 2025 to 13.7 million healthcare professionals, in addition to approximately 1,000 nursing schools and 1 million nursing students. Population growth, evolving healthcare needs, new treatment methodologies, increasing workforce complexity and regulatory training requirements support demand for its solutions.

The company is seeing broad-based strength across Learning, Credentialing and Scheduling, its three main application suites. Its Learning platform offers more than 20,000 courses from over 90 industry partners.

CredentialStream revenues grew 15% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, while ShiftWizard, its flagship scheduling application, increased 20%. The Resuscitation Suite and Competency product family grew 14% and 10%, respectively. Additionally, myClinicalExchange, which connects nursing and allied health students with clinical rotations, recorded 26.5% revenue growth.

These gains reflect demand across multiple areas of healthcare workforce management and strengthen opportunities to cross-sell complementary applications. Its investments in enterprise applications, platform capabilities and AI-enabled assessment tools strengthen its product offerings and further support cross-selling. Recent acquisitions, including Virsys12 and MissionCare Collective, are also contributing to revenue growth and broadening its capabilities.

HealthStream's SaaS business model provides a highly predictable revenue stream, with subscription services accounting for 96% of revenues in the first nine months of 2026. The company reported 10.6% revenue growth, 25.7% operating income growth, 13.6% net income growth and 13.4% adjusted EBITDA growth during this period.

As a result, management projected a slight increase in its full-year 2026 revenue guidance. Its strong balance sheet, with $115.2 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and no outstanding debt as of September 30, provides ample financial flexibility to support product development, acquisitions and other growth initiatives.

That said, higher labor costs, third-party software expenses, royalties, hosting costs and acquisition-related amortization are weighing on margins and profitability. Legacy products, which continue to account for approximately 10% of revenues, are also a drag on overall growth. Revenues from recently acquired businesses are tracking below management's expectations, raising questions about the pace of integration and returns on these investments.

Cybersecurity threats remain an ongoing concern given the sensitive healthcare information handled by the company. A recent data breach involving its credentialing product resulted in $250,000 in expenses after insurance recoveries, while privacy-related class-action lawsuits are ongoing. Although the financial impact is not expected to be material at present, the incident introduces uncertainty regarding potential litigation, remediation costs and reputational risks.

HealthStream topped EPS estimates ny 20% in the last quarter. The 2026 estimate increased 9 cents (12.5%) in the last 30 days while the 2027 estimate increased 10 cents (12.2%). Revenue and EPS increased a respective 9.2% 15.7% in 2026 and 4.5% and 13.6% 2027.

The shares of this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock have gained 13.3% over the past year.

Macroeconomic and Competitive Challenges Weigh on Growth: increasing macroeconomic uncertainty is leading to tighter enterprise budgets, longer sales cycles and increased scrutiny of technology spending, which are at times delaying purchasing decisions. Higher interest rates increase borrowing costs and raise the cost of funding investments across the Internet Services industry. However, smaller companies, particularly those focused on AI and infrastructure, are more exposed to these pressures because of their limited financial resources, greater dependence on external capital and lower financial flexibility, potentially widening the resource gap between them and larger players. They also have to compete for consumer attention, advertising budgets and online transactions, with the resultant pricing pressure and increase in customer acquisition costs limiting their ability to monetize their offerings and generate attractive returns. At the same time, increasingly accessible AI tools are lowering barriers to entry, allowing smaller players and new entrants to develop competing products and services with fewer resources. This creates opportunities for a broader range of companies to participate in the industry, while intensifying competitive pressures for established players. Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Near-Term Pressure The Zacks Internet - Services industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #160, which places it among the bottom 35% of more than 245 Zacks-classified industries. The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average rank of all the member stocks, indicates that constituent companies may be undergoing some difficulties. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions over the past year, there have been significant improvements in both the 2026 and 2027 estimates. The 2026 estimates were growing gradually until June this year, but shot up after that. Even with the slight moderation from the September peak, they still aggregated a 77.2% increase from November 2025. The 2027 estimate jumped in April, peaked in June but has moderated only slightly since then, netting a 15.7% increase from November 2025 actuals. Historically, the top 50% of Zacks-ranked industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1. So the industry being in the bottom 50% indicates that investor sentiments remain muted. Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock-market performance and valuation picture. Stock Market Performance Weakened Recently The industry has returned more than both the broader Technology sector and the S&P 500 through most of the past year, starting a downward trajectory in August. The industry’s net loss of 1.4% over the past year is considerably weaker performance than the broader sector’s 6.1% gain and the S&P 500’s 10.7% gain. Industry Valuation: Reasonable On the basis of forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, we see that the industry is currently trading at an 18.27X multiple, which is a discount to its median value of 24X over the past year. This is close to the S&P 500’s 18.29X although a significant premium to the broader technology sector’s 16.61X. Overall, the industry has traded between a low of 17.72X and a high of 29.79X over the past year, both points being a premium to the sector. The S&P 500 has traded within a tighter range over the past year. At these levels the industry appears fairly valued. 2 Solid Bets Sprout Social, Inc: Sprout Social, Inc. is a cloud-based software company headquartered in Chicago, IL. It provides businesses with tools to manage, analyze and optimize their social-media presence across platforms such as Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Facebook and X. Its subscription-based platform integrates content publishing, message management, customer service, social listening, influencer marketing and performance analytics into a unified dashboard. Businesses use Sprout to schedule posts, respond to customers through a centralized inbox, monitor brand sentiment and generate data-driven marketing insights. The company is increasingly incorporating AI to automate workflows, analyze social data and help organizations turn online conversations into actionable business intelligence and more effective customer engagement strategies. As social media evolves from a marketing channel into a broader business platform supporting customer care, brand monitoring, crisis management, sales discovery and reputation analytics, demand for integrated SaaS solutions that can manage these functions is increasing. Sprout Social is increasing its focus on large enterprises, where broader adoption across departments, higher subscription values and opportunities to expand product usage can support revenue growth. This strategy is gaining traction, with the number of customers contributing at least $30,000 in annual recurring revenue reaching 3,925 at the end of the third quarter of 2026, up 6% year over year, while customers contributing at least $50,000 grew 11% to 2,155. Average contract value increased 12% to $18,009. Larger enterprise relationships also offer opportunities to deepen customer engagement through additional users, social profiles and product modules, supporting cross-selling opportunity, recurring revenues and customer lifetime value. As subscription revenues expand, the scalability of the SaaS model offers scope for operating leverage and margin improvement. AI presents both competitive challenges and opportunities for Sprout. While generative AI lowers barriers to entry and enables competitors, including social media platforms, to develop their own analytics and engagement tools, Sprout's established platform, accumulated social data, data normalization capabilities and analytical infrastructure provide potential differentiation. Processing and interpreting large volumes of unstructured social data across platforms, while maintaining historical context and delivering actionable insights, requires specialized capabilities and ongoing investment. Sprout is also embedding AI into sentiment analysis, social listening and customer engagement workflows through its Trellis agentic AI capabilities, which can automate tasks and make its platform more valuable to customers. Its ability to combine extensive social data, analytical tools and integrated workflows could help it maintain a competitive position as AI reshapes the industry. The estimated trailing 12-month subscription revenue contribution from customers with at least $30,000 in ARR grew 18% year over year to $301.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, indicating increasing revenue contribution from larger customers. Reallocation of resources to larger, more sophisticated customers could weaken revenue and retention of smaller customers. Although the number of customers contributing at least $30,000 in ARR increased in the last quarter, it declined slightly sequentially, indicating some moderation in new customer additions within this segment. The transition is occurring against a backdrop of macroeconomic uncertainty, tighter customer budgets, greater scrutiny of spending and more demanding purchasing approvals, which are lengthening sales cycles and weighing on both new business and customer expansion. If larger-account acquisition and expansion do not accelerate sufficiently to compensate for the slower growth in smaller customer segments, revenue growth could be muted for a prolonged period of time as the company reshapes its customer base. Sprout topped estimates in the last quarter, with EPS beating by 50%. The 2026 estimate has increased 22 cents (20.2%) in the last 30 days while the 2027 estimate increased 28 cents (18.4%). Revenue and EPS increased 7.8% and 59.8% in 2026 and 3.9% and 38% in 2027. The shares of this Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stock have gained 8.2% over the past year. HealthStream, Inc. : The Nashville, TN-headquartered healthcare technology company primarily provides cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) applications to US-based healthcare providers including hospitals and other care institutions, both government and private, as well as pharmaceutical and medical device companies, nursing schools and nursing students. Its technology facilitates workforce development, training and learning, clinical education, competency assessment, nurse and staff scheduling, credentialing, privileging and provider enrollment. Its product portfolio also includes performance assessment and simulation-based education solutions, supported by its proprietary hStream technology platform, which facilitates interoperability across applications. HealthStream is positioned to benefit from secular demand for trained healthcare professionals and the need for hospitals and healthcare systems to effectively deploy and manage their workforces. Its addressable market expanded 9% in 2025 to 13.7 million healthcare professionals, in addition to approximately 1,000 nursing schools and 1 million nursing students. Population growth, evolving healthcare needs, new treatment methodologies, increasing workforce complexity and regulatory training requirements support demand for its solutions. The company is seeing broad-based strength across Learning, Credentialing and Scheduling, its three main application suites. Its Learning platform offers more than 20,000 courses from over 90 industry partners. CredentialStream revenues grew 15% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, while ShiftWizard, its flagship scheduling application, increased 20%. The Resuscitation Suite and Competency product family grew 14% and 10%, respectively. Additionally, myClinicalExchange, which connects nursing and allied health students with clinical rotations, recorded 26.5% revenue growth. These gains reflect demand across multiple areas of healthcare workforce management and strengthen opportunities to cross-sell complementary applications. Its investments in enterprise applications, platform capabilities and AI-enabled assessment tools strengthen its product offerings and further support cross-selling. Recent acquisitions, including Virsys12 and MissionCare Collective, are also contributing to revenue growth and broadening its capabilities. HealthStream's SaaS business model provides a highly predictable revenue stream, with subscription services accounting for 96% of revenues in the first nine months of 2026. The company reported 10.6% revenue growth, 25.7% operating income growth, 13.6% net income growth and 13.4% adjusted EBITDA growth during this period. As a result, management projected a slight increase in its full-year 2026 revenue guidance. Its strong balance sheet, with $115.2 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and no outstanding debt as of September 30, provides ample financial flexibility to support product development, acquisitions and other growth initiatives. That said, higher labor costs, third-party software expenses, royalties, hosting costs and acquisition-related amortization are weighing on margins and profitability. Legacy products, which continue to account for approximately 10% of revenues, are also a drag on overall growth. Revenues from recently acquired businesses are tracking below management's expectations, raising questions about the pace of integration and returns on these investments. Cybersecurity threats remain an ongoing concern given the sensitive healthcare information handled by the company. A recent data breach involving its credentialing product resulted in $250,000 in expenses after insurance recoveries, while privacy-related class-action lawsuits are ongoing. Although the financial impact is not expected to be material at present, the incident introduces uncertainty regarding potential litigation, remediation costs and reputational risks. HealthStream topped EPS estimates ny 20% in the last quarter. The 2026 estimate increased 9 cents (12.5%) in the last 30 days while the 2027 estimate increased 10 cents (12.2%). Revenue and EPS increased a respective 9.2% 15.7% in 2026 and 4.5% and 13.6% 2027. The shares of this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock have gained 13.3% over the past year.
