html_content:
Sector - Health fund seekers may want to consider taking a look at Macquarie Healthcare I (DLHIX). DLHIX bears a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank of 3 (Hold), which is based on various forecasting factors like size, cost, and past performance.

Objective

The world of Sector - Health funds is an area filled with options, such as DLHIX. Healthcare is one of the biggest sectors of the American economy, and Sector - Health mutual funds provide a great opportunity to invest in this industry. Here, funds can include everything from for-profit hospitals to pharmaceutical companies and medical device manufacturers.

History of Fund/Manager

Nomura is responsible for DLHIX, and the company is based out of New York, NY. The Macquarie Healthcare I made its debut in September of 2007 and DLHIX has managed to accumulate roughly $597.41 million in assets, as of the most recently available information. The fund's current manager, Liu Er Chen, has been in charge of the fund since September of 2007.

Performance

Of course, investors look for strong performance in funds. This fund in particular has delivered a 5-year annualized total return of 9.81%, and it sits in the top third among its category peers. If you're interested in shorter time frames, do not dismiss looking at the fund's 3-year annualized total return of 19.69%, which places it in the top third during this time-frame.

It is important to note that the product's returns may not reflect all its expenses. Any fees not reflected would lower the returns. Total returns do not reflect the fund's [%] sale charge. If sales charges were included, total returns would have been lower.

When looking at a fund's performance, it is also important to note the standard deviation of the returns. The lower the standard deviation, the less volatility the fund experiences. Compared to the category average of 12.23%, the standard deviation of DLHIX over the past three years is 14.06%. Over the past 5 years, the standard deviation of the fund is 14.2% compared to the category average of 13.88%. This makes the fund more volatile than its peers over the past half-decade.

Risk Factors

The fund has a 5-year beta of 0.5, so investors should note that it is hypothetically less volatile than the market at large. Alpha is an additional metric to take into consideration, since it represents a portfolio's performance on a risk-adjusted basis relative to a benchmark, which in this case, is the S&P 500. DLHIX has generated a positive alpha over the past five years of 1.86, demonstrating that managers in this portfolio are skilled in picking securities that generate better-than-benchmark returns.

Expenses

Costs are increasingly important for mutual fund investing, and particularly as competition heats up in this market. And all things being equal, a lower cost product will outperform its otherwise identical counterpart, so taking a closer look at these metrics is key for investors. In terms of fees, DLHIX is a no load fund. It has an expense ratio of 0.96% compared to the category average of 0.97%. DLHIX is actually cheaper than its peers when you consider factors like cost.

Investors need to be aware that with this product, the minimum initial investment is $0; each subsequent investment has no minimum amount.

Fees charged by investment advisors have not been taken into consideration. Returns would be less if those were included.

Bottom Line

Overall, Macquarie Healthcare I ( DLHIX ) has a neutral Zacks Mutual Fund rank, and in conjunction with its comparatively strong performance, average downside risk, and lower fees, this fund looks like a somewhat average choice for investors right now.

This could just be the start of your research on DLHIX in the Sector - Health category. Performance

excerpt: Three mid-cap blend funds offer exposure to growth and value stocks, with three-year annualized returns ranging from 13.4% to 22%.
headline: 3 Top-Ranked Mid-Cap Blend Funds With Strong Return Potential
html_content:
Investors interested in comparatively less risky returns through exposure to both growth and value securities may opt for mid-cap blend mutual funds. While mid-cap funds are expected to offer the best of both large- and small-cap ones, blend funds, also known as "hybrid funds," aim for value appreciation through capital gains. Companies with market capitalization between $2 billion and $10 billion are generally considered mid-cap firms.

Moreover, mid-cap funds are believed to provide higher returns than their large-cap counterparts while witnessing a lower level of volatility than the small-cap ones. Meanwhile, blend funds provide significant exposure to both growth and value stocks. These funds owe their origin to a graphical representation of a fund's equity-style box.

Below, we will share with you three mid-cap blend mutual funds, namely The Gabelli Value 25 Fund GABVX, Hartford Schroders US Midcap Opportunities Fund SMDIX and Ave Maria Value AVEMX. Each has earned a Zacks Mutual Fund #1 Rank (Strong Buy), as we expect these mutual funds to outperform their peers in the future. To view the Zacks Rank and past performance of all mid-cap blend funds, investors can click here to see the complete list of funds.

The Gabelli Value 25 Fund seeks capital appreciation by primarily investing in equity securities of companies that are trading at substantial discounts to their private market value. GABVX advisors may also invest in securities involved in tender offers, mergers, liquidations or similar corporate reorganizations.

The Gabelli Value 25 Fund has three-year annualized returns of 22%. As of the end of June 2026, GABVX had 70 issues and invested 7.9% of its net assets in Madison Square Garden.

Hartford Schroders US Midcap Opportunities Fund invests most of its net assets in common and preferred stocksof mid-cap companies located in the United States. SMDIX advisors may also invest in over-the-counter securities.

Hartford Schroders US Midcap Opportunities Fund has three-year annualized returns of 19.4%. SMDIX has an expense ratio of 0.92%.

Ave Maria Value Fund invests most of its net assets in common stocks, preferred stocks and securities convertible into common stock in companies meeting its religious criteria, irrespective of their market capitalization. AVEMX chooses to invest in companies that its advisors believe are priced at a discount to their actual value.

Ave Maria Value Fund has three-year annualized returns of 13.4%.Timothy Schwartz has been one of the fund managers of AVEMX since January 2016.

excerpt: ALCEX, AVUNX and AVDNX offer diversified U.S. and international equity exposure, combining factor investing, strong returns and low expense ratios.
headline: 3 Avantis Mutual Funds Capitalizing on Factor Investing
html_content:
Established in 2019 as an integrated unit of American Century Investments, Avantis Investors launched its first investment strategies in September of that year. The firm was created to bridge the gap between passive indexing and traditional active management, offering diversified portfolios with the potential to enhance long-term returns through disciplined investment decisions.

American Century, its parent company, was founded in Kansas City by Jim Stowers in 1958. The established asset manager provided Avantis with an experienced investment platform, research capabilities and operational infrastructure to expand its offerings. Since inception, Avantis has steadily broadened its investment capabilities across equities, fixed income and real assets, while expanding its reach to international markets.

Avantis follows a research-driven investment approach emphasizing company valuations, profitability and expected returns. It seeks to identify attractively priced businesses with sound fundamentals, while maintaining diversification and managing trading costs. The firm combines rules-based portfolio construction with active oversight, allowing flexibility in security selection and portfolio implementation as market conditions change.

Investor interest has fueled impressive expansion, with assets under management surpassing $150 billion in June 2026, less than seven years after launch. Avantis' focus on transparent processes, competitive fees and long-term investment discipline positions it for continued growth, although factor-based strategies may experience prolonged periods of underperformance.

Astute investors might choose to consider such funds at present. Mutual funds, in general, reduce transaction costs and diversify portfolios without an array of commission charges that are mostly associated with stock purchases (read more: Mutual Funds: Advantages, Disadvantages, and How They Make Investors Money).

We have thus selected three mutual funds that boast a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), have positive three-year and five-year annualized returns and minimum initial investments within $5000, as well as carry a low expense ratio.

Avantis U.S. Large Cap Value ALCEX primarily invests in diversified U.S. large-cap stocks, emphasizing value, profitability and relatively smaller companies within its universe. It uses financial data to select, weight and adjust holdings, and may lend securities and invest collateral in eligible assets.

Mitchell J. Firestein has been the lead manager of ALCEX since 2022. The three top holdings for ALCEX are Amazon (3.2%), Microsoft (3.2%) and Micron Tech (3.2%).

ALCEX’s 1-year and 3-year returns are 34.1% and 25.6%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.15%. ALCEX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1. To see how this fund performed compared to its category, and other 1 and 2 Ranked Mutual Funds, please click here.

Avantis U.S. Equity AVUNX invests in diversified U.S. equities across sectors and market capitalizations, emphasizing smaller companies with stronger profitability and value characteristics to pursue higher expected returns.

Daniel C. Ong has been the lead manager of AVUNX since 2019. The three top holdings for AVUNX are Nvidia (5.6%), Apple (5.4%) and Microsoft (4.4%).

AVUNX’s 1-year and 3-year returns are 18.4% and 23.5%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.15%. AVUNX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

Avantis International Equity AVDNX primarily invests in diversified non-U.S. equities across countries, sectors and market capitalizations, including foreign-currency securities and depositary receipts, to provide international exposure.

Mitchell J. Firestein has been the lead manager of AVDNX since 2019. The three top holdings for AVDNX are ASML (1.3%), Roche (0.9%) and Shell (0.8%).

AVDNX’s 1-year and 3-year returns are 16.8% and 22.4%, respectively, and its net expense ratio is 0.23%. AVDNX has a Zacks Mutual Fund Rank #1.

Bottom Line

Avantis has experienced rapid growth in investor adoption, reflecting rising demand for research-driven, cost-conscious investment strategies. Its combination of academic research, disciplined portfolio management and broad diversification provides a distinctive positioning in an increasingly competitive asset-management industry.

excerpt: Stran & Company posts higher Q3 revenues, improved margins and positive earnings, supported by strong SLS performance despite rising expenses.
headline: SWAG Stock Declines 12% Despite Q3 Earnings Turnaround, Margin Gains
html_content:
Shares of Stran & Company, Inc. SWAG have lost 12.1% since the company reported third-quarter 2026 earnings, underperforming the S&P 500 Index's 1.7% decline over the same period. Over the past month, the stock has lost 8.7% compared with the S&P 500's 4.3% decrease.

Stran reported third-quarter break-even earnings per share against a loss of 7 cents in the year-ago quarter. Net sales increased 8.2% year over year to $28.1 million from $26 million. Net income was approximately $35,000 against a net loss of $1.2 million a year earlier. Improved gross margins supported the profitability turnaround, partially offset by higher operating expenses.

Stran & Company, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Stran & Company, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Stran & Company, Inc. Quote

SWAG's Other Key Financial Metrics

Gross profit increased 32.4% to $9.4 million from $7.1 million in the prior-year quarter. Gross margin expanded approximately 610 basis points to 33.3% from 27.2%.

Operating expenses rose 7.5% to $9.5 million from $8.9 million. However, operating expenses as a percentage of sales declined to 33.9% from 34.1%. Operating loss narrowed to approximately $153,000 from $1.8 million. EBITDA improved to $260,000 from negative $1.1 million in the prior-year period.

The Stran segment's sales increased 4.7% to $18.5 million from $17.6 million. Segment gross profit grew 15.4% to $6.4 million, while gross margin improved to 34.4% from 31.2%.

Stran Loyalty Solutions (SLS) revenues increased 15.4% to $9.6 million from $8.3 million. Segment gross profit surged 92.4% to $3 million, with gross margin expanding to 31.2% from 18.7%. SLS generated operating income of approximately $687,000, reversing the prior-year operating loss of approximately $0.4 million.

For the first nine months of 2026, revenues increased 6.3% to $92.7 million, while net income reached $1.1 million against a $1 million loss a year earlier.

Operating cash flow improved to $1.8 million from negative $4.8 million in the year-ago comparable nine-month period.

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $7.4 million compared with $6.8 million at Dec. 31, 2025. Investments increased to $5.2 million from $4.9 million. Total current assets rose to $42.6 million from $38.6 million, while current liabilities rose to $19.6 million from $16.5 million.

SWAG's Management Commentary

Chief executive officer Andrew Shape emphasized the company's transition from investment and expansion toward profitable growth and stronger cash generation.

Management highlighted efforts to secure larger, comprehensive customer programs rather than individual promotional product orders. The strategy seeks to deepen customer relationships and improve operating efficiency.

Stran is also deploying artificial intelligence across order entry, quoting, artwork preparation, inventory management and customer service to automate processes and support scalability. Management identified SLS expansion, organic growth and selective acquisitions as strategic priorities.

Factors Influencing SWAG's Performance

Improved customer mix, effective cost management and lower tariffs supported margin expansion. SLS also benefited from an approximately $0.2 million tariff refund, which may not recur.

Higher employee-related costs and investments in Stran Digital Solutions increased expenses in the core segment. Corporate expenses also rose due to higher legal and accounting costs.

Despite improved profitability, tariffs, customer concentration and fluctuations in corporate spending remain potential headwinds.

SWAG's Outlook

Stran intends to accelerate profitable organic growth, expand SLS operations and leverage technology investments to improve margins and cash generation.

Management also plans to evaluate acquisitions involving complementary marketing services, emphasizing strategic fit and profitability rather than expansion alone.

Other Developments

During the quarter, Stran repurchased approximately 109,000 shares for $208,000. Around $5.6 million remained available under its authorized repurchase program at quarter-end.

Subsequently, approximately 4.3 million publicly traded warrants expired unexercised on Nov. 9, 2026. Another 5.7 million warrants were scheduled to expire by Dec. 10, potentially eliminating a substantial source of future shareholder dilution.

excerpt: Investors need to pay close attention to JCI stock based on the movements in the options market lately.
headline: Implied Volatility Surging for Johnson Controls International Stock Options
html_content:
Investors in Johnson Controls International plc JCI need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Jan 15, 2027 $45 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Johnson Controls International shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Johnson Controls International is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Building Products – Wood industry that ranks in the Bottom 6% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 30 days, two analysts have increased their earnings estimates for the current quarter, while one analyst has revised the estimate downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from $1.12 per share to $1.15 in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Johnson Controls International right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there’s a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

excerpt: China's trade surplus tops $1 trillion as AI-driven exports surge, creating opportunities in tech-oriented ETFs while highlighting domestic demand weakness.
headline: China's Trade Surplus Exceeds $1T: Time to Rebalance Your ETF Portfolio?
html_content:
China’s trade surplus reached $1.043 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, surpassing $1 trillion for the second straight year and crossing the threshold a month earlier than in 2025. This development comes against a backdrop of persistently sluggish domestic consumption, a prolonged property market downturn and an economy increasingly reliant on foreign demand. 

The nation’s October exports surged 35.2% year over year to $412.33 billion, driven by the global artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom, with semiconductor exports jumping 111.1% in the first 10 months. Imports also rose 41.6% to $307.05 billion, reflecting efforts to address trade imbalances. 

For exchange-traded fund (ETF) investors, this milestone places a spotlight on their portfolio exposure to Chinese equities, particularly those tracking export-oriented sectors, while raising questions about sustainability amid growing trade tensions with the United States and the European Union.

The question for investors is what China’s trade surplus means for its broader economy and how those effects could shape Chinese stocks and the ETFs that hold them.

China’s Surplus Paradox

China’s $1 trillion surplus is a double-edged sword. It underscores the competitiveness of Chinese manufacturers, particularly in high-tech sectors benefiting from the AI boom.

Notably, semiconductor and automatic data processing machine exports have been standout performers, with overall high-tech exports rising 47.9% in the first 10 months. Industries expected to benefit include semiconductors, consumer electronics, electric vehicles, and industrial machinery — all key components of China’s export engine.

However, the surplus also reflects structural weaknesses. Household consumption in China sits at just 39-40% of GDP versus 68% in the United States, with Chinese households saving one-third or more of earnings due to a thin social safety net and falling property wealth. 

Government spending on healthcare, pensions, and welfare accounts for only 10% of GDP, far below the OECD average of 23%. 

Consequently, the impressive trade surplus largely reflects China’s export strength masking weak domestic demand. 

Looking Through the ETF Lens

China’s current situation suggests export-oriented companies may see earnings boosts, while consumer-facing sectors could lag. 

Headwinds include potential protectionist measures like the EU recently capping Chinese hybrid EV imports at 350,000 units annually and the risk that global demand may not absorb China’s excess capacity indefinitely.

The key nuance is that while export strength supports near-term earnings, sustainable growth requires rebalancing toward domestic consumption — a shift Beijing is yet to achieve meaningfully.

Thus, for ETF investors, China’s trade surplus story translates into targeted opportunities. 

In particular, ETFs tracking Chinese technology and semiconductor stocks stand to benefit from the AI-driven export surge. Investors may also consider ETFs focused on high-tech manufacturing and export-oriented industrials, while being mindful of geopolitical risks that could trigger volatility from time to time.  

On the contrary, a prudent investor might want to avoid ETFs with exposure to Chinese consumer staples or retail, for the time being, considering weak domestic consumption demand. 

China ETFs in Spotlight

Considering the aforementioned discussion, investors might want to increase their exposure to the following Chinese ETFs:

Invesco China Technology ETF CQQQ

This fund, with a market value worth $1.71 billion, offers exposure to 219 information technology securities. CQQQ charges 65 basis points (bps) in fees.

PDD Holdings enjoys the first spot in this fund, holding 12.53% of its assets. Notably, PDD Holdings owns Temu, an international e-commerce marketplace that generates massive sales globally across more than 90 markets. 

Themes China Generative Artificial Intelligence ETF DRGN 

This fund, with a net asset value of $26.64, includes 23 publicly traded Chinese companies, which derive significant revenues from Generative AI-related activities, including AI model training and provision, Generative AI application software, AI infrastructure and hardware and General AI application software. DRGN charges 39 bps in fees.

Xiaomi Corp enjoys the first spot in this fund, holding 8.81% of its assets. Xiaomi, well known globally for its smartphone brands, is heavily export-oriented. Its smartphone shipments have ranked No. 3 globally for 24 consecutive quarters.

Rayliant-ChinaAMC Transformative China Tech ETF CNQQ

text_content: China’s trade surplus reached $1.043 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, surpassing $1 trillion for the second straight year and crossing the threshold a month earlier than in 2025. This development comes against a backdrop of persistently sluggish domestic consumption, a prolonged property market downturn and an economy increasingly reliant on foreign demand. The nation’s October exports surged 35.2% year over year to $412.33 billion, driven by the global artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom, with semiconductor exports jumping 111.1% in the first 10 months. Imports also rose 41.6% to $307.05 billion, reflecting efforts to address trade imbalances. For exchange-traded fund (ETF) investors, this milestone places a spotlight on their portfolio exposure to Chinese equities, particularly those tracking export-oriented sectors, while raising questions about sustainability amid growing trade tensions with the United States and the European Union. The question for investors is what China’s trade surplus means for its broader economy and how those effects could shape Chinese stocks and the ETFs that hold them. China’s Surplus Paradox China’s $1 trillion surplus is a double-edged sword. It underscores the competitiveness of Chinese manufacturers, particularly in high-tech sectors benefiting from the AI boom. Notably, semiconductor and automatic data processing machine exports have been standout performers, with overall high-tech exports rising 47.9% in the first 10 months. Industries expected to benefit include semiconductors, consumer electronics, electric vehicles, and industrial machinery — all key components of China’s export engine. However, the surplus also reflects structural weaknesses. Household consumption in China sits at just 39-40% of GDP versus 68% in the United States, with Chinese households saving one-third or more of earnings due to a thin social safety net and falling property wealth. Government spending on healthcare, pensions, and welfare accounts for only 10% of GDP, far below the OECD average of 23%. Consequently, the impressive trade surplus largely reflects China’s export strength masking weak domestic demand. Looking Through the ETF Lens China’s current situation suggests export-oriented companies may see earnings boosts, while consumer-facing sectors could lag. Headwinds include potential protectionist measures like the EU recently capping Chinese hybrid EV imports at 350,000 units annually and the risk that global demand may not absorb China’s excess capacity indefinitely. The key nuance is that while export strength supports near-term earnings, sustainable growth requires rebalancing toward domestic consumption — a shift Beijing is yet to achieve meaningfully. Thus, for ETF investors, China’s trade surplus story translates into targeted opportunities. In particular, ETFs tracking Chinese technology and semiconductor stocks stand to benefit from the AI-driven export surge. Investors may also consider ETFs focused on high-tech manufacturing and export-oriented industrials, while being mindful of geopolitical risks that could trigger volatility from time to time. On the contrary, a prudent investor might want to avoid ETFs with exposure to Chinese consumer staples or retail, for the time being, considering weak domestic consumption demand. excerpt: UUP climbs to a 52-week high as hawkish Fed expectations boost the greenback. Can the rally continue?
headline: US Dollar ETF (UUP) Hits New 52-Week High
html_content:
For investors seeking momentum, Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish ETF UUP is probably on the radar now. The fund just hit a 52-week high and has risen 12.01% from its 52-week low price of $26.40 per share.

But are there more gains in store for this ETF? Let’s take a quick look at the fund and the near-term outlook to get a better idea of where it might head:

UUP in Focus

The underlying Deutsche Bank Long USD Currency Portfolio Index - Excess Return is a rules-based index composed solely of long U.S. Dollar Index futures contracts that trade on the ICE futures exchange. The product charges 70 bps in annual fees (See: All Currency ETFs).

Why the Move?

The U.S. dollar has strengthened as hawkish comments from Fed policymakers have reinforced expectations of further interest rate hikes. The value of the greenback is closely related to the Fed’s monetary policy, as its value moves inversely with interest rate adjustments by the Fed. Therefore, expectations for a more hawkish Fed stance could provide further support to the dollar.

According to TradingView, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) has gained about 0.54% over the past five days. The index has risen 5.01% over the past three months and 5.66% year to date.

More Gains Ahead?

Currently, UUP has a Zacks ETF Rank #3 (Hold) with a Medium risk outlook. It might continue its strong performance in the near term, with a positive weighted alpha of 6.58 (as per Barchart.com), which gives cues of a further rally.

excerpt: Disney plans to reinvest roughly $3 billion savings annually by fiscal 2029 in content, technology and marketing while prioritizing streaming and Experiences.
headline: Disney Q4 Earnings Call Details Plans to Reinvest Savings
html_content:
The Walt Disney Company DIS is budgeting more for content in fiscal 2027 while targeting roughly $3 billion in annual operating expense savings by fiscal 2029. Chief executive officer Josh D’Amaro said streaming and Experiences are the company’s main investment priorities.

Disney reported fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.77 per share, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.67. Revenues of $25.95 billion exceeded the $25.26 billion consensus estimate.

The Walt Disney Company Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

The Walt Disney Company price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | The Walt Disney Company Quote

DIS Keeps Its Fiscal 2027 Earnings Outlook

Disney reiterated its forecast for double-digit adjusted earnings per share growth in fiscal 2027, excluding the effect of fiscal 2026’s 53rd week. The outlook assumes no material deterioration in the global economy.

The company also expects total segment operating income to grow approximately 8% after adjusting for the extra week and reporting changes. It expects most of the year’s growth in both measures to occur in the first half.

In response to Morgan Stanley, chief financial officer Hugh Johnston identified procurement, IT and real estate consolidation, and shared services as sources of savings. Disney plans to reinvest most of the savings in content, technology and marketing, primarily in its direct-to-consumer businesses.

Disney Brings Hulu Into a Unified App

D’Amaro told Goldman Sachs that subscribers will get a fully integrated Disney+ and Hulu experience in December. Disney also plans to introduce creator content through its TikTok agreement ahead of the Dec. 18 release of Avengers: Doomsday.

The company is exploring a free streaming product. D’Amaro said it could attract price-sensitive viewers, give Disney more advertising inventory and help retain users.

Disney expects fiscal 2027 cash content spending to reach approximately $26 billion, up about 9%. In response to Wolfe Research, Johnston pointed to expanded college football rights and international programming, along with theatrical films that can also draw audiences on streaming.

DIS Shifts the Focus to Entertainment Margins

Disney will stop separately reporting subscription streaming operating income beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The metric reached $824 million in the fourth quarter, including an estimated $160 million benefit from the extra week.

In response to Guggenheim, Johnston said Disney wants flexibility to manage costs across Entertainment and earn returns on content across platforms. Disney will continue reporting subscription streaming revenues and add a category covering content and intellectual property revenues.

Asked by Barclays about reinvestment, Johnston said Disney remains focused on expanding streaming margins over time and expects Entertainment margins to expand. He said international content investment will take time to scale.

Disney Counts on Bookings as Capacity Grows

Johnston told Wolfe Research that forward bookings and added capacity underpin the forecast for high-single-digit Experiences operating income growth, excluding the extra week and incorporating the reporting changes.

Asked by BofA about cruise demand, D’Amaro said it was too early to gauge the effect of regional weakness on the Disney Adventure. Booked occupancy elsewhere in the fleet was holding up as capacity grew.

Disney expects consumer pressure at its Hong Kong and Shanghai parks to persist in fiscal 2027. At Walt Disney World, first-quarter resort bookings were running ahead of the prior year.

DIS Expands ESPN’s College Football Rights

Beginning in 2027, the expanded College Football Playoff will increase to 23 games from 11. ESPN holds exclusive rights across all rounds and can distribute games across ESPN and ABC.

Johnston told Guggenheim that ESPN can sublicense games and will evaluate those arrangements case by case. He expects sublicensing to play a limited role.

Disney expects reported Sports operating income to decline in the first quarter because of playoff scheduling, then grow strongly in the second quarter with help from ESPN’s first Super Bowl broadcast.

Disney Sets a May Investor Event

Johnston pointed Barclays to streaming and Experiences performance, segment operating margins, earnings and free cash flow as measures of returns on reinvestment.

D’Amaro said Disney will outline its longer-term strategy at an investor event in May 2027.

What Zacks Rank and Style Scores Signal for DIS

DIS carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), which points to a neutral near-term outlook based on earnings estimate revisions. Its Growth Score of B is its strongest individual grade, ahead of its Value Score of C and Momentum Score of D.

You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

The VGM Score of C indicates a middle-tier reading across the three styles. The Zacks Rank can change as analysts revise earnings estimates after the latest results.

excerpt: Interlink's Q3 loss per share narrows year over year on strong sensor shipments, but rising production costs and weaker Calman sales pressure margins.
headline: LINK's Q3 Loss Narrows Year Over Year on Sensor Demand Growth
html_content:
Shares of Interlink Electronics, Inc. LINK have declined 13.5% since the company reported its earnings for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026. This compares with the S&P 500 index’s 2.6% decline over the same period. Over the past month, the stock has fallen 30.5%, underperforming the S&P 500’s 4.3% decline.

Interlink incurred a loss of 2 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026, narrower than the year-ago loss of 3 cents per share. 

Revenues increased 3.4% year over year to $3.1 million from $3 million, driven by higher shipments of force-sensing and gas-sensor products, partially offset by lower sales of Calman printed electronic products. 

Net loss narrowed to $0.32 million from $0.34 million in the prior-year quarter.

Interlink Electronics, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Interlink Electronics, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Interlink Electronics, Inc. Quote

LINK's Other Key Financial Metrics

Gross profit declined 7.8% year over year to $1.1 million from $1.2 million. Gross margin contracted 450 basis points to 37.3% from 41.8%, reflecting higher material and production expenses and an unfavorable product mix.

Operating expenses decreased 2.6% to $1.5 million from $1.6 million. Engineering, research and development expenses declined 10.7% to $0.3 million, while selling, general and administrative expenses remained relatively stable at $1.2 million.

Operating loss widened to $0.4 million from $0.3 million a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA loss increased to $0.2 million from $0.06 million, indicating continued pressure on underlying operating profitability.

LINK's Balance Sheet Position

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $2.3 million, down from $2.7 million at Dec. 31, 2025. 

Total assets decreased to $11.4 million from $11.7 million, and stockholders' equity fell to $8.8 million from $9.2 million.

LINK's Management Commentary

Chairman, president and chief executive officer Steven N. Bronson emphasized continued investment in the company's operations to support long-term growth.
Management expressed confidence that its existing technologies, manufacturing capabilities and additional sales and marketing resources would support organic growth in the coming years.

During the quarter, Interlink established a 4,000-square-foot research and development center in Rotherham, UK, focused on next-generation smart functional textiles.

The company also added a 10,000-square-foot facility adjacent to its existing operations in Irvine, Scotland. The facility will support high-volume conductive transfer printing and printed electrode production for medical and diagnostic applications.

Factors Influencing LINK's Performance

Higher demand for force-sensing and gas-sensor products supported quarterly revenue growth. However, weaker Calman printed electronics sales and increased production costs pressured gross profitability.

Management also noted that customer ordering patterns and production cycles influence shipment timing and volumes, potentially creating quarterly revenue fluctuations.

Despite reduced operating expenses, lower gross profit contributed to a wider operating loss. Continued investments in product development and manufacturing capacity could support future growth, although their financial contributions remain uncertain.

Other Developments

Interlink reiterated expectations that its previously announced transformative acquisition could close before the end of 2026, subject to satisfactory due diligence, execution of necessary documentation and financing availability.
The proposed transaction is projected to generate approximately $50 million in combined revenues and more than $4 million in adjusted EBITDA for 2026 on a pro forma basis.

These projections represent the anticipated combined business rather than Interlink's standalone results. Completion remains contingent on financing and other closing conditions, while the integration of acquired operations could introduce additional execution risks.

excerpt: Orbit International's Q3 loss per share narrows year over year as sales rise 6.5%, but margin pressure and contract delays persist despite a backlog increase.
headline: ORBT Reports Narrower Q3 Loss on Rising Power Group Demand
html_content:
Shares of Orbit International Corp. ORBT have declined 6.3% since the company reported its earnings for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500 Index’s 2.6% drop over the same period. Over the past month, the stock has fallen 11.2% compared with the S&P 500’s 4.3% decline.

Orbit International incurred a loss of 20 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026, narrower than the year-ago loss of 26 cents. 

Net sales increased 6.5% year over year to $6.2 million from $5.8 million. 

Net loss narrowed to $0.8 million from $0.9 million in the prior-year quarter. However, weaker gross margins and higher interest expenses continued to weigh on operating performance.

Orbit International Corp. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Orbit International Corp. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Orbit International Corp. Quote

ORBT's Other Key Financial Metrics

Gross profit declined 4.1% year over year to $1.8 million from $1.9 million. Gross margin contracted 320 basis points to 28.7% from 31.9%, indicating continued pressure on profitability despite higher sales.

Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased 3.8% to $2.4 million from $2.5 million. Interest expenses increased to $0.1 million from $0.05 million in the prior-year quarter.

Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $0.6 million from a loss of $0.5 million a year earlier.

Backlog stood at approximately $14.9 million as of Sept. 30, 2026, up from $12.3 million as of Dec. 31, 2025, reaching its highest level since September 2024. Backlog increased 27.5% at the Orbit Instrument division and 40.7% at Simulator Product Solutions (“SPS”), while the Orbit Power Group (“OPG”) recorded a modest increase.

Cash and cash equivalents increased to $0.9 million from $0.7 million at the end of 2025. Inventories rose to $9.3 million from $8.5 million. 

Total assets edged down to $22.16 million from $22.21 million.

Stockholders' equity remained relatively stable at $12.8 million. Book value per share declined to $2.58 from $3.83 over the same period.

For the first nine months of 2026, operating cash outflows increased to $3.8 million from $3.5 million in the corresponding prior-year period.

ORBT's Management Commentary

President and CEO Mitchell Binder attributed weaker operating performance to delayed government contracts and lower bookings, particularly at the Orbit Instrument division. Customer delays in awarding follow-on contracts and temporary production pauses disrupted delivery schedules.

Management highlighted improved profitability at OPG, supported by higher sales and stronger margins. SPS also recorded improved operating results over the nine months, although supply-chain disruptions delayed certain third-quarter shipments.

Binder noted that SPS continues to face elevated legal expenses and requires additional sales growth to achieve profitability.

Factors Influencing ORBT's Results

Contract timing remained a major challenge, with delayed awards affecting production schedules and fixed-cost absorption at the Electronics Group. Supply-chain disruptions further constrained SPS shipments, while litigation-related expenses pressured costs.

Conversely, improved demand for OPG's power products provided some support. OPG bookings through Oct. 31, 2026 increased 42.9% year over year, while bookings for VPX-based power supplies exceeded $5 million for the first time.

SPS bookings rose 6.4% over the same period, indicating improving order activity despite execution challenges.

ORBT's Outlook

Management expects improved delivery schedules at Orbit Instrument and stronger operating results at SPS during the fourth quarter of 2026.
However, approximately $6 million in outstanding proposals from two major Orbit Instrument customers are now expected to receive awards in the first half of 2027.

Management also expects VPX power supplies to support future OPG revenue growth. Potential production awards associated with Q-Vio's next-generation handheld military equipment program are not anticipated before the second half of 2027, reflecting government funding uncertainties.

Other Developments at ORBT

Orbit International strengthened its liquidity through a $4.1 million equity private placement and a new asset-based credit facility providing up to $6 million in financing, subject to borrowing-base availability. The placement involved issuing 1.6 million common shares at $2.50 each.

excerpt: Housing Starts Increased More Than Expected
headline: Housing Starts Increased More Than Expected
html_content:
Pre-market futures are attempting to break the spell of falling markets this morning, and NVIDIA’s (NVDA) winning Q3 report yesterday afternoon looks to be contributing the desired effect: the Dow is up just +15 points, but the Nasdaq is a much stronger +217 points, with the small-cap Russell 2000 down -6 points.

Crude oil prices continue to drift downward, and bond yields are holding steady. Perhaps tomorrow’s IPO of Anthropic will continue to garner positive sentiment. Lord knows we could use it, after the last six or seven weeks of trading.

Housing Starts, Building Permits Mixed for October

Ahead of today’s open, Housing Starts posted their first up-month of the past four, with 1.31 million seasonally adjusted, annualized units for October +9.9% above the downwardly revised 1.19 million in the previous month. Single-family houses grew +4% last month, whereas Multi-family far outperformed, +24%. We’re still well off the 67-year average on monthly housing starts, but we’ll take good news where we can get it.

The problem in this report came in the proxy for future Starts: Building Permits, which fell -7.4% to 1.295 million seasonally adjusted, annualized units in October. This is the lowest number of new permits since the initial months of the Covid pandemic, and it points to lower Starts in future months. Building permits have delivered negative numbers in eight of the past 12 months.

Earnings Results at a Glance: TGT, LOW, TJX

Shares of Target (TGT) are up slightly following the big-box retailer’s Q3 earnings report this morning. The company reported earnings of $2.65 per share versus expectations of $2.05, although this is partly seen as the company benefiting from the tariff reimbursement. Target raised its full-year outlook by +1%.

Lowe’s (LOW also came in ahead of expectations on its Q3 report ahead of today’s open. However, the tariff reimbursement looks to have made up the lion’s share of the quarterly beat — earnings of $3.10 per share were ahead of the $2.86 in the Zacks consensus — and earnings guidance for the full year was a tad weak. Shares are down -5.7% on the news.

The TJX Companies (TJX) also beat earnings estimates this morning, if only by a penny to $1.34 per share. Revenues came in ahead of forecasts, as well, and strong comps helped the shares gain +6% in early trading. (Also, this stock had been down -15% year to date.)

Anthropic Sets IPO Price Today

It’s almost here: the first of the mega pure-play AI stocks, Anthropic, sets the share price for its Initial Public Offering (IPO) later today. Originally put in the range of $70-78 per share, which would bring the company to a market capitalization of $1.4 trillion. Sources now say these figures may come in higher for the enterprise-based developer of AI assistant Claude. Reportedly, there is $100 billion in retail demand for the shares.

The company must close its order books and lock-in total demand by the closing bell of today’s trading session. Then, the stock will be available under the ticker symbol “ANT” starting tomorrow.

excerpt: BOK Financial (BOKF) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Why Is BOK Financial (BOKF) Up 1.9% Since Last Earnings Report?
html_content:
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for BOK Financial (BOKF). Shares have added about 1.9% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

But investors have to be wondering, will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is BOK Financial due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for BOK Financial Corporation before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

BOK Financial Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates as NII & Loans Rise Y/Y

BOK Financial’s third-quarter 2026 earnings of $2.64 per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.54. The bottom line jumped 18.9% from the prior-year quarter.

Results benefited from higher net interest income (NII) and loan growth. A decline in operating expenses was another positive. However, lower total fees and commissions and sequentially lower deposits were major undermining factors.

Net income attributable to shareholders (GAAP basis) was $159.9 million compared with $140.9 million in the prior-year quarter.

Revenues Rise & Expenses Decline

Quarterly net revenues of $561.4 million (NII and total other operating revenues) rose 2.4% year over year. The reported revenue figure of $557.93 million in the supplied earnings-estimate table missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.91%.

NII was $370 million, up 9.6% year over year. The net interest margin expanded 9 basis points to 3.00%.

Total fees and commissions were $188 million, down 8.1% year over year. The decline was driven by lower brokerage and trading revenues, mortgage banking revenues, and other revenues, partially offset by higher fiduciary and asset management revenues, transaction card revenues, and deposit service charges and fees.

Total other operating expenses were $360.7 million, down 2.5% year over year. This decline was mainly driven by lower personnel, professional fees and services, FDIC and other insurance, business promotion, printing, postage and supplies, and amortization of intangible assets expenses, partially offset by higher data processing and communications and other expenses.

The efficiency ratio was 63.52% compared with the prior-year quarter’s 66.66%. A fall in the efficiency ratio indicates a rise in profitability.

Commercial Banking’s net income before taxes was $140.7 million, up 1.7% year over year. Consumer Banking’s net income before taxes was $14.5 million, down 0.2% year over year. Wealth Management’s net income before taxes was $28.8 million, down 21.2% year over year.

Loans Rise & Deposits Decline Sequentially

As of Sept. 30, 2026, total loans were $27.7 billion, up 2.4% from the prior quarter and 11.5% year over year. The sequential increase was driven by growth in energy, commercial real estate loans secured by industrial facilities, and mortgage finance loans.

Total deposits were $39.5 billion, down 0.8% sequentially but up 2.7% year over year. The sequential decline was due to lower demand, interest-bearing transaction and savings deposits, partially offset by higher time deposits.

Credit Quality Improves Y/Y

As of Sept. 30, 2026, non-performing assets were $66.6 million, or 0.24% of outstanding loans and repossessed assets, compared with $74.1 million, or 0.30%, in the prior-year quarter.

The company recorded nil provisions for credit losses compared with $2 million in the prior-year quarter.

The company recorded net charge-offs of $886,000 compared with $3.6 million in the year-ago quarter.

The allowance for loan losses was 0.98% of outstanding loans as of September 30, 2026, which declined 14 bps from the year-ago quarter.

Capital & Profitability Ratios

As of Sept. 30, 2026, the common equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 12.73% compared with 13.60% a year earlier. The Tier 1 capital ratio and total capital ratio were 12.73% and 14.43%, respectively, compared with 13.61% and 14.48% as of September 30, 2025.

At the end of the third quarter, return on average equity was 10.43%, up from the year-earlier quarter’s 9.38%. Return on average assets was 1.15%, up from 1.08% a year ago.

Share Repurchase Update

The company did not repurchase any shares during the third quarter of 2026, compared with 365,547 shares for $40.6 million at an average price of $111 per share in the prior-year quarter.

2026 Outlook

The company expects end-of-period loan growth of more than 10% from the 2025 reported level, compared with the prior outlook of 10%.

Management expects NII to be in the range of $1.43-$1.44 billion for 2026.
Total fees and commission revenues are anticipated to be more than $800 million, primarily due to a mix shift from trading fees to net interest income.

Non-interest expenses (excluding the FDIC special assessment) are expected to grow nearly 1% from the year-ago level.

Total revenues are expected to grow in the mid-single-digit guidance from the $2.2 billion reported in 2025. 

Management now expects the efficiency ratio to be approximately 62%, compared with the previous outlook of 62%. 

The company expects provision expenses to be below $10 million.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

In the past month, investors have witnessed a flat trend in estimates revision.

VGM Scores

At this time, BOK Financial has a poor Growth Score of F, however its Momentum Score is doing a lot better with a C. Following the exact same course, the stock has a grade of C on the value side, putting it in the middle 20% for value investors.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of D. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

BOK Financial has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

excerpt: W.R. Berkley (WRB) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Why Is W.R. Berkley (WRB) Up 6% Since Last Earnings Report?
html_content:
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for W.R. Berkley (WRB). Shares have added about 6% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is W.R. Berkley due for a pullback? Before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late, let's take a quick look at the most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the important catalysts.

W.R. Berkley Q3 Earnings Beat, Revenues Miss, Premiums Rise Y/Y

W.R. Berkley Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 operating income of $1.17 per share, which beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.63%. The bottom line increased 6.4% year over year. Operating revenues of $3.76 billion rose 1.8% year over year but missed the consensus estimate by 1.19%.

The insurer benefited from higher premiums and increased net investment income, partly offset by higher expenses and catastrophe losses. Net premiums earned jumped 1.8% year over year.

WRB's Q3 Performance Highlights

W.R. Berkley’s net premiums written increased 1.3% year over year to $3.27 billion, driven by growth in the Insurance segment. Net premiums earned rose to $3.21 billion from $3.16 billion in the year-ago quarter. Our estimate was pegged at $3.31 billion.

Net investment income grew 9.2% year over year to $383.5 million, supported by higher income from the core investment portfolio. Income from fixed-maturity securities increased 10.3%, while the core portfolio contributed $369.1 million, up 12% year over year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at $398.2 million. Our estimate was pegged at $384.3 billion.

Total expenses jumped 1.4% year over year to $3.16 billion, reflecting higher loss and loss expenses and other operating costs, partly offset by lower expenses from non-insurance businesses. Our estimate was pegged at $3.25 billion.

The consolidated loss ratio improved 20 basis points (bps) year over year to 62.2%. Our estimate was pegged at 63.6%, while the Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at 63.6%.

The expense ratio deteriorated 10 bps to 28.6%. Our estimate was pegged at 29.2%, while the Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at 28.3%.
The combined ratio, a measure of underwriting profitability, improved 10 bps to 90.8%. Our estimate was pegged at 92.8%, while the Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at 90.95%.

Catastrophe losses increased to $85.9 million from $78.5 million in the year-ago quarter. The current accident year combined ratio, excluding catastrophe losses, was 88.1%.

Berkley's Insurance Segment Results

Net premiums written at the Insurance segment increased 3.2% year over year to $2.9 billion in the quarter, in line with our estimate. Growth was primarily driven by higher premiums from other liability, auto, professional liability and short-tail lines.

Gross premiums written rose 4.9% to $3.56 billion, reflecting continued underwriting activity across the segment. Our estimate was pegged at $2.95 billion.

The segment's combined ratio improved 60 bps year over year to 91.7%. Our estimate was pegged at 93.4%, while the Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at 91.7%.

The loss ratio improved 60 bps to 63.3%. Our estimate was pegged at 64.5%, while the Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at 63.7%.

The expense ratio remained unchanged at 28.4%. Our estimate was pegged at 28.9%, while the Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at 28%.

W.R. Berkley exited the third quarter of 2026 with total assets worth $45.68 billion compared with $43.93 billion at the 2025-end level.

Senior notes and other debt declined slightly from the 2025-end level to $1.83 billion. Book value per share increased 0.6% from the 2025-end level to $25.87.

W.R. Berkley repurchased approximately 309,508 common shares for $21.1 million during the third quarter of 2026, continuing its capital return activities.

During the first nine months of 2026, the insurer returned $728.6 million to shareholders, including $435.1 million through share repurchases.

excerpt: Zions (ZION) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.
headline: Why Is Zions (ZION) Down 0.7% Since Last Earnings Report?
html_content:
It has been about a month since the last earnings report for Zions (ZION). Shares have lost about 0.7% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

But investors have to be wondering, will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Zions due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Zions Bancorporation, N.A. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

Zions Q3 Earnings Beat on Higher Revenues & Provision Benefit

Zions’ third-quarter 2026 earnings of $1.78 per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.64. The bottom line increased 20.3% from the year-ago quarter.

Results benefited from higher NII, growth in customer-related fee income and improved credit quality. However, increased operating expenses and a contraction in NIM were headwinds.

Net income attributable to common shareholders (GAAP) was $262 million, up 18.6% year over year. We had projected the metric to be $230.7 million.

Revenues Improve, Expenses Rise

Net revenues (taxable-equivalent) were $893 million, up 2.4% year over year. The top line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $892.9 million.

NII was $684 million, up 1.8% from the prior-year quarter. The increase was primarily driven by lower funding costs and growth in average loans, money market investments and deposits. NIM declined 5 bps year over year to 3.23%. Our estimates for NII and NIM were $684 million and 3.27%, respectively.

Non-interest income was $197 million, up 4.2%. Customer-related non-interest income rose 17.8% to $192 million, reflecting broad-based growth across fee-generating businesses. Adjusted customer-related non-interest income was $182 million, up 4.6%. We had projected non-interest income of $191.8 million.

Adjusted non-interest expenses were $549 million, up 5.6% year over year. Higher salaries and employee benefits, technology costs and professional and legal services primarily drove the increase. Our estimate for the metric was $553.5 million.

The adjusted efficiency ratio was 61.9% compared with 59.6% in the year-ago quarter, indicating higher expenses relative to revenues.

Loan Balances Remain Stable, Deposits Grow

As of Sept. 30, 2026, net loans and leases held for investment were $61.8 billion, stable sequentially. Total deposits were $77.9 billion, up 1.7% from the prior quarter. Our estimates for net loans and leases held for investment and total deposits were $62.7 billion and $77.7 billion, respectively.

Credit Quality Improves

The ratio of non-performing assets to loans and leases and other real estate owned declined to 0.50% from 0.54% in the year-ago quarter. Net loan and lease charge-offs were $3 million, down from $56 million in the prior-year quarter.

The company recorded a provision for credit losses benefit of $8 million against an expense of $49 million in the year-ago quarter. 

Classified loans declined to 3.40% of total loans from 4.01%, while criticized loans decreased to 4.20% from 4.75%. The allowance for credit losses represented 1.11% of loans and leases, down from 1.20%.

Strong Capital & Profitability Ratios

As of Sept. 30, 2026, the estimated common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 11.8%, up from 11.3% in the year-ago quarter. The Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio was 11.9% compared with 11.4% a year ago, while the Tier 1 leverage ratio improved to 9.2% from 8.8% at the end of the year-ago quarter.

Return on average assets was 1.14% compared with 0.99% a year ago. Return on average tangible common equity increased to 16.2% from 16%.

Share Repurchase Update

During the quarter, the company repurchased 1.1 million shares for $75 million.

Third-Quarter 2027 Outlook

The company expects period-end loan balances to increase 2-4% on a year-over-year basis. Growth will be driven by an increase in C&I loans and owner-occupied CRE. Further, CRE loans are expected to rise in the 1-3% range (below the overall loan portfolio's anticipated growth) because of higher interest rates and competitive pressures

NII is expected to witness 8-12% year-over-year growth, primarily driven by fixed-rate loan repricing, securities reinvestment and the assumption of three interest rate hikes in December 2026, March 2027 and June 2027. 

Adjusted customer-related non-interest income is anticipated to grow 6.-9% from the prior year, with capital markets and wealth management contributing in an outsized way.


Adjusted non-interest expenses are projected to witness a 4-6% increase year over year. Technology costs, increased marketing expenses and continued investments in revenue-generating businesses are expected to put pressure on non-interest expenses.

Management now expects 40-50 bps of positive operating leverage for 2026 compared with its earlier guidance of 100-150 bps. The downward revision reflects the acquisition of Basis Investment Group's multifamily agency platform.

How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

Since the earnings release, investors have witnessed a upward trend in fresh estimates.

VGM Scores

Currently, Zions has a average Growth Score of C, however its Momentum Score is doing a bit better with a B. Charting a somewhat similar path, the stock has a grade of A on the value side, putting it in the top quintile for value investors.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of A. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Interestingly, Zions has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

excerpt: Crude oil prices and crack spreads have retreated as geopolitical tensions have cooled. But if they rise again Delek US Holdings shares would likely attract more buyers.
headline: Bull of the Day: Delek US Holdings (DK)
html_content:
The oil and gas sector has shown relative outperformance throughout the year, and amid the recent rise in volatility and correction in AI stocks, it continues to stand out.

While other defensive sectors, including healthcare and consumer staples, have also attracted investor interest, energy has additional catalysts, particularly renewed geopolitical tensions surrounding the conflict in the Middle East.

Delek US Holdings (DK), an independent refiner, transporter and marketer of petroleum products, boasts a top Zacks Rank and strong price action.

More specifically, Delek is a bet on refining margins, commonly measured by crack spreads, or the difference between the price of crude oil and the petroleum products refined from it. These spreads have benefited from disruptions and uncertainty surrounding the conflict in the Middle East, and a continuation of those tensions could keep margins elevated.

That makes Delek a more targeted way to express a bullish view on the energy sector and the persistence of geopolitical tensions, though an easing of the conflict and normalization of refining margins would present risks to the thesis.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

DK Shares Gain Following Upgrades but Falls on Earnings

Analysts have revised DK’s earnings estimates sharply higher as crack spreads widened to record levels this fall, lifting the stock to a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Its most recent earnings report was a blowout, with record net income of $1.13 billion and refining EBITDA of $1.24 billion, up from $697 million a year ago. Management credited the quarter in part to its “industry leading distillate and jet yield.” Diesel and jet fuel made up about 40% of DK’s refinery output in Q3, which puts the company squarely in the part of the fuel market where supply is tightest.

But shares wobbled after the results. The stock has since regained its footing, though the initial reaction suggests the market may be betting that crack spreads will soon revert toward their historical averages.

For investors looking to hedge against the possibility that this doesn’t happen, and that spreads stay elevated because of a prolonged Middle East conflict or continued tightness in refined product markets, DK offers a compelling opportunity.

Below, we’ll look at the game theory behind why crack spreads could stay elevated longer than the market expects.


Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Why Refining Margins May Stay Elevated

Start with Iran. The IRGC has little reason to settle quickly. Each month Hormuz stays disrupted, Tehran adds pressure on the US economy and builds leverage at the negotiating table. It has refused to send its enriched uranium abroad, which Washington wants included in any first deal, and its record over the past year gives it little reason to trust US guarantees.

Even if a deal comes, the refined product market doesn’t snap back. The headline 3-2-1 crack spread has fallen by about half from its September record, but nearly all of that drop came from gasoline, which typically weakens after the summer driving season. Diesel margins have barely moved and are still roughly three times their historical norm.

The supply picture behind diesel keeps tightening. US distillate inventories are 8% below their five-year average and below even the 2022 lows for this time of year. Russia is restricting diesel exports through January, and Middle East crude flows have recovered much faster than fuel supply. Cheaper crude and scarce products are exactly the mix that widens refining margins.

This is where DK’s product mix matters. Diesel and jet fuel made up roughly 40% of DK’s refinery output last quarter. At current benchmark spreads, a barrel of diesel earns about four times the margin of a barrel of gasoline, so DK’s distillate output likely generates around three-quarters of its refining margin.

The market is pricing DK’s Q3 as the peak. For diesel-driven margins, it could be closer to a new floor.

Should Investors Buy Shares in DK?

Delek offers investors an interesting way to position for continued tightness in energy markets, particularly in diesel and other refined products.

The stock's top Zacks Rank reflects sharply rising earnings expectations, while its recent price action suggests investors remain skeptical that current refining margins are sustainable.

That skepticism is understandable as refining is a cyclical business, and a resolution to the conflict in the Middle East could bring substantial pressure on crack spreads and DK shares.

However, with distillate inventories already tight and supply disruptions unlikely to resolve overnight, there is a credible case that elevated margins could persist longer than expected.

For investors who share that view, DK offers a compelling opportunity, with the potential for further earnings upside if refining margins remain elevated into 2027.

excerpt: Rising demand for premium footwear and digital expansion fuels industry growth. Shoes & Retail Apparel industry players like ADDYY, SHOO, WWW, CRI and CAL are positioned for long-term gains.
headline: 5 Shoes & Retail Apparel Stocks to Watch as Industry Momentum Builds
html_content:
The Shoes and Retail Apparel industry is benefiting from increasing demand for premium, performance-oriented and versatile products. Growing consumer emphasis on comfort, functionality and durability, alongside rising participation in fitness and outdoor activities, is fueling demand for technical footwear, athleisure and lifestyle apparel. Continued innovation in materials, cushioning technologies, sustainable products and design is strengthening brand differentiation and supporting premium pricing opportunities.

The expansion of direct-to-consumer and digital channels is reshaping the industry's growth prospects. Investments in e-commerce, omnichannel capabilities, personalized marketing and loyalty programs are enhancing consumer engagement and brand visibility. Data-driven inventory planning, faster fulfillment and supply-chain efficiencies are also improving operational flexibility and profitability.

However, cautious discretionary spending, heightened promotional activity and intense competition remain key challenges. Elevated sourcing, labor and freight costs, alongside inventory imbalances, continue to pressure margins. Effective pricing strategies, inventory discipline and cost optimization remain crucial for sustaining profitability and long-term growth.

Looking ahead, sustainable growth will depend on innovation, digital capabilities, supply-chain agility and deeper consumer engagement. Established players such as adidas AG ADDYY, Steven Madden, Ltd. SHOO, Wolverine World Wide, Inc. WWW, Carter’s, Inc. CRI and Caleres, Inc. CAL appear well-positioned to manage near-term headwinds while pursuing long-term growth opportunities.

About the Industry

The Zacks Shoes and Retail Apparel industry comprises companies engaged in the design, sourcing, marketing and distribution of footwear, apparel and accessories for men, women and children across a diverse portfolio of brands. Their product offerings typically span athletic and casual footwear, fashion apparel, activewear, sports equipment, bags, balls and a broad range of sports and lifestyle accessories. Industry participants market their products through multiple channels, including company-operated stores, branded websites and other digital platforms. Many companies also maintain extensive wholesale distribution networks, selling through national retail chains, e-commerce platforms, sporting goods stores, department stores, mass merchandisers, independent retailers and catalogs.

A Look at What's Shaping the Shoes & Retail Apparel Industry

Premiumization & Performance Innovation: The Shoes and Retail Apparel industry continues to benefit from a structural shift toward premium, performance-oriented products. Consumers are increasingly prioritizing functionality, comfort and durability across categories, ranging from running footwear and athleisure to everyday apparel. Advances in cushioning systems, technical materials, sustainable fabrics and product customization are enabling brands to justify higher price points while strengthening customer loyalty and brand equity. Rising health awareness, greater participation in fitness activities and the growing adoption of active lifestyles are fueling the demand for technical footwear and versatile apparel that can transition seamlessly from workouts to everyday use. As brands increasingly combine fashion, innovation and performance, premiumization remains an important lever for margin expansion, customer retention and competitive differentiation.

Direct-to-Consumer Expansion & Digital Acceleration: The continued expansion of direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels and digital commerce represents another key growth driver for the Shoes and Retail Apparel industry. Brands are investing in e-commerce platforms, mobile applications, customer data analytics and loyalty ecosystems to deepen consumer relationships while gaining greater control over pricing, merchandising and distribution. Personalized marketing, membership programs and integrated omnichannel experiences are helping drive engagement, repeat purchases and higher customer lifetime value, while reducing the dependence on third-party retailers. Concurrently, investments in faster fulfillment, inventory optimization, supply-chain automation and localized sourcing are improving operational agility and responsiveness to rapidly changing consumer trends. As digital penetration increases and brands leverage first-party data more effectively, DTC expansion should support better inventory productivity, stronger brand economics and more sustainable long-term growth.

Margin Pressure From Promotions & Cost Inflation: Industry participants continue to face meaningful pressure on profitability. Elevated promotional activity, excess inventory in certain categories, cautious consumer spending and intense competitive discounting can constrain pricing power and force brands to rely on markdowns to stimulate demand. At the same time, persistent cost pressures across raw materials, labor, freight and sourcing continue to weigh on gross margins. Although supply-chain conditions have improved considerably from prior disruptions, structurally higher operating costs, unfavorable product mix and continued promotional intensity may limit the pace of margin recovery. Moreover, footwear and apparel remain discretionary categories and are therefore particularly sensitive to inflation, weakening consumer confidence and shifts in household spending priorities. Consequently, revenue growth may not always translate into comparable earnings growth, making disciplined inventory management, cost control and pricing execution increasingly critical to profitability.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Prospects

The Zacks Shoes and Retail Apparel Industry is a 10-stock group within the broader Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector. The industry currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #98, which places it in the top 40% of more than 250 Zacks industries.

The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates bright prospects for the near term. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

The industry’s positioning in the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is the result of a positive earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are gradually gaining confidence in this group’s earnings growth potential.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let us look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation picture.

Industry vs. Sector

The Zacks Shoes and Retail Apparel industry has underperformed the sector and the S&P 500 in the past year.

Stocks in the industry have collectively declined 33% in the past year. Meanwhile, the Zacks Consumer Discretionary sector has fallen 6.4%, while the Zacks S&P 500 composite has risen 10.9%.

1-Year Price Performance

Shoes & Retail Apparel Industry's Valuation

On the basis of forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E), commonly used for valuing Consumer Discretionary stocks, the industry is currently trading at 22.68X compared with the S&P 500’s 18.29X and the sector’s 16.16X.

Over the last five years, the industry traded as high as 36.62X and as low as 17.37X, with a median of 25.42X, as the chart below shows.

5 Shoes & Retail Apparel Stocks to Watch

Wolverine: The company is engaged in designing, manufacturing and distributing a wide variety of casual and active apparel and footwear. It also manufactures children’s footwear and specially designed boots and accessories for industrial purposes. Wolverine’s focus on brand structure, increasing efficiency by removing costs, strategic review of its portfolio, improving working capital and lowering leverage bode well. The company continues to focus on strengthening its DTC business. Speed-to-market initiatives, deployment of digital product development tools, expansion of e-commerce platforms and frequent product introductions are steadily contributing to Wolverine’s performance.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for WWW’s 2026 sales and earnings suggests growth of 7.3% and 44%, respectively, from the year-ago quarter’s reported figures. The consensus estimate for WWW’s 2026 EPS has moved up 17.7% in the past seven days. The company has a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 23.2%, on average. Shares of this Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) company have surged 65.4% in the past year. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Price & Consensus: WWW

Steven Madden: This Long Island City, NY-based company is well-positioned to deliver durable upside, driven by a strategic shift toward higher-margin direct-to-consumer channels, wherein accelerating online and owned-store growth enhances pricing power and customer economics. SHOO’s acquisition of a complementary international DTC platform meaningfully expands scale, improves geographic mix and unlocks revenue and margin synergies through distribution and marketing integration.

Steve Madden continues to deepen consumer engagement and cultural relevance, particularly among Gen Z and millennials, key demographics for growth. SHOO has a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 14.8%, on average. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company’s 2026 sales and earnings indicates growth of 12.8% and 27.7%, respectively, from the year-ago quarter’s reported figures. The consensus estimate for SHOO’s 2026 EPS has increased 0.9% in the past 30 days. Shares of this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company have risen 8.2% in the past year.

Price & Consensus: SHOO

adidas: This leading manufacturer and seller of athletic and sports lifestyle products in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, North America, Greater China, the Asia Pacific and Latin America is poised to gain from strong demand, compelling products and the robust performance of its online business. ADDYY has been benefiting from improved sell-through of all Adidas products in the market. The company has been witnessing improved margins, driven by the recently implemented price increases and an improved channel mix.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADDYY’s 2026 sales and earnings indicates growth of 8.3% and 29.4%, respectively, from the year-ago quarter’s reported figures. The consensus estimate for ADDYY’s 2026 EPS has moved down by a penny in the past seven days. adidas delivered a negative earnings surprise of 1.9%, on average, in the trailing four quarters. This Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) stock has gained 7.4% in the past year.

Price & Consensus: ADDYY

Carter’s: This is the leading marketer of branded apparel and products for babies and young children in North America. The company has taken significant steps in pricing to adapt to market conditions and boost profitability. Its emphasis on essential core products and strong value offerings, particularly in inflationary markets, appeals to budget-conscious shoppers. Carter’s has also seen a notable increase in margin rates due to reduced inbound freight costs, which is a key factor in margin growth. This reflects the company's focus on efficient cost management and operational improvements.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CRI’s 2026 sales indicates growth of 3.1% from the year-ago quarter’s reported figure. The consensus estimate for CRI’s 2026 EPS has moved up 1.2% in the past 30 days. The company has a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 422.5%, on average. Shares of this Zacks Rank #3 company have rallied 21.5% in the past year.

Price & Consensus: CRI

Caleres: This Saint Louis, MO-based company designs, develops, sources, manufactures and distributes footwear in the United States, Canada, East Asia and internationally. Caleres offers a steadily improving investment case, supported by strong momentum in its brand portfolio, wherein lead brands continue to gain share and deliver healthy growth. The recent addition of Stuart Weitzman expands its premium positioning, with integration efforts expected to unlock meaningful cost synergies over time. The company is also seeing improving trends at Famous Footwear and strong e-commerce traction, signaling stabilizing consumer demand.

Caleres is prioritizing cost discipline, inventory management and structural efficiencies. These actions position the company for more durable margins and a stronger long-term financial profile. CAL has a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 26%, on average. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company’s fiscal 2026 sales and earnings indicates growth of 3.8% and 35.3%, respectively, from the year-ago quarter’s reported figures. The consensus estimate for CAL’s fiscal 2026 EPS has been unchanged in the past 30 days. Shares of this Zacks Rank #3 company jumped 31.1% in the past year. 

Price & Consensus: CAL
